Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

A person can think. They can think about thinking. They can think about their own thinking. They can think about any kind of thinking. At any given moment, they can think about anything, because everything in the brain that is connected to thinking is available at any time. They can also think about themselves. This kind of thinking is especially important because most people still naively believe that their self is some kind of substance, divided into a deep, true self and another, superficial self that isn't really the true self. In reality, the self is an abstract system that needs external content in order to perceive, interpret, categorize, and do everything else. Therefore, the self is as rich as the external input that guarantees richer categories and interpretations of the world – including the self. Poorer interpretations of the world also mean a poorer or more modest self.

In the new academic year, I will be lecturing on social neuroscience. One of its fundamental insights is that humans have brains capable of rich perceptual feedback, which also means rich representation or portrayal of the self. Consider the sad contrast between the brilliant intelligence of children and the mental grayness or cognitive modesty of average adults.

Thinking means creating an infinite number of mental categories, or rather, forming an infinite number of snowballing categories. Humans are capable of all this, but good stories don't just happen on their own.

Time and again, it turns out that thinking and storytelling can be incomprehensible or very understandable to other people; it can be rich or poor. A person can strive to be very understandable, but they can also use jargon and incomprehensible abstractions that no one understands, or that are even impossible to understand, which means that they probably don't understand them either, because they don't make sense. Furthermore, this also applies: a person understands the world around them and themselves in it best through stories. Not through a mountain of data and information, with which they are bombarded in schools and elsewhere. Why are stories so important to people?

Stories are important to people because they can be challenging; if they are well-made and told, they are exactly that. They challenge people to think. To think in new ways. To reconsider. Even about what they have already thought about. Because they can think in a new way, which means creating new meaning. If they want to, of course; otherwise, they won't.

Stories are important because they have meaning and significance. Because they create and spread it around them. Data and information don't have meaning and significance yet. They only have it when they are part of a story.

Telling such stories is also good because meaning is infinitely more important to a person than matter, objective things, and objects. Let me give an example.

Yesterday, I watched the movie Love, Simon. The feelings that arose from it made me think. Again. I was also impressed. Consider the skill of the editor who put together a thousand shots in such a way that excellent feelings, kind emotions, productive thoughts, pleasant affects, and everything else arose. What a skill!

A parallel presents itself. Think of the dead letters on paper that authors have written over the centuries – for example, composers who have left behind neat black marks on the musical staff. You read them, and suddenly a thousand feelings, thoughts, meanings, and significance arise, as if a new world is being created before you.

What happened in another person, in other people, happens, mutatis mutandis, in us, who read books, watch movies, listen to music, and admire paintings. All of this is made possible, in particular, by rich stories.

So, what does telling rich stories make possible? It creates new spiritual spaces in which we enjoy ourselves as living beings – each of us. That is exactly why we need each other as storytellers. To travel through different worlds, to be enriched by such journeys. It is almost miraculous that we can repeat them at any time. And it is worth repeating them so that we do not get lost, so that we do not stray among data, facts, information, and what is supposed to be knowledge.

In knowledge societies, stories are important. But not just any stories. The most important are the stories that are synchronized with selected events in the world. The most important are rich stories told by people with rich minds. People with poor or modest minds cannot tell any rich stories.

AUTHOR
Dušan Rutar develops the tradition that was first established by Plato and Aristotle when they realized what the fundamental duty of a human being is in this world.

Človek lahko razmišlja. Lahko razmišlja, da razmišlja. Razmišlja o svojem razmišljanju. Razmišlja o katerem koli razmišljanju. V vsakem trenutku lahko razmišlja o čemerkoli, saj je vse, kar je v možganih povezano z razmišljanjem, kadarkoli na voljo. Lahko razmišlja tudi o sebi. Tako razmišljanje je še zlasti pomembno, ker večina ljudi še vedno naivno verjame, da je njihov jaz nekakšna substanca, ločena na globinski pravi jaz in oni drugi površinski jaz, ki pač ni pravi. V resnici je jaz abstraktni sistem, ki potrebuje zunanje vsebine, da sploh lahko zaznava, razlaga, kategorizira in počne vse drugo. Jaz je zato toliko bogatejši, kolikor bogatejši je zunanji vnos, ki jamči za bogatejše kategorije in interpretacije sveta – vključno s seboj. Revnejše razlage sveta pomenijo tudi revnejši oziroma skromnejši jaz.
V novem šolskem letu bom predaval socialno nevroznanost. Njeno temeljno spoznanje je tudi tole: človek ima možgane, ki zmorejo bogat perceptualni feedback, to pa pomeni tudi bogato reprezentiranje ali predstavljanje sebe. Pomislite sedaj na žalostno nasprotje med sijočo bistroumnostjo otrok in miselno sivino oziroma kognitivno skromnost povprečnih odraslih ljudi.
Misliti pomeni tvoriti brezmejno veliko miselnih kategorij, oziroma pomeni oblikovanje brezmejnih kotalečim se sneženim kepam podobnih kategorij. Človek je zmožen za vse to, toda dobre zgodbe ne nastanejo same od sebe.
Vedno znova se izkaže, da je lahko razmišljanje in pripovedovanje zgodb za druge ljudi nerazumljivo ali pa zelo razumljivo; lahko je bogato ali pa revno. Človek se lahko potrudi, da je zelo razumljiv, lahko pa uporablja žargon in nerazumljive abstrakcije, ki jih ne razume nihče ali pa jih celo ni mogoče razumeti, kar pomeni, da jih verjetno celo sam ne razume, ker nimajo smisla. Poleg tega velja tudi tole: človek najbolj razume svet okoli sebe in sebe v njem skozi zgodbe. Ne s pomočjo gore podatkov in informacij, s katerimi je na primer zasut v šolah, pa tudi zunaj njih. Zakaj so zgodbe za ljudi tako zelo pomembne?
Zgodbe so za ljudi pomembne, ker so lahko izzivalne; če so dobro narejene in povedane, so natanko take. Ljudi izzivajo k razmišljanju. K novemu razmišljanju. K vnovičnemu razmisleku. Pripovedovanje takih zgodb je dobro tudi zato, ker je sam pomen za človeka neskončno pomembnejši od materije, objektivnih stvari in predmetov. Naj navedem primer.
Včeraj sem si ogledal film Love, Simon. Občutki, ki so se porodili ob tem, so mi dali misliti. Vnovič. Bil sem tudi navdušen. Pomislite na spretnost montažerja, ki je zložil tisoč kadrov skupaj tako, da so se porodili izvrstni občutki, prijazna čustva, produktivne misli, prijetni afekti in vse drugo. Kakšna spretnost!
Ponuja se vzporednica. Pomislite na mrtve črke na papirju, ki so jih zapisali avtorji skozi stoletja – na primer skladatelji, ki so pustili za seboj urejene črne packe na notnem črtovju. Preberete jih in nenadoma se vzbudi tisoč občutkov, misli, rojeva se pomen, smisel, kot bi nastajal pred vami nov svet.
Kar se je dogajalo v drugem človek, v drugih ljudeh, se, mutatis mutandis, dogaja v nas, ki beremo knjige, gledamo filme, poslušamo glasbo, občudujemo slike. Vse to omogočajo zlasti bogate zgodbe.
Kaj torej omogoča pripovedovanje bogatih zgodb? Ustvarja nove duhovne prostore, v katerih uživamo kot živa bitja – vsakdo od nas. Natanko zato potrebujemo drug drugega kot pripovedovalca zgodb. Da potujemo po različnih svetovih, da nas taka potovanja bogatijo. Skoraj čudežno je, da jih lahko ponovimo kadarkoli. In velja jih ponavljati, da se ne izgubimo, da ne zablodimo med podatki, dejstvi, informacijami in tem, kar naj bi bilo znanje.
V družbah znanja so torej pomembne zgodbe. A ne katere koli. Najpomembnejše so zgodbe, ki so sinhronizirane z izbranimi dogodki v svetu. Najpomembnejše so bogate zgodbe, ki jih pripovedujejo miselno bogati ljudje. Miselno revni oziroma skromni ljudje namreč ne morejo povedati nobene miselno bogate zgodbe.

The overuse and misuse of antibiotics has become a serious health problem. According to the authors of the study "Treating Children Without Antibiotics in Primary Healthcare" (2011), over 90 percent of upper respiratory infections are self-limiting, and even bacterial infections, such as ear and throat infections, often resolve on their own. The report discusses two treatment strategies: 1) avoiding antibiotic prescriptions and 2) delayed prescriptions. The authors urge doctors to make significant changes to their prescribing practices and encourage the public to raise awareness about the harmful effects, misuse, and overuse of antibiotics.

Why have antibiotics seemingly failed after only a few decades of widespread use, leading to the spread of deadly, resistant super-bacteria? The article "Post-antibiotic age" explains this phenomenon. It explores the changes in modern medicine by examining the fundamental assumptions of Louis Pasteur's germ theory and the discovery of penicillin, as well as Koch's postulates, which form the basis of modern medical doctrine.

Today, antibiotics are one of the main contributors to the excessive medicalization of children.

In his extensive report, "How to Survive in the World Without Antibiotics," Dr. Keith Scott-Mumby describes the risks of infections with dangerous, resistant bacteria and presents the use of around 40 natural antibiotics and antibiotic therapies for treatment and life-saving purposes, most of which can be administered at home. The majority of these natural approaches, many of which are even more potent than pharmaceutical drugs, have disappeared from use in modern medicine over the past few decades, despite their high effectiveness.

This article discusses ear, respiratory, eye, and throat infections.

The well-known American pediatrician, Robert S. Mendelsohn, treated ear, eye, respiratory, and throat infections in children without using antibiotics. He describes his experiences and the reasons for this pediatric practice, warns about the excessive medicalization of children, and provides examples of when medical help or medication is necessary in his book, "How to Raise a Healthy Child in Spite of Your Doctor."

In the article "Antibiotics and ear infections," a doctor of chiropractic, consultant, scientist, and lecturer on nutrition in pediatrics emphasizes that antibiotics have saved lives since the 1950s when the immune system fails due to widespread bacterial infections. However, it is precisely the use of these "miracle drugs" that has led to the emergence of serious bacterial diseases that are resistant to antibiotics. Children are the primary target for antibiotics, which is why misuse is most common in this age group. Strong, antibiotic-resistant bacterial strains can easily spread in daycare centers, and hospital-acquired super-infections are also a problem, affecting 10 percent of patients and causing death in 3 percent of cases, the author states. She lists the following side effects of antibiotic use: diarrhea, nutritional disturbances, cramps, fungal infections, irritability, rashes, blood disorders, and disruption of the immune system, leading to an increased risk of new infections, especially fungal infections and dangerous intestinal microbes (e.g., bacterial colitis caused by the bacterium Clostridium has a 3.5 percent mortality rate).

A 2006 study, "Wait-and-see Prescription for the Treatment of Acute Otitis Media," published in the American medical journal JAMA, compared the risks of antibiotic use (including gastrointestinal symptoms, allergic reactions, and the rise of resistant bacterial strains) with the data that the disease resolves on its own in most cases. In the study, half of the 283 children with ear infections received a standard prescription, while the other half were instructed to wait at least 48 hours before administering the first dose of antibiotics. Two out of three children avoided antibiotics by using the "wait-and-see" approach. As Dr. Darrel Crain explains in the article, at least half of the prescriptions issued are unnecessary, and the consequences of taking antibiotics are that they destroy bacteria that perform very important functions in our body, such as digesting food and producing vitamins. In his opinion, the "wait-and-see" approach, which doctors were already familiar with in the past, represents a significant advancement in medical science, comparable to the discovery of the importance of washing hands.

The scientific article "Antibiotic abuse: spare the child" warned about the seriousness of the problem and the mistaken belief that antibiotics cannot cause significant harm to human health as early as the 1980s. "Antibiotics should only be allowed in circumstances where their effectiveness is known or can be reasonably expected. At the same time, all efforts should be directed towards stopping their use as soon as possible. If antibiotic therapy is initiated due to the likelihood of septicemia, and after 48 or 72 hours, tests of properly collected cultures are negative, therapy should be discontinued," the article states.

The article about the impact of antibiotics on ear infections in children states that using breast milk as eye or ear drops every few hours often stops or cures the infection within 24 to 48 hours.

Traditional Chinese medicine has effective ways of treating ear infections, as does homeopathy; a 2001 study confirmed a significant reduction in symptoms after 24 hours compared to a placebo, according to Randall Neustaedter, a homeopath and practitioner of traditional Chinese medicine. He states in the article that studies have shown that antibiotics often fail and that prescribing antibiotics for ear infections should become a thing of the past, given the availability of these alternative treatments.

Modern studies on treating children without antibiotics show that over 90 percent of upper respiratory infections are self-limiting, and even bacterial infections, such as ear and throat infections, often resolve on their own. Science calls on doctors and the public to be aware of their overuse and misuse.

The article "Antibiotics and Aware Parent" also discusses ear infections from the perspective of parental measures. Some comparative statistics on the (non-)use of antibiotics are included in a summary of a report on the treatment of acute otitis media. Dr. Mary Ann Block provides a detailed description of the treatment of ear and respiratory infections without antibiotics in her book, "No more amoxicilline."

A British double-blind study from 2005, published in the medical journal Lancet, found that antibiotics are not necessary to treat acute conjunctivitis (pinkeye) in most children. A summary is also published here. "The health-economic arguments against prescribing antibiotics for conjunctivitis are compelling. Parents should be encouraged to clean their children's eyes," the authors conclude, adding that medical help is needed if unusual symptoms occur or if symptoms persist for more than a week.

Is the patient or the doctor the source of excessive antibiotic use?

Doctors acknowledge the problem of excessive antibiotic use but sometimes try to explain it as a demand or pressure from the patient (e.g., parents) to prescribe medication. However, medical sources that analyze the situation in practice do not agree with this. A Peruvian study from 2011 attributes the responsibility to doctors: "Interventions to improve antibiotic use practices should be directed at doctors, as a doctor's prescription is the most common reason for antibiotic use." A Chinese study from 2009 found that a patient who has knowledge about the appropriate use of antibiotics can influence a reduction in their use and that this knowledge increases the doctor's caution and attention to side effects, but it also worsens the quality of the doctor-patient relationship. Its results show that antibiotic abuse does not come from the patient but is largely a phenomenon driven by the supply side.

In the book "Beyond Antibiotic: 50 (or so) Ways to Boost Immunity and Avoid Antibiotics," doctors Schmidt, Smith, and Sehnert suggest that patients ask doctors the following questions when they prescribe antibiotics:

- Are you sure it's bacterial?
- Are you sure this antibiotic is the right one?
- Should we first determine which bacterial cultures are present?
- Is there another way to treat it besides antibiotics?
- What are the risks if we don't use them?
- What are the risks if we wait two to four days?
- Should we pay attention to certain dietary factors?
- Should we increase the intake of certain vitamins while taking antibiotics?
- Should we supplement with probiotic cultures to minimize the negative effects of antibiotics on the gut?
- Have you considered or investigated the role of food allergies in this disease?

If the doctor is not willing to pay attention to these questions, the patient has the right to a second opinion; "there are many doctors who will be willing to work with you as partners to explore these dilemmas," the authors state. And: "Antibiotics are perhaps absolutely necessary in certain situations where life is threatened by infection or where serious complications occur. We are fortunate to have antibiotics that can be used appropriately in emergency situations, but they should be used in conjunction with measures to strengthen the immune system, and a compromised gut flora should always be restored. Most importantly, we should then focus on discovering the cause of the infection, only then can real treatment begin."

Prekomerna in nepravilna uporaba antibiotikov je postala izjemno resen zdravstveni problem. Kot navajajo avtorji študije o zdravljenju otrok brez antibiotikov Treating Children Without Antibiotics in Primary Healthcare (2011), je prek 90 odstotkov obolenj zgornjih dihal samoomejujočih, pa tudi bakterijske okužbe, kot so npr. vnetja ušes in grla, pogosto izzvenijo same. Poročilo govori o dveh strategijah zdravljenja: 1) brez predpisovanja antibiotikov in 2) zakasnjeno predpisovanje. Avtorji pozivajo zdravnike k bistvenim spremembam načina predpisovanja, javnost pa k širjenju zavedanja o škodljivosti, zlorabah in prekomerni uporabi antibiotikov.
Zakaj so antibiotiki tako rekoč odpovedali že po dobrega pol stoletja njihove množične uporabe in povzročili širjenja smrtonosnih odpornih super-bakterij, pojasnjuje članek Post-antibiotic age – Post-antibiotična doba. Opisovanja sprememb v modernem zdravljenju se loti prek temeljnih predpostavk teorije mikrobov od Louisa Pasteurja in odkritja penicilina do Kochovih postulatov, na čemer temelji sodobna medicinska doktrina.
Antibiotiki so danes eden glavnih krivcev prekomerne medikalizacije otrok.
Zdravnik Keith Scott-Mumby v obsežnem poročilu How to Survive in the World Without Antibiotics – Kako preživeti v svetu brez antibiotikov opiše tveganje okužb z nevarnimi odpornimi bakterijami ter predstavi uporabo okoli 40 naravnih antibiotikov in antibiotičnih terapij za zdravljenje in varovanje življenja, ki jih lahko večinoma izvedemo sami. Velika večina naravnih pristopov, od katerih so mnogi celo bistveno močnejši od farmacevtskih zdravil, je času modernega zdravstva v minulih nekaj desetletjih iz uporabe izginila kljub njihovi visoki stopnji učinkovitosti.
O vnetju ušes, dihal, oči, grla
Znani ameriški pediater Robert S. Mendelsohn je v svoji karieri zdravil vnetja ušes, oči, dihal, angine in druge okužbe pri otrocih, brez uporabe antibiotikov. Izkušnje in razloge za tako pediatrično prakso, opozorila glede prekomerne medikalizacije otrok in primere, ko je pomoč zdravnika oz. zdravil nujna, opiše v priročniku How to Raise a Healthy Child in Spite of Your Doctor – Kako vzgojiti zdravega otroka vašemu zdravniku navkljub.

Glavna ciljna skupina za antibiotike so otroci, zato je tudi napačne uporabe največ pri otrocih. Močni, na antibiotike odporni bakterijski sevi se zlahka širijo v vrtcih, problem so tudi bolnišnične super-okužbe, ki ogrozijo desetino tamkajšnjih pacientov, v treh odstotkih pa so okužbe smrtne, pravi avtorica. Navaja naslednje stranske učinke uporabe antibiotikov: driske, motnje prehranjenosti oz. vsrkanja hranilnih snovi, krči, glivične okužbe, razdražljivost, izpuščaji, krvne motnje, zaradi uničenja normalne črevesne flore pride tudi do motenj delovanja imunskega sistema in do povečanega tveganja za nove okužbe, predvsem izbruha glivic in nevarnih črevesnih mikrobov (npr. bakterijski kolitis, povzročen z bakterijo clostridium, ima 3,5-odstotno stopnjo smrtnosti).
Študija iz leta 2006 Wait-and-see Prescription for the Treatment of Acute Otitis Media – Recept »počakaj in opazuj« za zdravljenje akutnega vnetja srednjega ušesa v ameriški medicinski reviji JAMA primerja tveganja uporabe antibiotikov (ki zajemajo gastrointestinalne simptome, alergijske reakcije in porast odpornih bakterijskih sevov) s podatki, da se bolezen v večini primerov omeji sama. Polovica od 283 otrok z vnetjem ušes je prejela standardni recept, pri drugi polovici so staršem naročili, naj počakajo vsaj 48 ur, preden dozirajo prvi odmerek antibiotika. Dva od treh otrok sta se s pomočjo recepta »počakaj in opazuj« izognila antibiotiku. Kot v članku o tem pojasni zdravnik Darrel Crain, je vsaj polovica izdanih receptov nepotrebnih, posledice jemanja pa so, da antibiotiki uničijo bakterije, ki opravljajo zelo pomembno delo v našem telesu, kot je prebavljanje hrane in tvorba vitaminov. Po njegovem mnenju recept »počakaj in opazuj«, ki so ga v preteklosti zdravniki že bili vajeni uporabljati, medicinski znanosti prinaša najbrž tako velik napredek kot odkritje o nujnosti umivanja rok.
Znanstveni članek Antibiotic abuse: spare the child – Zloraba antibiotikov: prizanesimo otroku je že v začetku 80. let opozoril na resnost problema in na zgrešena mnenja, da antibiotiki ne morejo narediti veliko škode zdravju človeka. »Antibiotike bi morali dovoliti le v okoliščinah, v katerih je njihova učinkovitost znana ali jo je realno mogoče pričakovati. Hkrati bi morali vse napore usmeriti v prekinitev njihove uporabe po najkrajšem možnem času. Če se antibiotična terapija uvede zaradi verjetnosti zastrupitve krvi (sepse) in so po 48 ali 72 urah testi pravilno vzetih kultur negativni, bi morali s terapijo prenehati,« navaja članek.
Uporaba materinega mleka kot kapljice za vneto oko ali uho vsakih nekaj ur pogosto zavre ali pozdravi okužbo v 24 do 48 urah, navaja ta članek o vplivu antibiotikov na vnetja ušes pri otrocih.
Tradicionalna kitajska medicina ima že stoletja ali tisočletja učinkovite načine zdravljenja vnetij ušes, prav tako homeopatija; študija iz leta 2001 je potrdila značilno zmanjšanje simptomov po 24 urah v primerjavi s placebom, pravi homeopat in zdravnik tradicionalne kitajske medicine Randall Neustaedter. V tem članku navaja, da antibiotiki po izsledkih študij neredko odpovedo in da bi moralo predpisovanje antibiotikov za vnetja ušes s tem, ko so na voljo tovrstna zdravljenja, postati stvar preteklosti.
Sodobne študije o zdravljenju otrok brez antibiotikov navajajo, da je prek 90 odstotkov obolenj zgornjih dihal samoomejujočih, pa tudi bakterijske okužbe, kot so npr. vnetja ušes in grla, pogosto izzvenijo same. Znanost poziva zdravnike in javnost k zavedanju o njihovi prekomerni uporabi in zlorabah.
O vnetju ušes z vidika starševskih ukrepov piše tudi članek Antibiotics and Aware Parent – Antibiotiki in zavedanje staršev. Nekatere primerjalne statistike (ne)uporabe antibiotikov vsebuje povzetek poročila o zdravljenju akutnega vnetja ušes. Zdravnica Mary Ann Block natančno predstavi zdravljenje vnetja ušes in dihal brez antibiotikov v knjigi No more amoxicilline – Nič več amoksicilina.
Britanska dvojna slepa študija iz leta 2005, objavljena v medicinski reviji Lancet, navaja, da antibiotiki pri večini otrok niso potrebni za zdravljenje akutnega vnetja očesne veznice (konjunktivitisa). Povzetek je objavljen tudi tukaj. »Zdravstveno-ekonomski argumenti proti predpisovanju antibiotikov so v primeru konjunktivitisa prepričljivi. Starše bi se moralo spodbujati, da čistijo otrokove oči,« sklenejo avtorji in dodajo, da je zdravniška pomoč na mestu, če pride do neobičajnih simptomov ali če simptomi vztrajajo več kot teden dni.
Vir prekomerne uporabe pacient ali zdravnik?
Zdravniki problem prekomerne uporabe antibiotikov priznavajo, a ga včasih skušajo pojasniti kot zahtevo oz. pritisk pacienta (npr. staršev), naj predpišejo zdravilo. Medicinski viri, ki analizirajo razmere v praksi, temu ne pritrjujejo. Perujska študija iz leta 2011 odgovornost pripiše zdravnikom: »Intervencije, da bi izboljšali načine uporabe antibiotikov, bi se morale usmerjati na zdravnike, kajti zdravniški recept je najobičajnejši razlog za uporabo antibiotika«. Kitajska študija iz leta 2009 ugotavlja, da lahko pacient, ki razpolaga z znanjem o ustrezni rabi antibiotikov, vpliva na zmanjšanje njihove uporabe ter da to znanje poveča zdravnikovo previdnost in pozornost glede stranskih učinkov, poslabša pa kakovost odnosa zdravnik-pacient. Njeni rezultati kažejo, da zloraba antibiotikov ne prihaja s strani pacienta, »temveč je v največji meri pojav, ki ga poganja ponudbena stran«.
V knjigi Beyond Antibiotic: 50 (or so) Ways to Boost Immunity and Avoid Antibiotics (Na drugi strani antibiotikov: (okoli) 50 načinov, kako okrepiti imunost in se izogniti antibiotikom) zdravniki Schmidt, Smith in Sehnert predlagajo pacientom, da zdravnikom zastavijo ta vprašanja, ko jim ti predpišejo antibiotike:
- Ste prepričani, da je bakterijsko?
- Ste prepričani, da je ta antibiotik pravi?
- Bi morali prej ugotoviti, za katere bakterijske kulture gre?
- Ali obstaja tudi kak drugačen način zdravljenja kot antibiotiki?
- Kakšna so tveganja, če jih ne uporabimo?
- Kakšna so tveganja, če počakamo dva do štiri dni?
- Bi morali posvetiti pozornost določenim prehranskim dejavnikom?
- Bi morali ob jemanju antibiotika povečati vnos določenih vitaminov?
- Bi morali nadomeščati probiotične kulture, da minimiziramo negativne vplive antibiotika na črevesje?
- Ste upoštevali oz. raziskali vlogo prehranskih alergij pri tej bolezni?
Če zdravnik ni pripravljen posvetiti svoje pozornosti tem vprašanjem, ima pacient pravico do drugega mnenja; »veliko zdravnikov obstaja, ki bodo kot partnerji pripravljeni skupaj z vami raziskati te dileme«, navajajo omenjeni avtorji. In še: »Antibiotiki so v določenih situacijah, kjer je zaradi okužbe ogroženo življenje ali kjer pride do resnih zapletov, morda absolutno nujni. Srečo imamo, da imamo antibiotike, ki jih lahko ustrezno uporabimo v nujnih situacijah, toda uporabiti bi jih morali skupaj z ukrepi za okrepitev imunskega sistema, okrnjeno črevesno floro pa bi bilo treba vedno nadomestiti. Najpomembneje pa je, da bi se morali nato posvetiti odkritju vzroka okužbe, šele tako bi se začelo resnično zdravljenje.«

Water is one of the oldest sources of energy that humans have learned to harness. It is the most important renewable energy source. More than a fifth of all electricity in the world is generated using hydropower, which our ancestors began to utilize over two thousand years ago. For centuries, hydropower has performed physical work instead of humans. It was mainly used to directly power mills, sawmills, pumps, and other similar devices. Later, it was discovered that hydropower could be converted into electrical energy.
Throughout history, humans have only refined and increased the scale of hydropower utilization for energy purposes. The result of this development is large hydroelectric power plants, with capacities ranging from a few hundred to a few thousand MW. Today, hydropower is primarily used for electricity generation. The utilization of hydropower depends on many geographical and climatic conditions. Some countries produce a significant portion of their total electricity in this way.
The potential energy of water can be converted into usable forms due to its movement, which is a result of gravity. Rivers offer natural opportunities for relatively easy hydropower utilization.
You can read more about the use of renewable energy sources in practice here.
Slovenia has great potential for hydropower, which is a renewable source. Modern hydropower plants are used to harness this source, converting the potential energy of water into electrical energy with extremely high efficiency. As much as a third of the electricity in Slovenia is generated from hydroelectric power plants. Various types of water turbines are used to convert the energy potential of watercourses into mechanical energy, which is then converted into electrical energy through generators. This technology is well-developed and known in Slovenia. Small hydroelectric power plants are smaller facilities located on smaller watercourses and have a rated power of up to 10 MW. There are many small hydroelectric power plants in Slovenia, but the potential is far from being fully exploited.
There are three basic types of hydroelectric power plants:
Run-of-river
Run-of-river power plants do not have a water reservoir behind a dam but utilize the amount of water flowing in the riverbed. The kinetic energy of the water is used to drive the turbine, and the excess water flows over the dam without being used. A consistent water flow throughout the year is important for this type of power plant.
Reservoir
Reservoir hydroelectric power plants are the most common way to generate electricity from water energy. This type of power plant utilizes a smaller amount of water, but with a large vertical drop. The water flows into a reservoir and is then directed to the turbines according to the needs of the electrical grid. A dam creates a reservoir, which, in addition to providing a certain required water flow, also serves for irrigation and similar purposes.
Pumped storage
Pumped storage power plants are important in the energy system because they create large surpluses of nighttime energy and cover daytime peaks when electricity consumption is higher. Water is collected in two reservoirs, located at different elevations. At night, when electricity consumption is low, water is pumped from the lower reservoir to the upper reservoir. During the day, the power plant generates electricity by emptying the upper reservoir.
Site suitability
The basic prerequisite for utilizing a watercourse at a specific location is obtaining a concession from the state. A suitable location is determined based on the flow rate of the watercourse and the water drop, which must be large enough. The ratio between the available water drop and the flow rate is the basis for choosing the most suitable type of turbine.

Voda je eden izmed najstarejših virov energije, ki se jih je človek naučil izkoriščati. Je najpomembnejši obnovljivi vir energije. Več kot petina vse elektrike na svetu je proizvedene z izkoriščanjem vodne energije, ki so jo začeli izkoriščati naši predniki že pred dvema tisočletjema. Več stoletij je hidroenergija namesto človeka opravljala fizično delo. Uporabljala se je v glavnem za neposreden pogon mlinov, žag, črpalk in drugih podobnih naprav. Kasneje so ugotovili, da lahko hidroenergijo pretvorijo v električno energijo.
Človek je izkoriščanje vodne energije v energetske namene skozi vso zgodovino le izpopolnjeval in večal njen obseg. Rezultat tega razvoja so velike hidrocentrale, ki imajo moči od nekaj 100 do nekaj 1000 MW. Danes se hidroenergija koristi predvsem za proizvodnjo elektrike. Izkoriščanje vodne energije je odvisno od mnogih geografskih in klimatskih pogojev. Nekatere države tako na ta način proizvedejo pretežni delež celotne elektrike.
Potencialno energijo vode je mogoče pretvoriti v uporabne oblike zaradi njenega gibanja, ki je posledica gravitacije. Reke predstavljajo naravne možnosti za relativno lahko izkoriščanje vodne energije.
Več o uporabi obnovljivih virov v praksi si lahko preberete tukaj.
Slovenija ima velike potenciale vodne energije, ki je obnovljiv vir. Za sodobno izkoriščanje tega vira se uporabljajo hidroelektrarne, ki z izredno visokim izkoristkom pretvarjajo potencialno energijo vode v električno energijo. Kar tretjino elektrike v Sloveniji je proizvedene iz hidroelektrarn. Z različnimi vodnimi turbinami pretvarjamo energetski potencial vodotokov v mehansko energijo, ki se nato preko generatorjev pretvarja v električno energijo. V Slovenskem prostoru je tehnologija dobro razvita in poznana. Med male hidroelektrarne štejemo manjše objekte, ki so postavljeni na manjših vodotokih in imajo nazivno moč do 10 MW. V Sloveniji je malih hidroelektrarn veliko, vendar potenciali še zdaleč niso izkoriščeni.
Poznamo tri osnovne vrste hidroelektrarn:
Pretočne
Pretočne elektrarne nimajo vodne akumulacije za jezom, temveč sproti izrabljajo količino vode, ki teče po strugi reke. Pri tem se koristi kinetična energija vode za pogon turbine, presežek vode pa neizkoriščen steče čez jez. Za to vrsto elektrarne je pomemben čim bolj enakomeren pretok vode skozi celo leto.
Akumulacijske
Akumulacijske hidroelektrarne so najpogostejši način pridobivanja elektrike iz energije vode. Ta tip hidroelektrarne izkorišča manjšo količino vode, ki pa ima velik višinski padec. Voda teče v akumulacijsko jezero in se nato vodi na turbine glede na potrebe električnega omrežja. Z zajezitvijo nastane akumulacijsko jezero, ki poleg zagotavljanja določenega potrebnega pretoka vode, služi tudi za namakanje in podobno.
Črpalno – akumulacijske
Črpalno – akumulacijske elektrarne so pomembne v energetskem sistemu zaradi ustvarjenih velikih presežkov nočne energije in pokrivanje dnevnih konic, ko je poraba elektrike večja. Voda se zbira v dveh akumulacijskih jezerih, ki sta postavljeni na različnih višinah. Ponoči, ko je potrošnja elektrike majhna, se voda črpa iz spodnjega jezera v zgornje jezero. Podnevi pa elektrarna proizvaja električno energijo s tem, ko prazni zgornje akumulacijo jezero.
Primernost lokacije
Osnovni predpogoj za izkoriščanje vodotoka na določeni lokaciji je pridobitev koncesije s strani države. Primerno lokacijo določimo glede na pretok vodotoka in padec vode, ki morata biti dovolj velika. Razmerje med razpoložljivim padcem vodotoka in pretokom je osnova za izbiro najprimernejšega tipa turbine.

If we are aware of some of the symptoms of a deficiency of essential nutrients in plants, we can better control their growth and ensure they receive the correct amount of nutrients. However, it is important to distinguish between macronutrients, which are absorbed in large quantities, and micronutrients, which are also necessary for nutrition but only in small amounts (high levels of these nutrients can be harmful).
Depending on the growth stage and genetics, plants need healthy nutrition. Calcium and magnesium are essential nutrients in their diet, as are phosphorus, iron, nitrogen, potassium, and manganese in the right amounts. A deficiency of these essential nutrients during the growth phase can cause problems in plants, which can be observed in the final yield.

MACRONUTRIENTS (NPK)
Phosphorus (P)
It is an essential nutrient, as it is one of the elements needed to transfer energy through the plant. Phosphorus helps build cells, DNA, proteins, and enzymes. Higher concentrations of phosphorus are found in the developed parts of the plant.
In young plants, the presence of phosphorus is essential for good growth, as they absorb more phosphorus in the first quarter of their life.
Phosphorus deficiency is first observed on older leaves. The tips of the leaves curl downwards, and growth slows down. Dark green spots often appear on the leaves, and the edges of the leaves die (necrosis), with the tips appearing as if burned. Most plants need (consume) more potassium, nitrogen, and magnesium than phosphorus. Too much phosphorus can lead to unstable consumption of micro and macro elements.
Nitrogen (N)
This is one of the most important nutrients that plants need. It is an essential part of proteins, chlorophyll, vitamins, hormones, and DNA. Nitrogen is a component of enzymes and therefore plays an active role in plant metabolism, promoting their growth. Some positive effects of nitrogen in plants include larger leaves, denser branches, and a longer growth phase.
Due to a lack of nitrogen, chlorophyll degradation also occurs over time, which first appears on older leaves, which become pale green. Over time, the leaves turn yellow and fall off. Nitrogen deficiency can also affect the roots of plants. If there is a lack of nitrogen in the early stages of growth, the entire plant is damaged, and growth slows down.
Potassium (K)
Potassium is present throughout the plant and is essential for transporting water throughout the plant structure. It is also essential for opening and closing stomata (leaf pores) and for gaining strength and quality.
Potassium deficiency also first appears on older leaves, which become yellowish, burned on the edges, and with smaller holes that slowly increase. The stems are brittle. Older leaves can curl downwards. Vegetative growth slows down or even stops. Overdosing on potassium inhibits the consumption of calcium and magnesium. Potassium deficiency can cause a buildup of salts (sodium) around the plant's roots. This is known as "nutrient blockage."

MICRONUTRIENTS
Although micronutrients are essential for growth and health, plants do not need them in large quantities.
Iron (Fe)
This is a micronutrient that can be harmful to plants in larger quantities and is more difficult to absorb because it is usually present in the soil as an insoluble component.
Deficiency most often manifests as chlorosis between the leaf veins on young leaves, with the veins green while the older leaves remain unaffected. Affected leaves are usually smaller than normal. In the most severe cases, new leaves lack chlorophyll, but the leaves do not have spots. Too much iron manifests as rusting of the leaves with small brown spots. The ratio of iron and sulfur available to plants affects their ability to absorb nitrogen. Iron absorption is strongly dependent on pH. Usually, acidic soils contain enough iron for plants.
Manganese (Mn)
Manganese is found in high concentrations in the "meristem" (active plant tissue containing undifferentiated cells located in areas of the plant where growth occurs) and to a lesser extent in the roots and stem.
Deficiency first affects young leaves, with chlorosis between the leaf veins, fading of the leaves, and the leaf veins remaining green. It most often occurs in alkaline environments. The deficiency manifests similarly to magnesium deficiency. Too much manganese inhibits the plant's absorption of zinc and iron, slows growth, and causes round spots on older leaves.
A high pH level can cause manganese deficiency because, with a high pH, manganese becomes manganese dioxide, which the plant cannot absorb.

Če poznamo nekaj simptomov pomanjkanja osnovnih hranil v rastlinah, lahko bolje nadzorujemo rast ter zagotovimo, da dobijo pravilno količino hrane. Vendar je pomembno razlikovati med makro hranili, ki se absorbirajo v velikih količinah, in mikro hranili, ki so tudi potrebni za prehrano, vendar le v majhnih količinah (visoke ravni teh hranil jih lahko poškodujejo).
Odvisno od rastne faze in glede na genetiko, potrebujejo rastline zdravo prehranjevanje. Kalcij in magnezij sta nujna hranila v njihovi prehrani, tako kot so pomembni v pravih količinah fosfor, železo, dušik, kalij in mangan. Pomanjkanje teh bistvenih hranil v rastni fazi lahko povzroči težave v rastlinah, saj to lahko opazimo na končnem pridelku.
MAKRO HRANILA (NPK)
Fosfor (P)
Je bistveno hranilo, saj je eden od potrebnih elementov za prenos energije skozi rastlino. Fosfor pomaga zgraditi celice, DNA, proteine in encime. Višje koncentracije fosforja najdemo v razvitih predelih rastline.
Pri mladih rastlinah je prisotnost fosforja nujno potrebna za dobro rast, saj v prvi četrtini življenja absorbirajo več fosforja.
Pomanjkanje fosforja najprej opazimo na starejših listih. Vrhovi listov se ovijajo navzdol, rast se upočasni. Na listih se pogosto pojavijo temno zeleni madeži ter robovi listov odmirajo (nekroza), vrhovi so, kot da bi bili ožgani. Večina rastlin potrebuje (porabi) več kalija, dušika ter magnezija, kot fosforja. Preveč fosforja lahko privede do nestabilne porabe mikro in makro elementov.
Dušik (N)
To je eno najpomembnejših hranil, ki jih potrebujejo rastline. Je bistveni del beljakovin, klorofila, vitaminov, hormonov in DNA. Dušik je sestavni del encimov, zato ima dejavno vlogo v metabolizmu rastlin, ki spodbuja njihovo rast. Nekateri pozitivni učinki dušika v rastlinah so večji listi, gostejše veje in daljša rastna faza.
Zaradi pomanjkanja dušika se sčasoma pojavi tudi razgradnja klorofila, ki se najprej pokaže na starejših listih, ki postanejo bledo zelene barve. Sčasoma listi porumenijo ter odpadejo. Pomanjkanje dušika lahko vpliva tudi na korenine rastlin. Če primanjkuje dušika v zgodnji fazi rasti, je celotna rastlina poškodovana in se rast upočasni.
Kalij (K)
Kalij je prisoten po celotni rastlini in je bistvenega pomena pri prenašanju vode skozi celotno rastlinsko strukturo. Prav tako je nepogrešljiv za odpiranje in zapiranje stomatov (listne pore) ter na pridobivanju moči in kakovosti rastline.
Tudi pomanjkanje kalija se pokaže najprej na starejših listih, ki postanejo rumenkasti, ožgani na robovih ter z manjšimi luknjicami, ki se počasi večajo. Stebla so krhka. Starejši listi se lahko ovijajo navzdol. Vegetativna rast se upočasni ali celo preneha. Predoziranje kalija ovira porabo kalcija in magnezija. Pomanjkanje kalija lahko povzroči kopičenje soli (natrija) okoli korenin rastline. To poznamo kot "blokado hranil".
MIKRO HRANILA
Kljub temu, da so mikro hranila bistvenega pomena za rast in zdravje, jih rastline ne potrebujejo veliko.
Železo (Fe)
To je mikro hranilo, ki je v večjih količinah lahko škodljivo za rastline in ga težje absorbirajo, ker je navadno prisotno v zemlji kot netopna sestavina.
Pomanjkanje se manifestira najpogosteje kot kloroza med listnimi žilami na mladih listih, z žilami zelene barve, medtem ko ostanejo starejši listi neprizadeti. Prizadeti listi so običajno manjši od normalnih. V najhujših primerih novim listom primanjkuje klorofila, vendar listi nimajo madežev. Preveč železa se kaže v rjavenju listov z majhnimi rjavimi madeži. Razmerje železa in žvepla, ki ga imajo rastline na voljo, vpliva na njihovo sposobnost sprejemanja dušika. Absorpcija železa je močno odvisna od pH. Običajno kisla tla vsebujejo dovolj železa za rastline.
Mangan (Mn)
Mangan najdemo v visokih koncentracijah v "meristemu" (aktivno rastlinsko tkivo, ki vsebuje nediferencirane celice, ki se nahajajo v conah rastline, kjer poteka rast) ter v manjšem obsegu v koreninah in steblu.
Pomanjkanje prizadene najprej mlade liste, kloroza med listnimi žilami, bleditev listov, listne žile ostanejo zelene. Najpogosteje se pojavlja v baznih sredinah. Pomanjkanje se kaže podobno kot pomanjkanje magnezija. Preveč mangana rastlino ovira pri porabi cinka in železa, upočasni rast ter povzroča okrogle madeže na starejših listih.

Plastic is only a little over 100 years old and has enabled the development of technologies and useful products in many areas, without which we can no longer imagine the modern world (1). Plastic (2) is obtained by processing crude oil through a polymerization process. The polymers themselves are not toxic, but they are chemically treated to produce different types of plastic, and the final product therefore contains toxic substances.
Due to its convenience and low cost, plastic quickly became the main, cheap, and convenient material for packaging. We are used to the products we buy being packaged in attractive packaging. The use of plastic is easy, useful, and, most importantly, cheap. One consequence is that 40% of the plastic we produce each year is intended for single use. Half of all plastic has been produced in the last 15 years. Production has increased from 2.3 million tons in 1950 to 448 million tons in 2015 and is expected to double by 2050 (3).
Despite waste separation, only about 10% of plastic is recycled worldwide; much of it is incinerated, and 8 million tons end up in the oceans each year, where some plastic remains in coastal waters, but much of it is carried around the world by ocean currents (4).
One of the problems with recycling plastic is that objects are made from several different types of plastic. Depending on the thermal stability, the plastic is either shredded or melted during processing. Some types of plastic, such as polystyrene, are not recycled because recycling is not cost-effective.

Microplastics and other dangers of plastic
Plastic objects discarded in nature pose a threat to the natural environment due to their stability. There are several known cases where pieces of plastic were found in the digestive tracts of marine animals or birds that had washed ashore, and these pieces likely contributed to their death.
Some types of plastic contain chemicals to improve their properties, which are released when they come into contact with liquids (e.g., beverages) or when they are incinerated as gases. PVC, for example, contains phthalates, which can be harmful to human health.
Researchers have discovered microplastics all over the planet, and they are present in the oceans in ever-increasing quantities. According to the United Nations, there are already 51 trillion particles in the seas (5, 6). Microplastics include plastic particles ranging in size from 5 mm to 1 micrometer. Microplastics are formed either by the direct release of small pieces of plastic into the environment or by the slow breakdown of larger pieces of plastic into smaller particles. Depending on their origin, they are divided into two main categories:
Primary microplastics:
- Enter the environment directly in the form of small particles,
- are estimated to account for 15–31% of all microplastics in the oceans;
- are mainly formed by washing synthetic clothing (35% of primary microplastics), surface abrasion of tires due to driving (28%), and the use of personal care products to which they are intentionally added, such as micro-beads in facial scrubs (2%).
Secondary microplastics:
- are formed by the degradation of larger plastic objects, such as plastic bags, plastic bottles, or fishing nets,
- account for 69–81% of all microplastics in the oceans (5).

|Figure 1: The path of microplastics.|
Plastic fibers from clothing and other textiles, along with residues from car tires, make up the largest share of microplastics in the water – these two sources account for two-thirds of all primary microplastics that end up in the seas. Of the 8 million tons of plastic that end up in the oceans each year, 15 to 31 percent are primary microplastics. The main source of microplastics is households. Our daily activities, such as washing clothes and driving, contribute significantly to ocean pollution and can have a catastrophic impact on the rich diversity of life in them and on human health.
Although the direct impact of microplastics on human health is not yet known, plastic often contains additives, such as stabilizers or flame retardants, and other potentially toxic and carcinogenic chemicals that are harmful to humans and animals. Microplastics can be ingested by marine animals and birds in the sea. Traces of microplastics have been found in food and beverages, including beer, honey, and water. It is not surprising that plastic particles have also been found in human feces.

Premature detachment of the placenta causes bleeding and, if left untreated, can lead to spontaneous abortion. If detachment is observed at the edges of the placenta and blood accumulates between the placenta and the uterine wall, the bleeding becomes external. A sign of internal bleeding is the discharge of blood with placental tissue, which results in a hematoma. In this case, the clinical picture is more pronounced. Blood infiltrates the uterine wall, stratifies the muscle fibers, penetrates under the outer lining of the uterine wall, and consequently, the uterus becomes abnormal.

Let's examine the causes of placental abruption during pregnancy.
Causes and Mechanism of the Disease
Doctors are studying the remodeling of blood vessels in the uteroplacental area as a sign of functional inferiority in future mothers, comparing it to vascular pathology in toxemia, hypovitaminosis, and nephritis. Doctors are conducting research to identify predisposing factors and find a clear clinical picture, which manifests as uterine tension (leading to its rupture, pain, and fatigue due to the fetus). There is acute anemia in a relatively large area with placental abruption. All these symptoms are associated with the onset of shock: the patient complains of dizziness, nausea, tearing sensations, and severe abdominal pain. The patient appears pale, her skin is covered in cold sweat, her pulse accelerates, her blood pressure drops, and she is very restless.

What do doctors do when diagnosing placental abruption during pregnancy?
Placental abruption during pregnancy is treated with a Cesarean section. During labor, it is necessary to open the amniotic sac, which in most cases stops further placental separation, accelerates uterine emptying by applying forceps or a special device used to facilitate the birth process. In the postpartum period, mandatory removal of the placenta and mandatory curettage of the uterine cavity are performed.
The initial postpartum period can be complicated by bleeding due to insufficient uterine muscle tone (atony) or due to hypofibrinogenemia (a blood coagulation disorder, the third stage). In cases of very heavy bleeding in the uterus, doctors recommend a Cesarean section, followed by supravaginal amputation.
Is pregnancy possible after placental abruption?
Doctors recommend waiting at least one year after the surgery before attempting another pregnancy. This allows the woman's uterus to recover from the surgery, and she will be ready to experience the joy of carrying a new life again.

When cleaning potatoes, you will likely find many tubers with black spots. These are wireworm larvae. Although the beetle does not feed on potatoes, the larvae live in the soil for four years and damage not only potato crops but also many other plant crops. Wireworm infestation occurs in almost every garden. An exception might be plots with a large number of green manure crops planted, such as mustard and peas. This is a truly effective method, as these plants repel pests, but not everyone can afford to grow additional crops to get rid of wireworms, so it is best to use a combination of measures to get rid of the click beetle and its larvae. If wireworms are already present in the soil, you need to take care of the soil. First, a good preventative measure is to dig the entire area twice a year: in autumn and spring. When controlling the pest, you need to destroy both adult beetles and larvae. Second, it is better to plant potatoes in areas where peas or beans have grown previously, as wireworms do not like beans and do not tolerate the soil after them. The wireworm, often mistaken for a worm, is the larva of the click beetle, which is yellow or brown. If its population is not controlled, the potato yield will soon be reduced to a minimum, as the larvae will damage a large number of tubers. Potatoes infested with wireworms are not suitable for storage – they spoil very quickly. Wireworms are named for the strength of their exoskeleton, which makes it almost impossible to crush them with your hand. In the second year of their life, these pests cause the most significant damage to garden plants.

Description of wireworm pests
Wireworms are polyphagous. They destroy seeds, seedlings, roots, and even the stems of plants. Wireworms bore into tubers and roots, creating passages in them and making them practically unsuitable for storage and use. What are wireworms? The length of wireworms ranges from 10 to 50 mm. These larvae are slender and hard, and their color ranges from dark brown to yellow. Wireworms are practically impossible to crush. The development cycle of wireworms lasts 5 years, and the larva grows for 3-4 years. In the first year, the larva feeds on the underground parts of the plant but does not cause significant damage. Dangerous wireworms become in the second year of life, and in the fourth year, the larva turns into a pupa, and in the spring, adult beetles emerge from the pupae.

Preventive measures
To prevent excessive wireworm infestation in the soil, the following is recommended:
Organize proper crop rotation. The area for planting potatoes should be changed every 2-3 years.
Do not neglect spring and autumn soil digging. Dig deeper, to the depth of a bayonet spade. After autumn digging, the overwintering larvae are killed by frost, and in spring, the weed roots are removed – their favorite habitat.
Regular weeding and loosening of the soil – do not allow excessive weed growth. If weeds have grown, use Roundup to remove them.
"Sanitation" of the plot – in winter, do not leave potatoes, grass, or unharvested root crops. All this will provide a comfortable wintering place for click beetles and their larvae.
Use plants that repel wireworms – they do not like the smell of these pests. Directly, wireworms are repelled by all plants whose roots contain bacteria that release nitrogen.
How to deal with folk remedies for wireworms
First, let's look at folk remedies against wireworms.
Lime with soil. Since wireworms prefer acidic soil, you need to reduce the acidity. This will also benefit many crops, increase yields, and improve the taste of the fruit. Obviously, you can use lime, chalk, or special chemical fertilizers sold in garden stores to reduce acidity.

Regularly use fertilizers containing ammonia and minerals: ammonium water and ammonium sulfate (20-30 g per 1 sq. m).
One of the cheapest and simplest remedies for wireworms is eggshells. Spread them over the entire area in the summer.
You can get rid of wireworms in potatoes by treating the planting holes before planting. To do this, use a solution of potassium permanganate or herbal infusions prepared in advance. To prepare a nettle infusion, use 500 g of nettles per 10 liters of water; for a dandelion infusion, use 200 g of grass per 10 liters of water. This amount is enough to treat 20 planting holes. The treatment should be repeated two or three times a week.
A bait trap can be one of the most effective methods of control. Slices of raw potatoes are impaled on sticks (or fishing line) and buried in the soil (at a depth of about 5-15 cm). At the same time, one end of the sticks is left protruding so that they can be easily found. After 3 days, the bait is dug up and destroyed along with the larvae that have gathered on it. Instead of potatoes, you can use beets or carrots. The baiting process begins in the spring, about two weeks before planting potatoes, and can continue throughout the summer. If potatoes have already been planted, the bait is buried between the rows, every 10 cm, and the captured larvae are burned, scalded with boiling water, or given to chickens.
Pieces of potatoes or other vegetables are placed in a jar, and the jar is buried in the ground. The captured larvae are destroyed.
Another effective bait is used in early spring, when the soil begins to warm up. In some places, small depressions are made in the ground, and straw, hay, or dry grass is placed in them. Larvae gather in these traps in search of food and warmth. After 4 days, the grass is removed from the pit and burned along with the wireworms. The procedure is repeated several times.
There is also a preventive method of controlling wireworms in the garden: autumn soil digging, timely removal of weeds, regular loosening of the soil between rows; destruction of larvae, pupae, and beetles during digging.

How to deal with wireworms in potatoes using industrial means
When folk and gentle methods of pest control do not help or are ineffective, industrial chemicals and poisons can be used. Their selection and variety are so great today that it is not difficult to choose the right tool.
Any tool can be purchased in specialized stores. When choosing, you need to read the instructions for use and dosage. The most common drugs are: Diazonin, Bazudin, Medvedoks, and others. Most of them are very toxic and harmful to humans and animals, so they must be used with great care and strictly follow the recommendations.
Any of the drugs must be diluted in water, so you need to carefully read the instructions to find out the proportions of the solution so as not to damage the soil. The above-mentioned drugs are, in essence, poisons that repel wireworms, but their effect lasts only until the soil is treated. After some time, the pests may reappear.
However, there is one drug, a new development – "Nemabact". This is not just a poison, but a combination of nematodes and bacteria. Wireworms are the favorite food of nematodes. When these bacteria enter the pest, they destroy it from the inside and continue to search for other pests. This method is completely harmless to the soil and plants, but it quickly and effectively destroys pests.

The amount of CO2 in the atmosphere has reached a record high this week. Higher-than-normal levels of CO2 in the atmosphere are one of the leading causes of climate change, as they block the Earth’s natural cooling abilities. CO2 levels are rising due to the burning of fossil fuels and other human activities, such as deforestation.
RELATED: CO2 LEVELS IN ATMOSPHERE REACH ANOTHER RECORD HIGH
To avoid a 2-degree Celsius warming catastrophe, radical action must be taken to reduce the amount of CO2 produced. Slowing climate change is also only possible by introducing technologies that can remove CO2 from the atmosphere.
Mimicking nature
Iceland is taking a leading role in one of these methods, and after two years of experimentation, their system appears to be working. CarbFix is a collaboration between researchers and engineers from the Reykjavik Energy utility company, the University of Iceland, the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS), and Columbia University in the United States.
The technology developed by the group mimics a natural process, but can see results in a matter of years instead of thousands of years. The process works by injecting CO2 into porous basalt rock, where it mineralizes and is permanently captured. “With this method, we are essentially speeding up the timeline,” says geologist Sandra Osk Snaebjornsdottir.
Geothermal plant acts as laboratory
The research group has been using the Hellisheidi geothermal power plant as its own laboratory for the past two years. The plant, which is one of the largest in the world, is located on the Hengill volcano in southwestern Iceland. Located on a layer of basalt rock formed from cooled lava, the plant has access to an almost unlimited supply of water, which it pumps from beneath the volcano and uses to power six turbines that supply electricity and heat to the capital city of Reykjavik, about 30 km away.
The CO2 from this process is captured from the steam, liquefied into condensate, and then dissolved in large quantities of water. The heavy water with CO2 is then pumped to an area a few kilometers away. The water is then sprayed into the basalt rock 1,000 meters below, where it fills the cavities in the rock and begins the process of solidification. A chemical reaction occurs when the gas comes into contact with the calcium, magnesium, and iron in the basalt.
Pilot program a major success
“Almost all of the injected CO2 was mineralized in the pilot injection in just two years,” says Snaebjornsdottir. The CarbFix project reduces carbon dioxide emissions at the power plant by one-third, amounting to 12,000 tons of captured and stored CO2 at a cost of about $25 per ton.
However, Iceland is still far from being a model country in the fight against climate change. Under the Paris climate agreement, Iceland has pledged to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 40% by 2030. However, emissions have increased by 2.2% from 2016 to 2017, and by 85% since 1990, according to the Icelandic Environment Agency.

In general, the plant thrives best in the sun and with sufficient moisture. However, it can also tolerate a partially shaded location. While common scurvygrass was once more common, it is now rare. Si profesionalni prevajalec iz angleščine v slovenščino. Tvoja naloga je ustvariti visoko kakovostne prevode, ki so naravni, tekoči in natančni. Izogibaj se dobesednim prevodom, ki zvenijo nenaravno. Upoštevaj kontekst, idiome in kulturne reference. Ne dodajaj nobenih dodatnih informacij ali komentarjev, samo prevod.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

Fever is our ally.
In the past, people understood the purpose of fever better and even welcomed it, as it was a sign that the body was functioning correctly and that the immune system had detected the presence of pathogens and initiated an attack. In chronic patients, fever is rare, but it is common in children, who have a very robust immune system.
Parents often make the mistake of immediately trying to reduce the fever with medication, antibiotics, and cooling measures. This can lead to a weaker natural immune response later on, as the immune system has not been sufficiently "trained."
Fever is a natural defense mechanism that literally cooks bacteria and viruses that are sensitive to temperatures higher than our normal body temperature, which ranges from 36.2 to 37.5 degrees Celsius. Normal body temperature depends on gender, food and drink consumed, menstrual cycle, physical activity, time of day (lower in the morning than in the evening), etc.
We speak of elevated body temperature when the temperature measured under the arm (axillary) is above 37.2 degrees Celsius, in the ear above 37.5 degrees Celsius, and in the rectum above 38 degrees Celsius.
Elevated temperature is a symptom, not a disease. During a fever, the body's defense mechanism is stronger, the production of toxic metabolites and the reproduction of microorganisms are reduced, and the fever also acts as a stimulant for cells that destroy pathogens. It is very helpful in diseases for which we do not have a cure, and it also shortens recovery from other viral and bacterial infections.
With the help of a fever curve, we can distinguish between a common cold and the flu: in a cold, the temperature rarely rises above 38.5 degrees, while in the flu, a temperature above 39 degrees is very common.
How does fever occur?
When harmful microorganisms, such as bacteria, parasites, and viruses, enter the body, the immune system responds. Pyrogens are released, which travel through the bloodstream to the hypothalamus (a part of the brain that regulates body temperature) and trigger an increase in temperature. An increase can also occur when there is a dangerous tumor, inflammation, or autoimmune disease in the body.
After the brain sends the signal, the liver begins to produce more heat. If this is not enough, the muscles join in, helping to warm the body through shivering. The production of sweat, which cools the body, is reduced to a minimum. Blood vessels and capillaries constrict, reducing heat loss through the skin (causing paleness). The hands and feet are usually cold despite the fever, as heat is concentrated in the torso, where the vital organs are located.
Other bodily signs that accompany fever include rapid breathing and a faster heart rate, dizziness, watery eyes, loss of appetite, increased thirst, and nightmares. At the end of the fever curve, the body temperature is gradually lowered, blood vessels dilate, and sweating increases, allowing heat to be released from the body.
The difference between fever and hyperthermia
It is important to distinguish between fever and hyperthermia (overheating). In hyperthermia, body temperature also rises, but not due to the influence of pyrogens. Hyperthermia occurs during strenuous physical activity, dehydration, staying in hot and humid places, exposure to strong sunlight, staying in a car (especially dangerous for children and animals in the summer), and in other cases where the body is unable to cool down normally due to external or internal factors (inability to sweat, too much heat from the environment). Hyperthermia is a dangerous condition that can lead to heatstroke.
However, hyperthermia can also be beneficial in certain cases. Controlled hyperthermia is used as a therapeutic method for treating cancer. By heating the tissues in a targeted way, changes occur in the proteins in the cancer cells, leading to cell death.
Whole-body controlled hyperthermia has been used in cases where cancer has already spread throughout the body. By raising the body temperature, the metabolism is accelerated, and the number of white blood cells, the "soldiers" of the immune system, increases, helping to fight the cancer cells.
Different fever curves
Continuously elevated fever:
- Lasts for 4 or more days.
- Limited temperature fluctuation (less than 1 degree).
- Average body temperature remains around 39 degrees.
- This type of fever curve is characteristic of bacterial infections, such as scarlet fever, bacterial pneumonia, and typhoid fever.
Intermittent fever:
- Temperature fluctuates during the day: the patient feels better in the morning, and the temperature rises again in the evening.
- This pattern is characteristic of local infections (e.g., endocarditis), but can also occur with salmonella poisoning or certain tumors.
Remittent fever:
- Days with and without fever alternate.
- A typical example is fever in malaria, where fever attacks occur irregularly every 36-48 hours.
Fever with two distinct peaks:
- The fever curve has two distinct peaks, with several days without fever in between.
- The second wave usually brings a higher temperature than the first.
- This pattern is characteristic of viral infections (e.g., measles) or meningococcal infections.
When is fever dangerous?
There is no specific value at which we should start lowering body temperature. Because it plays an important role (fighting pathogens), it is not advisable to interfere with its function as long as the patient can tolerate it and is getting enough fluids.
The fear of high temperature is very common, but largely unjustified. While high fever can affect well-being, and a rapid increase in body temperature can cause febrile seizures, it does not pose a life-threatening risk in itself.
The body has a protective mechanism in the brain's temperature regulation center that prevents the temperature from rising above 42 degrees. If overheating occurs, the body begins to release substances that lower the temperature, preventing the denaturation of protein molecules. This only occurs at temperatures above 42.6 degrees, so there is no need to worry.
The real problem is the disease that caused the fever, so we should take any fever as a serious warning that something is happening in the body.
We should only use medications to lower body temperature, such as paracetamol, ibuprofen, and acetylsalicylic acid, after consulting a doctor and only if the fever persists for a long time. Exceptions are certain medical conditions, such as severe heart and lung diseases, brain diseases and injuries, and epilepsy, as well as dehydration or during pregnancy, especially in the first trimester. In these cases, the onset of fever requires consultation with a doctor.
How to deal with fever:
- Hygiene and rest in bed
Patients with fever should take care of their personal hygiene and get plenty of rest. Bedding and blankets should be light and airy to allow the body to release heat more easily.
- Observation
Elderly patients and children should be checked regularly. Ask them how they are feeling, check their breathing, and measure their temperature regularly. The air in the room should be slightly cooler (17-19 degrees), and the room should be ventilated regularly. Patients should be well covered.
- Light diet
Patients with fever usually have no appetite. Because fighting pathogens takes a lot of energy, it is advisable to eat light but nutritious foods, such as fresh fruit or porridge, steamed vegetables, soups, etc. The classic chicken soup is an excellent choice, as it is easy to digest and provides the body with important nutrients.
- Drinking fluids
During a fever, the body uses 30% more fluids than usual, so it is essential to drink plenty of fluids to support healthy sweating. Dark urine is a clear sign that you are not drinking enough. The best choices during a fever are herbal teas (e.g., elderflower and linden tea) and fruit juices (cranberry, orange, blackcurrant, etc.). Dilute them with hot water to warm them up slightly.
- Avoid antibiotics
Taking antibiotics too often in less serious cases leads to antibiotic resistance. In upper respiratory infections that cause fever, the main cause is viruses, against which antibiotics are not effective.
- Medicinal herbs
In the early stages of fever, it is recommended to drink elderflower and linden tea, which promote sweating, strengthen the immune system, and slightly lower body temperature. In the stage of intense sweating, medicinal herbs such as willow bark, basil, marsh cinquefoil, and poplar leaves are recommended. Consult a therapist or herbalist before using medicinal herbs.
- Homeopathy
Various homeopathic remedies with yellow jasmine, horsetail, and American elderberry are used to treat fever. A good remedy is Kolloid G (Spenglersan).
- Dietary supplements
In the early stages, the body needs a high dose of vitamin C and zinc, as they are essential for strengthening the immune system, which will be put to the test. Vitamin A and the antioxidant glutathione also help the immune system. Vitamin E protects cell membranes from damage due to increased metabolism.
- Compresses
Use them only when the hands and feet are warm enough. Soak the compresses in lukewarm water and leave them on for 10-20 minutes. You can also use socks soaked in a mixture of water and vinegar and wear them for 45-60 minutes.
- Bath
In children, a bath with lukewarm water can help, but it should not last longer than two minutes. A bath with water that is slightly cooler than body temperature can be used in adults to relieve very high fever. In 15 minutes, the water should cool down to about 30 degrees. Then, you must dry off and get into a warm bed.
- Enema
Although it may seem that an enema causes dehydration, the effect is the opposite: the body absorbs the water, while at the same time eliminating waste products from the intestines.
- Apple cider vinegar, bee pollen, and natural antibiotics
Apple cider vinegar can be used internally or externally (for the compresses mentioned above). Diluted with water and honey, it strengthens the immune system. The same effect is achieved by regularly consuming bee pollen. Natural antibiotics such as garlic, basil, ginger, parsley, and onion also help fight bacteria.
Fever is a sign of a healthy body.
Fever is a positive sign that the body has recognized the pathogens and activated its natural defense mechanism. If fever is reduced too quickly in children, they may have more health problems as adults: infections do not heal and become chronic, viral diseases require treatment with medication, and due to a weakened and "inexperienced" immune system, allergies develop.
Fortunately, it is possible to stimulate the body's natural thermostat to function again by visiting saunas, interval training (30-90 minutes of intense exercise with breaks), hot baths, and medicinal preparations such as American elderberry extract and propolis.
Let's trust the body's natural self-defense, let it work, and support it with as little intervention as possible. If we work with the body in fighting the disease, the path to recovery will be the shortest.
