Vročina je naša zaveznica
Nekoč so ljudje bolje poznali namen vročine in so jo celo pozdravljali, saj je bila znak, da telo deluje pravilno in da je imunski sistem zaznal vdor patogenov ter sprožil napad. Pri kroničnih bolnikih se vročina redko pojavlja, pri otrocih, ki imajo še zelo žilav imunski sistem, pa je pogosta.
Starši neredko storijo napako, ko nemudoma pričnejo z zniževanjem vročine z zdravili, antibiotiki in ohlajanjem pri otrocih. Ti imajo kasneje slabše razvito naravno odpornost, saj imunski sistem ni dovolj »treniral«.
Vročina je naravni obrambni mehanizem, s katerim telo dobesedno skuha bakterije in viruse, ki so občutljivi na temperature, višje od naše normalne telesne temperature. Ta se giblje med 36,2 in 37,5 stopinj Celzija. Normalna telesna temperatura je odvisna od spola, zaužite hrane in pijače, menstrualnega ciklusa, telesne aktivnosti, dela dneva (zjutraj je nižja kot zvečer), itd.
O zvišani telesni temperaturi govorimo, ko je temperatura, izmerjena pod pazduho (aksilarno) nad 37,2 stopinje Celzija, v ušesu nad 37,5 stopinje Celzija in v danki (rektalno) nad 38 stopinj Celzija.
Povišana temperatura je simptom in ne bolezen. Med vročino je obrambni mehanizem telesa močnejši, tvorjenje strupenih presnovkov in razmnoževanje mikroorganizmov se zmanjša, vročina deluje tudi kot spodbujevalec celic, ki uničujejo patogene. V veliko pomoč nam je pri obolenjih, za katere ne poznamo zdravila, prav tako skrajšuje okrevanje pri drugih virusnih in bakterijskih obolenjih.
S pomočjo vročinske krivulje lahko razlikujemo med navadnim prehladom in gripo: pri prehladu se temperatura le redko dvigne nad 38,5 stopinje, pri gripi pa je vročina nad 39 stopinj zelo pogosta.
Kako pride do pojava vročine?
Ob vdoru škodljivih mikroorganizmov, kot so bakterije, paraziti in virusi, se imunski sistem nanje odzove. Sproščati se začnejo pirogeni, ki preko krvi pristanejo v hipotalamusu (delu možganov, ki skrbi za termoregulacijo) in sprožijo ukaz za dvig temperature. Do dviga lahko pride tudi ko se v telesu nahaja nevarni tumor, vnetno dogajanje ali avtoimunsko obolenje.
Po ukazu možganov prične v jetrih nastajati več toplote. Če to ne zadostuje, se jetrom pridružijo še mišice, ki pomagajo telo segrevati z drgetanjem. Nastajanje potu, ki ohlaja telo, se zmanjša na minimalno raven. Krvne žile in kapilare se zožijo in s tem zmanjšajo izgubo toplote preko kože (pojav bledice). Roke in noge so kljub vročini navadno hladne, saj se toplota koncentrira v trupu, kjer so vitalni organi.
Drugi telesni znaki, ki spremljajo vročino, so pospešeno dihanje in hitrejši utrip srca, vrtoglavica, solzne oči, pomanjkanje apetita, povečana žeja in pojav nočnih mor. Na koncu vročinske krivulje se telesna temperatura kontrolirano spusti, žile se razširijo, poveča se potenje in s tem oddajanje toplote iz telesa.
Razlika med vročino in hipertermijo
Ob tem je potrebno razlikovati med vročino in hipertermijo (pregrevanje telesa). Pri slednji se prav tako pojavi dvig telesne temperature, vendar ne zaradi vpliva pirogenov. Hipertermija se pojavi ob velikih telesnih naporih, dehidraciji, bivanju v vročih in vlažnih krajih, izpostavljanju močnemu soncu, zadrževanju v avtomobilu (še posebej nevarno za otroke in živali v poletnem času) in nekaterih drugih primerih, ko se telo zaradi zunanjih ali notranjih dejavnikov ne uspe normalno ohlajati (nezmožnost potenja, preveč toplote iz okolja). Hipertermija je nevarno stanje, ki lahko povzroči toplotni udar oziroma vročinsko kap.
Vendar je lahko tudi hipertermija v določenih primerih koristna. Nadzorovana hipertermija se uporablja kot terapevtska metoda za zdravljenje rakavih obolenj. Z usmerjenim segrevanjem tkiv pride do sprememb beljakovin pri rakavih celic, kar vodi v celično smrt.
Nadzorovana hipertermija celotnega telesa se uporabljala pri primerih, kjer se je rak že razsejal po telesu. Zaradi dviga telesne temperature je presnova hitrejša, poveča se tudi število belih krvnih celic – »vojakov« imunskega sistema, ki se borijo proti rakavim zasevkom.
Različne vročinske krivulje
Kontinuirano povišana vročina:
- Vztraja 4 ali več dni;
- Omejeno nihanje temperature (manj kot 1 stopinja);
- Povprečna telesna temperatura vztraja pri okoli 39 stopinjah;
- Taka vročinska krivulja je značilna za bakterijska vnetja, kot so škrlatinka, bakterijsko vnetje pljuč in tifus.
Prekinjajoč pojav vročine:
- Temperatura tekom dneva niha: zjutraj se bolnik počuti bolje, zvečer temperatura ponovno naraste;
- Tak potek je značilen za lokalne infekcije (npr. endokarditis), lahko pa se pojavi tudi pri zastrupitvi s salmonelo ali pri določenih tumorjih.
Izmenjujoč pojav vročine:
- Izmenjujejo se dnevi brez in z vročino;
- Tipičen primer je vročina pri malariji, pri kateri se vročinski napadi neredno pojavljajo na 36-48 ur.
Pojav vročine z dvema izrazitima vrhoma:
- Vročinska krivulja ima dva izrazita vrha, med katerima mine več dni brez vročine;
- Drugi val prinaša navadno višjo temperaturo kot prvi;
- Tak pojav je značilen za virusne infekcije (npr. ošpice) ali meningokokne okužbe.
Kdaj je vročina nevarna?
Vrednost, pri kateri bi morali pričeti z zniževanjem telesne temperature, ni določena. Ker opravlja pomembno nalogo (boj s povzročitelji bolezni), ni smotrno posegati v njeno delovanje, vse dokler jo bolnik lahko tolerira in skrbi za zadosten vnos tekočine.
Strah pred visoko temperaturo je zelo razširjen, vendar v veliki meri neupravičen. Visoka vročina sicer vpliva na počutje, prav tako lahko hiter dvig telesne temperature povzroči vročinske krče, vendar sama po sebi ne ogroža življenja.
Telo ima varovalni mehanizem v možganskem centru za termoregulacijo, ki preprečuje dvig temperature nad 42 stopinj. Ob morebitnem pregrevanju se pričnejo izločati telesu lastne snovi za zniževanje temperature, ki onemogočajo denaturalizacijo beljakovinskih molekul. Ta nastopi šele pri temperaturah nad 42,6 stopinj, zato je bojazen odveč.
Resnično težavo predstavlja bolezen, ki je povzročila dvig temperature, zato moramo vsak pojav vročine jemati kot resno opozorilo, da se v telesu nekaj dogaja.
Po sredstvih za zniževanje telesne temperature, kot so paracetamol, ibuprofen in acetilsalicilna kislina, posežemo po navodilu zdravnika šele, ko vročina vztraja dlje časa. Izjema so določena bolezenska stanja, kot so hujša obolenja srca in pljuč, bolezni in poškodbe možganov in epilepsija ter pri dehidraciji ali v času nosečnosti, še posebej v prvem trimesečju. V teh primerih nastop vročine zahteva posvet z zdravnikom.
Kako ravnamo ob nastopu vročine?
- Higiena in počitek v postelji
Bolniki z vročino naj skrbijo za telesno higieno, privoščijo naj si veliko počitka. Posteljnina in odeje naj bodo lahke in zračne, da telo lažje oddaja toploto.
- Opazovanje
Starejše bolnike in otroke redno preverjamo. Povprašamo jih po počutju, kontroliramo dihanje in redno merimo temperaturo. Zrak v sobi naj ima nekoliko nižjo temperaturo (17 – 19 stopinj), redno ga zračimo, bolniki naj bodo dobro pokriti.
- Lahka prehrana
Bolniki z vročino navadno nimajo apetita. Ker boj s povzročitelji bolezni telesu vzame veliko energije, je priporočljivo, da se oseba kljub temu uživa lahka, a hranljiva živila, kot so sveže sadje ali kašice, dušena zelenjava, juhe … Dobra stara kokošja juha je odlična izbira, saj je lahko prebavljiva, hkrati pa oskrbi telo s pomembnimi hranili.
- Pitje vode
V času vročine telo porabi 30% vode več kot običajno, zato je za zdravo potenje nujno potrebno uživati več tekočine. Temno obarvan urin je jasen znak, da pijemo premalo. Najboljša izbira v času vročine so zeliščni čaji (npr. bezgov in lipov čaj) ter sadni sokovi (brusnica, pomaranča, črni ribez …). Redčimo jih z vročo vodo in s tem nekoliko segrejemo.
- Izogibamo se antibiotikom
Prepogosto jemanje antibiotikov v manj resnih primerih vodi v odpornost bakterij. Pri vnetjih zgornjih dihal, ki povzročajo vročino, so glavni povzročitelji virusi, proti katerim antibiotiki niso učinkoviti.
- Zdravilna zelišča
V prvi fazi pojava vročina se priporoča pitje bezgovega in lipovega čaja, ki pospešujeta potenje, krepita imunski sistem in rahlo znižujeta telesno temperaturo. V fazi intenzivnega potenja se priporočajo zdravilna zelišča, kot so vrba, bazilika, močvirski oslad ter listi topola. Pred uporabo zdravilnih zelišč se posvetujemo s terapevtom ali zdravilcem.
- Homeopatija
Pri vročini se s pridom uporabljajo različni homeopatski pripravki z rumenim jasminom, konjsko grivo in ameriškim slamnikom. Odličen je preparat Kolloid G (podjetje Spenglersan).
- Prehranska dopolnila
V začetni fazi telo potrebuje visok odmerek vitamina C in cinka, saj sta ključna za krepitev imunskega sistema, ki bo na preizkušnji. Tudi vitamin A in antioksidant glutation pomagata imunskemu sistemu. Vitamin E varuje celične membrane pred poškodbami zaradi pospešene presnove.
- Obkladki
Uporabljamo jih le, ko so roke in noge dovolj tople. Obkladke namočimo v mlačno vodo in pustimo učinkovati 10 – 20 minut. Uporabimo lahko tudi nogavice, namočene v mešanico vode in kisa, ki jih obujemo za 45 – 60 minut.
- Kopel
Pri otrocih pomaga kopel z mlačno vodo, ki naj ne traja dlje kot dve minuti. Kopel z vodo, ki je nekoliko hladnejša od telesne temperature, se lahko uporablja pri odraslih pri lajšanju zelo visoke temperature. V 15 minutah naj se voda shladi na okoli 30 stopinj. Nato moramo nujno osušiti in leči v ogreto posteljo.
- Klistriranje
Čeprav bi na prvi pogled rekli, da klistriranje povzroči dehidracijo, pa je učinek prav nasproten – telo vodo vsrka, hkrati pa se znebi odpadnih snovi iz črevesja.
- Jabolčni kis, cvetni prah in naravni antibiotiki
Jabolčni kis lahko uporabljamo notranje ali zunanje (za prej omenjene obkladke). Razredčen z vodo in medom krepi imunski sistem. Enak učinek ima tudi redno uživanje cvetnega prahu. V boju z bakterijami pomagajo tudi naravni antibiotiki – česen, bazilika, ingver, peteršilj, čebula …
Vročina je znak zdravega organizma
Vročina je torej pozitiven znak, da je telo prepoznalo povzročitelje bolezni in aktiviralo svoj naravni obrambni mehanizem. Če se pri otrocih vročino prehitro znižuje, imajo lahko kot odrasli večje zdravstvene težave: vnetja se ne zdravijo in postanejo kronična, virusna obolenja zahtevajo zdravljenje z zdravili, zaradi oslabljenega in »neizkušenega« imunskega sistema se pojavljajo alergije.
Na srečo je mogoče delovanje naravnega telesnega termostata možno ponovno spodbuditi k delovanju z obiskom savn, intervalnim treningom (30 – 90 intenzivna vadba z odmori), vročimi kopelmi ter zdravilnimi pripravki, kot sta izvleček ameriškega slamnika in propolis.
Zaupajmo v naravno samoobrambo telesa, pustimo ji učinkovati in jo s čim manjšim posredovanjem podprimo. Če pri boju z boleznijo sodelujemo s telesom, bo pot do ozdravitve najkrajša.

Si profesionalni prevajalec iz angleščine v slovenščino. Tvoja naloga je ustvariti visoko kakovostne prevode, ki so naravni, tekoči in natančni. Izogibaj se dobesednim prevodom, ki zvenijo nenaravno. Upoštevaj kontekst, idiome in kulturne reference. Ne dodajaj nobenih dodatnih informacij ali komentarjev, samo prevod.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

Gastrointestinal Infections
Cold and humid weather, such as we experience during winter, creates an opportunity for gastrointestinal infections to spread more quickly. This leads to the appearance of typical gastrointestinal illnesses in the form of vomiting, diarrhea, nausea, cramps, and elevated body temperature.
There are several possible causes, but viruses are usually the culprits (rotavirus infection is very common).
SYMPTOMS
The illness usually begins with vomiting and diarrhea. The stool is liquid, sometimes green, and may contain mucus; blood may also be present, as the virus attacks the intestinal cells and causes them to die. The illness is also accompanied by elevated body temperature, cramps, nausea, and general malaise. Anyone can get sick, but children are more likely to be affected. Diarrhea and vomiting are also more dangerous for infants and young children, as there is a greater risk of dehydration – loss of fluids.
HOW THE INFECTION IS TRANSMITTED
The infection is transmitted through contact – via the hands, which come into contact with either feces or objects and surfaces contaminated with feces. It can also be transmitted through the air – the virus can be inhaled from vomit. Feces are highly contagious, so hygiene is of paramount importance in preventing the spread of infection.
The incubation period (the period from infection to the appearance of the first symptoms) is approximately 24 to 48 hours, and the virus is shed for at least 6 days – during this time, the individual is contagious, so it is advisable to stay at home. After recovering from the infection, reinfection is possible, which means that there is no lasting immunity! The illness usually subsides in 5 to 7 days. When children are sick, they should stay at home. Children who have recovered from the infection should stay at home for at least 1 more day after the end of the illness, due to the possibility of transmission.
TREATMENT
First and foremost, it is important and necessary to replace the fluids and electrolytes that are lost through diarrhea and vomiting. Oral rehydration salts are available, which can be obtained from a pharmacy (also without a prescription) and dissolved in boiled and cooled water. The child should drink the liquid in small sips, not all at once, otherwise it may cause further vomiting. Blueberry tea is also recommended, as it helps to stop diarrhea. Fluid intake should be as high as possible and should be sufficient to meet daily needs and replace fluids lost through vomiting and diarrhea.
All these measures replace lost fluids, but they do not help to normalize the intestinal flora, which is disrupted in gastrointestinal illnesses. Therefore, it is advisable to take probiotics, which contain lactic acid bacteria (lactobacilli and bifidobacteria) and normalize the intestinal flora. Probiotic cultures are available in medicines and dietary supplements, which can be obtained from a pharmacy without a prescription (Linex capsules, Prolife, Probiolex, Biogaya drops) and help to restore the balance of the disrupted intestinal flora.
DIET
In the past, a special diet was recommended for diarrhea and vomiting, but today, advice on a strict diet has been replaced by advice on normal eating, while avoiding sweet, fatty, and heavily spiced foods. defining nationality
There are many ways to categorize people. We can be categorized by nationality, social status, ideology, or for many other reasons. One of these is the ethnic group to which we belong. The physical characteristics that define a particular population are the basic constitutive elements of an ethnic group.
In addition to physical characteristics (such as skin or hair color), there are other aspects related to the concept of nationality, such as language, customs, or religion. However, in a globalized world, there is no universal criterion for describing each ethnic group, as skin color is not always associated with language, religion, territory, or tradition.
The concept of nationality
Each race has created a sense of belonging, and this phenomenon is known as nationality. This feeling arises when the population of each ethnic group recognizes its differences from others. The idea of ethnicity is a form of identification and, therefore, relates to how an ethnic or ethno-rational group sees itself. Although the idea of nationality expresses the bonds that unite a community, we must not forget that racial differences have been a fundamental aspect of social conflict. Racism in various forms, the Jewish Holocaust, the persecution of Roma, or the persecution of Australian Aboriginals are some examples that illustrate the social tensions arising from the ethnic factor.
Nationality and race
Both terms are used as synonyms in everyday language. However, the term race refers to the physical characteristics of individuals, while the idea of ethnic affiliation relates to the cultural dimension of a community. Consequently, someone can be part of a race due to their physical characteristics but not necessarily the cultural tradition associated with that race.
Different ethnic groups on the planet
The classification of ethnic groups has evolved over time, but currently, the scientific community agrees that there are seven main races:
- The Black race is the origin of all the others, and the vast majority are on the African continent.
- The White or Caucasian race is the majority in Europe, the USA, Canada, and Australia.

Heat promotes dehydration
In hot weather, we sweat more, causing the body to lose vital fluids. This leads to faster dehydration, and if lost fluids are not regularly replaced with drinking water, mild or even severe dehydration can occur. The consequences for health and survival can be dangerous, even fatal.
Healthcare professionals warn that it is necessary to drink plain water constantly in hot weather, especially for young children and the elderly, as they have a reduced sense of thirst.
Dangers of dehydration
The body is 70 percent water, which regulates body temperature, protects joints and organs, and helps transport oxygen to cells. In a state of dehydration, kidney failure, stroke, and heart attack can occur. Heat accelerates sweating, which cools the body. During this process, we lose more water, which needs to be replaced.
Each adult should drink 2 to 3 liters of water per day in the summer, and a child should drink 1.5 liters of water per day.
Signs of dehydration appear when the body loses about two percent of its normal fluid volume. Dehydration is indicated by headache, dizziness, thirst, constipation, loss of appetite, decreased efficiency and endurance, decreased energy and concentration, prolonged reaction time to events in the environment, and possible elevated body temperature and nausea.
Color of urine
The color of urine indicates dehydration. Light yellow or colorless urine indicates adequate hydration. Dark yellow or brown urine with a strong odor indicates insufficient fluid intake.
We die without water
How long we can survive without water depends on the individual's condition and the environment. It has been calculated that a person can survive without water for about a week on average. In extreme conditions, an adult can lose a liter to a liter and a half of fluid through sweating. If this is not replaced, dehydration occurs and can lead to death. Adults should drink 35 milliliters of water per kilogram of body weight per day.
We also lose electrolytes, especially sodium, through sweating, which is why the skin is salty. These substances are not replaced by drinking water. Therefore, when sweating heavily, it is recommended to drink isotonic drinks with electrolytes. However, these drinks also contain harmful additives (sugar, artificial sweeteners, dyes, etc.). Therefore, it is better to consume natural substances rich in electrolytes. One such substance is coconut water, which is rich in potassium, calcium, sodium, natural antioxidants, cytokinins, and plant hormones. A drink made from water with a teaspoon of salt, lemon juice, and chopped pieces of leafy greens is also beneficial.

The amount of water to drink depends on overall health, the type of activity and work, and the amount of sweating. Drinking water when we are thirsty is already a sign of partial dehydration.
Mild signs of dehydration are mild to severe thirst, loss of appetite, dry mouth, flushed skin, fatigue, headache, very little dark urine, weak muscles, dizziness, and lightheadedness. Severe signs of dehydration are rapid pulse and breathing, absence of sweating and urination, elevated temperature, fatigue, muscle cramps, headache, and nausea. When the body loses ten percent of its water, the situation is critical. Critical signs of dehydration are muscle cramps, vomiting, tachycardia, visual disturbances, hot skin, painful urination, confusion, breathing difficulties, seizures, chest and abdominal pain, and loss of consciousness.
There are signs of chronic dehydration, which can lead to kidney failure, stroke, heart attack, the formation of kidney stones, and many other diseases (migraine headaches, lower back pain, heartburn). Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

A nine-year-old tells his mother, who is pressuring him to study, "Mom, stop bothering me!" With this behavior, the child demonstrates that he is guided by the "pleasure principle," the principle of pleasantness. In moments when studying is mentioned, his mother becomes merely an annoying distraction that causes him great discomfort. When his mother mentions studying, the child imagines himself studying, and even the thought causes him significant discomfort. The child emotionally becomes a "victim" of studying, which hasn't even begun yet. Therefore, the child tries to aggressively silence his mother, whom he believes is subjecting him to "psychological abuse."
Most people behave in relation to someone or something based on how they feel about that person, thing, or concept. A feeling of pleasantness triggers a desire for closeness. A feeling of unpleasantness triggers a desire for distance. Experiencing a feeling of pleasantness or unpleasantness is our internal signal that helps us assess something as positive or negative.
If things were simple, people could simply rely on their feelings. The problem is that feelings are the result of someone's internal processing of information, and it is known that people process information differently internally. A small child and an adult do not react to a situation in the same way. Even two adult and rational people usually do not react to a situation with the same feeling, the same sensation, and the same emotion. If our unconscious processing of information is incorrect, then our resulting emotion is also incorrect. Therefore, feelings can "deceive" us. This is especially true for small children, who do not yet have enough information, so they behave solely based on how they feel, how they sense things.
In the first months of life, a child learns that it is very bad when he feels the unpleasantness of hunger, and that it is good when he feels the pleasantness of fullness after being fed. He believes that everything that is pleasant is also beneficial for him. And everything that is unpleasant is harmful to him. Based on this established logic, the child experiences playing with toys as pleasant and therefore beneficial. He will experience the parent's request to put the toys away after playing as unpleasant and therefore harmful. Therefore, the child wants to play and does not want to put the toys away. Sigmund Freud called this motivation of the child the "pleasure principle." The task of parents is to help the child overcome this motivation, because a person who remains at this stage will never become a functional adult. He will be a lazy, selfish person without work and other useful habits.
Parents must teach the child a new logic: that it is not important to pursue everything in life based on whether it is pleasant or unpleasant, but it is important to determine what is beneficial and what is harmful. Of course, the child will resist this upbringing with all his might, because he wrongly believes that his parents do not love him when they do not allow him to enjoy himself or force him into unpleasant, painful actions.
When the child finally abandons the pleasure principle under the influence of his parents, so that he is no longer guided by the criterion of "pleasant-unpleasant," but by the assessment of "beneficial-harmful," then, according to Freud, the child develops the dominance of the "reality principle." This is a big step for the child towards emotional maturity. The mental structures of such a child are now different, the processing of internal information is of higher quality, so that the child can now rely more often and more safely on his intuition and internal feelings, which will be more real than before.

Če bi bile stvari enostavne, bi se lahko ljudje zgolj naslanjali na svoje občutke. Problem je v tem, da so občutja nekoga rezultat njegove notranje obdelave podatkov, in znano je, da ljudje različno notranje obdelujemo informacije. Ni enako, kako se na neko situacijo odzove majhen otrok ali odrasla oseba. To še posebej velja za majhne otroke, ki še nimajo dovolj informacij, zato se vedejo (obnašajo) izključno na podlagi tega, kako se počutijo, kako čustvujejo.

Misli, da je vse, kar mu je prijetno, tudi koristno zanj. In vse, kar mu je neprijetno, je zanj škodljivo. Po tej utrjeni logiki otrok igranje z igračkami doživlja kot prijetno in zato koristno. Zahtevo starša, da po igranju igrače za seboj pospravi, pa bo doživel kot neprijetno in zato zanj škodljivo. Zato se otrok hoče igrati in noče pospravljati igračk. Tako motivacijo otroka je Sigmund Freud poimenoval »princip prijetnosti«. Naloga staršev je, da pomagajo otroku premagovati to motivacijo, kajti oseba, ki ostane na tej stopnji, ne bo nikoli postala funkcionalni odrasli. Bo lena, sebična oseba brez delovnih in drugih koristnih navad.
Starši morajo otroka naučiti novo logiko: da ni pomembno vse v življenju zasledovati na podlagi tega, ali je to prijetno ali neprijetno, temveč je pomembno ugotoviti, kaj je koristno in kaj je škodljivo. Seveda se bo otrok taki vzgoji z vsemi štirimi upiral, ker napačno veruje, da ga starši nimajo radi, kadar mu ne omogočajo uživanja oz. ga silijo v neprijetna, mučna dejanja.
Ko otrok končno pod vplivom starša opusti princip prijetnosti, tako da ga ne vodi več merilo »prijetno-neprijetno«, ampak ocena »koristno-nekoristno«, takrat otrok razvije po Freudu prevlado »principa realnosti«. Duševne strukture takega otroka so sedaj drugačne, obdelovanje notranjih informacij je kakovostnejše, tako da se otrok sedaj lahko večkrat in bolj varno nasloni na svojo intuicijo in notranje občutke, ki bodo bolj realni kot prej.

The pleasant weather is perfect for outdoor activities. Young families, eager to spend their free time actively, often ask us about using training wheels to help their toddlers learn to ride a bike. We advise them with the following facts, but ultimately leave the decision to them.

Cycling is very important for a child's development. It's an activity that engages both hemispheres of the brain. Because it involves alternating the use of each leg (there's no other way to do it), we talk about dissociation of movement in the lower limbs and pelvis. Cycling helps children develop muscle strength, coordination, and balance, which strengthens the cardiovascular system.

Since learning to cycle takes time, we advise parents to offer their toddlers a balance bike before they start cycling. The size of the balance bike must be appropriate for the child. The seat height should be adjusted so that the child can still reach the ground with both feet. With a balance bike, children learn important motor skills. They feel safer because they don't need to use their legs to push the pedals. They learn to balance and coordinate their movements. It's important to emphasize that the child should push off with alternating legs, not with both legs at the same time. When using a balance bike, children often lift both feet and learn to balance – just like when cycling. Cvijetićanin (2011) says that the balance bike was invented not only to develop balance but also to ensure the correct development of a child's spine.

Around the age of three (on average), a child is ready to learn to cycle. At this stage, the child begins to develop body rotations (counter-rotations), which is very important for cycling. As with the balance bike, it's also important that the child can reach the pedals with both feet. Because this skill is very demanding and requires everything to "click" into place, parents often offer their child help – training wheels. We advise against using them. With training wheels, a child only learns to pedal. They lose the sense of balance, and their coordination deteriorates.

We especially advise against using training wheels for children who haven't used a balance bike before, as we agree with the expert's opinion (Cvijetićanin 2011), who says that when a child is put on a bike with training wheels and doesn't yet have developed balance, they will try to compensate for the lack of balance, which can lead to spinal curvature. The child leans from one side to the other and twists their spine, which can have lasting consequences. Of course, this also depends on the amount of time the child spends on the bike.

Our opinion is: it's better to help your child learn to ride a bike by holding them by the seat and never by the handlebars. With frequent attempts, the time will come when they won't even realize that you've let go and that they're riding without your help. At that moment, they'll experience an indescribable joy – they've succeeded!

The ability to regulate blood glucose levels and release its energy potential is also crucial for our physical and mental energy. The brain requires the most glucose, consuming approximately a quarter of the energy the body derives from food, followed by the liver and skeletal muscles. The remaining glucose is used by the heart, the immune system, and other organs.

In the past, conventional medicine recognized only one type of abnormal blood sugar concentration – diabetes. Today, we know that there are barely noticeable levels of this imbalance, which can be an important indicator of health problems, and diabetes is simply the final stage.

Sugar is an oxidant – it oxidizes and damages certain substances, especially proteins. A toxic byproduct of glucose is so-called AGE. If there is too much glucose in the blood, it damages cells and causes them to age faster. AGE also damages blood fats, weakening the body's ability to eliminate excess cholesterol, and collagen, making the skin less elastic.

Most body cells require proper insulin function, which stimulates the absorption of glucose into the liver and muscle cells. However, there are three organs that do not require this: the kidneys, the eyes, and the nerves. In both diabetes and Syndrome X, these organs become overloaded with glucose. This explains why blindness, kidney disease, and nerve damage are such common complications of diabetes.

Diabetes is a condition in which blood sugar levels are significantly elevated because the body cannot transfer excess glucose from the blood into cells and store it there. The blood is merely a "transport medium" for glucose (the end product of carbohydrate metabolism) to the cells, so an excess of glucose in the blood means that there is a deficiency in the cells, which manifests as mental and physical fatigue and occasional loss of consciousness.

There are two main types of diabetes, each with different causes. One type begins when the immune system destroys the cells in the pancreas that produce insulin. The other type is non-insulin-dependent diabetes, which develops in adulthood and is known as diabetes mellitus. The primary cause is poor diet, with sugar being the main culprit. It is treated with a carefully controlled diet. A third, transient form of diabetes can occur during pregnancy.

Although it is true that insulin-dependent diabetes is genetically determined, this is only part of the story. It has been shown that genetically predisposed children who were partially breastfed for at least seven months or exclusively breastfed for at least three to four months are significantly less likely to develop this type of diabetes. The risk is also lower in children who do not receive cow's milk until the age of four months or later. Dr. Hans-Michael Dosch, a professor of immunology in New York, discovered a specific factor in dairy products, bovine serum albumin (BSA), which increases the likelihood of developing diabetes. He proved that it has an adverse effect on pancreatic cells. He hypothesized that if children genetically predisposed to diabetes are exposed to BSA before the age of four months (when the intestinal wall is not yet fully developed and is partially permeable), the body will react to BSA with an allergic reaction, in which immune cells mistakenly destroy not only BSA molecules but also pancreatic tissue. Based on this evidence, the risk of developing diabetes is halved if infants are not fed dairy products in the first six months of life. Unfortunately, BSA can also pass into breast milk through the mother's diet. If breastfeeding mothers do not consume beef and dairy products, the risk of developing insulin-dependent diabetes in genetically predisposed children is virtually eliminated. Early introduction of dairy products into a child's diet, which can cause an allergy to BSA, is one such factor, but it is certainly not the only one.

ADULT DIABETES IS A RESULT OF POOR DIET

A poor diet puts tremendous stress on the body and its ability to adapt. In fact, it is remarkable that only 10% of the population develops diabetes, considering not only the increase in sugar consumption but also the general decline in fiber intake (which slows the release of natural sugars from food into the bloodstream) and the widespread deficiency of vitamins and minerals needed for metabolism, transport, and utilization of sugar. Complications of diabetes include blindness, kidney disease, heart and blood vessel disease, and nerve damage.

New evidence confirms that adult diabetes develops slowly and gradually. Before it develops, the affected person may have various levels of dysglycemia, i.e., an imbalance in blood sugar levels. This initially manifests as insulin resistance – insensitivity to the hormone's action. When we consume carbohydrates, the body produces insulin, which is supposed to help remove glucose from the bloodstream. Symptoms of the disease include fatigue, nausea, dizziness, nervousness, irritability, and difficulty concentrating. The patient is often obese and has a strong craving for sweets or stimulants – pastries, chocolate, coffee, tea, or cigarettes.

The patient begins to gain weight because the body's metabolic mechanisms cannot effectively remove glucose from the blood, so they adapt to the situation and store it as fat, which is of no benefit and often leads to constant fatigue.

Insulin resistance, also known as Syndrome X, has far-reaching consequences for health. It is associated with heart and blood vessel disease, elevated cholesterol levels, inflammatory diseases, tumors, and ultimately, diabetes. This is the downside. The other side is that by properly maintaining blood glucose levels, we can limit the risk of all these major causes of premature death.

Identifying Syndrome X

Conventional tests for diagnosing diabetes (which involve measuring blood sugar levels after consuming a sugary meal, e.g., a sweetened drink) either confirm or deny the presence of diabetes but do not detect the presence of Syndrome X and are therefore not an effective early warning sign. The syndrome can be detected by simultaneously measuring insulin levels in the blood. If insulin levels are high and glucose levels are relatively high two hours after consuming a measured amount of glucose, there is suspicion of insulin resistance. Insulin is clearly not working properly, so blood sugar levels remain high, and the body continues to produce insulin. Another blood test, which is more accurate, measures "glycated" hemoglobin – it determines the extent to which red blood cells have become coated with sugar. If blood sugar levels are frequently too high because cells are resistant to insulin, red blood cells slowly become coated with glucose. Both of these tests can be performed by your general practitioner.

The Dangers of Too Much Insulin

Insulin is a chemically very potent substance, so we do not want it in excessive amounts in the bloodstream: it stimulates the production of stress hormones in the adrenal glands and inhibits the production of DHEA hormone, which protects against stress. The ultimate result of too much insulin is reduced resistance to stress. Too much insulin also stimulates the production of testosterone, which disrupts the balance of sex hormones and causes fat to accumulate in the abdomen and upper body.

However, insulin does not act alone. It is produced by the most important vitamins and minerals, which also help it to function. Vitamin B6 and the mineral zinc are important for its production, and the presence of chromium significantly increases its effectiveness. A deficiency of chromium forces the body to produce more insulin. With an average diet, the body receives only about 30 kilojoules (kJ) of chromium per day: much of it is lost during the processing of food – up to 90% of the chromium in flour, rice, and sugar. Adding chromium to the diet (200 kJ) helps to balance blood sugar levels, reduces the need for insulin, lowers cholesterol and triglyceride levels in the blood, and increases levels of high-density lipoproteins.

CHANGE YOUR DIET

Because the root causes lie in the diet, the best way to prevent and control blood sugar imbalances is to start making changes to your eating habits. Because the ability to regulate blood sugar is linked to maintaining high energy levels, you can incorporate the following recommendations into your plan for an energetic life.

- Limit or gradually eliminate the consumption of all stimulants and sedatives, including coffee, tea, chocolate, cigarettes, or alcohol! This is especially important for anyone who shows signs of addiction (e.g., regularly drinking coffee or tea every day).
- Eat as many whole foods as possible! These include brown rice, whole-wheat bread, whole-wheat pasta, and natural whole foods such as nuts, seeds, lentils, beans, fruits, and vegetables.
- Most of the carbohydrates you eat should be on the list of foods with a low glycemic index! These are foods that release their glucose slowly, such as apples, oats, whole grains, lentils, beans, tofu, and raw vegetables.
- People with fluctuating blood sugar levels (dysglycemia) will find it easier to maintain normal levels if they eat a small amount of fatty protein with carbohydrates. You can eat, for example, a few nuts with fruit or tofu or fish with rice or pasta.
- Take vitamin C and B-complex supplements, which are needed for proper metabolism (high doses of B vitamins and 2000 mg of vitamin C per day).
- Take complex antioxidant supplements. This will prevent cell damage from the formation of toxic byproducts of glucose.
- People with dysglycemia can additionally take 90 mg of coenzyme Q10 and 100 mg of lipoic acid per day.

Od sposobnosti nadziranja ravnovesja glukoze v telesu in sproščanje njenega energijskega potenciala sta odvisni tudi naša telesna in duševna energija. Največ glukoze potrebujejo možgani, ki porabijo približno četrtino energije, ki jo telo predela iz hrane, sledijo jetra in skeletne mišice. Ostanek porabijo srce, imunski sistem in drugi organi.
Uradna medicina je v preteklosti priznavala le eno vrsto nepravilne koncentracije sladkorja v krvi – sladkorno bolezen. Danes vemo, da obstajajo komaj opazne stopnje takšnega neravnovesja, ki so lahko pomemben znanilec zdravstvenih težav, sladkorna bolezen pa je preprosto le zadnja stopnja.
Sladkor je oksidant – oksidira in poškoduje določene snovi, zlasti beljakovine. Toksični stranski produkt glukoze je t.i. AGE. Če po krvi potuje preveč glukoze, ta okvari celice in povzroči, a se hitreje starajo. AGE okvari tudi krvne maščobe, saj oslabi sposobnosti telesa, da bi se znebilo odvečnega holesterola, ter kolagen, zaradi česar je koža manj elastična.
Večina telesnih celic zahteva nemoteno delovanje inzulina, ki spodbuja vsrkavanje glukoze v jetra in mišične celice, vendar obstajajo trije organi, ki tega ne potrebujejo – ledvice, oči in živci. Tako pri sladkorni bolezni kot pri sindromu X postanejo preobremenjeni zaradi glukoze. To nam pojasni, zakaj so slepota, bolezni ledvic in okvare živčevja tako pogosti zapleti sladkorne bolezni.
Diabetes je stanje, pri katerem je koncentracija sladkorja v krvi močno povišana, saj telo presežne glukoze iz krvi ne more prenesti v celice in je tam uskladiščiti. Kri je za glukozo (končni proizvod presnove ogljikovih hidratov) le "transportno sredstvo" do celic, zato presežek glukoze v krvi pomeni, da je v celicah primanjkuje; to se odraža v duševni in telesni utrujenosti in občasnih izgubah zavesti.
Poznamo dve poglavitni vrsti sladkorne bolezni, ki imata različna vzroka. Bolezen se začne tako, da imunski sistem uniči celice v trebušni slinavki, ki proizvaja inzulin. Druga vrsta je od inzulina neodvisna sladkorna bolezen, ki se pojavi v odrasli dobi. Znana je pod imenom diabetes mellitus. Osnovni vzrok zanjo je nepravilna prehrana, glavni krivec pa sladkor. Zdravimo jo s skrbno urejeno dieto. Tretja, prehodna oblika sladkorne bolezni se lahko pojavi med nosečnostjo.
Čeprav je res, da je od inzulina odvisna sladkorna bolezen genetsko pogojena, je to le del resnice. Pokazalo se je, da dedno dovzetni otroci, ki so bili delno dojeni vsaj sedem mesecev ali izključno dojeni vsaj tri do štiri mesece, bistveno redkeje obolijo za to vrsto sladkorne bolezni. Tveganje je manjše tudi pri otrocih, ki ne dobivajo kravjega mleka do četrtega meseca starosti ali dlje. Dr. Hans – Michael Dosch, profesor imunologije v New Yorku, je v mlečnih izdelkih odkril poseben dejavnik, bovinski serumski albumin (BSA), ki povečuje verjetnost nastanka sladkorne bolezni; dokazal je, da neugodno deluje na celice trebušne slinavke. Domneval je naslednje: če pridejo otroci, dednostno nagnjeni k sladkorni bolezni, v stik z BSA še pred dopolnjenim četrtim mesecem starosti (ko črevesna stena še ni popolnoma razvita in je delno prepustna), se bo organizem na BSA odzval z alergijsko reakcijo, pri katerem bodo imunske celice pomotoma uničile ne le molekule BSA, temveč tudi tkivo trebušne slinavke. Na podlagi teh dokazov je tveganje za nastanek sladkorne bolezni za polovico manjše, če dojenčkov v prvih šestih mesecev starosti ne hranimo z mlečnimi izdelki. Žal pa lahko BSA s hrano, ki jo uživa mati, preide tudi v materino mleko. Če doječe matere ne uživajo govejega mesa in mlečnih izdelkov, tveganja za razvoj od inzulina odvisne sladkorne bolezni pri otrocih, ki so za to genetsko dovzetni, praktično ni. Zgodnje uvajanje mlečnih izdelkov v otrokovo prehrano, ki lahko povzroči alergijo na BSA, je sicer eden izmed takšnih dejavnikov, zagotovo pa ni edini.
SLADKORNA BOLEZEN PRI ODRASLIH JE POSLEDICA NEPRAVILNE PREHRANE
Nepravilna prehrana pomeni za telo in njegovo sposobnost prilagajanja izjemen stres. Pravzaprav je čudež, da za sladkorno boleznijo zboli le 10 % prebivalstva, če pri tem upoštevamo ne le porasta porabe sladkorja, temveč tudi splošen upad porabe vlaknin (ki sicer upočasnijo sproščanje naravnega sladkorja iz hrane v krvni obtok) ter vsesplošno pomanjkanje vitaminov in mineralov, ki so potrebni za presnovo, prenos ter izrabo sladkorja. Zapleti pri sladkorni bolezni so slepota, bolezni ledvic, srca in ožilja ter okvare živčevja.
Novi dokazi potrjujejo, da sladkorna bolezen odraslih nastaja počasi in postopoma. Preden se razvije, ima lahko prizadeta oseba različne stopnje disglikemije, tj. neravnovesja vsebnosti krvnega sladkorja. To se najprej kaže kot odpornost proti učinkom inzulina – neobčutljivost za delovanje hormona. Ko uživamo ogljikove hidrate, telo proizvaja inzulin, ki naj bi pomagal odstraniti glukozo iz krvnega obtoka. Simptomi bolezni so utrujenost, slabost, omotičnost, živčnost, razdražljivost in težave z zbranostjo. Bolnik je pogosto debel, ima tudi močno željo po sladkorjih ali poživilih – slaščicah, čokoladi, kavi, čaju ali cigaretah.
Bolnik se začne rediti, ker mehanizmi telesne presnove ne morejo učinkovito odstraniti glukoze iz krvi, zato se prilagodijo stanju in jo skladiščijo kot maščobe, od nje nimajo nikakršne koristi in so pogosto neprestano utrujene.
Odpornost proti inzulinu, znano tudi kot sindrom X, ima obsežne posledice za zdravje. Povezana je z boleznimi srca in ožilja, povišano vrednostjo holesterola, vnetnimi boleznimi, protinom in nenazadnje – sladkorno boleznijo. To je slaba stran. Druga stran pa je, da lahko s pravilnim vzdrževanjem koncentracije krvne glukoze omejimo tveganj vseh teh glavnih vzrokov za prezgodnjo smrt.
Ugotavljanje sindroma X
Konvencionalne preiskave za ugotavljanje sladkorne bolezni (ki zajemajo merjenje vsebnosti krvnega sladkorja po zaužitju sladkega obroka, npr. oslajenega napitka) sicer potrdijo ali zanikajo navzočnost sladkorne bolezni, ne zaznajo pa navzočnosti sindroma X in zato niso učinkovit zgodnji znak za preplah. Sindrom lahko odkrijemo s hkratnim merjenjem vsebnosti inzulina v krvi. Če je koncentracija inzulina visoka, glukoza pa sorazmerno visoka še dve uri po zaužitju izmerjene količine glukoze, obstaja sum na odpornost proti inzulinu. Inzulin očitno ne deluje pravilno, zato je koncentracija sladkorja v krvi še vedno visoka, telo pa še vedno tvori inzulin. Druga krvna preiskava, ki je natančnejša, meri »glikozirani« hemoglobin – ugotavlja, do kakšne mere so rdeče krvne celice postale obložene s sladkorjem. Če je koncentracija sladkorja v krvi pogosto previsoka, ker so celice odporne proti inzulinu, se rdeče krvne celice počasi prevlečejo z glukozo. Oba opisana testa lahko pravi vaš splošni zdravnik.
Nevarnosti prevelike količine inzulina
Inzulin je kemično zelo močna snov, zato si ga v krvnem obtoku ne želimo v prevelikih količinah: spodbuja nastajanje stresnih hormonov v nadledvičnih žlezah, hkrati pa zavira nastajanje DHEA hormona, ki varuje pred stresom. Končni rezultat prevelike količine inzulina je tako manjša odpornost proti stresu. Preveč inzulina spodbuja tudi nastajanje testosterona, to pa poruši ravnovesje spolnih hormonov in povzroči nabiranje maščevja na trebuhu in zgornjem delu telesa.
Inzulin pa ne deluje sam. Proizvajajo ga najpomembnejši vitamini in minerali, ki mu tudi pomagajo pri delu. Vitamina B6 in mineral cink sta pomembna za njegov nastanek, navzočnost kroma pa bistveno poveča njegovo učinkovitost. Pomanjkanje kroma zato prisili telo, da prideluje več inzulina. S povprečno prehrano dobi telo le približno 30 kilojoulov (kJ) kroma na dan: veliko se ga izgubi s prečiščevanjem živil – kar 90 % kroma iz moke, riža in sladkorja. Dodajanje kroma na dan (200 kJ) pomaga izravnati ravnovesje sladkorja v krvi, zmanjša potrebo po inzulinu, zniža vsebnost holesterola in trigliceridov v krvi ter poveča raven lipoproteinov visoke gostote.
SPREMENITE PREHRANO
Ker osnovni vzroki tičijo v prehrani, je za preprečevanje in nadziranje neravnovesja krvnega sladkorja najbolje, da začnete uvajati spremembe v načinu prehranjevanja. Ker je sposobnost nadziranja koncentracije sladkorja povezana z vzdrževanjem visoke energetske ravni, lahko naslednja priporočila vključite v svoj načrt za energetsko polno življenje.
- Omejite ali postopoma opustite uživanje vseh poživil in pomirjeval, vključno s kavo, pravim čajem, čokolado, cigaretami ali alkoholom! To je še zlasti pomembno za vse, ki kažejo znake odvisnosti (npr. redno pitje kave ali čaja vsak dan).
- Uživajte čim več polnovrednih živil! Sem sodijo rjavi riž, črni kruh, testenine iz polnovredne moke in naravna polnovredna živila, kot oreščki, semena, leča, fižol, sadje in zelenjava.
- Večina ogljikovih hidratov, ki jih zaužijete, naj bo na seznamu živil z nizkim glikemičnim indeksom! To so živila, ki svojo glukozo sproščajo počasi, npr. jabolka, oves, polnozrnata žita, leča, fižol, tofu in surova zelenjava.
- Osebe z nihanji koncentracije krvnega sladkorja (disglikemija) bodo lažje vzdrževale normalno koncentracijo, če bodo ob ogljikovih hidratih uživali malo mastne beljakovine. Pojeste lahko npr. nekaj oreščkov s sadjem ali pa tofu oz. ribo z rižem ali testeninami.
- Uživajte dodatke vitaminov C in skupine B, ki so potrebni za pravilno presnovo (visoki odmerki vitaminov skupine B in 2000 mg vitamina C na dan).
- Uživajte kompleksne dodatke antioksidantov. Tako boste preprečili okvare celic zaradi nastajanja toksičnih stranskih produktov glukoze.
- Osebe z disglikemijo lahko dodatno jemljejo 90 mg koencima Q10 in 100 mg lipoične kisline na dan.

Examples include the colors of a rainbow, microwaves, ultraviolet radiation, and X-rays. Each element in a material has a characteristic spectrum. Continuous and line spectra are two types of spectra; the main difference is that a continuous spectrum contains no gaps, while a line spectrum contains many gaps. However, it is important to know more about absorption and emission spectra, which are two main types of spectra, before learning the difference between continuous and line spectra, because both absorption and emission spectra are responsible for creating continuous and line spectra.

This article explores:
1. What is an absorption spectrum
2. What is an emission spectrum
3. What is a continuous spectrum
4. What is a line spectrum
5. What is the difference between a continuous spectrum and a line spectrum

What is an absorption spectrum?
When electromagnetic radiation passes through a specific material, some elements in the material absorb certain characteristic wavelengths. However, the re-emitted photons are not emitted in the same direction. Due to the absence of this absorbed electromagnetic radiation, dark lines appear in the spectrum. An absorption spectrum is drawn with absorption on the y-axis and wavelength or frequency on the x-axis. Absorption spectra are used in various analytical techniques, such as atomic absorption spectroscopy and UV-Vis spectroscopy. These techniques are used to identify a specific substance in a given mixture or to confirm the identity of a specific substance.

What is an emission spectrum?
When a beam of electromagnetic radiation is passed through a sample of atoms or molecules, the electrons in them absorb energy and are transferred to a higher energy state. They then return to their previous energy states by emitting excess energy that they absorbed. When the released energy is reflected against a wavelength, this is called an emission spectrum.

An absorption spectrum is characterized by dark lines in a bright background, while an emission spectrum is the opposite. These two types are opposite. For a specific element, the absorption lines correspond to the frequencies of the emission lines. This is because the energy absorbed by the electrons of a specific element to reach higher energy levels is emitted when they return to their previously occupied energy level.

What is a continuous spectrum?
A continuous spectrum is created by combining both absorption and emission spectra. The main requirement for a spectrum to be a continuous spectrum is that it must contain all wavelengths within a given range. Visible light, when reflected, produces a continuous spectrum. A rainbow contains seven colors that blend into each other without leaving any gaps. When a black object is heated, it emits radiation in a continuous spectrum.

However, scientists say that a continuous spectrum also contains gaps and can only be seen when analyzed with a spectrometer. An ideal continuous spectrum should not contain any gaps. This can only be achieved in perfect laboratory settings and is very rare.

Figure 1: Formation of a continuous spectrum

What is a line spectrum?
Line spectra are generated only in absorption or emission spectra. It displays separate, distinct lines in a given spectrum. These can be absorption lines, which appear as dark lines on a bright background, or bright emission lines that appear on a dark background.

A line spectrum can be produced using the same light source that produces a continuous spectrum. At high pressure, a gas produces a continuous spectrum. However, at low pressure, the same gas can produce an absorption or emission spectrum. If the gas is cold, it produces an absorption spectrum. If the gas is produced in conjunction with heat, it produces an emission spectrum.

Figure 2: Emission spectrum of iron

Difference between a continuous spectrum and a line spectrum

Definition
Continuous spectrum: A continuous spectrum is a superimposed image of absorption and emission spectra.
Line spectrum: A line spectrum is either an absorption spectrum (dark lines on a bright background) or an emission spectrum (bright lines on a dark background).

Gaps
Continuous spectrum: Continuous spectra contain no noticeable gaps.
Line spectrum: There are large gaps between the lines.

Wavelength
Continuous spectrum: A continuous spectrum contains all wavelengths of a given range.
Line spectrum: A line spectrum contains only a few wavelengths.

Examples
Continuous spectrum: The radiation of a rainbow and a black body are examples of a continuous spectrum.
Line spectrum: The emission spectra of hydrogen and the absorption spectra of hydrogen are examples of a line spectrum.

Conclusion
The main difference between a continuous spectrum and a line spectrum is that line spectra can be seen as isolated emission lines or absorption lines, with large gaps between them, while continuous spectra contain no gaps and can be created by overlapping emission and absorption spectra of the same element.

At that time, he was approached by a group of farmers who were facing diseases and phenomena in their barns, fields, and orchards that they had not encountered before due to industrial farming methods, and they did not know how to solve them with the knowledge shaped by the traditional Central European farming practices. Lightning is undoubtedly one of the natural phenomena that leaves no one completely indifferent. The powerful flash of light accompanied by thunder has frightened people for millennia. The lack of understanding of the reasons for electrical discharge in the atmosphere and its consequences led to lightning being almost worshipped as a divine force. Throughout history, various cultures around the world have associated this natural phenomenon, which arrives with storms, ignites fires, kills living beings, causes chaos, and often brings misfortune and despair, with one of their gods. But is anything different today? Experts assure us that we are truly safe from lightning strikes only inside a building with a proper lightning rod or in a car. The latter, in a way, embodies the characteristics of a Faraday cage. Airplanes are also not immune to lightning strikes, but these usually end without serious consequences.
Today, we understand the mechanism of lightning much better. It is a discharge of electrical current when negative charges from the bottom of a storm cloud find a path to the less negatively charged ground. Measurements have shown that the cloud in the sky becomes charged in such a way that its lower edge becomes negative. An electric field, a voltage, appears between the ground and the cloud, which pulls negative electrons towards the ground. The greater this voltage, the more electrons accumulate at the bottom of the cloud. But the air is not conductive, and the electrons cannot simply reach the ground. When this voltage is high enough and the field is strong enough (typically in clouds with many droplets moving rapidly in strong winds), the electrons ionize otherwise neutral air molecules along their path, creating new pairs of electrons and ions that act as a conductive wire. Lightning thus finds a path and creates a conductive channel through which fast electrons travel towards the ground, and slow ions travel towards the cloud. After a few dozen meters, the field of positive ions stops the penetration of electrons towards the ground, and the process pauses for a moment. But through the conductive channel that has formed, new electrons flow from the bottom of the cloud, and the process repeats. In photographs of lightning, you will notice that they consist of many broken segments. Once the conductive channel to the ground is established, it is as if the cloud and the ground are connected by a wire. The electrons accelerate greatly, colliding with air molecules, which glow. This is what we see as a flash. For the same reason, the air also heats up rapidly and expands like an explosion, which we hear as thunder. We all know that the flash of light travels almost instantaneously, while thunder travels slowly at the speed of sound, about one kilometer every three seconds. Even as children, we would huddle under the covers and count the seconds between the flash and the thunder, thus determining the distance of the lightning. Today, the electromagnetic pulse emitted by the current surge of lightning is measured at several locations (antennas) around the world, allowing us to monitor the event quite accurately in real-time.

Heat storms are most common in spring and summer, when the air becomes very warm. Cold fronts are most often associated with violent and sudden storms. Where the weather was clear and the sky was clear just moments ago, cumulus clouds quickly form, and a storm soon breaks out.
During storms and lightning strikes, we must first be aware that the first rule is that there are no rules. It is true that the probability of lightning striking a tall and exposed object is greater than striking a lower object. Similarly, the probability of storms is low between eight in the morning and eleven in the morning. But this does not mean that lightning will not strike us when we are standing near a church, or that a violent storm will not surprise us in the middle of the day. The probability of being struck by lightning is also not very high. Only one in 700,000. But this is just statistics. And just as we can win a large prize in the lottery...
So, what should we do to avoid being struck by lightning, or to avoid being injured by a strike near us? A well-known rule is to avoid solitary trees, as well as all other tall objects that do not have proper grounding. Although we are not completely safe in the forest either, the danger is much less than in more exposed places. Still, move away from taller trees. If we are outdoors and cannot take shelter, crouch down, keep our legs together, remove all objects that are highly conductive, and avoid umbrellas with steel tips, which are excellent lightning rods. And we, along with them. If we have something that is at least partially an insulator, put it under us. The same applies if we are caught in a storm in the mountains. Avoid points where the probability of a lightning strike is highest. Peaks, ridges, exposed points. Avoid wet or damp walls, the edges of cliffs (even the shock wave of air can push us into the abyss). Various alcoves and small caves do not offer protection; they can even be more dangerous places than crouching in the middle of a scree slope. Larger caves are relatively safe, but do not lean against their walls. If there is no possibility of taking shelter, move to a scree slope or another place where there are no exposed objects, and act as we have already described in the case where we are caught in a storm in the lowlands outdoors. Try to position yourself as low as possible, but do not lie on the ground with your entire body. Crouch down so that you are standing on the ground only with your feet or on your toes. Keep your feet as close together as possible. Lower your head to your knees, close your eyes, and cover your ears. If you have a pad made of non-conductive foam or rubber, stand on it. Lightning always tries to find the most conductive path to the ground. By reducing the contact area and using an insulator, we ensure that this path does not go through our body.
Since the mortality rate from lightning strikes is between 15 and 20 percent, the injured person has a good chance of surviving with proper assistance. The most common consequences of a lightning strike are cardiac arrest and cessation of breathing. In addition, those struck often suffer burns, damage to the nervous system, bone fractures, loss of hearing, vision, confusion, unconsciousness, and memory loss. It is safe to touch a person who has been struck by lightning. It is necessary to check for breathing and pulse and to use resuscitation techniques if necessary. Medical assistance is essential, even if the injured person has no visible injuries. Even if they appear only stunned or dazed and have no visible injuries, they may have some damage to internal tissues, such as the nervous system, blood vessels, or heart, which may have serious consequences that only appear after some time.

Your high school years are coming to an end, and you have no idea where you want to apply? Or perhaps you don't even know what you want to do with your life? There are several options. After completing vocational secondary school, you can find a job in your field. After graduating from a general secondary school, further academic pursuits are almost inevitable. But how do you decide when there are so many choices? You have three options: a higher vocational school, a higher education institution, or a university.
Regardless of which you choose, you will earn credit points (each subject has a specific number of credits), take exams, and attend lectures and seminars in the coming years. In the end, you will also achieve a degree, which varies from school to school.
CREDIT POINTS
Credit points, or ECTS, are points that make it easier to evaluate studies across Europe. One academic year consists of 60 credit points, and one credit point requires approximately 25 to 30 hours of student workload.
HIGHER VOCATIONAL SCHOOL
A higher vocational school lasts for 2 years. After completing it, you will earn 120 credit points and achieve a degree level of 6/1. A higher vocational school is more practically oriented and trains you for a specific profession. 40 percent of the curriculum consists of practical work. The prerequisite for enrollment in a higher vocational school is a vocational matriculation exam. Higher vocational schools are both public and private, and enrollment options are full-time and part-time.
HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTION
A higher education institution lasts for 3 years. After completing it, you will earn 180 credit points and achieve a degree level of 6/2. You also need to gain practical experience at a higher education institution, but there is considerably less practical work than at a higher vocational school. You can continue your studies at the second Bologna level. The prerequisite for enrollment is a vocational matriculation exam; some programs also require a fifth subject in addition to the vocational matriculation exam. Enrollment options are also full-time and part-time. After completing your studies, you can continue to the second Bologna level.
UNIVERSITY
A university lasts for 3 or 4 years, depending on whether it follows a new or old program. The old program lasts for four years, and you earn 240 credit points. The revised three-year program earns you 180 credit points. The universities that are currently still four-year programs are the Faculty of Law, the Faculty of Social Work, and the Faculty of Education. The Faculty of Social Sciences is transitioning to a three-year program this academic year.
At the university level, you can also expect a lot more studying, and in the end, you will achieve a degree level of 6/2, which is the same as if you choose a higher education institution. A vocational matriculation exam is not enough to enroll in a university. You must pass a general matriculation exam or a vocational matriculation exam plus a fifth subject. After completing your studies, you can continue to the second Bologna level.
The second Bologna level is one or two years long, depending on whether you previously attended a three- or four-year program. At the second level, you will complete a master's thesis and achieve a degree level of 7.
So, if you are a more practical person who doesn't like studying and knows what you want to do in the future, it is best to enroll in a higher vocational school, where you will gain many practical skills. However, if you don't know what you want to do in the future, or if you are determined that you don't mind studying and having a mostly theoretical curriculum, then a university is definitely the best choice for you.
Higher vocational schools have their own public and private institutions, while higher education institutions and universities are part of four universities (University of Ljubljana, University of Maribor, University of Primorska, and University of Nova Gorica) and some independent higher education institutions. In short, the range of higher vocational schools, higher education institutions, and universities is large, so you will definitely find something that suits your taste and desires. Good luck!

Skratka nabor višjih, visokih šol in fakultet je velik, tako da boš zagotovo našel nekaj za svoj okus in svoje želje. Pa srečno!

Exposure to cold was once a completely normal and natural part of life, when we lived in nature or as hunters and gatherers.
Cold temperature (of the air or water we are exposed to) acts as a stressor on the body. Stress (short-term) is good. It activates survival mechanisms. The body senses that it might not survive the cold, so it activates survival mechanisms. These mechanisms have a beneficial effect on our health, both physically and mentally. Why? Because they stimulate the body to ‘upgrade’ to a better version of itself – a version that can survive the given conditions.
This process is called thermogenesis, or the body's own heat production.
What happens in the body when we are exposed to cold?
Prolonged exposure to cold has negative effects because the body is exposed to stressors for too long. However, a little stress stimulates certain mechanisms, just as other stressors like (intermittent) fasting, increased (and shorter) physical activity, or exposure to heat (e.g., sauna) can.
The effect of cold works by immediately stimulating the creation of new mitochondria (the cellular energy factories that produce ATP) in fat cells, and the fat begins to change from white to brown. We have two types of fat in our body: white and brown. White fat is the fat associated with obesity. It is located around internal organs (around the abdomen), on the sides, and on the thighs. Brown fat is more prevalent in the neck, shoulders, and around the ribs. The more brown fat we have, the more efficient our metabolism is. When the body is exposed to cold, it wants to use the energy stored in fat more efficiently to warm itself. This increases metabolism. The body begins to convert white fat into brown fat and ‘burn’ it to heat the body. This is called cold thermogenesis.
Babies and lean people have the most brown fat, while overweight people have the most white fat. The more we expose ourselves to extreme cold, the more brown fat is created, and the leaner we become.
Comparison of white and brown fat: White fat stores energy, while brown fat generates heat.
Brown fat cells warm the body without shivering. Shivering involves the intervention of muscle tissue (muscle contractions), which is also a form of thermogenesis (but not cold thermogenesis) and is more ‘wasteful’ in terms of energy. Engaging muscle fibers consumes more energy. If we are frequently exposed to cold, the body will adapt with a more economical method, i.e., by using fat.
If we are regularly exposed to cold, the body adapts and becomes more tolerant to cold over time (automatically activating warming mechanisms), which is good news for those who are sensitive to cold, including myself.
Although metabolism increases and fat is burned for energy, the heart rate decreases. Therefore, cold thermogenesis can be a very good way to combat obesity and metabolic diseases.
Did you know that decades ago, NASA scientists and their ‘colleagues’ in the former Soviet Union discovered the benefits of cold exposure, which are greater than those of physical activity? This helped astronauts and cosmonauts stay fit in space. And not only that, it also reduced their appetite!
And did you know that adaptation to cold and exposure to cold for 3 hours (10–12°C on the skin) can burn up to 3,800 calories! (A marathon run burns about 2,600 calories).
Deliberate exposure to short periods of cold is called cryotherapy.
What are the benefits of occasional, short exposure to (extreme) cold, or cryotherapy?
- Regulation of body weight – weight loss, better metabolism
- Brain health – improved cognitive function, concentration, memory, less anxiety and depression, reduced risk of degenerative brain diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. (Cold exposure stimulates the production of the RBM3 protein, which prevents the degradation of synapses.)
- Better immune system – improved body resistance, increased production of white blood cells and T lymphocytes, which fight cancer cells. Reduces chronic inflammation and helps the body heal faster. Increases levels of norepinephrine, which increases the number of natural killer cells. It also increases levels of interleukin 6 (which can have anti-inflammatory effects).
- Reduction of (chronic) inflammation – by reducing the production of TNF-alpha molecules and other inflammatory cytokines (which can help with inflammatory diseases such as arthritis).
- Better sleep – the most important key to essential body regeneration. Cryotherapy helps us fall asleep faster, sleep more deeply, and sleep more quality.
- Increased antioxidant activity in the body
- Stimulates collagen production
- Regulation of the vagus nerve

- Insufficient nitrogen leads to lighter foliage.
- Reduced phosphorus content causes brown spots to appear on the leaves, while the leaf plates remain dark green.
The consequences of nutrient deficiencies can be:
- Soil depletion is one of the causes of so-called "grape bunch rot," which results in small berries and poor bunch formation.
- Sulfur deficiency causes the growth points of new shoots to die.
- Copper deficiency reduces the plant's drought and frost resistance and slows down vine growth.
Proper vine fertilization leads to the following results:
- After applying nitrogen-containing fertilizers, the green mass increases significantly.
- Phosphorus ensures the formation of ovaries.
- Potassium, boron, and zinc help accelerate the ripening of grapes.
- Sulfur accelerates protein metabolism in tissues and improves plant immunity.
Spring vine fertilization is carried out in three stages.
The first stage is before the start of sap flow. Depending on the region, fertilization is carried out from the end of March to mid-April. The second stage is during the period when the ovaries appear on the vine (early to mid-May), and the third stage is in the last days of May.
How to fertilize vines
The plant is fertilized using both foliar and root methods. Using only one of them, the grower will not be able to ensure normal vine growth; therefore, it is better to supplement the addition of nutrients to the soil with foliar applications.
The rate of assimilation of vine fertilizers depends on how they are delivered to the root system. The vineyard owner should be aware that only a portion of the elements sprayed on the fertilizer surface enters the tissue of the vine; moreover, foliar application helps in the development of secondary shoots, which inhibits the development of the vine. Experienced gardeners recommend improving root nutrition as follows:
- During each planting, it is desirable to dig a trench with a diameter of 100 mm to a depth of approximately 0.5 m. The trench is placed at the same distance from the bush.
- Trenches with a depth of 0.5 m are dug around the bush at a distance of 0.5-0.7 m. Fertilizer is poured into the trench and covered with soil.
The need to apply nutrients at this level is due to the depth of the main roots of the vine. For this reason, pipes are used to deliver water and fertilizer to the bushes.
Ingredients for vine fertilization
Most often, in the spring, vines are fertilized with the following mineral fertilizers:
- potassium sulfate;
- ammonium nitrate;
- superphosphate.
A solution of these chemical compounds with water is used to provide the plant with complete nutrition.
The composition of a complex fertilizer for 1 bush is as follows:
- 2 tbsp. superphosphate;
- 1 tbsp. ammonium nitrate;
- 1 tsp potassium sulfate;
- 10 liters of water at room temperature.
The solution is applied to the soil in the first two stages; the third application is carried out without dissolving the salts in water, as this stimulates the growth of green mass, which inhibits the development of the grapes.
There are also ready-made complex fertilizers for plant nutrition.
They already contain a balanced amount of essential nutrients. If a beginner finds it difficult to prepare a mixture independently, they can use compounds such as Mortar, Florovit, Akvarin, and Novofert. Fertilizer containers are equipped with instructions for use.
For the full development of grapes, the use of organic fertilizers is also important. They are used as an independent means of feeding the bush, but organic substances are often used in combination with chemical fertilizers.
Chicken manure is suitable for feeding the roots. A liquid infusion is prepared from it:
- 1 liter of manure;
- 4 liters of water.
4 weeks after preparation, the solution is applied to the soil. Before this, its volume is adjusted with water to 10 liters. 1 liter of infusion is enough for each bush.
Ash infusion will help to compensate for the lack of potassium. The infusion is made from 2 liters of ash and 8 liters of water. After one day, it can be applied to the soil. 1 liter of the mixture is taken for each plant and diluted in 10 liters of water.
The soil under the vineyard is enriched with beneficial microflora, phosphorus, nitrogen, and potassium, and compost is added. It is introduced into the soil to a depth of 30 cm. Compost is often used instead of fertilizer. It should be remembered that such organic matter can be used only in early spring.
Another type of organic fertilizer is slurry. It is prepared by mixing manure with water in a ratio of 1:2. After 10 days, water is added to the liquid (6 parts of water for 1 part of slurry). 10 liters of organic solution are needed to feed each bush.
Foliar top dressing of vines
Inexperienced gardeners are interested in how to feed vines using the foliar method. With this form of nutrition, nutrients are delivered to the plant through the leaves. Dissolved substances in water are easily absorbed by the tissues of the bush and enhance the effect of fertilizers received through the root system.
Vines are sprayed with a solution of superphosphate, ammonium nitrate, and potassium sulfate, and trace elements such as boron, copper, and zinc are added. To prevent the mixture from evaporating too quickly from the leaves, 2-3 tablespoons of sugar are added to the solution. Fertilizers that are ready for use are also suitable for spraying.
Gardeners often use infusions of ash and herbs. It is prepared as follows:
- A container is filled halfway with grass;
- Water is poured in;
- It is left to ferment (10-14 days).
Before spraying, 1 liter of this liquid is added to 0.5 liters of ash infusion and 10 liters of water.
The first spraying of vines is carried out before flowering to prevent the flowers from falling off and increase the number of ovaries. During flowering, spraying is carried out using drugs that promote better pollination of the vine. Humisol, Gumat potassium, etc. are suitable for top dressing.
The next spraying should be carried out immediately after flowering with a fertilizer that does not contain nitrogen.
3 days before flowering, the vines are sprayed with a solution of boric acid powder. The mixture is prepared from 5 g of the substance and 10 liters of water. Boron is important for the development of the vine and increases the yield of the plant, but its excess impairs photosynthesis. Do not forget about the toxicity of the substance.
Vinegrowers advise how to feed vines in May in the spring. They suggest preparing a nutrient solution:
- 2 g of boric acid;
- 2 g of zinc sulfate (zinc is almost not absorbed through the roots);
- 0.5 g of potassium permanganate;
- 0.5 g of ammonium molybdate;
- 0.5 g of cobalt sulfate;
- 10 liters of water.
Spraying is carried out in 2-3 days after foliar application with complex fertilizers. The solution stimulates flowering and improves the quality of the grapes.
How to spray vines best
To make the results of spraying more effective, you should follow a few simple rules:
- The work is carried out in the morning, in the evening, or on a cloudy day (it is important that the leaves do not burn, as the drops of water act on them as lenses).
- Do not spray the vineyard before rain or in windy weather, as the fertilizers will be washed away or evaporate too quickly.
- The optimal ambient temperature during spraying is +18 ... +22 °C.
Proper vine fertilization will yield a good harvest, and the vine will bear fruit for a long time, pleasing the owners.
