Care and Maintenance of Fruit Trees
The main purpose of fruit trees is to provide us with as much fruit as possible each year. If we do not care for the trees and leave them to their own devices, the yield will be smaller and the quality of the fruit will be poorer. If we carefully care for the trees throughout the year, we will be rewarded in the autumn with a large harvest of beautiful and delicious fruit.
The care of fruit trees begins at the end of winter or early spring with pruning. Pruning is essential for maintaining the proper shape of the crown and for stimulating fruit production.
In early spring, we fertilize all young trees and trees that are not thriving and producing poorly with manure or compost. If we decide to use artificial fertilizers, which is not generally recommended for home gardens, we spread them on the ground up to the edge of the crown. If we notice that the trees are lacking certain elements (e.g., potassium, magnesium, etc.), we use special fertilizers, applying them strictly according to the manufacturer's instructions.
We regularly mow the grass around the trees. We can remove the mown grass, but it is better to leave it to decompose, as this returns nutrients to the soil. This is especially important if the trees are suffering from a lack of potassium.
When the fruit begins to develop, we need to thin the fruit on some tree species and varieties to obtain large, tasty fruit and prevent the branches from breaking due to the weight of the fruit. Thinning is especially necessary for pears, apples, and plums. By regularly removing excess fruit on some varieties, we ensure a large harvest in the following year. The number of thinnings depends on the individual species, but usually, we thin twice. The first thinning is done when the fruit begins to form. We remove all damaged or affected fruit. The second thinning is done when the fruit is more developed. We remove individual fruit to make room for others. We thin with scissors or by hand.
We water as needed on dry and hot summer days.
Branches that grow freely will droop heavily under the weight of the fruit and may break in strong winds. To prevent this, we support the branches with stakes or props. We make sure to protect the point of contact with a soft material to prevent damage to the bark. If there are many such branches, we can place a stake next to the trunk and tie the branches to it from the top.
We regularly inspect the stakes and supports and replace or repair any damaged ones as needed.
Spring frosts can cause a lot of damage to fruit trees. Spring frosts can cause the flowers or fruit to die, resulting in a smaller harvest or no harvest at all. The best solution is to choose more frost-resistant varieties or varieties that bloom later in the spring. When frost is forecast, we can cover smaller trees and shrubs with a cloth.
We regularly inspect the fruit trees, at least once a week, and look for any pests or diseases. We treat them as soon as possible to prevent them from multiplying and causing more damage.

We can’t deny it; we have a sweet tooth. Unfortunately, too much sugar can lead to weight gain, and excess weight can contribute to a number of serious health problems, including high blood pressure, high cholesterol, type 2 diabetes, heart disease, stroke, gallbladder disease, osteoarthritis, or even cancer.
A diet high in sugar can also cause an imbalance in the gut microbiome, where trillions of microorganisms reside in the digestive tract. A study published in September 2022 examined the effects of a high-sugar, high-fat diet, which was tested on mice for four weeks. Scientists found that the mice’s microbiomes changed dramatically during this period, with specific segmented filamentous bacteria (SFB) declining sharply, while the number of other bacteria increased. Previous research has shown that SFB bacteria play a significant role in maintaining the gut’s immune system.
The decline in this bacteria reduced the number of Th17 immune cells in the gut. These immune cells produce molecules that slow the absorption of ‘bad’ lipids (fatty compounds) from the gut and reduce gut inflammation. In other words, they keep the gut healthy and protect the body from absorbing pathogenic lipids.
Scientists found that fat was not the cause of an unhealthy gut, so they fed some mice a high-fat diet without sugar; these mice retained their Th17 immune cells and were protected from developing obesity and diabetes, even though they consumed the same number of calories.
Although the findings of these studies cannot be directly applied to humans, we are aware that it is important to maintain a healthy gut flora.
Most of the research in this area has been based on mice, but a study published in the journal Inflammatory Bowel Diseases examined data from 366,351 human participants with inflammatory bowel disease, who also recorded details about their dietary intake. Researchers found a link between the risk of ulcerative colitis (a type of inflammatory bowel disease) and high intake of sugar and soft drinks. While scientists found that sugar can promote the growth of bacteria that erode the protective mucus layer in the gut, they also emphasized that those who eat more vegetables have a lower risk of ulcerative colitis.

The Role of Fiber in a Healthy Gut
Fiber promotes beneficial gut microbes. Fiber can balance out the bacterial imbalance caused by sugar, slow down the absorption of sugar in the gut, and help improve blood sugar levels. A high-fiber diet can also reduce the risk of type 2 diabetes.
A glass of apple juice is a source of sugar that does not hinder digestion and metabolism. On the other hand, an apple has both soluble and insoluble fiber, and the presence of both slows down the absorption of blood sugar. Fruits and vegetables, as well as yogurt without added sugar, are the only foods with simple sugars that can benefit the gut. Sugar comes in various forms (e.g., fructose and sucrose), but the most problematic are processed, added artificial sugars.
The main sources of added sugars are sweetened beverages and desserts, as well as sweet snacks such as cookies, cakes, pies, ice cream, frozen dairy desserts, donuts, and pastries. About a quarter of added sugars are found in sweet beverages (such as soft drinks, fruit juices, and sports and energy drinks).
Should we completely stop eating sugar?
Not necessarily. However, each individual should assess their relationship with sugar.
Is it a harmful relationship because you turn to sugar when you want to comfort yourself or soothe your emotions? Or do you not use sugar as a drug, but as an occasional treat, without feeling guilt or shame?
You should also consider your overall health: do you have excess weight, prediabetes, etc.? People with these conditions usually need to limit their sugar intake more than others and consult with a doctor to make sure that their sugar intake does not worsen their condition.
Eliminating sugar from the diet is a complex behavioral change. It does not happen overnight, and many people struggle for some time before they succeed.
In conclusion: The answer is moderation. It is okay to indulge in sweets occasionally, but it is generally beneficial to limit added sugars to no more than 10 percent of daily calories.

Prehrana z veliko sladkorja lahko povzroči tudi neravnovesje v črevesnem mikrobiomu, kjer v prebavilih prebiva na milijone mikroorganizmov. Študija, objavljena septembra 2022, je preučevala učinke diete z visoko vsebnostjo sladkorja in maščob, ki so jo štiri tedne testirali na miših. Znanstveniki so ugotovili, da so se mikrobiomi miši v tem časovnem obdobju dramatično spremenili, saj so specifične segmentirane filamentne bakterije (SFB) močno padle, število drugih bakterij pa se je povečalo. Prejšnje raziskave so pokazale, da imajo mikrobi SFB močno vlogo pri ohranjanju črevesnega imunskega sistema.
Padec te bakterije je zmanjšal število imunskih celic Th17 v črevesju. Te imunske celice proizvajajo molekule, ki upočasnjujejo absorpcijo ‘slabih’ lipidov (maščobnih spojin) iz črevesja in zmanjšujejo vnetje črevesja. Z drugimi besedami, ohranjajo črevesje zdravo in ščitijo telo pred absorpcijo patogenih lipidov.
Znanstveniki so ugotovili, da maščoba ni vzrok za nezdravo črevesje, tako da so nekatere miši hranili z visoko vsebnostjo maščob brez sladkorja; te miši so ohranile imunske celice Th17 in bile zaščitene pred razvojem debelosti in diabetesa, čeprav so zaužile enako število kalorij.

Večina raziskav na tem področju je temeljila na miših, vendar je študija, objavljena v reviji Inflammatory Bowel Diseases, preučila podatke 366.351 človeških udeležencev z vnetno črevesno boleznijo, ki so beležili tudi podrobnosti o svojem prehranskem vnosu. Raziskovalci so odkrili povezavo med tveganjem za ulcerozni kolitis (vrsta črevesne vnetne bolezni) ter visokim vnosom sladkorja in brezalkoholnih pijač. Medtem ko so znanstveniki ugotovili, da lahko sladkor spodbuja vrste bakterij, ki razjedajo zaščitno plast sluzi v črevesju, so poudarili tudi, da imajo tisti, ki jedo več zelenjave, manjše tveganje za ulcerozni kolitis.
Vloga vlaknin v zdravem črevesju
Vlaknine spodbujajo koristne črevesne mikrobe. Vlaknine lahko izravnajo bakterijsko neravnovesje zaradi sladkorja, upočasnijo absorpcijo sladkorja v črevesju in pomagajo izboljšati raven sladkorja v krvi. Prehrana z veliko vlakninami lahko tudi zmanjša tveganje za sladkorno bolezen tipa 2.
Kozarec jabolčnega soka je vir sladkorja, ki nič ne ovira prebave in presnove. Po drugi strani pa ima jabolko tako topne kot netopne vlaknine in prisotnost obeh upočasni absorpcijo krvnega sladkorja. Sadje in zelenjava, kot tudi jogurt brez dodanega sladkorja, so edina hrana z enostavnimi sladkorji, ki lahko koristijo črevesju. Sladkor poznamo v različnih oblikah (npr. fruktoza in saharoza), a problematični so predvsem predelani dodani umetni sladkorji.
Glavni viri dodanih sladkorjev so sladkane pijače in sladice ter sladki prigrizki, kot so piškoti, torte, pite, sladoled, zamrznjene mlečne sladice, krofi in pecivo. Približno četrtina dodanih sladkorjev je v sladkih pijačah (kot so brezalkoholne pijače, sadne pijače ter športne in energijske pijače).
Ali naj popolnoma prenehamo jesti sladkor?

Deforestation impacts devastating biodiversity and exacerbates the greenhouse effect.
"Terra Indígena Pirititi, Roraima", Felipe Werneck / Ibama (CC BY-SA 2.0)
Before defining and explaining deforestation, we need to know: what are forests?
Forests are areas with a high density of trees, where the canopies touch and form a kind of green "roof." They are essential for human life. According to the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), approximately 1.6 billion people depend on forest-related activities, and about 60 million indigenous people worldwide depend exclusively on them for their survival. Furthermore, forests are the habitat of numerous animal and plant species.
Now, we can explain what deforestation is, also known as forest clearing or forest removal. According to the dictionary, deforestation is "the act of clearing land of trees," meaning the complete or partial removal of trees, forests, and other vegetation in a specific region.
Today, deforestation is one of the most serious environmental problems, as it not only destroys forests and natural resources but also threatens the planet's balance in various aspects, including ecosystems, which also significantly impacts the economy and society. In Brazil, there is growing concern about deforestation in the Amazon, which reached record levels in 2019.
An edited image by Marcin Kempe is available on Unsplash.
Causes of Deforestation
The causes of deforestation are diverse and mostly consist of human activities that cause or exacerbate this problem, such as: agricultural expansion (clearing land for agriculture, pasture, or land awaiting financial assessment), mining activities (areas devastated by the installation of equipment and activities for exploring gold, silver, bauxite/aluminum, iron, zinc, etc.), intensive and increasing exploitation of natural resources due to the demand for raw materials, increasing urbanization, and increased burning, whether accidental or intentional.
Consequences and Impacts of Deforestation
The consequences and impacts of deforestation are devastating. The first to be affected is local biodiversity, as the destruction of forests leads to the loss of the natural habitat of numerous species, contributing to the death of many animals and even the extinction of endemic species, causing problems in the food chain and local ecosystems. This loss can even affect economic activities such as hunting and fishing.
Deforestation also has negative consequences for water and soil. Since forests are responsible for regulating approximately 57% of the world's surface freshwater, they contribute to providing moisture to the environment. In other words, their removal alters the climate balance of many regions and exacerbates the greenhouse effect. Furthermore, they improve soil drainage, and their absence increases landslides on steep slopes, exacerbates floods, facilitates soil erosion, and leads to desertification. This results in a lack of nutrients in the soil, causing rivers and lakes to silt up with deposited soil. Deforestation is a major cause of soil degradation.
Humans are also affected by the consequences of their own actions, as 1.6 billion people today depend directly or indirectly on forest-related activities. Humans are not only deprived of the potential for continued timber production but also of numerous other valuable natural products, such as fruits, almonds, fibers, resins, oils, and medicinal substances, on which humanity depends for its survival.
In Brazil, the Amazon is a major concern. The forest, covering 6.9 million square kilometers, has suffered from deforestation, which has already affected 18% of its territory since 1970, an area equivalent to the states of Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, Paraná, Rio de Janeiro, and Espírito Santo.
- Deforestation in the Amazon: causes and how to combat it
What can be done to change this paradigm?
For all these reasons, the UN and other international organizations, as well as numerous regional entities, recognize and emphasize that the solution requires a comprehensive, multidisciplinary project that considers local and global factors. This should involve not only scientists, governments, companies, and institutions but also the population, especially local communities, as they are the origin and the end of all processes. The path to this is education and various incentives to clarify the benefits that forests provide and to change ways of thinking and practices related to production and consumption that lead to deforestation.
The goals set by the United Nations were:
- Eliminate global forest cover loss through sustainable management, protection, restoration, and afforestation, and reduce forest degradation;
- Highlight the economic, social, and environmental benefits that forests provide and improve the living conditions of populations that depend on them;
- Significantly expand the global area of protected and sustainably managed forests and promote the consumption of forest products from well-managed forests;
- Reverse the decline in official aid for sustainable projects and mobilize significantly more resources to promote sustainable management.
The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) also recommends the following main strategies for conserving forests and their sustainable management:
- Create well-planned afforestation projects and invest in environmental services;
- Promote small and medium-sized development projects based on forests, especially for the poorest populations, those who depend on them the most;
- Promote the use of wood as an energy source and reuse or recycle wood products;
- Improve international communication and cooperation, promote environmental research and education, facilitate loans, and integrate forestry projects into macroeconomics.
Approximately 31% of the world's land area is still covered by forests with varying degrees of conservation, and about 22% is still in pristine condition. However, despite the considerable forest cover that remains, it is estimated that half of the world's forests have already disappeared, so we urgently need to return to a healthy planet. To combat deforestation, you can support causes such as the Zero Deforestation movement, consume products from environmentally responsible companies, spread awareness about this issue, and be aware of political positions related to environmental issues (both regarding the government and actions).
Watch the Greenpeace video about the Zero Deforestation movement!

Preden določimo in razložimo krčenje gozdov, moramo vedeti: kaj so gozdovi?
Gozdovi so območja z veliko gostoto dreves, kjer se krošnje dotikajo in tvorijo nekakšno zeleno "streho". So temeljnega pomena za človeško življenje. Po podatkih Programa Združenih narodov za okolje (UNEP) se približno 1,6 milijarde ljudi preživlja z neko dejavnostjo, povezano z gozdovi, in približno 60 milijonov avtohtonih prebivalcev po vsem svetu je izključno od njih odvisno preživetje, poleg tega pa je življenjski prostor številnih vrst živali in rastlin.
Zdaj lahko razložimo, kaj je krčenje gozdov, čemur lahko rečemo tudi krčenje gozdov ali krčenje gozdov. Lahko rečemo, da je krčenje gozdov po slovarju "dejanje, ki sestoji iz čiščenja grmovja", to je popolna ali delna odstranitev dreves, gozdov in druge vegetacije v določeni regiji.
Krčenje gozdov je danes ena najresnejših okoljskih težav, saj poleg uničujočih gozdov in naravnih virov ogroža ravnovesje planeta v različnih elementih, vključno z ekosistemi, ki resno vplivajo tudi na gospodarstvo in družbo. V Braziliji narašča zaskrbljenost zaradi krčenja gozdov v Amazoniji, ki je leta 2019 podrla rekorde.
Urejena in spremenjena slika Marcina Kempe je na voljo na Unsplash
Vzroki krčenja gozdov
Vzroki za krčenje gozdov so raznoliki in večinoma sestavljeni iz človekovih dejavnosti, ki povzročajo ali stopnjujejo pojav tega problema, kot so: kmetijska širitev (odpiranje površin za kmetijstvo, paša ali podeželje, ki čakajo na finančno oceno), rudarska dejavnost (območja, ki so opustošena zaradi namestitve opreme in dejavnosti za raziskovanje zlata, srebra, boksita / aluminija, železa, cinka itd.), intenzivno in vedno večje izkoriščanje naravnih virov zaradi povpraševanja po surovinah, naraščajoče povečana urbanizacija in povečano gorenje, naključno ali namerno.
Posledice in vplivi krčenja gozdov
Posledice in vplivi krčenja gozdov so uničujoči. In prva prizadeta je lokalna biotska raznovrstnost, saj ko se uničijo gozdovi, se naravni življenjski prostor številnih vrst izgubi , kar prispeva k smrti mnogih živali in celo izumrtju endemičnih vrst, kar povzroča težave prehranjevalna veriga in lokalni ekosistemi. Ta izguba lahko vpliva celo na gospodarske dejavnosti, kot sta lov in ribolov.
Krčenje gozdov ima tudi negativne posledice za vodo in tla. Ker so gozdovi odgovorni za uravnavanje približno 57% površinske sladke vode na svetu, prispevajo tako, da okolju zagotavljajo vlago. Z drugimi besedami, njihovo odstranjevanje pomeni spreminjanje podnebnega ravnovesja številnih regij, da ne omenjamo krepitve učinka tople grede. Poleg tega izboljšajo odvodnjavanje tal, njihova odsotnost pa okrepi plazove na strmih pobočjih, poudari poplave, olajša erozijo tal in dezertifikacijo. Posledica tega je pomanjkanje hranilnih snovi v tleh, ki povzročajo zamuljenje rek in jezer z odlaganjem naložene zemlje v njenih strugah. Krčenje gozdov je glavni vzrok za degradacijo tal.
Človek je še en, ki trpi posledice lastnih dejanj, saj je, kot že rečeno, 1,6 milijarde ljudi danes neposredno ali posredno odvisnih od dejavnosti, povezanih z gozdovi. Človek ni prikrajšan samo za potencialno neprekinjeno proizvodnjo lesa, temveč tudi za številne druge dragocene naravne izdelke, kot so sadje, mandlji, vlakna, smole, olja in zdravilne snovi, od katerih je človeštvo odvisno od svojega preživetja.
V Braziliji je ena največjih skrbi Amazonka. Gozd s 6,9 milijona kvadratnih kilometrov trpi zaradi krčenja gozdov, ki je od leta 1970 dosegel že 18% svojega ozemlja, kar je območje, ki ustreza območjem Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, Paraná, Rio de Janeiro in Sveti Duh.
- Krčenje gozdov v Amazoniji: vzroki in kako se boriti
Kaj storiti, da spremenimo to paradigmo?
Zaradi vseh teh razlogov OZN in drugi mednarodni organi ter številni regionalni subjekti priznavajo in povzemajo dejstvo, da mora rešitev pri obsežnem multidisciplinarnem projektu upoštevati lokalne in globalne dejavnike. V to ne smejo biti vključeni samo znanstveniki, vlade, podjetja in ustanove, ampak tudi prebivalstvo, še posebej pa prebivalstvo, saj je to izvor in konec vseh procesov. Pot do tega je izobraževanje in različne spodbude za razjasnitev koristi, ki jih prinašajo gozdovi, in za spreminjanje načinov razmišljanja ter navad pridelave in porabe, ki vodijo v krčenje gozdov.
Cilji, ki so jih določili Združeni narodi, so bili:
- Odpraviti izgubo gozdne pokrovnosti po svetu s trajnostnim gospodarjenjem, zaščito, obnovo in pogozdovanjem ter zmanjšati propadanje gozdov;
- Poudariti gospodarske, socialne in okoljske koristi, ki jih prinašajo gozdovi, in izboljšati življenjske pogoje prebivalstva, ki je od njih odvisno;
- Znatno razširiti svetovno območje zaščitenih in trajnostno upravljanih gozdov ter spodbujati porabo gozdnih proizvodov iz dobro urejenih gozdov;
- Obrniti upad uradne pomoči trajnostnim projektom in mobilizirati bistveno več sredstev za spodbujanje trajnostnega upravljanja.
Organizacija Združenih narodov za prehrano in kmetijstvo (FAO) priporoča tudi naslednje glavne strategije za ohranjanje gozdov in njihovo dobro upravljanje:

- Spodbujati male in srednje velike razvojne projekte, ki temeljijo na gozdovih, zlasti za najrevnejše populacije, tiste, ki so od njih najbolj odvisne;

Si profesionalni prevajalec iz angleščine v slovenščino. Tvoja naloga je ustvariti visoko kakovostne prevode, ki so naravni, tekoči in natančni. Izogibaj se dobesednim prevodom, ki zvenijo nenaravno. Upoštevaj kontekst, idiome in kulturne reference. Ne dodajaj nobenih dodatnih informacij ali komentarjev, samo prevod.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

Many children suck on pacifiers or fingers to soothe themselves, while others bite their lips or cheeks. Infants use sucking as a way to interact with their environment and explore the world around them. However, it is important to discourage or prevent these habits as early as possible to avoid changes to the tooth surface and irregularities in the position of the teeth and jaw. We will discuss some of the negative consequences of these habits and explain why it is important to be consistent and persistent when trying to break them.

Each pacifier limits the space available to the tongue.
Regardless of how popular and widely accepted pacifiers are, they are foreign objects in a child's mouth. Children who suck on pacifiers in the first six weeks of life are more likely to have difficulty breastfeeding because the sucking motion is different from that of breastfeeding. While pacifiers can be specially designed and orthopedically adapted, this does not change the fact that they alter the balance of forces in the mouth. The normal balance is maintained by the force of the cheek, lip, and tongue muscles, as well as biting. If a pacifier takes up space in the mouth, the tongue is pushed further back, which can prevent the normal development of the upper jaw.

The long-term consequences of prolonged pacifier use can include an open bite, mouth breathing, and incorrect swallowing. The muscles exert pressure on the bones in the wrong places, which can lead to changes in the shape of both dental arches. In young children, these changes may be small and go unnoticed by parents. However, if these habits are not corrected, they can have a negative impact on the growth of the teeth and jaw. Misaligned jaws and teeth can become more noticeable and problematic. The most common problems include unilateral crossbite with a narrow upper jaw, open bite, and deep bite. These problems require orthodontic treatment. Misalignment of the teeth and jaws can also cause speech problems, especially with sibilant sounds. Children may push their tongue between their teeth when speaking, which can result in a lisp. Speech therapy may be necessary to correct these problems.

Pacifier weaning should be gradual but consistent.
If you choose to use a pacifier, it should be used for as short a time as possible to minimize its impact on the development of the mouth. Always clean the pacifier before use, and make sure that each child has their own pacifier and does not share it with siblings or other children. It is recommended to discontinue pacifier use completely after the age of 18 months, and it is best to gradually wean the child off the pacifier. You can determine the best method for weaning your child based on your knowledge of their interests. Consistency and determination are essential during the weaning process. Do not give the pacifier back to the child, even if they are crying. Explain the situation in a way that is appropriate for their age and reassure them. If the child needs physical comfort, hold them.

Children who use pacifiers often also develop a habit of drinking from a bottle. While bottles are widely used, it is best to encourage children to drink from a cup as early as possible, ideally before the age of one year. A major problem with bottle feeding is the contents of the bottle. Do not give children sugary drinks, sweetened beverages, or tea made from granules in a bottle. Sugar can make children feel good, but if they drink slowly from a bottle, the sugar will remain on the surface of their teeth for a long time, which can lead to early childhood caries, also known as bottle caries. This type of tooth decay is common in children under the age of three and often affects the upper front teeth and the first molars. The decay starts as a white spot and progresses to a brown spot, eventually causing a cavity.

If the decay reaches the pulp, the living tissue inside the tooth, the tooth may need to be extracted. This can result in the child losing a tooth that could have been used for many years for chewing and speech development. Studies have also shown that children who have experienced tooth decay in early childhood are more likely to develop tooth decay in their permanent teeth. To prevent tooth decay, practice good oral hygiene with your child, including brushing with a soft toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste. Take your child for regular dental checkups, at least once a year.

Thumb sucking is a difficult habit to break, so prevention is key.
Similar to pacifier use, thumb sucking can have negative consequences. Open bite is more common with thumb sucking, where the front teeth do not meet when the mouth is closed, and the upper front teeth are tilted forward, while the lower front teeth are tilted backward.

Most children stop thumb sucking on their own, but those who do not may need help. Thumb sucking can be more difficult to break than pacifier use because the thumb is always available. Children who continue to suck their thumbs after the age of two or three may be more anxious and insecure than their peers. It is important to try to identify any factors that may be contributing to the child's anxiety.

To help your child break the habit, avoid punishing them and instead redirect their attention to another activity, such as one that requires the use of both hands. Sometimes, children are more likely to stop thumb sucking if they are told by other children. Patience and encouragement are essential, and the time it takes to break the habit can vary from child to child.

Lip biting and nail biting are less common habits, but they can still have negative consequences. Lip biting can develop in childhood or adulthood, often in response to stress. The wounds from lip biting usually heal quickly, but if they are repeated over a long period of time, they can lead to unwanted changes.

Nail biting can also have a negative impact on the development of the jaw and teeth. It can also lead to problems with the skin around the nails, such as inflammation, redness, and crusting, as well as an increased risk of infection. Bacteria can also be transferred from the fingers to the mouth. To help your child break the habit, try applying a bitter-tasting nail polish to their nails. You can also try redirecting their attention and distracting them. Encourage them to be motivated to change.

Persistence, patience, and determination are key to overcoming any habit.
Just as it can be difficult for adults to break habits, it can also be difficult for children. They need help, encouragement, and support. Often, these habits can be prevented, so it is important to be persistent from the beginning.

Številni otroci za pomiritev sesajo dudo, nekateri prst, grizljajo ustnico ali lice. Dojenčki s sesanjem ustvarjajo stik z okoljem, spoznavajo svet okrog sebe, a jih je vredno omenjenih razvad čim prej odvaditi ali pa jih preprečiti. Le tako preprečimo nastanek sprememb na površini zob in nepravilnosti v položaju zob in čeljusti. Predstavljamo vam nekaj pomembnih neželenih posledic omenjenih razvad in vam želimo pojasniti, zakaj je pomembno, da ste pri odpravljanju teh razvad do otroka odločni in vztrajni.
Vsaka duda jeziku omejuje prostor
Ne glede na priljubljenost in vsesplošno sprejetost dud, je duda v otroških ustih tujek. Otroci, ki sesajo dudo v prvih 6 tednih življenja imajo več težav z dojenjem, ker sesanje dude poteka drugače kot sesanje prsne bradavice. Duda je lahko posebej oblikovana, ortopedsko prilagojena, a to dejstva, da spreminja ravnovesje med običajnimi silami v ustni votlini, ne spremeni. Normalno ravnovesje je zagotovljeno s silo mišic lic, ustnic, jezika in grizenja. Če duda jeziku odvzame prostor, se jezik pomakne bolj proti ustnemu dnu in ni možnosti, da bi spodbujal normalni razvoj zgornje čeljusti.
Posledice dolgotrajnejšega, večletnega sesanja dude se kažejo pri otroku z držo odprtih ust, dihanjem na usta namesto skozi nos in nepravilnim požiranjem z vrivanjem jezika med zobe. Mišice tako na nepravih mestih pritiskajo na kosti, posledica so spremembe v obliki obeh zobnih lokov. Pri najmlajših gre za zelo majhna odstopanja, starši mogoče niti ne opazijo, da je karkoli narobe s postavitvijo zob. Če pa teh motenih funkcij in razvad ne odpravimo, neželeno vplivajo na nadaljnjo rast zob in čeljusti. Narobe razvite čeljusti in napačna postavitev zob postanejo vedno bolj opazni in moteči. Najpogosteje se izrazijo kot enostranski križni ugriz z ozko zgornjo čeljustjo, zato se spodnja čeljust pri ugrizu zamakne v eno stran, odprti ugriz, pri katerem ostaja tudi po ugrizu presledek med sprednjimi zobmi ali globoki ugriz s slabo razvito spodnjo čeljustjo. Omenjene nepravilnosti je potrebno ortodontsko obravnavati. Zaradi nepravilnosti odnosov med čeljustmi ali zobmi imajo otroci lahko težave pri izgovorjavi določenih glasov, še posebej sičnikov in šumnikov. Izgovarjajo jih tako, da jezik potiskajo med zobe, namesto da bi jezik ostal za zobmi, kar se sliši kot sesljanje. Za odpravljanje težav z govorom je največkrat potrebna pomoč logopeda.
Odvajanje od dude naj bo postopno, a dosledno
V kolikor se pri otroku odločite za uporabo dude, naj bo v ustih čim krajši čas, da tako manj vpliva na razvoj ustne votline. Dudo pred uporabo vedno očistite, poleg tega naj ima vsak otrok vedno le svojo dudo in je naj ne izmenjuje z brati, sestrami, ali drugimi otroki. Po dopolnjenem letu in pol, je dudo priporočljivo dokončno umakniti, na ločitev od dude pa je smiselno otroka postopoma navajati. Način odvajanja boste za svojega otroka glede na poznavanje njegovih interesov najlažje prepoznali sami. Pri odvajanju je vedno potrebna odločnost, otroku dude ne vrnite tudi če ne neha jokati. Prilagodite razlago ustrezno njegovi starosti, ga pomirite. Če otrok potrebuje telesni stik, ga vzemite v naročje.
Otrok se ob dudi pogosto navadi tudi na pitje iz stekleničke. Kljub široki razširjenosti otroških stekleničk je otroka dobro čim prej, za večino otrok do starosti prvega leta, navaditi na pitje iz skodelice. Velika težava pri sesanju stekleničk je pogosto tudi v vsebini stekleničke. Otroku nikar ne dajajte v stekleničko sladkih sokov, sladkanih napitkov ali čaja iz granul. Sladkor daje otrokom občutek ugodja, a bo ob počasnem pitju iz stekleničke veliko časa na površini zob, kar lahko zgodaj vodi v pojav posebno težke oblike zobne gnilobe, tako imenovane steklenični karies. Gre za zobno gnilobo pri otrocih do tretjega leta, ki se največkrat pojavi na zgornjih sprednjih zobeh in na prvih mlečnih kočnikih, to so zobje, ki že zgodaj izrastejo v ustno votlino in so pred nastankom zobne gnilobe slabše zavarovani z delovanjem sline kot spodnji zobje. Spremembe se razvijejo okrog celotne površine zoba, najprej kot belkasto zabarvanje, ki napreduje proti rjavkastemu, vse do vdrtja povrhnje plasti sklenine.
Če pride še do vnetja živčno-žilnega pleteža v notranjosti zob, to je zobne pulpe, je takšen zob pogosto potrebno izpuliti. When air moves, we call it wind. But why does air start moving in the first place? What sets it in motion? The physical causes are clear. An imbalance of forces causes movement. We learned this back in elementary school. So, we just need to figure out which forces are acting on a particular mass of air. Gravity certainly plays a role, but it acts towards the center of the Earth, and air cannot move downwards. The strongest force that starts moving air is the difference in air pressure. We call these winds gradient winds (the gradient tells us how quickly or to what extent a quantity changes in a particular direction or over time, for example). The windiest weather occurs in areas with cyclones, especially tropical ones. That’s where the pressure differences are the greatest. Once a mass of air starts moving, the Coriolis force also acts on it – this is a force that arises due to the Earth’s rotation. Air also experiences friction with the ground as it moves, like any other body, and under the influence of these different forces, a vortex – a cyclone – is formed. Of course, cyclones are large formations, with a diameter of around 1000 kilometers. There are also smaller ones, for example, those that form in the Mediterranean. On the edge of cyclones, the winds are usually weaker, but as you move towards the center, they become stronger. And since the centers of cyclones generally travel north of our region, the stronger winds are found north of the Alps, where they are not hindered as much by hills as they are by extensive plains and plateaus. This is another reason why we don’t experience strong winds as often.

Another reason can be the difference in air temperature. Because warmer air is lighter, it starts to rise, and colder air flows in to replace it – aha, if it flows in, it must be moving. Winds that are created due to these differences in heating are called thermal winds. These are usually weaker than gradient winds, so they become noticeable in areas of high air pressure, when the differences in air pressure are small, and it is often calm. An example of this is a slope wind or a valley wind in the mountains. At night, it blows from higher altitudes to lower altitudes, down the slope, and during the day, in the opposite direction. Or, for example, at the sea – at night and in the morning, it blows from the land to the sea, and when the land warms up enough, it blows from the sea to the land, creating the maestral wind. Of course, when the pressure difference increases, gradient winds “take over” from thermal winds.

By pruning fruit trees, we achieve uniform growth and productivity of shrubs and trees. Woody plants have an incredible ability to regenerate, and by pruning and removing old, degenerated branches, we stimulate the growth of new, more productive shoots, resulting in a better and more abundant harvest. Pruning trees not only improves their appearance in the spring but is also an important agrotechnical measure that helps maintain a balance between shoot growth and productivity, leading to more controlled growth and higher-quality fruits.

Timing of Pruning
In April, fruit trees are just before flowering, but it is still a good time to prune branches, especially those that grow very vigorously. Just before flowering, there are already many nutrients in the tree's crown, which are removed by pruning. This weakens or slows down the tree, which then produces weaker, one-year-old shoots that bear more fruiting wood. In other words, late pruning will result in fewer very long shoots at the top of the tree, which we remove every year. Late pruning is therefore recommended for vigorously growing trees.
When pruning, it is also important to consider air humidity; we want the weather to be as sunny and dry as possible. In rainy weather, various fungi and bacteria settle on the wounds, penetrate the tree's vascular system, and cause the drying and decay of branches. This often happens with apricots, so apricots are pruned during the growing season – on dry days before or after harvesting. Plums are also pruned when they are almost in bloom. Because plums grow vigorously, pruning helps to control their growth, and late pruning also results in slightly shorter new shoots. The same applies to pruning the top shoot of apple trees. We shorten it only in June, and from then on, only shorter, sloping shoots grow, which are not too long in the following years and bear fruit quickly.
We prune thicker branches of walnut trees in August because that is when the tree has the least sap, which would otherwise flow out of the large wound. We also prune young walnut trees in April, and to prevent sap from leaking, we seal the wounds with grafting wax. Therefore, pruning trees is not just a one-time spring task; it is good to have pruning shears in hand throughout the year. In particular, summer pruning is necessary for peaches, which completely cover the fruits with their new shoots. We also remove one-year-old shoots from vigorously growing apple and pear trees, shortening their top shoots in early July, which allows sunlight to reach the fruits. Everything must be done with a certain feel – not too much and not too little. For the good nutrition of one apple, we need 40–50 leaves. Photosynthesis takes place in them, which is the factory for building sugars that the fruits need.
Berry plants are plants that mainly grow in the form of shrubs. Basic pruning is done in the spring, and some is also done during the growing season.
Pruning Black and Red Currants
When planting black currants, we plant them deeper so that more shoots grow from the root. In the first year, we prune the shoots almost to the ground, which stimulates the growth of new, stronger shoots. We leave only 3–4 of the strongest shoots and prune the rest. We do this in the summer. There should not be too many shoots in a black currant bush. In a fully productive bush, there should always be some one-year-old shoots. They will not bear fruit this year, but they will bear a rich harvest next year. The most productive wood is one-year-old shoots that grow from two- and three-year-old wood. On four-year-old wood, we have very short one-year-old shoots, so the yield is also smaller. Therefore, in healthy black currant bushes, we have ¼ one-year-old shoots, ¼ two-year-old, ¼ three-year-old, and ¼ four-year-old shoots each year.
We plant red currants similarly to black currants, and if we don't distinguish them from black currants, we break off a twig or crush a bud, which immediately has a characteristic scent in black currants. We leave two to six shoots in a red currant bush. We leave a single branch in the bush for a longer time, even up to eight years, and then replace it with a young shoot, cutting the old shoot at the ground. We prune gooseberries similarly, or flowering shrubs such as forsythia, weigela, and others. The difference is that with flowering shrubs, we wait for them to finish flowering and then prune them.

Blackberries and raspberries bear fruit on one-year-old shoots that grow from the root crown or roots. With everbearing raspberries, the shoot dries up after harvesting, so we cut it off immediately or in the spring. We cut the shoot or cane just above the ground. We also prune out thin and dense shoots, leaving strong canes about 10 cm apart. If the canes are too long, we can shorten them to 1.5 m. The shoots should be in a row, and then we surround them with wire or string, which serves as support. With primocane-bearing raspberries, we expect the harvest somewhat later, from the end of July to November. One-year-old, fruiting shoots do not dry up in these raspberries but can bear fruit again next year. We can prune them to 0.5 m, and new shoots will grow more quickly from the stub in the spring. We can expect the harvest a week earlier than those that are pruned to the ground. Due to fungal diseases on the stems of raspberries, the stems of primocane-bearing raspberries are usually pruned to the ground in the spring, and the canes are removed and destroyed. New shoots grow from the roots, which bear fruit somewhat later, i.e., from the end of July and bear fruit until the autumn. Raspberries will bear a very good harvest if we fertilize them with well-rotted manure or compost in the autumn or spring.
Blackberries bear fruit in August and are more heat-demanding than raspberries. Thornless blackberries produce lateral shoots, which we can shorten to 2–4 leaves in the summer, or in the spring. We also cut out overly long shoots. We shorten the tops of young shoots to 2 to 2.5 m in length. We tie all the canes to a support, which should be similar to the support for grapevines.
Pruning Jostaberry
Jostaberry is most similar to black currant, so we do not shorten one-year-old wood that grows from two-year-old or older wood. There should be 5 to 6 shoots in the bush, which we replace with new ones every 5 years. We cut the old shoots at the ground.
Pruning Blueberries
We plant blueberries in acidic soil, the pH of which should be 4.5. We achieve this with acidic peat and partially with soil that we collect under coniferous trees. To maintain this soil acidity, we need to add a few liters of acidic peat or soil to each blueberry every year. After planting, we cut out damaged and weak shoots and remove the flowers so that the plant can recover. We leave 6 to 8 strong shoots in the bush, where the framework branches are for fruit growth. We remove the other shoots. After six years, we begin to replace older, degenerated shoots with new, vigorous shoots that will grow from the ground. We do not shorten one-year-old shoots because the fruiting buds are at the end of the shoots.
Pruning Figs
We prune figs very little because the wounds heal poorly. We seal the wounds with grafting wax. Before the start of growth, we can remove those buds that would produce unwanted shoots and avoid pruning. Before leafing out, we can shorten one-year-old shoots where the fig is poorly covered, thus increasing the coverage. We can also prune figs in the summer, cutting young shoots to 10 cm, thus increasing the coverage with young shoots 20 to 30 cm long. The highest-quality fruits develop on last year's wood; those on this year's wood are of lower quality and are very difficult to ripen.
Pruning Persimmon
With the warming of the climate, some fruit species are moving to the continental region, which were previously grown only on the coast. Persimmons grow poorly for several years after planting. We spread the branches of young trees and tie them in a rectangular position relative to the trunk. This is important because the wood is very brittle and breaks easily. In productivity, we shorten the branches so that the fruits are as close to the trunk as possible because the fruits break the branches at the end of the branches due to their weight. We prune drooping branches. We make sure that there is enough one-year-old wood in the crown that grows from two-year-old wood. The crowns should not be too dense; otherwise, the productivity will move to the outside of the crown.

Kiwi is a vine that requires support similar to grapevines. A special feature of this fruit species is that we need female plants for fruit production and male plants for pollination. Usually, this is in a ratio of four to one. In the autumn, we enjoy the hairy fruits, which we call kiwis. Pruning this fruit species is similar to pruning grapevines. We prune kiwis early, at least 20 days before budding; otherwise, there will be strong sap flow. After planting, we leave only one shoot, which we train as a trunk to the desired height (2 m; we prune it several times). We shorten a strong shoot, which then produces at least two shoots, which we train on both sides of the wire or on one side, thus obtaining a cordon system. In productivity, we prune one-year-old wood to 20 cm long shoots on which fruiting shoots grow. These can be up to two meters long and have 15 buds. One plant can have up to 300 well-developed fruiting buds. Thin young shoots produce poorer fruits, so we prune them out. We obtain thicker fruits also when we prune the fruiting young shoots in June behind the fourth fruit.

Z rezjo sadnega drevja dosežemo enakomerno rast in rodnost grmičevja in dreves. Lesnate rastline imajo neverjetno sposobnost regeneracije in z rezjo in odstranjevanjem starih, izrojenih vej vzpodbudimo rast novih, bolj rodnih poganjkov in s tem lepši in boljši pridelek. Rezanje oziroma obrezovanje dreves ne vpliva le na lepši spomladanski videz, ampak je to pomemben agrotehnični ukrep, s katerim dosežemo ravnotežje med rastjo poganjkov in rodnostjo ter posledično bolj umirjeno rast in kvalitetnejše sadeže.
Čas rezi
Aprila je sadno drevje tik pred cvetenjem, vendar je še pravi čas za rezanje vej, predvsem pri tistih drevesih, ki zelo bujno rastejo. Tik pred cvetenjem je v drevesni krošnji že veliko hranil, ki jih z rezjo odstranimo. S tem oslabimo oziroma umirimo drevo, ki posledično požene bolj šibke, enoletne poganjke, ki nosijo več rodnega lesa. Povedano drugače: zaradi pozne rezi bo manj zelo dolgih poganjkov na vrhu drevesa, katere vsako leto odstranjujemo. Pozna rez je zato priporočena za bujno rastoča drevesa.
Pri rezi je pomembna tudi zračna vlaga oziroma želimo čim bolj sončno in suho vreme. Ob dežju se na rane naselijo razne glivice in bakterije, ki prodirajo po prevodnih sistemih v drevo in povzročajo sušenje in propadanje vej. To se pogosto zgodi pri marelicah, zato marelice režemo v vegetaciji – v suhih dnevih pred ali po obiranju. Tudi slive režemo, ko že skoraj cvetijo. Ker slive bujno rastejo, jim z rezjo umirimo rast in zaradi pozne rezi so tudi novi poganjki nekoliko krajši. Podobno je z rezjo vrhnjega poganjka pri jablani. Prikrajšamo ga šele junija in od takrat poženejo le krajši poševni poganjki, ki v naslednjih letih niso predolgi in hitro zarodijo.
Debelejše veje pri orehih režemo v avgustu, ker je takrat v drevesu najmanj sokov, ki bi iztekali iz velike rane. Mlade orehe režemo tudi v aprilu in za preprečitev iztekanja sokov, rane zamažemo s cepilno smolo. Rezanje dreves torej ni samo enkratno spomladansko opravilo, ampak je dobro imeti škarje v roki skozi celo leto. Predvsem je potrebno izvesti še poletno rez pri breskvah, ki s svojimi novimi poganjki popolnoma prekrijejo plodove. Enoletne poganjke odstranimo tudi pri bujno rastočih jablanah in hruškah, katerih vrhnje poganjke porežemo v začetku julija in s tem omogočimo dostop soncu do plodov. Vse mora biti izvedeno z določenim občutkom – ne preveč in ne premalo. Za dobro prehrano enega jabolka potrebujemo 40 – 50 listov. V njih se izvaja fotosinteza, ki je tovarna za izgradnjo sladkorjev, ki jih potrebujejo plodovi.
Med jagodičevje spadajo rastline, ki rastejo pretežno v obliki grmov. Osnovno rez izvedemo spomladi, nekaj pa tudi v vegetaciji.
Rez črnega in rdečega ribeza
Črni ribez pri sajenju posadimo bolj globoko, da iz korenine požene več poganjkov. Prvo leto poganjke porežemo skoraj do tal in s tem vzpodbudimo rast novih, močnejših poganjkov. Pustimo le 3- 4 najmočnejše poganjke, ostale porežemo. To storimo že v poletju. V grmu črnega ribeza naj ne bo preveč poganjkov. Pri grmu v polni rodnosti naj bo vedno nekaj enoletnih poganjkov. V letošnjem letu še ne bodo rodili, vendar bodo bogato rodili v naslednjem letu. Najbolj roden les so enoletni poganjki, ki izraščajo iz dve in triletnega lesa. Na štiriletnem lesu imamo zelo kratke enoletne poganjke, zato je tudi pridelek manjši. V vitalnih grmih črnega ribeza imamo torej vsako leto ¼ enoletnih poganjkov, ¼ dvoletnih, ¼ triletnih in ¼ štiriletnih poganjkov.
Rdeči ribez sadimo podobno kot črnega in če ga ne ločimo od črnega, prelomimo vejico, oziroma zmečkamo brst, ki pri črnem ribezu takoj značilno zadiši. V grmu rdečega ribeza pustimo dva do šest poganjkov. Posamezno vejo pustimo v grmu nekoliko dalj časa, tudi do osem let, šele nato jo zamenjamo z mladim poganjkom, star poganjek pa izrežemo pri tleh. Podobno režemo tudi kosmulje, ali pa cvetoče grme kot so forzicije, vajgelije in druge. Razlika je, da pri cvetočih grmovnicah počakamo, da odcvetijo in jih nato porežemo.
Rez enkrat in dvakrat rodnih malin ter robid
Robide in maline rodijo na enoletnih poganjkih, ki zrastejo iz koreninskega vratu ali korenin. Pri enkrat rodnih malinah se po obiranju poganjek posuši, zato ga takoj odrežemo, ali pa to storimo spomladi. Poganjek ali rozgo porežemo tik nad tlemi. Porežemo tudi predrobne in pregoste poganjke, tako, da pustimo močne rozge na deset cm narazen. Če so rozge predolge, jih lahko prikrajšamo na 1,5 m dolžine. Poganjki naj bodo v vrsti, nato jih obdamo z žico ali vrvico, ki služi za oporo. Pri večkrat rodnih malinah pričakujemo pridelek nekoliko kasneje, konec julija pa vse do novembra. Enoletni, rodni poganjki se pri teh malinah ne posušijo, ampak lahko rodijo še naslednje leto. Lahko jih porežemo na 0,5 m in iz te šibe bodo spomladi hitreje pognali novi poganjki. Pridelek lahko pričakujemo kakšen teden pred tistimi, ki jih porežemo do tal. Zaradi glivične bolezni na steblih malin, se običajno stebla večkrat rodnih malin spomladi porežejo do tal in rozge odstranijo in uničijo. Iz korenin poženejo novi poganjki, ki zarodijo nekoliko kasneje, torej konec julija in rodijo vse do jesenskih ohladitev. Maline bodo zelo dobro rodile, či jih jeseni ali spomladi pognojimo z odležanim hlevskim gnojem ali kompostno zemljo.
Robide rodijo v avgustu in so toplotno bolj zahtevne od malin. Breztrne robide poženejo stranske poganjke, ki jih lahko prikrajšamo na 2- 4 liste že v poletju, sicer pa spomladi. Odrežemo tudi predolge poganjke. Vrhove mladih poganjkov prikrajšamo na 2 do 2,5 m dolžine. Vse rozge privežemo ob oporo, ki naj bo podobna opori za trto.
Rez joste
Josta je najbolj podobna črnemu ribezu, zato tudi tukaj enoletnega lesa, ki izrašča iz dveletnega ali starejšega lesa ne krajšamo. V grmu naj bo 5 do 6 poganjkov, ki jih vsakih 5 let zamenjamo z novimi. Stare poganjke izrežemo pri tleh.
Rez borovnic
Borovnice sadimo v kislo zemljo, katere pH naj bo 4,5. To dosežemo s kislo šoto in delno tudi z zemljo, ki jo naberemo pod iglavci. Da vzdržujemo to kislost tal, je potrebno vsako leto dodati nekaj litrov kisle šote ali zemlje k vsaki borovnici. Po sajenju izrežemo poškodovane in slabotne poganjke in odstranimo cvetove, da se rastlina okrepi. V grmu pustimo 6 do 8 močnih poganjkov, kjer so ogrodne veje za rast plodov. Ostale poganjke odstranimo. Po šestem letu začnemo starejše, izrojene poganjke nadomeščati z novimi, krepkimi poganjki, ki bodo pognali iz tal. Enoletnih poganjkov ne krajšamo, ker so rodni brsti na koncu poganjkov.
Rez smokev ali fig
Fige režemo zelo malo, ker se rane slabo celijo. Rane zamažemo s cepilno smolo. Pred pričetkom rasti lahko odstranimo tiste brste, ki bi pognali v neželjen poganjek in se izognemo rezi. Pred olistanjem lahko prikrajšamo enoletne poganjke tam, kjer je figa slabo obraščena in tako povečamo obraščenost. Fige lahko režemo tudi poleti, ko mladike porežemo na 10 cm in tako povečamo obraščenost z mladimi 20 do 30 cm dolgimi poganjki. Najkvalitetnejši plodovi se razvijejo na lanskem lesu, tisti na letošnjem so slabše kvalitete in zelo težko dozorijo.
Rez kakija
Z ogrevanjem podnebja, se na celinsko območje selijo nekatere sadne vrste, ki so jih včasih gojili le na Primorskem. Kaki po sajenju nekaj let slabo raste. Mladim drevesom razpiramo veje in jih vežemo v pravokoten položaj glede na deblo. To je pomembno, ker je les zelo krhek in se hitro zlomi. V rodnosti veje krajšamo, da so plodovi čim bliže deblu, kajti plodovi zaradi teže na koncu vej hitro zlomijo veje. Povešene veje spodrezujemo. Pazimo, da je v krošnji dovolj enoletnega lesa, ki izrašča iz dvoletnega. Krošnje ne smejo biti pregoste, sicer se rodnost preseli na zunanji del oziroma obod krošnje.
Rez aktinidije
Aktinidija je ovijalka, ki zahteva oporo podobno kot vinska trta. Posebnost te sadne vrste je, da potrebujemo ženske rastline za rodnost in moške rastline za opraševanje. Navadno je to v razmerju štiri proti ena. Jeseni se veselimo kosmatih plodov, ki jim rečemo kivi. Rez te sadne vrste je podobna rezi vinske trte. Aktinidijo režemo zgodaj, vsaj 20 dni pred brstenjem, sicer pride do močnega solzenja. Po sajenju pustimo le en poganjek, ki ga vzgojimo kot deblo do željene višine (2m; večkrat režemo). Tu prikrajšamo močen poganjek, ki nato požene vsaj dva poganjka, ki ju ob žici speljemo na obe strani ali le enega na eno stran in dobimo tako imenovano kordonsko vzgojo. V rodnosti enoleten les režemo na 20 cm dolge reznike na katerih zrastejo rodni poganjki. Ti so lahko dolgi tudi do dveh metrov in imajo po 15 brstov. Ena rastlina ima lahko celo 300 dobro razvitih rodnih brstov. Drobne mladike rodijo slabše plodove, zato jih pri rezi izrežemo. Debelejše plodove dobimo tudi takrat, če rodne mladike v juniju odrežemo za četrtim plodom.
Ana Ogorelec, KGZS – Zavod Ljubljana
S pomočjo literature: Marko Babnik, Sadno drevje, Kmečki glas, 1994

1. If we are concerned about what is best for the climate, we should spend money on carbon quotas instead of subsidizing expensive electric cars.
Electric cars are best for the climate, and carbon quotas do not solve the problem of emissions from vehicle traffic. If you buy a new fossil fuel car now, it will be in the car fleet for many years and will lock in the consumption of fossil fuels and greenhouse gas emissions. There is also strong evidence that the price of electric cars will decrease significantly, which further weakens the argument that carbon quotas are cheaper.

2. Electric cars require much more energy to produce than conventional cars, especially due to the batteries. Therefore, electric cars need to be driven for a longer period before they can be considered zero-emission vehicles.
The production of batteries does cause greenhouse gas emissions, but mainly because the batteries are produced in Asia and China. Even there, the mix of energy sources is becoming cleaner. Eventually, when we can produce batteries with electricity from renewable energy sources, the batteries will be emission-free.

3. Norway is part of the European electricity market. Therefore, Norwegians cannot claim that their electric cars are powered by clean Norwegian hydropower. The electricity they use is also produced from coal and gas.
However, because electricity is bought and sold, some of the electricity from wall sockets in Norway can sometimes come from coal from abroad. However, life cycle studies show that electric cars are more environmentally friendly than fossil fuel cars, regardless of the energy source mix.

4. Batteries are an environmental time bomb because they cannot be reused. Many of them end up in landfills and contribute to environmental pollution.
Electric car batteries will not end up in landfills – they are too valuable for that. Today, batteries often get a new life in the energy system to support the gradual introduction of wind and solar energy. Then, it will be worthwhile to recycle them, as they contain valuable materials.

5. The increasing number of electric cars is increasing the load on the electricity grid. To meet the demand, more poles need to be built and more powerful cables added.
The electricity grid can easily handle more electric cars, especially if we can better control when cars are charged during the day and night. Our need to strengthen the electricity grid does not come from electric cars, but from the increasing electrification in general.

6. People with electric cars stop using public transport and thus contribute to increased traffic overall.
This is not certain, but it is clear that access to bus lanes and lower tolls, as in Norway, can increase the attractiveness of using electric cars. Over time, these benefits will disappear, and then more people will choose public transport again.

7. People who buy electric cars often have more cars, so they do not contribute to reducing the number of cars.
More and more people have an electric car as their only car. There are probably some who previously had only one car and now also buy an electric car. And many who would have had two cars anyway now have an electric car as their second car. In the short term, this may result in more cars, but not necessarily more cars on the road.

8. The production of car batteries is harmful to rare and non-renewable resources, especially lithium and other precious metals. This is not sustainable.
It is not correct to say that batteries contain rare resources. Metals such as cobalt and lithium are found in many places, but there will be a shortage of them in the short term, as the needs will increase every year. However, battery manufacturers are constantly striving to reduce the use of the most expensive metals, and eventually, we will get batteries with a completely different composition than today.

9. Electric cars create more particulate matter because they are heavier and cause more wear on asphalt.
Electric cars are generally heavier than equivalent fossil fuel cars. On the other hand, electric cars do not produce particulate matter emissions or engine noise, which are major problems with fossil fuel cars.

If the energy source to power these cars is not solar cells, wind turbines, or even nuclear or hydropower plants, their CO2 emissions will be much higher. Although there is still much room for improvement, electric cars, as they are today, are generally more environmentally friendly than conventional fossil fuel cars over their life cycle, especially if they are powered by clean electricity.

3. Wasting time. You waste time writing unnecessary words, reading unnecessary words, rereading unnecessary words, and searching for key concepts.
4. They do not encourage creativity. The way of note-taking prevents the brain from connecting concepts, which inhibits creativity and weakens memory.

Advantages of thought patterns:
1. Colors. They stimulate and attract.
2. A complete, coherent whole. When you reduce the text to important and key words and enter them into a thought pattern, you get a clear and meaningfully connected overall picture of the subject matter.
3. Time-saving. Because the entire text is condensed, it saves time when writing, reading notes, and reviewing.
4. Complementary. Because thought patterns are open on all sides, they allow for continuous supplementation and updating.
5. They encourage creativity.

Rules for creating thought patterns:
1. Use emphasis:
* Start with a central image or word that focuses the eyes and brain and triggers numerous thought connections.
* Use images, as they balance your visual and verbal abilities.
* Use three or more colors for the central image, as colors stimulate memory and creativity. Using colors avoids monotony.
* Images and words should be of different sizes. The most important words should be written larger or even in three dimensions.
* Arrange the thought pattern nicely in space, so choose an appropriate size and layout of the sheet (a horizontal layout of the paper allows for more freedom and space). A good arrangement makes the image clearer, facilitates classification by levels or classes, and allows for later supplementation of the thought pattern.
2. Connect:
* Use arrows, as they automatically guide your eyes to connect parts of the thought pattern. You can use unidirectional, multidirectional, different lengths, thicknesses, and shapes.
* Use symbols. By using symbols (dashes, crosses, circles, triangles, stars, etc.), you can instantly connect different parts of the thought pattern. Symbols further strengthen and improve the classification by classes and levels.
3. Be clear:
* Use only one word for each line, as each word has multiple possible connections.
* Print all letters. Printed letters have a more distinct shape, so they are easier to read.
* Print keywords on the lines, as lines allow for order and clarity, which improves clarity and memory.
* The length of the lines should be equal to the length of the words. This allows the word to be closer to another word, which facilitates connection. At the same time, it also saves space.
* The main branches should be connected to the central image. Connecting will also help you connect your thoughts.
* The central lines should be thicker, as this will give them importance.
* The thought pattern should be clear, as this facilitates understanding and memory.
* The letters should be as vertical as possible. The inclination should not be greater than 45 degrees, as vertical letters are more legible.
4. Develop a personal style:
Thought patterns reflect the patterns in your brain, so it is important to develop your own personal style. You can opt for the 1+ rule, which means that each of your subsequent thought patterns should be more colorful, more logical, more three-dimensional, and more beautiful.

Some more suggestions:
How to strengthen a thought pattern?
* Repeatedly review thought patterns. If you need to remember a thought pattern, you need to repeat it several times, after 10–30 minutes of learning, after one day, one week, one month, three months, and after six months.
* For review, create a new thought pattern in which you summarize everything you remember from the original thought pattern. If you only review the original thought pattern, it will be just an external stimulus for the brain, reminding it of what it has already done. If you create a new thought pattern, you test what you remember without an external stimulus.

Prepare for creation:
* Establish an appropriate mood: Approach the creation of a thought pattern with a positive attitude, even if it includes things that we consider negative (an exam, a public performance, a defense). If possible, start by imitating other thought patterns, images, and works of art.
* Prepare the workspace and environment: Make your workspace pleasant (you can enhance it with some pleasant pictures). Ensure enough fresh air and natural light.

Slabosti linearnih zapiskov
1. Prikrivanje ključnih besed. Ključne besede se v zapiskih pojavljajo na različnih straneh in v množici manj pomembnih besed, kar možgane ovira pri povezovanju najpomembnejših idej.
2. Oteženo pomnenje. Enobarvni in enolični zapiski so dolgočasni, zato možgani padejo v polsen, kar preprečuje, da bi si zapomnili vsebino.
3. Zapravljanje časa. Čas zapravljate s pisanjem nepotrebnih besed, branjem nepotrebnih besed, ponovnim branjem nepotrebnih besed in iskanjem ključnih pojmov.4. Ne spodbujajo ustvarjalnosti. Način zapisovanja možganom preprečuje, da bi povezovali pojme med seboj, kar zavira ustvarjalnost in slabi pomnenje.
Prednosti miselnih vzorcev
1. Barve. Spodbujajo in privlačijo.
2. Celotna podobna snovi. Ko besedilo skrčite na pomembne in ključne besede, ki jih vpišete v miselni vzorec, dobite pregledno in smiselno povezano celotno podobo snovi.
3. Prihranek časa. Ker je celotno besedilo skrčeno, to prihrani čas pri zapisovanju, branju zapiskov in ponavljanju.
4. Dopolnjevanje. Ker so miselni vzorci odprti na vse strani, omogočajo stalno dopolnjevanje in posodabljanje.
5. Spodbujajo ustvarjalnost.
Pravila za oblikovanje miselnih vzorcev
1. Uporabljajte poudarke
* Začnite s središčno sliko ali besedo, ki osredotoči oči in možgane ter sproži številne miselne povezave.
* Uporabljajte slike, saj uravnotežijo vaše vidne in besedne sposobnosti.
* Za osrednjo sliko uporabite tri barve ali več, saj barve spodbujajo spomin in ustvarjalnost. Z uporabo barv se izognete enoličnosti.
* Slike in besede naj bodo različne velikosti. Najpomembnejše besede naj bodo napisane večje ali celo v treh razsežnostih.
* Miselni vzorec lepo razporedite po prostoru, zato izberite ustrezno velikost in postavitev lista (vodoravna postavitev papirja omogoča več svobode in prostora). Dobra razporeditev naredi sliko jasnejšo, olajša razvrstitev po stopnjah ali razredih in omogoča kasnejše dopolnjevanje miselnega vzorca.
2. Povezujte
* Uporabljajte puščice, saj te samodejno vodijo vaše oči, da povezujete dele miselnega vzorca. Lahko uporabite enosmerne, večsmerne, različne dolžine, debeline in oblike.
* Þ Uporabljajte znake. Z uporabo znakov (črtice, križci, krogci, trikotniki, zvezdice in drugo) lahko v trenutku povežete različne dele miselnega vzroca. Znaki še okrepijo in izboljšajo razvrstitev po razredih in stopnjah.
3. Bodite jasni
* Uporabljajte samo eno besedo za vsako črto, saj ima vsaka beseda več možnih povezav.
* Vse črke tiskajte. Tiskane črke imajo namreč izrazitejšo obliko, zato jih hitreje razberete.
* Ključne besede tiskajte na črtah, saj črte omogočajo urejenost in preglednost, kar izboljša jasnost in pomnenje.
* Dolžina črt naj bo enaka dolžini besed. Tako se beseda lahko približa drugi besedi, kar olajša povezovanje. Hkrati prihranite tudi prostor.
* Glavne veje naj bodo povezane z osrednjo sliko. Povezovanje vam bo pomagalo tudi pri povezovanju misli.
* Osrednje črte naj bodo debelejše, saj jim boste tako dali pomembnost.
* Miselni vzorec naj bo jasen, saj to olajša razumevanje in pomnenje.
* Črke naj bodo čim bolj pokončne. Nagib naj ne bo večji od 45 stopinj, saj so pokončne črke bolj čitljive.
4. Razvijajte osebni slog
Miselni vzorci odsevajo vzorce v vaših možganih, zato je pomembno, da razvijete svoj osebni slog. Lahko se odločite za pravilo 1+, kar pomeni, da naj bo vsak vaš naslednji miselni vzorec bolj barvit, bolj logičen, bolj tridimenzionalen in lepši.
Še nekaj predlogov
Kako okrepiti miselni vzorec?
* Ponovno pregledovanje miselnih vzorcev. Če si morate nek miselni vzorec zapomniti, ga morate večkrat ponoviti, in sicer po 10–30 minutah učenja, čez en dan, en teden, en mesec, tri mesece in čez šest mesecev.
* Za ponovitev naredite nov miselni vzorec, v katerem povzemite vse, kar se spomnite od originalnega miselnega vzorca. Če boste originalni miselni vzorec samo pregledali, bo to za možgane samo zunanji dražljaj, ki jih spomni, kaj so že naredili, če pa boste naredili nov miselni vzorec, se preizkusite, kaj se spomnite brez zunanjega dražljaja.
Pripravite se na ustvarjanje
* Vzpostavite ustrezno razpoloženje: Oblikovanja miselnega vzorca se lotite pozitivno naravnani, čeprav bo vključeval stvari, ki jih imamo za negativne (izpit, nastop v javnosti, zagovor). Če je mogoče, za začetek posnemajte druge miselne vzorce, slike in umetniška dela.
* Pripravite delovni prostor in okolje: Naj bo vaš delovni kotiček prijeten (popestri ga lahko že nekaj prijetnih slik). Zagotovite dovolj svežega zraka in naravne svetlobe.

Lidewei Vergeynst, a Belgian doctoral student from the Faculty of Biology at the University of Ghent, is researching how we can interpret the sounds that plants emit when they lack water. Lidewei has developed a method for analyzing the sounds produced by plants. She captures plant sounds using acoustic sensors attached to the plants. This allows her to determine how loudly a plant is “calling” for water.
If this is indeed the case, it is an important development in light of climate change, which is already happening and has a particularly negative impact on the agricultural sector.
The measurements are taken with an acoustic detector attached to the outside of the stem or branches of perennial plants, which detects sounds within the plant. This is similar to how doctors use a stethoscope to listen to our breathing. Under normal conditions, plants transpire water through their leaves, which they absorb through a network of tubes (veins), creating a negative pressure throughout the water system. This suction is similar to how we drink water from a glass using a straw.
Water enters the plant through the roots and flows through the cells and the space between the cells to the xylem. The xylem consists of tubes made of dead cells that are interconnected throughout the height of the plant and serve as veins for water transport. The water ends its journey in the leaves, where some of it evaporates into the air – transpiration. The other part of the water carries the products of photosynthesis and transports them throughout the plant. This part occurs through active transport in the phloem. The phloem consists of veins made of living cells that work to move water through the tree.
When plants need water, acoustic sensors can detect (hear) the noise they emit. These noises are essentially a kind of clicks. Previous similar research focused on counting these clicks. The more clicks were heard (detected), the greater the plant’s need for water. The problem was that these clicks were also heard when the plant was already completely withered (dried out). This led researchers to question this type of research.
In the current research, however, student (or rather, young researcher) Lidewei Vergeynst has made a breakthrough by analyzing these clicks in more detail. She found that these clicks are actually different and vary in the composition of their sound waves. Her supervisor, Prof. Dr. Kathy Steppe from the Laboratory of Plant Ecology at the University of Ghent, expects that this method will become a standard. The research is funded by FWO (Fonds Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek).
From the perspective of climate change, this is certainly very important news, as we will be able to detect when plants lack water, the amount of this deficiency, and even how much water is in the plants at a given time by combining different sensors. This will give us a completely new (better) insight into the process of water circulation in plants, which is essential in the current weather conditions and adapting to them.
Best regards, Blaž

Lidewei je razvila metodo za analizo zvokov, ki jih proizvedejo rastline. Rastlinske zvoke zajema preko akustičnih senzorjev, ki jih pritrdi na rastline. Na ta način, lahko ugotovi, kako glasno rastlina »kliče« po vodi.
Če je temu res tako je to pomembna novica z vidika podnebnih sprememb, ki se (na žalost) že dogajajo in imajo predvsem negativen vpliv na kmetijsko panogo.
Meritve se izvajajo z akustičnim detektorjem pritrjenim na zunanji strani stebla ali vejah trajnih rastlin, ki zaznava zvoke znotraj rastline. Podobno to počnejo zdravniki s stetoskopom, ko nam poslušajo dihanje. V normalnih razmerah, rastline transpirirajo vodo preko listov, ki jo sesajo po cevnem sistemu (žilah), tako da je celotni vodni režim v podtlaku. To sesanje je podobno, kot če mi preko slamice srkamo vodo iz kozarca.
Voda vstopa v rastlino preko koreninah in teče skozi celice in po prostoru med celicami do ksilema. Ksilem so cevčice iz odmrlih celic, ki so medsebojno povezane po vsej višini rastline in služijo kot žile za pretok vode. Voda konča svojo pot v listih, kjer je del izhlapi v zrak – transpiracija. Drugi del vode prevzame produkte fotosinteze in jih odnese po rastlini. Ta del poteka z aktivnim transportom po floemu. Floem so žile sestavljene iz živih celic, ki opravljajo delo, da premikajo vodo po drevesu.
Ko v rastlinah nastopi potreba po vodi lahko preko akustičnih senzorjev zaznamo (slišimo) hrup, ki ga ob tem rastlina oddaja. Ti hrupi so v bistvu neke vrste kliki. Vse prejšnje podobne raziskave so šle v smeri štetja teh klikov. Več kot so klikov slišali (zaznali), večja je bila potreba rastline po vodi. Problem je nastajal, da so te klike slišali tudi ko je rastlina že popolnoma propadla (se izsušila). Zaradi tega so v tovrstne raziskave raziskovalci začeli dvomiti.
Pri sedanji raziskavi, pa je študentka oz. po naše mlada raziskovalka Lidewei Vergeyst naredila preboj, ker je podrobneje analiziral te klike. Tako ugotavlja, da so ti kliki v bistvu različni in se medsebojno razlikujejo po sestavi zvočnih valovanj. Mentorica prof. dr. Kathy Steppe iz laboratorija za rastlinsko ekologijo iz Univerze Ghent, pričakuje, da bo ta metoda postala referenčna. Raziskavo financira FWO (Fonds Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek).

Tako bomo dobili povsem nov (boljši) vpogled v proces kroženja vode po rastlinah, ki je bistvenega pomena bi sedanjih vremenskih razmerah in prilagajanje na njih.

Lash is associate dean at the University of Southern California Law School. Johnson is a justice on California's Second District Court of Appeal. Lash and Johnson are co-chairs of the California Commission on Access to Justice. The full report can be viewed at (www.calbar.org). In her year-long odyssey through the California justice system, Katherine, a 35-year-old single mother with three children, experienced failure at every turn. Leaving her abusive husband, she moved into the only apartment she could afford, and soon discovered a broken toilet and non- working oven, rats and roaches, and a fourthfloor landing with no railing. She began withholding rent pending repairs her landlord refused to make, but then her Medi-Cal benefits were cut off when she could not provide rent receipts. She lost health care for her children and herself, although she is a borderline diabetic in need of medication and her children were suffering from rat bites. Katherine tried to seek help through the courts. Representing herself at an administrative hearing, she lost her appeal to restore Medi-Cal benefits because she did not have proper documentation of the rent account. When she went to a courthouse to file a complaint against her landlord, she found the process so confusing that she gave up and went home. According to "The Path to Justice: A Five-Year Status Report on Access to Justice in California," prepared by the California Commission on Access to Justice, Katherine is just one of 4.6 million poor Californians whose basic civil legal needs -- often involving such critical needs as housing, health care, education, employment, safety and transportation -- are not being addressed. California has a critical dearth of legal services for the poor, and, as this report makes clear, it is imperative that the state join with the federal government and private funders to increase resources so that all Californians, regardless of income, have equal access to our justice system. Our justice system is predicated on the assumption that both parties will be represented by lawyers who act as gatekeepers and guides through a complex legal system that would otherwise be inaccessible to many of us. Unfortunately, the most vulnerable members of our society are the least able to afford legal services. California does have a strong network of legal aid organizations that try to help meet the needs of the poor, but there's just one legal aid lawyer available per 10,000 poor people. Fever is not something abnormal. The body itself generates heat. Sometimes, we may overreact to it. We have all experienced that when we are very engaged in something, we feel warm. There are two main groups of responses to fever:

We observe the heat ratios: we can wrap warm thighs, give the child linden and elderflower tea. These two teas promote sweating, and the body cools down through sweating. A child with a fever should not be confined.
Just as anyone who has done hard work needs rest, a child needs rest after the fever subsides. This rest lasts for one day. If the child is still sick (3 to 5 days), it is advisable to follow the rest rule:
Day 1 without fever: stay in bed.
