Rumors - causes of decline, latest technologies in restoration
Hearing loss, processing techniques
The highest threshold for sound perception for human hearing is 140 decibels. This can be compared to the sound of a working jet engine. Normal conversation is between 50 and 60 decibels.
A positive background for the human ear in terms of sanitary standards is a background noise intensity of 55 decibels during the day and 40 dB at night.
Transforming sound waves into audibility
To understand the causes of hearing loss, you need to know the structure of the ear and the physical phenomenon of converting sounds into audibility.
Therefore, sound enters the human ear in the form of vibrations in the air, i.e., a sound wave. It passes through the external auditory canal and reaches the tympanic membrane, which begins to vibrate. These vibrations are transmitted to the system of auditory ossicles. This system allows for an increase in the sound pressure, which is transmitted to the system of the inner ear through the oscillatory movements of the levers of the auditory bones.
Inside the inner ear, there are sensory cells that perceive the oscillations and convert them into electrical impulses. These impulses are transmitted to the auditory nerve. From a visual perspective, it is the cochlea, and each region is responsible for a specific frequency stimulation. All this information is then transmitted to the fibers of the auditory nerve. The person perceives the sounds of the environment.
Factors affecting changes in hearing
- Hearing loss occurs when there is negative noise. The sensory cells suffer. Moreover, they do not die, but lose their function in the proper way. It has been found that young people experience hearing loss due to listening to loud music in headphones. Prolonged noise on the auditory receptor apparatus causes hearing loss.
- The presence of craniocerebral trauma, infectious diseases - meningococcal infections can cause complete deafness.
- Damage to the tympanic membrane due to cleaning the ears can also cause hearing loss.
Why is the saying correct: "The bear came to the ear"?
Everyone can develop a musical ear. This is the ability to distinguish musical information into separate components: rhythm, timbre, etc. But if a person does not use the ability to develop a musical ear, does not participate, does not practice, then such abilities are lost.
When hearing decreases, this can be understood as a state of the person. People who suffer from hearing loss spontaneously change their habits. They suddenly increase the volume on the television or ask more often. The readability of speech decreases. This is the first sign that you should be careful and undergo a hearing test. Before resorting to radical methods of fighting hearing loss, you can try special exercises at home.
According to statistics, every sixth inhabitant of our planet has reduced hearing. Among every thousand newborns, one child is born with complete deafness.
The causes of hearing loss are both congenital and acquired. Genetic predisposition can affect the development of the child. The mother transmits the disease during pregnancy: viral infections, toxic lesions, the use of antibiotics or other drugs that have toxic effects.
As a result, the child can be born completely deaf. The maternity hospital examines and detects such a pathology.
Currently, there are many hearing aids that help people with reduced hearing. But they are not always suitable. With 4th-degree deafness, the device will not help. However, there is already a new generation of devices that solve the problem by 100%.
Cochlear Implants
They consist of two parts. One part, called the internal part, is implanted into the human body: the temporal bone or the head. The other part is external. This is a sound or speech processor. It is worn directly on the ear using special fastening elements. A special magnet attaches this part to the implant of the internal part.
Classical hearing aids only amplify sound, like loudspeakers. Cochlear implants are a converter of audio signals into electricity, which is transmitted through the auditory nerve to the auditory cortex in the brain.
The internal part of the device does not require replacement for 90 years. The external part is adjusted, and the battery in the device is changed. The installation is performed by a surgeon. The implantation operation is a high-tech procedure and is performed according to special state quotas. The state allocates quotas, and they can be used by everyone who needs them. The operation itself will cost one million rubles.
For the purpose of prevention, follow simple instructions and maintain your hearing.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

On November 1, 2005, the United Nations General Assembly, during its session, declared January 27 as the International Day of Commemoration in Memory of the Victims of the Holocaust with resolution 60/7. On this day in 1945, the Russian army liberated the largest concentration camp, Auschwitz-Birkenau, in Poland. However, it wasn't until 2012 that Germany erected a monument in Berlin to commemorate the Roma and Sinti people who were victims of the Nazi Holocaust.

Historians and theorists debate whether the Nazis truly perpetrated a Holocaust against the Roma and Sinti. H. Friedlander believes that the Roma were victims of the Holocaust, while G. Lewy argues that we cannot speak of a Holocaust in the case of the Roma and Sinti, as the Nazis had been persecuting the Roma long before, even before World War I. The Nazi mechanism was primarily intended for the extermination of Jews, and the Roma were only included in the Nazi killing machine by chance.

What does the term "Holocaust" actually mean? The term "Holocaust" originates from Greek: λόκαυστος (holókaustos), consisting of two parts: hólos (whole) and kaustós (burnt), and literally means the complete burning of a specific ethnic, racial, or national group. Historical sources report that on December 16, 1942, Heinrich Himmler ordered the deportation of all Roma living within the Third Reich with the so-called Auschwitz Decree, which demanded the complete destruction of the ethnic minorities of Sinti and Roma. To deny that a Holocaust was perpetrated against the Roma and Sinti under the pretext that the killings were not planned is a reflection of tasteless arrogance.

From Antisemitism to Porajmos

The seeds of the later Nazi persecution of Roma and Sinti date back to the late 19th century. As Mag. Rinaldo Diriccardi states in his scientific monograph, "Even God Turned Away from the Roma/Gypsies" (2011, 65-75), the Swabian parliament organized a conference called "Das Zigeunergeschmeiss" (The Gypsy Mess) in 1890. At that time, the general practice of warning with church bells when citizens noticed Gypsies entering the city was also established. Later, in 1899, Alfred Dillmann founded the "Nachrichtendienst in Bezug auf die Zigeuner" (Information Service Regarding the Gypsies) in Munich. This was the first register that recorded the Roma population, containing names, surnames, fingerprints, photographs, and records of criminal acts. In 1905, Dillmann's register evolved into the "Zigeuner Buch" (Gypsy Book), which was used in Germany until 1970. Dillmann's book contained 3 chapters with explanations and arguments as to why it was necessary to monitor the Roma. One of the arguments was that the German people suffered too much from the "Gypsy stench," so the Roma needed to be separated from the German population. Later, in 1933, the Nazi party adopted the Law on Eugenics and Sterilization, which primarily targeted the Roma. In January 1934, German Sinti and Roma were deported to the concentration camps of Dachau, Dieselstrasse, Sachenhausen, Marzahn, and Vennhausen, where they were subjected to sterilization and castration experiments. In 1941, Himmler devised criteria for determining racial purity for the Roma, proposing that the Roma's genealogy be researched up to three generations and classified according to the criteria: pure Gypsy, more than half Gypsy, less than half Gypsy, and non-Gypsy. In 1941, the Independent State of Croatia opened the first concentration camp in Croatia in Jasenovac. On November 15, 1943, Himmler officially equated the Roma with the Jews.

The number of Roma and Sinti killed during the genocide is unknown. Sources cite slightly over half a million, but the number is likely higher, as, for example, the Kingdom of Yugoslavia did not keep records of members of the Roma community.

Why did the world turn its back on the Roma?

Unlike the Jews, the Roma did not possess any capital, so they did not have as much political influence, and they had no one to report the "Porajmos," the Holocaust that was perpetrated against them, as they were never even listened to. The Roma did not even have a state that would accept them after the war, protect them, and safeguard them. After the war, German officials concluded that the Nazis had followed the laws that were in force before the war, enacted to sanction criminals and thieves, and that some Gypsies had been killed in the process, which was justified because they had earned it with their criminal acts. Discrimination against the Roma thus deepened, and the exclusion of the Roma was reinforced, as this attitude towards the Roma was practiced throughout Europe, which had been enacting anti-Roma laws since the 15th century (whipping, hanging, persecution). In 1554, England even passed a law that considered every Roma unconditionally guilty, simply because they were Roma. After World War II, the Roma were certainly betrayed, denied, and ostracized. And what about today?

Under the pretext of the Declaration of Human Rights, the situation in the field of Roma issues is supposedly improving, but only on paper. Haris Tahirović, delegate of ERTF, president of the Anglunipe – RIC association, and president of the Umbrella – Association of Roma Communities of Slovenia, points out a phenomenon he calls the "Roma industry." As much as the Roma were discredited after World War II, they are now being exploited in a more sophisticated way – and capital is again key. "The Roma in Europe are what the Native Americans are in the United States. First, they were killed, and then they were saved – of course, with the aim of profiting from them."

Generalna skupščina Združenih narodov je 1. novembra 2005 na svojem zasedanju z resolucijo 60/7 proglasila 27. januar za Svetovni dan spomina na žrtve holokavsta. Tega dne, leta 1945, je namreč Ruska armada osvobodila največje koncentracijsko taborišče Auschwitz-Birkenau na Poljskem. Šele leta 2012 pa se je Nemčija v Berlinu s spomenikom poklonila tudi Romom in Sintom, ki so bili žrtve nacističnega holokavsta.
Zgodovinarji in teoretiki polemizirajo ali se je nad Romi in Sinti res vršil nacistični holokavst. H. Friedlander meni, da so Romi bili žrtve holokavsta, medtem ko G. Lewy opominja, da v primeru Romov in Sintov ne moremo govoriti o holokavstu, saj so Cigane nacisti preganjali že veliko prej, še pred 1. svetovno vojno, nacistični mehanizem pa je bil namenjen iztrebljanju Judov; v nacistični morilski stroj so Rome vključevali zgolj po naključju.
Kaj pravzaprav pomeni holokavst? Izraz holokavst je izvorno grški: λόκαυστος (holókaustos), sestoji iz dveh členov, t.j. hólos (celota) in kaustós (zažgan), pomeni pa dobesedno celoten zažig določene etnične, rasne ali narodnostne skupine. Zgodovinski viri poročajo, da je 16.12.1942 Heinrich Himmler ukazal deportacijo vseh Ciganov, bivajočih znotraj Tretjega Rajha, s t.i. Auschwitz-dekretom, ki je zahteval popolno uničenje etničnih manjšin Sintov in Romov. Zanikati, da se je nad Romi in Sinti vršil holokavst pod pretvezo, da poboj ni bil načrtovan, je odraz neokusne arogance.
Od antisemitizma do porrajmosa
Zametki kasnejšega nacističnega poboja Romov in Sintov segajo že v konec 19. stoletja. Kot navaja mag. Rinaldo Diriccardi v znanstveni monografiji Tudi Bog je umaknil svoj pogled od Ciganov/Romov (2011, 65-75) je švabski parlament leta 1890 organiziral konferenco Das Zigeunergeschmeiss (Ciganski mrčes), takrat se je tudi uveljavila splošna praksa opozarjanja s cerkvenimi zvonovi, ko bi meščani opazili, da v mesto prihajajo Cigani. Kasneje, leta 1899, je Alfred Dillmann v Münchnu ustanovil Nachrichtendienst in Bezug auf die Zigeuner (Obveščevalno – podatkovno službo, v zvezi s Cigani). To je bil prvi register, ki je popisoval Romsko populacijo – vseboval je tako imena in priimke, prstne odtise Ciganov, njihove fotografije, popis kriminalnih dejanj idr. Leta 1905 je Dillmanov register prerasel v Zigeuner Buch (Cigansko knjigo), ki je bila v Nemčiji v uporabi vse do leta 1970. Dillmanova knjiga je vsebovala 3 poglavja z razlagami in argumenti, zakaj je potreben nadzor nad Cigani; eden izmed navedenih argumentov je ta, da nemški narod preveč trpi zaradi ciganskega smradu, zato je Cigane treba ločiti od nemške populacije. Kasneje, leta 1933, je nacistična stranka sprejela Zakon o evgeniki in sterilizaciji; z zakonom so apelirali predvsem na Cigane. Januarja 1934 nemške Sinte in Rome deportirajo v koncentracijska taborišča Dachau, Dieselstrasse, Sachenhausen, Marzahn in Vennhausen in na njih izvajajo poskuse sterilizacije in kastracije. Leta 1941 Himmler izumi kriterije za označevanje rasne čistosti za Cigane; predlaga, da se Cigana genealoško razišče do treh generacij in se ga klasificira po kriterijih: za čistega Cigana, za več kot pol Cigana, za manj kot pol Cigana, za Ne-Cigana. Leta 1941 NDH odpre prvo koncentracijsko taborišče na Hrvaškem v Jasenovcu. 15. novembra 1943 Himmler Rome tudi uradno izenači z Judi.
Število med genocidom pobitih Romov in Sintov ni znano. Viri navajajo nekaj čez pol milijona pobitih, vendar je številka verjetno višja, saj na primer Kraljevina Jugoslavija ni vodila evidence pripadnikov romske skupnosti.
Zakaj je svet obrnil hrbet Romom?
Romi za razliko od Judov niso posedovali nikakršnega kapitala, zato tudi niso imeli tako močne politične veljave in o porrajmosu kot so sami poimenovali holokavst, ki se je vršil nad njimi, niso imeli nikomur poročati, saj jih nikoli niti ni bil noben pripravljen poslušati. Romi niso imeli niti države, ki bi jih po vojni sprejela, jih zaščitila in obvarovala. »Romsko vprašanje« so nemški uradniki po vojni pripeljali celo do zaključka, da so nacisti sledili zakonom, ki so bili v veljavi še pred vojno, uzakonjeni z namenom sankcioniranja kriminalcev in lopovov, med izvajanjem zakonov pa je kakšen izmed Ciganov bil tudi ubit in to po pravici, saj si je to s svojimi kriminalnimi dejanji tudi zaslužil. Diskriminacija nad Romi se je tako še poglabljala, izključevanje Romov se je utrjevalo, saj je bil takšen odnos do Romov v praksi po vsej Evropi, ki je izvajala proti-romske zakone že vse od 15. stoletja naprej (bičanje, obešanje, preganjanje). 1554 je v Angliji bil celo sprejet zakon, ki je vsakega Roma brezpogojno smatral za krivega, samo zato, ker je bil Rom. Po 2. svetovni vojni so Romi vsekakor bili izdani, zanikani, izobčeni. In kako je danes?
Pod pretvezo Deklaracije o človekovih pravicah se stanje na področju romske problematike bojda izboljšuje, vendar zgolj na papirju. Delegat ERTF, predsednik Društva Anglunipe – RIC in predsednik Zveze Romske skupnosti Slovenije Umbrella – Dežnik, Haris Tahirović, opozarja na pojav, ki ga imenuje »romska industrija«. Kolikor se je Rome po 2. svetovni vojni diskreditiralo, se jih danes – in znova je tukaj ključnega pomena kapital – posiljuje na bolj prefinjen način. »Romi v Evropi so tisto, kar so Indijanci v ZDA. Najprej se jih je pobijalo, potem pa reševalo – seveda z namenom okoriščanja na njihov račun.«

The first roots took hold in American soil.
Common sunflowers originate from North America. Native Americans cultivated them more than 3,000 years ago for the production of medicines, oil, and food. Thanks to them, sunflowers today have a tall stem with a single large flower – although initially, they had multiple flowers on the stem. In the 16th century, the Spanish brought the common sunflower to Europe, where it quickly became popular due to its beauty and usefulness. By the 19th century, sunflowers were grown on an area of more than 8,000 square kilometers in Russia. To this day, it is considered the country with the largest area of sunflowers planted.
If you would like to plant a common sunflower yourself, the process is very simple – all you need is a sunflower seed.
Sunflower seeds are beneficial for health.
Sunflower seeds are a popular snack. They are recommended because they do not cause allergies (note: sunflower pollen does cause allergies). They contain protein, potassium, magnesium, calcium, iron, and vitamin E.
Sunlight is essential.
Their name was not chosen by chance: sunflowers need sunlight to thrive. They need six to eight hours of sun each day. The flowers turn towards the sun from east to west, and at night or early in the morning, they turn towards the east.
An inflorescence of over 1000 flowers.
The appearance of sunflowers is deceiving – a single flower consists of 1,000 to 2,000 smaller flowers. The ray and tubular flowers of the sunflower are grouped together in an inflorescence called a head. There are 500 to 1,000 flowers in the head. First, the flowers on the edge of the head bloom, and finally, the center of the head blooms. The sunflower blooms in spiral circles from the outside to the inside. All the flowers in one head bloom in 7 to 10 days.
The sunflower is a nectar-rich plant. Its large flowers are very attractive to bees and represent an important source of bee forage. The main pollinators are bees, bumblebees, and wasps.
A muse for artists.
Sunflowers have been and still are a source of inspiration for many painters. Vincent van Gogh was one of the most famous painters who depicted them repeatedly in his works. They also inspired the creators of the popular video game Minecraft and the film Spiderman.

Navadne sončnice izvirajo iz Severne Amerike. Indijanci so jih pred več kot 3000 let pred našim štetjem že gojili za proizvodnjo zdravil, olja in hrane. Prav z njihovo pomočjo imajo sončnice danes visoko steblo in na njem en velik cvet – sicer so sprva imele na steblu več cvetov. V 16. stoletju so Španci navadno sončnico prinesli v Evropo, kjer so takoj postale priljubljene zaradi svoje lepote in uporabnosti. Do 19. stoletja so v Rusiji sončnice sadili na več kot 8000 kvadratnih kilometrih veliki površini. Še danes veljajo za državo, ki ima posajenih največ sončnic.
Če bi navadno sončnico radi posadili sami, je postopek zelo enostaven – vse, kar potrebujete, je sončnično seme.
Sončnična semena koristijo zdravju
Sončnična semena (rožke) so priljubljen prigrizek. Priporočajo jih, ker ne povzročajo alergij (pozor: cvetnih prah sončnic pa povzroča alergije). Vsebujejo proteine, kalij, magnezij, kalcij, železo in vitamin E.

Njihovo ime ni bilo izbrano po naključju: sončnice potrebujejo sončno svetlobo, da uspevajo. Vsak dan potrebujejo od šest do osem ur sonca. Cvetovi se obračajo v smeri sonca od vzhoda proti zahodu, ponoči ali zgodaj zjutraj se obrnejo na vzhod.
Socvetje več 1000 cvetov
Videz sončnic vara – en cvet je sestavljen iz 1000 do 2000 manjših cvetov. Jezičasti in cevasti cvetovi sončnice so združeni v socvetje, ki ga imenujemo košek. Vseh cvetov v košku je od 500 do 1000. Najprej cvetijo cvetovi na obodu koška, na koncu zacveti še sredina koška. Sončnica cveti v spiralnih krogih od zunanjega proti notranjemu. Vsi cvetovi ene glave odcvetijo v 7 do 10 dneh.
Sončnica je medovita rastlina. Njeni veliki cvetovi so izredno privlačni za čebele in predstavljajo pomemben vir čebelje paše. Glavni opraševalci so čebele, čmrlji in ose.
Muze za umetnike
Sončnice so bile in še vedno so vir navdiha za številne slikarje. Vincent Van Gogh je bil eden izmed najbolj slavnih slikarjev, ki jih je večkrat upodobil v svojih umetninah. Navdihnile so tudi ustvarjalce priljubljene videoigre Minecraft in filma Spiderman.

Sugar causes cravings for sweets.
The more sugar you eat, the more you will crave it. A meal high in sugar raises blood glucose levels, which triggers the release of insulin. The added insulin causes cravings for even more sugar, leading to new fluctuations.
Sensitivity to sugar
It has been proven that some people are more sensitive to sugar, meaning that sugar directly affects their behavior. Children are particularly sensitive, with younger children being more affected than older ones (as stated by Dr. Keith Conners in the book Feeding the Brain). This may be related to the fact that the brain develops very rapidly during preschool years, and therefore the effects of sugar on behavior and learning ability are greater in children.
Proven: Sugar affects children's learning abilities and behavior
Researchers offered preschool children a drink high in sugar and compared their behavior to children who drank an unsweetened drink. The children in the group who drank the sweetened drink had more difficulty solving tasks and were also more restless. The more sugar children consume, the less their ability to concentrate and learn.
In children, the increase in adrenaline after consuming sugar is greater and lasts longer than in adults. After consuming sugar, activity increases in both hyperactive and normal children, but hyperactive children also become more aggressive. A meal high in sugar also increases the release of the stress hormone cortisol, which plays a crucial role in regulating blood sugar. High levels of adrenaline or low blood sugar levels cause abnormal behavior.
Sugar – a toxin that causes alcohol intoxication
Sugar is the favorite food of parasites and fungi that poison us with aflatoxins. In the process of sugar metabolism, fermentation occurs, producing alcohol, which is a toxin for brain cells. Alcohol also causes dehydration – without water, the brain cannot function properly, as it contains 80 to 90% water.
Today, it is much more difficult to control the amount of sugar consumed than in the past, as sugar is added to products where you would not expect it. Sugar is a cheap "filler" that increases the volume or weight of the product. It greatly improves the taste of food that would otherwise taste like cardboard, along with other potentially harmful additives. This significantly increases the manufacturer's profit.
If we want to know how much sugar is in our diet, we need to get used to carefully checking the labels on products, eating as few ready-made meals as possible, and preparing as many meals as possible ourselves from basic ingredients.
Appropriate size and composition of children's meals
Children are two, three, or four times lighter than adults, so the amount of food should also be correspondingly smaller. We should not forget this when preparing meals, especially when it comes to the amount of sweets and other foods that contain sugar (e.g., fresh or dried fruit).
Unfortunately, children's breakfasts are often full of simple and complex carbohydrates. Various ready-made breakfast cereals contain large amounts of sugar and complex carbohydrates, which are converted into sugar in the body, so they are not the best choice. Brown sugar is only slightly better than white sugar, and fructose, fruit sugar, honey, or maple syrup also cause the same response in the body.
Adding protein to the diet and reducing sugar intake alleviates behavioral and learning problems, so it is very important that each meal is balanced. This is especially true for breakfast, which is the most important meal of the day. You can read more about what modern nutrition should be like in the article Modern Nutritional Pyramid.

Občutljivost na sladkor
Dokazano je, da so nekateri ljudje bolj občutljivi na sladkor, kar pomeni, da sladkor neposredno vpliva na njihovo vedenje. Še posebej občutljivi so otroci, mlajši bolj kot starejši (kot navaja Dr. Keith Conners v knjigi Feeding the Brain). To je lahko povezano z dejstvom, da se možgani v predšolski dobi zelo hitro razvijajo in so zato tudi vplivi sladkorja na vedenje in sposobnost učenja pri otrocih toliko večji.
Dokazano: sladkor vpliva na učne sposobnosti in vedenje otrok
Raziskovalci so predšolskim otrokom ponudili pijačo z velikim deležem sladkorja in njihovo vedenje primerjali z otroci, ki so popili nesladkano pijačo. Otroci v skupini, ki je spila sladkano pijačo, so imeli pri reševanju nalog več težav, bili pa so tudi bolj nemirni. Več ko otroci zaužijejo sladkorja, manjša je njihova sposobnost koncentracije in učenja.
Pri otrocih je dvig adrenalina po zaužitem sladkorju večji in traja dlje časa, kot pri odraslih. Po zaužitju sladkorja se poveča aktivnost tako pri hiperaktivnih kot pri normalnih otrocih, vendar hiperaktivni otroci postanejo tudi bolj agresivni. Zaradi obroka z veliko sladkorja se poveča tudi izločanje stresnega hormona kortizola, ki ima odločilno vlogo pri uravnavanju krvnega sladkorja. Visok nivo adrenalina ali nizek nivo sladkorja v krvi pa povzročita nenormalno vedenje.
Sladkor – strup, ki povzroča alkoholno omamo
Sladkor je najljubša hrana parazitov in glivic, ki nas zastrupljajo z aflatoksini. V procesu presnove sladkorja pride do vretja, pri čemer nastaja alkohol, ki je strup za možganske celice. Alkohol povzroča tudi dehidriranost – brez vode pa možgani ne morejo dobro delovati, saj vsebujejo kar od 80 do 90 % vode.
Količino zaužitega sladkorja je danes veliko težje nadzorovati, kot nekoč, saj sladkor dodajajo tudi v izdelke, kjer ga sploh ne bi pričakovali. Sladkor je ceneno »mašilo«, ki poveča volumen oziroma težo izdelka. Hrani, ki bi sicer imela okus po kartonu, skupaj z drugimi potencialno škodljivimi aditivi močno izboljša okus. Dobiček proizvajalca je tako precej večji.
Če želimo vedeti, koliko sladkorja je v naši prehrani, se moramo navaditi dobro pregledovati deklaracije na izdelkih, uživati čim manj že pripravljenih obrokov in čim več obrokov pripraviti sami iz osnovnih živil.
Primerna velikost in sestava otroških obrokov
Otroci so dva-, tri- ali štirikrat lažji od odraslih ljudi, zato mora biti tudi količina hrane ustrezno manjša. Na to dejstvo ne bi smeli pozabiti pri obrokih, še posebej pa ne pri količini sladkarij in drugih živil, ki vsebujejo sladkor (npr. sveže ali suho sadje).
Otroški zajtrki so žal velikokrat polni enostavnih in sestavljenih ogljikovih hidratov. Različni že pripravljeni kosmiči za zajtrk vsebujejo velike količine sladkorja in sestavljenih ogljikovih hidratov, ki se v telesu spremenijo v sladkor, zato niso najboljša izbira. Rjavi sladkor je le za odtenek boljši od belega, pa tudi fruktoza, sadni sladkor, med ali javorjev sirup v telesu povzročijo povsem enak odziv.
Dodajanje beljakovin v prehrano in izločanje sladkorja omili vedenjske in učne težave, zato je zelo pomembno, da je vsak obrok uravnotežen. Še zlasti to velja za zajtrk kot najpomembnejši obrok dneva. Še več o tem, kakšna naj bo sodobna prehrana, lahko preberete v članku Sodobna prehranska piramida.

Animal bites can cause a fatal disease – rabies.
A dangerous infectious disease that is very painful and debilitating.
Rabies is an infectious disease that affects the nervous system, not just the central nervous system, but also the peripheral nervous system. The disease has been known since ancient times; it was even described as hydrophobia in the 5th century BC.
The pathogen is transmitted through the saliva of animals, so the source of infection can be not only a bite but also contact with saliva. After entering the bloodstream, the virus spreads throughout the body and affects the entire nervous system. The sources of the disease are domestic and wild animals.
Rabies is a particularly dangerous infection because, after the first symptoms appear, the outcome is fatal. It is listed alongside polio and the human immunodeficiency virus.
Incubation period:
The duration ranges from 10 to 90 days, and in some cases, up to one year. The time of symptom manifestation depends on the location of the infection; the further it is from the brain, the longer the incubation period.
Stages of the disease:
- Depression stage (initial) – Clinical symptoms are common; the wound is already healed, with pain and a burning sensation. The temperature remains low. The first symptoms of nervous system dysfunction are evident: vague fear, possible increased irritability, loss of sleep, and anxiety. This stage lasts about three days. All symptoms are accompanied by an increased heart rate and a feeling of chest tightness.
- Excitement stage – The first signs of hydrophobia (water aversion) appear; the patient cannot drink water due to muscle spasms in the throat. Breathing becomes noisy. Seizures are triggered by any stimulus, leading to aerophobia (fear of wind), photophobia (fear of light), and acousticophobia (fear of loud noises). The pupils dilate, and vision becomes blurred. Tachycardia, excessive salivation, and sweating occur. The patient becomes nervous and may spit, bite, or fight. Consciousness is clouded. The patient may occasionally have moments of lucidity, assess the situation, and answer questions rationally. If death does not occur within three days of the onset of this stage, facial and limb paralysis develops.
- Paralysis stage – Motor and sensory functions are impaired. The fear of water and seizures subside. People often think the patient's condition is improving, but this is actually the first sign of approaching death. The body temperature rises to 42 degrees Celsius. Death occurs within 10 to 20 hours due to paralysis of the heart or respiratory muscles.
Diagnosis:
The virus can be diagnosed by isolating it from cerebrospinal fluid or saliva, but this process is lengthy and expensive, and it is rarely used in clinical medicine.
The main criteria are:
- Epidemiological history (animal bite or contact with saliva on mucous membranes);
- Clinical picture (signs of the initial stage and the stage of dysfunction).
After death, the patient's brain is examined for Negri bodies to confirm the cause of death.
Treatment:
Currently, there is no cure for rabies. The patient is isolated and provided with the most comfortable conditions, and sources of air currents, light, water, and noise are eliminated. Symptomatic treatment is used. The outcome is always fatal.
Prevention:
The primary prevention measure is the destruction of infected animals, which reduces the likelihood of bites from wild animals. Cattle are vaccinated. Farmers, veterinarians, and others receive planned immunization with the rabies vaccine.
When an animal bites, the wound is washed and treated with an antiseptic. A course of preventive rabies vaccination is administered to prevent the virus from spreading throughout the body.
In 2005, Dr. Rodney Wylloba in the United States successfully treated a case of rabies, but according to statistics, this has only been achieved in 1000 cases.

Role in Nature
Like all organisms, the nandu has a very special place in the food web.
By consuming plants, they promote their growth and seed production, and they also act as important dispersers, providing seeds with “free transport” to more distant locations. For plant species, dispersal to new locations is extremely important, as this prevents young plants from competing with their “parents” for nutrients and space, and it also ensures greater genetic diversity for new generations. Nandus thus limit their numbers, prevent excessive population growth, and the associated spread of various diseases.
Occasional Scavengers
They occasionally eat carrion and act as environmental cleaners. As the largest bird in South America, capable of delivering very strong and painful kicks, the nandu is protected from most predators, but it still sometimes becomes prey for pumas or jaguars. Their nests with eggs are an important food source for some lizards, maned wolves, forest dogs, opossums, and some birds of prey.
Causes of Endangerment
The cause of the nandu’s endangerment is humans.
The population status of nandus in the wild is difficult to assess due to escaped individuals from captivity. Their numbers have declined significantly in recent decades, which scientists attribute to excessive hunting, as nandus are a desirable prey both for their meat and their leather. The collection of eggs from nests also poses a serious threat. In 1980, as many as 50,000 nandu skins were exported from Paraguay, mainly to Japan and the United States.
Due to the rapid decline in numbers, nandus are considered a potentially endangered species that will likely become vulnerable soon without additional measures.
Habitat Loss and Fragmentation
They are also threatened by habitat loss and fragmentation. Many areas suitable for nandus have been converted into fields and fenced pastures for livestock in recent decades. In some places, large areas have been burned, resulting in the death of many animals. Because farmers perceive nandus as pests, this creates additional pressure on their population.
How Can You Help?
Be an Eco-Traveler
When traveling, check what you are buying to ensure that souvenirs do not contain animal parts (skin, teeth, claws, bile, etc.). Even if some animal species are not yet endangered, the widespread sale of their body parts for souvenirs causes this to happen.
Nandus are listed in Appendix II of the international CITES agreement, which restricts trade in their products. Additional measures are also being prepared to enable the conservation of their habitat and better restrict hunting. Learn more about the CITES convention.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

Considering the indifference that cats often display towards their owners, one might wonder how well they actually see. But putting that aside, the question of what the world looks like through a cat's eyes is still an interesting one. And when we answer it, we see that cats see some things worse than we do, but in certain cases, they actually see better.
Their field of vision is 20 degrees wider than ours, as human eyes capture 180 degrees, while cats capture 200, but cats are limited when it comes to observing distant objects. Things that humans can see clearly at a distance of up to 60 meters become problematic for cats after just six meters, as they receive a blurred image instead of a sharp one. However, they perform better when viewing in the dark and in terms of eye responsiveness to rapidly moving objects or animals. A significant difference between humans and cats also lies in which colors they perceive. In the past, scientists assumed that cats could only see two colors, but that's not entirely true. They are indeed most sensitive to blue-violet and yellow hues, but they can also see some shades of green, while they don't perceive red at all.
Ultraviolet Signaling
Compared to cats, dogs see even fewer colors, as they only perceive blue and yellow, but not red and green, which means they have the same problem as humans with color blindness. However, they have a much better sense of smell and a much wider peripheral vision than humans, exceeding ours by 60 degrees. But when it comes to colors, we certainly can't compete with tetrachromatic birds, which can see ultraviolet in addition to red, green, and blue, or with bees, which don't see red but can perceive orange and yellow, as well as ultraviolet, which is important for their honey gathering. Ultraviolet colors and patterns on the flower's pollen communicate to bees how full it is with nectar, and also serve as a signal for them to land on the flower. A butterfly's eye is made up of 12,000 "micro-eyes" called ommatidia, which together form a single image of what the butterfly is looking at, and they perceive red, green, blue, and ultraviolet, as well as shades of red, albeit less well. A butterfly's image is much less sharp than a human's, so at a distance of 50 centimeters, it will barely notice a coin, but this doesn't prevent it from hitting the pollen.
An Eye for Depth
The most complex vision among animals is found in mantis shrimp, which have up to 16 photoreceptors, and these also perceive ultraviolet and polarized light. With one of its eyes, it can also perceive depth, and the eyes can move independently of each other. In addition to the aforementioned species of crustaceans, scarab beetles and bats can also see polarized light, and bats have another interesting feature, as they use sound instead of sight for their orientation. When they fly, they constantly emit high-frequency tones that only they can hear, and the sound waves that are created are reflected off obstacles, even if it's just an insect, and return to the bat, which then orients itself during flight based on them.

Ob brezbrižnosti, ki jo mačke večino časa izkazujejo svojim lastnikom, bi se človek lahko vprašal, kako dobro nas sploh vidijo. A šalo na stran, vprašanje, kako je svet videti skozi mačje oči, vseeno ni nezanimivo. In ko nanj odgovorimo, vidimo, da mačke nekatere stvari res vidijo slabše od nas, v določenih primerih pa jim gre bolje.
Njihovo vidno polje je za 20 stopinj širše od našega, saj človeške oči zajamejo 180 stopinj, mačje pa 200, so pa mačke prikrajšane pri opazovanju oddaljenih predmetov. Stvari, ki jih bodo ljudje dobro videli na razdalji do 60 metrov, mačkam delajo težave že po šestih metrih, saj namesto ostre slike dobijo zamegljeno podobo, se pa zato bolje odrežejo pri gledanju v temi in odzivnosti oči ob hitrem premikanju predmetov ali živali, ki jo gledajo. Pomembna razlika med ljudmi in mačkami je tudi v tem, katere barve zaznajo slednje. V preteklosti so znanstveniki domnevali, da mačke vidijo samo dve barvi, vendar ni čisto tako. Najobčutljivejše so sicer res za modro-vijolične in rumene odtenke, vendar vidijo tudi nekoliko zelene barve, medtem ko rdeče sploh ne zaznajo.
Ultravijolična signalizacija
Psi v primerjavi z mačkami vidijo še manj barvito, saj zaznavajo le modro in rumeno, ne pa rdeče in zelene, kar pomeni, da imajo enak problem kot ljudje z barvno slepoto. Imajo pa zato toliko boljši nos pa tudi veliko širši periferni vid od ljudi, saj ga presegajo za 60 stopinj. Se pa pri barvah zagotovo ne moremo kosati s tetrakromatičnimi pticami, ki poleg rdeče, zelene in modre lahko vidijo tudi ultravijolično, ali čebelami, ki sicer ne vidijo rdeče, zaznajo pa oranžno in rumeno ter ultravijolično, ki je pomembna pri njihovem pridobivanju medu. Ultravijolične barve in vzorci na prašniku cveta namreč sporočajo čebelam, kako polni so nektarja, obenem pa delujejo tudi kot signalizacija za njihovo pristajanje na cvetlici. Oči metulja so sestavljene iz po 12.000 »mikroočes« omatidijev, ki skupno sestavljajo eno sliko tega, kar metulj gleda, zaznavajo pa rdečo, zeleno, modro in ultravijolično pa tudi odtenke rdeče, le da slabše. Metuljeva slika je sicer veliko manj ostra od človeške, tako da bo na 50-centimetrski razdalji komaj opazil kovanec, ga pa to vseeno ne ovira tako, da ne bi zadel prašnika.
Oko za globino
Najkompleksnejši vid med živalmi imajo morske bogomolke, ki imajo do 16 fotoreceptorjev, ti pa zaznavajo tudi ultravijolično in polarizirano svetlobo. Z enim od očes lahko zaznavajo tudi globino, sicer pa oči lahko premikajo samostojno oziroma neodvisno drugo od drugega. Polarizirano svetlobo poleg omenjene vrste rakov med drugim vidijo tudi hrošči skarabeji in netopirji, ki imajo še eno zanimivo lastnost, saj namesto vida za svoje lociranje uporabljajo zvok. Ko letijo, tako nenehno spuščajo visokofrekvenčne tone, ki jih slišijo samo oni, zvočni valovi, ki pri tem nastanejo, pa se, ko naletijo na oviro, četudi gre samo za žuželko, odbijejo od nje in se vrnejo k netopirju, ki se pri letenju nato orientira po njih.

Upoštevaj kontekst, idiome in kulturne reference. Ne dodajaj nobenih dodatnih informacij ali komentarjev, samo prevod.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

While modern fruits and vegetables are increasingly beautiful, larger, more colorful, and shinier, they are simultaneously becoming emptier in terms of the nutrients we need for good health. They are increasingly filled with – especially fruits – only sugar, which is an additional drawback.
We would be exaggerating if we said that the carrots you eat today contain almost no nutrients – but they certainly contain significantly fewer than, for example, 50 years ago.
Fruits and vegetables grown decades ago were incomparably richer in vitamins and minerals than they are today. The main culprit for this worrying trend is soil depletion: modern intensive farming methods are removing more and more nutrients from the soil in which the food we eat grows.
Increasingly beautiful – and increasingly worse
While modern fruits and vegetables are increasingly beautiful, larger, more colorful, and shinier, they are simultaneously becoming emptier in terms of the nutrients we need for good health. They are increasingly filled with – especially fruits – only sugar, which is an additional drawback.
This means that each successive generation of fruits and vegetables is actually less beneficial to you than the previous one (and, with the possible use of pesticides, also more harmful).
“The decline in nutrients means that our bodies have fewer of the components they need to defend against chronic diseases – this will reduce the value of food as preventive medicine,” says David R. Montgomery, a professor of geomorfology at the University of Washington in Seattle and co-author of the book What Your Food Ate with Anne Biklé.
Concerning data from studies
A groundbreaking study on this topic was published in December 2004 in the Journal of the American College of Nutrition by Donald Davis and a team of researchers from the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry at the University of Texas (UT) in Austin. They analyzed nutritional data from the US Department of Agriculture from 1950 and 1999 for 43 different types of vegetables and fruits and found a “significant decrease” in the amount of protein, calcium, phosphorus, iron, riboflavin (vitamin B2), and vitamin C in the last half-century.
Davis and his colleagues believe that the decrease in nutritional value is due to prevailing agricultural practices, which aim to improve characteristics (size, growth rate, pest resistance) but destroy nutritional value. And while the situation in Slovenia was relatively acceptable at the time, today, even in terms of diet, we are increasingly following in the footsteps of the USA.
“Efforts to breed new crop varieties that provide higher yields, pest resistance, and climate adaptability have made crops larger and faster,” Davis reported, “but their ability to produce or absorb nutrients has not kept pace with their rapid growth.”
According to him, the amount of other nutrients, such as magnesium, zinc, and vitamins B6 and E, has also decreased, but these were not studied in 1950, so further research is needed to determine how much less of these key vitamins and minerals we are getting.
Associations of organic consumers also cite several other studies with similar findings: the Kushi Institute, in an analysis of nutrient data from 1975 to 1997, found that the average calcium content in 12 types of fresh vegetables decreased by 27 percent, iron by 37 percent, vitamin A by 21 percent, and vitamin C by 30 percent.
A similar study of British nutrient data from 1930 to 1980, published in the British Food Journal, showed that the average calcium content in 20 types of vegetables decreased by 19 percent, iron by 22 percent, and potassium by 14 percent.
And if this was in 1980 – what is the situation today, 44 years later? It is certainly not better, as later studies have confirmed that the nutrient content is decreasing. A study in the January 2022 issue of the journal Foods showed that most vegetables grown in Australia between 1980 and 2010 had relatively similar iron content, but the iron content in some types of vegetables decreased significantly.
A decrease in iron content, from 30 to 50 percent, occurred in sweet corn, red-skinned potatoes, cauliflower, string beans, green peas, and chickpeas.
Another study showed that today, you would have to eat eight oranges to get the same amount of vitamin A that our grandparents got from one orange.
Experts say that the quality of grains has also deteriorated: a study in the journal Scientific Reports from 2020 showed that the protein content in wheat decreased by 23 percent from 1955 to 2016, and the content of manganese, iron, zinc, and magnesium also decreased significantly.
This worrying decrease also has consequences for those who eat meat. According to Montgomery, cows, pigs, goats, and lambs are fed less nutritious grasses and grains, so meat and other animal products are less nutritious than they used to be.
A vicious circle
Several factors contribute to the problem: the first is modern agricultural practices, which aim to increase crop yields.
“By learning that plants grow bigger and faster, plants cannot keep up with absorbing nutrients from the soil or synthesizing nutrients within themselves,” explains Donald R. Davis of the University of Texas at Austin. The retired chemist and nutrition researcher was the lead author of the 2004 study that opened eyes and the author of later articles on the topic.
Higher yields mean that nutrients from the soil must be distributed over a larger quantity of crops, so the nutrients produced by fruits and vegetables are actually diluted. “Unfortunately, farmers are paid for the weight of their crops, so this encourages them to do things that are not good for nutrient content,” Davis adds.
“Another culprit is soil damage caused by high-yielding crops. Wheat, corn, rice, soybeans, potatoes, bananas, yam, and flax benefit from collaborating with key fungi that improve the plant's ability to access nutrients and water from the soil. Fungi act as an extension of the plant's roots,” says Montgomery. However, high-yielding agriculture depletes the soil, which to some extent impairs the plant's ability to establish a partnership with mycorrhizal fungi, Montgomery explains.
Regardless of who consumes them, foods with fewer nutrients may lack another important property: taste. Many compounds that protect health also give food its taste, so some of the shifts in agricultural practices that are responsible for lower nutrient content are the same as those that contribute to their bland taste (we are talking about tasteless tomatoes and bland carrots).
What can we do?
The first step is to leave the soil as undisturbed as possible and reduce soil processing with pesticides, which leads to mineral depletion and the destruction of microorganisms. By planting cover crops (grown to cover the soil and protect it), such as clover, rye, or peas, we can prevent erosion and suppress weed growth. By rotating the crops grown in a field, we can improve the nutrient content in subsequent crops.
The key to healthier crops is healthier soil. An important step would be to rotate fields between growing seasons so that the soil can recover. Abandoning pesticides and fertilizers in favor of organic farming methods is also good for the soil, crops, and their consumers, as these destroy microorganisms in the soil – which are essential for healthy soil and later healthy crops.
One strategy to improve soil is also regenerative agriculture – a comprehensive set of practices that can restore soil fertility. A study in the January 2022 issue of the journal PeerJ: Life & Environment shows that regenerative agricultural practices allow for the production of crops with higher levels of organic matter in the soil, a measure of soil health, and higher levels of some vitamins, minerals, and phytochemicals.
Those who want to get the most nutritious fruits and vegetables should buy from local organic farmers, but it should be noted that the situation is not the same as it was 50 years ago. An additional problem is that, due to stress – emotional and chemical (air, water, food pollution, etc.) – people need more nutrients, not less, so supplementation is beneficial.
Are these the same as if you got them from food? Certainly not exactly the same – but it is better than the deficiency, which sooner or later can lead to health problems and even serious diseases.

Medtem, ko sta sodobno sadje in zelenjava čedalje lepša, večja, bolj pisana in bleščeča, pa sta hkrati čedalje bolj prazna hranil, ki jih potrebujemo za dobro zdravje. Čedalje bolj polna – sploh sadje – sta le sladkorja, kar je še dodatni minus.
Pretiravali bi, če bi rekli, da korenje, ki ga jeste danes, skorajda ne vsebuje hranilnih snovi – jih pa vsekakor vsebuje bistveno manj kot pred npr. 50 leti.
Sadje in zelenjava, pridelani pred desetletji, so bili neprimerljivo bogatejši z vitamini in minerali kot so dandanes. Glavni krivec za ta zaskrbljujoč trend je izčrpavanje tal: sodobne intenzivne kmetijske metode iz tal, v katerih raste hrana, ki jo uživamo, odvzemajo čedalje več hranilnih snovi.
Čedalje lepša – in čedalje slabša
In medtem, ko sta sodobno sadje in zelenjava čedalje lepša, večja, bolj pisana in bleščeča, pa sta hkrati čedalje bolj prazna hranil, ki jih potrebujemo za dobro zdravje. Čedalje bolj polna – sploh sadje – sta le sladkorja, kar je še dodatni minus.
To pomeni, da je vsaka naslednja generacija sadja in zelenjave dejansko manj koristna za vas kot prejšnja (in ob morebitni uporabi pesticidov tudi bolj škodljiva).
“Upadanje hranil povzroči, imajo naša telesa čedalje manj sestavin, ki jih potrebujejo za obrambo pred kroničnimi boleznimi – to bo zmanjšalo vrednost hrane kot preventivne medicine,” pravi David R. Montgomery, profesor geomorfologije na Univerzi Washington v Seattlu in soavtor knjige What Your Food Ate z Anne Biklé.
Zaskrbljujoči podatki študij
Prelomna je bila študija na to temo, ki jo je decembra 2004 v reviji Journal of the American College of Nutrition objavil Donald Davis z ekipo raziskovalcev z oddelka za kemijo in biokemijo teksaške univerze (UT) v Austinu. Preučevali so prehranske podatke ameriškega ministrstva za kmetijstvo iz let 1950 in 1999 za 43 različnih vrst zelenjave in sadja ter ugotovili “opazno zmanjšanje” količine beljakovin, kalcija, fosforja, železa, riboflavina (vitamina B2) in vitamina C v zadnje pol stoletja.
Davis in njegovi sodelavci menijo, da se je hranilna vrednost zmanjšala zaradi prevladujočih kmetijskih praks, katerih namen naj bi bil izboljšati lastnosti (velikost, hitrost rasti, odpornost proti škodljivcem), ki pa uničujejo hranljivost. In če je bilo takrat v Sloveniji še relativno sprejemljivo stanje, dandanes tudi glede prehrane čedalje bolj stopamo po stopinjah ZDA.
“Prizadevanja za vzgojo novih sort poljščin, ki zagotavljajo večji pridelek, odpornost proti škodljivcem in prilagodljivost podnebju, so omogočila, da so poljščine večje in hitrejše,” je poročal Davis, “vendar njihova sposobnost proizvajanja ali sprejemanja hranil ni sledila njihovi hitri rasti.”
Po njegovih besedah se je zmanjšalo tudi število drugih hranil, kot so magnezij, cink ter vitamina B6 in E, vendar jih leta 1950 niso preučevali, zato so potrebne dodatne raziskave, da bi ugotovili, koliko manj teh ključnih vitaminov in mineralov dobimo.
Združenja ekoloških potrošnikov navajajo tudi več drugih študij s podobnimi ugotovitvami: Kushijev inštitut je v analizi podatkov o hranilnih snoveh od leta 1975 do 1997 ugotovil, da se je povprečna vsebnost kalcija v 12 vrstah sveže zelenjave zmanjšala za 27 odstotkov, železa za 37 odstotkov, vitamina A za 21 odstotkov in vitamina C za 30 odstotkov.
Podobna študija britanskih podatkov o hranilnih snoveh od leta 1930 do leta 1980, objavljena v reviji British Food Journal, je pokazala, da se je povprečna vsebnost kalcija v 20 vrstah zelenjave zmanjšala za 19 odstotkov, železa za 22 odstotkov in kalija za 14 odstotkov.
In če je bilo to leta 1980 – kakšno je stanje šele danes, kar 44 let kasneje? Boljše prav zagotovo ne, saj so tudi kasnejše študije potrdile, da se vsebnost hranilnih snovi zmanjšuje. Raziskava v januarski številki revije Foods iz leta 2022 je pokazala, da je imela večina zelenjave, pridelane v Avstraliji, med letoma 1980 in 2010 razmeroma podobno vsebnost železa, vendar se je vsebnost železa v nekaterih vrstah zelenjave opazno zmanjšala.
Do zmanjšanja vsebnosti železa, in sicer od 30 do 50 odstotkov, je prišlo pri sladki koruzi, krompirju z rdečo lupino, cvetači, stročjem fižolu, zelenem grahu in čičeriki.
Še ena študija je pokazala, da bi danes morali pojesti osem pomaranč, da bi dobili enako količino vitamina A, kot so jo dobili naši stari starši z eno pomarančo.
Strokovnjaki pravijo, da se je poslabšala tudi kakovost žit: študija v reviji Scientific Reports iz leta 2020 je pokazala, da se je vsebnost beljakovin v pšenici od leta 1955 do leta 2016 zmanjšala za 23 odstotkov, opazno pa se je zmanjšala tudi vsebnost mangana, železa, cinka in magnezija.
Skrb vzbujajoče zmanjšanje ima posledice tudi za tiste, ki jedo meso. Po besedah Montgomeryja se krave, prašiči, koze in jagnjeta prehranjujejo z manj hranljivimi travami in žiti, zato so meso in drugi izdelki živalskega izvora manj hranljivi kot nekoč.
Začarani krog
K problemu prispeva več dejavnikov: prvi je sodobna kmetijska praksa, ki je namenjena povečanju donosov pridelkov.
“Z učenjem, da rastline rastejo večje in hitrejše, rastline ne morejo dohajati absorpcije hranil iz tal ali sintetizirati hranil znotraj sebe,” pojasnjuje Donald R. Davis s teksaške univerze v Austinu. Upokojeni kemik in raziskovalec prehrane je bil glavni avtor študije iz leta 2004, ki je odprla oči, ter avtor poznejših člankov na to temo.
Večji pridelek pomeni, da je treba hranila iz tal porazdeliti po večji količini pridelkov, zato se hranila, ki jih proizvede sadje in zelenjava, dejansko razredčijo. “Na žalost so kmetje plačani za težo svojih pridelkov, zato jih to spodbuja, da počnejo stvari, ki niso dobre za vsebnost hranil,” dodaja Davis.
“Drugi krivec je poškodba tal, ki nastane zaradi pridelkov z visokim donosom. Pšenica, koruza, riž, soja, krompir, banane, jam in lan imajo koristi od sodelovanja s ključnimi glivami, ki izboljšujejo sposobnost rastlin za dostop do hranil in vode iz tal. Glive delujejo kot podaljšek korenin rastline,” pravi Montgomery. Vendar pa visoko donosno kmetijstvo izčrpava tla, kar do neke mere ogroža sposobnost rastlin, da vzpostavijo partnerstvo z mikoriznimi glivami, pojasnjuje Montgomery.
Ne glede na to, kdo jih uživa, lahko živilom z manj hranil manjka še ena pomembna lastnost: okus. Veliko spojin, ki varujejo zdravje, daje živilom tudi okus, zato so nekateri premiki v kmetijskih praksah, ki so odgovorni za nižjo vsebnost hranilnih snovi, isti, ki prispevajo k njihovemu meh okusu (govorimo o vas, paradižniki brez okusa in mlačno korenje).
Kaj lahko storimo?
Prvi korak je, da pustimo tla čim bolj pri miru in zmanjšamo obdelavo tal s pesticidi, ki vodi v izčrpavanje mineralov in uničevanje mikroorganizmov. S sajenjem pokrovnih rastlin (ki se gojijo za prekrivanje tal, da bi jih zaščitili), kot so detelja, ržena trava ali grašica, lahko preprečimo erozijo in zatremo rast plevela. Z menjavanjem rastlin, ki se gojijo na posameznem polju, lahko izboljšamo vsebnost hranil v naslednjih pridelkih.
Ključ do bolj zdravih pridelkov je bolj zdrava zemlja. Pomemben korak bi bilo menjavanje polj med rastnimi sezonami, da bi se zemlja lahko obnovila. Tudi opustitev pesticidov in gnojil v korist ekoloških načinov pridelave je dobra za tla, pridelke in njihove potrošnike, saj ti uničujejo mikroorganizme v tleh – ti pa so nujni za zdravo zemljo in kasneje zdrav pridelek.
Ena od strategij za izboljšanje tal je tudi regenerativno kmetijstvo – obsežen sklop praks, ki lahko obnovijo rodovitnost tal. Študija v januarski številki revije PeerJ: Life & Environment iz leta 2022 kaže, da regenerativne kmetijske prakse omogočajo pridelavo pridelkov z višjimi ravnmi organske snovi v tleh, oceno zdravja tal in višjimi ravnmi nekaterih vitaminov, mineralov in fitokemikalij.
Tisti, ki želijo dobiti najbolj hranljivo sadje in zelenjavo, bi morali kupovati pri lokalnih ekoloških pridelovalcih, a zavedati se je treba, da tudi tu stanje ni enako kot pred 50 leti. Še dodatni problem pa predstavlja dejstvo, da zaradi stresa – čustvenega in kemičnega (onesnažen zrak, voda, hrana …) – ljudje potrebujemo kvečjemu več hranil, ne manj, zato je koristno dodajanje v obliki prehranskih dopolnil.
So ta enaka, kot če bi to dobili iz hrane? Prav zagotovo to ni povsem enako – je pa boljše kot pomanjkanje, ki prej ko slej lahko privede do zdravstvenih težav in celo resnih bolezni.

Wireworms, the larvae of click beetles, are a nightmare for gardeners. They are an even bigger problem when they infest fields. They look like hard, small worms. The young ones are almost pale yellow, about a centimeter long, while the older ones are reddish-brown, 15–35 millimeters long, and, most importantly, very voracious. For a long time, it was believed that they couldn't be eradicated because they don't disappear in a single season. It is essential to understand their life cycle to effectively control them, as it can last from three to five years, depending on the weather.

They thrive in gardens, pastures, and fields.
We are often the cause of wireworm infestations in our cultivated areas. Their development is favored by areas where crop rotation is practiced occasionally, or where potatoes are planted after a two-year period of grain or grass-legume mixtures. They also thrive in neglected, weedy areas, where female click beetles lay their eggs in the soil, from which wireworms develop in the garden. They also thrive in pastures, clover fields, and grain fields. When the click beetles mature, they feed on the pollen of flowering weeds. They appear in larger numbers during dry periods because they try to compensate for the lost moisture by sucking on potato tubers.

The larvae need to be eliminated.
The most effective way to control wireworms is during their feeding and migration period, which usually occurs in May and September, and sometimes even in early October. The best results are achieved by applying the treatment in the evening. Because they burrow into the soil in dry weather, the treatment won't reach them, so it's crucial to do this after rain or to thoroughly water the beds before application. In the past, farmers and gardeners had access to chemical treatments that were more harmful than beneficial, but today, organic alternatives are available. There is a fungus, Beauveria bassiana, that affects the pest by infecting the larvae, which then become ill and die. The treatment only works if the wireworms are present. After two days, check in the morning to see if the larvae have been attracted to the bait. Mark the location of the potatoes by sticking a twig into them and tying a ribbon to the end of the twig, then apply the treatment. You can also use nematodes, entomopathogenic nematodes Steinernema carpocapsae and Steinernema feltiae. Because biological treatments only work on the early stages of the larvae, the process needs to be repeated for at least three to four years.

The seeds can be crushed and sprinkled like flour on the affected areas. Another method recommended by experts is to bury the remains of cruciferous plants, with arugula and white mustard proving to be the most effective. The areas should be sown in early April or mid-August and then mowed just before flowering, as this is when the most biomass will be obtained. A sufficient amount of gas, which will destroy the wireworms, will only be obtained with a sufficient amount of moisture.

Writing and Posture at the Desk
The proper way to hold a pen or pencil begins very early in a child's life, even before they start school. As children begin to draw and scribble, parents check, or don't check, how the child holds the writing instrument. Rarely do they put the pen in the child's hand themselves or encourage them to use it correctly.
Preschool children who can hold a pen or pencil nicely and relaxed are becoming a rarity, as little importance is given to the correct grip these days.
Writing is, like any other skill, the result of practice for every writer. It requires the ability to precisely control motor skills, flawless coordination, and visual-motor control over the fingers and hand – all in accordance with the writer's age.
Correct Body Posture While Sitting at the Desk
Incorrect body posture and, consequently, poor posture while sitting can affect writing. The more the hands and palms have to support the upper part of the torso, the more the hand presses on the writing surface, which limits the movement of the fingers and palms. Children are increasingly writing from the wrist, and jerky movements distort the basic form of writing. As a result, writing is slower, the hand is harder to move, and children get tired more quickly.
The child should sit upright at the desk with relaxed shoulders. The height of the desk and chair should be adjusted so that the child's feet are completely on the floor. The forearms rest relaxed on the desk at a 90-degree angle. The elbow is not raised, the hand does not exert any pressure on the writing surface, and the shoulder does not push the hand down. The hand can move freely in all directions, allowing for fluid writing.
Children need to be encouraged and reminded about the correct posture until they adopt it. In any case, they will adopt it – the only question is whether the result will be helpful or a burden for the child.
A Good Pen Grip
A good pen grip can be illustrated by first asking the child to place their hand on the desk in a position similar to writing. All joints now rest relaxed in the middle position. Then, place the pen in the child's hand from above, and the child gently holds it and moves it slightly across the paper. The pen is easiest to hold with three fingers: the thumb, index finger, and middle finger (the latter also provides support from behind). If the joints are in an unusual position, a cramp will appear in the muscles, and movement will be limited. The middle position of the joints allows for the greatest possible freedom of movement. By moving the wrist and fingers simultaneously, the child can now easily move the pen in all directions. It is important that the hand rests on the paper at a 45-degree angle, so that the child uses the wrist when drawing vertical lines and the fingers when drawing horizontal lines.
Correct Pen Holding
Incorrect Pen Holding
Basic Shapes and Directions of Movement
Children are able to copy simple words and sentences just a few weeks after starting school. To avoid burdening them, we pay little attention to the correct formation of letters, as they have not yet fully mastered this at this stage.
Therefore, it is necessary to consistently practice the basic elements in the form of preparatory and supporting activities when learning letters. Uniform strokes give the child a sense of security and orientation, which is meaningful in terms of later learning cursive writing:
- Horizontal lines are drawn from left to right;
- Diagonal and zigzag lines (e.g., in the letter A) are drawn from the middle diagonally downwards to the left, and then from the middle diagonally downwards to the right;
- Zigzag letters (e.g., as in the letter V) are drawn from left to top and down to the middle and right;
- Ovals are practiced as left-leaning ovals;
- Arcs and curves are practiced with large movements, as children have difficulty changing directions.
Drawing patterns that include the above skills can be fun. Especially if colored pencils are included. Children are excellent aesthetes, and they proudly show everything they create and put effort into, just like us. Learning a new skill requires practice, dedication, time, and a lot of encouragement. The effort you put into a child will pay off for both you and your child. It's worth it!
Until next time!
The Prvošolec.si Team

If you don't exercise your muscles enough, you will lose a significant amount of muscle mass over time. There's a saying about muscles: "Use it or lose it!" However, many experienced athletes notice that they continue to lose muscle mass even with regular exercise. This is particularly noticeable in the leg muscles. Cyclists may ride the same distances, train for speed, and even incorporate regular strength training into their routines, but when they compare photos from previous years, they notice that their legs are no longer as strong as they once were.

As we age, muscle mass decreases. We cannot completely avoid this. As a result, we become slower. However, athletes and everyone else must fight this as much as possible. We want to slow down the process of sarcopenia, or muscle atrophy.

Causes and Consequences
The technical term for the loss of muscle mass due to aging is sarcopenia. It begins as early as our 30s. The theory suggests that the causes lie in anabolic hormones, which are responsible for muscle growth, in the decreased neuromuscular efficiency, or in the poorer connection or communication between the brain, the central nervous system, and the muscles, and in the reduced ability to synthesize or produce proteins.

Inactivity causes an average loss of 3 to 5% of muscle mass over ten years. We know that we can slow down muscle loss with regular physical activity. However, regardless of the activity we perform, age affects muscle mass.

Muscle loss is gradual until our 50s or 60s, after which it accelerates. There is no conclusive evidence that gender affects the rate of muscle loss. In women, menopause affects hormones, while in men, andropause causes a decrease in anabolic components. Both have the same effect on muscle loss. Research suggests that aging affects fast-twitch muscle fibers, which are used for short, explosive movements such as sprinting, throwing, and jumping, more than it affects activities with lower intensity and endurance, such as long-distance running.

Many older cyclists switch to longer and easier rides over the years because fast-twitch muscle fibers wear out faster. This shift further accelerates or encourages fast-twitch muscle fibers to change their structure and become slow-twitch. In addition, the elasticity of muscles, tendons, and ligaments decreases with age. If training does not include jumps, sprints, strength training, and speed work, the elasticity of the tissue deteriorates even faster. The less elastic our muscles and tendons are, the less fluid our movements become. This affects the deterioration of reaction time when changing terrain (roots, stones, holes, etc.).

The problem lies in the transfer of force that develops during movement. This is especially noticeable in running. The absorption of force on the joints is four times the body weight. Most of this force is transferred through the joints to the muscles of the buttocks and thighs. Poorer muscle tone makes it difficult to transfer such large forces. The gluteus (buttock muscles) and hamstrings (back of the thigh muscles) also weaken. The reason is increased sitting. When a runner wants to run or a cyclist wants to ride, these muscles are also weakened and contribute less to good performance.

Even if cycling or running doesn't interest you, you shouldn't be indifferent to what's happening to your muscles and, consequently, to your entire musculoskeletal system as you age. Weakened muscles and bones are a warning sign for injuries.

What to do?
Strength training
The more muscle mass you have lost, the harder you will have to work. Train 2 times a week. However, the quality of training is always more important than the quantity. Focus on large muscle groups with exercises such as squats, leg raises, torso raises, and bodyweight exercises.

Do "drills"
Do you want to improve neuromuscular connections? Perform fast, light, coordinated movements such as changes of direction, agility drills, sprint drills, fast reaction drills, skipping, and jumping. Perform drills 2 times a week. It's better to skip a ride and do a good drill.

Regularly perform intervals
Recruit fast-twitch muscle fibers! Include short, intense intervals in cycling, either on flat ground or uphill.

Balanced diet
This means that you don't just eat protein, which is essential for muscle recovery, but all high-quality macronutrients: fats, carbohydrates, proteins, minerals, and water. Don't forget about fiber, which helps with digestion (vegetables, seeds, fruit). Keep a food diary in which you list what you ate in each meal and focus on having adequate macronutrients and fiber in at least 2 meals a day.

If you have a truly busy schedule and cannot take care of a balanced meal, consult a doctor or specialist about the need for additional protein and vitamins. After a strenuous workout, make sure you have a high-quality meal. Eat it about an hour after your workout.

Lifestyle
A strenuous workout will not help you if you sit for 10 hours afterward. Get plenty of fresh air, use the stairs instead of the elevator, cycle instead of driving, walk, and sit as little as possible so that your gluteus and hamstrings do not atrophy. This will make it easier and faster for you to cycle or run and perform everyday tasks and avoid potential injuries.

Even after fruits and vegetables are harvested, they continue to “live” in a way. A process occurs within them that is the opposite of photosynthesis, called respiration. While the fruit is still part of the plant, the bonds of carbohydrates formed through photosynthesis and oxygen gradually break down into water and carbon dioxide. This process provides the plant with the energy it needs for growth and development. However, this very process of respiration is what causes problems when storing produce. Through respiration, fruits and vegetables lose the quality of their components, their taste, aroma, sweetness, water content, weight, and nutritional value in our home storage.

The Influence of the Ripening Gas Ethylene
After some types of fruits and vegetables (and even flowers) are harvested, they undergo a more intense process of respiration. As a result, they have a shorter shelf life, which is understandable since the fruits are using up their stored energy. The intensity of respiration can also be influenced by factors such as the growing area and climatic conditions. The intensity of respiration in produce has another important dimension – it directly affects the generation of heat. Therefore, we need to provide cooler storage for varieties with a high respiration rate than for those with a lower rate. In addition to this process, the amount of ethylene is also important for the quality of stored produce. Ethylene is the only plant hormone that exists in a gaseous state. Most often, plants produce it during ripening, but there are exceptions where it is produced even in fruits that are not yet ripe. These fruits become more colorful and softer in our storage. Ethylene is most often produced by fruits such as apples, pears, peaches, plums, figs, kiwis, and tropical fruits, among which we eat the most bananas, mangoes, and avocados. Fruits and vegetables that produce higher amounts of ethylene after harvest lose quality faster, and the fruit also spoils more quickly. Even a low concentration of this gas, which most vegetables have, manifests as a brownish discoloration of the central vein in lettuce, yellowing of broccoli, kale, spinach, cucumbers, and cabbage, a dried-out appearance and bitter taste in root vegetables, browning in the flesh of eggplant, and softening and spotting in pumpkins, peppers, and watermelons.

Proper Ventilation is Essential for Storage
The best way to avoid the damage caused by ethylene is to store fruits and vegetables separately. Ideally, we would have multiple storage areas, as different produce has different requirements. However, since this is not always possible, it is better to focus on providing a temperature that suits most fruits, which is between 2 and 5 degrees Celsius. Freshness is also maintained by regularly inspecting the stored products, which means removing any overripe or rotten ones. We should also pay attention to the relative humidity, which has a considerable range: it ranges from 50 to 95 percent relative humidity, which is often a problem when storing in a single space. The simplest and most important measure to ensure that stored produce retains its essential properties is ventilation. By regularly exchanging the air, we can help regulate humidity (if it is lacking, we ventilate when it is raining outside) and temperature (when it freezes at night, we open doors or windows during the day). Most importantly, regular ventilation removes ethylene from the storage area.

1. Understand the difference between a hearing aid and a cochlear implant. Hearing aids amplify or increase sounds so that damaged ears can hear them. Cochlear implants bypass the damaged parts of the ear that are unable to hear and directly stimulate the auditory nerve. Then, the signals that the implant sends travel from the auditory nerve to the brain. The brain deciphers these signals as sound. Although people with cochlear implants must learn the process of hearing, they can recognize alarm signals, understand different environmental sounds, and sometimes, for the first time in their lives, have a conversation with a friend or talk on the phone.

2. Learn about the different parts of a cochlear implant. These include the microphone, which collects sound from the environment; the speech processor, which selects and codes the sounds from the microphone; the receiver/stimulator, which receives signals from the processor and converts them into electrical impulses; and the electrode array, which is a collection of electrodes that deliver the electrical impulses to different areas of the auditory nerve.

3. Be aware that, unfortunately, not everyone can be helped with a cochlear implant. First, the person’s hearing loss must be bilateral, or in both ears, and profound. Profound hearing loss is defined as a hearing loss of at least 90 decibels. The degree of hearing loss is determined by measuring the hearing threshold, or the level in decibels (dB) at which a sound is barely audible. The louder the sound has to be to be heard, the greater the degree of hearing loss. Second, the person must be able to recognize at least 30 percent of sounds, even in the best conditions. Children who are at least two years old and have severe sensorineural hearing loss in both ears are also candidates for cochlear implantation.

4. Understand how the ear and hearing work. The cochlea is a very small structure in the ear that is shaped like a snail shell. It is the most important part of the hearing process and is located in the inner ear. When someone has cochlear damage, it means that part or all of the inner ear is damaged, and the hearing loss is permanent. This is called sensorineural hearing loss. This damage can be caused by illness, loud noises, certain medications, tumors, or natural aging.
