Vročina in vzdržljivostni športi
Za povprečnega rekreativnega športnika pa večinoma velja, da se zaradi slabe tehnike in pomanjkanja spretnosti za primerljive dosežke bistveno bolj prešvica. Lahko bi tudi rekli, da gre veliko več energije v nič.
Ko povišani temperaturi okolja ob stopnji telesne dejavnosti dodamo še dejavnike trajanja športne dejavnosti, visoke vlage v zraku, starosti in spola, hitro ugotovimo, da vročina in vlaga omejujeta zmožnost oddajanja toplote med telesno dejavnostjo in vplivata na vzdržljivostne dosežke.
Hkrati se povečuje tveganje za nastanek bolezenskih stanj zaradi telesnega naprezanja v vročini, kot so toplotni krči, toplotna izčrpanost in toplotni udar. Bolj pri starejših in malenkost bolj pri ženskah.
Kakšna je naša običajna telesna temperatura?
V stanju neaktivnost in za telo prijetnem okolju je temperatura jedra človeškega telesa približno 37 °C, mišic in kože pa 35 oziroma 31 °C. Pri telesni dejavnosti v vročem okolju, ob ponavljajočem se mišičnem delu, na primer teku, hoji, nastajajo velike količine toplote, kar viša temperaturo v mišicah in zvišuje temperaturo jedra telesa. Ta lahko naraste tudi na več kot 40 °C.
Za oceno toplotne obremenitve se uporabljajo različni kazalniki, med pogostimi je WBGT, ki se izračuna po podatkih o suhi temperaturi zraka (z običajnim termometrom), o vlažni temperaturi zraka (ta odraža dejansko zmožnost zraka za izhlapevanje vode glede na relativno vlažnost in hitrost zraka) in temperaturi sončnega sevanja, ki jo izmerimo s posebnim (globus) termometrom. Na ta način lahko nekako standardiziramo temperaturno obremenitev, kar nam omogoča primerjavo.
Na primer,* isto vrednost WBGT (27 °C) lahko dosežemo v vročem in suhem okolju (svetovno prvenstvo v cestnem kolesarstvu 2016 v Katarju: 37 °C, 25-odstotna relativna vlažnost) ter toplem in vlažnem okolju (svetovno prvenstvo v nogometu 2014 v Braziliji: 28 °C, 75-odstotna relativna vlažnost). Ta kazalnik ima sicer omejitve, je pa eden boljših, ki se uporabljajo tudi pri krojenju razmer za tekmovanja, kot so letošnje olimpijske igre v Tokiu.
Previsoka telesna temperatura je nezdrava
Telo običajno oddaja toploto v okolje skozi kožo, ne da bi se tega zavedalo. To poteka v procesu konvekcije (prevajanja) in sevanja toplote. Tisto, kar zaznamo, pa je oddajanje toplote z izhlapevanjem, predvsem v obliki znojenja. Ker je v vročem okolju, je temperaturni gradient med kožo in okolico zelo majhen, lahko celo negativen, telo toplote ne more prevajati v okolje in tako se oddaja pretežno kot izhlapevanje znoja.
Kadar je posameznik dehidriran, se ti procesi začnejo zapletati. Ne samo da se toplota ne more oddajati, zaradi pomanjkljive cirkulacije ob bolj praznih žilah zaradi dehidracije se presnovna toplota od delujočih mišic sploh ne more prenesti do kože (ali pljuč), da bi izhlapela. Zmanjša se tudi količina vode v ožilju, kar se sicer kaže kot »dober hemoglobin«, preveč dobrega lahko tudi ubija.
Na primer s kapjo, ki je posledica krvnih strdkov v različnih žilah. Ker so te žile pogosto v možganih, srcu in pljučih, so ti incidenti v poletni vročini neredko smrtni. Dehidracija torej pri telesni dejavnosti v vročem okolju še dodatno obremeni srčno-žilni sistem in je podlaga za tihega ubijalca. Zaradi povečane obremenitve srčno-žilnega sistema posameznik tudi občuti telesno dejavnost kot bolj naporno.
Procesi, ki vodijo do toplotne preobremenitve, se v telesu sprožijo že po nekaj minutah vadbe na vročini, zato se je treba nanjo vedno pripraviti.
Kako zmanjšati vpliv toplotne preobremenitve?
Mehanizmi za izboljšanje odpornosti proti vročinskemu napadu so različni in dokaj kompleksni. Samo to, da pijemo vodo, ne zadošča. Ta strategija zna biti pri večjih tekočinskih izgubah z znojenjem celo nasprotno učinkovita, ker telo za samo vsrkavanje vode potrebuje tudi elektrolite, predvsem natrij. Ta se namreč pri pitju izloča v črevo, da se vzpostavi neke vrste gradient, ki omogoča vsrkavanje vode.
Treba ji je dodati tudi sol, potrebe so sicer zelo individualno pogojene, a že količina (2,5 g ali pol male žličke na 1 liter vode), ki je v standardni rehidracijski raztopini, lahko naredi življenjsko pomembno razliko. Še učinkovitejša je resorpcija vode, če je v raztopini tudi glukoza, zato so v izotoničnih pijačah in rehidracijskih tekočinah tudi enostavni sladkorji.
Poleg ustreznega pitja je ključni proces navajanje telesa na povišano temperaturo, imenuje se aklimatizacija. Aklimatizacija na vročino poteka vsaj dva tedna (v povprečju 7–10 dni), pri vrhunskih športnikih, ki bodo tekmovali na olimpijskih igrah v Tokiu, se uporabljajo kompleksne strategije različnih oblik aklimatizacije v kombinaciji z mehanizmi aklimatizacije z najmanj dvotedenskim treningom v vročini. O aklimatizaciji govorimo pri uporabi simuliranega okolja v namensko zasnovanih komorah oziroma preprostih improviziranih »vročih sobah«. Privajanje na vročino v savni je tipičen primer aklimatizacije. Najopaznejši znaki, da se je telo z redno vadbo v vročini nekako prilagodilo razmeram, so: povišana stopnja znojenja, nižji srčni utrip pri dani intenzivnosti, boljše zadrževanje elektrolitov in nižja temperatura jedra.
Znanstveni podatki tudi nakazujejo, da aklimatizacija na vročino učinkovito dopolni druge strategije za izboljšanje telesne zmogljivosti (npr. višinski trening). Zmanjša tudi tveganje za pojav bolezenskih stanj, povezanih z visokimi temperaturami. Prav tako ne zmanjšuje telesne zmogljivosti v hladnejših okoljih, v določenih okoliščinah jo lahko celo izboljša.
Kako ukrepati?
Če se pojavijo bolezenski znaki in simptomi zaradi vročega vremena, je treba ukrepati. Ker je vročinska preobremenitev resno zdravstveno stanje, ob najmanjših bolezenskih znakih pokličite zdravniško pomoč. Posameznika umaknite od vira vročine (npr. s sonca v senco), in če je mogoče, začnite aktivno ohlajanje. To izvajamo z mrzlimi obkladki po telesu, zlasti na predelu velikih žil (pazduha, dimlje). Takoj ko je mogoče, naj posameznik začne rehidracijo, če je le možno, s praški za rehidracijske tekočine ali vsaj izotoničnimi športnimi napitki. Sposobnost črevesja za resorpcijo tekočine je odvisna od njegovega stanja, je pa pomembno tudi, da se zavedamo pomena postopnosti rehidracije. S tem, da se naenkrat napijemo, pogosto težave še poslabšamo.
Ko posameznik ni več omotičen in smo dosegli njegovo normalno telesno maso (kar je cilj rehidracije), naj nadaljuje strategijo pitja vsaj nekaj decilitrov na uro. Vnos tekočine naj bo prilagojen tudi tako, da izguba skupne telesne mase ne preseže 2–3 odstotke.

The First 1000 Days of Life

During the period of most intense growth, establishing a healthy gut microbiota is extremely important. In fact, this is when the foundation is laid, which will significantly impact an individual's health and well-being later in life. The microbiota that develops in the first 1000 days after conception prepares our immune system to cope with environmental factors and plays a crucial role in utilizing nutrients from food. Experts agree that the development of the gut microbiota is influenced by genetic factors, the mother's health during pregnancy, and her lifestyle.

Today, it is known that microorganisms pass through the placenta (transplacentally) into the fetus while it is still in the mother's womb. It is there that the phenomenon of so-called "primary colonization" occurs, which is crucial for the development of the child's immune system. According to the "first 1000 days" hypothesis, the period of development within the womb and during breastfeeding is the most important for forming the gut microbiota and programming the child's immune system. If a child does not come into contact with appropriate microorganisms from the environment during this early period, inappropriate environmental influences can lead to hypersensitivity to various chronic diseases. Due to so-called inappropriate epigenetic regulation, the child is often a victim of atopic predisposition, which later manifests primarily in the form of chronic respiratory and skin diseases. For this reason, and because the Th2 immune response, which is associated with a higher risk of allergic reactions, predominates in the embryonic phase, pregnancy represents an important window for therapeutic intervention. According to experts, probiotics are particularly important in specific cases, such as after a Cesarean section or when the mother is exposed to antibiotic treatment.

Data show that the mother's diet during pregnancy already influences the formation of the gut microbiota in the child, or even earlier – her lifestyle shapes the composition of microorganisms in her body. Bacteria from the vagina pass to the child during vaginal delivery, and a similar process occurs later; during the so-called primary colonization, microorganisms also pass from breast milk, from the mother's skin, and to a large extent, they create the child's microbiota.

In addition to diet, other factors influence the mother's microorganisms or her microbiota, so a holistic lifestyle for the future mother is actually important. This includes factors that we all know – sufficient physical activity, enough sleep, a non-smoking lifestyle, and a healthy approach to stress.

The Gut Microbiota in Newborns After Cesarean Section

In the intestines of prematurely born children and children born by Cesarean section, certain bacteria from the mother's birth canal are missing, and the intestine is colonized by microorganisms that are more common in the hospital environment, and to a greater extent and more intensely than in a vaginally born child. To improve the balance between beneficial and potentially harmful microorganisms from the hospital, newborns have been wiped with the mother's vaginal fluid after birth in some places, but the safety and effectiveness of this method, known as "vaginal seeding," is unknown. The Baby Biome Study is intensively researching how the mode of delivery affects the microbiota. In this study, British researchers (Shao Y, Nature 2019) published interesting results that reveal a high degree of colonization of the intestine with hospital bacteria. In this study, potentially harmful hospital bacteria, such as enterococci (Enterococcus) and Klebsiella, predominated in the intestines of children born by Cesarean section. Genomic analysis of hundreds of bacteria from the intestines of newborns revealed genes responsible for antibiotic resistance and virulence, and also confirmed that the bacteria are related to opportunistic bacteria from the hospital environment. Other factors undoubtedly contribute to the imbalance between bacteria in the gut microbiota of children born by Cesarean section. One such factor is certainly the administration of antibiotics to the mother after a Cesarean section, longer hospitalization of the child and mother after a Cesarean section, and later access to breast milk. A healthy microbiota certainly has a beneficial effect on the maturation of the child's immune system, and epidemiological data show a higher risk of developing asthma and obesity later in life in children born by Cesarean section.

Infant Diet and Microbiota

Today, we know that the microbiota is created even before birth, and the so-called intensive primary colonization occurs at birth; the child acquires microorganisms from the mother's birth canal or from the hospital environment in the case of a Cesarean section. Of course, the composition of microorganisms in the child's intestine also changes very intensely after birth, and their main source is the diet the child receives.

Breastfeeding is optimal in the first six months.

In the first six months, breast milk is also very important in terms of creating the child's healthy microbiota, and the World Health Organization (WHO) recommends exclusive breastfeeding during this period. Breast milk is an optimal source of nutrients, but it is also important because it allows the growth of beneficial bacteria in the child's intestine. It contains oligosaccharides, which are an ideal prebiotic and allow the selective growth of so-called symbiotic bacteria and at the same time inhibit the growth of potentially harmful bacteria. Various antimicrobial substances in breast milk also prevent their growth.

With the introduction of solid foods, the child's microbiome begins to develop. The simple microbiome based on bifidobacteria, which primarily metabolize oligosaccharides from breast milk, begins to be supplemented by bacteria that also metabolize other foods. Bacteria of the Bacteroides genus "grow" on starch from more complex meals, and the period when breastfeeding gradually ends has the most significant impact on the microbiota [1].

Genetic Influence on the Gut Microbiota

Researchers have long known that the microbiota in the intestines of related individuals is often similar. Of course, we immediately think of environmental factors, such as the fact that relatives live in the same household and eat very similarly, which of course greatly affects the structure of their microbiota. Studies conducted on monozygotic twins, or studies in which environmental influences are excluded as much as possible, have shown that the microbiota is also conditioned by the individual's genes. Unfortunately, most of the data are found in studies on animals – in mice, for example, they have succeeded in discovering genomic regions that show a link between genes and the presence of specific microorganisms in the intestine. We do not yet have such data for humans.

Environmental Influence is Much Greater

Biologist Eran Segal came to interesting data by analyzing data from a study of the microbiota in 1,126 pairs of monozygotic twins conducted in 2016. He showed that the genetic influence on the microbiota is relatively small and amounts to about 1.9 to 8.1 percent. Segal also obtained very similar results when analyzing the microbiota of over 1,000 genetically diverse Orthodox Jews who emigrated to Israel and live there in very similar conditions. He confirmed the assumption that heredity has a relatively small influence on the composition of the gut microbiota compared to the environment [2].

Water is a major component of our body, accounting for approximately 75% of our total body weight in a healthy individual. Maintaining an optimal level of water in our body is crucial for the proper functioning of various tissues and cells.

What is dehydration?
Water is a vital component of our body, and it's essential to ensure that it constitutes 75% of our total body weight in a healthy individual. Maintaining an optimal level of water in our body is crucial for the proper functioning of numerous cells and tissues.

Water is typically lost through breathing, sweating, urination, and defecation. These losses need to be replenished by consuming water and other fluids. Dehydration refers to a condition where the body loses more water than it takes in, resulting in a deficiency of water.

Infants and children are particularly susceptible to dehydration, but it can also occur in adults. Severe dehydration can be life-threatening. Regular consumption of water and other fluids is necessary to maintain the body's proper hydration.

What causes dehydration?
As mentioned earlier, dehydration occurs when there is an imbalance between the amount of water lost and the amount of water and other fluids consumed. Therefore, dehydration can result from excessive water loss or insufficient water intake. In some cases, a combination of both factors can lead to dehydration.

Infants, children, the elderly, and individuals suffering from chronic illnesses are more likely to develop dehydration.

Vomiting and diarrhea are two of the most common causes of dehydration, as they lead to significant water loss and the depletion of essential minerals called electrolytes (typically minerals like sodium and potassium). These conditions can quickly lead to dehydration in infants and young children. Other causes of increased water loss include excessive urination (often seen in individuals with diabetes), excessive sweating (due to strenuous exercise, heat exposure, or outdoor activities), and illnesses that cause fever. In severe cases, burn injuries can cause significant water loss from the body, potentially leading to a life-threatening situation.

Typically, we lose about 10 cups of water from our body each day, and this needs to be replenished. Failure to replace lost water can lead to dehydration. We often tend to drink less water and other fluids when we are busy or sick. Limited access to drinking water when traveling or engaging in outdoor activities like hiking and camping can also reduce the amount of water we consume, leading to dehydration.

What are the symptoms and signs of dehydration?
Increased thirst is one of the first signs of reduced water content in our body. However, in some cases, we may not be able to drink water or other fluids immediately, and the condition progresses to dehydration. Reduced water content in the body is also reflected in the urine we produce. Urine output decreases when the body is experiencing water deficiency. It also becomes darker and more concentrated.

As dehydration progresses, we may start to feel weak or dizzy and may be unable to stand or walk properly. Our mouth may feel dry and sticky, and we may feel tired and unwell. In cases of prolonged dehydration, our eyes may become sunken, and we may experience a decrease in tear production.

How does dehydration manifest in infants and young children?
Infants and young children may not be able to express their thirst verbally. In such cases, parents need to be vigilant for signs of dehydration, especially if the child is experiencing vomiting or diarrhea. Dehydrated infants and young children may exhibit symptoms such as a dry, sticky mouth, dry lips, and decreased tear production. As mentioned earlier, the oceans are the largest producers of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere. However, because the oceans are so vast and it takes at least a few hundred years for them to fully warm up or cool down, there is an approximately eight-hundred-year difference between changes in atmospheric temperature and the amount of carbon dioxide. Scientists therefore argue that the oceans have a kind of "memory" of temperature changes. The warmer the atmosphere, the more plant and animal life there is, which means more carbon dioxide emissions and more life.

The greenhouse effect is just one small part of the Earth's climate system, and carbon dioxide has a relatively small impact on the overall greenhouse gas system, which includes water vapor (the most important greenhouse gas), carbon dioxide, nitrous oxide, methane, and ozone. The claim that any greenhouse gas has a leading impact on climate change has no basis in any credible scientific research on climate change.

Apocalyptic predictions about the impacts of climate change on life on Earth have become commonplace in our society. However, what needs to be understood is that these predictions are not new and that this theatrical performance has been going on for decades, with only the story changing slightly each time, but the effect remains the same. In the mid-1970s, we witnessed a widespread panic that the Earth's atmosphere would continue to cool, possibly leading to a new ice age. This theory was proven false when the atmospheric temperature began to rise again after 1975. In the mid-1970s, the theory of global warming began to be politicized. This was partly because some leaders, such as Margaret Thatcher, advocated for energy independence from global oil trade, with the Middle East being the largest exporter. The promotion of nuclear energy became a trend. The theory of global warming thus gained traction for political and economic reasons.

This game took on a new dimension when the United Nations established the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) in 1988, an organization that brought together scientists from around the world to prove the theory of human-caused global warming. Many scientists who participated in the research eventually withdrew and did not want their names on the list of public reports issued by the forum. The reasons are numerous, including misleading the public with false or even fabricated data and analysis results, most of which were based on computer modeling, and censoring comments from climate scientists who disagreed with the forum's official reports. Their requests to be removed from the official list of 2,500 scientists (the so-called "scientific community" that proponents of the theory always talk about) were not granted, and many began to seek justice in the courts. In addition to legal battles, many report harassment and threats, even death threats. It has become a very dirty political game, and anyone who disagrees with the accepted view is quickly and effectively silenced and removed from the stage.

In just the last two decades, proponents of the theory have presented us with several embellished fairy tales about what will happen in the next ten years due to drastic climate changes caused by humans. In December 2007, the BBC published an article titled "Arctic summers ice-free by 2013," claiming that the Arctic would be completely ice-free in the summer months by 2013. In 2005, the United Nations predicted that by 2015, there would be 50 million climate refugees fleeing the dire consequences of global warming. Today, we are witnessing a migration of people to the West, but these migrations have nothing to do with climate change. In 2003, the Pentagon issued a report predicting that California would be flooded by 2013 and that parts of the Netherlands would be completely uninhabitable. California was indeed flooded during this time, but only with illegal immigrants, drugs, homeless people, human waste, medieval diseases, and economic debt, and it has become a Third World country in which the wealthy leftist elites, who advocate for the theory, are increasingly distancing themselves from the dying middle class and the growing number of poor and homeless people. The Netherlands, except for the increasing number of Islamic ghettos and attacks by illegal immigrants, remains geographically the same country. In 2000, climate alarmists predicted that snowy winters in Great Britain would be just a memory. In 2009, England had one of the coldest winters in its documented climate history.

The theory of global warming has a powerful institutional driving force behind it today. In fact, we can speak of a "global warming promotion industry." This industry fills the pockets of many public employees, NGO activists, supervisors, environmental journalists, and others. What we are witnessing today is the rise of a giant bureaucratic monster that extends its tentacles into all areas of human life, with the sole desire to establish complete control over every individual on this planet. Control and taxation of carbon dioxide emissions is a form of neo-imperialism. The goal of these political movements is to prevent developing countries from developing their industries, becoming independent, and strong enough to resist the globalist world order. The programs that the United Nations has introduced to combat climate change are a complete waste of money and serve only to destroy the economies of all countries in the world.

The theory of global warming has become a new secular religion that is completely intolerant of those who think differently. Its adherents attack the Western way of life with the aim of completely destroying the social system and establishing a totalitarian ideological regime that serves only one purpose: to create a two-class social system in which the elites own all the wealth of the world and the slaves below them have no rights. On the way to this goal, they use every weapon at their disposal – the public school system, scientific organizations, political movements, the media, and even sixteen-year-old autistic children, whom they put on stage, give them a microphone, and laugh and applaud their foolish behavior.

Človeške aktivnosti skozi našo celotno zgodovino nikoli niso imele vpliva na podnebne spremembe. Tudi segrevanje ozračja, ki smo mu priča danes ni nekaj edinstvenega, nenaravnega, ampak se je v Zemljini preteklosti že večkrat zgodilo. Samo v zadnjih nekaj stoletjih je bilo človeštvo priča velikim podnebnim spremembam. Dva taka primera sta srednjeveško toplo obdobje (Medieval Warm Period), znano tudi kot srednjeveški klimatski optimum (Medieval Climactic Optimum), v severno-atlantski regiji, ki je trajalo približno od leta 900 do leta 1300 ter t.i. mala ledena doba (Little Ice Age), obdobje močne ohladitve, ki je nastopilo takoj po srednjeveškem toplem obdobju, približno od leta 1300 do leta 1850.
Moderna gibanja proti podnebnim spremembam temeljijo na lažeh in so v resnici politična gibanja katerih pravi nameni in cilji so številnim akademikom, znanstvenikom, politikom in medijem tako kot tudi širši javnosti prikriti. Mediji in znanstveniki vedno znova poudarjajo kako katastrofalno ljudje vplivamo na klimatske spremembe na našem planetu. Da nas je veliko preveč in da bi se moralo svetovno prebivalstvo drastično zmanjšati, ker več ljudi pomeni več ogljikovega dioksida in posledično bolj onesnaženo ozračje. Kako naša industrija z emisijami ogljikovega dioksida pripomore k visokemu dvigu temperature zraka in vode in kako bodo posledično številne živalske in rastlinske vrste izumrle, na koncu pa seveda tudi človek. Ideja, da je ogljikov dioksid onesnaževalec okolja je naravnost nora. Ogljikov dioksid je eden od štirih elementov, ki so potrebni za življenje na tem planetu, poleg vode, kisika in svetlobe. Ljudje smo relativno majhni proizvajalci ogljikovega dioksida, kljub vsej naši industriji in emisijam je naš delež prispevka zanemarljiv v primerjavi z drugimi proizvajalci ogljikovega dioksida. Odmrlo rastlinje, živalske fekalije in bakterije letno spustijo v ozračje veliko več ogljikovega dioksida kot ga človeštvo z industrijo. Vulkani so prav tako ogromen proizvajalec ogljikovega dioksida in en sam izbruh ogromnega vulkana lahko spusti v atmosfero več ogljikovega dioksida kot ga je človeštvo v vsej svoji zgodovini obstoja. Največji proizvajalec ogljikovega dioksida v ozračju pa so oceani. Ti letno vsrkavajo in izločajo ogromne količine ogljikovega dioksida, koliko, pa je odvisno od temperature ozračja.
Teorija o globalnem segrevanju trdi, da večanje emisij ogljikovega dioksida v ozračju povzroča višanje temperature ozračja. Podnebni paničarji nas prepričujejo, da je industrijska družba s svojimi emisijami uničila krhko ravnovesje v naši atmosferi in da bo to vodilo do drastičnih podnebnih sprememb, ekstremnih vremenskih fenomenov, popolnega taljenja ledu na polarnih območjih in uničenja gozdnatega sveta, izumrtja vrst ter širitev puščave. Znanost pa trdi nekaj povsem drugega.
Prvič, nikjer ni dokazano, da segrevanje ozračja, kot smo mu priča danes vodi do izumrtja živali in rastlin ter širjenja do puščave. Ravno nasprotno, globalno segrevanje vodi v veliko bolj zeleno okolje, bogato z raznolikimi živalskimi in rastlinskimi vrstami. Polarni medvedi so preživeli veliki holocenski klimatski optimum (The Holocene Climate Optimum), obdobje termalnega maksimuma, ki je trajalo približno 8.000 let. Drugič, nikjer ni dokazano da globalno segrevanje vodi v ekstremne vremenske primere. Ekstremni vremenski primeri so posledica mešanja toplih in mrzlih zračnih tokov. Globalno segrevanje v bistvu pomeni manj ekstremne vremenske razmere. In tretjič, nikjer ni dokazano, da globalno segrevanje, kot smo mu priča danes vodi v popolno uničenje ledenih polov. Znanstveniki so dokazali, da se led na Arktiki in Antarktiki letno krči in širi. Ta proces je bil dokumentiran skozi stoletja, seže celo v 10. stoletje, ko so vikingi opazovali premike ledu na Grenlandiji. Sploh pa samo bistvo teorije temelji na postavki, ki izraža popolno nasprotje realnosti. Višanje koncentracije ogljikovega dioksida v ozračju je posledica višanja temperature ozračja in ne obratno, kot trdi teorija. Paleoklimatologi, ki so preučevali primerke ledu so v številnih raziskavah prišli do istega zaključka: temperatura naraste ali pade in po nekaj sto letih ogljikov dioksid sledi. Temperatura torej vodi ogljikov dioksid in ne obratno. Ogljikov dioksid je produkt temperaturnih sprememb.
Kot je bilo omenjeno že zgoraj so največji proizvajalci ogljikovega dioksida v ozračju oceani. Toplejši kot so več ogljikovega dioksida spustijo v ozračje in hladnejši kot so, več ga vsrkajo vase. A ker so oceani tako ogromni in je potrebo vsaj nekaj sto let preden se popolnoma ogrejejo oziroma ohladijo je med spremembo temperature ozračja in količino ogljikovega dioksida približno osemstoletna razlika. Znanstveniki zato trdijo, da imajo oceani t.i. spomin o temperaturnih spremembah. Toplejše kot je ozračje več je tudi rastlinja in živalskih vrst kar pomeni več emisij ogljikovega dioksida v ozračje in več življenja.
Efekt tople grede je le en majhen del zemeljskega podnebnega sistema in ogljikov dioksid ima v celotnem sistemu toplogrednih plinov (sestavljajo ga vodna para, ki je najpomembnejši toplogredni plin, ogljikov dioksid, dušikov oksid, metan in ozon) relativno majhen vpliv. Trditev, da ima katerikoli toplogredni plin vodilni vpliv na klimatske spremembe nima nobenih temeljev v nobeni verodostojni znanstveni raziskavi o podnebnih spremembah.
Apokaliptične napovedi glede vplivov klimatskih sprememb na življenje na Zemlji so danes v naši družbi postale nekaj povsem vsakdanjega. Vendar kar je potrebno razumeti je to, da nikakor niso nekaj novega in da se ta teatrična predstava odvija že nekaj desetletij, le zgodba je vsakokrat malce spremenjena, njen učinek pa je vedno isti. V sredini sedemdesetih let smo bili priča vsesplošnemu preplahu, da se bo zemeljsko ozračje vedno bolj ohlajalo dokler ne bo nastopila mogoče celo nova ledena doba. Te teorija je bila dokazana kot lažna, ko se je po letu 1975 temperatura ozračja ponovno začela dvigovati. V sredini sedemdesetih let se je začela politizacija teorije globalnega segrevanja. Razlog je bil predvsem v tem, da so nekateri voditelji, kot na primer Margaret Thatcher zagovarjali energijsko neodvisnost od globalnega trgovanja z nafto kateri največji izvoznik so bile države Bližnjega vzhoda. Promocija nuklearne energije je postala trend. Teorija o globalnem segrevanju je tako pridobila na veljavi zaradi političnih in ekonomskih razlogov.
Ta igra je dobila novo razsežnost, ko so Združeni narodi leta 1988 ustanovili t.i. Medvladni forum za podnebne spremembe (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change – IPCC), organizacijo, ki je povezala znanstvenike iz vsega sveta z namenom, da dokažejo teorijo globalnega segrevanja, ki naj bi ga povzročal človek, kot verodostojno. Številni znanstveniki, ki so sodelovali pri raziskavah so sčasoma prekinili sodelovanje in niso hoteli svojih imen na spisku javnih poročil, ki jih je forum izdajal javnosti. Razlogi so številni, kakor oni sami navajajo, med drugimi zavajanje javnosti z napačnimi ali celo izmišljenimi podatki in analiznimi rezultati, katerih velika večina je temeljila na računalniškem modeliranju in cenzuriranju komentarjev podnebnih znanstvenikov, ki se ne strinjajo z uradnimi poročili foruma. Njihovim prošnjam o odstranitvi iz uradnega seznama 2.500 znanstvenikov (t.i. scientific community o katerem privrženci teorije vedno govorijo) ni bilo ustreženo in številni so pravico začeli iskati na sodiščih. Poleg pravnih bitk mnogi poročajo o ustrahovanju in grožnjah, celo s smrtjo. Vse skupaj je postala zelo umazana politična igra in vsi, ki se s sprejetim mišljenjem ne strinjajo so hitro in učinkovito utišani in odstranjeni z odra.
Samo v zadnjih dveh desetletjih so nam zagovorniki teorije postregli s kar nekaj začinjenimi pravljicami o tem, kaj naj bi se v desetih letih od danes zgodilo zaradi drastičnih klimatskih sprememb, ki naj bi jih povzročal človek. BBC je decembra 2007 objavil članek Arctic summers ice-free by 2013, v katerem trdijo da bo Arktika že leta 2013 v poletnih mesecih popolnoma brez ledu. Leta 2005 so Združeni narodi napovedali do bo do leta 2015 petdeset milijonov podnebnih prebežnikov, ki bodo bežali pred grozovitimi posledicami globalnega segrevanja. Danes sicer smo priča invaziji migrantov in to na Zahod. Vendar te migracije seveda nimajo nobene veze s klimatskimi spremembami. Leta 2003 je Pentagon izdal poročilo v katerem napovedujejo, da bo Kalifornija do leta 2013 poplavljena in da bodo deli Nizozemske popolnoma neprimerni za bivanje. Kalifornija je v tem času sicer res bila poplavljena a zgolj z ilegalnimi migranti, drogami, brezdomci, človeškimi fekalijami, srednjeveškimi boleznimi in ekonomskim dolgom ter se je spremenila v državo tretjega sveta v kateri se bogate levičarske elite, ki zagovarjajo teorijo, vedno bolj oddaljujejo od umirajočega srednjega razreda in naraščajočega števila revežev in brezdomcev. Nizozemska pa razen seveda naraščajočega števila islamskih getov in napadov ilegalnih migrantov zaenkrat geografsko še vedno ostaja enaka država. Leta 2000 so podnebni paničarji napovedali, da so zime polne snega v Veliki Britaniji samo še spomin. Leta 2009 je Anglija imela eno najbolj mrzlih zim v dokumentirani klimatski zgodovini otoške države.
Teorija o globalnem segrevanju ima danes za seboj mogočno institucionalno gonilno silo. Dejansko lahko govorimo o „industriji promocije globalnega segrevanja“. Ta industrija polni žepe številnim javnim uslužbencem, nevladnim aktivistom, nadzornikom, okoljskim novinarjem in drugim. Čemur smo danes priča je vzpon gigantske birokratske pošasti, ki steguje svoje lovke na vsa področja človeškega bivanja in katere edina želja je vzpostaviti popoln nadzor nad vsakim posameznikom na tem planetu. Kontrola in obdavčevanje emisij ogljikovega dioksida je oblika neoimperializma. Cilj teh političnih gibanj je preprečiti državam tretjega sveta, da bi razvile svojo industrijo, postale neodvisne, močne in tako sposobne upreti se globalističnemu svetovnemu redu. Programi, ki so jih Združeni narodi uvedli za boj proti klimatskim spremembam so popolna izguba denarja in služijo samo temu, da uničijo ekonomije vseh držav po svetu.
Teorija o globalnem segrevanju je postala nova sekularna religija, ki je povsem netolerantna do drugače mislečih. Njeni privrženci napadajo zahodnjaški način življenja z razlogom, da popolnoma zrušijo družbeni sistem in vzpostavijo totalitarni ideološki režim, ki služi samo enemu namenu: ustvariti dvorazredni družbeni sistem v katerem vladajo elite, ki si lastijo vse premoženje sveta in pod njimi sužnji, ki nimajo nobenih pravic. Na poti k temu cilju uporabljajo vsako orožje, ki jim je na voljo – javni šolski sistem, znanstvene organizacije, politična gibanja, medije in tudi šestnajstletne avtistične otroke katere postavijo na podij, jim potisnejo mikrofon v roko ter se smejijo in ploskajo njihovemu neumnemu vedenju.

Iron is an important component of proteins that transport oxygen throughout the body. Hemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen in red blood cells, accounts for approximately two-thirds of the body's iron stores. Smaller amounts are found in myoglobin, the protein that supplies oxygen to muscles, and in enzymes that are needed for various biochemical reactions.
In addition, varying amounts of iron are stored in proteins that release it into the bloodstream as needed. The more iron that is absorbed from food, the higher the level of stored iron.
Iron deficiency can cause a number of unpleasant symptoms, including fatigue and weakness, poor work performance, an increased risk of infection, difficulty maintaining body temperature, dizziness, rapid heartbeat, and shortness of breath.
Population studies have shown that people who regularly engage in strenuous exercise, especially adolescents and vegetarians, are at increased risk of developing iron deficiency anemia.
There are two types of iron in the diet: heme iron and non-heme iron. Heme iron, which is found only in meat and fish, is much better absorbed than non-heme iron, which is found in vegetables, fortified foods, supplements, and foods cooked in cast iron cookware.
While 15 to 30 percent of heme iron is absorbed, only five percent of non-heme iron enters the bloodstream.
Various factors can either worsen or improve iron absorption. Some vegetables, such as spinach, contain oxalic acid, which inhibits absorption.
High-fiber foods, such as whole grains containing phytates, and foods high in calcium also reduce the amount of iron that enters the bloodstream. However, vitamin C and other acids naturally present in fruits, fruit juices, and some vegetables improve its absorption.
Iron deficiency anemia (sideropenic deficiency anemia – SDA) accounts for half of all forms of anemia. However, when we talk about low iron levels, we are not necessarily talking about SDA. Iron deficiency anemia develops over a longer period.
In the early stages, iron levels gradually decrease, as do levels of ferritin, the main iron storage protein. In the next phase, iron levels decrease further, and transferrin levels (which is responsible for transporting iron ions in the human body) increase – an adaptive response that attempts to increase iron absorption. In the final, third phase, iron deficiency prevents the formation of hemoglobin, causing red blood cells to shrink and become “pale,” and blood tests show anemia. Fatigue (given that hemoglobin carries oxygen to body cells) is just one of the symptoms.
Sideropenic anemia develops slowly, so patients often do not experience symptoms for a long time. General symptoms of anemia may appear, including fatigue, nausea, shortness of breath during exertion, tachycardia, and changes in behavior; headache, irritability, and tingling in the body. Loss of appetite, nausea, and constipation are also common, as is pallor of the skin and mucous membranes. The recommended daily intake of iron for an adult is 14 mg. The main sources in the diet are cereals and cereal products, meat and meat products, fish, legumes, vegetables, and fruits.

Železo je pomemben del beljakovin, ki prenašajo kisik v telesu. Hemoglobin, beljakovina, ki prenaša kisik v rdečih krvničkah, predstavlja približno dve tretjini telesnih zalog železa. Manjše količine so v mioglobinu, beljakovini, ki oskrbuje mišice s kisikom, in v encimih, ki so potrebni za različne biokemične reakcije.
Poleg tega je različna količina železa shranjena v beljakovinah, ki ga po potrebi sprostijo v kri. Več ko se ga absorbira s hrano, višja je raven shranjenega železa.
Pomanjkanje železa lahko povzroči številne neprijetne simptome, med drugim utrujenost in šibkost, slabo delovno učinkovitost, povečano tveganje za okužbe, težave z ohranjanjem toplote, vrtoglavico, hitro bitje srca in zadihanost.
Populacijske študije so pokazale, da so ljudje, ki se redno ukvarjajo z naporno vadbo, zlasti mladostniki in vegetarijanci, izpostavljeni večjemu tveganju za razvoj anemije zaradi pomanjkanja železa.
V prehrani sta dve vrsti železa, hemsko in nehemsko. Hemsko, ki ga najdemo le v mesu in ribah, se veliko bolje absorbira kot nehemsko, ki je v zelenjavi, obogateni hrani, prehranskih dopolnilih in kislih živilih, pripravljenih v litoželeznih posodah.
Medtem ko se absorbira 15 do 30 odstotkov hemskega železa, pride v kri le pet odstotkov nehemskega.
Izkoristek železa lahko poslabšajo ali izboljšajo različni dejavniki. Nekatera zelenjava, na primer špinača, vsebuje oksalno kislino, ki ovira absorpcijo.
Živila z veliko vlakninami, kot so polnozrnata žita, ki vsebujejo fitate, in živila z visoko vsebnostjo kalcija prav tako zmanjšujejo količino železa, ki pride v kri. Toda vitamin C in druge kisline, ki so naravno prisotne v sadju, sadnih sokovih in nekaterih vrstah zelenjave, njegovo absorpcijo izboljšajo.
Anemija zaradi pomanjkanja železa (sideropenična deficitarna anemija – SDA) obsega kar polovico vseh oblik slabokrvnosti. A ko govorimo o znižani ravni železa, ne govorimo obenem tudi o SDA. Anemija zaradi pomanjkanja se namreč razvija dlje.
V zgodnejši fazi raven železa postopoma upada, tako kot raven beljakovine feritin, železovega poglavitnega skladiščnega mesta. V naslednji fazi se ravni železa še bolj znižajo, ravni transferina (v človeškem telesu namenjen prenosu železovih ionov) pa povišajo – prilagoditveni odgovor poskuša povečati absorpcijo železa. V zadnji, tretji fazi pomanjkanje železa onemogoča oblikovanje hemoglobina, zaradi česar se rdeče krvničke pomanjšajo in »obledijo«, krvni testi pa pokažejo na anemijo. Utrujenost (glede na to, da hemoglobin vodi kisik do telesnih celic) je samo eden od znakov.

Rust is a common form of corrosion that occurs when metal atoms react with their environment. Salt water doesn’t cause metal to rust, but it does accelerate the rusting process because the electrons in salt water move more easily than in fresh water.
How metals rust
Not all metals rust. For example, aluminum doesn’t rust because it has a protective layer of aluminum oxide on its surface. This prevents the metal from coming into direct contact with water (or moisture in the air) and oxygen. On the other hand, iron does rust because it forms hydrated iron oxide when it comes into contact with water (or moisture in the air) and oxygen.
Rust cannot form without water and oxygen. Water helps iron react with oxygen by breaking down the oxygen molecule. In the early stages of rusting, iron loses electrons, and oxygen gains electrons. The iron and iron ions then react with water to form iron hydroxide, iron hydroxide, and hydrogen. The hydroxides lose water and form even more iron compounds. The sum of all these chemical reactions causes the rust to flake off, so it falls off the iron and exposes new iron, which can then also begin to rust.
Salt water vs. Fresh water
Current flows more easily in salt water than in fresh water. This is because salt water, a solution of electrolytes, contains more dissolved ions than fresh water, which means that electrons can move more easily. Because rust is all about the movement of electrons, iron rusts faster in salt water than in fresh water. Some metal objects that spend a lot of time submerged in salt water, such as boat engines, rust quickly. However, objects do not have to be completely submerged in salt water for this to happen, because increased humidity in the air and airborne salt can provide the cation electrolyte (positive ions) and anions (negative ions).
Preventing metal from rusting
Coating iron with a protective layer of zinc prevents it from rusting because the zinc stops the reaction between the iron and oxygen and water. This is known as galvanization. A specially made paint can also prevent salt water or salty air from rusting metal.

Protection of Farm Animals
Farm animals are animals that are raised or bred for the production of food, wool, hides, or fur. Their protection involves measures to prevent unnecessary suffering or injury to the animals and to ensure appropriate housing, food, and care. To maintain animal welfare, keepers are required to monitor the health of the animals and regularly inspect the technical equipment used in intensive animal farming systems.

Cattle
Tethering of Calves
Calves up to 6 months of age are prohibited from being tethered.
There are several reasons for this prohibition:
- When resting or sleeping, calves adopt various positions, which may involve having their legs extended, their heads resting on the ground, or resting on their legs. If a calf is physically prevented from adopting such a position or if there is a risk of pain in that position, the calf will adopt a less comfortable position and try to rest or sleep differently. However, this type of rest is much less effective.
- Exploratory behavior (searching in the bedding) and escape from perceived danger (real or imaginary) are very important parts of calf behavior and are present in all calves. Preventing such behavior likely causes the development of stereotypies (one of the more obvious behavioral indicators of stress) and other behavioral disorders. In addition to the possibility of free movement, calves also need bedding.
- Movement is essential for normal development of bones and muscles. If calves are prevented from moving, they can develop serious musculoskeletal problems, which can manifest as difficulty walking. Transport to the slaughterhouse is consequently much more strenuous for them, and stress indicators are also more obvious in these animals.
Wintering of Grazing Animals Outdoors
This is an increasingly common farming method that, if properly implemented, does not pose a risk to animal welfare. It is practiced with various types and categories of animals. Cattle (especially dairy cows, dry cows, and breeding heifers), as well as sheep and horses, are suitable for this type of farming. Wintering cows outdoors during lactation presents a greater challenge for farmers, as these animals need to be provided with a special feeding regime to prevent a drop in milk production. The energy requirement of grazing animals increases by 15 to 20% on very cold days. At that time, the animals eat more feed to ensure they have enough energy to maintain their body temperature.
A farmer who decides to winter his animals outdoors must first become well acquainted with the specific weather conditions (temperature, precipitation, wind) and other environmental characteristics of the area where he intends to winter his animals (terrain, watercourses, possible floods, flash floods, landslides, etc.).
It is important that the animals are in good physical condition at the beginning of winter. As throughout the year, animals outdoors must be protected from adverse weather conditions, predators, and other dangers. In adverse weather conditions, they must have at least protection from strong winds and a dry place to rest. Shelter can be natural (bushes, forest) or built. An adequate supply of feed and drinking water must be ensured.
During severe cold, it is important that the animals are clean and dry, as wet and muddy fur has less insulating capacity.
Winter temperatures in Slovenia are usually between 0°C and 5°C, rarely -10°C or -15°C. These climatic conditions are very suitable for wintering sheep and other grazing animals outdoors.
Important advantages of proper wintering of grazing animals outdoors include greater overall resistance of the animals, more profitable meat production, and a beneficial effect on the health of the musculoskeletal system.

Pigs
Castration of Piglets
Castration of piglets is only permitted if it does not involve tearing of tissue. This procedure is permitted in piglets up to the seventh day of age. Later, it can only be performed by a veterinarian using anesthesia or long-term pain relief.
Tail Docking of Piglets
Routine tail docking is not permitted. The keeper must implement other measures to reduce aggression between animals before performing this procedure. These usually include reducing the stocking density of the pens and introducing toys and manipulable materials (e.g., straw). Tail docking is also only permitted up to the seventh day of age. Later, it can only be performed by a veterinarian using anesthesia or long-term pain relief.

Laying Hens
Elimination of Unenriched Cages for Laying Hens
On January 1, 2012, the use of unenriched cages for raising laying hens was prohibited throughout the European Union (EU). Laying hens can now only be raised in enriched cages, which must be designed in a prescribed manner, or in "alternative" systems (barn systems, free-range systems).
Egg Labeling
Every egg you buy in a store must be labeled with a registration number, consisting of numbers (e.g., 2SI062502), which means:
- type of farming,
- country code (Sl),
- two-digit TRACES number of the regional office of the Administration for Food Safety, Veterinary and Plant Protection (from 01 to 13),
- serial number of the farm, and
- serial number of the facility.
The number for the type of farming is assigned according to the following code:
- number 1 for free-range farming,
- number 2 for barn farming,
- number 3 for battery farming,
- number 0 for organic farming.
This method of egg labeling allows consumers to decide whether to support animal-friendly farming practices by purchasing eggs.

Animal Protection During Stunning and Slaughter
Care for animal welfare does not end when the animal leaves the farm, but it is necessary to ensure that the animal is cared for until the last moment of its life, i.e., also during the procedures involving slaughter or euthanasia.
Therefore, animal slaughter and related procedures must be carried out in a way that causes the most humane death to the animal, in a way that minimizes pain, distress, fear, and suffering that cannot be avoided. Animal protection during slaughter begins on the farm with the preparation of the animal for slaughter, followed by ensuring that it is suitable for transport and finally with the procedures leading to slaughter in a slaughterhouse or on a farm.
Personnel involved in loading and unloading, moving, housing, care, restraint, stunning, slaughter, and bleeding of animals play an important role in the welfare of these animals. Therefore, there must be an adequate number of personnel who are patient, considerate, competent, and properly trained.
Scientific opinions on animal stunning are publicly available on the website of the European Food Safety Agency (EFSA).

Authority for Supervision of Animal Protection During Stunning and Slaughter
The Administration for Food Safety, Veterinary and Plant Protection has the authority to supervise the implementation of the Regulation on Animal Protection During Euthanasia, except for the supervision of the suitability of instructions for the use of equipment for restricting movement and stunning animals. The Market Inspectorate of the Republic of Slovenia carries out supervision of this.

Achievements in the Field of Animal Welfare
Animal welfare is a priority for the EU. Over the past 40 years, EU legislation on animal welfare has evolved based on solid scientific evidence, public expectations, and market demands.
To ensure a uniform approach to the implementation of animal welfare legislation throughout the EU, the European Commission has been funding initiatives and training workshops for experts both within and outside the EU since 2006. This ensures that animal products produced in the EU are of high quality and also meet consumer expectations regarding animal welfare.
More than 2,000 veterinarians have been trained in animal welfare through the European Commission's program.
In 2012, the ban on raising laying hens in conventional cages came into force in the EU. The hens now have more space in the cages, which are equipped with a nest, perches, and bedding, which allows them to satisfy their behavioral needs. Extensive resources are available to demonstrate that the health and welfare of the hens have improved significantly.
Greater respect for the behavioral needs of pigs leads to higher quality pork, which is an area where the EU is a major producer and exporter. By the end of 2012, sows were living in individual stalls, where their behavioral needs were not met due to the impoverished environment. The EU adopted special legislation to improve pig welfare, which abolished the use of individual stalls. Sows are housed in groups during gestation. This is a key element for the welfare of these highly social animals. The sows can now move freely, and the pens are also equipped with suitable nesting material.
In 2017, the EU Platform for Animal Welfare was established, which is a forum for dialogue between various stakeholders, a place for exchanging good practices and voluntary initiatives. It also serves as an advisory body to the European Commission on animal welfare.

The European Convention for the Protection of Animals Kept for Farming Purposes applies to animals that are raised or bred for the production of food, wool, hides, or fur. To maintain animal welfare, keepers are required to monitor the health of the animals and regularly inspect the technical equipment used in intensive animal farming systems.

Kokoši nesnice je poslej dovoljeno gojiti zgolj v obogatenih kletkah, ki morajo biti oblikovane na predpisan način ali pa v »alternativnih« rejah (hlevska reja, prosta reja).

Zato morajo biti zakol živali in z njim povezani postopki opravljeni tako, da povzročijo čim bolj humano smrt živali in sicer na način, ki zmanjša bolečino, stisko, strah in trpljenje, ki se ji ni mogoče izogniti, kar na najmanjšo mero. Zaščita živali pri zakolu pa se začne že na gospodarstvu in sicer s pripravo živali za zakol, nadalje z zagotovitvijo, da je primerna za prevoz in končno s postopki, ki vodijo do zakola v klavnici ali na kmetiji.

Dobrobit živali je prednostna naloga EU. V zadnjih 40 letih se je zakonodaja EU o dobrobiti živali razvila na podlagi trdnih znanstvenih spoznanj, pričakovanj državljanov in zahtev trga.
Da bi zagotovila enoten način uveljavljanja zakonodaje o dobrobiti živali po vsej EU, je Evropska komisija od leta 2006 financirala pobude in delavnice za usposabljanje strokovnjakov znotraj in zunaj EU. To zagotavlja, da so živila živalskega izvora, proizvedena v EU, kakovostna, hkrati pa izpolnjujejo pričakovanja potrošnika glede dobrobiti živali.
Več kot 2.000 veterinarjev je bilo usposobljenih na področju dobrobiti živali iz programa Evropske komisije.
V letu 2012 je začela v EU veljati prepoved reje kokoši nesnic v konvencionalnih kletkah. Zdaj imajo kokoši nesnice več prostora v kletkah, slednje pa so opremljene z gnezdom, gredmi in nastiljem, kar omogoča zadovoljitev vedenjskih potreb kokoši. Večje spoštovanje vedenjskih potreb prašičev vodi v kakovostnejše prašičje meso, to pa je področje, kjer je EU glavni proizvajalec in izvoznik. Do konca leta 2012 so breje svinje preživljale življenje v individualnih kletkah, kjer vedenjske potrebe zaradi osiromašenega okolja niso bile spoštovane. EU je za izboljšanje dobrobiti svinj sprejela posebno zakonodajo, s katero je ukinila uporabo individualnih namestitev. Svinje se med brejostjo namestijo v skupine. To je ključni element za dobrobit teh zelo družabnih živali. Zdaj se svinje lahko prosto gibljejo, boksi pa so opremljeni tudi z ustreznim gnezdilnim materialom.
V letu 2017 je bila ustanovljena Platforma EU za dobrobit živali, ki je mesto dialoga med različnimi deležniki, mesto izmenjave dobrih praks in prostovoljnih pobud. Hkrati deluje kot svetovalno telo Evropski komisiji na področju dobrobiti živali.

Children are much more susceptible to various diseases because their immune systems are not as well-developed as those of adults. Furthermore, they spend a lot of time in environments where the transmission of such infections is high (daycare, playgrounds, etc.). In general, infectious childhood diseases are not dangerous if they proceed without complications, and the child actually develops immunity to them – meaning they will not recur in later life; the only exception is scarlet fever, which a child can contract multiple times.
In the vast majority of cases, these diseases are accompanied by a fever, which is the first warning sign that something is happening to the child, so we must pay special attention to it.

Chickenpox
This is the most common and highly contagious viral (herpes virus) childhood disease, but despite its invasiveness, it is not dangerous. It is also true that the infection manifests more severely in adults (i.e., if they did not have chickenpox in childhood) than in children, so it is actually beneficial for a child to contract this disease as soon as possible. Most often, children between the ages of 5 and 10 contract the disease between January and May. The infection is transmitted through the virulent rash on the skin, i.e., through droplets when in contact with an infected person. Incubation period: 10–21 days.

Symptoms
The disease progresses in three stages. In the first stage (2 days), the disease erupts. A fever appears, along with a runny nose, sore throat, and headache. In the second stage, fluid-filled blisters appear all over the body. These can be anywhere, including the scalp, ears, throat, genitals, and, of course, on the skin all over the body. The appearance of the blisters occurs in waves, so some may be very fresh, while others are already drying up. The last, third stage involves the drying of these blisters. This creates scabs and shallow ulcers on the skin, which can remain visible for life.

What to do?
Reduce any fever with appropriate medication; provide the child with plenty of fluids and rest. Sometimes, the use of products to help dry out the blisters (liquid powders, etc.) was recommended for their care, but now it is more or less accepted that we should reduce the feeling of itching that the blisters cause. In this case, the doctor will prescribe a syrup with an antihistamine or advise the use of products that are applied to the skin and locally relieve itching. By preventing scratching, we reduce the risk of permanent visible consequences of chickenpox on the child's skin in the form of the aforementioned scars.

Scarlet Fever
This is the only disease listed here that is of bacterial origin. It is also the only one that a child can contract multiple times before developing immunity to it. It is transmitted through droplets and can also be transmitted through contaminated objects. It erupts suddenly, with a high fever, headache, and accompanying abdominal pain, which may be accompanied by vomiting and/or diarrhea. Incubation period: 3–5 days.

Symptoms:
fever, pain anywhere in the body, especially in the abdomen. A severe sore throat develops, with redness on the cheeks and a characteristic whitish area around the mouth. The tongue is very red, rough, and coated with a white layer. A characteristic red rash appears 2 days after the onset of symptoms and is in the form of small areas of red, rough skin, especially in the abdomen and armpits, and begins to fade about 3–5 days after its onset. The end of the disease is marked in its second week, when the skin on the soles of the feet and palms begins to peel off in layers.

What to do?
The doctor will prescribe an appropriate antibiotic and a medication to reduce the fever, and we must also ensure that the child drinks plenty of fluids and gets plenty of rest during the illness.

All infectious childhood diseases are quite taxing for a child, so we should ensure that they get plenty of rest during the illness. Because these diseases are usually accompanied by a fever, which can cause dehydration, we must offer the child plenty of fluids.

Fifth Disease
(erythema infectiosum) This is an infectious childhood disease transmitted by a virus, which is accompanied by a characteristic rash. It is less often accompanied by pain due to inflammation in the joints. The virus affects cells in the bone marrow, from which red blood cells (erythrocytes) later develop, so a consequence of fifth disease is often mild and transient anemia. The infection is transmitted through droplets and is more common in spring. Incubation period: 7–14 days, in some cases up to 21 days.

Symptoms:
a characteristic red rash on the child's cheeks; this can also spread to other parts of the body (especially on the limbs and buttocks); the rash is sharply defined and is usually in the shape of a butterfly; mild fever at the onset of the disease; joint pain (less common), anemia.

What to do?
In fact, there is nothing we can do. Any fever can be reduced with suppositories or syrup for fever, and the same medications can be used to relieve pain from any joint inflammation. Anemia is treated with iron supplements as directed by a doctor. The disease resolves on its own in a few days, the rash disappears in 2–30 days, and rest is recommended for the child's care.

Fever appears well before the characteristic rash, so when a child has a fever, we should also consider the possibility that they have one of the infectious childhood diseases.

Sixth Disease (roseola infantum)
This is an acute viral childhood illness, very similar to fifth disease. The two diseases differ in the height of the fever – in sixth disease, the fever can reach up to 40 °C at the onset of the disease, so it is essential to reduce it appropriately in this case. In young children (up to 2 years), we must also be aware of the possibility of febrile seizures with such a high fever. The fever is usually persistent and can last up to 3 days. Accompanying inflammation of the upper respiratory tract can also cause additional problems. When the temperature drops, a characteristic red rash appears in the child, and at that time the child is no longer contagious. Incubation period: 7–14 days.

Symptoms:
high fever, lasting up to 3 days, followed by the appearance of a red rash all over the child's body; the rash can also appear in the form of small spots that affect the skin all over the child's body.

What to do?
First of all, ensure that the child's fever is reduced appropriately, give them plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration, and allow them to rest.

The impact of a child's immunity on infectious diseases
Children who have a well-developed immune system are less likely to contract the aforementioned infectious diseases. The most we can do for a child's immunity is to offer them a varied, vitamin-rich diet. Children who are not eating well are also more likely to get sick. In addition, we must ensure that the child gets as much exercise as possible in the fresh air and, of course, gets enough rest to build up their strength and thus be better able to defend themselves against diseases.

The article was published in the magazine Naša lekarna, No. 61, March 2012.

Morebitno povišano telesno temperaturo znižujemo z za to ustreznimi sredstvi; otroku nudimo dovolj tekočine in počitka. Včasih so za nego mehurčkov priporočali uporabo sredstev, ki so jih pomagali sušiti (tekoči pudri ipd.), zdaj pa bolj ali manj velja, da zmanjšujemo občutek srbečice, ki ga mehurčki povzročajo. Značilen rdeč izpuščaj se pojavi 2 dni po nastopu simptomov in je v obliki drobnih predelov rdeče, hrapave kože zlasti na področju trebuha in pazduh ter začne bledeti približno 3–5 dni po svojem izbruhu. Zdravnik bo otroku predpisal ustrezen antibiotik in sredstvo za zniževanje temperature, prav tako pa moramo poskrbeti, da bo otrok tekom bolezni pil dovolj tekočine in veliko počival.

Pravzaprav ne moremo narediti ničesar. Morebitno povišano telesno temperaturo znižujemo s svečkami ali sirupom proti vročini, prav tako z istimi sredstvi blažimo bolečino zaradi morebitnega vnetja v sklepih. Pri majhnih otrocih (do 2 let) moramo biti ob takšni vročini pozorni tudi na pojav vročinskih krčev. Povišana temperatura je običajno vztrajna in se lahko vleče tudi do 3 dni. Predvsem skrbimo za to, da otroku ustrezno znižujemo povišano telesno temperaturo, mu hkrati dajemo za piti dovolj tekočine, da preprečimo morebitno dehidracijo, in mu omogočimo dovolj počitka.

Otroci, ki imajo dobro razvit imunski sistem, redkeje zbolevajo za omenjenimi nalezljivimi boleznimi. Beets are relatively easy to grow, but if agricultural practices are not followed, the leaves can turn red. In such cases, the plants are stunted and develop improperly.
It is important to note that red leaves on beets are not always a sign of disease. In some varieties (Sugar and Burgundy), the tips turn red due to frequent and heavy watering. Usually, this vegetable is not well-nourished, but this redness does not affect the quality or yield. Therefore, if the plant is developing normally, there is no need to worry. However, if growth is stunted, the cause should be identified and addressed as soon as possible.

Reason 1: Acidic soil
This is the most common cause of red beet leaves. Beets prefer soil with a neutral pH, so acidic soil should be prepared before planting (carefully mix with a mixture of ash - 2-3 glasses of wood ash per 10 liters of water). In the fall, it is recommended to add lime or dolomite flour (450-500 g per square meter) to the soil.
Liming the soil not only reduces acidity but also helps with phosphorus absorption, which is an important element for the proper development of this plant.
Reason 2: Nutrient deficiencies
Redness of the beet tips can be caused by a lack of phosphorus, potassium, magnesium, manganese, or sodium. For example, a phosphorus deficiency causes the above-ground part of the plant to first turn dark green and then red after a certain period.
A potassium deficiency also causes the leaves to turn dark red (especially along the edges), and in severe cases, they become diseased and dry out. This disease is often called laconic necrosis.
A magnesium deficiency causes the tips to turn color and curl, while a manganese and sodium deficiency also causes redness on the cut part of the plant.
Regular fertilization will help to replenish the missing elements in the soil. To correct a magnesium and manganese deficiency, it is recommended to use a manure solution (1:10) or chicken manure solution (1:20). The application rate is 1 liter per 1 running meter.
Beets need well-fertilized soil with a neutral pH.
Red beets also benefit from being treated with lime and potassium: 200 g of lime and 80 g of potassium chloride are dissolved in 10 liters of water, everything is mixed well, and the plants are watered every 14 days at a rate of 1 liter of solution per meter. Fertilization is stopped when the signs of nutrient deficiency disappear.
To correct a sodium deficiency, add it to the irrigation water (at a rate of 1 tablespoon per 10 liters of water). A phosphorus deficiency is compensated for with superphosphate at a rate of 30-40 g per square meter.
Keep in mind that if there is an excess of micro- and macro-elements, the beet leaves can also turn red. Therefore, follow the fertilizer application rates carefully.
Reason 3: Cooling of beets
This problem is more difficult to address than the previous ones. If the beet leaves are not only red but also have edges that are curled and the entire leaf blade is covered with brown-chestnut dry spots in which holes form, then the plant has been attacked by a fungal disease - cercosporosis.
Symptoms of cercosporosis in beets
This disease affects both sugar and fodder beets. It most often occurs in the second half of summer in wet weather. The fungus can reduce the yield by almost half. Therefore, it is important to start treatment in a timely manner and not to forget about preventive measures.
Before planting, treat the seeds with a solution of potassium permanganate. After the seedlings appear, spray the plants 3-4 times during the growing season with any fungicide, and once every 10-14 days, treat them with copper-containing preparations (for example, a 1% solution of blue vitriol).
In addition, remove damaged and dried leaves from the bed in a timely manner. The bed should be well-ventilated. In hot and dry weather, water the plants abundantly and loosen the soil around them.
Careful care of beets is the key to healthy tops and tasty roots. To properly care for the plants and prevent changes in the color of the leaves, use our tips from the article "Growing Beets - Revealing All the Secrets."

The Eye and Correction of Vision Problems
The eye is a sensory organ that detects optical information. It perceives visible light, which has a wavelength between 380 and 700 nm (the wavelength of light is expressed in nm or nanometers, one nanometer is one millionth of a millimeter). Below 380 nm is UV light, which is extremely harmful to the eye, as it can cause irreparable damage. It is recommended to use lenses that block UV light – especially sunglasses, which should be of high quality to prevent eye damage. Above 700 nm is IR (infrared) light or thermal radiation, which is also dangerous for the eye.

The Visual Pathway
The visual pathway begins with the reflection of light from the observed object. The light travels through the cornea, where the refraction of light begins, to the pupil. This is an opening in the iris, the diameter of which changes and thus regulates the amount of light that enters the eye – in bright light, it can narrow to 2mm, and in low-light conditions, it opens up to 8mm. The light is then refracted in the lens, passes through the vitreous humor, and is refracted in the macula. In the macula are photoreceptors, which, under the influence of light, send electrical signals along the nerves to the visual center in the brain, where the image is created and processed.

Proper care for crops begins only with sowing. The soil crust, weeds, diseases, pests, and other factors threaten the crop. If left to its own devices, these factors will weaken it, resulting in a poor yield.
The worst enemies of a newly emerging crop are weeds and the soil crust, so we must keep the soil surface loose and weed-free, at least until the crop covers the soil. Until then, the surface is exposed to rain, sun, and wind, which destroy the favorable soil structure and create a crust.
Soil Crust
The alternating effects of rain, sun, and wind cause the formation of a soil crust. Raindrops hit the soil, breaking up the soil particles, which then spread and muddy the soil surface. This effect is particularly strong when rain falls in a downpour. This muddy soil quickly dries and hardens in sunny, windy weather, forming a crust.
A thick, hardened crust prevents emergence, especially for small seeds of clover, poppies, cruciferous plants, various vegetables, etc. The emerging plants twist under the crust, and if not helped, they quickly perish. Such a crop will be sparse, and the yield will be poor. If the crust appears only after emergence, the seedlings are cemented in it.
Some advantages of a soil cover:
1. bare topsoil forms a crust,
2. a harrow breaks up the crust,
3. a living plant cover best preserves the soil's fertility.
The soil crust not only hinders germination but is also otherwise harmful because it prevents and destroys the soil's fertility. Crusted soil does not aerate. Instead of oxygen, carbon dioxide is present in the soil's air pores. This inhibits the activity of microorganisms, plant food is lacking, and plant development becomes increasingly poor. The respiration of the underground parts of the plants is also impaired. Loosening the soil and breaking up the crust has a beneficial effect on plant growth. Shallow loosening makes the soil surface crumbly and loose. This surface protects the soil in depth from drying out and keeps it fertile.
Harrowing and Rolling
We destroy the crust by harrowing and rolling. Wire or mesh harrows and spiked rollers are particularly effective. These harrows only loosen the surface and do not go deep. Cereals can be harrowed up to emergence and again later, when they have developed three leaves; they are very sensitive to harrowing in between. In addition to the crust, harrowing also destroys many weeds, especially when harrowing during germination.
A harrow only works well as long as the crust has not dried and hardened. Then, a spiked or similar roller or a PULER cultivator can be used to help, which also effectively controls weeds in your cultivated fields. Crops that are sown at a greater distance in rows should be cared for by hoeing.
Hoeing
Hoeing also loosens the soil, allows for gas exchange, preserves moisture in the soil, accelerates its fertility, and destroys weeds.
We can only hoe crops where the distance between rows is at least 20 cm.
Depending on how deeply we hoe, we distinguish three types of hoeing:
– shallow: up to 3 cm deep,
– medium-deep: up to 6-7 cm deep,
– deep: up to 10-12 cm deep.
Usually, shallow hoeing is sufficient, as deep hoeing generally does not provide any particular benefits. Deep hoeing is used when it is necessary to aerate the soil more deeply, but it consumes water. Shallow hoeing is better for controlling weeds and preserving moisture and fertility. The depth is also limited by the roots of the crops. If the roots are shallow, the hoeing should also be shallow. The deeper the root system, the deeper the hoeing can be.
The frequency of hoeing is dictated by the needs. If the crops are growing in soil that tends to crust or become weedy, we must hoe more often. It is best to do this as soon as the soil closes, crusts, or becomes weedy. The main thing is that it is not too dry or muddy.
We can hoe manually, with animal traction, or with machinery. Machine hoeing is the most economical and fastest. For machine hoeing, the rows should be perfectly straight and adapted to the tractor and the hoeing machine.
The hoeing blades should always be sharp so that they work well and smoothly undercut the weeds. Before starting, carefully adjust the hoeing blades to the required width and desired depth. This protects the roots and plants from damage.
Rolling
Rolling is most often used as a care measure:
– Immediately after sowing, to press small seeds of cruciferous plants, grasses, clover, etc., into the soil.
– If a hard crust forms after sowing or after emergence, which harrows can no longer break up.
– Early in spring, if frost has heaved cereal plants or loosened the soil surface.
Rolling the soil allows for capillary rise of water to the loose layer created after harrowing. A smooth ROLER roller can be used for rolling, which is used immediately after sowing cereals, corn, grasses, and other crops (when the plants are not yet above ground). This will ensure both faster germination and more reliable growth of your plants.
Earthing Up
Earthing up is necessary to bring more soil to the plants and onto them. This improves their nutrition. Most of the plants that we earth up develop rootlets from the base of the stem. Earthing up accelerates the growth of these rootlets. In addition, earthing up thoroughly aerates the soil, so that it warms up more quickly.
Among crops, earthing up is most beneficial for potatoes, which grow in heavy soil, and earthed-up potatoes develop more shoots. The earthed-up soil also prevents the tubers from turning green.
Earthing up is not beneficial, and in a dry climate, it can even be harmful for corn. Earthing up inhibits the development of the main roots and promotes the development of roots in the surface layer of the soil. Earthing up also increases the surface area of the soil and thus evaporation.

Prava skrb za posevke se začne šele s setvijo. Posevek ogroža skorja prsti, plevel, bolezni, škodljivci in drugo. Če ga prepustimo samemu sebi, ga te nadloge oslabe, tako da bo pridelek pičel.
Najhujša sovražnika komaj vzniklega posevka sta plevel in skorja, zato moramo vzdrževati površje zemlje rahlo in nezapleveljeno, vsaj dokler posevek ne prekrije zemlje. Do tedaj je površje izpostavljeno dežju, soncu in vetru, ki uničujejo ugodno strukturo zemlje in delajo skorjo.
Skorja
Menjava dežja, sonca in vetra povzroča nastajanje skorje. Dežne kapljice udarjajo na zemljo, drobe mrvice, ki se razlezejo in zablatijo površje zemlje. Ta učinek je posebno močan, če pade dež v nalivu. Tako zablatena zemlja se ob sončnem, vetrovnem vremenu hitro zasuši in zaskorji.
Debela, zasušena skorja onemogoča vznik, posebej še drobnim semenom detelje, maka, križnic, raznih vrtnin itd. Kaleče rastline se pod skorjo zvijajo, in če jim ne pomagamo, hitro propadejo. Tak posevek bo redek, pridelek pa slab. Če pa se skorja pojavi šele po vzniku, so rastlinice v njej zacementirane.
Nekatere prednosti talne odeje:
1. gola ornica se zaskorji,
2. brana zdrobi skorjo,
3. najbolj ohranja godnost zemlje živa rastlinska odeja.
Skorja ne ovira samo kalitve, ampak je tudi sicer škodljiva, ker onemogoča in uničuje godnost zemlje. Zaskorjena zemlja se ne zrači. Namesto kisika je v zračnih porah zemlje ogljikov dioksid. Ta zavira delovanje drobnoživk, rastlinske hrane primanjkuje in razvoj rastlin je vse slabši. Slabše je tudi dihanje podzemnih delov rastlin. Rahljanje zemlje in drobljenje skorje ugodno vpliva na rast rastlin. Plitko rahljanje napravi površje zemlje mrvičasto, rahlo. Tako površje varuje zemljo v globini, da se ne izsuši in ostane godna.
Brananje in valjanje
Skorjo uničujemo z brananjem in valjanjem. Dobro se izkažejo zlasti žične ali mrežaste brane ter ježasti valjarji. Te brane rahljajo le površinsko in ne gredo globoko. Žita smemo branati do vznika in spet pozneje, ko razvijejo tri liste; vmes so za brananje zelo občutljiva. Poleg skorje uničimo z brananjem tudi veliko plevela, zlasti če branamo tedaj, ko kali.
Brana dobro dela le, dokler se skorja ne zasuši in strdi. Tedaj si za silo pomagamo z ježastim ali podobnim valjarjem ali s česalom PULER, ki med drugim tudi učinkovito zatira plevel na vaših obdelovalnih tleh. Posevke, ki jih sejemo na večjo razdaljo v vrstah in med njimi, pa raje oskrbujemo z okopavanjem.
Okopavanje
Tudi okopavanje rahlja zemljo, omogoča izmenjavo plinov, ohranitev vlage v zemlji, pospeši njeno godnost in uničuje plevele.
Okopavamo lahko le posevke, pri kateri je razdalja med vrstami vsaj 20 cm.
Po tem, kako globoko okopavamo, ločimo tri vrste okopavanja:
– plitko: do 3 cm globoko,
– srednje globoko: do 6-7 cm globoko,
– globoko: do 10-12 cm globoko.
Navadno zadostuje plitko okopavanje, saj globoko večinoma ne prinaša posebnih koristi. Globoko okopavamo, če je potrebno zemljo globlje prezračiti, pomeni pa potrato vode. Za zatiranje plevela, ohranitev vlage in godnosti je boljše plitko okopavanje. Globino nam omejujejo tudi korenine poljščin. Če so te plitke, naj bo tudi okopavanje plitko. Čim globlji je splet korenin, tem globlje je lahko okopavanje.
Pogostost okopavanja narekujejo potrebe. Če posevki rastejo na zemlji, ki se rada zaskorji ali zapleveli, moramo okopavati večkrat. Najbolje je takoj, ko se zemlja zapre, zaskorji ali zapleveli. Glavno je, da le ni presuha ali da se ne maže.
Okopavamo ročno, vprežno ali strojno. Ekonomično in hitro je le strojno okopavanje. Za strojno okopavanje naj bodo vrste popolnoma ravne in prilagojene traktorju ter okopalniku.
Okopalniki naj bodo vedno ostri, da bodo dobro delali in gladko spodrezovali plevel. Pred delom natančno uravnamo okopalnike na potrebno širino in zaželeno globino. S tem korenine in rastline obvarujemo pred poškodbami.
Valjanje
Valjanje kot oskrbovalni ukrep najpogosteje uporabljamo:
– Takoj po setvi, da pritisnemo v zemljo drobno seme križnic, trav, detelj…
– Če se po setvi ali po vzniku napravi trdna skorja, ki jo brane ne drobe več.
– Zgodaj spomladi, če je srež izpulil žitne rastline ali zrahljaj rušo.
Z valjanjem tal je omogočen kapilarni vzpon vode do rahle plasti, nastale po brananju. Za valjanje lahko uporabite gladki valj ROLER, ki se uporablja takoj po setvi žita, koruze, travinja in drugi tal (takrat, ko še rastline niso zunaj). Z njim boste poskrbeli tako za hitrejšo kaljivost kot za zanesljivejšo rast vaših rastlin.
Osipavanje
Osipavanje je potrebno, da prigrnemo k rastlinam in nanje več zemlje. Tako izboljšamo njihovo prehrano. Večina rastlin, ki jih osipavamo, poganja iz pritalnega dela stebla koreninice. Rast koreninic osipavanje pospešuje. Poleg tega z osipavanjem zemljo temeljito prezračimo, da se bolj in prej ogreje.
Med poljščinami osipavanje najbolj koristi krompirju, ki raste v težji zemlji, osut krompir pa močneje odganja pritlike. Zgrnjena zemlja pa prepreči ozelenitev gomoljev.
Nekoristno, v sušnem podnebju pa celo škodljivo, je osipavanje koruze. Osipavanje namreč zadržuje razvoj glavnih korenin in pospešuje razvoj korenin v površinskem sloju zemlje. Osipavanje tudi poveča površino zemlje in s tem izhlapevanje.
