Takoj po končani množitvi moški umre. Iz jajc ličinke ugasnejo v dveh do štirih dneh in takoj začnejo tvoriti gibe v zgornji plasti povrhnjice. Tri do štiri dni se molt pojavlja v ličinkah in preidejo v naslednjo stopnjo - protonimf.
Še tri do pet dni pride do novega moltinga in se parazit pretvori vtelemonitor, ki raste v polnopravni ženski ali moški po petih do šestih dneh. Okužba se prenaša preko odraslih oplojenih žensk. V luči časa, pršice ne kažejo aktivnosti. Ženke postanejo aktivne zvečer, začnejo se voziti po koži. Produktivnost je približno 2-3 mm na dan. Ponoči se porazdeli, pri čemer se samice plazijo do površine povrhnjice. V tem času se poveča tveganje za okužbo, zato se bolezen prenaša.
Kako se prenašajo kraste od osebe do osebe
V veliki večini primerov se bolezen prenaša z gostim kožnim stikom zdrave osebe s kožo okužene osebe. Najpogostejši načini okužbe so predstavljeni v tabeli:
|Pot se prenaša||Opis|
|Spolno||Okužba se prenaša z dolgotrajnim in tesnim stikom teles.|
|S komunikacijo z ljudmi||Klopi se prenašajo prek tesnih stikov: pogoste ali močne stike, kontaktni športi. Od staršev do otrok ali, nasprotno, pride do okužbe, ko pride do spanja.|
|Z uporabo blaga||Tveganje za okužbo s povezavo do hiše je zelo majhno in predstavlja izjemne primere. Na primer, okužba se prenaša v bližini norveškega bolnika z nožnico. Ta vrsta bolezni vključuje prisotnost več milijonov klopov na človeškem telesu. Standardni znesek: 1-20.|
Kako je okužba s škofami
Trajanje inkubacijske dobeparazit je približno dva tedna po tem, ko parazit zadene človeško povrhnjico. Oplojena ženska, ko je v stiku s kožo, raztopi posebne encime s keratinom na koži, poteka skozi meje stratum corneum epidermisa, kjer začne odložiti z dveh na štiri jajca na noč. Živi samci izdelujejo stranske veje. Pričakovana življenjska doba ženske je 4-6 tednov.
Svrab predstavlja ukrivljeno ali ravno črto v dolžini od 0,5 do 0,7 cm. Linija ima sivkasto-umazano ali belo barvo in se dviga na glavnem sloju povrhnjice. Postopoma se pod stenami želodca razvije mehurček votline ali papula diskoidne oblike. Obstajajo tri skupine metod:
- Premik, kjer je ženska pršica, so položena jajca, njihove prazne lupine.
- Sprehodite se kot rezultat povratnega razvoja prvega tipa. Ta oblika je del končne faze delovanja, ko ženska umre, število ličink se zmanjša. Izgleda kot točka ali linija, razdeljena in skorja.
- Razvija se od začetnega tečaja v primeru sekundarne okužbe in gnojenja. Obstaja smrt jajc.
Ali se je mogoče okužiti z živaljo
Ljudje in živali parazitirajo različne oblike pršic. Klop, ki ga je moški ali pes prenesel moški, lahko nekaj časa reši življenje in poskuša prodreti v človeško kožo. To je posledica simptomov, ki so podobni človeškim šibam. Država se imenuje "psevdoschetka". Človeška koža je za živalske pršice neužitna, zato pršica hitro propade, včasih zapusti zaradi ugrizadraženje, mehurji in piling. Zato se bolezen ne prenaša.
Simptomi bolezni
Znani so načini prenosa kraste, vendar je treba ugotoviti, kako je bolezen odkrita. Klinični simptomi so posledica imunsko-alergijske reakcije organizma na produkte delovanja patogena. Znaki se pojavijo po senzibilizaciji bolnika. Asimptomatsko obdobje traja do enega meseca s primarno okužbo in do 24 ur s ponovitvijo. Glavni simptom je srbenje na trebuhu, ki je posledica občutljivosti na slino, jajca in izločke klopov. Če želite narediti diagnozo praske.
Zaradi želje po praskanju na koži so glavnik, ki lahko okuži infekcijske patogene in povzroči abscese. V norveški obliki lahko pride do hiperkeratoze in pri vseh drugih pojavnih oblikah bolezni vozlički spominjajo na kožo. Ko ženska pride na kožo, začne delati "kraste", vidne s prostim očesom, kot belkaste celične linije velikosti 1-10 mm.
Po srbenju in kapi je primarni izpuščaj v obliki majhnih eritematoznih papul. Lahko so neprivlačne enotirne ali večkratne drenaže. Sčasoma papule tvorijo vezikule (mehurčke) ali naboje. Za identifikacijo izpuščaja je mogoče prste med prsti, zapestji, ščetkami, penisom in mošnjo pri moških, pod prsmi žensk. Izpuščaj je viden na upogibih komolcev, nogah, pazduhah, na trebuhu, na pasu in zadnjici. Pri otrocih, mlajših od treh let, se pojavijo obraze in lasni mešički na glavi.
Ob kontaktu z dermatologompregleda pacienta in postavi diagnozo na podlagi naslednjih simptomov: pustule, gnojne in krvave hrbtenice, nemirne izpuščaje v intersticijskih gubah. Zapleti vključujejo pioderme, mikrobni ekcem, alergijski dermatitis. Otroci razvijejo paronihijo, oniii, simptome podobne koprivnici, sepso se lahko razvije, pojavijo se razpoke in suhost kože. 7% bolnikov trpi za limfoplazijo scabiosis - nastanek tjulnjev na koži (kraste v obliki suhe papule), kar vodi do hiperplazije limfoidnega tkiva.
Kako ustaviti širjenje šibke
Da bi se odzvali na kraste, morate postaviti objektivno diagnozo in nato določiti posebno zdravljenje. Njegov cilj je uničiti patogen z akaricidnimi zdravili s skabicidi. Terapija se izvaja pod zdravniškim nadzorom, v primeru, da je pri eni družini prisotna tudi kraska, oseba doživlja vse stike z njim. Priprave se uporabljajo za celotno telo, podrgnil s čopičem, bolnik je na kratko obrezan nohti, zdravljenje se izvaja v večernih urah, lahko speremo 12 ur po uporabi zdravila.
Za otroke in šolarje je 10-dnevna karantena, za vse ostale - sprememba postelje in posteljnine po koncu zdravljenja in zdravniški pregled v 14 dneh. Kot terapija za svrab se uporabljajo številna zdravila proti skabiozi, medtem ko se uporablja post-sciatično zdravljenje. Med zdravili, ki ubijajo načine za okužbo, so:
- Benzil benzoat - suspenzija za milo z vodo ali emulzijaubije vse aktivne faze klopa, razen jajc. Njena podrgnil v kožo za 1 in 4 dni tečaja, pustite za 8-10 ur. Potek se ponovi po 10 dneh. Proti - Občutek pečenja, draženje kože, vročina, ni primerna za nosečnost.
- Piretrini, piretroidi - ubijajo populacije, središča porazdelitve žuželk na kateri koli stopnji. Zdravilo Medifox se nanese na celotno telo v prvih treh dneh zdravljenja. Zdravilo Spragal se uporablja za pršenje telesa in drgnjenje v kožo, čas izpostavljenosti je 12 ur, potem ko je zdravilo oprano z vodo in milom.
- Lindan se je aktivno uporabljal v sedemdesetih letih prejšnjega stoletja, zdaj pa ga zaradi nevrotoksičnosti praktično ni. Izdana je pod blagovno znamko Yakutin, ki se uporablja 6 ur, je odporna.
- Sulfurna mazilo - v koncentraciji 5-10% se čez noč potegne v epitelno plast, in sicer 5-7 dni. Za 6-8 dni zamenjajte obleko, obleko. Od minusov so neprijeten vonj, draženje kože, učinki na ledvice in živčni sistem.
- Ivermektin je novo kompleksno zdravilo v obliki mazila ali raztopine za subkutane injekcije. Brez stranskih učinkov, primeren za otroke in odrasle. Enkratna uporaba zdravila odpravi antigene krastavosti pri 70% bolnikov.
- Antihistaminiki zmanjšajo občutljivost.
Preprečevanje
Ker se kuga prenaša od osebe do osebe, je treba sprejeti ukrepe za preprečitev okužbe bolezni. Ti vključujejo naslednje ukrepe:
- zdravljenje stvari, brisač in perila, ki so bile v stiku s pacientom;
- skladnostosebna higiena bolnika, da se preprečijo okuženi družinski člani;
- spoštovanje osebne higiene, čistoča;
- preprečevanje kontracepcijskih preprek, čitljivost pri izbiri spolnega partnerja, opuščanje neurejenega načina življenja;
- pravočasno izvesti laboratorijske teste.
Video
Informacije v članku so informativne narave. Materiali članka ne zahtevajo neodvisne obravnave. Le kvalificiran zdravnik lahko diagnosticira in svetuje glede zdravljenja na podlagi individualnih značilnosti posameznega bolnika.

prompt.content:
Si profesionalni prevajalec iz angleščine v slovenščino. Tvoja naloga je ustvariti visoko kakovostne prevode, ki so naravni, tekoči in natančni. Izogibaj se dobesednim prevodom, ki zvenijo nenaravno. Upoštevaj kontekst, idiome in kulturne reference. Ne dodajaj nobenih dodatnih informacij ali komentarjev, samo prevod.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

Unlike the Greek, Egyptian, or Indian civilizations, which have been thoroughly researched over the past two centuries, new discoveries of unknown civilizations continue to emerge on the American continent. However, unlike the civilizations of the Old World, which are considered the cradle of culture, the cultures of the Americas have acquired a negative reputation as being bloodthirsty, prone to human sacrifice, and barbaric.

However, considering the way in which American regions were “discovered” in the 16th century and subsequent centuries, it is not surprising that Europeans formed such an impression. For a very long time, the biased accounts of Catholic priests who traveled there with the conquistadors were the only source of information about the indigenous American cultures. Their education and narrow-mindedness, characteristic of European culture, which was just emerging from the dark Middle Ages, were the cause of many prejudices and misunderstandings of these ancient civilizations. The desire to suppress all written and oral traces of the culture of these peoples was strong, as evidenced by the accounts of contemporary witnesses. Books were burned, monuments were destroyed, and stone was used to build Christian cathedrals. The population was forcibly converted to Christianity, their customs were declared the work of the devil, and they were prohibited. Therefore, the state in which the first explorers of the 18th and 19th centuries encountered the descendants of these peoples only confirmed the ingrained prejudice about “primitive savages.”

Augustus Le Plongeon, a French explorer of the 19th century, managed to get closer to the Maya than any explorer before him. He was even given the nickname “Great Black Beard,” which proves that he was truly accepted – although outsiders from the West were feared. While living among them, he helped to uncover the veil that had covered Mayan civilization for centuries.

Le Plongeon was characterized not only by a sense of empathy but also by a versatile, restless, and adventurous spirit. A turning point was his honeymoon trip to Yucatan, Mexico, which “extended” to twenty years.

He and his wife, Alice, initially lived in the city of Merida on the Yucatan Peninsula, where Le Plongeon quickly established close relationships with the local population and learned their language. He believed that knowledge of their language was essential for serious research. He criticized his academic colleagues for drawing conclusions about Mayan culture without knowing even a word of their language and being unable to decipher “even a tenth of the hieroglyphs.”

The couple soon decided to begin exploring the ruins of the ancient city of Chichen Itza. They lived in settlements in the middle of the jungle and shared all the hardships of their poverty, disease, and unbearable humid climate with the local people. Throughout their time among the locals, they were threatened by local insurgent guerrillas, the so-called “sublevados,” who attacked outsiders from the West and accused them of stealing land and trampling on human rights. Le Plongeon often spoke out against the inhumane treatment of the indigenous population, which often led to him falling out of favor with the authorities.

He extended his research to the entire Yucatan Peninsula. He copied and deciphered inscriptions he found on ancient monuments. He claimed that he had learned to decipher the hieroglyphs from Mayan ruins from an old Indian who was one hundred and fifty years old, and that they spoke of the history of this people, which dates back thousands of years.

His relationship with the Maya was heartfelt and filled with mutual respect. He said that he was allowed to attend ceremonies that no foreigner had ever witnessed. He claimed that he was taught teachings that had been preserved for centuries and that he was explained the meaning of many symbols that remained a mystery to other explorers.

During their exploration in Chichen Itza and Uxmal, Le Plongeon and Alice took approximately five hundred photographs, which even their greatest opponents acknowledge as their greatest contribution. This is because, in some cases, these photographs are the only source from which it is possible to study the monuments, as they were taken before the great destruction caused by treasure hunters and, in the 20th century, tourists. Seeing the danger of looting and trafficking of Mayan artifacts on commission from prestigious museums, they also meticulously made sketches and replicas of archaeological remains.

Chac Mool

Le Plongeon’s name in the history of American archaeology is most often associated with the discovery of the magnificent statue of Chac Mool. Based on his “arbitrary, imaginative, and amateurish” interpretations of Mayan hieroglyphs, Le Plongeon hypothesized where the statue was buried.

In the fortified city, his assistants dug long and tirelessly until, finally, at a depth of seven meters, their shovels struck a hard surface. With great effort, without technical aids, and with Le Plongeon’s engineering skills, they managed to pull the multi-ton monolith to the surface and drag it out of the jungle into the city of Merida. Le Plongeon hoped that this discovery would finally confirm the validity of his research. In 1876, he intended to transport the statue to Philadelphia for an exhibition, but the Mexican government immediately seized the find and sent it to Mexico City. Le Plongeon had nothing left to do but send photographs of Chac Mool to Philadelphia.

The photographs did not have a major impact, but they were noticed by Stephen Salisbury Jr., a wealthy philanthropist and one of the founders of the American Antiquarian Society. This is how Le Plongeon found a wealthy and influential patron who published an important article about his work in the Societies newspaper. However, this patronage did not last long, as Le Plongeon’s theories about the origin of ancient cultures seemed too bold even to Salisbury.

The Continent of Mu – the Remains of Atlantis?

Based on deciphered texts (Codex Troano, Codex Cortesianus, inscriptions on ruins), Le Plongeon concluded that the Maya had a much longer and richer history than recognized by historical circles. He claimed that the texts identified the homeland of the Maya as the long-lost continent of Mu, which Le Plongeon identified with Plato’s remains of Atlantis.

His interpretations of the hieroglyphs spoke in detail about the catastrophe that befell this continent, as well as about the travels of the inhabitants of Atlantis and their settlement of the new continent. In Chichen Itza, he found particularly interesting inscriptions about Queen Moo, her brother and husband, Prince Cohu, and her jealous suitor, Prince Aac. These inscriptions state that they fled the sunken continent of Mu and settled in Mayab (the land of the Maya in Yucatan), where their people already had colonies.

Le Plongeon went a step further than this “heretical” idea, which had been developed a century before him by the priest and explorer Brasseur de Bourbourg, who first translated the Mayan book Popol Vuh. He claimed that, according to numerous sources (he cites four: Codex Troano, Codex Cortesianus, a stone relief in the Chichen Itza complex, and an epic poem from Athens, Greece, written in the Euclidean era by a poet in the Mayan language), the Maya were great travelers, sailors, and civilizers. According to his hypothesis, the Maya were also the founders of the great civilizations of India, Mesopotamia, and Egypt.

When studying parts of Valmiki’s Ramayana, in which the name “Maya” is mentioned, he concluded that this people, which boasted great sailors and exceptional warriors, conquered the southern part of the Indochinese Peninsula and settled there in that distant time.

Similarly, Plutarch’s accounts of the great Athenian legislator Solon, who studied in Egyptian temples, state that two Egyptian priests told him that, 9,000 years ago (today – 11,500 years ago), the connections between the Egyptians and the inhabitants of the “western lands” were broken due to large deposits of silt that appeared after the sinking of Atlantis.

In addition, he found similar words and roots of words in the Maya, Egyptians, Chaldeans, and Indians. He cited parts of the myths of these peoples, which described people “from the sea” who brought writing, social organization, ceremonies, and mysteries to these peoples.

Le Plongeon discovered another interesting fact – an inscription from the Mayan temple of Kabul in Izamal was written in Egyptian hieratic script. From this, he drew an optimistic conclusion that it is necessary to study several cultures at the same time – using analogies, especially in language, writing, and symbols – because he believed that this is the easiest way to discover the secrets of still undeciphered texts.

From the work of the historian Berosus, who studied Chaldean history, he cites descriptions of civilizers who came across the sea from the “Western Land” and lists similarities between Mayan and Mesopotamian culture, words, and symbols.

Stormy Reactions

Given the hypotheses presented, it is not difficult to guess what the reaction of the scientific community was. Le Plongeon’s scientific credibility was completely destroyed. He was publicly ridiculed and attacked, but he did not spare words either and criticized these “salon researchers” who had never engaged in fieldwork and knew nothing about American civilizations except what was written in books.

He accused university authorities of hindering new facts and data obtained through fieldwork. He also advised his readers not to take anything for granted and to “confirm it with experience after learning it, otherwise knowledge is in vain.”

In 1885, the couple returned to New York, as they no longer had enough money for their research. With great effort and expense, they brought large replicas of Mayan monuments with them. They donated them to the Metropolitan Museum, but the director stored them in the basement, far from public view, as they were not considered “beautiful” or “important” enough.

While in America, the couple unsuccessfully sought someone who would be willing to financially support further research. Le Plongeon spoke of the existence of secret Mayan books that were said to be hidden during the invasion of the Nahuatl people from Tule, who had conquered Yucatan long before the Spanish. He offered information about the place where they could be found, but no one was interested in this undertaking. This tormented him until his death, as he hoped that, when these books were found, he would gain many valuable insights that would complete the fragments of what was already known.

Augustus Le Plongeon died in 1908 at the age of 83. His wife, Alice, who was a friend of Annie Besant, another president of the Theosophical Society, remained active in theosophical circles until her death. She took care of an extensive archive of notes, sketches, and maps with marked locations where the books were said to be hidden. Before her death, she entrusted them to a friend to keep them safe.

This treasure remained forgotten for a long time until recent times, when there was a renewed desire for more serious research into the history of ancient America.

Common Origin of Cultures

Today, even Le Plongeon’s boldest claims do not seem impossible and inspire many seekers. Although newer research challenges some of Le Plongeon’s conclusions, especially those about the Maya as the founders of other great civilizations, the former claim that all ancient civilizations are too similar in their most important achievements (religion, architecture, astronomical knowledge, etc.) to be coincidental is becoming increasingly accepted. The idea of a common origin of Egyptian, Mayan, Mesopotamian, and other ancient civilizations is gaining ground. Atlantis is no longer ceasing to be a topic of discussion, and experts are increasingly accepting it as a logical explanation for these similarities.

Augustus and Alice Le Plongeon left a strong mark in archaeology and the history of humanity. They were particularly committed to independent research, supported by findings, original texts, and the traditions of still-living descendants of historical peoples. They dreamed of free science and hoped that the future would reveal all the secrets of the past to diligent and dedicated seekers. They showed that a researcher must have enough breadth to compare numerous sources found in completely different parts of our planet. This attitude is the basis of the increasingly popular trend of comparative study of various sciences, religions, and traditions in order to arrive at the most reliable knowledge.

Augustus and Alice Le Plongeon remained researchers until their last days, because being a researcher is not a profession, but a way of life for those who want to know the truth.

Za razliko od grške, egipčanske ali indijske civilizacije, ki so bile v preteklih dveh stoletjih temeljito raziskane, na ameriški celini na površje vedno znova priplavajo nova odkritja neznanih civilizacij. Toda za razliko od civilizacij starega sveta, ki veljajo za zibelko kulture, se je na ameriške kulture prilepil slab sloves krvoločnih, človeškim žrtvam naklonjenih, barbarskih družb.
Toda če upoštevamo način “odkrivanja” ameriških področij v XVI. in v naslednjih stoletjih, niti ne preseneča, da so prebivalci Evrope dobili takšen vtis. Zelo dolgo časa so bili namreč pristranski opisi katoliških duhovnikov, ki so odhajali tja skupaj s konkvistadorji, edini vir informacij o izvornih ameriških kulturah. Njihova izobrazba in ozkoglednost, značilni za evropsko kulturo, ki se je komaj poslavljala od temačnega srednjega veka, sta bili vzrok za številne predsodke in nerazumevanje teh starodavnih civilizacij. Težnje po zatiranju vseh pisnih in ustnih sledi kulture teh ljudstev so bile po zapisih pričevalcev tedanjega časa močne. Požigali so knjige, uničevali so spomenike, kamen pa so uporabljali za gradnjo krščanskih katedral. Prebivalstvo so na silo pokristjanjevali, njihove običaje razglasili za hudičevo delo in jih prepovedali. Zato je stanje, v katerem so prvi raziskovalci iz XVIII. in XIX. stoletja naleteli na potomce teh ljudstev, samo potrdilo ukoreninjen predsodek o “primitivnih divjakih”.
Augustus Le Plongeon, francoski raziskovalec iz XIX. stoletja, se je Majem uspel približati kot še noben raziskovalec pred njim. Nadeli so mu celo vzdevek “Velika črna brada”, kar dokazuje, da je bil resnično sprejet – sicer so se prišlekov z zahoda bali. Medtem ko je prebival pri njih, je pomagal odstreti tančico, s katero je bila stoletja prekrita majevska civilizacija.
Le Plongeona je poleg čuta za sočloveka označeval tudi vsestranski, nemiren, pustolovski duh. Prelomnico je predstavljalo poročno potovanje na Jukatan v Mehiki, ki se je “podaljšalo” kar na dvajset let.
Najprej sta z ženo Alice bivala v mestu Merida na polotoku Jukatan, kjer je Le Plongeon hitro vzpostavil tesne odnose z lokalnim prebivalstvom in se naučil njihov jezik. Menil je, da je poznavanje njihovega jezika nepogrešljivo za resno raziskovanje. Svojim akademskim kolegom je očital, da so prihajali do zaključkov o majevski kulturi, čeprav niso znali niti besedice njihovega jezika in niso mogli razvozlati “niti desetine hieroglifov”.
Kmalu sta se zakonca Le Plongeon odločila, da bosta začela raziskovati ruševine starodavnega mesta Chicen Itze. Živela sta v naselbinah sredi džungle ter z domačimi prebivalci delila vse tegobe njihove revščine, bolezni in nevzdržnega vlažnega podnebja. Ves čas svojega bivanja med domačini so ju ogrožali tamkajšnji uporniški gverilci, ti. “sublevadosi”, ki so napadali prišleke z zahoda in jih obtoževali, da kradejo zemljo in teptajo človekove pravice. Le Plongeon je pogosto dvignil svoj glas proti nečloveškemu ravnanju z indijanskim prebivalstvom, zato je pri oblasteh neredko zapadel v nemilost.
Svoje raziskovanje je razširil na celoten polotok Jukatan. Prepisoval in razvozlaval je napise, ki jih je našel na starodavnih spomenikih. Trdil je, da se je od nekega sto petdeset let starega Indijanca naučil razvozlavati hieroglife z majevskih ruševin in da ti govorijo o zgodovini tega ljudstva, ki naj bi segala tisoče let v preteklost.
Njegovi odnosi z Maji so bili srčni in prežeti z obojestranskim spoštovanjem. Dejal je, da mu je bilo dovoljeno prisostvovati obredom, ki jih ni videl niti en tujec. Prenesli naj bi mu učenja, ki so se ohranjala od vekomaj, in pojasnili pomen številnih simbolov, ki so za druge raziskovalce ostali skrivnost.
Le Plongeon in Alice sta med raziskovanjem v Chicen Itzi in Uxmalu posnela približno petsto fotografij, kar jima danes tudi največji nasprotniki priznavajo za največji prispevek. Kajti v nekaterih primerih so te fotografije edini vir, na podlagi katerega je možno preučevati spomenike. Posnete so bile namreč še pred velikim uničenjem, ki so ga povzročili lovci na starine in v XX. stoletju tudi turisti. Ker sta videla nevarnost kraj in tihotapljenja majevskih umetnin po naročilu uglednih muzejev, sta vestno izdelovala tudi skice in replike arheoloških ostankov.
Chac Mool
Le Plongeonovo ime v zgodovini ameriške arheologije najpogosteje povezujejo z odkritjem veličastnega kipa Chac Moola. Le Plongeon je na osnovi svojih “svojevoljnih, domišljijskih in amaterskih” razlag majevskih hieroglifov predpostavil, kje naj bi bil zakopan kip.
Na utrjenem mestu so njegovi pomočniki dolgo in neutrudno kopali, dokler niso naposled na globini sedmih metrov lopate udarile ob trdo podlago. Z izrednimi napori, brez tehničnih pomagal in z Le Plongeonovo inženirsko veščino so uspeli nekajtonski monolit potegniti na površje in ga odvleči iz džungle v mesto Merido. Le Plongeon je upal, da bo s to najdbo končno potrdil veljavnost svojih raziskav. Kip je leta 1876 nameraval prenesti v Filadelfijo na razstavo, toda mehiška vlada je takoj zaplenila najdbo in jo poslala v Mexico City. Le Plongeonu ni preostalo nič drugega, kot da v Filadelfijo pošlje samo fotografije Chac Moola.
Fotografije niso imele večjega odmeva, toda kljub temu jih je opazil bogat filantrop in eden od ustanoviteljev Ameriškega društva za starine (American Antiquarian Society, op. prev.) Stephen Salisbury mlajši. Tako je Le Plongeon dobil bogatega in vplivnega pokrovitelja, ki je o njegovem delu objavil pomemben članek v časopisu Societies. Toda to pokroviteljstvo ni dolgo trajalo, ker so se Le Plongeonove teorije o izvoru starodavnih kultur zdele preveč drzne celo Salisburyiju.
Celina Mu – ostanki Atlantide?
Le Plongeon je na podlagi razvozlanih zapisov (Codex Troano, Codex Cortesianus, napisi na ruševinah) zaključil, da imajo Maji veliko daljšo in bogatejšo zgodovino, kakor priznavajo zgodovinarski krogi. Trdil je, da zapisi kot domovino Majev navajajo davno potopljeno celino Mu, ki jo je Le Plongeon poistovetil s Platonovimi ostanki Atlantide.
Njegove razlage hieroglifov so na izčrpen način govorile o katastrofi, ki naj bi doletela to celino, kot tudi o potovanjih prebivalcev Atlantide in njihovem naseljevanju nove celine. V Chichen Itzi je našel še posebej zanimive napise o kraljici Moo, njenem bratu in možu princu Cohu ter ljubosumnem snubcu princu Aacu. Ti napisi navajajo, da so zbežali s potopljene celine Mu in se naselili v Mayachu (dežela Majev na Jukatanu), kjer je njihovo ljudstvo že pred tem imelo svoje kolonije.
Le Plongeon je šel še korak dlje od te “heretične” ideje, ki jo je stoletje pred njim razvijal že svečenik in raziskovalec Brasseur de Bourbourg, ki je prvi prevedel majevsko knjigo Popol Vuh. Trdil je, da glede na številne vire (sam jih navaja štiri: Codex Troano, Codex Cortesianus, kamniti relief v kompleksu Chichen Itza in epska pesnitev iz Aten v Grčiji, ki jo je v Evklidovem času napisal pesnik v majevskem jeziku) lahko zaključimo, da so bili Maji veliki popotniki, pomorščaki in civilizatorji. Po njegovih predpostavkah naj bi bili Maji tudi začetniki velikih civilizacij Indije, Mezopotamije in Egipta.
Ko je proučeval dele Valmikijeve Ramajane, v katerem je navedeno poimenovanje “Maji”, je prišel do zaključka, da naj bi to ljudstvo, ki se je ponašalo z velikimi pomorščaki in izjemnimi bojevniki, v tem davnem času osvojilo južni del Indokitajskega polotoka in se tam naselilo.
Podobno tudi Plutarhovi zapisi o velikem atenskem zakonodajalcu Solonu, ki se je učil v egipčanskih templjih, navajajo, da sta mu dva egipčanska svečenika govorila o tem, da so bile pred 9000 leti (danes – 11500 leti) povezave med Egipčani in prebivalci “zahodnih dežel” prekinjene zaradi velikih nanosov mulja, ki so se pojavili po potopitvi Atlantide.
Poleg tega je tako pri Majih, Egipčanih, Kaldejcih kot tudi Indijcih našel podobne besede in korene besed. Navajal je dele mitov teh ljudstev, kateri so opisovali ljudi “z morja”, ki naj bi tem ljudstvom prinesli pisavo, družbeno organizacijo, ceremonije in misterije.
Le Plongeon je odkril še eno zanimivost – napis z majevskega templja Kabul v Izamalu naj bi bil zapisan z egipčansko hieratsko* pisavo. Iz tega je izpeljal optimističen zaključek, da je treba proučevati več kultur hkrati – s pomočjo analogij, predvsem v jeziku, pisavi in simbolih – kajti menil je, da je na ta način veliko lažje odkriti skrivnosti še nerazvozlanih zapisov.
Iz dela zgodovinarja Berosa, ki je raziskoval kaldejsko zgodovino, navaja opise civilizatorjev, ki so prišli preko morja iz “Zahodne dežele”, in našteva podobnosti med majevsko in mezopotamsko kulturo, besedami in simboli.
Burni odzivi
Glede na predstavljene hipoteze ni težko uganiti, kakšen je bil odziv znanstvenih krogov. Le Plongeonova znanstvena verodostojnost je bila popolnoma uničena. Javno so se mu posmehovali in ga napadali, vendar niti on ni varčeval z besedami in je kritiziral te “salonske raziskovalce”, ki se nikoli niso lotili terenskega dela in razen dejstev, zapisanih v knjigah, niso vedeli ničesar o ameriških civilizacijah.
Univerzitetnim avtoritetam je očital, da so ovirale nova dejstva in podatke, pridobljene z raziskovanjem na terenu. Tudi svojim bralcem je svetoval, da ničesar ne jemljejo za suho zlato in da “potem, ko se nekaj naučijo, to potrdijo še z izkušnjo, sicer je znanje zaman.”
Leta 1885 sta se zakonca Le Plongeon vrnila v New York, saj nista imela dovolj denarja za svoje raziskovanje. S seboj sta z velikimi napori in stroški prinesla velike replike majevskih spomenikov. Podarila sta jih muzeju Metropolitan, toda tam jih je direktor shranil v klet, daleč od oči javnosti, saj naj ne bi bili dovolj “lepi” in “pomembni”.
Med bivanjem v Ameriki sta zakonca zaman iskala nekoga, ki bi bil pripravljen denarno podpreti nadaljnja raziskovanja. Le Plongeon je govoril o obstoju skrivnih majevskih knjig, ki naj bi bile skrite med vdorom ljudstva Nahuatl iz Tule, ki je že zdavnaj pred Španci osvojilo Jukatan. Ponujal je podatke o kraju, kjer bi jih bilo možno najti, vendar nikogar ni zanimal ta podvig. To ga je mučilo do smrti, kajti upal je, da bo takrat, ko bodo te knjige najdene, dobil številna dragocena spoznanja, ki bodo sestavila fragmente tega, kar je že znano.
Augustus Le Plongeon je umrl leta 1908 v 83. letu starosti. Žena Alice, ki je bila prijateljica Annie Besant, druge predsednice Teozofskega društva, je bila vse do svoje smrti dejavna v teozofskih krogih. Skrbela je za obsežen arhiv zapiskov, skic in zemljevidov z označenimi kraji, kjer naj bi bile skrite knjige. Pred smrtjo jih je zaupala svoji prijateljici, da jih shrani.
Ta zaklad je dolgo ostal pozabljen vse do novejših časov, ko se je znova prebudila težnja po resnejšem raziskovanju zgodovine stare Amerike.
Skupen izvor kultur
Danes niti najdrznejše Le Plongeonove trditve ne zvenijo nemogoče in navdihujejo številne iskalce. Čeprav novejše raziskave spodbijajo nekatere Le Plongeonove zaključke, predvsem tiste o Majih kot začetnikih drugih velikih civilizacij, pa se vse bolj uveljavlja nekdanja trditev, da so vse stare civilizacije preveč podobne v svojih najpomembnejših dosežkih (religija, arhitektura, astronomska znanja itn.), da bi bilo to naključno. Vse bolj si utira pot ideja o skupnem izvoru egipčanske, majevske, mezopotamskih in drugih starodavnih civilizacij. Atlantida ne preneha biti tema razprav in vse pogosteje jo strokovnjaki sprejemajo kot logično pojasnitev teh podobnosti.
Augustus in Alice Le Plongeon sta zapustila močno sled v arheologiji in zgodovini človeštva. Še posebej sta se zavzemala za lastno samostojno raziskovanje, podkrepljeno z najdbami, izvornimi teksti in izročili še živečih potomcev zgodovinskih ljudstev. Sanjala sta o svobodni znanosti, upala sta, da bo prihodnost prizadevnim in posvečenim iskalcem razkrila vse skrivnosti preteklosti. Pokazala sta, da mora imeti raziskovalec dovolj širine, da bi primerjal številne vire, najdene na popolnoma različnih predelih našega planeta. Takšen odnos je zametek danes vse glasnejše struje primerjalnega preučevanja različnih znanosti, religij in tradicij, da bi na tak način prišli do kar najverodostojnejših znanj.
Augustus in Alice Le Plongeon sta ostala raziskovalca vse do svojih poslednjih dni, kajti biti raziskovalec ni poklic, temveč življenjska drža tistih, ki želijo spoznati resnico.

Podocyte
|Podocyte|
|Structure of the renal corpuscle

Blood flows in through the afferent arteriole (9) at the top and flows out through the efferent arteriole (11) at the bottom. In between, the blood is distributed through the glomerular capillaries (10), where it is filtered under pressure. Podocytes (3a and 3b, green) surround the capillaries, and blood is filtered through the slits between the podocytes. The filtered urine leaves the glomerulus through the proximal tubule (B, yellow) on the right.
Podocytes (also called visceral epithelial cells) are large epithelial cells in Bowman's capsule on the outer surface of the capillaries in the renal glomeruli, which have numerous finger-like processes.[1][2] Bowman's capsule filters blood, allowing small molecules such as water, salts, and sugar to pass through, while large molecules, such as proteins, are retained in the blood. This is the first step in urine formation.
The finger-like processes of the podocytes wrap around the capillaries, and narrow slits are formed between them. Blood can be filtered through these slits. Certain proteins are essential for the normal function of these podocyte processes, and in children born with defects in these proteins, such as nephrin or CD2AP protein, the kidneys do not function normally. In humans, there are several variants of these proteins, and some are thought to be associated with a susceptibility to kidney failure later in life. Nephrin is a protein that forms the slits between the podocyte processes in a zipper-like manner; small pores are formed between the "teeth" of the zipper, which are large enough for sugar and water molecules to pass through, but retain protein molecules. The CD2AP protein forms the cytoskeleton in podocytes and stabilizes the slits.[3]
Role[edit | edit source]
Adjacent podocytes adhere to each other and cover the basal lamina, which continuously covers the glomerular capillaries. However, small gaps, or slits, appear between the podocytes, allowing blood to be filtered.
The slits are covered by a membrane composed of numerous surface proteins, including nephrin, podocalixin, and P-cadherin, which prevent larger molecules (e.g., serum albumin and immunoglobulins) from leaving the bloodstream.
Podocytes also regulate the rate of glomerular filtration (GFR). When they contract, they close the filtration slits, and the rate of glomerular filtration is reduced due to the decrease in the surface area through which glomerular filtration is possible.
Structure[edit | edit source]
The structure of podocytes indicates a high degree of vesicular transport in these cells – numerous vesicles are visible on the basolateral side of the podocytes.
The finger-like processes extend from the podocytes and increase the surface area of the cells, which is essential for efficient ultrafiltration.[5]
Pathology[edit | edit source]
Damage to the membrane covering the slits between the podocytes, or the degeneration of podocytes, can cause severe proteinuria, in which a large number of proteins are lost from the bloodstream into the urine. This can occur, for example, in a congenital disorder called Finnish nephrosis, which is characterized by the appearance of proteinuria in the newborn and leads to kidney failure. The cause is a mutation in the gene for nephrin.

Podocit
|Podocit|
|Zgradba ledvičnega telesca


Kri priteče po aferentni arterioli (9) na vrhu in odteka po eferentni arterioli (11) na dnu. Vmes se kri porazporedi po glomerulnih kapilarah (10), kjer se pod tlakom filtrira. Podociti (3a in 3b, zeleno) obdajajo kapilare, kri pa se filtrira skozi reže med podociti. Filtrirani seč zapušča glomerul skozi proksimalni tubul (B, rumen) na desnem.
Podocíti (tudi epicíti) so velike epitelijske celice v Bowmanovi ovojnici na zunanjem površju kapilar v ledvičnih glomerulih, ki imajo številne prstaste podaljške.[1][2] Bowmanova ovojnica filtrira kri, pri čemer skoznjo prehajajo majhne molekule, kot so voda, soli, sladkor, velike molekule, npr. beljakovine, pa se zadržijo v krvi. To je prvi korak v tvorbi seča.
Prstasti podaljški podocitov zaojemajo kapilare, med njimi pa nastajajo ozke reže. Skozi te reže se lahko kri filtrira. Za normalno delovanje teh podocitnih podaljškov so nujne določene beljakovine in pri otrocih, ki se rodijo z napakami v teh beljakovinah, npr. nefrinu ali beljakovini CD2AP, ledvice ne delujejo normalno. Pri ljudeh se pojavlja več različic teh beljakovin in določene naj bi bile nosilke dovzetnosti za ledvično odpoved kasneje v življenju. Nefrin je beljakovina, ki tvori reže med podocitnimi podaljški podobno kot zadrga; med "zobci zadrge" nastajajo majhne režice, dovolj velike, da morejo molekule sladkorja in vode prehajati skoznje, zadržijo pa molekule beljakovin. Beljakovina CD2AP tvori citoskelet v podocitih in stabilizira reže.[3]
Vloga[uredi | uredi kodo]
Sosednji podociti se prilegajo eden ob drugega in prekrivajo bazalno lamino, ki neprekinjeno prekriva glomerulne kapilare. Vendar se med podociti pojavljajo manjše vrzeli, reže, ki omogočajo filtracijo krvi.
Reže so prekrite z opno, sestavljeno iz številnih površinskih beljakovin, vključno z nefrinom, podocaliksinom in kadherinom P, ki preprečujejo večjim molekulam (npr. serumskemu albuminu in gamaglobulinom), da bi zapuščale krvni obtok.
Podociti tudi uravnavajo hitrost glomerulne filtracije (GFR). Če kontrahirajo (se skrčijo), zaprejo filtracijske reže in zaradi zmanjšanja površine, skozi katero je omogočena glomerulna filtracija, se njena hitrost zavre.
Zgradba[uredi | uredi kodo]
Zgradba podocitov kaže na visoko stopnjo vezikularnega transporta v teh celicah – na bazolateralni strani podocitov so vidni številni mešički.
Prstasti podaljški molijo iz podocitov in povečujejo površino celic, kar je bistveno za učinkovito ultrafiltracijo.[5]
Patologija[uredi | uredi kodo]
Poškodbe open, ki prekrivajo reže med podociti, ali propadanje podocitov lahko povzročijo hudo proteinurijo, pri čemer se iz krvnega obroka izgulja s sečem veliko število beljakovin. Do takega stanja pride na primer pri prirojeni motnji, imenovani finska nefroza, za katero je značilno, da se proteinurija pojavi že pri novorojenčku in vodi do ledvične odpovedi. Vzrok je mutacija na genu za nefrin.

Discover the Importance of National Parks
In the current scenario, we are facing a faster rate of habitat and species loss. Given the negative impact on the environment, the role of protected areas becomes fundamental, helping to conserve water, acting as carbon sinks, and contributing to climate stabilization. The goal of national parks is to protect natural biodiversity along with the basic ecological structure and environmental processes upon which it rests. On the other hand, they also strive to promote education and recreational use. This is how the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) defines them.
The role of these areas is not only important for conserving ecosystems and biodiversity. It is estimated that the global network of protected areas stores at least 15% of terrestrial carbon, and its importance in relation to climate change is increasingly recognized. National parks are one of many classifications that make up protected areas, geographically defined areas that are recognized and managed to achieve long-term conservation of nature, its ecosystems, and cultural values. The IUCN classifies them as Category II for conserving ecosystems and protecting the system it has designed to achieve global understanding of protected area management. The definitions of this organization are adopted by the United Nations and the Convention on Biological Diversity. They are also guided by national governments. As precisely defined by the Argentine Biodiversity Information System, each country should have 5% of its territory with an evenly distributed area among all biogeographic units.
National Parks in Latin America According to CEPALSTAT (the database and statistical publications of the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean) for 2012, Brazil is the country in the region with the largest number of national parks, with 69 on its territory, making it the fifth largest in the world and the largest in the region. It is followed by Mexico (66), Colombia (56), Venezuela (43), Chile (36), and Argentina (34). Four parks in the latter country are UNESCO World Heritage sites. According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), the main challenge in the region is combating deforestation, which has been decreasing in recent years but remains significant. However, this organization emphasizes that the area of forests dedicated to conserving biodiversity in the region has increased to 3 million hectares per year since 2000.

The US Environmental Protection Agency recommends drinking water with a pH between 6.5 and 8.5. Hard water, or water with a high pH, contains a high concentration of dissolved minerals. While this is healthy for our bodies, minerals like calcium can cause problems with scaling on ceramic surfaces and a bitter taste. Minerals deposit on tubs and fixtures, leaving a flaky residue. Soft water, or water with a low pH, usually has higher concentrations of metals like manganese and iron. These metals can corrode pipes in older homes.

The Importance of pH in Streams and Lakes
Maintaining a balanced pH in water is crucial for aquatic health. Fish and other organisms depend on high-quality water with just the right amount of dissolved oxygen and nutrients. High or low pH can disrupt the chemical balance in the water and mobilize contaminants, creating toxic conditions. Aquatic organisms can experience population declines and increased mortality. For this reason, pH is often sampled by scientists to assess the health of streams, lakes, rivers, and groundwater.

Factors That Cause pH to Vary
Pollution is a major contributor to changes in the pH of natural water. Acid rain, which has a very low pH, causes environmental problems that harm animals, plants, and people. In addition to the acidity caused by precipitation, pollutants can enter the water through the atmosphere. Many environmental laws and regulations are now in place to manage and control the harmful effects of pollutants in water.

Understanding How to Test for pH
To understand how small changes in pH affect water, it is helpful to understand how scientists measure it. Two commonly used methods are pH meters and litmus paper. Scientists use pH meters by placing a water sample in a beaker and inserting the probe of the pH meter into the sample and reading the electronic display. The litmus paper method is less accurate, but it is easy to use. A drop of the water sample is placed on the litmus paper, and the color changes. The color is then compared to a pH value chart.

Just think about the destructive force of a river that changes its banks and causes floods, or the high waves that crash onto coastal shores. You can imagine how powerful the energy of water is.
This energy can be harnessed and converted into electricity. Generating electricity from hydropower does not produce emissions of greenhouse gases. It is also a renewable source, as the water cycle and the Earth’s hydrological cycle are constantly being renewed. All that a hydropower system needs is a constant source of flowing water (e.g., a stream or river). Unlike wind or solar energy, this source can provide electricity generation 24 hours a day.
Wave energy
The World Energy Council estimates that up to two terawatts of electricity could be generated from wave energy each year. This is twice the current global electricity production and is equivalent to the energy produced by 2,000 large oil, coal, or nuclear power plants. The renewable energy stored in the oceans (if it could all be harnessed) would be 5,000 times greater than current global electricity needs. So far, the idea of harnessing this energy has only been a theoretical possibility. The fact is that it is a technology that is still under development. Currently, it is not possible to estimate how soon and to what extent it will be able to contribute to the global energy landscape.
River energy
Hydropower harnesses the energy of water as it flows from higher levels to lower levels (as water flows downstream). The greater the drop, the more energy the water has, and the more electricity can be produced.
The construction of large hydropower plants usually requires the construction of dams, which in turn leads to the flooding of large ecosystems. When placing these facilities, it is also necessary to take into account the water needs of settlements, agriculture, and also the ecosystems located downstream along the rivers.
Small hydropower plants can also produce large amounts of electricity without requiring large reservoirs. Hydropower plants are classified as “small,” “mini,” or “micro” based on their electricity production. Their advantage is that they do not significantly alter the flow of water or its natural course for electricity production.

Our solar system consists of 8 planets (that’s how many we know of so far) and a large star – the Sun.
The Sun has been producing energy for billions of years.
Without the Sun, the Earth would freeze, and plants would not be able to grow or produce oxygen, which means there would be no life on it.
Renewable Energy Sources
Renewable energy comes from natural sources that can be replenished more easily.
Sunlight, which is never-ending, is also a renewable energy source.
Other sources of renewable energy include wind, water, and geothermal energy.
These sources cause little or no pollution and will be available for thousands or even millions of years.
What is Solar Energy?
The term solar energy refers to energy obtained from the sun.
This energy is the most important source of energy for all living things.
Unlike non-renewable energy sources, such as fossil fuels, solar energy is a renewable source.
The main advantage of solar energy is that it does not produce any pollutants and is one of the cleanest forms of energy.
Its only limitation is that the amount of sunlight that reaches the Earth’s surface is not constant.
It varies depending on the location, time of day, season, and weather conditions.
Uneven sunlight, of course, can also affect the efficiency of solar energy generation.
What is a Solar Cell?
A solar cell converts sunlight into electricity.
Do you remember photosynthesis?
The solar cells in a plant are called chloroplasts – they collect sunlight and convert it into usable energy.
When we use the sun to generate energy, solar cells are also called photovoltaic cells.
Photovoltaic cells (the term means “light electricity”) convert sunlight directly into electrical energy.
The cells are made of materials that can conduct electricity and help capture light.
Sunlight is made up of tiny particles of light energy. When sunlight hits a photovoltaic cell, it is either reflected, passes through, or is absorbed (just like in plants, where chloroplast cells absorb light).
Only the absorbed light provides the energy that can be used for electricity.
Are you interested in how solar power plants work?
Solar panels, which are installed on the roof of a house, capture the energy of the sun.
This energy is used to supply the house with electricity and even hot water.
A single photovoltaic cell can produce a small amount of electricity, so several cells are combined into panels.
If you walk around your neighborhood, you can see solar panels on the roofs of homes and businesses nearby.
The panels must be carefully installed so that they are as well exposed to the sun as possible and can convert the maximum amount of sunlight into energy.
In the Northern Hemisphere, most solar cells are facing south.
When the sun is at its highest point in the sky, it shines from the south. When the sun hits the panels, the energy is converted into electricity.
Supplying electricity through solar power plants is one of the most efficient, sustainable, mobile, and clean ways to generate energy in the world.
How can we use solar energy?
Solar energy can be used to heat rooms, water, swimming pools, and to produce electricity for lighting and household appliances.
It is the energy of the future, which is good for our planet, because its production does not pollute the environment, does not create noise, and does not produce greenhouse gas emissions during operation.
Did you know?
- That the Sun is by far the largest object in the solar system.
- That astronauts cannot visit the Sun because its surface is too hot. The temperature on the surface is about 5500 degrees Celsius.
- That it takes less than 10 minutes for sunlight to reach the Earth (the distance from the Sun to the Earth is 149,600,000 km).
- That to meet the needs of all households in the world, solar power plants would have to be installed on less than 1 percent of the Earth.
- That the largest solar power plant in the world is located in the Mojave Desert in the USA.

Obnovljiva energija prihaja iz naravnih virov, ki jih je mogoče lažje obnoviti.

Kaj je sončna energija?
Izraz sončna energija se nanaša na energijo, pridobljeno iz sonca.
Ta energija je najpomembnejši vir energije za vsa živa bitja.
Drugače kot pri neobnovljivih virih energije, kot so fosilna goriva, gre pri sončni energiji za obnovljiv vir.

Kaj je sončna celica?

Se spomniš fotosinteze?
Sončne celice v rastlini se imenujejo kloroplasti – ti zbirajo sončno svetlobo in jo pretvarjajo v uporabno energijo.

Sončno energijo lahko uporabimo za ogrevanje prostorov, vode, bazenov in za proizvodnjo elektrike za osvetljevanje in hišne porabnike.
Je energija prihodnosti, ki je dobra za naš planet, saj njena proizvodnja ne onesnažuje okolja, ne ustvarja hrupa, med obratovanjem pa ne prihaja niti do izpustov toplogrednih plinov..

Oceans act as thermal regulators, absorbing carbon dioxide. Covering nearly the entire planet, their waters absorb vast amounts of CO2. Several major currents exist, such as the Gulf Stream or the Antarctic Circumpolar Current. These play a vital role in regulating the climate and circulating nutrients in the water. This ensures that all the animals living in the ocean have the food they need to survive, from krill to white sharks.

Ocean currents can be cold, originating from polar and temperate latitudes, or warm, originating from the tropics and extending to higher latitudes. When several of these currents combine, they form what are known as gyres, which rotate clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and counterclockwise in the Southern Hemisphere.

This is precisely what we are witnessing today: many plants and animals are beginning to die, while others struggle to adapt. All are facing significant challenges. Algae and plankton sustain animals, and small creatures like krill are eaten by much larger fish, such as whales and seals. Thus, the entire food chain is severely threatened, a danger that already exists in this area, as the krill population has declined by more than 80% in many areas. Krill thrive in cold waters near sea ice. As temperatures rise, there is less sea ice.

On the other hand, corals are ocean animals that are highly sensitive to changes. However, when the water gets too warm, the algae can no longer carry out this vital process, and they eventually die, causing the corals to lose their color, weaken, and eventually die.

Oceans absorb up to a quarter of the CO2 emitted by humans, but they may be paying a high price. As we have seen, the ocean influences the climate, whether near the coast or thousands of kilometers inland. Thanks to what is known as the thermohaline circulation, Europe enjoys a pleasant climate. Without it, we would have to wear warm fleece clothing during the winter months.

This current travels across the entire planet, carrying warm water from the Pacific and Indian Oceans to Antarctica, where it sinks into the Norwegian Sea. How to measure the amount of oxygen throughout history
Fire needs fuel, a spark, and oxygen. Undoubtedly, the sparks in ancient times were lightning strikes, which still cause many fires today. The fuel was plant life and enormous fungi that were just beginning to colonize land. Oxygen is the most controversial of the three, as experts disagree on how much there was, when, and how its concentration changed throughout history.
Scientists infer the amount of oxygen based on coal in swamps, mountain building, erosion, and the chemical processes associated with them. All of these methods are valid, but none are as accurate as analyzing the remains of fires – charcoal.
They analyzed burnt plants and fungi
The charcoal they analyzed is part of the fossil remains of burnt plants and fungi called Prototaxites, which are found in sedimentary rocks, and we know how old they are. Since we know that fires began almost simultaneously with the growth of land plants and fungi, the new study also pushes their origin back by about 10 million years, to 430 million years ago.

The time when the first plants moved onto land was the Silurian geological period. During this period, about 60% of aquatic organisms became extinct. The reason for this is believed to be toxic metals that began to be released from the ocean floor due to the reduced concentration of oxygen. The first hypothesis is that at some point, the concentration of nitrogen increased, which stimulated the growth of plants that consumed more oxygen. The second hypothesis states that due to the higher temperatures in this period, oxygen began to leave the sea, starting from the bottom.
The new study adds to one of the older studies that examined pockets of fluid in halite, a special type of sodium chloride or salt. It showed that the concentration of oxygen in the Silurian was about 21% or even higher. Previous models predicted less oxygen in the atmosphere and even less in earlier periods. The new study could overturn both of these.

Weeds are not a specific type of plant. In nature, they have the same rights as all other members of the flora. The term "weeds" refers to those plants that interfere with the cultivation of vegetables, berries, flowers, and fruits. All wild plants in the garden are considered enemies to them. If you ask any gardener whether weeds are necessary in the garden, they will all answer – no, and they will be right.

However, it's not that simple. Besides the obvious drawbacks, weeds also have benefits for people and plants. Some of them help control various pests that plague garden crops. They provide signals about the acidity and fertility of the soil. Many can serve as mulch and even fertilizer. In short, weeds have many functions. But first, let's consider the harm they cause.

The Harm Caused by Weeds

What harm do weeds cause to cultivated plants, animals, and people?

- They take food from cultivated plants, making it difficult for them to develop. Weeds are adapted by nature to grow without human intervention, ensuring their survival in various ways. In terms of water consumption and nutrient uptake, most weeds outcompete cultivated plants. Tall weeds that shade cultivated plants hinder their photosynthesis process, which can even lead to plant death. Controlling weeds improves the living conditions of cultivated plants. According to statistics, crop losses in agriculture due to weeds can reach a quarter, and their widespread distribution can cover half of the field. Of course, in their own garden, a gardener will not allow such weeds to flourish and will remove them promptly, ideally in the seedling stage. An unconnected root will not sprout. If the root of a weed has already begun to split, it must be dug out, ensuring that no pieces of the root remain in the soil.

- They can serve as carriers of dangerous diseases, even if they themselves are not affected. Chickweed and nettle can infect grain with rust. The same wheatgrass carries the ergot pathogen and powdery mildew to cultivated plants. Together with bindweed and wild oats, they infect garden crops with root rot. Black nightshade carries potato cancer, and wild crucifers are a source of clubroot. Many viruses that infect cultivated plants first appear on weeds and are then transmitted to vegetables or grains by sucking insects. Couch grass is a grass that is very difficult to remove from the garden. It can even sprout from a 1 cm piece of root. When digging, use a fork rather than a hoe, as a hoe will cut the couch grass into pieces. Carefully remove even small pieces of the root.

- They provide shelter for various pests of garden crops. Thistles and sowthistles are places where the winter moth lays its eggs. Its caterpillars feed on plants from the cereal family. They are also affected by flies – Swedish and Hessian – which lay their eggs on the roots of cereal weeds. Wild crucifers are a source of pests for cultivated varieties of this family: cabbage moths, flea beetles, and cabbage white butterflies.

- The moth lays its eggs on chickweed and lamb's quarters, and its caterpillars damage many garden crops. Where there is a lot of couch grass, there are also many wireworms, which contribute to its reproduction. Even if there are no weeds in the beds themselves, but they grow in the surrounding areas, pests can easily move to cultivated plants. Mow the grass along the edges, along fences, and in the garden to prevent pests from multiplying.

- Weeds can parasitize cultivated plants and draw nutrients from them. This includes both parasitic and semi-parasitic plants.

- If weed seeds get into animal feed, it can cause poisoning. If weed seeds get into grain, the flour not only loses its taste but can also become toxic.

- Wild plants can cross-pollinate with cultivated varieties, degrading their varietal quality. This phenomenon occurs in cereals and crucifers. When growing cabbage seedlings, make sure that there are no wild mustards, radishes, and other wild crucifers growing nearby.

- Ragweed is a weed that causes serious allergic reactions in people.

This is how weeds behave in fields and garden beds. Of course, they have no place there. But all these plants can also be found in areas that have not been developed by humans. Gathered there, they can be useful to humans.

The Usefulness of Weeds

How can weeds be used to benefit humans and cultivated plants? The uses of these plants are very diverse, and the benefits of weeds are undeniable.

- They can be used as food. Surprisingly, many weeds can be successfully used as edible plants. When properly prepared, they are not only healthy but also tasty. It turns out that purslane can be added to soups and salads, and even pickled like cabbage.

- The roots of salsify are perfectly edible, boiled and fried. In Japan, this plant is grown as a crop, and no wild varieties are grown there. Many people prepare dishes from Siberian cress. The roots of couch grass can be ground in a meat grinder and made into cutlets. The leaves of dandelion, young leaves of clover, and plantain are added to salads. Wood sorrel, mixed with other herbs, can be an excellent filling for pies.

- The leaves of wild strawberries contain a record amount of vitamin C, which is very important in the spring, when they are used in salads. Dandelion contains a lot of beta-carotene. And soup made from young nettles is a classic. You can even make desserts from weeds, for example, by making a delicious and healthy jam. When using wild plants for food, remember that collecting near busy roads is not possible. Plants tend to absorb harmful substances emitted by exhaust fumes.

- Many weeds are also medicinal. Their list is very long, and they often cure diseases more effectively than conventional medicines. It is enough to remember chamomile, dandelion, nettle, clover, horsetail, and St. John's wort, which can cure many diseases. The same couch grass helps with joint pain, kidney problems, and respiratory diseases. There are plants that help manage even oncology. These are hemlock and aconite. Simple salsify is an excellent preventive measure against oncological diseases. The rubber molecules contained in the roots are similar to cancer cells. When they enter the human body, they force it to produce special immune cells to destroy them. At the same time, all other atypical cells, including cancer cells, are destroyed.

Japan is known for its dietary programs, which emphasize the consumption of salsify. It is not surprising that the Japanese are the healthiest people in the world. Even the best medicinal plants have contraindications for their use. Consider this before using herbal remedies.

- They can also be good in the garden. Over time, when they decompose in a compost heap, they will be invaluable to gardeners, who will use them to enrich the soil with organic matter and many useful substances. Most plants are rich in nitrogen, dandelion and plantain leaves contain a lot of phosphorus, and chamomile, yarrow, and nettle are sources of potassium. Horsetail will enrich the compost with silicon. There are also trace elements in trace amounts. If cultivated plants have already gained strength, the control of weeds, especially annuals, can be slightly relaxed. They cover the soil with a green carpet, which protects it from overheating. Left for the winter, they will enrich the soil with organic matter, and their dead roots will become food for earthworms. Do not allow the plants that remain in the beds to seed, so that you do not have to fight with them with double the force next season.

- The rich mineral composition of weeds allows you to prepare a very useful fertilizer for garden plants. The richer the herbal composition of this fertilizer, the greater the benefit to garden crops. The technology for its preparation is very simple. A container is filled with chopped greens and filled with water. During fermentation, the water is enriched with nutrients. After a week, the solution can be used for feeding, diluting it ten times with water. This green elixir is not only suitable for onions and garlic. All other garden plants respond to such a supplement with increased growth. You cannot use metal utensils to prepare such a fertilizer. An unwanted oxidation process may occur in it.

- Weeds also help control pests. Plants containing substances such as wormwood, walnut, and dandelion are natural insecticides against insects, ticks, and many other pests. Decoctions and infusions are gentle and effective remedies. Unlike chemicals, natural remedies are safe for humans, so their use is more desirable.

- Weeds can be an indicator that signals the condition of the soil. Horsetail, creeping cinquefoil, violet, and wood sorrel indicate that the soil is too acidic and that it is time to lime it. If a large amount of shepherd's purse has settled in potato fields, the field is depleted and it is time to change it. If there is a lot of chamomile in the garden, the soil is too heavy and needs to be loosened more often. The distribution of crucifers indicates an excess of potassium in the soil.

- Weeds can also perform another very important function for gardeners: they can create an excellent mulch that will help reduce the number of waterings, prevent overheating of the soil, and increase its fertility. There are plants whose mulching can prevent plant diseases. For example, a layer of nettles under tomatoes will be a prophylactic against late blight.

It is impossible to use for mulching weeds that have already seeded, otherwise you can spread them with your own hands in the garden.

Conclusion

There is nothing superfluous in nature. Weeds have the same right to exist as cultivated plants. But maintaining the balance between the number of different plants is a human task.

2018
The squat is one of the fundamental movement patterns in the human body, so it’s no surprise that it’s also one of the most popular exercises for developing strength. When we talk about squats as a strength exercise, we quickly come to the question of how deep we should squat and how to achieve a deep squat if we can’t currently do it.
Let’s debunk some myths about squat depth:
1) Everyone should be able to perform a deep squat.
This way of thinking is very dangerous, as it can lead to hip injuries in some cases. People have different hip joint structures. To put it simply, some of us have hips that are built for deep squats, while others don’t. Someone with hips that aren’t built for deep squats will never be able to achieve that position (at least not with proper technique), so it’s neither sensible nor safe for them to train deep squats. Everyone should work with a trainer to determine the exact foot width and position, as well as the squat depth that suits them based on their hip structure.
2) Deep squats are dangerous.
The most common argument is that some people’s knees go past their toes in a deep squat. According to some research from the 1960s, this is harmful to the structures in the knee. To date, more than 10 studies have been conducted that have refuted this hypothesis. Whether the knees go past the toes primarily depends on the individual’s femur length. If the heels are in contact with the ground at all times, pushing the knees past the level of the toes is definitely not a dangerous action.
3) Tight hamstring muscles limit squat depth.
The hamstring muscles run across the hip and knee. It’s true that they stretch when the hip flexes, but they also shorten with plantarflexion (flexion) of the ankle on the way down into the bottom position of the squat. This means that these muscles don’t stretch much during a deep squat and therefore can’t be the limiting factor in mobility. The real limiting factors are hip and/or ankle mobility. In today’s article, let’s take a closer look at how ankle mobility affects squat depth.
Ankle mobility as a limiting factor in squat depth
If the ankle has been identified as a limiting factor in squat depth, we need to focus directly on improving the mobility of this joint. The best way to do this is from two angles. First, do as much deep squatting as possible. In the initial phases, you can help yourself by using elevated heels. This will relieve the ankles and actually allow for a greater range of motion and more weight on the bar. Second, do isolation exercises for ankle mobility directly before squat training, preferably in the warm-up phase. This exercise should bring the ankle into a position as close as possible to the one in a deep squat. It’s also important that the knee is in a flexed position, as this relieves the gastrocnemius muscle, which is relaxed in a deep squat. This applies only to deep squats, where the hips are lowered below the level of the knees. In individuals who don’t squat deeply due to the structure of their hips or other limitations, ankle mobility doesn’t play a significant role.
#1 exercise to increase ankle mobility
The exercise that has proven to be the most useful in my coaching practice is the ankle stretch using a band on a box. This exercise is extremely effective and comfortable, as you choose a box that is high enough so that you can stand. The key is to use your hand to manipulate the knee in the direction it goes in the bottom position of the squat. This will always be forward and at the same time slightly in the direction of external rotation (see video at 0:22). You can make the exercise more intense by using a band. Attach it so that the ankle is pulled backward (see video at 0:30) or so that it is pulled inward (see video at 0:37). Depending on when you feel the “pinch” in your ankle more: when you push the knee forward or in external rotation. Of course, you can choose both variations, one in the first set and the other in the second set. It’s best to do this exercise in two sets of 30 seconds directly before squat training. In the warm-up sets, before loading the bar with the working weight, you can do a few repetitions of squats with a 5–10 second pause in the bottom position. Here, focus on pushing the hips forward in the direction of the feet. This will further push the ankle into plantarflexion and make it more mobile for the later working sets of squats.
Tine Seražin Lisjak

1) Vsak posameznik bi moral biti sposoben iti v globok počep.
Tako razmišljanje je zelo nevarno, saj lahko v nekaterih primerih vodi do poškodb kolka. Ljudje imamo različne strukture kolčnega sklepa. Če močno poenostavim, to pomeni, da so kolki nekaterih izmed nas zgrajeni za globok počep, kolki drugih pa ne. Posameznik s kolki, ki niso zgrajeni za globok počep ne bo nikdar prišel v ta položaj (vsaj s pravilno tehniko ne) in zanj zato ni smiselno niti varno trenirati počepa v globino. Vsak posameznik mora s pomočjo trenerja ugotoviti točno širino in pozicijo stopal ter samo globino počepa, ki mu odgovarja glede na strukturo njegovih kolkov.

Najpogostejši argument je ta, da gredo pri nekaterih posameznikih kolena v globokem počepu čez prste. To naj bi bilo po neki raziskavi iz 60. let prejšnjega stoletja škodljivo za strukture v kolenu. Do današnjega dne je bilo narejenih že več kot 10 raziskav, ki so to hipotezo ovrgle. Ali gredo kolena čez prste je na prvem mestu odvisno od dolžine stegnenice posameznika. V kolikor so pete ves čas v stiku s tlemi, potisk kolen čez nivo prstov stopala vsekakor ni nevarno početje.

Mišice upogibalke kolena (v nadaljevanju zadnje stegenske mišice) potekajo čez kolk in koleno. Res je, da se z upogibom kolka raztegujejo, vendar se hkrati skrajšujejo z dorifleksijo (upogibom) gležnja na poti v spodnjo pozicijo počepa. Pri posameznikih, ki zaradi strukture svojih kolkov ali drugih omejitev ne počepajo globoko, mobilnost gležnjev ne igra posebne vloge.

Vaja, ki se je v moji trenerski praksi izkazala za najbolj uporabno je razteg gležnja s pomočjo ročke na box-u. Vaja je skrajno učinkovita in udobna, saj izberemo tako visok box, da stojimo. Vajo je najbolje izvajati v dveh serijah po 30 sekund neposredno pred treningom počepa. At the end of the 19th century, American chemist and physiologist Wilbur Atwater calculated the number of calories in different foods and derived the 4-4-9 formula. According to this formula, the energy value of carbohydrates and proteins is 4 kcal/g, and that of fats is 9 kcal/g. With this system, Atwater aimed to determine how many calories a person needs each day to provide the body with energy. This simple formula is still popular among nutrition experts, but its accuracy and relevance are being questioned by modern scientists.

What manufacturers state on the packaging
Manufacturers state the calorie information on the packaging, obtained in a laboratory where the food is literally burned. Experts place the food in a special chamber – a calorimeter – and measure how much heat (energy) is released during combustion. This determines the energy value of each product. In the laboratory, this process takes seconds. The human body takes 8 to 80 hours to "burn" food and assimilates calories in different ways. Consequently, the laboratory data and the actual data do not match.
Susan Roberts, a nutritionist at Tufts University in Boston, found that the number of calories on American labels is, on average, inaccurate by 8%.
What changes the energy value
When food is cut into small pieces, the cellular structures are broken down. In this way, part of the body's digestion is done in advance, and the body uses less energy to digest soft food. Also, parts of vegetables and fruits that differ in density do not have the same energy value.
Jeffrey Livesey, an independent British nutritionist and a food expert for the UN, notes that the number of calories also depends on the fiber content, which accounts for 5% of the product's energy value. In an interview with The Independent, Livesey emphasizes that the existing formula does not take fiber into account, so foods that contain it are actually more caloric than manufacturers state.
© Dan Gold / Unsplash
How calories are used
Atwater's System incorrectly calculates the amount of calories used.
Three-quarters of the average person's daily energy expenditure is used for daily activities, the functioning of organs, digestion, and maintaining a constant body temperature, not for sports. Therefore, the claim that it is easy to burn off excess calories through exercise is mainly true for professional athletes.
Experiments measuring the energy value of different products using the same criteria also lead to incorrect results. A lollipop and an orange may have the same number of calories, but the body absorbs them differently, and they cannot be counted in the same way.
In addition, there are foods with "negative" calories. Ice water does not provide energy but forces the body to burn calories to maintain the desired temperature.
Why tasty food is healthier than low-calorie food
Mexican nutritionist Salvador Camacho and his supporters argue that low-calorie processed foods and sugars destroy the hormonal system. High levels of insulin cause energy to be converted into fat and not used to nourish the body. As a result, a person constantly feels hungry and starts overeating.
Camacho warned that by counting calories, we eat less than the body needs and limit our food choices. Fresh, natural products are more effective in avoiding problems than low-calorie processed foods, especially since the data on the energy value of frozen and reheated processed foods can differ from the actual numbers by up to 70%. The nutritionist advises not to give up tasty, even if high-calorie, food – it simply doesn't have to be turned into a daily habit.
© Gardie Design Social / Unsplash
Who needs the changes
The British food company Weight Watchers introduced a points system in 2001, which shifted the focus from counting calories to classifying foods according to their sugar and saturated fat content and their impact on appetite. Chris Stirk, the executive director of Weight Watchers in the UK, pointed out that the idea of relying on calorie counting for weight loss is "outdated": "Science is evolving every day, every month, every year, let alone the nineteenth century." But for now, it is the only major company that has begun to change the existing system.
Experts from the World Health Organization and the UN Food and Agriculture Organization agreed with the "Weight Watchers" approach in 2002, but in the last 17 years, they have not taken any practical steps to support the company's initiative.
Richard Wrangham, a professor of biology and anthropology at Harvard University, pointed out in an interview with The Independent that "scientists have known for decades that Atwater's research is unreliable, but the issue has not been important enough. As a result, consumers are still receiving incorrect information.">

Have you ever wondered why wisdom teeth take so long to erupt? A study published a few months ago in the journal Science Advances offers one of the most compelling explanations for this phenomenon.
Delayed tooth eruption is linked to slow craniofacial development.
The time gap between the eruption of other teeth and the eruption of wisdom teeth is unusually long. Furthermore, the eruption of wisdom teeth is often unusually painful. There is often limited space in the mouth, so wisdom teeth often erupt at unusual angles, which can compromise adjacent teeth. As a result, tooth extraction is often necessary.
Chimpanzees are the primates that most closely resemble humans in this regard. Their teeth typically complete their development around the age of 12. The researchers who conducted the aforementioned study believe they have found an explanation for the unusually slow development of human teeth. Their research suggests that this phenomenon is linked to biomechanical constraints during craniofacial development, i.e., the development of the skull and face. The delay in the eruption of wisdom teeth is therefore linked to the relatively slow craniofacial development in humans. Wisdom teeth begin to erupt only when there is at least theoretically enough space for them. However, as mentioned, the available space is often not optimal, so the eruption of the last molars can lead to what is known as crowding.
Jaw muscle strengthening is needed before wisdom tooth eruption.
The delayed eruption of wisdom teeth in humans is directly linked to the slow development of the jaw. Furthermore, the human face is unusually short. Wisdom teeth therefore wait for the most optimal moment, and the waiting time can be particularly long in some individuals. The eruption of wisdom teeth is therefore also conditioned by purely individual factors. It depends primarily on the size or the rate of development of our jaw and on the development of our chewing muscles, which move the lower jaw. If wisdom teeth were to erupt too early, they would encounter a system that is not yet ready for them. An attempt to use prematurely erupted wisdom teeth for chewing would most likely lead to damage to the temporomandibular joint.
Researchers compared models of jaw and skull development in different primates.
Although tooth development is faster in other primates, a similar principle was also found in other species. The researchers created three-dimensional models of skull and chewing muscle development in more than twenty groups of primates, including gorillas and lemurs. They then compared these models with data on the rate of jaw development. In this context, the delayed development of wisdom teeth in humans becomes much more logical.

The researchers' findings are very valuable for both the theoretical and practical aspects of dental medicine. A detailed examination of the created models could help to better understand the specifics of wisdom tooth eruption, which could lead to the development of methods to prevent the pain that is often associated with the final stage of our tooth development.
Quick help for pain associated with wisdom tooth growth.
Severe pain that occurs during wisdom tooth eruption requires consultation with a dentist, who will suggest the most appropriate measures. If crowding is diagnosed, you will most likely be referred to an oral surgeon, who will take care of safe extraction. In the case of less intense pain, you can also help yourself with some natural remedies, such as salt water, mint, clove oil, garlic, oregano oil, or aloe vera.

As the vibration passes through these bones, it is further amplified and travels to the cochlea, which contains fluid and sensory cells surrounded by hair cells.
