As we mentioned earlier, the ear also provides us with balance, in addition to hearing. This involves three semicircular canals located near the cochlea. Like the cochlea, the canals are filled with fluid and contain hair cells inside. The canals lie in three directions, and the fluid also flows in these directions: left-right, forward-backward, and up-down. The hair cells are covered with balance stones that are weighted in the direction of the Earth’s gravity.
The vibration of these hair cells, along with the fluid, causes the creation of a nerve signal that is transmitted to the balance center in the brain. This allows us to perceive our position in space, or to maintain our balance.

Če je otrokov kazalnik višji od 6,1 mmol / l, potem je potrebno ponovno opraviti teste in izključiti tveganje za nastanek diabetes mellitusa.
Do danes ni načinov in zdravil za ozdravitev diabetesa mellitusa, saj znanost še ne ve, kako obnoviti ali nadomestiti celice, odgovorne za proizvodnjo inzulina - hormona, ki se proizvaja v trebušni slinavki in znižuje raven sladkorja v krvi. Kadar je v telesu motena proizvodnja inzulina, se razvije sladkorna bolezen tipa 1, pri sladkorni bolezni tipa 2 pa se inzulin normalno proizvaja, vendar telo ne ve, kako ga pravilno uporabljati.
V telesu inzulin pomaga sladkorju iz krvnega obtoka v celico, prav tako kot ključ nam pomaga odpreti ključavnico vrat in vstopiti domov. Ko je proizvodnja inzulina motena, pride do njegove pomanjkljivosti, sladkor pa ostane v krvi, vendar ne more vstopiti v celice in stradajo. Zato bolnik s prvo vrsto sladkorne bolezni nenehno čuti lakoto. Tudi po jedi se ne počuti polno. Da se znebi lakote in pomaga sladkorju priti v celice, mu mora nenehno vbrizgati inzulin.
Ni preprečevanja diabetesa mellitusa tipa 1, se pravi, da človek sam ne more narediti ničesar, da ne bi imel sladkorne bolezni. Če pa ste diagnosticirali sladkorno bolezen tipa 1 ali imate v svoji družini sorodnike, ki trpijo zaradi te bolezni, poskušajte otroke odvrniti od rojstva. Dokazano je, da je tveganje za diabetes diabetes mellitus pri otrocih z oslabljeno imuniteto mnogokrat večje kot pri otrocih, ki se ukvarjajo s športom in redko trpijo za prehladom.
Pri drugi vrsti diabetesa mellitus trebušna slinavka proizvede normalne količine inzulina, vendar premalo inzulina za vzdrževanje normalne ravni krvnega sladkorja. V 96% je to posledica dejstva, da človek redno prenajeda in ima prekomerno težo. Drugo vrsto sladkorne bolezni lahko preprečimo, če jo preprečimo pravočasno. Če je kdo od staršev ali sorodnikov zbolel za sladkorno boleznijo tipa 2, potem strogo spremljajte, da otrok ne razvije debelosti.
Od 10. leta naprej redno preverjajte sladkor pri otroku v krvi, saj je v zadnjih letih sladkorna bolezen tipa 2 postala veliko mlajša, danes pa jo pogosto diagnosticiramo pri otrocih, starejših od te starosti..
Test krvnega sladkorja se naredi na prazen želodec, torej ne morete ničesar jesti ali piti 8-10 ur pred jemanjem. Če pijete čaj ali jeste pred krvnim testom, bo raven sladkorja višja od običajne. Poleg tega lahko na natančnost rezultata vpliva nedavna okužba in stres. Zato je takoj po bolezni bolje, da ne darujete krvi za sladkor, ampak pred analizo morate dobro spati.
Prvi simptomi sladkorne bolezni so nenehna žeja, pogosto uriniranje in utrujenost. Razlog za to je, da je krvni sladkor količina glukoze v krvi, ki zagotavlja energijo vsem organom in tkivom. Ko raven sladkorja v krvi naraste, ga naše ledvice poskušajo odstraniti iz telesa in ga začnejo izločati v urin. Toda sladkor lahko iz telesa odstranimo le skupaj s tekočino, v kateri je raztopljen. Zato skupaj s sladkorjem, ki se izloča z urinom, določena količina vode zapusti telo in človek doživi stalno žejo..
Več sladkorja se izloči z urinom, več tekočine se izloči iz telesa, manj energijskih celic dobi, zaradi česar želi človek nenehno piti, spati in jesti.
Z močnim zvišanjem krvnega sladkorja se simptomi bolezni povečajo: ketonska telesa v krvi se povečajo, kar vodi v močno dehidracijo in znižanje krvnega tlaka. Ko je raven sladkorja več kot 33 mmol / L, lahko pride do hiperglikemične kome in z vrednostmi nad 55 mmol / L nastane hipersmolarna koma. Zapleti teh grudic so zelo resni - od akutne odpovedi ledvic do tromboze globokih žil. S hipersmolarno komo smrtnost doseže 50%.

One of the most dangerous plant pests is the root-knot nematode. These microscopic worms live in the roots, stems, leaves, and even fruits of plants, and they reproduce very quickly. Root-knot nematodes pose a significant threat to plants, as they cause galls to form on the roots. These galls are actually swellings that are caused by the nematode feeding on the plant's tissues. What they are and how to deal with them will be discussed in this article.

Description
There are approximately thirty species of these worms in nature. Some affect plants, others affect animals, and still others affect humans. We will focus on root-knot nematodes, which parasitize the roots of plants:

- Male nematodes are mobile, unlike the sedentary females. Their bodies are worm-like, 0.5–2 mm long, tapering at the front and rounded at the back.
- The larvae resemble the males in shape but are smaller. The posterior end of the body is more transparent and pointed.
- Eggs are microscopic and white. The female lays them in so-called egg sacs, which are made of a gelatinous film. Each sac contains a large number of eggs.

At the anterior end of the root-knot nematode (photo in the article) is a mouth opening, inside which is a hard needle called a stylet. With this apparatus, they pierce the plant's root and suck out the sap. The worms have a small head, mobile lips, and tiny eyes. The outside of the body is covered with an impermeable but flexible cuticle that is very resistant to chemicals.

Biology of Roundworms
They reproduce in two ways:

- The female is on the surface of the root and lays eggs in a sac, from which the larvae emerge and enter the soil, then penetrate the root system of the host plant, infecting it.
- The female is completely within the root tissue and lays eggs there. The hatched larvae move through the root tissue, settling there to feed and develop. They are no longer biologically protected.

It should be noted that under favorable conditions, the larvae can move from the roots through all the organs of the plant.

Root-Knot Nematode Attack
The most favorable conditions for their reproduction are high soil moisture and air temperature above 18 degrees Celsius. The period of root-knot nematode formation is approximately one month. They can reproduce up to six generations per year. Plants affected by these pests have the following characteristics:

- Stunted growth
- Curling of leaves
- Cessation of growth
- Formation of yellow galls
- Growth of numerous thread-like roots (root beard).

It is important to distinguish the galls on diseased plants from natural thickenings of a white color that retain moisture.

Origin of Root-Knot Nematodes
Infection with nematodes occurs through the soil and planting material. It is also possible to introduce these tiny parasites with contaminated tools, pots, and even water that drips from a damaged plant during watering.

Nematodes are found not only in gardens but also in forests, compost, and humus. Even purchased soil with raw earth in greenhouses can contain them.

Cucumber Pests
These tiny worms are voracious and prolific. They quickly accumulate in large numbers in the soil, especially if the crop is planted in the same place year after year. The most root-knot nematodes are found on cucumbers and tomatoes. The parasites create small swellings in the roots, lay eggs, and the larvae that hatch feed on everything around them. When they feed on the roots, the worms prevent the cucumbers from developing properly, depriving them of the ability to feed normally. The roots of the plant affected by nematodes become swollen and have brownish thickenings. The branches weaken, the leaves fall off, and the cucumbers die.

The problem is that, due to their small size, the pest is very difficult to detect in the early stages of development. To prevent this, crop rotation should be practiced, changing the crops grown in a particular area each year. Where these parasites have appeared, plant garlic or cabbage instead of cucumbers. Nematodes do not tolerate these plants.

Nematodes in Open Ground
In open fields in the temperate European region, two species of root-knot nematodes are observed:

- Birch nematode - it only affects birch roots and does not pose a significant threat.
- Northern nematode - it lives in legumes, umbrella plants, ranunculus, and Compositae crops. Although this pest infects a large number of plants, it does not pose a great threat to annuals. This species has only one generation per year and does not have time to settle in the roots of the plant to weaken it significantly.

Soon, a new parasite, the Colombian root-knot nematode, is expected to appear in our country. It has already been brought to Europe and is successfully damaging roots, potatoes, beets, peas, and many other crops in open and closed ground. The damage reduces the proportion of tubers and reduces the yield. Losses reach up to 80%. It overwinters in the roots of cultivated plants and weeds, and in the egg stage, it is also in the soil. This parasite reproduces both sexually and asexually. The life cycle lasts up to four weeks.

Nematodes Not Found in Russia
There are four types of these pests that cause plant diseases but are not yet found in Russia. These include: Colombian, root, false Colombian, and false Gallic. The countries from which they can be imported are Ecuador, America, Mexico, and Chile.

One of the most dangerous and polyphagous is the root nematode. The exact range of its host plants has not yet been fully determined, but it has been found to affect economically important crops such as beans, soybeans, eggplants, cucumbers, watermelons, and tomatoes.

The false root nematode is no less dangerous. Its main hosts are potatoes and sugar beets. Infection with this species is possible through planting material (rhizomes, tubers) and soil. The worms of this genus form galls. They are most noticeable on sugar beets, from which small, numerous roots emerge. Symptoms of the disease appear five days after infection.

How to Fight?
The following agents are used to control root-knot nematodes:

- Chemical preparations are the most effective: Rogor, Nemafos, Bi-58, Dimethoat. The substance is dissolved according to the instructions, and the resulting mixture is used to treat the soil. This procedure is carried out several times per season, as the poisons kill only the adults.
- Biological agents. These substances are made from natural ingredients and are therefore not harmful to plants and humans. "Nematofagin" is often used. Read and follow the instructions before use.
- Heat treatment. The plant is removed from the soil, the severely affected roots are cut off, and the galls are removed. The rhizome is immersed in water at a temperature of 50 degrees Celsius for five minutes. The soil is replaced with another that has a loose structure, and a nematicide is added.

In case of severe damage, the plant is simply burned to prevent the pests from finding another victim.

Preventive Measures
Detecting and eliminating nematodes is very difficult, so it is best to take preventive measures to prevent these parasites from appearing. To do this, you need to:

- Carefully carry out autumn soil treatment
- Destroy weeds in a timely manner
- Do not bring plants with closed root systems from botanical gardens, greenhouses, and stores into greenhouses
- Clean up fallen leaves
- Observe crop rotation
- Regularly loosen the soil
- Fertilize the soil with organic matter
- Occasionally carry out abundant watering of the soil, followed by drying
- Try not to over-water the soil.

One of the modern ways to protect greenhouses from pests is the use of sulfur bombs.

Conclusion
Parasites that live in the roots of plants are dangerous pests that are difficult to detect. The main manifestations of the disease are swellings and galls that appear on the root system. When such formations are detected, microscopic examinations should be carried out, as they are not always caused by the presence of nematodes.

Eden najnevarnejših rastlinskih škodljivcev so ogorčice (okrogli črvi). So mikroskopske velikosti, živijo v koreninah, steblih, listih in celo plodovih, se zelo hitro razmnožujejo. Veliko nevarnost za rastline ustvarjajo žolčne ogorčice - škodljivci, ki živijo v njihovih koreninah. Paraziti s prodiranjem v tkiva prispevajo k nastanku izrastkov in oteklin (žolčev) v njih, od tod tudi njihovo ime. Kaj je in kako ravnati z njimi, bomo razpravljali v članku.
Opis
V naravi je približno trideset vrst teh črvov. Nekateri od njih vplivajo na rastline, drugi na živali, tretji pa na ljudi. Nadalje bomo govorili samo o koreninskih ogorčicah, ki parazitirajo v koreninah rastlin:
- Moški ogorčici so mobilni, za razliko od vretenastih nepremičnih samic. Njihovo telo je črvasto, dolgo 0,5–2 mm, spredaj zoženo in zadaj zaobljeno.
- Ličinke spominjajo na obliko samca, vendar so manjše. Zadnji del telesa je bolj pregleden in koničast.
- Jajca- mikroskopska, bela. Samica jih odloži v tako imenovane jajčne vrečke, ki so sestavljene iz želatinastega filma. Ena taka vrečka jih vsebuje ogromno.
Na koncu sprednjega dela koreninskih ogorčic (fotografija v članku) je ustna odprtina, znotraj katere je trda igla, imenovana stilet. S pomočjo tega aparata prebodejo korenino rastline in izsesajo sokove. Črvi imajo majhno glavo, premične ustnice in drobne oči. Zunanja stran telesa je prekrita z neprepustno, a fleksibilno kožico, ki je zelo odporna na kemikalije.
Biologija okroglih črvov
Razmnožujejo se na dva načina:
- Samica je na površini korenine in odloži jajčeca v vrečko, iz katere ličinke najprej vstopijo v zemljo, nato pa se prebijejo v koreninski sistem rastline gostiteljice, nato pa se okuži.
- Samica je popolnoma v tkivih korenine in v njej odlaga jajčeca. Izležene ličinke se premikajo po tkivih korenine in se v njej naselijo za prehrano in razvoj. Niso več biološko zaščiteni.
Upoštevati je treba, da se ličinke iz korenin pod ugodnimi pogoji lahko premikajo skozi vse organe rastline.
napad koreninskih ogorčic
Najprimernejši pogoji za njihovo razmnoževanje so visoka vlažnost tal in temperatura zraka nad 18 stopinj. Obdobje nastanka koreninske žolčne ogorčice je približnomesec. Lahko razmnožuje do šest generacij na leto. Rastline, ki jih prizadenejo škodljivci, imajo naslednje značilnosti:
- zatirani pogled;
- kodranje listov;
- ustavi rast;
- tvorba rumenega žolča;
- rast številnih niti podobnih korenin (koreninska brada).
Zelo pomembno je ločiti žolče obolele rastline od naravnih zadebelitev bele barve, ki zadržujejo vlago.
Od kod izvira koreninska ogorčica
Okužba z ogorčico se pojavi skozi zemljo in sadilni material. Popolnoma pa je mogoče vnesti drobne parazite z uporabo kontaminiranih pripomočkov, loncev in celo vode, ki pri zalivanju kaplja iz poškodovane rastline.
Nematode najdemo ne samo na vrtu, ampak tudi v gozdu, kompostu in humusu. In celo kupljena tla z surovo zemljo v rastlinjakih jih lahko vsebujejo.
Zajedavci kumare
Drobni črvi imajo strašno požrešnost in plodnost. Hitro in v velikih količinah se kopičijo v tleh, še posebej, če je pridelek posajen na enem mestu. Največ žolčnih ogorčic najdemo na kumarah in paradižniku. Paraziti, ki ustvarjajo majhne zadebelitve v koreninah, odlagajo jajčeca, iz katerih se pojavijo ličinke, ki požrejo vse okoli sebe. Če jedo korenine, črvi ne dovolijo, da se kumare razvije, kar ji prikrajša možnost, da bi normalno jedla. Korenine rastline, ki jih prizadene ogorčica, postanejo vodene, z odebelitvami rjavkastega odtenka. Veje oslabijo, listi odpadejoin kumare umirajo.
Težave so v tem, da je škodljivca zaradi majhne velikosti zelo težko odkriti v zgodnji fazi razvoja. Za preprečevanje ne smemo pozabiti na kolobarjenje, letno spreminjati gojenje pridelkov na mestu. Kjer so se ti paraziti pojavili, namesto kumar posadite česen ali zelje. Nematode ne prenašajo teh rastlin.
Ogorčice na odprtem tleh
Na odprtem polju v zmernem evropskem delu opazimo dve vrsti koreninskih ogorčic:
- Breza - naseli se samo na brezovih koreninah in ne predstavlja posebne nevarnosti.
- Severna - živi v stročnicah, dežnikih, velebiljih, ranunculusih in pridelkih Compositae. Čeprav škodljivec okuži ogromno rastlin, ne predstavlja velike nevarnosti za enoletnice. Ta vrsta ima samo eno generacijo na leto in se nima časa naseliti v koreninah rastline, da bi jo močno oslabila.
Kmalu naj bi na ozemlju naše države pričakovali novega parazita - kolumbijsko koreninsko ogorčico. V Evropo so ga že prinesli in uspešno škoduje korenju, krompirju, pesi, grahu in številnim drugim pridelkom v odprtih in zaprtih tleh. Zaradi poškodb se delež gomoljev zmanjša, pridelek pa se zmanjša. Izgube dosežejo do 80%. Prezimuje v koreninah gojenih rastlin in plevela, v fazi jajčec pa je tudi v zemlji. Ta parazit se razmnožuje tako spolno kot nespolno. Življenjski cikel traja do štiritednov.
Nematode, ki jih v Rusiji ni
Obstajajo štiri vrste teh škodljivcev, ki povzročajo bolezni rastlin, vendar še niso na voljo v Rusiji. Sem spadajo: kolumbijski, koreninski, lažni kolumbijski in lažni galski. Države, iz katerih jih je mogoče uvažati, so Ekvador, Amerika, Mehika, Čile.
Eden najbolj nevarnih in polifagnih je koren. Natančen obseg njegovih gostiteljskih rastlin še ni v celoti ugotovljen, vendar je ugotovljeno, da škodljivec prizadene gospodarsko pomembne pridelke: fižol, sojo, jajčevce, kumare, lubenice in paradižnike.
Nič manj nevarna ni lažna koreninska ogorčica. Njeni glavni gostitelji so krompir in sladkorna pesa. Okužba s to vrsto je možna preko sadilnega materiala (korenike, gomolji) in tal. Črvi tega rodu tvorijo žolče. Najbolj opazne so na sladkorni pesi, iz odebelitev katere izvirajo majhne številne korenine. Simptomi bolezni se pojavijo peti dan po okužbi.
Kako se boriti?

Soil Properties
If water runs off the surface and doesn’t penetrate deep into the soil, this indicates poor soil structure. Our walking on wet soil and tilling it before it has dried sufficiently can also contribute to this. In sandy soils, however, the opposite is true: water disappears before plants can meet their needs.
Trees and Shrubs
Due to their well-developed root systems that penetrate deep below the surface, trees and shrubs are less likely to suffer from water shortages. The exception is young plants, which need to be watered to prevent them from being affected. The same applies to plants that have been planted in containers. These are entirely dependent on our help, so regular watering ensures that they don’t suffer from a lack of water.
Lawns
With lawns, the amount of water is more important than the frequency of watering. If watering is insufficient, and only the top layer is moistened, the roots don’t penetrate deep, making the lawn more susceptible to drought. The penetration of water into deeper layers can also be hindered by thatch (dead grass) and remnants of cut grass, which clog and obstruct the supply of water to the roots. As a rule, at least 15 centimeters should be moistened during watering. This will keep the lawn looking beautiful and green even during dry periods.
Vegetable Gardens
Some vegetables are more sensitive to water shortages than others. In particular, fruiting vegetables require regular watering if we want to get a good yield. However, watering can also be a double-edged sword, as it can create favorable conditions for the development of fungal diseases.
Ornamental Plants
Along with water, we should also provide them with some foliar fertilizer, which they will repay us for with abundant flowering. During drought or after hail, we should spray them, as well as other affected plants, with products to promote rapid recovery (e.g., a solution of baking soda, a preparation made from nettles, etc.).
Watering Time
If possible, it is best to water garden plants in the early morning or during the morning hours; if not, we can also do it in the evening. Evening watering has some drawbacks, mainly because it creates excellent conditions for the development of fungal diseases. Try to water the plants only at the base, so that the leaves remain dry.
Measures to Improve Soil and Water Management
With some measures, we can also contribute to improving the conditions for water penetration and preventing excessive losses due to transpiration (water evaporation through the green parts of the plant). We can do this by breaking up the soil crust and interrupting the capillary connections; a hoe or other convenient tool will be helpful. Weeds also consume a lot of water at the expense of vegetables, so we should regularly remove them from the garden beds. With appropriate fertilization, especially with compost and organic fertilizers, the conditions for the formation of humus will be ensured, which is important for fertility and water retention. Mulch will also help to overcome dry days; we can use cut grass for this. This will also inhibit the growth of weeds, and if they do sprout, we can easily pull them out.
The summer heat will put both us and our garden plants to the test, but with watering, we can ensure that our garden remains a dream come true.

Infectious mononucleosis in children and adolescents is much more common than in older people. The disease was first described by N. F. Filatov in 1885. He called it idiopathic inflammation of the cervical glands. A few years later, Pfeiffer added to the description and gave the disease another name: "glandular fever."

Infectious mononucleosis in children: etiology
Previously, some scientists isolated bacteria from the Listerella group from patients with symptoms similar to the clinical picture of this disease. However, further studies showed that listerellosis and mononucleosis are not the same thing. At present, a virus is considered the causative agent of the disease, although its nature has not yet been precisely determined.

Infectious mononucleosis in children: epidemiology
The source of this infection is viral carriers and, of course, the sick person themselves. It is assumed that the main route of infection with mononucleosis is airborne transmission. The virus is present in particles of fluid or dust and enters the body in this way. Infection is also possible through everyday objects. In most cases, isolated cases of the disease are observed. However, outbreaks can occur in maternity hospitals, families, and among students. The contagiousness is low.

Infectious mononucleosis in a child: symptoms
The incubation period can be short (4 days) and very long (4 weeks), but on average, it lasts 1-2 weeks. The temperature rises sharply on the first day. The child feels generally unwell, has a headache, and a sore throat. In rare cases, the temperature may be subfebrile or even normal. The posterior cervical lymph nodes reach their maximum size by the 3rd-4th day. They can reach the size of a walnut. When touched, the lymph nodes are almost painless and slightly thickened. Sometimes, the surrounding cervical tissue swells around them. Other lymph nodes may also be affected, but to a lesser extent. Another common symptom is a sore throat. Its development contributes to secondary bacterial flora. The nasopharyngeal tonsil is also affected. Simultaneously with lymphadenitis, there is an increase in the size of the spleen and liver, and their functions are impaired. Dyspeptic symptoms are often observed. Some patients have a yellowish tinge to the whites of their eyes and skin. Sometimes, a rash appears. The disease lasts up to two weeks, rarely longer. First, the temperature decreases, the sore throat subsides, then the lymphadenitis resolves, and the size of the spleen and liver normalizes. However, changes in the blood may persist for a long time.

Infectious mononucleosis in children: diagnosis
Recognizing the disease can be problematic in some cases. In practice, misdiagnoses are common, such as lymphadenitis, sore throat, or diphtheria. To avoid this, the following characteristic features of the disease should be considered. Even before the development of a sore throat, lymphadenitis appears, the spleen enlarges, and the posterior lymph nodes are affected. Chronic mononucleosis, in which the infectious form persists because the virus remains in the body for too long, is even more difficult to diagnose correctly. To clarify the diagnosis, it is desirable to perform several histological tests. Blood tests also help in the diagnosis.

Najprej se temperatura zniža, angina izgine, nato preide limfadenitis, velikost vranice in jeter se normalizira. Toda na strani krvi se lahko spremembe dolgo zadržijo.

Priznavanje bolezni v nekaterih primerih povzroča znane težave. V praksi se pogosto pojavljajo napačne diagnoze: limfadenitis, vneto grlo, davica. Kronična mononukleoza, pri kateri se pretaka infekcijska oblika, če virus ostane v telesu predolgo, je še težje pravilno diagnosticirati. Za pojasnitev diagnoze je zaželeno, da se opravi več histoloških testov. Testiranje krvi pomaga pri diagnozi.

Si profesionalni prevajalec iz angleščine v slovenščino. Tvoja naloga je ustvariti visoko kakovostne prevode, ki so naravni, tekoči in natančni. Izogibaj se dobesednim prevodom, ki zvenijo nenaravno. Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

Lupus, type 1 diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, multiple sclerosis… In all of these, the basic mechanism of development is the same: antibodies begin to attack and destroy the body's own cells.
“We divide the immune system in humans into innate and acquired immunity. Innate immunity consists of those parts of the immune system that respond in the same way, regardless of whether we have encountered a particular infection for the first time, the second time, the third time… Its effects are primarily recognized as inflammation, fever, joint pain, and general malaise. The immune system that develops only after the first infection with a particular infectious disease is defined as acquired immunity. The acquired immune response is not particularly important during the first infection, but it is very important in subsequent infections with the same pathogen. It is responsible for the production of antibodies, which in this case prevent the disease in subsequent infections with the same pathogen,” says Prof. Dr. Alojz Ihan, head of the Department of Immunology at the Institute of Microbiology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Ljubljana.
What happens when bacteria and viruses invade our body?
When we become infected, cells and mechanisms of the innate immune system are activated, which we feel as fever, general malaise, joint pain… This is a response without antibodies, which takes about 14 days to develop and manifests as inflammation. Innate immunity is less precise than acquired immunity and causes us quite a few problems. It can happen that it harms our body to the same extent that it harms the microbe. Would antibodies be produced even without the activation of the innate immune system?
No. Without the action of the innate immune system, antibodies are not produced. The primary task of acquired immunity is the production of antibodies. B lymphocytes play a crucial role in this process. They develop in the bone marrow, and during development, they are precisely selected so that all those that could potentially be dangerous to our own cells are eliminated. Only those that do not recognize our molecules enter the bloodstream and have “traps” (receptors) for many other molecules. Of course, errors can occur in this process.
Is inflammation a necessary condition for the development of autoimmune diseases?
A genetic defect creates a condition for an error in the selection of autoimmune lymphocytes, which allows the development of an autoimmune disease. When an incorrect autoimmune lymphocyte enters the bloodstream, it circulates there for a few weeks. If an infection or inflammation occurs in an organ during this time, in which the autoimmune lymphocyte can cause the disease, the autoimmune lymphocyte enters that organ and causes an attack, thus leading to the development of an autoimmune disease.
Does hypothyroidism develop in the same way?
Yes.
The lymphocyte enters the inflamed thyroid gland, begins to multiply, and attacks the cells that produce thyroxine and triiodothyronine (thyroid hormones). Antibodies, on the one hand, stimulate the production of the hormone, which is produced in excess (hyperthyroidism) and is no longer regulated by the brain, and on the other hand, they destroy the thyroid cells. The latter still work, but there are fewer and fewer of them due to the antibodies. The level of the hormone slowly decreases to a normal level, and the person appears to recover, although only a quarter of the cells in the thyroid gland are still functioning. The antibodies continue to destroy them, and we develop hypothyroidism. The process takes years because the access of antibodies to the thyroid gland is poorer due to its location.
What happens in type 1 diabetes?
Type 1 diabetes most often develops in childhood because that is when we are most often infected with viruses that attack the glands. During the infection, we develop antibodies, which is why we are protected from them in adulthood. If a lymphocyte, which mistakenly recognizes a pancreatic cell as foreign, circulates in the blood and the pancreas is inflamed at that time, the lymphocyte that survived the error can meet the pancreatic tissue. After the age of 20, this rarely happens. In the pancreas, immune cells begin to multiply and attack the cells that produce insulin. The consequence is type 1 diabetes, which develops in one month and is an example of complete and very rapid destruction of the body's own cells.
What about type 2 diabetes?
Type 2 diabetes is a completely different type of disease. Inflammation is also important here, but the main problem is that the pancreas, due to age, cannot produce enough insulin to meet the body's needs. In youth, it can easily supply 150 kg of body tissue, but with age, there are fewer and fewer cells that secrete insulin, so that at the age of 60 or 70, its ability is reduced by half. Every cell in our body needs insulin, and the more body mass we have, the more we need.
How many daily attacks by microbes do we actually notice?
Very few, less than one percent. We only notice those that are caused by microbial species that are extremely pathogenic and depend on attacking us for survival.
Are we more resistant if we survive more infections?
There is no such thing as training the immune system in a way that infections strengthen it. However, it is true that the more diverse the microbes that populate our skin and intestines, the less likely we are to develop autoimmune diseases. If there are enough non-disease-causing immune responses – caused by bacteria that are not dangerous to us, but we still react to them – there is less chance that individual incorrect cells will be able to trigger an autoimmune response. The key is not in learning or training the system, but in a larger number of immune cells.
Why are we physically less capable and less resistant under the influence of negative stress?
Stress hormones are inhibitors of the immune system. However, it is not only the immune system. The skin and mucous membranes play an important role in protecting the body from microbes. Cortisol causes the body to focus only on maintaining survival, and all other functions are partially or completely turned off. If we are under stress for a long time and operate with regenerative functions turned off, the mucous membranes are more fragile, so the same amount of microbes penetrates them more quickly and causes disease. In positive stress, when the body is flooded with serotonin, this process does not occur.

Aphids
When it comes to fighting aphids, lavender, marigolds, and nasturtiums are the most effective. Protect fruit trees from aphids by planting nasturtiums underneath them. These greenish insects prefer to settle on them rather than sucking the sap from tree leaves. If aphids are spoiling the beautiful appearance of roses, wash them off the plant with a stream of water in the morning. Lavender, which grows in close proximity to roses, further reduces the number of aphids. Protect beans from insect pests by planting marigolds. When aphids become a major problem, use a spray made from nettles, which is effective for all plants and all types of aphids. If one spraying is not enough, repeat the process after a few days.

Slugs
Slugs are a major nuisance in gardens, as there are not enough natural predators, such as hedgehogs, shrews, lizards, and frogs. The latter can be attracted if you have a large enough garden. An Indian runner duck also finds a garden full of slugs a paradise, as it feeds on them. You can also control slugs yourself by picking them up in the morning and evening and scalding them in a pot. The cooled liquid is very unpleasant for slugs, so spray it on young, vulnerable plants of cucumbers, zucchini, sunflowers, marigolds, dahlias, lettuce, etc. Place the dead animals on the compost. You can also deter slugs by planting or sowing plants with a scent that they dislike in critical areas. These include mustard, garlic, onions, nasturtiums, sage, and thyme. Different types of mustard work well in spring among young vegetables. Larger mustard can simply be cut and left on the ground.

When it comes to fighting aphids, lavender, marigolds, and nasturtiums are the most effective. Protect fruit trees from aphids by planting nasturtiums underneath them. Ants
Although ants are welcome in gardens, as they destroy many plant pests, they often carry aphids onto plants. Ants feed on the sweet secretions of these 'friends'. Where they are a nuisance in the garden, drive them away with lavender, peppermint, or chamomile. Ants also flee from the scent of tomato leaves or tansy. You can make a 'sweet' trap for ants from a clean mushroom, sprinkle sugar on it, and the ants will quickly move in. Then throw the mushroom into boiling water.

Wireworm
Without resorting to chemical agents, you can destroy wireworms by pouring a little cooking oil mixed with water into their burrows, which are just below the surface. It is even better to nip the persistent root and tuber eater in the bud by removing the offshoots. In June, a generation of 200 to 300 larvae hatches in a hole under the ground, which can be found by following the burrow. Drip it with cooking oil, then pour water into the nest. Wireworms that crawl on the ground at night can be caught in empty flower pots that are buried to the brim in the ground in suspicious places.

Vole, Mouse
Voles and mice will not easily give up on the roots of fruit trees, vegetables, and ornamental plants, so action must be taken. Dig crushed glass around fruit trees to protect the roots from gnawing. Bottles buried to the neck, which make a whistling sound in the wind, drive away unwanted guests from the garden, as the noise of the whistling bottles disturbs them. Planting garlic and euphorbia is recommended to protect vegetables from small rodents, as they avoid them due to the unpleasant smell, especially mice. They also shy away from the scent of cypress and walnut, so it is advisable to insert cypress twigs or walnut leaves into mouse holes.

Colorado Potato Beetle
The Colorado potato beetle is a persistent pest on potatoes, as it is often unsuccessfully controlled due to its resistance to most common insecticides. A natural approach to defending against the orange-yellow beetle is to pick its larvae from potato leaves, or to protect potato beds by planting some horseradish roots at the ends. The cabbage white butterfly is a very charming white butterfly with black spots, while its caterpillars are not exactly welcome in our gardens, as they eat the leaves of cabbage plants (radish, turnip, kohlrabi, cabbage, kale, arugula, etc.). The flea beetle is a beetle that bites the leaves of red radish, white radish, and cabbage in spring. It is driven away if lettuce and spinach are added to the mentioned cabbage plants. An infestation of flea beetles is prevented by ensuring loose, constantly covered, and moist soil. Repeated spraying with wormwood preparation and sprinkling tobacco dust also help.

Root Fly
Root flies are deterred by planting species of onion, garlic, leek, and sage near the roots. Damaged roots should be removed from the bed immediately. In the following year, plant onion, garlic, or leek in that place.

Polži
Polži na vrtovih predstavljajo veliko nadlogo, saj ni dovolj naravnih uničevalcev, kot so jež, slepec, kuščarji in žabe. Zadnje lahko naselimo, če imamo dovolj velik vrt. Ohlajen poparek je polžem zelo neprijeten, zato z njim poškropimo mlade ogrožene rastline kumar, bučk, sončnic, žametnic, dalij, solat itd. Poginule živali damo na kompost. Koloradski hrošč
Koloradski hrošč je zvest škodljivec na krompirju, saj ga zaradi njegove odpornosti na večino najbolj razširjenih insekticidov pogosto neuspešno zatiramo. Naravni pristop k obrambi pred oranžno rumenim hroščem je ta, da pobiramo njegove ličinke s krompirjevih listov, lahko pa krompirjeve grede zaščitimo tako, da ob koncih zasadimo nekaj korenin hrena. Hrenov vonj hrošče odvrača, krompir pa dobi v soseščini hrena boljši okus.
Kapusov belin
Kapusov belin je nadvse očarljiv belokrilni metulj s črnimi lisami, medtem ko njegove gosenice niso ravno zaželene na naših vrtovih, saj objedajo liste kapusnic (redkev, repa, koleraba, zelje, ohrovt, rukola itd.). Odlaganje številnih jajčec kapusovega belina na zeljnate rastline lahko preprečimo z razpeto gosto mrežo ali s polaganjem praprotnih listov na rastline. Pri odvračanju belina so se obnesle tudi mešane kulture s paradižnikom, zeleno, žajbljem, koprom, timijanom, rožmariom in poprovo meto. Rastline zaščitimo tudi s škropivom iz pelina. Pobiranje jajčec in gosenic je nadvse slastna naloga sinic, ki jih poskušamo zadržati v bližini zelenjavnih gred z zimskim krmljenjem.
Bolhač
Bolhač je hrošč, ki spomladi ogrize liste rdeče redkvice, bele redkve in zelja. Preženemo ga, če se omenjenim kapusnicam pridružita solata in špinača. Naval bolhačev preprečimo s tem, da skrbimo za rahlo, stalno pokrito in vlažno zemljo. Tudi večkratno škropljenje s pelinovim pripravkom in potresanje tobakovega prahu pomagata.
Korenjeva muha
Korenjevo muho odvračajo ob korenju zasajene vrste čebule, česna, pora in žajbelj. Poškodovano korenje takoj odstranimo z grede. V prihodnjem letu zasadimo na to mesto čebulo, česen ali por.

To answer the questions posed, we need to delve into the magical world of microorganisms, which includes the group of bacteria known as lactic acid bacteria. Humans observed their effects thousands of years ago when they noticed that milk, when left out, would spoil. Instead of consuming all of it, they would save some for later. The process of souring, which we now call fermentation, was carried out by those lactic acid bacteria that dominated a particular geographical and climatic area. Thus, in areas with warm climates, yogurt was created, while in colder areas, sour milk was produced.
Fermented milk was recognized very early on as having beneficial health effects, particularly in treating diarrhea, but its connection to lactic acid bacteria was established much later, with the invention of the microscope and a better understanding of the role of the intestinal microflora. The digestive tract of an adult human is inhabited by approximately one hundred trillion bacteria, which make up 1 to 2 kilograms of human weight. Most of these are 'good' bacteria (including lactic acid bacteria), which protect us from harmful invaders, stimulate our immune system, and help us break down food. A healthy microflora can be disrupted by infections, medication, chemotherapy, radiation, and post-operative conditions that interfere with normal eating, as well as stressful situations related to irregular eating habits.
The most common probiotic bacteria are primarily representatives of lactobacilli and bifidobacteria, as they are natural members of the healthy microflora of the digestive tract, and they are also considered safe bacteria, as humans have been consuming them for thousands of years along with fermented foods. However, this does not mean that all lactobacilli and bifidobacteria are probiotics. Probiotic bacteria must have specific abilities to compete with harmful bacteria in the digestive tract, break down food components, stimulate digestive function, and help boost the immune system. In fermented dairy products, they are often added in addition to those that simultaneously create a delicious product, resulting in a probiotic yogurt – in addition to the traditional yogurt culture (Streptococcus thermophilus and Lactobacillus bulgaricus), it also contains a probiotic bacterium (e.g., a selected strain of Lactobacillus acidophilus). It is a misconception that a single probiotic bacterium has all of the above-mentioned beneficial effects. Some are more successful in fighting harmful bacteria, others in stimulating digestive function, and still others in boosting the immune system.
Finally, let's return to 'ordinary' yogurt. It also has numerous beneficial effects on the digestive tract due to the substances produced during fermentation. When they reach our digestive tract, they prevent the growth of harmful bacteria and accelerate and/or regulate digestion. Consuming fermented milk increases the secretion of saliva, bile, and gastric juice, and also improves calcium absorption. Therefore, experts recommend it as a daily meal or addition to another meal.
My Health No. 31 / February 6, 2007

Za odgovore na zastavljena vprašanja moramo pokukati v čarobni mikrobni svet, kateremu pripada tudi skupina bakterij, ki jim pravimo mlečno-kislinske bakterije. Njihovo delovanje je človek opazil že pred tisočletji, ko pomolženega mleka ni zaužil v celoti, temveč si ga je nekaj pustil za kasneje. Mleko se je skisalo. Proces kisanja, ki ga sodobno imenujemo fermentacija, so izpeljale tiste mlečno-kislinske bakterije, ki so prevladovale na določenem geografskem in klimatskem področju. Tako je v področjih s toplo klimo nastal jogurt, v hladnejših področjih pa kislo mleko.
Fermentiranemu mleku so že zelo zgodaj pripisovali ugodne zdravstvene učinke, predvsem pri zdravljenju driske, vendar so jih začeli povezovati z mlečno-kislinskimi bakterijami precej kasneje, z odkritjem mikroskopa in vse boljšim poznavanjem vloge črevesne mikroflore. Prebavni trakt odraslega človeka poseljuje okoli sto tisoč milijard bakterij, ki predstavljajo od 1 do 2 kilograma človeške teže. Večino predstavljajo 'dobre' bakterije (mednje sodijo tudi mlečno-kislinske bakterije), ki nas ščitijo pred škodljivimi vsiljivci, vzpodbujajo naš imunski sistem ter nam pomagajo pri razgradnji hrane. Zdravo mikrofloro lahko porušijo okužbe, zdravljenje z zdravili, kemoterapije, obsevanja in po-operativna stanja, pri katerih je moteno normalno prehranjevanje, pa tudi stresne situacije, povezane z nerednim prehranjevanjem.
Najpogostejše probiotične bakterije so predvsem predstavniki laktobacilov in bifidobakterij, saj so naravni člani zdrave mikroflore prebavil, poleg tega pa veljajo za varne bakterije, saj jih človek že tisočletja uživa skupaj s fermentirano hrano. To pa ne pomeni, da so vsi laktobacili in bifidobakterije, probiotiki. Probiotične bakterije morajo imeti posebne sposobnosti, da lahko v prebavnem traktu tekmujejo z zdravju škodljivimi bakterijami, razgrajujejo sestavine hrane, vzpodbujajo delovanje prebavil, pomagajo pri dvigovanju imunske odpornosti. V fermentirane mlečne izdelke jih največkrat dodajamo poleg tistih, ki nam istočasno naredijo okusen izdelek in tako dobimo probiotični jogurt – poleg tradicionalne jogurtove kulture (Streptococcus thermophilus in Lactobacillus bulgaricus) vsebuje še probiotično bakterijo (npr. izbran sev Lactobacillus acidophilus). Zmotno je mišljenje, da ima ena probiotična bakterija vse zgoraj naštete ugodne učinke. Ene so uspešnejše pri borbi proti škodljivim bakterijam, druge pri vzpodbujanju delovanja prebavil, tretje zopet pri vzpodbujanju imunskega sistema.
Za konec pa se vrnimo k 'navadnemu' jogurtu. Tudi ta ima številne blagodejne učinke na prebavni trakt zaradi snovi, ki nastajajo med fermentacijo. Ko prispejo v naš prebavni trakt preprečujejo rast zdravju škodljivih bakterij, pospešujejo in/ali urejajo prebavo. Pri uživanju fermentiranega mleka se poveča izločanje sline, žolča in želodčnega soka, izboljša pa se tudi izkoriščanje kalcija. Zato ga strokovnjaki priporočajo kot vsakodnevni samostojni obrok ali dodatek drugemu obroku.

Hot and indigestible carbon dioxide
Last July, the concentration of CO2 in the atmosphere was 408 ppm. In the last 400 million years, a CO2 concentration of 300 ppm was considered high. Therefore, the high CO2 concentration we are experiencing now has never been reached in the last half a billion years. This increase will certainly affect plant growth in the coming decades.
In fact, plants are happy when there is more CO2 available in the atmosphere, as more CO2 means more food. CO2 is a basic component of plants and is actually the basis for all biological molecules. Through photosynthesis, plants can capture carbon from CO2 and put it into carbon chains, also known as carbohydrates or sugars.
The increase in CO2 is expected to increase the rate of photosynthesis and thus improve the growth of the world's vegetation. This greening of the Earth could mitigate climate change if the carbon were removed from the atmosphere and stored in trees. Various models have predicted that the Earth will become greener in colder areas, especially in high-altitude regions. However, even though CO2 is more readily available to plants, a lack of water and a lack of nutrients in the soil can limit plant growth.
Climate change has other components that may harm plant growth in the future. Global warming, which comes with rising CO2 levels, will reduce plant growth.
The enzyme that allows plants to take carbon from CO2 into carbon chains is called Rubisco. This enzyme becomes less efficient at high temperatures because it fixes oxygen instead of carbon. Then the plant begins to photorespirate, which is completely useless for carbon fixation. This is a kind of enzyme waste, which loses energy and reduces sugar synthesis. Global warming and photorespiration can seriously reduce the ability of plants to store carbon and mitigate climate change.
It is still unknown which factor will have the most important effect on the greening of the Earth: will plants grow faster and fix more carbon, or will global warming slow down their growth?
Another consequence of rising CO2 is a change in the food we grow. In an atmosphere enriched with CO2, a plant has easier access to carbon than nitrogen, so it stores more carbon as starch and sugars. This will make food more energy-rich but poorer in micronutrients.
In an article published in the journal Nature in 2014, Samuel Myers and his team warned of a reduction in micronutrients in common crops grown in an atmosphere enriched with CO2. They reported that wheat, rice, soybeans, and peas grown under such conditions had lower levels of iron and zinc. These two minerals are already often lacking in our diet, and further reduction could seriously endanger the health of millions of people, especially in poor neighborhoods. Iron deficiency creates anemia, while zinc deficiency weakens the immune system. Today, many other studies have been published warning of a reduction in vitamins and minerals in crops grown in an atmosphere enriched with CO2.
The best-case scenario for humanity would be to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and hope for a climate change mechanism that we have prepared to slow down. People should stop consuming useless goods and wasting food or energy. Companies should acquire natural resources and the profitability of goods. I don't think we will succeed in time. Too many people want a car and the latest smartphone or laptop. Too many companies are focused on maximizing profits without paying much attention to their environmental and social impact. Some organizations doubt the current consumer system, and movements such as freeganism and degrowth seem promising, but they still gather a minority of people.
Billions of Chinese and Indians want to enjoy a market economy, buy a variety of goods, and escape poverty. Millions of people in developed countries have a large environmental footprint and are not willing to give up their comfort to reduce it.
I predict that companies will continue as usual, and the level of CO2 in the atmosphere will continue to increase, increasing the catastrophic effects of climate change. People in poor, remote areas will likely suffer from rising sea levels and extreme weather events. I also predict that the rich will be able to avoid the consequences of climate change. They will buy nutrient-rich food, get an air-conditioned house on top of a hill, and enjoy life while watching the news on TV. Isn't that a bright future? I think so, if you can afford it.

Vroči in neprebavljivi ogljikov dioksid
Lani julija je bila koncentracija CO2 v ozračju 408 ppm. V zadnjih 400 milijonih let je bila koncentracija CO2 300 ppm ocenjena kot visoka. Zato visoka koncentracija CO2, ki jo doživljamo zdaj, ni bila nikoli dosežena v zadnjih pol milijarde let. To povečanje bo zagotovo vplivalo na rast rastlin v naslednjih desetletjih.
Rastline so pravzaprav srečne, če imajo v ozračju na voljo več CO2, več CO2 pomeni več hrane. CO2 je osnovna sestavina rastlin in je pravzaprav osnova za vse biološke molekule. S fotosintezo lahko rastline ujamejo ogljik iz CO2 in ga dajo v ogljikove verige, imenovane tudi ogljikovi hidrati ali sladkor.
Povišanje CO2 naj bi povečalo stopnjo fotosinteze in s tem izboljšalo rast svetovne vegetacije. To ozelenjevanje Zemlje bi lahko omililo podnebne spremembe, če bi ogljik odneslo iz ozračja in ga shranilo v drevesa. Različni modeli so napovedovali, da bo Zemlja postala bolj zelena v hladnih območjih, zlasti v visokogorskih regijah. Kljub temu, da je CO2 rastlinam pogostejši, lahko pomanjkanje vode in pomanjkanje hranil v tleh omejijo rast rastlin.
Podnebne spremembe imajo druge sestavine, ki lahko v prihodnosti škodijo rasti rastlin. Globalno segrevanje, ki prihaja z naraščajočo raven CO2, bo zmanjšalo rast rastlin.
Encim, ki rastlinam omogoča vnos ogljika iz CO2 v ogljikove verige, se imenuje RubisCO. Ta encim postane manj učinkovit pri visoki temperaturi, ker fiksira kisik namesto ogljika. Potem rastlina začne fotorespirati, kar je za fiksacijo ogljika popolnoma neuporabno. To je neke vrste odlaganje encimov, ki izgublja energijo in zmanjšuje sintezo sladkorja. Globalno segrevanje in fotorespiracija lahko resno zmanjšata zmogljivost rastlin za shranjevanje ogljika in blažitev podnebnih sprememb.
Še vedno ni znano, kateri dejavnik bo imel najpomembnejši postopek pri ozelenjevanju zemlje: bodo rastline hitreje rasle in določile več ogljika ali bodo zaradi globalnega segrevanja upočasnile rast?
Druga posledica dviga CO2 je sprememba hrane, ki jo gojimo. V atmosferi, obogateni s CO2, ima rastlina lažji dostop do ogljika kot dušik, zato skladišči več ogljika kot škroba in sladkorjev. Zaradi tega bo hrana bogatejša z energijo, vendar slabša z mikrohranili.

Pomanjkanje železa ustvarja slabokrvnost, medtem ko pomanjkanje cinka poslabša imunski sistem. Danes so bile objavljene številne druge študije, ki opozarjajo na zmanjšanje vitaminov in mineralov poljščin, gojenih v atmosferi, obogateni s CO2.
Najboljši scenarij za človeštvo bi bilo zmanjšanje emisij toplogrednih plinov in moljenje za mehanizem podnebnih sprememb, ki smo ga pripravili, da se upočasni. Ljudje bi morali prenehati porabljati neuporabno blago in zapravljati hrano ali energijo. Podjetje bi moralo pridobivati naravne vire in donosnost blaga. Ne verjamem, da nam bo to uspelo pravočasno. In many ways, we live in a society that runs on batteries. From our cell phones, laptops, and other electronic devices to children’s toys and cars, modern life is powered by batteries. But they are not just used in consumer goods. When storms knock out the power grid, batteries continue to power hospital equipment and run trains. If you have a landline phone, you can still make and receive calls because the phone lines are powered by batteries. But batteries can seriously harm the environment and human health if they are not disposed of properly.

How Batteries Work
Before the invention of the battery, it was necessary to have a direct connection to a power source to generate electricity. This is because electricity cannot be stored. Batteries work by converting chemical energy into electrical energy. The two ends of a battery – the anode and the cathode – use chemicals to create an electrical circuit called an electrolyte, which sends electrical energy to a device, such as a cell phone, when the device is connected to the battery.
Batteries and the Environment
The exact combination and number of chemicals in a battery vary depending on the type of battery, but cadmium, lead, mercury, nickel, lithium, and electrolytes are all on the list. When batteries are thrown away with household trash, they end up in landfills. As the battery casing corrodes, the chemicals leach into the soil and make their way into our water supply. Eventually, they make their way to the ocean. Lithium in batteries also reacts violently when exposed. According to Battery University, lithium can cause fires in landfills that can burn for years underground. This releases toxic chemicals into the air, increasing the potential for human exposure.
Batteries and Human Health
According to the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry, cadmium and nickel are known human carcinogens. Lead is linked to birth defects, as well as neurological and developmental damage. Mercury is also highly toxic, especially in vapor form, which is why the government banned its use in batteries in 1996. Trace amounts of mercury can still be found in other materials used to make batteries, but they do not pose a health risk to humans.
How to Recycle Batteries
Rechargeable batteries contain hazardous heavy metals and should always be recycled. New cell phones are often packaged with a mail-in recycling program so that consumers can return old phones for recycling. National recycling programs, such as Call2Recycle (listed in the Resources section), accept spent rechargeable batteries as a public service. Lead-acid batteries, which are used in cars, can be recycled at local or state hazardous waste programs. Most auto parts stores will accept old car batteries and send them to the appropriate recycling facility. Single-use alkaline batteries used to contain large amounts of mercury, but since a federal law in 1996 banned mercury in batteries, they are now considered safe to throw away. It is still a good idea to recycle alkaline batteries, but since they are not considered hazardous waste, it can be difficult to find recycling programs that accept them. Some local municipalities may accept them for recycling. Another option is to recycle them in bulk. A company called Big Green Box (listed in the Resources section) offers this service.

V mnogih pogledih živimo v družbi, ki deluje na baterije. Od naših mobilnih telefonov, prenosnikov in drugih elektronskih naprav do otroških igrač in avtomobilov moderno življenje teče na baterije. Vendar se ne uporabljajo samo v potrošniškem blagu. Ko nevihte izbijejo električno omrežje, akumulatorji še naprej delujejo v bolnišnični opremi in vozijo vlaki. Če imate stacionarni telefon, lahko še vedno kličete in sprejemate klice, ker telefonske linije napajajo baterije. Toda baterije lahko resno škodujejo okolju in zdravju ljudi, če jih ne odstranite pravilno.
Kako delujejo baterije
Pred izumom baterije je bila za proizvodnjo električne energije potrebna neposredna povezava z virom električne energije. To je zato, ker električne energije ni mogoče shraniti. Baterije delujejo tako, da pretvarjajo kemično energijo v električno. Nasprotna konca baterije - anoda in katoda - s pomočjo kemikalij ustvarita električni tokokrog imenovani elektroliti, ki pošljejo električno energijo v napravo, kot je mobilni telefon, ko je naprava priključena na baterijo.
Baterije in okolje
Natančna kombinacija in število kemikalij v bateriji se razlikujeta glede na vrsto baterije, vendar je na seznamu kadmij, svinec, živo srebro, nikelj, litij in elektroliti. Ko jih baterije odvržejo med gospodinjske smeti, se znajdejo na odlagališčih. Ko ohišje akumulatorja korodira, se kemikalije izpirajo v tla in se pretakajo v naš vodovod. Sčasoma pridejo do oceana. Tudi litij v baterijah reagira hlapno, kadar je izpostavljen. Po navedbah univerze Battery lahko litij povzroči požar na odlagališčih, ki lahko leta gorijo pod zemljo. To sprošča strupene kemikalije v zrak, kar povečuje možnost izpostavljenosti ljudi.
Baterije in zdravje ljudi
Po podatkih Agencije za register toksičnih snovi in bolezni sta kadmij in nikelj znana človeška rakotvorna snov. Svinec je povezan z prirojenimi napakami ter z nevrološkimi in razvojnimi poškodbami. Živo srebro je tudi zelo strupeno, zlasti v obliki hlapov, zato je vlada leta 1996 prepovedala njegovo uporabo v baterijah. Še vedno se lahko pojavijo zanemarljive količine živega srebra, ki jih lahko sledimo drugim materialom, uporabljenim pri izdelavi baterij, vendar ne predstavljajo nevarnosti za zdravje ljudi.
Kako reciklirati baterije
Polnilne baterije vsebujejo nevarne težke kovine in jih je treba vedno reciklirati. Novi mobilni telefoni so običajno pakirani s prodajalci, tako da lahko potrošniki vrnejo stare telefone v recikliranje. Nacionalni programi za recikliranje, kot je Call2Recycle (navedeni v razdelku Viri), sprejemajo izrabljene polnilne baterije kot javno storitev. Svinčeve akumulatorje, ki se uporabljajo v avtomobilih, je mogoče reciklirati v lokalnih ali državnih programih za nevarne odpadke. Večina trgovin z avtomobilsko opremo bo sprejela stare avtomobilske akumulatorje in jih poslala ustreznim organom za recikliranje. Water is the source of life. A lack of water in plants is quickly noticeable, as their leaves wilt, because water in the leaves maintains the pressure that gives them their shape.
Water is essential for the functioning of enzymes and proteins, and it is also a basic component in photosynthesis, as plants combine it with carbon dioxide from the air to create sugars, which are the most important source of energy for plant growth and development.
Drought stress
If a plant is not watered enough, it can experience drought stress. This is often present even before obvious signs appear, such as wilting leaves; at that point, the plant has already been functioning abnormally for a few days.
We need to observe plants and determine how they respond to watering, when it is best to water them, and how much. We should always follow the rule of ‘less is more,’ especially in winter, when plants are mostly dormant and need significantly less water than during the growing season.
Too much water
If there is too much water in the soil, there is less space for oxygen, which is also extremely important in the soil, as the underground parts of the plant need it to survive. When there is a lack of oxygen in the soil, the roots begin to die, and excess moisture can cause rot and destroy the plant in a relatively short time.
How much we water is definitely an important factor, but the type of water we use is also important. Water is an ideal solvent, and minerals and organic substances dissolve in it; some of these are beneficial, while others can be harmful to plants. It is important to ensure the quality of the water.
Hard water
Tap water is the most common source of water for watering, but it is not the most suitable. This water is of verified quality and is suitable for humans, but not for plants. It has high concentrations of certain minerals, mainly calcium and magnesium carbonates, which are the minerals that form calcareous deposits (limescale).
Calcium and magnesium are essential for plants, but they are usually present in sufficient quantities in substrates and fertilizers for plants, so watering with hard water can lead to an excess of these substances in the soil. The accumulation of certain substances can displace others, preventing the plant from absorbing other nutrients; in the case of an excess of calcium and magnesium, potassium and sodium are displaced, which are also extremely important nutrients.
Plants cannot thrive without all the essential minerals, and this condition can also be caused by incorrect fertilizer dosage, so it is always necessary to follow the instructions.
Soft water
Therefore, it is best to use soft water for watering. Soft water contains fewer minerals that could disrupt the nutrient balance.
Distilled water is theoretically the most suitable, as it contains no minerals or organic substances, but soft water can also be obtained in other ways. Collecting rainwater is one of the methods.
If you do not have the option of collecting rainwater, you can obtain soft water in a very simple way. Fill clean bottles/containers to the top with tap water and place them in a location where you will not move them for at least 24 hours. During this time, the minerals will settle to the bottom due to their weight.
However, we must be careful to use only the top 2/3 of the water for watering, as the minerals have concentrated at the bottom of the container.
Soft water can also be used for spraying houseplants or in humidifiers to increase air humidity, especially in winter.

One kilogram of beef results in 57 kilograms of CO2, which is equivalent to approximately 100 liters of fuel in your car.
Cattle also require more land and resources than almost any other livestock. For every kilogram of beef that reaches the market, 10 to 14 kilograms of feed are used. Because farmers need space to grow feed, cattle farming also contributes to deforestation.
Sheep, like cows, are ruminants and cause the same problems, but they are often overlooked due to their size. In reality, the carbon footprint of lamb is only slightly smaller, at 55 kilograms of CO2 per kilogram of meat.
Shellfish also contribute, with each kilogram of shellfish releasing 24 kilograms of CO2 into the atmosphere. Pork follows, with one kilogram of meat contributing approximately 17 kilograms of CO2.
For dedicated meat-eaters, the most environmentally friendly option is to replace beef and lamb with chicken. The only meat that is more environmentally friendly than chicken is fish, which produces only 11 kilograms of CO2 per kilogram of meat.
Fish have one of the lowest CO2 emissions per kilogram of all types of meat, at 7.5 kilograms. However, it is best to avoid tuna and salmon. Tuna is overfished, leading to a decline in the population of this species, and most salmon are farmed, which has its own environmental consequences.
Therefore, if you want to contribute to reducing the impact of your diet on the planet, the best option is to replace steak with chicken breast or wild-caught fish. Even better (for the planet) is to try replacing meat dishes with beans or legumes, which, like meat, are high in protein.

Fruits and Vegetables
Although it does not have as great an impact as livestock farming, agriculture and the cultivation of fruits and vegetables generally have an impact on the environment, but the following crops are more harmful than others.
Avocados may not produce much CO2, but they have a high water requirement. If they are grown in their native, tropical climate, the water they need is not such a big problem. However, in California, which is prone to drought (where most of the avocados consumed by Americans come from), water resources are much more limited.
Bananas have an environmental impact due to transportation, and they also spoil during transport. Bananas are said to account for the largest amount of food waste for food retailers and the largest environmental costs due to this waste.
Vegetables have the least impact on the environment. If you already eat a plant-based diet, you are doing the planet a great service. In addition, you can also help by buying seasonal fruits and vegetables and local produce.

Carbohydrates and Other Foods
Carbohydrates are surprisingly environmentally friendly. Most grains produce only 1.1 kilograms of CO2 per kilogram of food, which is much less than meat, dairy products, and even vegetables grown in greenhouses. However, this does not mean that all carbohydrates are the same, as some are more harmful to the environment.
Rice stands out among carbohydrates as being more harmful to the environment than others. Rice cultivation accounts for a third of the world's annual freshwater consumption. Fortunately, new methods of rice cultivation are significantly reducing water consumption, leading to much more sustainable agriculture.
In addition to rice, sugar production also has an environmental impact. Not only does sugar production require a large amount of water, but it also uses a lot of fertilizers and chemicals, which are often washed into freshwater rivers and streams.

The dairy industry poses many of the same environmental problems as beef, as it comes from the same source. However, because milk can be obtained from the same cow multiple times, the carbon footprint is much smaller. Milk contributes only about 2.6 kilograms of CO2 per kilogram of food, while a processed product, such as butter, produces up to 26.5 kilograms of CO2 per kilogram of product.

We have entered March, the third month in the Gregorian calendar, which gets its name from the Roman god Mars, while its original Slovenian name is "sušec." This month is when we remember folk customs associated with St. Gregory's Day, and we also commemorate St. George's Day. Several holidays are celebrated during this time. Today, we will focus on three of them.

Why is March 8th International Women's Day?
Since March 8th is the first of these three holidays in the calendar, we will start with it. March 8th is International Women's Day. Its origins date back to 1857 when female textile workers in New York decided to protest against low wages and poor working conditions. The attempt was unsuccessful, as the workers were arrested by the police, but because women are persistent, the next step was taken two years later when women established the first labor union.
On March 8, 1908, 15,000 women gathered in the streets of New York. They demanded higher wages and better working conditions, and their slogan was "Bread and Roses." At that time, bread symbolized economic security, and roses represented a good quality of life.
The original name of the holiday, as we know it today, is "Working Women's Day," and on this day, we celebrate the economic, political, and social equality and achievements of women.
How was women's equality celebrated in Slovenia?
The first women's newspaper, called "Slovenka," began publication in 1897, and the first women's association was established in 1898. The Slovenian People's Party was the first political advocate for women.
What did people give women in the past, and what do we give them today?
International Women's Day is associated with flowers, as men expressed their affection for women on March 8th by giving them a bouquet of flowers or a single flower, a tradition that has continued to this day. The Slovenian floral stereotype is the carnation, a symbol of friendship and respect. We can say that carnations were very popular in the past, as people would rush to flower shops and stop only in front of the buckets filled with carnations. Children would pick snowdrops and give them to their teachers, mothers, and grandmothers. This is a classic way of showing appreciation to women.
Today, we most often give a bouquet of flowers or a single flower, but the only difference is that the choice of flower types is no longer so strictly limited – today, in addition to carnations, we also give roses, orchids, seasonal flowers, and even a box of chocolates. When choosing flowers, we don't focus so much on their meaning but choose the flowers that we like or that we believe the person we are giving them to will like.
Today, in addition to flowers, we also give jewelry, scented candles, teas, and other small gifts that almost every woman would appreciate.
Perhaps the key difference between the past and today is that in the past, flowers were also picked from home gardens and meadows, while today, we prefer to go to a flower shop.

Mother's Day – the origins of the holiday date back to the USA
On March 25th, on the Christian holiday of the Annunciation, we celebrate Mother's Day. The holiday originated in the early 20th century and began in America, from where Mother's Day spread around the world. The difference between March 8th and March 25th is that International Women's Day is celebrated on the same day in all countries, while Mother's Day has been adapted to the calendar of different cultures. The initiator of Mother's Day was Anna Marie Jarvis, who organized a meeting in memory of her mother on May 12, 1907, on the Sunday after the second anniversary of her mother's death. She expressed her love for her mother by distributing 500 white carnations in front of the church.
When did we start celebrating Mother's Day in Slovenia?
In Slovenia, Mother's Day appeared after World War I, and we celebrated it on March 15th, but then we moved it to March 25th. More significant changes occurred after World War II, when Mother's Day was not celebrated for some time due to the celebration of International Women's Day, but then we revived it.
What did people give their mothers in the past, and what do we give them today?
Mother's Day is characterized by the fact that everyone, regardless of age, thanks their mother for her care and sacrifices. In the past, children would give their mothers picked flowers, especially snowdrops, but today, there are no limits. We choose gifts that express our gratitude and love. Most often, we choose flowers, either a bouquet or a potted plant. Jewelry, cosmetics, chocolate, vases, paintings, scented candles, dinners, and vouchers for wellness and shops are common gifts that mothers appreciate on Mother's Day today.
If we are creative, we can make a small gift ourselves. Regardless of what we give for Mother's Day, let's not forget – the best gift for every mother is a warm hug and a sincere thank you.
Every mother is a true mother,
made for happiness and joy.
True. And one of a kind.
For a lifetime.
(Tone Pavček)

Men also have their holiday – the day of the martyrs
Since we celebrate women in March with two holidays, men have also secured one for themselves. March 10th is recorded in the Christian church as the day of the martyrs. The story dates back to the years 308 to 324, when Emperor Licinius clashed with Constantine the Great. Due to their disagreement, Licinius perceived Christians as enemies who needed to be converted or killed. Forty soldiers opposed his belief and were willing to die for their faith. But the cruel emperor did not spare them. The naked soldiers were thrown into a freezing cold pond in Armenia during the harsh winter. But that was not all. He offered them one last chance to convert. Next to the icy pond, a warm bath awaited those who wanted to convert. One of the soldiers changed his mind and ran from the icy pond into the warm bath, but due to the rapid change in temperature, he suffered a stroke and died. So, 39 soldiers died in the pond. Because one of the guards was moved by the courage of the soldiers, he also went into the pond. This is where the name of the holiday comes from – the 40 martyrs.
All of this is said to have happened on March 9th, but because the bodies of the dead were burned the next day, the day of the martyrs became March 10th.
What do we give men on the day of the martyrs?
Traditionally, men are given a symbolic gift. This includes dried plums, thorns, and sausage, which are actually far from being a gift. This gift is meant to remind men that martyrdom has not ended. However, Slovenians tend to perceive the day of the martyrs as Father's Day, as it is a holiday for all men. In reality, this holiday has no connection to fatherhood, but Father's Day, an informal holiday, does, and it is celebrated on the third Sunday in June. Father's Day also originated in America but is slowly becoming established in other countries. There is no rule about what to give a father on this day. Children can soften their father's heart with a drawing or a bouquet picked from a nearby meadow, but we can also choose classic gifts for men – a razor, perfume, a Swiss Army knife, a watch, and many choose funny or amusing gifts. Whatever you give your father, don't give him dried plums, thorns, and sausage on Father's Day.

Sara Savec

Kaj podarimo moškim na dan mučenikov?

Vendar pa Slovenci radi dojemamo dan mučenikov kot dan očetov, saj gre za praznik vseh moških. Otroci lahko očetovo srce omehčajo s kakšno risbico ali s šopkom, nabranim na sosednjem travniku, sicer pa se lahko odločimo tudi za klasična darila za moške – brivnik, parfum, švicarski nož, ura, mnogi pa se odločajo tudi za smešna oziroma zabavna darila. Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

All humans have an innate desire for sweetness, especially younger people, adolescents, and children who are still growing. Sweet things are usually calorie-rich (which promotes growth and provides energy) and are not poisonous.
As children, we certainly loved sugar, but our desire for sweetness is not always beneficial. Compared to our ancestors, we live in a world where sugar is abundant and its use is excessive, while we consume much less energy, and this is where we actually run into problems. Problems that are called too much sugar!
The concept of sugar encompasses several types of molecular configurations:
- Monosaccharides, also known as simple sugars, include fructose, glucose, and galactose. They are found in nature in fruits and are the fastest to digest, providing the human body with the most energy in a short period.
- Disaccharides are complex sugars formed when two monosaccharides combine. Disaccharides include lactose (milk sugar), maltose, and sucrose (table sugar).
Sometimes, the term sugar is also used to describe ingredients such as granulated sugar, honey, or maple syrup, high-fructose corn syrup, or any other sweetener with a high sugar content.
Sugar is present to some extent in most foods. It is naturally present in root vegetables, fruits, and whole grains. In foods such as sweetened carbonated drinks, candies, baked goods, processed cereals, or spices, it is added.
In what follows, you will see that there is a big difference between these two types.
Sugar, which is a subtype of carbohydrates, can be digested and easily converted into glucose, which is essential for energy. While macronutrients such as protein can be converted into glucose without carbohydrates, this conversion is somewhat more metabolically demanding than simply consuming carbohydrates, and most people feel best when their diet includes some sources of naturally occurring sugars.
Food with naturally occurring sugars is quite different from food with added sugars.
Avoiding foods with natural sugars would be very challenging and would eventually lead to a significant deficiency in the diet, as these foods also contain many essential nutrients. However, drastically reducing or even eliminating foods with added sugars, which are usually processed and have low nutritional value, would probably be one of our healthiest dietary decisions (although not the easiest).
While sugar from whole foods is part of a healthy diet, sugars in processed foods and drinks are just empty calories.
SOURCES OF SUGAR
Natural sugar is, as mentioned, practically in all plant-based foods, with the most in fruits (because they are sweet). In addition to fruits, vegetables, legumes, certain types of nuts, and seeds, sugar can also be found in dairy products. In concentrated forms, it is present in foods such as honey, dried fruit, and fruit juices.
Moving one step further in food processing, sugar can be found in partially processed foods such as maple syrup, coconut sugar, agave nectar, and sugar derived from either sugarcane or sugar beets. The forms of sugar in these foods still contain some minerals and nutrients.
When sugar is further processed into white granules, powder, or syrup, all the nutrients are lost in the process. This is usually the type of sugar found in processed, commercialized foods and drinks and can be very harmful to health in excessive amounts (if consumed in more than 5–10 percent of total daily food intake).
Remember: the highest quality sources of sugar are in unprocessed or minimally processed foods.
DEFICIENCIES
When sugar is consumed as a whole food, it also provides a wide range of other nutrients. For example, if sugar is naturally present in blueberries, you also consume vitamin C, fiber, and many other healthy phytonutrients along with the sugar.
In other words, when sugar is part of a whole food, you consume all known (and unknown!) nutrients present in the whole food along with the sugar.
Therefore, sugar itself is not necessary; the nutrients through which we consume it are. If we wanted to give up all foods that contain sugar (which would mean all fruits, vegetables, grains, legumes, etc.), we would also give up essential sources of vitamins, minerals, and fiber.
EXCESS/TOXICITY
In moderate amounts, sugar is a source of energy. If we consume sugar in excess, in a greater amount than the body needs for energy, it will start to cause problems in the body.
When sugar is converted into energy in the body, which is stored and ready to be used during exercise or a quick run to catch the bus, this is acceptable. However, if we chronically consume sugar in excess, it begins to be stored as fat. Excessive sugar consumption puts the body in a phase where it doesn't know what to do with the amount of sugar, the sugar circulates in the blood, and this can lead to health problems such as diabetes, obesity, heart disease, and other health complications.
If we chronically consume sugar in excess, it begins to be stored as fat.
When reducing sugar intake in the body, it is necessary to examine all the sugars in the existing diet. In most cases, the complications arise from the large amount of sugar in processed foods with added sugars, such as sweetened breakfast cereals, sweetened iced coffee drinks, sweetened carbonated drinks, cookies, muffins, energy bars, sweetened yogurts, candies, desserts, etc. In extremely rare cases, health problems are caused by sugars in whole foods.
Therefore, when we decide to reduce sugar intake or even give it up, let's not be afraid of bananas, but of processed foods with added sugars that are on our menu.
