Večina staršev vzgaja na način, ki so ga prenesli iz svoje družine. Mladi starši pogosto želijo vzgajati svoje otroke drugače kot so bili sami vzgajani, a ker nimajo ustreznih informacij in znanja, pogosto ponavljajo iste napake in slišijo sebe, kako otroka kritizirajo na isti strog način, kot so bili kritizirani sami.
Tako kot starši kaznujejo in kritizirajo otroka, tako otrok kaznuje in kritizira sebe, saj ponotranji odnos staršev do sebe. Zato je pomembno, da se starši naučijo ustreznega načina podajanja kritike.
KRITIKA
Kdaj kritiziramo? Takrat, ko je za nas vedenje druge osebe nesprejemljivo in želimo, da oseba to vedenje spremeni.
Običajno kritiko pojmujemo kot nekaj negativnega in slabega. Slovenci jo najpogosteje razumejo kot napad nase, kot katastrofo. Zato si kritike ne želijo in se je tudi izogibajo. Ker verjamejo, da drugi o njih misli slabo in so zato slabi v celoti. V teorijo rečemo, da gre za enačenje osebnosti in vedenja. Oseba verjame, da je nevredna, če je njeno vedenje neustrezno. To je razlog, zakaj ljudje kritiko sprejmejo s takšnim strahom in občutijo toliko neprijetnosti ob tem.
A kritika ni sodba, ampak je mnenje druge osebe o našem vedenju. Ker vsak od nas na svet gleda s svojimi očmi, ima vsak svoje mnenje.
PODAJANJE KRITIKE
Podajanje kritike je običajno neprijetno opravilo, saj ne želimo, da bi se drugi počutili neprijetno. To je tudi razlog, zakaj drugim težko povemo, kaj nas moti. A če želimo, da drug spremeni neko svoje vedenje, ki nam ni všeč, moramo uporabiti kritiko.
Še posebej težko je podati kritiko svojemu otroku, saj ne želimo, da se počuti slabo in mu je neprijetno. A podajanje kritike je način vzgoje, saj tako starš otroku pove, katero njegove vedenje je primerno in katero ni. Gre torej za način učenja, saj otroka učimo, kaj je prav in kaj ne. In prej ko začnemo, laže bo otroku in tudi nam. Saj s pravilnim podajanjem kritike starši vzgojijo odgovornega, samostojnega in zadovoljnega otroka.
Pri podajanju kritike je pomembno, na kakšen način starši to počnejo in tega se lahko naučijo!
KONSTRUKTIVNA KRITIKA
Pri graditvi zdrave samopodobe, je pomembno, da starši otroku podajajo kritiko na način, ki je spoštljiv in jasen. Da otroku povedo, katero njegovo vedenje ni bilo ustrezno, kaj je naredil narobe (»Nisem zadovoljna s tem, kako si pospravila sobo. Na tleh je ostalo še veliko igrač.« ) ne pa da kritizirajo njegovo osebnost (»Si neroden-a, len-a, površen.a..«).
Neprimerna kritika je torej kritika, ki je podana na osebnost otroka. Ker otrok tako dobi sporočilo: »Nisem v redu, takšen kot sem. Z mano je nekaj narobe!«
Otrok vzame nase takšne kritike in se počuti slabo. Otrok, ki ne verjame, da je dober, tudi ko naredi napako, se izogiba reševanju težav, saj se počuti nesposobnega in nemočnega. Ker ne zaupa v svoje sposobnosti, za težave krivi sebe ali druge.
Nasprotno pa se otrok, ki verjame v svoje sposobnosti, sooča s problemi in išče rešitve, ker se ne boji narediti napake. Ker verjame, da je v redu, tudi če naredi napako, sprejeme, da ne zna vsega, prosi za pomoč in tako kreativno rešuje težave.
Zato je pomembno, da starš otroku posreduje sporočila, da je dober, vreden in pomemben in mu, da dovoljenje, da naredi napako ter informacijo, kako jo popravi ali se iz nje nekaj nauči.Če otrok razbije vazo se starš lahko odzove:
- Kritika na otrokovo osebnost, ki je neustrezna in nesprejemljiva:
»Kako si neroden! S tabo je nekaj narobe! Zakaj si to naredil?«
- Kritika na otrokovo vedenje, to je konstruktivna kritika:
»Jezna sem, da si razbil vazo. Ne dovolim, da po dnevni sobi brcaš žogo.«
Če kritiziramo otrokovo vedenje, ima možnost izbire in lahko popravi ali spremeni svoje vedenje. Če pa kritiziramo otroka kot osebnost, je ta v stiski in se počuti slabo, saj ne more ničesar spremeniti.
Napotki za podajanje konstruktivne kritike:
- Kritiziramo le vedenje in ne osebe in lastnosti, ki jih ne more spremeniti.
(namesto »Kakšna lenoba si« rečemo »Nisi pospravila kopalnice za sabo.«)
- Konkretno povemo, katero vedenje nas moti
(namesto »Nikoli ne pospraviš svoje sobe« rečemo »Danes po obisku prijateljice nisi pospravila sobe za sabo.«)
- Izražajmo se jasno in direktno, ne iščemo ovinkov, saj tako nismo razumljivi
(namesto »Koliko dela imam s pospravljanjem za vsemi vami« rečemo »Prosim te, da sam odneseš v koš svoje umazano perilo.«)
- Stopnjevanje kritike:
1. Kritiko stopnjujemo, če otrok ne upošteva naše kritike in ne spremeni vedenja (»Kot sem ti že rekla, želim, da ugasneš računalnik.«)
2. mu napovemo kazen (»Če ne ugasneš računalnika, boš moral priti v kuhinjo.«)
3. in če otrok kljub temu ne upošteva naše zahteve, izvedemo kazen (»Ugasni računalnik in pridi v kuhinjo!«.)
SENDVIČ TEHNIKA – pohvala osebe + kritika vedenja + pohvala osebe
Predstavljamo si, da je kritika klobasa, ki je položena med dve rezini kruha pohval. Ta način kritiziranja je zelo uporaben za majhne otroke, saj združimo dve pohvali in podamo eno kritiko na otrokovo vedenje.
Na začetku in na koncu izpostavimo pozitivne lastnosti osebe, vmes pa natančno povemo, katero vedenje osebe nas moti – kaj je oseba rekla ali naredila narobe in ne posplošujmo, ter se izogibamo uporabi stereotipov in besed »nikoli, vedno …«.
»Si krasen otrok, vendar me moti, ko vidim, da po jedi ne pospraviš posode za seboj, saj si sicer zelo vestna punca!«
Začnimo pri sebi!
Starši so otroku največji zgled. Otroci vidijo, kakšen odnos imajo starši do sebe, kako sprejemajo kritiko, kakšen odnos imajo do napak, do svojega telesa in tudi kakšen je odnos med partnerjema. V družini si otroci najprej oblikujejo predstavo o tem, kakšni smo odrasli in kakšen je ta svet. Če je to varen prostor, kjer so starši zadovoljni in se medsebojno spoštujejo, je to zelo dobra popotnica za dobro otrokovo samopodobo. Če rešujemo težave in nanje gledamo kot na izzive, tako dajemo otroku jasna sporočila in dober zgled. Če znamo poiskati pomoč, ko se čutimo nemočni, pomeni da si dopuščamo delati napake in smo kreativni pri iskanju rešitev. Če ima starš sam težave s sprejemanjem ali podajanjem kritike, lahko to vidi kot priložnost za osebno rast in učenje ustreznega načina komuniciranja, ki ga bo prenesel tudi na svojega otroka.
Kdaj poiskati pomoč?
Če starš ne zaupa vase, če se počuti krivo, da ni dovolj dober in ne najde načinov, kako otroku postaviti mejo, je vse bolj izčrpan in se začne vrteti v začaranem krogu. Pogosto se mamice znajdejo ujete v takšnem krogu, ko se razdajajo pri skrbi za otroka in družino preko svojih moči, so vse bolj utrujene, tudi partnerski odnos se vse bolj krha, a ne najdejo prave poti. Takrat je skrajni čas, da poiščejo ustrezno pomoč zase.
Kje najti pomoč?
Starševstvo je vloga, ki se je moramo naučiti. Kvalitetne informacije o vzgoji otroka so staršem dobrodošla podpora. Te informacije lahko najdejo starši v priročnikih, na raznih delavnicah, predavanjih ali v obliki individualnih svetovanj in psihoterapije. Na trgu je široka paleta ponudbe pomoči družinam, ki jo nudijo svetovalnice, centri za pomoč ali ustrezni usposobljeni svetovalci ali psihoterapevti. Običajno izhajajo iz različnih teoretskih prepričanj, zato je smiselno raziskati, kaj nam je kot staršu blizu.
Treningi asertivnosti. Za zelo učinkovite pri učenju učinkovite komunikacije in izboljšanja samozavesti so se izkazali tudi treningi asertivnosti, ki temeljijo na tem, da udeležencem dajo konkretne informacije, kako ravnati v posamezni situaciji (kako sprejeti in kako podati kritiko, kako reči ne, kako dati pohvalo, izboljšati samopodobo..).
Pohvala kot protiutež kritiki
Kritika je le ena izmed veščin, ki so bistvene pri vzgoji ne preveč razvajenega in ne preveč poslušnega otroka. Poleg kritike in kazni sta pri vzgoji zelo pomembni veščini še pohvala in nagrada ter starševske zahteve. S kritiko in kaznijo otroku povemo, katerega njegovega vedenja en odobravamo in je neustrezno. S pohvalo in nagrado, pa otroku povemo, katero njegovo vedenje je ustrezno.
Za konec pa še …
Kritiziram vedenje, ne osebe in lastnosti, ki jih ne more spremeniti.
Povejmo otroku, da je krasen in da ga imamo radi!

Rejuvenating pruning of old hedges
Hedges age over the years and become unsightly, and often no longer perform their basic function. This is most noticeable in deciduous hedges made of hornbeam, beech, or maple. After 20 to 30 years, we need to prune them thoroughly.
Each pruning represents stressful conditions for the plant. In some cases, excessive pruning can cause the plant to die. Therefore, we should prune gradually over a period of two years. In the first year, we perform a thorough pruning on the inside of the hedge. We shorten the old branches by 10 to 15 cm. On the outside, we prune normally. The following year, or two years later, depending on the plant's ability to recover, we do the same on the outside. On the inside, we perform normal pruning.
This intensive pruning on one side will accelerate the growth of new shoots, and in two or three years, the hedge will be denser and more beautiful than it was before the rejuvenation.

Heart Murmur

Parents fear the worst when a doctor tells them their child has a "heart murmur." They don't realize that this diagnosis is very common. Many children have heart murmurs as they grow, but in most cases, there is no cause for alarm, as it doesn't affect their health.

Due to the widespread (and incorrect) belief that a "heart murmur" always indicates a serious illness, it's important for parents to understand what type of murmur their child has and whether further diagnostic testing is needed.

How Does the Heart Work?

To better understand, it's helpful to have a basic understanding of how the heart works. The heart consists of four chambers and four valves, which act as one-way doors. The valves open and close with each heartbeat, ensuring that blood flows in the correct direction with each pump. The lower chambers are responsible for pumping blood and are called ventricles (left and right). The upper chambers are reservoirs and are called atria (again, left and right).

The heart's job is to pump blood throughout the body: blood coming from the body contains little oxygen and enters the right atrium. It then flows through the first valve (the tricuspid valve) into the right ventricle, and with each heartbeat, it flows through the second valve (the pulmonary valve) into the pulmonary artery, where it picks up oxygen. Oxygen-rich blood returns to the so-called left side of the heart – first to the left atrium, then through the third valve (the mitral valve) into the left ventricle. From there, the heart pumps it through the fourth valve (the aortic valve) into the aorta, a large vessel that carries blood throughout the body, supplying it with oxygen.

What is a Murmur?

It's a whooshing or whistling sound that a doctor hears when listening to a child's heart with a stethoscope.

How Does a Doctor Detect a "Heart Murmur"?

When listening to a child's heart, the doctor places the stethoscope in different locations on the child's chest. While listening, the doctor listens for the closing of the valves. These are the sounds we call "heartbeat," and we hear them when we place our ear on someone's chest. If we listen carefully, we'll soon realize that these are repeating sound phenomena that can be roughly described as "lub-dub." The doctor calls the first sound the first tone and the second sound the second tone. The first tone occurs when the valves that control blood flow from the atria to the ventricles close. The second tone indicates the closing of the valves that control blood flow from the ventricles to the pulmonary artery and aorta. A murmur is an additional third sound that the doctor hears during the examination. In most cases, this additional sound is simply the sound of blood flowing through a normal, healthy heart. However, sometimes it can be a sign of a heart condition.

How Does a Doctor Describe a Murmur?

The doctor assesses the murmur based on several criteria:

•Its loudness is described on a scale of 1 to 6. 1 means a very quiet, barely audible murmur, while 6 means a very loud murmur.
•It is determined when in the cardiac cycle the murmur occurs.
•The location where the murmur is heard most clearly is identified.
•It is described as high-pitched or low-pitched.
•It is checked whether the murmur changes with changes in the child's position.

My Child Has a Murmur – What Does That Mean?

A doctor will hear a heart murmur in 30-50% of children during a routine check-up. This happens for several reasons. "Innocent" murmurs come and go, depending on the child's heart rate, position during the examination, and any elevated body temperature. Some newly detected murmurs may alert us to a developing heart condition. Finally, in some congenital heart defects, a murmur may not be heard at birth but appears later.

What is an "Innocent" Murmur?

It is the most common type of heart murmur in children. Instead of "innocent," the doctor may also call it a "functional" or "normal" heart murmur. It is caused by increased blood flow through the valves in a completely healthy heart.

Causes of an "Innocent" Murmur:

•Elevated body temperature
When a child has a fever, the body's energy needs are higher. To meet these needs, the heart must pump blood faster throughout the body.
•Anemia
When the concentration of red blood cells is reduced, blood flows faster through the body.
•Thin chest wall and a very flat back
Due to the anatomical position, which brings the heart closer to the chest wall. This makes it easier to hear the blood flow through the heart.
•Still's murmur
It is most often heard in active, healthy children between the ages of three and seven. The murmur represents a normal sound caused by blood being ejected into the aorta with each heartbeat.

Children, compared to adults, have less fat and muscle tissue and thinner bones. This means that during an examination, their heart is closer to the stethoscope membrane, and therefore murmurs are better and easier to hear. As the child grows, the murmur gradually becomes less audible and eventually disappears completely. Children with an "innocent" murmur do not need treatment, a special diet, or activity restrictions. Those old enough to understand that they have a "heart murmur" need reassurance from their parents that they are no different from other children. In simple terms, an "innocent" murmur is the sound of normal blood flowing through a normal, healthy heart in a normal way.

Congenital Heart Defects

Some murmurs are caused by congenital heart defects. Such a murmur is non-functional or organic.

They are caused by:

•A narrowed valve (valve stenosis)
When blood flows through the heart, it encounters a valve that is narrower than it should be. The blood flow becomes turbulent and faster due to the narrower opening, causing a murmur.
•A leaky valve (valve insufficiency)
When the valves close and the heart contracts, some blood flows in the wrong direction (backwards, from where it came). This again creates a sound phenomenon, a murmur.
•Pathological connections between the heart chambers
Because the pressure in the different chambers of the heart is not the same, blood will flow from the chamber with higher pressure to the chamber with lower pressure, again creating a murmur.

If the doctor suspects a non-functional murmur, they will refer the child to a cardiologist. The cardiologist will carefully examine the child and perform some additional tests, such as a chest X-ray, EKG, and echocardiogram.

Children with congenital heart defects have other problems or symptoms in addition to the murmur. The symptoms of a congenital heart defect are noticeable in some children in the first few days after birth. However, problems may appear later in childhood in a child who was previously completely healthy.

Additional symptoms in a child with a heart defect:

•Newborns and infants: rapid breathing, difficulty feeding (tires quickly), bluish lips, failure to gain weight, excessive sweating.
•Children and adolescents: failure to thrive, fatigue and shortness of breath with moderate physical activity, chest pain, dizziness, and fainting.

If you notice any of these symptoms in your child, contact your child's pediatrician.

•A heart murmur is not a disease; it is an additional sound that the doctor hears when listening to a child's heart.
•Most murmurs are not dangerous – "innocent" murmurs. These are common in healthy children. A child with an "innocent" murmur has a healthy heart.
•Sometimes, a heart murmur is a sign of a disease. In this case, the child also has other problems or symptoms.
•The doctor will carefully listen to the child's heart and, based on what they hear, decide whether the murmur is innocent or not.

Šum na srcu
Starši se bojijo najhujšega, ko jim zdravnik pove, da ima njihov otrok »šum na srcu«. Ne vedo, da je diagnoza zelo pogosta. Veliko otrok ima med odraščanjem srčni šum, vendar pri večini ni razloga za preplah, saj ne vpliva na zdravje.
Zaradi splošno veljavnega (zmotnega) prepričanja, da »šum na srcu« vedno pomeni resno bolezen, je pomembno, da starši vedo in razumejo, kateri tip šuma ima njihov otrok in ali bo potrebna nadaljnja diagnostična obdelava.
Kako deluje srce?
Da bi bolje razumeli, je treba v grobem poznati delovanje srca. Srce sestavljajo štiri votline in štiri zaklopke, ki delujejo kot enosmerna vrata. Zaklopke se ob vsakem srčnem utripu odprejo in zaprejo ter tako zagotavljajo, da kri z vsakim udarcem teče v pravo smer. Spodnji votlini sta odgovorni za črpanje krvi, imenujemo ju ventrikla ali prekata (levi in desni). Zgornji votlini sta zbiralnika in ju imenujemo atrija ali preddvora (ponovno levi in desni).
Naloga srca je potiskanje krvi po telesu, in sicer: kri, ki prihaja iz telesa, vsebuje malo kisika in gre v desno zbiralno votlino (desni preddvor). Nato teče skozi prvo zaklopko (trikuspidalna zaklopka) v desno črpalno votlino (desni prekat) in nato ob srčnem utripu skozi drugo zaklopko (pulmonalna zaklopka) v pljučno žilje, kjer se napolni s kisikom. S kisikom bogata kri se vrne v tako imenovano levo srce – najprej v levo zbiralno votlino (levi preddvor), skozi tretjo zaklopko (mitralna zaklopka) v levo črpalno votlino (levi prekat). Od tam jo srce potisne skozi četrto zaklopko (aortna zaklopka) v aorto, veliko žilo, ki raznese kri po telesu in ga oskrbi s kisikom.
Kaj je šum?
Je pihajoč ali žvižgajoč zvok, ki ga sliši zdravnik, ko posluša otrokovo srce s stetoskopom.
Kako zdravnik ugotovi »šum na srcu«?
Med poslušanjem otrokovega srca zdravnik postavlja stetoskop na različna mesta na otrokovem prsnem košu. Ko posluša otrokovo srce, posluša zapiranje zaklopk. To so zvoki, ki jih sami poimenujemo kot »utrip oz. bitje srca« in jih slišimo, ko nekomu na prsni koš prislonimo svoje uho. Če poslušamo pozorno, bomo kmalu ugotovili, da gre za ponavljajoča zvočna fenomena, ki ju v grobem lahko zapišemo kot »lab-dab«. Tema zvokoma zdravnik pravi prvi in drugi ton. Prvi ton se pojavi, ko se zapreta zaklopki, ki nadzirata pretok krvi iz zbiralnih votlin v črpalni votlini (torej iz preddvorov v prekate). Drugi ton pomeni zapiranje zaklopk, ki sta odgovorni, da kri iz črpalnih votlin (prekatov) teče v pljučno žilje in aorto. Šum predstavlja dodaten tretji zvok, ki ga zdravnik sliši med pregledom. V večini primerov je ta dodatni zvok samo zvok krvi, ki teče skozi normalno, zdravo srce. Včasih pa je lahko znak bolezni srca.
Kako zdravnik opiše šum?
Zdravnik šum oceni po različnih kriterijih:
•Njegovo glasnost opiše z lestvico od 1 do 6. 1 pomeni zelo tih, komaj slišen šum, 6 pomeni zelo glasen šum.
•Določi, kdaj v srčnem ciklu se pojavi.
•Poišče mesto, kjer se šum sliši najglasneje.
•Ga opiše – visoko- ali nizkofrekvenčen.
•Preveri, ali se s spreminjanjem otrokovega položaja spreminja tudi šum.

To se zgodi iz več razlogov. »Nedolžni« šumi se pojavljajo in izginjajo, odvisno od otrokove frekvence srca, položaja pri pregledu in morebitno prisotne povišane telesne temperature. Nekateri novonastali šumi nas lahko opozorijo na razvijajočo se bolezen srca. In končno, pri nekaterih prirojenih boleznih srca (kongenitalne srčne napake) ob rojstvu mogoče šuma ne slišimo in se ta pojavi šele kasneje.
Kaj je »nedolžen« šum?
Je najpogostejši srčni šum pri otrocih. Namesto »nedolžen« ga lahko zdravnik poimenuje tudi kot »funkcionalen« ali »normalen« srčni šum. Nastane zaradi pospešenega toka krvi skozi zaklopke pri popolnoma zdravem srcu.
Vzroki za nastanek »nedolžnega« šuma:
•Povišana telesna temperatura
Ko ima otrok vročino, so energetske potrebe telesa višje. Da bi jih zadovoljilo, mora srce zagotoviti hitrejši pretok krvi po telesu.
•Anemija (slabokrvnost)
Kadar je koncentracija eritrocitov zmanjšana, teče kri po telesu hitreje.
•Tanka prsna stena in zelo raven hrbet
Zaradi anatomskega položaja, ki približa srce prsni steni. Tako se lažje sliši tok krvi skozi srce.

Najpogosteje je slišen pri aktivnih, zdravih od tri- do sedemtletnikih. Šum predsatvlja normalen zvok, ki ga povzroči iztis krvi v aorto ob srčnem utripu.
Otroci imajo, v primerjavi z odraslimi, manj maščobnega in mišičnega tkiva ter drobnejše kosti. Tako je pri pregledu njihovo srce bližje membrani stetoskopa, in zato so šumi pri njih bolje in lažje slišni. Ko otrok raste, postaja šum postopoma vedno slabše slišen in polagoma popolnoma izgine. Otroci z »nedolžnim« šumom ne potrebujejo zdravljenja, posebne diete ali omejitve aktivnosti. Tisti, dovolj stari, da razumejo, da imajo »šum na srcu«, potrebujejo zagotovilo staršev, da se v ničemer ne razlikujejo od ostalih otrok. Poenostavljeno povedano: »nedolžen« šum je zvok normalne krvi, ki teče skozi normalno, zdravo srce po normalni poti.

Nekateri šumi nastanejo zaradi prirojenih srčnih napak. Takšen šum je nefunkcionalen oz. organski.
Povzročijo ga:

Ko kri teče skozi srce, naleti na zaklopko, ki je ožja, kot bi morala biti. Tok krvi postane turbuenten in zaradi ožjega ustja tudi hitrejši, zato nastane šum.
•Zaklopka, ki pušča (insuficienca zaklopke)
Ko se zaklopke zaprejo in se srce skrči, del krvi teče v napačno smer (zateka nazaj, od koder je prišla). Ponovno nastane zvočni fenomen, šum.

Ker pritisk v različnih votlinah srca ni enak, bo kri tekla iz votline z višjim tlakom v votlino z nižjim tlakom in ponovno bo nastal šum.
Če bo zdravnik posumil, da gre za nefunkcionalen šum, bo otroka napotil h kardiologu. Ta bo otroka natančno pregledal in naredil nekaj dodatnih preiskav, kot so rentgenogram prsnih organov, EKG in ultrazvok srca.
Otroci s kongenitalno srčno napako imajo poleg šuma še druge težave oziroma znake bolezni. Znaki prirojene srčne napake so pri nekaterh otrocih opazni že v prvih dneh po rojstvu. Lahko pa se težave pojavijo šele kasneje v otroštvu pri otroku, ki je bil do tedaj navzven popolnoma zdrav.
Dodatni znaki pri otroku s srčno napako:
•Novorojenčki in dojenčki: pospešeno dihanje, težave pri hranjenju (hitro se utrudi), modrikasta barva ustnic, ne pridobiva teže, se močno poti.
•Otroci in mladostniki: ne napreduje kot bi moral, se hitro utrudi in ima občutek oteženega dihanja oziroma težke sape že pri zmernih telesnih aktivnostih, bolečina v prsnem košu, vrtoglavost in omedlevice.
Če opazite pri svojem otroku navedene znake, se obrnite na otrokovega izbranega pediatra.
•Šum na srcu ni bolezen, je dodaten zvok, ki gra zdravnik sliši, ko posluša otrokovo srce.
•Večina šumov ni nevarnih – »nedolžni« šumi. Takšni so pogosti pri zdravih otrocih. Otrok z »nedolžnim« šumom ima zdravo srce.
•Včasih je srčni šum znak bolezni. Takrat ima otrok tudi druge težave ali znake bolezni.
•Zdravnik bo pozorno poslušal delovanje otrokovega srca in se na podlagi slišanega odločil, ali je šum nedolžen ali ne.

Currently, we classify five species of hornwort (Ceratophyllum), which inhabit virtually all continents. All species are characterized by bright green stems with thin, needle-like leaves. The plant can grow either floating or vertically, with the lower leaves transforming into “anchors” that hold the plant in the sediment.
Algae and plants have very similar structures, so they essentially require the same nutrients for growth and development, with phosphates and nitrates being particularly important.
Plants, as more highly developed organisms, are more efficient at absorbing nutrients, so a simple equation applies: the more plants there are, the fewer nutrients are available for algae. As a byproduct of photosynthesis, plants release oxygen. Most pond plants are marginal, meaning they only have their roots in the water. The oxygen produced in the chlorophyll of the green parts above the water surface is thus released into the air. Aquatic plants, on the other hand, are completely submerged, so they can only release oxygen into the water, thereby increasing the oxygen levels in the water. This not only benefits fish but is also essential for the survival of beneficial bacteria in the filter. A third reason why it is advisable to cultivate true aquatic plants is their algicidal effect. Plants and algae compete not only for nutrients but also for living space and light. Plants overgrown with algae do not receive enough light, so plants have evolved numerous defense mechanisms to prevent algae growth. Aquatic plants thus release natural compounds into the water that inhibit algae growth and act as natural algicides.

Planting in a pond
As mentioned earlier, hornwort can grow either freely floating or anchored in the substrate. In ponds without sand (only a liner/mold), take the stems out of the bunch and release them into the pond. In ponds with sand, you can leave the hornwort in the bunch and sink it to the bottom of the pond to a maximum depth of 1 meter.
In the fall, the plants sink to the bottom, from where they float back to the surface in the spring.

Planting in an aquarium
Hornwort is one of the better nutrient consumers and also provides excellent hiding places for fry (e.g., livebearers such as guppies and platies) and shrimp. Labyrinth fish (especially bettas and gouramis) use hornwort to build their nests, and fish that swim just below the surface (e.g., pike) find shelter and a sense of security in it.

Propagation and cutting
The plant is easiest to propagate vegetatively by dividing the stem, but it is theoretically also possible to do so with seeds.
In ponds with a lot of organic pollution, hornwort should be thinned out regularly.

Si profesionalni prevajalec iz angleščine v slovenščino. Tvoja naloga je ustvariti visoko kakovostne prevode, ki so naravni, tekoči in natančni. Izogibaj se dobesednim prevodom, ki zvenijo nenaravno. Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

During the drive along the eastern coast of Argentina, there isn't much to see. The landscape is mostly barren, a dry steppe with no trees or shrubs, just dry, tufted grass. There's nothing around for miles, no mountains, no points of interest, except for a small green patch on the map, marking a national park called Bosque Petrificado (Petrified Forest).

How and why did the forest become petrified?
What we see in the park today are the remains of a forest that existed 150 million years ago! Yes, you read that right, 150 million years. During the Jurassic period, this area was very different. South America was connected to Africa, the climate was humid and cooler, and forests thrived. The climate was so favorable that huge trees grew here, ancestors of the araucarias (Chilean pines, which we first saw in Nahuelbuta National Park), which were over 100 meters tall and up to 3 meters in diameter.
However, when tectonic shifts began, they brought with them extremely strong winds that toppled these large and sturdy trees. (It is estimated that wind speeds exceeded 300 km/h). Volcanoes also erupted, and during the eruptions, the landscape was covered with volcanic ash. The fallen trees were then hermetically sealed, and the normal decomposition of biological material (decay, rotting, etc.) was prevented.
Rain that fell later on this volcanic dust dissolved minerals and seeped through the layer of dust to the trees below. There, the water filled all the pores and holes in the trees, and the minerals crystallized, thus copying or preserving the shape of the trees. Over time, new sediments were deposited on top of the volcanic ash, further sealing the trees and preventing oxygen from reaching them. At the same time, the new sediments brought new minerals that could crystallize in the trunks below. The entire process is called petrification.
Millennia later, a new process began: wind erosion, which is the reason for the discovery of the surface. The wind carries away the upper layers of sediment, and thus the petrified trees came to the surface and were noticed by people.
Visiting the Petrified Trees Today
Bosque Petrificado National Park covers a larger area of the former forest of giant araucarias, now petrified trunks. There is no entrance fee (which is nice!), but there are very strict rules regarding visits. For a long time, people were taking pieces of the petrified trees – just a small piece, as a souvenir. Today, the path through the park is fenced off, and walking outside the path is not allowed. It is also not allowed to touch the trees, and of course, you are not allowed to take anything with you. In principle, you only go on the tour with a camera in your hand; backpacks and bags are not allowed. If you do have them, they are carefully inspected before and after the tour.
Bosque Petrificado National Park is located about 50 km west of the main road, Route 3, and 580 km north of Rio Gallegos. There is no public transport to the park; the road is unpaved, but it can be driven on with a regular car.
And what do the petrified trees look like?
In short: incredibly interesting!
First, we watched a video about the petrification process in a small museum, and the friendly park ranger answered all our questions in English. She also showed us some examples of fossils, imprints of araucaria branches in stones, and we were able to touch and feel some of the petrified trunks – these are the only pieces in the park that you can touch! It's really cool to hold a petrified tree; the trunk is brown and looks like a real trunk, but when you hold it in your hand, it's as heavy as lead! Because it's petrified, of course!
Next, we took a walk through the park, where we could see many petrified trees. In fact, only the trunks have been preserved; the branches have mostly been lost. Still, it's amazing to see such huge trees lying there in the barren landscape and to realize that they are actually all minerals and no longer trees. It's truly fascinating! The landscape around is also amazing, different, and wild. In the distance, you can see the extinct volcano Madre y Hija, which is said to be the reason for the desolation. The rocks around are of different colors: white, pink, red, brown, green, black... Guanacos were walking around, and 150 million-year-old trees were lying on the ground. Amazing.
On the way out of the park, we were lucky enough to see another type of South American animal: a mara. The mara is a very interesting animal. When it sits, it looks like a rabbit, only with slightly shorter ears. But when it stands up and starts walking or running, it looks like a deer. It's a really funny combination. And to top it off: it's mostly brown, but it has a large black patch on its rump and a white stripe underneath. Why this is useful, I don't know, but it looks very fun and cute at the same time.
In summary, the trip to Bosque Petrificado, even though it was quite a detour, was a great decision. The landscape changes from a completely flat, dry steppe to a more gravelly, dry steppe with hills. Seeing 150 million-year-old trees and learning about the process of how they became petrified was extremely interesting for me. And because we also met so many animals (guanacos, maras, foxes), it made the trip perfect.

Tekom vožnje ob argentinski vzhodni obali ni videti kaj dosti zanimivih stvari. Pokrajina je večinoma pusta, suha stepa, brez dreves ali grmovja, pač pa samo s suho šopasto travo. Daleč naokoli ni ničesar, nobene gore, nobene zanimivosti, edino tam na zemljevidu je bila majhna zelena packa, ki označuje nacionalni park z imenom Bosque Petrificado (okamneli gozd).
Kako in zakaj je gozd okamnel?
Kar danes vidimo v tem parku, so ostanki gozdu izpred 150 milijonov let! Ja, prav ste prebrali, 150 milijonov. V času jure je bilo to področje zelo drugačno. Južna Amerika se je stikala z Afriko, podnebje je bilo vlažno in hladnejše in uspevali so gozdovi. Klima je bila tako zelo ugodna, da so tu rasla ogromna drevesa, predniki aravkarij (čilske smreke, ki sva jo prvič videla v parku Nahuelbuta), ki so bila visoka preko 100m in debela do 3m.
Ko pa so se začeli tektonski premiki, so se z njimi pojavili izredno močni vetrovi, ki so ta velika in močna drevesa podrli. (Ugibajo, da so hitrosti vetrov presegle 300km/h). Dvignili so se tudi vulkani in ob izbruhu pokrajino prekrili z vulkanskim pepelom. Tako so bila padla drevesa nepredušno pokrita in normalna razgradnja biološkega materiala (trohnjene, gnitje …) je bila onemogočena.
Dež, ki je kasneje padal na ta vulkanski prah, je spiral minerale in pronical skozi plast prahu do dreves spodaj. Tam je voda zapolnila vse pore in luknje v drevesih, minerali pa so kristalizirali in tako skopirali oz. ohranili obliko dreves. S časom so preko vulkanskega prahu prišli še novi sedimenti in drevesa še bolj zatesnili pred dostopom kisika, hkrati pa so novi sedimenti prinesli nove minerale, ki so lahko kristalizirali v deblih spodaj. Celoten proces se imenuje petrifikacija (okamnitev).
Tisočljetja kasneje se je začel nov proces, veterna erozija, ki je razlog za odkrivanje površja. Veter namreč odnaša zgornje plasti sedimentov in tako so okamnela drevesa prišla na površje in so jih ljudje opazili.
Ogled okamnelih dreves danes
Park Bosque Petrificado zavzema širše področje nekdanjega gozdu gigantskih aravkarij, danes okamnelih debel. Vstopnine ne zaračunavajo (lepo, kajne?), imajo pa zelo striktna pravila glede obiska. Namreč dolgo časa se je dogajalo, da so ljudje odnašali koščke okamnelih dreves – pač tako malo, za spomin. Danes je pot po parku ograjena, hoja izven te poti pa ni dovoljena. Prav tako ni dovoljeno dotikanje dreves in seveda ne smeš ničesar vzeti s seboj. Načeloma greš na ogled samo s fotoaparatom v roki, nahrbtnikov in torb ne dovolijo. Če že, pa jih pred in po ogledu skrbno preiščejo.
Park Bosque Petrificado se nahaja približno 50km zahodno od glavne ceste, Rute 3 in 580km severno od kraja Rio Galegos. Javnega prevoza do tja ni, cesta je makadamska, a se jo da prevoziti tudi z navadnim avtomobilom.
In kako zgledajo okamnela drevesa?
Na kratko: noro zanimivo!
Najprej sva si v majhnem muzeju ogledala postopek petrifikacije, prijazna oskrbnica parka pa nama je v angleščini odgovorila na vsa najina vprašanja. Pokazala nama je tudi nekaj primerov fosilov, odtisov vej aravkarij v kamnih in potežkala ter pretipala sva lahko nekaj okamnelih debel – to so tudi edini kosi, ki se jih v parku lahko dotakneš! Res je hecno prijeti okamnelo drevo, deblo je rjave barve in zgleda pač kot da bi bilo pravo deblo, ko pa ga primeš v roke pa je težko kot svinec! Ker je okamnelo, seveda!
Sledil je sprehod po parku, kjer se da videti številna okamnela drevesa. Pravzaprav so se ohranila so se samo debla, veje so se večinoma izgubile. Vseeno je noro videti tako ogromna drevesa, ležati tam v sušnati pokrajini in se zavedati, da so to pravzaprav vse minerali in ne več drevesa. Res fascinantno! Pa tudi pokrajina okoli je nora, drugačna, divja. V daljavi se vidi ugasli vulkan Madre y Hija, ki naj bi bil razlog za opustošenje. Kamine naokoli so različnih barv; bele, roza, rdeče, rjave, zelene, črne … Mimo naju so se sprehajali gvanaki in tam na tleh so ležala 150 milijonov let stara drevesa. Noro.
Na poti iz parka sva imela srečo videti še eno vrsto južnoameriških živali: maro. Mara je taka zanimiva živalca. Ko sedi, spominja na zajca, le ušesa ima malo krajša. Ko pa vstane in začne hoditi ali teči, pa zgleda kot kakšna srna. Res hecna kombinacija. Za nameček pa še to: večinoma je rjave barve, le na zadku ima veliko črno zaplato in pod njo belo črto. Zakaj je to koristno, ne vem, zgleda pa zelo zabavno, a prikupno hkrati.
Če povzamem, izlet do Bosque Petrificado, četudi je bil kar konkretno iz najine poti, je bil super odločitev. Pokrajina se spremeni iz popolnoma ravne suhe stepe v bolj gruščnato suho stepo z vzpetinami. Videti 150 milijonov let stara drevesa in se naučiti postopka, kako so okamnela, je bilo zame izredno zanimivo. Ker sva ob tem srečala še toliko živali (gvanake, mare, lisice), pa je to izlet naredilo popoln.

Si profesionalni prevajalec iz angleščine v slovenščino. Tvoja naloga je ustvariti visoko kakovostne prevode, ki so naravni, tekoči in natančni. Izogibaj se dobesednim prevodom, ki zvenijo nenaravno. Upoštevaj kontekst, idiome in kulturne reference. Ne dodajaj nobenih dodatnih informacij ali komentarjev, samo prevod.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

All people are daily in contact with many bacteria and viruses found in the air, water, soil, and everywhere else around us. Some of these can cause serious infectious diseases – we call them pathogens. We are protected from them by the immune system, without which we cannot effectively defend ourselves even against the mildest infections. However, the immune system also needs to learn throughout life how to successfully fight against dangerous microorganisms. Vaccination helps it do this by showing it, even before its encounter with the causative agent of infection, which bacteria and viruses it needs to overcome.
If we want to understand how vaccination works, we must first understand how the immune system responds to infection. You have surely heard someone say at some point: ''Since I've already had chickenpox, I can't get it again.'' The same applies to many other diseases.
When a virus or bacterium enters the body, the cells of the immune system are activated. Some are ready immediately, but are less effective against many diseases. Others fight pathogens by marking them with antibodies. These disable the pathogen's function, while at the same time marking it so that other cells in the body can easily destroy it. But on the first contact with a pathogen, the immune system will need at least a week or two to begin producing antibodies effectively. Upon first contact, we therefore still get sick before the immune system produces enough antibodies to defeat the pathogen. With this, however, the immune system learns an important lesson. To defend itself against the next contact with the same pathogen, it has a special weapon: immune memory. Memory cells are created, whose task is to remember which pathogen they have already encountered, and to activate immediately upon the next encounter. The immune response is therefore much faster and more effective on the next encounter – although we come into contact with the pathogen, we do not get sick.
With vaccination, we take advantage of this natural ability of the body to defend itself. We introduce into the body such modified particles of pathogens that they do not cause disease, but do create immune memory. So even when meeting the pathogen, the child does not get sick with the disease we are vaccinating against. In this way, just as with infection by wild microbes, we teach the immune system how to defend itself, but without risking infection, its potentially severe complications, or even death.
Through vaccination, we educate and strengthen the immune system without the risk of the consequences of the first infection.
VACCINATION SCHEDULE
In Slovenia, we mandatorily vaccinate against nine diseases: diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, Haemophilus influenzae b, polio, hepatitis B, measles, rubella, and mumps. Vaccination against HPV, which causes cervical cancer and other types of cancer, is also highly recommended; vaccination against rotavirus and pneumococcal infections is also recommended.
If we vaccinate too early, the effectiveness of the vaccine may be lower than we would like; if we vaccinate too late, we leave the child unprotected for too long. With later vaccination than recommended, side effects with some vaccines can also be more frequent. The vaccination schedule is designed to find a balance between these risks and ensure the best possible vaccine effectiveness and protection against disease.
With the year 2020, Slovenia will move closer to modern European countries and the USA with a change to the vaccination schedule. Children will be vaccinated against hepatitis B for the first time at 3 months, which will better protect them against this potentially chronic infection, which can eventually cause cirrhosis and liver cancer.
The vaccines in the vaccination schedule are combined: the hexavalent vaccine against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, Haemophilus influenzae B, polio, and hepatitis B protects against all six diseases, but is a single injection. The same applies to the trivalent vaccine against measles, mumps, and rubella. This is also less stressful for children, who receive fewer injections, while still being protected against the same number of diseases.
SIDE EFFECTS
Side effects after vaccination are mild and harmless. Because we stimulate the immune system, you can expect mild pain, warmth, and redness at the injection site, which will disappear in less than one week. Mild fever is possible, lasting less than two days.
More severe side effects are extremely rare, especially compared to other medications. Side effects are also reported and monitored in a system, so we have constant oversight of vaccine safety. In Slovenia, they can be reported by anyone. There are several systems for ongoing monitoring of post-vaccination events; the USA alone has more than five.
When is vaccination not recommended? Such cases are very rare.
Vaccination is not appropriate in cases of severe sensitivity or allergy to the contents of an individual vaccine. In some cases of allergies, vaccination can still be carried out in a hospital under medical supervision, if the threat of the disease is greater than the threat of the allergy. Egg allergy is no longer a contraindication for vaccination, since monitoring of side effects has not shown severe reactions in this group of allergic individuals.
A severe infectious disease usually means that vaccination is postponed somewhat. A cold is usually not a contraindication for vaccination.
Vaccination may be ineffective in some cases of congenital diseases of the immune system.
If any of these are suspected, consultation with a doctor who knows your child and will be able to weigh the options regarding vaccination is essential.
COMPOSITION OF VACCINES
The key components of vaccines are the active substances. These can be weakened viruses, dead microbes, or just their constituent parts. When the immune system comes into contact with them, it learns how to defend against them and remembers this. Against some diseases, such as measles, this immune memory lasts a lifetime. Every day we come into contact with an incomparably greater number of microbes that live on our skin, mucous membranes, or enter the body through wounds.
The major part of vaccine content is water. The quantity of the entire vaccine is small – most vaccines contain only 0.5 ml of liquid.
Some vaccines, all of them inactivated, contain aluminum salts. These bind the active substances, stimulate the immune response when meeting microbes, and in this way increase the effectiveness of vaccines. Aluminum is the most common metal in the Earth's crust. We are exposed to its compounds daily through food, drinking water, and children also through breast milk or milk formulas. Regardless of the source, they are excreted equally through the kidneys, and the quantities in vaccines are proven safe. The intake from vaccines is small compared to other sources and does not significantly affect the quantity in the body.
Some attenuated vaccines contain gelatin, which prevents the active substances from breaking down with temperature fluctuations. Other ingredients used for a similar purpose are some sugars, sweeteners, and amino acids.
During production, some antibiotics are also used, which may be present in trace amounts in vaccines. These are antibiotics that are used only rarely for treatment, and to which hypersensitivity is equally rare. Formaldehyde is also used for the inactivation of some microbes and their toxins in vaccine production. It is produced continuously in our bodies during metabolism. In the blood of a two-month-old child, there is ten times more formaldehyde than is contained in any vaccine.
WHY VACCINATE
It is well known that in old times, a huge number of children died in the first years of life. A major cause of this was childhood infectious diseases, which can have severe complications and can also lead to death. In some parts of the world, people did not even name their children until they had survived measles, since the probability of death was so great. Even when children did not die, many diseases left severe consequences behind them: blindness, deafness, paralysis, mental retardation, infertility, and many others.
Even with all modern technology and tremendous progress in medicine, for many of these diseases we still do not know a cure today and can only prevent them. Vaccination therefore provides personal protection for the individual. It also represents protection for the entire community through herd immunity.
If a large enough percentage of the population is vaccinated, pathogens can no longer survive within anyone, their spread is greatly slowed, and the disease ceases to occur. Part of the population, for various reasons, cannot be vaccinated, or vaccination does not work for them due to a deficient immune system. These are mostly the most medically vulnerable individuals, for whom infection means greater risk of severe consequences, including death: infants, cancer patients, and the immunocompromised. Because the disease cannot spread and occur due to herd immunity, through vaccination we also protect the most vulnerable individuals in our community who cannot be vaccinated themselves from the disease.
The benefits of vaccination extend even further: with sufficiently high vaccination coverage, we can completely eradicate some diseases. We have already succeeded in this with smallpox and the cattle disease rinderpest, against which vaccination is no longer necessary, since there is no longer any danger of infection. We are also on the threshold of success with polio. With sufficiently high vaccination coverage, in the future we could also eradicate measles and rubella, as well as cervical cancer, which is the fourth most common cancer in women worldwide. It is prevented by HPV vaccination.
VACCINATION DURING PREGNANCY
During pregnancy, antibodies are transferred from mother to child through the placenta, as well as during breastfeeding. The child is therefore protected during pregnancy and in the first months of life against those diseases against which the pregnant woman was vaccinated. Some vaccines are also recommended during pregnancy, since they ensure a high increase in antibodies and better protection of the child. This is especially important because newborns and infants are even more vulnerable to various diseases. Whooping cough, for example, is much more dangerous for infants and carries a much greater risk of suffocation, since they have much narrower airways than adults.
During pregnancy, vaccination against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, and influenza is especially recommended. Both vaccines (one of these is combined: diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough) against these diseases are inactivated, so they pose no risk that unborn children could be infected through them, but rather they greatly contribute to their health in the first months of life. They are recommended as soon as possible after completing the 24th week of pregnancy.
Vaccination with live vaccines (measles, mumps, rubella; yellow fever among travel vaccines) is contraindicated during pregnancy, because there is a small theoretical possibility that the weakened live viruses could harm the fetus. In practice, this has never been demonstrated, but it is still advised against out of caution. If it proves necessary, it is recommended at least one month before planned pregnancy, since the mother thus transfers more antibodies to the child and protects it more effectively.
Article source: National Institute of Public Health
Author: Imuno Project

Vsi ljudje smo vsakodnevno v stiku z mnogimi bakterijami in virusi, ki se nahajajo v zraku, vodi, zemlji ter povsod drugod okoli nas. Nekateri od teh lahko povzročajo hude nalezljive bolezni – pravimo jim patogeni. Pred njimi nas varuje imunski sistem, brez katerega se ne moremo učinkovito braniti niti pred najblažjimi okužbami. Vendar se mora tudi imunski sistem tekom življenja naučiti, kako se uspešno boriti proti nevarnim mikroorganizmom. Pri tem mu pomaga cepljenje, ki mu že pred srečanjem s povzročiteljem okužbe pokaže, katere bakterije in viruse mora premagati.
Če želimo razumeti delovanje cepljenja, moramo najprej razumeti, kako se imunski sistem odzove na okužbo. Gotovo ste že kdaj slišali koga reči: ‘‘Ker sem že prebolel norice, za njimi ne morem več zboleti.’’ Enako velja tudi za mnoge druge bolezni.
Ob vstopu virusa ali bakterije v telo se aktivirajo celice imunskega sistema. Nekatere so pripravljene takoj, vendar so proti mnogim boleznim manj učinkovite. Druge se proti patogenom borijo tako, da jih označujejo s protitelesi. Ta onemogočijo delovanje patogena, hkrati pa ga označijo tako, da ga druge celice v telesu zlahka uničijo. Toda ob prvem stiku s patogenom bo imunski sistem potreboval vsaj teden ali dva, da začne učinkovito izdelovati protitelesa. Ob prvem stiku zato vseeno zbolimo, preden imunski sistem izdela dovolj protiteles, da premaga patogen. S tem pa se imunski sistem nauči pomembne lekcije. Da se ubrani pred naslednjim stikom z enakim patogenom, ima posebno orožje: imunski spomin. Ustvarijo se spominske celice, katerih naloga je, da si zapomnijo, s katerim patogenom so se že srečale, in se ob naslednjem srečanju takoj aktivirajo. Imunski odziv je zato pri naslednjem srečanju mnogo hitrejši in učinkovitejši – čeprav pridemo v stik s patogenom, ne zbolimo.
Pri cepljenju izkoristimo to naravno sposobnost telesa za obrambo. V telo vnesemo tako prilagojene delce patogenov, da ne povzročijo bolezni, ustvarijo pa imunski spomin. Tako tudi ob srečanju s patogenom otrok ne zboli za boleznijo, proti kateri ga cepimo. Na ta način enako kot pri okužbi z divjimi mikrobi naučimo imunski sistem, kako se braniti, vendar pri tem ne tvegamo okužbe, njenih potencialnih hudih zapletov ali celo smrti.
S cepljenjem izobrazimo in okrepimo imunski sistem brez tveganja posledic prve okužbe.
KOLEDAR CEPLJENJA
V Sloveniji obvezno cepimo proti devetim boleznim: davici, tetanusu, oslovskemu kašlju, Hemofilusu influence b, otroški paralizi, hepatitisu B, ošpicam, rdečkam in mumpsu. Zelo je priporočljivo tudi cepljenje proti HPV, ki povzroča raka na materničnem vratu in druge vrste raka, priporoča se tudi cepljenje proti rotavirusu in pnevmokoknim okužbam.
Če cepimo prezgodaj, je učinkovitost cepiva lahko slabša, kot bi želeli; če cepimo prepozno, pa otroka predolgo pustimo nezaščitenega. Pri poznejšem cepljenju, kot je priporočeno, so lahko tudi neželeni učinki pri nekaterih cepivih pogostejši. Koledar cepljenja je zasnovan tako, da najde ravnotežje med temi tveganji in zagotavlja čim boljšo učinkovitost cepiva ter zaščito pred boleznijo.
Z letom 2020 se bomo v Sloveniji približali modernim evropskim državam in ZDA s spremembo urnika cepljenja. Otroci bodo proti hepatitisu B cepljeni prvič pri 3 mesecih, s čimer jih bomo bolje zavarovali pred to potencialno kronično okužbo, ki lahko sčasoma povzroči cirozo in raka jeter.
Cepiva v koledarju cepljenja so kombinirana: šestvalentno cepivo proti davici, tetanusu, oslovskemu kašlju, Hemofilusu influence B, otroški paralizi in hepatitisu B zaščiti proti vsem šestim boleznim, a gre za eno samo injekcijo. Enako velja za trovalentno cepivo proti ošpicam, mumpsu in rdečkam. To je tudi manj stresno za otroke, ki prejmejo manj vbodov, še vedno pa so zaščiteni pred enakim številom bolezni.
NEŽELENI UČINKI
Neželeni učinki po cepljenju so blagi in nenevarni. Ker stimuliramo imunski sistem, lahko pričakujete blažjo bolečino, toplino in rdečino na mestu vboda, ki bo izginila v manj kot enem tednu. Možna je blaga vročina, ki traja manj kot dva dni.
Hujši neželeni učinki so izjemno redki, sploh v primerjavi z drugimi zdravili. Neželeni učinki se tudi prijavljajo in spremljajo v sistemu, zato imamo nad varnostjo cepiv stalen pregled. V Sloveniji jih lahko prijavi kdor koli. Obstaja več sistemov sprotnega spremljanja pojavov po cepljenju; samo ZDA jih imajo več kot pet.
Kdaj pa se cepljenje odsvetuje? Taki primeri so zelo redki.
Cepljenje ni primerno pri hudi občutljivosti ali alergiji na vsebino posameznega cepiva. V nekaterih primerih alergij se lahko vseeno izvede cepljenje v bolnišnici pod zdravniškim nadzorom, če je grožnja bolezni večja od grožnje alergije. Alergija na jajca ni več kontraindikacija za cepljenje, saj spremljanje neželenih učinkov ni pokazalo hudih reakcij pri tej skupini alergikov.
Hujša infekcijska bolezen navadno pomeni, da se cepljenje nekoliko zamakne. Prehlad navadno ni kontraindikacija za cepljenje.
Cepljenje je lahko neučinkovito v nekaterih primerih prirojenih bolezni imunskega sistema.
Ob sumu na kar koli od tega je nujen posvet z zdravnikom, ki vašega otroka pozna in bo znal pretehtati možnosti glede cepljenja.
SESTAVA CEPIV
Ključne za cepiva so aktivne učinkovine. To so lahko oslabljeni virusi, mrtvi mikrobi ali zgolj njihovi sestavni deli. Ko pride imunski sistem v stik z njimi, se nauči, kako se pred njimi braniti, ter si to zapomni. Proti nekaterim boleznim, kot so npr. ošpice, traja ta imunski spomin celo življenje. Vsakodnevno prihajamo v stik z neprimerno večjim številom mikrobov, ki živijo na naši koži, sluznicah ali pridejo v telo skozi rane.
Večji del vsebine cepiva predstavlja voda. Količina celotnega cepiva je majhna – večina cepiv ima zgolj 0,5 ml tekočine.
Nekaj cepiv, vsa od njih inaktivirana, vsebujejo aluminijeve soli. Te vežejo aktivne učinkovine, spodbujajo imunski odziv ob srečanju z mikrobi in na ta način povečujejo učinkovitost cepiv. Aluminij je najpogostejša kovina v zemljinem plašču. Njegovim spojinam smo izpostavljeni vsakodnevno preko hrane, pitne vode, otroci pa tudi preko materinega mleka ali mlečnih formul. Ne glede na izvor se izločajo enako preko ledvic, količine v cepivih pa so dokazano varne. Vnos s cepivi je v primerjavi z drugimi viri majhen in ne vpliva bistveno na količino v telesu.
Nekatera oslabljena cepiva vsebujejo želatino, ki preprečuje, da bi aktivne učinkovine ob nihanju temperature razpadle. Druge sestavine, ki se uporabljajo za podoben namen, so nekateri sladkorji, sladila in aminokisline.
Med proizvodnjo se uporabljajo tudi nekateri antibiotiki, ki so lahko v cepivih prisotni v sledovih. Pri tem gre za antibiotike, ki se uporabljajo zgolj redko za zdravljenje in proti katerim je preobčutljivost prav tako redka. Za inaktivacijo nekaterih mikrobov in njihovih toksinov v proizvodnji cepiv se uporablja tudi formaldehid. V naših telesih nastaja sproti med metabolizmom. V krvi dvomesečnega otroka je prisotnega deset krat večja količina formaldehida, kot ga vsebuje katero koli cepivo.
ZAKAJ CEPITI
Dobro je znano, da je v starih časih ogromno število otrok umrlo že v prvih letih življenja. Velik vzrok za to so bile otroške nalezljive bolezni, ki imajo lahko hude zaplete in lahko privedejo tudi do smrti. V nekaterih delih sveta ljudje svojih otrok niso niti poimenovali, dokler ti niso preboleli ošpic, saj je bila verjetnost za smrt tako velika. Tudi kadar otroci niso umrli, so mnoge bolezni za sabo puščale hude posledice: slepoto, gluhost, ohromelost, duševno zaostalost, neplodnost in mnoge druge.
Tudi z vso moderno tehnologijo in ogromnim napredkom medicine za mnoge od teh bolezni še danes ne poznamo zdravila in jih znamo le preprečevati. Cepljenje torej zagotavlja osebno zaščito za posameznika. Predstavlja pa tudi zaščito za celotno skupnost preko kolektivne imunosti.
Če je cepljen dovolj velik odstotek prebivalstva, patogeni ne morejo več preživeti znotraj nikogar, njihovo širjenje se močno upočasni in bolezen se neha pojavljati. Del prebivalstva se zaradi različnih vzrokov ne more cepiti ali pa cepljenje pri njih zaradi pomanjkljivega imunskega sistema ne deluje. To so večinoma zdravstveno najbolj ranljivi posamezniki, katerim okužba pomeni večjo tveganje za hude posledice, tudi smrt: dojenčki, bolniki z rakom in imunsko oslabljeni. Ker se zaradi kolektivne imunosti bolezen ne more širiti in pojavljati, s cepljenjem pred boleznijo zaščitimo tudi najbolj ranljive posameznike v naši skupnosti, ki se sami ne morejo cepiti.
Koristi cepljenja segajo še dlje: z dovolj visoko precepljenostjo lahko nekatere bolezni popolnoma izkoreninimo. To nam je že uspelo s črnimi kozami in govejo boleznijo rinderpest, proti katerim zdaj ni več potrebno cepiti, saj ni več nevarnosti za okužbo. Na pragu uspeha pa smo tudi s otroško paralizo. Z dovolj visoko precepljenostjo bi lahko v prihodnosti izkoreninili tudi ošpice in rdečke, ter raka materničnega vratu , ki je v svetu četrti najpogostejši rak pri ženskah. Preprečuje ga cepljenje proti HPV.
CEPLJENJE V NOSEČNOSTI
Med nosečnostjo se protitelesa preko posteljice prenašajo z matere na otroka, prav tako med dojenjem. Otrok je zato med nosečnostjo in v prvih mesecih življenja zaščiten pred tistimi boleznimi, proti katerim je bila cepljena nosečnica. Nekatera cepiva se priporoča tudi med nosečnostjo, saj tako zagotovimo visok porast protiteles in boljšo zaščito otroka. To je še posebno pomembno, ker so novorojenčki in dojenčki še toliko bolj ranljivi za razne bolezni. Oslovski kašelj, na primer, je za dojenčke veliko bolj nevaren in nosi veliko večje tveganje zadušitve, saj imajo ti mnogo ožje dihalne poti kot odrasli.
Med nosečnostjo se posebej priporoča cepljenje proti davici, tetanusu, oslovskemu kašlju in gripi. Obe cepivi (eno izmed teh je kombinirano: davica, tetanus, oslovski kašelj) proti tem boleznim sta inaktivirani, zato ne predstavljajo tveganja, da bi se še nerojeni otroci preko njih okužili, temveč močno pripomoreta k njihovemu zdravju v prvih mesecih življenja. Priporočeni sta čim prej po dopolnjenem 24. tednu nosečnosti.
Cepljenje z živimi cepivi (ošpice, mumps, rdečke; rumena mrzlica med potovalnimi cepivi) je v nosečnosti kontraindicirano, ker obstaja majhna teoretična možnost, da bi oslabljeni živi virusi lahko škodovali plodu. V praksi to ni bilo še nikoli pokazano, vendar je iz previdnosti vseeno odsvetovano. Če se izkaže za potrebno, je priporočljivo vsaj en mesec pred načrtovano nosečnostjo, saj tako mati na otroka prenese več protiteles in ga učinkoviteje zavaruje.

Knowledge for Better Health
Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS)
Causative Agents
The disease is caused by viruses that are transmitted to the environment through the saliva and excrement of rodents, especially mice, voles, and rats, and possibly also moles. Rodents serve as a reservoir for the disease and are chronic carriers of the virus. Humans are accidental hosts. An increased number of cases is usually associated with an increased number of mice and similar rodents.
The disease is caused by RNA viruses of the Hanta genus, which belong to the Bunyaviridae family. More than 25 antigenically different viral species are known, including the Puumala and Dobrava viruses, which cause the disease in Slovenia.
Incubation Period
The time from infection to the onset of disease symptoms is usually 2 to 4 weeks, but can range from a few days to two months.
Mode of Transmission
It is believed that the disease is transmitted from rodents to humans through the inhalation of dust contaminated with rodent secretions, urine, feces, and saliva (e.g., during cleaning, especially dry cleaning of basements, attics). It can also be transmitted through the consumption of contaminated food or water and through direct contact with infected material through the skin (e.g., when swimming in surface waters, contact with contaminated soil).
Susceptibility to Infection
In Slovenia, the disease has been known since 1952, when the first patient, a seasonal forest worker in the Pohorje area, was identified. Currently, two natural foci are known: Dolenjska and Prekmurje. Both areas are predominantly rural, with numerous vineyards and agricultural land.
The disease occurs mainly in late spring, summer, and autumn. It is often associated with gardening, fieldwork, outdoor activities, camping, swimming, especially in natural swimming areas, recreation, and cleaning areas contaminated with rodent excrement. Therefore, the disease is more common in rural areas, but it can also occur in cities, where rodents contaminate objects and food in basements and warehouses with their excrement.
Climate conditions, terrain configuration, the presence of rodents, and the lifestyle of people who are often in contact with nature contribute to the existence of natural disease foci and human infection.
Symptoms of the Disease
The disease progresses in several stages.
Typical clinical symptoms include: elevated body temperature, fever, headache, and other general symptoms, back pain, nausea, vomiting, bleeding in the mucous membranes of the mouth and conjunctiva, nosebleeds, possible stiff neck, and frequent transient kidney failure.
Infectiousness
Transmission from human to human has not been proven.
Treatment
Intensive supportive treatment (dialysis) in the hospital is often necessary during the course of the disease. Recovery usually leads to complete healing. In untreated patients, death occurs in 5% to 15% of cases.
Prevention of Infection
Since the hantavirus that causes HFRS is transmitted by inhaling contaminated rodent secretions (rats, mice), an important preventive measure is to control rodents, i.e., deratization.
Preventive measures that reduce contact with rodents and their excrement include:
Housing and Food:
- Access of rodents to buildings, houses, and human dwellings must be prevented.
- Food for humans and animals should be stored in a way that prevents access by rodents.
- Before cleaning enclosed spaces such as basements, attics, sheds, barns, and apartments, if rodents have appeared in them or their excrement has been observed, the spaces should be well ventilated (ventilate for at least 30 minutes).
- During ventilation, people should be removed from the room.
- While ventilating, a chlorine disinfectant solution should be prepared by mixing one unit of disinfectant, e.g., bleach, with 10 units of water; when using a pre-prepared disinfectant, the manufacturer's instructions should be followed.
- When cleaning, use rubber gloves, masks, and clothing with long sleeves and pants.
- Surfaces contaminated with rodent excrement should be disinfected (thoroughly sprayed) with a disinfectant solution (minimum contact time of the disinfectant is 5 minutes).
- Disinfected excrement or dead rodents should be picked up with a paper towel, which should then be discarded in the trash; dead rodents should be buried in the ground and covered with lime.
- After removing dead rodents and excrement, it is recommended to disinfect other surfaces and objects that may be contaminated with excrement and therefore infected, and then it is recommended to mechanically clean with a cloth and a detergent solution (sweeping or vacuuming is not recommended).
- As much as possible, avoid inhaling dust when cleaning surfaces that may be contaminated with rodent excrement.
- After cleaning, thoroughly wash and disinfect cleaning tools before removing them, and also wash and disinfect the gloves, which should be discarded in general waste.
- After cleaning, thoroughly wash hands with warm water and soap.
In Nature:
- If traces or excrement of rodents are observed in nature, avoid staying in these areas, setting up tents, or engaging in sports activities, if possible.
Rodent Control:
- Systematic control and safe removal of rodents is necessary; do not touch dead rodents with bare hands.
- If a large number of dead mice are found in areas where livestock are kept (barns), the competent veterinarian should be notified.

Z znanjem do boljšega zdravja
Hemoragična mrzlica z renalnim sindromom (HMRS)
Povzročitelji
Povzročitelji bolezni so virusi, ki jih v okolje s slino in iztrebki izločajo glodavci, zlasti miši, voluharji in podgane, verjetno tudi krti. Glodavci predstavljajo rezervoar bolezni in so kronični nosilci virusa. Ljudje smo naključni gostitelji virusa. Povečano število obolenj je običajno povezano s povečanim številom miši in podobnih glodavcev.
Bolezen povzročajo RNA virusi iz rodu Hanta, ki spadajo v družino Bunyaviridae. Poznanih je več kot 25 antigensko različnih virusnih vrst, med njimi bolezen v Sloveniji povzročata virusa Puumala in Dobrava.
Doba inkubacije
Čas od okužbe do pojava znakov bolezni, je običajno 2 do 4 tedne, lahko pa od nekaj dni do dveh mesecev.
Način prenosa
Predpostavlja se, da se bolezen z glodavca na človeka prenese preko vdihavanja prahu, ki je okužen z izločki, s sečem, iztrebki in slino, glodavcev (npr. pri pospravljanju, predvsem suhem čiščenju kleti, podstrešja), lahko pa tudi z uživanjem okužene hrane ali vode ter pri stiku s kužnino direktno preko kože (npr. pri kopanju v površinskih vodah, stiku z okuženo zemljo).
Dovzetnost za okužbo
V Sloveniji je bolezen poznana od leta 1952, ko je bil odkrit prvi bolnik, sezonski gozdni delavec na območju Pohorja. Pri nas sta zaenkrat poznani dve naravni žarišči – Dolenjska in Prekmurje. Obe območji sta izrazito ruralni s številnimi vinogradi in poljedelskimi površinami.
Bolezen se pojavlja predvsem v poznih pomladanskih, poletnih in jesenskih mesecih. Pogosto je povezana z opravili na vrtu, polju, dejavnostmi v naravi, taborjenjem, kopanjem, zlasti na divjih kopališčih, rekreacijo, pa tudi s čiščenjem mest, onesnaženih z iztrebki glodavcev. Bolezen se torej pogosteje pojavlja na podeželju, vendar pa se lahko pojavi tudi v mestih, kjer glodavci z iztrebki okužijo predmete in hrano v kleteh, skladiščih.
Klimatski pogoji, konfiguracija terena, prisotnost glodavcev in način življenja ljudi, ki so pogosto v stiku z naravo, omogočajo obstoj naravnih žarišč bolezni in tudi okužbo ljudi.
Znaki bolezni
Bolezen poteka v več fazah.
Značilni klinični znaki so: povišana telesna temperatura, mrzlica, glavobol in drugi splošni znaki, bolečine v križu, slabost, bruhanje, krvavitve v sluznico ustne votline in veznico, krvavitve iz nosu, možen je otrpel tilnik, neredko se pojavi prehodna odpoved ledvic.
Kužnost
Prenos iz človeka na človeka ni dokazan.
Zdravljenje
Pogosto je v poteku zdravljenja bolezni potrebno intenzivno podporno zdravljenje (dializa) v bolnišnici. Okrevanje običajno privede do popolne ozdravitve. Pri nezdravljenih bolnikih se smrt pojavi v 5% do 15%.
Preprečevanje okužb
Ker se hantavirus, ki povzroča HMRS, prenaša z vdihavanjem kontaminiranih izločkov glodavcev (podgan, miši), je pomemben ukrep preprečevanja bolezni predvsem zatiranje glodavcev oziroma deratizacija.
Preventivni ukrepi, ki zmanjšajo kontakta z glodavci in njihovimi iztrebki so:
Bivališče, hrana:
- potrebno je onemogočiti dostop glodavcem v stavbe, hiše, oziroma bivališča ljudi,
- hrano za ljudi in živali se shranjuje na način, ki ne omogoča dostopa glodavcem.
- pred čiščenjem zaprtih prostorov kot so kleti, podstrešja, skednji, hlevi, lope, tudi stanovanja, če so se v njih pojavili glodavci oziroma smo opazili njihove iztrebke, dobro prezračimo prostore (zračimo vsaj 30 min),
- v času prezračevanja se ljudje odstranijo iz prostora,
- medtem se pripravi raztopina klorovega razkužila, kjer se enoto razkužila npr. varikine, zmeša z 10 enotami vode; ob uporabi že pripravljenega razkužila, je potrebno upoštevati navodila proizvajalca,
- pri čiščenju uporabimo gumijaste rokavice, maske, obleke z dolgimi rokavi in hlačnicami,
- površine, kontaminirane z iztrebki glodavcev, je potrebno dezinficirati (dobro poškropiti) z raztopino dezinfekcijskega sredstva (minimalni čas delovanja razkužila je 5 minut),
- razkužene iztrebke ali mrtve glodavce poberemo s papirnato brisačo, ki jo nato odvržemo v smeti), mrtve glodavce zakopljemo v zemljo in posujmo z apnom,
- po odstranitvi poginulih glodavcev in iztrebkov priporočamo razkuževanje ostalih površin in predmetov, ki so lahko onesnaženi z iztrebki in zato okuženi, nato je priporočljivo mehanično mokro čiščenje s krpo in raztopino detergenta (odsvetuje se pometanje ali sesanje),
- kolikor je mogoče, se izogibamo vdihavanja prahu pri čiščenju površin, ki bi lahko bile kontaminirane z iztrebki glodavcev,
- po čiščenju dobro operemo in razkužimo čistilne pripomočke, preden jih snamemo, speremo in razkužimo tudi rokavice, ki jih odvržemo med splošne komunalne odpadke,
- po čiščenju si temeljito umijemo roke s toplo vodo in milom.
V naravi:
- če v naravi opazimo sledove, iztrebke glodavcev, se na teh mestih, če je možno, ne zadržujemo, ne postavljamo šotorov, izvajamo športnih aktivnosti ipd.
Zatiranje glodavcev:
- potrebno je sistematično zatiranje glodavcev in njihovo varno odstranjevanje; mrtvih glodavcev se ne dotikamo z rokami,
- v primeru najdbe velikega števila poginulih miši v prostorih, kjer se nahajajo živina (hlevi), je o tem potrebno obvestiti pristojnega veterinarja.

ATTIC INSULATION Heat rises, and 25% escapes through the roof and attic. [3] It is not difficult to protect the attic with 300 mm of insulation material.
WINDOWS WITH DOUBLE OR TRIPLE GLAZING Approximately 10% of heat is lost through windows. [3] This can be prevented with high-quality window glazing. Triple-glazed windows are not significantly more expensive than double-glazed windows, but they are much more effective.
THERMAL INSULATION OF WALLS 35% of heat is lost through the walls. [3] Walls can be insulated from the outside or inside with insulation panels. [3]
THERMAL INSULATION OF FLOORS 15% of heat is lost where the building comes into contact with the ground. Proper floor insulation can prevent this. [3]
VENTILATION Air conditioning can be replaced with passive measures, such as opening windows in the morning and keeping them closed and shaded during the day.
THERMAL PROTECTION OF PIPES AND HOT WATER HEATERS Water heaters store hot water at 65°C. With inadequate thermal protection, a lot of heat can be lost, even in pipes and radiators.
PROTECTION AGAINST DRAFTS Air circulation throughout the building accounts for 15% of heat loss. [3] This can be easily prevented by using protective strips around doors and window frames.
INEFFICIENT VENTILATION PUMPS Using smart ventilation that turns off when ventilation is not needed can save a lot of energy. These pumps can account for approximately one-fifth of a household's energy bill. [7]
MODERN GAS OR BIOMASS BOILERS Condensing gas boilers achieve more than 90% efficiency due to two heat exchangers. [4] The average lifespan of a boiler is 15 years, so it is important to choose the most efficient model when purchasing and to have it regularly serviced during use. [5] Heat control means that the system can provide heat when and where it is needed.
The latest generation of wood biomass boilers is very efficient, as it allows for clean combustion, complete automation, and savings in time and money. In addition, these boilers use a sustainable renewable source, not fuel oil or gas. [6]

VERY EFFICIENT HOUSEHOLD APPLIANCES Household appliances, such as washing machines and dishwashers, available on the market vary in efficiency, from class A to G within the EU energy labeling scheme. In the EU, buildings consume 40% of energy and produce 36% of greenhouse gas emissions. [1]
Our homes come in different shapes, sizes, and ages, from single-family homes to multi-story buildings. However, almost all of them consume a lot of energy, making them expensive to maintain.
Rising costs and the increasing age of homes mean that more and more people will have difficulty paying their energy bills.

We use energy in our homes for various purposes: from heating and cooling to preparing hot water, electricity for lighting, appliances, and household items. However, there are many measures to use energy more efficiently, which can reduce energy consumption in homes.

Thousands of years ago, our ancestors, who were sailors, used wind to cross oceans in boats.

Scientists have long understood exactly how winds are formed.
Although air seems transparent, it is actually made up of billions of tiny particles.
There are many different types of particles, but most are made up of nitrogen and oxygen, gases that humans and other animals use to breathe.
Wind is created when these air particles move in the Earth's atmosphere.
The atmosphere is a gaseous envelope that covers the Earth's surface. It is about 100 km thick.
Most of the particles that make up the Earth's atmosphere are concentrated near the surface.
The higher you go, the fewer air particles there are, until eventually there are none left in space.
The weight of all these air particles that accumulate in the atmosphere presses down on the Earth's surface.
This is known as air pressure.
Air pressure changes depending on how warm or cold the Earth's surface is.
When the ground heats up, the air above it also heats up.
And when air heats up, it expands, the particles move further apart from each other, and move upwards and outwards.
When this happens, the space above the ground cools down because it is filled with only a few particles, so the air pressure is low.
So, the air in a warm and hot place, such as a desert, has lower air pressure than in a cold and dark place, such as the pole.

The movement of these air particles is driven by warm and cold areas, and this is what causes wind.

Knowledge for Better Health
Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS) (Mouse Fever)
In 1951, soldiers of the United Nations stationed in Korea also encountered the disease. The virus was named after the Hantaan River, which flows between North and South Korea, where infected mice were caught.
Another milestone was the outbreak of the disease among Native Americans in the Four Corners area of the United States in 1993, where the disease was caused by a hantavirus called Sin Nombre, which is much more fatal to humans. Unlike the viruses present in the Old World, whose target organ is the kidneys, this virus affects the lungs and the cardiovascular system. Due to impaired breathing, the mortality rate is as high as 60 percent. This disease is called hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS).
In our country, the disease is also called mouse fever.
Causative Agent
It is caused by RNA viruses of the genus Hanta, which belong to the family Bunyaviridae.
More than 25 antigenically different viral species are known. The disease in humans is mainly caused by the Hantaan, Seoul, Puumala, and Dobrava viruses.
In Slovenia, the disease is mainly caused by the Puumala and Dobrava viruses.
Incubation Period
The time from infection to the onset of disease symptoms is usually 2 to 4 weeks, but can range from a few days to two months.
Mode of Transmission
The causative agent circulates in natural foci, mainly among rodents such as mice, voles, and rats, which are chronic carriers. An increased number of cases is usually associated with an increased number of mice and similar rodents.
Humans are accidental hosts of the virus. It is assumed that the disease is transmitted from rodents to humans by inhaling viruses found in particles of rodent excreta (urine, feces, saliva). These excreta contaminate food, water, and the environment.
Susceptibility to Infection
The disease usually occurs in the spring, summer, and autumn months, when people spend more time outdoors or work in the fields and forests.
It is often associated with gardening, fieldwork, outdoor activities such as camping and swimming, especially in natural swimming areas, recreation, or cleaning places where there are visible traces or excrement of rodents. The disease is more common in rural areas, as well as in cities, where rodents contaminate objects and food in basements and warehouses with their excrement.
Symptoms and Signs of the Disease
The disease progresses in several phases.
The disease symptoms are partly dependent on the type of virus that caused the infection.
In the first phase, which lasts for a few days, there is mainly high fever, chills, severe headache, and severe pain in the lower back and abdomen. There is pain when moving the eyeballs, the conjunctiva is severely reddened, and the patient's face is red, as if sunburned. In milder forms, the disease also ends in this phase and recovery occurs without consequences.
In severe cases of the disease, after a few days of high fever, a hypotensive phase occurs, when there is a sudden drop in blood pressure. The patient becomes restless, and there are disturbances of consciousness, convulsions, and bleeding in the skin and mucous membranes.
This period is followed by a period in which the signs of kidney failure predominate (modest urine output, presence of protein and blood in the urine). In this period, there is also a high tendency to bleed. This period lasts for a few days, but the patient can also die in this phase.
The mortality rate of the disease is 5 to 15 percent.
The onset of increased urine output (polyuria) indicates the period of recovery. This period can last for several weeks or months and ends with complete recovery.
The most severe forms are usually caused by the Hantaan virus, while the Dobrava and Puumala viruses cause milder forms of the disease.
Infectiousness
The disease is not transmitted from person to person.
