Schools and Imperial, National, and Transnational Identifications: The Habsburg Monarchy, Yugoslavia, and Slovenia – A Foundational Project

Project Leader: Dr. Jovana Mihajlović Trbovc, ZRCD
Co-Researchers: Vita Zalar, Marko Zajc, PhD, Assist. Prof. Tamara Pavasović Trošt, Karin Almasy, PhD, Assist. Prof. Jernej Kosi

Project Code: ARRS J6-2573
Duration: September 1, 2020 – August 31, 2023
Leading Partner: –
Project Leader: –
Funding Source: Slovenian Research and Innovation Agency

Partners: Institute for Contemporary History, Faculty of Economics, University of Ljubljana
Schools and Nations
Universal compulsory primary education creates nations; without schools, they cannot exist! The fact is that mass schooling is perhaps the most important and successful strategy for nation-building.
Schools can intentionally promote a specific national or transnational identification, but at the same time, through their structure and operation, they can also help create and reproduce another national identity. For example, at the level of ideology, schools can promote a non-national imperial patriotism or a supra-national multicultural patriotism, while by dividing students into ethnolinguistic categories and/or using such categories in textbooks and teaching, they actually produce particular national divisions.
Why the Slovenian case?
Until recently, historiography explained the emergence of the Slovenian nation as a quasi-natural consequence of the prior existence of a Slovenian ethnic/linguistic community. However, recent reinterpretations, influenced by modernist approaches to nationalism and new research on Habsburg nationalisms, have convincingly shown that the idea of the Slovenian nation only emerged at the turn of the 19th century and that there was no Slovenian ethnic community before that.
Therefore, a new analysis of the circumstances and actors that enabled the emergence and evolution of the Slovenian nation is needed! The role of nationalists and their organizations cannot, of course, be overlooked and needs to be further investigated, but a few studies have already pointed out that the states in which the Slovenian nation emerged and was reproduced contributed to the establishment and consolidation of ethnolinguistic nationalism – often unintentionally, and sometimes even contrary to their goals.
Therefore, schools need to be re-examined. Their importance for the operation of nation-building states has been known at least since the classic study by Eugen Weber, *Peasants into Frenchmen*. However, their role in states that did not define themselves as national and did not want to nationalize the population has been much less researched in this context. However, we can assume that education was also extremely important here.
Project Goals
The goal of the proposed research project is to analyze to what extent the emergence of the Slovenian nation and its continued existence is a consequence of different national classifications in primary education. The project aims to achieve this goal by analyzing both school ideology and everyday practice over three centuries and in three states: the Habsburg Monarchy, Yugoslavia, and Slovenia.
These are, of course, very different state formations, but in the last two centuries, they have alternated in the role of (super)state framework in which Slovenian nationalism emerged and developed. The analysis of this process in the *longue durée* is one of the central features of the project. It will enable a comparative approach, in which different classifications will be observed and different policies will be compared in relation to their use and promotion.
While the research project will focus on the territory of present-day Slovenia, it promises a new understanding of the role of primary schools – and classifications in general – in establishing nations as relevant and enduring identification categories. This will have broader significance and can be applied to comparable cases.
In the first phase (months 1-2), which will begin with an introductory meeting, the team members will identify their case studies, review relevant secondary literature, and enter it into a bibliographic database.
In the second phase (months 3-16), primary sources will be collected in archives, libraries, and school museums. Public domain sources will be scanned and published on the SIstory online portal. To facilitate analytical consistency, team members will continue to develop a common set of research questions. At the end of the second phase, we will organize the first workshop, to which we will invite members of the advisory board and other external experts to more precisely define the research questions.
In the third phase (months 17-32), team members will analyze and interpret their case studies, using a common set of research questions to ensure comparability of interpretations.
In the fourth phase (months 33-36), team members will discuss and evaluate their work, develop comparable conclusions, and improve interpretations for the publication of results in a collective monograph. A second workshop, which will again include members of the advisory board and other external experts, will help the team members optimize the results.

Šole in narodi
Splošno obvezno osnovno izobraževanje ustvarja narode; brez šol ti ne morejo obstajati! Dejstvo je, je množično šolanje morda najbolj pomembna in uspešna strategija izgradnje naroda
Šole lahko namenoma propagirajo določeno narodno ali transnacionalno identifikacijo, a hkrati lahko s svojo strukturo in delovanjem pomagajo ustvariti in reproducirati tudi neko drugo nacionalno. Na primer: na nivoju ideologije lahko šole propagirajo ne-narodni imperialni patriotizem ali nad-narodni večkulturni patriotizem, medtem ko z delitvijo učencev v etnolingvistične kategorije in/ali z uporabo takih kategorij v učbenikih in pri pouku dejansko proizvajajo partikularne nacionalne delitve.
Zakaj slovenski primer?
Do nedavnega je zgodovinopisje nastanek slovenskega naroda razlagalo kot kvazinaravno posledico predhodnega obstoja slovenske etnične/jezikovne skupnosti. Toda nedavne reinterpretacije, nastale pod vplivom modernističnih pristopov k nacionalizmu in novih raziskav habsburških nacionalizmov, so prepričljivo pokazale, da se je ideja slovenskega naroda pojavila šele na prelomu 19. stoletja in da pred tem ni bilo slovenske etnične skupnosti.
Zato je potrebna nova analiza okoliščin in akterjev, ki so omogočili nastanek in evolucijo slovenskega naroda! Vloge nacionalistov in njihovih organizacij seveda ni mogoče spregledati in jo je potrebno še naprej raziskovati, toda peščica študij je že opozorila, da so države, v katerih je nastajal in se reproduciral slovenski narod, prispevale k vzpostavljanju in utrjevanju etnolingvističnega nacionalizma – pogosto nenačrtno, včasih pa tudi v nasprotju s svojimi cilji.
Zato si je šole potrebno ponovno ogledati. Njihov pomen za delovanje nacionalizirajočih držav je sicer znan vsaj od klasične študije Eugena Webra Peasants into Frenchmen. Bistveno manj je sicer v tem kontekstu raziskana njihova vloga v državah, ki se niso definirale kot nacionalne in niso želele nacionalizirati prebivalstva. Toda domnevamo lahko, da je bil tudi tu šolstvo izredno pomembno.
Cilji projekta
Cilj predlaganega raziskovalnega projekta je, da analizira koliko je nastanek slovenskega naroda in njegov nadaljnji obstoj posledica različnih nacionalnih klasifikacij v osnovnem šolstvu. Ta cilj želi projekt doseči z analizo tako šolske ideologije kot vsakodnevne prakse v treh stoletjih in treh državah: Habsburški monarhiji, Jugoslaviji in Sloveniji.
To so seveda zelo različne državne tvorbe, a so se vendar v zadnjih dveh stoletjih izmenjale v vlogi (nad)državnega okvirja v katerem je nastal in se razvijal slovenski nacionalizem. Analiza tega procesa v longue durée je ena osrednjih značilnosti projekta. Omogočila bo primerjalni pristop, v katerem bodo opazovane različne klasifikacije in primerjane različne politike v zvezi z njihovo uporabo in promocijo.
Medtem ko se bo raziskovalni projekt osredotočil na ozemlje današnje Slovenije, obeta novega razumevanja vloge osnovnih šol – in klasifikacij na splošno – pri uveljavitvi narodov kot relevantnih in obstojnih identifikacijskih kategorij. To bo imelo širši pomen in se bo lahko uporabilo za primerljive primere.
V prvi fazi (meseci 1-2), ki se bo začela z uvodnim sestankom, bodo člani skupine identificirali svoje študije primerov, pregledali ustrezno sekundarno literaturo in jo vnesli v bibliografsko podatkovno zbirko.
V drugi fazi (meseci 3-16) bo potekalo zbiranje primarnih virov v arhivih, knjižnicah in šolskih muzejih. Viri v javni lasti bodo skenirani in objavljeni na spletnem portalu SIstory. Da bi olajšali analitično skladnost, bodo člani skupine še naprej razvijali skupni sklop raziskovalnih vprašanj. Ob koncu druge faze bomo organizirali prvo delavnico, na katero bomo povabili člane svetovalnega odbora in druge zunanje strokovnjake, da bi natančneje definirali raziskovalna vprašanje.
V tretji fazi (meseci 17-32) bodo člani skupine analizirali in interpretirali svoje študije primerov, pri čemer bodo uporabili skupni sklop raziskovalnih vprašanj in s tem zagotovili primerljivost razlag.
V četrti fazi (meseci 33-36) bodo člani skupine razpravljali o svojem delu in ga ocenjevali, izdelali primerljive sklepe in izboljšali interpretacije za objavo rezultatov v skupinski monografiji. Druga delavnica, ki bo ponovno vključevala člane svetovalnega odbora in druge zunanje strokovnjake, bo pomagala članom ekipe optimizirati rezultatov.

What is learning:
Learning is a phenomenon or method associated with the act or effect of learning. Learning establishes connections between specific stimuli and equivalent responses, which leads to an increase in an organism's adaptation to its environment.
As a phenomenon that is part of pedagogy, learning is a change in an individual's behavior as a function of experience. School learning is characterized by its systematic and intentional nature and the organization of activities (stimuli) that trigger it, activities that are part of a framework of goals and requirements defined by the educational institution.
Psychological research on learning and the resulting theories have greatly influenced pedagogy, contributing to the decline of traditional teaching. The central point of the teaching and learning process has become the student's activity as a means of their learning, thereby ceasing to be a passive recipient of the teacher's instruction.
Learning difficulties are also a consequence of poor school performance, as they result from psychological or socio-cultural factors. Sensory and physical (visual, auditory, motor) deficits and physiological disorders cause specific types of learning difficulties.
In the field of ethology, learning is the fixation in memory of environmental impressions. It is based on a change in the mechanisms of the central nervous system, which later influence patterns of behavior.
The possibility or organization of learning depends on the degree of development of these mechanisms and depends on the number of available neurons. Almost all animals can learn. In animals with small brains, most neurons are used in establishing inherited automatic circuits, and only a few are available for learning. On the other hand, in animals with large brains (e.g., mammals), the number of neurons is sufficient to allow the formation of new circuits, which enables learning.

Learning and Development
Jean Piaget presented a distinction between learning and development, stating that many people confuse these two concepts. According to the Swiss epistemologist, development is related not only to physical development but also to the nervous system and mental functions, which are related to embryogenesis and knowledge structures. The concept of learning is simpler because it occurs through an intermediary (teacher), which is a process limited to a simpler structure than development.

Meaningful Learning
Meaningful learning is an important concept in learning theory, presented by David Ausubel. According to the American educational psychologist, meaningful learning means that new content learned by a student is organized and forms a hierarchy of concepts and relates to knowledge that the student has previously internalized.

Organizational Learning
Organizational learning consists of the learning absorbed by an organization, that is, the knowledge that enables a company to create practices that will help achieve desired results. The learning of knowledge, values, and skills can occur within or outside the organizational context, directly or indirectly, and contributes to the success of the organization.

Motor Learning
Motor learning occurs when certain cognitive processes are linked to practice and cause a lasting change in an individual's motor behavior.

Kaj je učenje:
Učenje je pojav ali metoda, povezana z dejanjem ali učinkom učenja . Učenje vzpostavlja povezave med določenimi dražljaji in enakovrednimi odzivi, kar povzroča povečanje prilagajanja živega bitja njegovi okolici.
Kot fenomen, ki je del pedagogike, je učenje sprememba obnašanja posameznika v funkciji izkušnje. Šolsko učenje se odlikuje po sistematičnem in namernem značaju in organizaciji aktivnosti (dražljajev), ki ga sprožijo, dejavnosti, ki so del okvira ciljev in zahtev, ki jih določi šolska ustanova.
Psihološke raziskave o učenju in nastale teorije so močno vplivale na pedagogiko, kar je prispevalo k upadanju tradicionalnega poučevanja. Osrednja točka procesa poučevanja in učenja je postala učenčeva dejavnost kot sredstvo njegovega učenja, s čimer je prenehala biti pasivni učitelj poučevanja učitelja.
Težave pri učenju so prav tako posledica slabega šolskega delovanja, saj so posledica psiholoških ali družbeno-kulturnih dejavnikov. Senzorični in fizični (vizualni, slušni, motorični) deficiti in fiziološke motnje povzročajo posebne vrste učnih težav.
Na področju etologije je učenje fiksacija na spomin okoljskih vtisov. Temelji na spremembi mehanizmov centralnega živčnega sistema, ki kasneje vplivajo na vzorce ravnanja.
Možnost ali ureditev učenja je odvisna od stopnje razvoja teh mehanizmov in je odvisna od števila razpoložljivih nevronov. Skoraj vse živali se lahko učijo. Pri živalih z majhnimi možgani se večina nevronov uporablja pri vzpostavljanju podedovanih avtomatskih vezij in le malo jih je na voljo za učenje. Po drugi strani pa je pri velikih možganskih živalih (na primer pri sesalcih) število nevronov zadostno, da omogoči nastanek novih vezij, kar omogoča učenje.
Učenje in razvoj
Jean Piaget je predstavil razliko med učenjem in razvojem, pri čemer je dejal, da mnogi ljudje zamenjujejo ta dva pojma. Po mnenju švicarskega epistemologa je razvoj povezan ne samo s fizičnim razvojem, ampak se nanaša tudi na živčni sistem in duševne funkcije, ki so povezane z embriogenezo in strukturami znanja. Koncept učenja je enostavnejši, ker se dogaja prek posrednika (učitelja), ki je proces, omejen na enostavnejšo strukturo kot razvoj.
Znatno učenje
Smiselno učenje je pomemben koncept v teoriji učenja, ki ga je predstavil David Ausubel. Po mnenju ameriškega izobraževalnega psihologa smiselno učenje pomeni, da so nove vsebine, ki jih je študent naučil, organizirane in tvorijo hierarhijo konceptov, in se nanašajo na znanje, ki ga je študent predhodno ponotranjil.
Organizacijsko učenje
Organizacijsko učenje je sestavljeno iz učenja, ki ga absorbira organizacija, to je znanje, ki podjetju omogoča ustvarjanje praks, ki bodo pomagale doseči želene rezultate. Učenje znanja, vrednot in spretnosti se lahko zgodi znotraj ali zunaj organizacijskega konteksta, neposredno ali posredno, in prispeva k uspehu organizacije.
Motorno učenje
Motorično učenje se zgodi, ko so določeni kognitivni procesi povezani s prakso vožnje in povzročajo stalno spremembo motoričnega vedenja posameznika.

Summer - long-awaited by many, but in the summer months there are situations where danger, at best, allows for fear afterwards, and at worst leads to death; drowning, in reality, is one of these situations. First aid for drowning provided immediately and correctly can save a life, and doing so, as you might guess, is not an exaggeration.
A man drowns: what happens to him?
At the moment a person drowns, water rushes through the upper airways, leading to the expulsion of air. Therefore, the first event in a drowning person is laryngospasm, a spasm of the folds in the vocal area, which due to the closure of the airway by the trachea simultaneously stops breathing. This type of choking is defined as "dry choking."
With too prolonged searching for the victim in the water and when a significant amount of liquid enters the airways, oxygen starvation occurs. This in turn leads to the shutdown of the key reflex action that operates in this case to stop breathing, so the drowning person simply "breathes" water, which then manifests in their lungs. Lack of first aid for drowning before rescuers arrive on the scene can cause the death of the victim.
The difference between sea water and fresh water
Of course, this means that the side does not matter. So, if more than one liter of water enters the human body, it causes disruption to many of its functions, which is important depending on the type of water involved.
If it is fresh water intake, it enters the blood. This in turn leads to changes in its composition, which is reflected particularly in the amount of proteins and salts. On the other hand, this leads to trembling of the heart chambers, a kind of "breakdown" of red blood cells.
When sea water collects in the lungs, blood plasma is already in the pulmonary alveoli with subsequent accumulation there. Over time, this leads to pulmonary edema.
Or, that water was in the body, its presence in such manifestations negatively affects the victim and is dangerous to their life.
With strong overheating in the sun, overeating, fatigue should refrain from swimming for some time. The fact is that jumping into cold water can lead to so-called reflex cardiac arrest, which can cause sudden death.
First aid for drowning
The main goal of providing first aid is to pull the victim out of the water and call an "ambulance." The procedure for drowning should be limited to the following, and as you can see, they are not exclusively measures of a medical nature:
- Call an "ambulance" upon seeing a person drowning.
- Evaluate your own ability regarding whether you have enough of your own strength to reach the victim, and whether you have enough to bring them back to shore. If in doubt, you should not make attempts to save the drowning man, otherwise you may need to be rescued yourself.
- Saving a drowning person makes it impossible to immediately jump into a pond unknown to you. The rescuer should not risk their own life. Enter the water slowly. In the case of such a condition on a river, try to have a long thread or rope, the other end of which should be held by an assistant on the shore. If possible, determine in advance where it is best to pull the victim onto the land.
- If you have found the drowning person conscious, you will need to calm them down, keeping some distance – a person all panicked, by chance, obeys the instinct of self-preservation, drowns along the bottom, and those who try to save them.
- Next, embrace the drowning man so that they do not interfere with your movements and do not hold your arms and legs. To do this, you need to pick them up under the armpits and turn them back to you – so it will be convenient to swim to shore. The only thing you need to take care of – the position of the victim's head above water.
- In case of cessation of breathing, you need to give the victim several air breaths while on the water (this is done only if you are already in shallow water and have the opportunity to stand up – every minute is important, so waiting to hit the shore is not necessary) – point "a" below.
- Have a look at the victim. An important step is the release of water and mud from the mouth, with a finger injected into the mouth, pre-wrapped in cloth (item "b"). With strong compression of the cavity refusing its need, use a solid object.
- Then you will need to turn the victim's stomach down and lay them on your knees so that their head hangs down. With this you will remove the water. The action involves the rescuer pressing on the ribs and back of the victim (point "C").
- Next is artificial respiration. For this, pinch the victim's nose, take a breath, and inject air into the mouth (point "G"). In this case, the chest fills with air, after which the victim can breathe.
- Artificial respiration should be performed up to 18 times per minute or once every 4 seconds. First aid measures in drowning
- When the heartbeat is missing, respirator actions should be combined with indirect cardiac massage. The surface on which the victim is placed should be firm, and you will need to take a position to the left of them. Then their hands should be clasped together at the heart of the victim, carrying out heavy pushes (50-60 per min.). In a combined approach in conjunction with CPR, approximately 5 clicks are performed on the heart area, then – inhaling air into the lungs.
- When you return the victim, continue to provide assistance, "quickly," because it may be needed in order not to exclude the danger of recurrent cardiac arrest.
- Warm the patient. If possible, wrap them in a blanket, give sweet warm tea.
- Also indicated for use in this situation are preparations for respiration (caffeine or camphor subcutaneously, ammonia high to the nose).

Moški utopi: kaj se dogaja z njim?
V trenutku, ko oseba utopi, je more vdreti voda skozi zgornje dihalne poti, kar vodi k njej izgonu zraku. Zato je prvi dogodek v laringospazem se utaplja, da krč gubami področju vokalne, zaradi zaprtja ceste s sapnikom hkrati ustavi dihanje. Ta vrsta zahlynannya opredeljena kot "suhi zahlynannya."

In the West, where a left-wing cultural hegemony prevails, the mainstream conservative camp, having lost the cultural battle, desperately tries to maintain itself. It attempts to do so by ideologically aligning itself with liberalism, thereby becoming a milder parody of itself and offering the population a false alternative to cultural Marxism.

Civic nationalism, also known as civil nationalism, is a version of nationalism that believes in traditional liberal ideas such as freedom, tolerance, equality, and human rights. In practice, civic nationalists take a lukewarm stance against LGBT and similar lobbies, rejecting only their most radical ideas. They are primarily known for advocating for migration to Western countries, provided that the migrants – regardless of their origin – are willing to assimilate. In doing so, they deny the diversity of peoples and thus embody the main left-wing ideas of universalism and egalitarianism. They support legal migration, which represents a poor compromise between liberals and the majority white population, which is increasingly becoming a victim of the consequences of the Great Replacement. The process of replacing whites in their homelands is acceptable to them only if it is done legally; the origin of the person is not important, only their passport. According to them, a document can turn an African from a resident of the Third World into an immigrant who successfully integrates into Western society and "enriches" it.

The myth of "racial equality"
Following the rise of the New Left and its critical race theory, cultural Marxists are trying to imply equality in all aspects of social life. They advocate the belief that humanity is monolithic, and that races exist only for racists who attack helpless minorities. They deny that there are different cognitive abilities between races, such as intelligence, and in doing so, they create discrimination that they supposedly try to prevent. The average IQ between white and black Americans differs by 25 points, and in a system created by whites, unintentional discrimination is inevitable. Like civic nationalists, liberals try to include black people in the system by imposing equality, and they blame whites and alleged systemic racism for any failure. Race is the foundation of every civilization, as the collective subconscious dictates certain guidelines in culture, perception of the world, and behavior for related peoples. Western civilization is a product of the white race, and only it can preserve it, which requires a majority white population in the West. Most mainstream moderate right-wingers do not want to recognize the important role that race plays in everyday life, as they have succumbed to left-wing dogmas about "universal humanity," and they are unable to correct the damage that has been done.

Civic nationalism is too weak to defend the West
The failed concept of civic nationalism claims that a diverse society, united by an abstract idea, can be more stable than one based on common ancestry. It argues that immigrants from the Middle East and Africa can coexist with the natives if they adopt liberal ideas and abandon their ethnic interests. They are convinced that anyone can become an American or European, as we are all ultimately migrants seeking opportunities for a better life. In their view, Western civilization has progressed by chance, and immigrants from Third World countries can easily integrate into society, manage it, and preserve it, as long as they value the same values. However, the purpose of foreigners who come to the West is precisely to replace and re-evaluate European traditions. Migration of pluralistic foreigners has so polarized Western societies that they are collapsing before our eyes. The strongest societies are connected by blood and soil, whose boundaries were drawn by the deaths of their ancestors. Ethnic nationalism is the only option that can defend the ethnic and racial integrity of Europeans, as it recognizes the natural diversity and conditions for the preservation of each nation. True nationalism advocates for the preservation of the culture of each nation and its majority in their homelands, regardless of their origin and beliefs. Unlike liberals, who see their ideology as superior and a moral excess that they believe they have the right to impose on everyone.

The degradation of people into commodities
Civic nationalists and most of today's right-wingers advocate for capitalist open markets, and concern for the nation is of secondary importance to them, as they see individuals only as profitable consumers. Desacralization is one of the main characteristics of liberalism, which they have adopted from other "marketing" right-wingers. Migration from poor or overpopulated countries to less vital but richer countries is, for them, an economic solution and an effective response to the aging European population. This is also a symbolic act, in which, after the destruction of original traditions, Western Europe commits ethnic suicide for the benefit of a materialistic industrialized system. One of the main thinkers of the New Right, Alain de Benoist, points out this problem, and he does not see the responsibility in the migrants, but in the industrialized nations of Europe, which, with similar plutocratic quasi-right-wingers at the helm, are the main culprits for the current situation. The relocation of nations is not in the interest of either the immigrants, who were forced to leave their homelands, or the indigenous population, who are facing changes in their societies. If this trend continues, it is possible to expect a conflict that will leave lasting negative consequences in European countries.

Opposition to the exploitation of the West
The war that cultural Marxists have declared against European tradition and its people needs a strong opposition that is capable of responding to all left-wing attacks and is immune to their vocabulary. With the liberalization of the right, it no longer represents the interests of Westerners, but merely postpones their decline for a few years. In America, Republicans have developed interesting responses to Democrats' accusations of racism and homophobia, accusing liberals of "true racism" and choosing a transgender person as their party mascot. "Right-wing" ideas were defended by homosexuals and immigrants at various American debates, while true nationalists began to be accused of discrimination and were excluded from their campaign. As an opposition to the left-wing support for Palestine, Republicans strongly support Israel and send it large sums of money, which is a constant among all right-wing parties. In the EU, the most obvious example of the liberal "right" is the EPP, which excludes parties with true nationalist programs and increasingly leans towards the left. Europe needs a true right-wing renaissance and a renewed commitment to views based on ancient European traditions, which will allow for the continued existence of the entire European ethnicity. The false civic nationalism, which is based on liberal values, must be replaced by true ethnic nationalism, which is based on blood, the unbroken bond between us and our ancestors.

Na Zahodu, kjer dominira levičarska kulturna hegemonija, se »mainstream« konservativni pol po izgubljenem kulturnem boju brezupno poskuša ohraniti. To poskuša doseči z ideološkim približevanjem liberalizmu, s čimer postaja njegova milejša parodija, prebivalcem pa ponuja lažno alternativo proti kulturnemu marksizmu.
Civilni nacionalizem, imenovan tudi državljanski nacionalizem, je različica nacionalizma, ki verjame v tradicionalne liberalne ideje, kot so svoboda, strpnost, enakost in človekove pravice. Civilni nacionalisti v praksi mlačno nastopajo proti LGBT in podobnih lobijih, s tem, ko zavračajo le njihove najradikalnejše ideje. Znani so predvsem po tem, da zagovarjajo migracije v zahodne države, če so se migranti –ne glede na to od kod so – pripravljeni asimilirati. Tako zanikajo raznolikost ljudstev in s tem poosebljajo glavni levičarski ideji univerzalizma in egalitarizma. Podpirajo legalne migracije, ki predstavljajo slab kompromis med liberalci in večinskim belim prebivalstvom, ki postaja vse večja žrtev posledic velike zamenjave. Proces zamenjave belcev v njihovih domovinah je zanje sprejemljiv le, »če se izvaja legalno,« pomemben pa ni izvor osebe, ampak le njegov potni list. Dokument, po njihovem mnenju lahko Afričana iz prebivalca tretjega sveta naredi v priseljenca, ki se uspešno vključi v zahodno družbo in jo »obogati«.
Mit o »rasni enakosti«
Po vzponu nove levice in njene kritične rasne teorije kulturni marksisti poskušajo enakost implicirati v vse vidike družbenega življenja. Ti zagovarjajo prepričanje, da je človeštvo monolitno, rase pa obstajajo le za rasiste, ki napadajo nemočne manjšine. Zanikajo, da med rasami obstajajo različne kognitivne sposobnosti npr. inteligenca, s tem pa sami ustvarjajo diskriminacijo, ki jo domnevno poskušajo preprečiti. Inteligenčni kvocient med belimi in temnopoltimi Američani se v povprečju razlikuje za 25 točk, v sistemu, ki so ga ustvarili belci, pa je nenamerna diskriminacija neizogibna. Liberalci, tako kot civilni nacionalisti, z vsiljevanjem enakosti temnopolte poskušajo vključiti v sistem, za neuspeh pa krivijo belce in domnevni sistemski rasizem. Rasa predstavlja temelj vsake civilizacije, saj kolektivna podzavest sorodnim narodom narekuje določene smernice v kulturi, dojemanju sveta in obnašanju. Zahodna civilizacija je produkt bele rase in le ta jo lahko ohrani, za to pa je na Zahodu treba zagotoviti večinsko belo prebivalstvo. Večina »mainstream« zmernih desničarjev ne želi prepoznati pomembne vloge, ki jo rasa igra v vsakodnevnem življenju, saj so podlegli levičarskim dogmam o »univerzalnem človeštvu«, zaradi katerega storjene škode niso zmožni popraviti.
Civilni nacionalizem je prešibek za ubranitev Zahoda
Neuspeli koncept civilnega nacionalizma trdi, da je raznolika družba, poenotena z abstraktno idejo, lahko stabilnejša kot ta, ki temelji na skupnih prednikih. Zagovarja trditev, da priseljenci z Bližnjega vzhoda in Afrike lahko shajajo z domačini, če bodo sprejeli liberalne ideje ter opustili svoje etnične interese. Prepričani so, da Američan ali Evropejec postane vsak, saj smo vsi konec koncev migranti, ki iščemo možnosti za boljše življenje. Po njihovem mnenju je Zahodna civilizacija napredovala po naključju, priseljenci iz tretjih držav pa se zaradi tega lahko brez težav vključijo v družbo, z njo upravljajo in jo ohranijo, dokler cenijo iste vrednote. Namen tujcev, ki prihajajo na Zahod pa je ravno nadomestiti in prevrednotiti evropske tradicije. Migracije pluralnih tujcev so tako močno polarizirale zahodne družbe, ki propadajo pred našimi očmi. Najtrdnejše družbe so povezane s krvjo in zemljo, katere meje so zarisale smrti njihovih prednikov. Etnični nacionalizem je edina možnost, ki lahko ubrani etnično ter rasno integriteto Evropejcev, saj priznava naravne raznolikosti in pogoje za ohranitev vsakega naroda. Pravi nacionalizem zagovarja ohranitev kulture vsakega naroda in njegove večine v svojih domovinah, ne glede na njihovo poreklo in prepričanje. Za razliko od liberalcev, ki svojo ideologijo vidijo za superiorno in moralni presežek, ki ga imajo po njihovem prepričanju pravico vsiljevati vsem.

Humans are contributing to climate change through various activities, primarily by burning fossil fuels, raising livestock, and deforesting.
Burning fossil fuels, which provides us with transportation and energy, leads to the release of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. These gases amplify the greenhouse effect, leading to atmospheric warming, ice melting, rising sea levels, and increased evaporation. We then observe these effects in the form of an unstable atmosphere, an increased number of stronger storms and hurricanes, which are often devastating, and droughts.
Greenhouse gases have always been present in nature, but burning fossil fuels increases the emission of carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, and fluorinated gases into the atmosphere. The melting of ice at the North and South Poles further accelerates the release of methane, which is a greenhouse gas several times more harmful than carbon dioxide.
Carbon dioxide accounts for 63% of all global warming caused by human activity. There is approximately 40% more carbon dioxide in the atmosphere now than there was at the beginning of the industrial era.
Reason:
Greenhouse gas emissions result from burning oil, natural gas, and coal. This primarily releases carbon dioxide. Naturally, extensive forests (especially in the equatorial region) absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, but today, humans are intensively cutting them down. As a result, the emitted carbon dioxide cannot be captured and stored in wood structures. The cleared areas are often burned, further releasing carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, and monocultures are planted in place of the former forests, which significantly reduces biodiversity.
A third harmful impact is livestock farming. Large amounts of methane are produced as a byproduct of the metabolism of cattle raised for meat. The same applies to sheep farming.
Due to these and other reasons, the global average temperature of the atmosphere is almost one degree higher than it was at the end of the 19th century. Leading global experts have concluded that climate change is almost certainly the result of human activity and has been noticeable since the mid-20th century.
If the atmosphere continues to warm and global temperatures exceed pre-industrial levels by 2 degrees Celsius or more, we face catastrophic changes that will lead to severe and highly damaging disasters. As a result, millions of human lives will be threatened by events such as floods, hurricanes, droughts, and similar occurrences.

Farmers are concerned about the health of their livestock and water quality, as they often face challenges with wet and muddy pastures, which can lead to livestock diseases and environmental pollution. Establishing appropriate systems for feeding animals in colder periods (autumn, winter) is often a challenge in livestock farming, as the goal is to make feeding as easy as possible while protecting the pastures. This is especially important in wet and muddy conditions, as livestock can trample and compact the soil, damaging it. To prevent this, livestock are often restricted in their outdoor movement in various ways.
Traditional restrictions can be uncomfortable for animals in some cases and reduce the efficiency of farming. We are also increasingly assessing and emphasizing the impact of fertilizer use on the environment, as maintaining water quality is very important. The system usually involves a shallow excavation filled with a layer of stone aggregate containing a network of perforated drainage pipes, covered with a thick layer of wood chips (20-50cm).
With a wood chip base, a surface layer is created on demanding soils where livestock are concentrated, above the soil layer into which water drains. These types of systems have already been used on farms for beef and dairy cattle farming in Ireland, the United Kingdom, and New Zealand, and more recently in the United States. Compared to other systems for winter-fed livestock, the PVVS (Pasture Vegetation and Water System) improves livestock feed intake and increases their body weight.
The head of the research group for composites from renewable materials at InnoRenew CoE, Dr. David DeVallance, has joined forces with Dr. Joshua Faulkner from the University of Vermont Extension Center for Sustainable Agriculture in Burlington, USA, to study this area in more detail and introduce it to Slovenian farms.
"Manure and waste entering water systems affect all people due to water pollution," said Dr. DeVallance. "To ease this burden on people and animals, our research focuses on the potential for innovative, thermally modified wood chip systems as part of a biomass-produced surface for areas where livestock farming is common."
"Partnering with Dr. Faulkner and learning from his experience, as he is an agricultural engineer who works extensively with PVVS on farms, will greatly facilitate the development of wood chips with improved properties for more efficient PVVS," added Dr. DeVallance.
The materials used in the system are crucial for effective PVVS. Wood biomass (i.e., wood chips) and biochar are renewable materials used for drainage and soil modification. Wood chips and biochar perform different functions for soil quality, pollution reduction, and drainage. So far, only wood chips have been used in these types of PVVS.
Dr. DeVallance and Dr. Faulkner have previously researched new PVVS concepts from deciduous trees, biochar, and thermally modified wood in the literature, as well as on shorter field trips in the USA (Christianson et al., 2017; Faulkner et al., 2015). The Tasmanian tiger (scientific name: Thylacinus cynocephalus) is an extinct species of marsupial. It originally lived in Tasmania and New Guinea, but when sailors began exploring New Guinea, it was exterminated there, leaving it only in Tasmania until 1936, when it was also exterminated there.
Description[edit | edit source]
Descriptions of the Tasmanian tiger come from preserved specimens, fossil finds, skins, and skeletal remains, as well as black and white photographs. The Tasmanian tiger resembled a large, short-haired dog with tiger stripes and a kangaroo-like tail. An adult Tasmanian tiger was 100 to 130 cm long, with a tail about 50 to 65 cm long, stood 60 cm tall, and weighed 20 to 30 kg. Males were larger than females. Its yellowish-brown fur had 15 to 20 distinct dark stripes on its back, rump, and lower part of the tail, from which it got its name.
All known recordings of live Tasmanian tigers in Australia were taken at the Hobart Zoo in Tasmania in 1911, 1928, and 1933. Two other films are known, taken at the London Zoo.
Early scientific studies show that it had a keen sense of smell, which allowed it to track prey, but analysis of its brain structure showed that its sense of smell was not well developed. It probably relied on sight and hearing when hunting.
The Tasmanian tiger could open its jaws to an unusual extent: up to 80 degrees. This ability is partially visible in a short black and white film from captivity in 1933. The jaws were muscular and had 46 teeth, but studies show that its jaw was too weak to kill a sheep.

Parents unintentionally say words that hurt their children. We are not deliberately clumsy in our expressions, but we still cause harm. To avoid hurtful words, we need to adapt the language of adults, especially when addressing the youngest children.
Often, words slip out of our mouths too quickly. Children see and perceive things differently, so they also hear differently. The aforementioned phrases often cause stress in a child. It is better to listen to the child than to create a power game and punishment with apparent authority.
Conversation is always a beginning, a stepping stone to resolving a difficult situation. To start a conversation, we need to find the right words so that the child is willing to talk about what they are experiencing. We present six phrases that, according to psychotherapist and counselor Isabelle Filliozat, negatively affect a child.
1
You are impossible!
These words are very often spoken out of parental helplessness. Parents are stressed and lash out at the child. These words are extremely harsh and toxic. The child may freeze, lose muscle tone, and their entire body may become rigid. But in the next moment, the body awakens, and the child becomes aggressive. They will not attack the parents, but one of their siblings. Inappropriate behavior is a response to extreme stress.
2
Get out of my sight!
This is a very stressful form of exclusion for a child. The statement is doubly negative, meaning "when you are not good, I don't want you around." At the moment when the child needs their parents the most, they are told to be alone. Brain areas for stress are activated.
The younger the child, the greater their need for parental proximity to regulate themselves. Before the age of 13 or 14, a child is not able to control their emotions. When we verbalize a child's sadness by saying, "I see tears running down your cheeks," it is the words themselves that weave the self-regulation of the child's emotions.
3
You are mocking me!
The brain develops slowly after birth. A two- or three-year-old child does not hear the denial. For example, if we say, "Don't come into the house with muddy boots!" they will hear, "Come in with muddy boots!" They will look directly at the parent to see if they have responded appropriately to the instruction. From the moment we forbid a child to do something, there is a risk that the child will do exactly that.
Parents feel that they are taking control, but they instill a sense of fear and shame in the child without actually educating them. The relationship between cause and effect is not defined. The child will repeat the forbidden action until they master the situation of fear and shame.
4
Stop whining!
When a child is upset, we need to find the real cause or need. The child is communicating something. For example, when they persistently ask to watch a cartoon, it does not mean that they deeply desire it. In reality, they are asking for connection, a hug, to calm down, to allow the brain to calm down. Depending on the situation and the child's personality, we suggest a short break or outdoor play in such cases.
5
Sit down!
This is one of the most toxic words we can say to a child. Forcing them to sit puts them under maximum stress; it is not natural for them. The child needs movement, running, climbing trees to feel good and improve concentration in class. Movement requires attention.
The more we force a child to do tasks while sitting, the greater the stress they experience, along with all the associated problems. Everyone has their preferences; some children can work standing up and adjust the height of their desk.
Constant sitting is harmful to muscles, the abdomen, and the spine. The child needs to develop muscles for proper body tone and to reduce stress. This ensures healthy brain development and emotional regulation.
6
You are tiring me!
With these words, parents transfer their own emotional state to the child and transfer responsibility for their state to them. This is a major stress factor for the child. Instead of burdening them with our own fatigue, we can communicate our feelings through images, for example, with magnets on the refrigerator. A sun for days when everything is fine, a cloud for moments when we feel a little worse, and a lightning bolt for difficult days. The child is naturally empathetic and will understand the parents' feelings and respond accordingly.
This article is based on the original published by the French edition of Aleteia. Translated and adapted by Lucija Rifel.

Over the past 100 years, we have begun to release increasingly large amounts of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere through the use of fossil fuels (coal, oil, and natural gas). These gases, while necessary in limited quantities for the survival of life on Earth, are now present in excessive amounts. The most common are carbon dioxide (CO2), water vapor, nitrous oxide (N2O), and methane (CH4). Their concentration has increased significantly in recent decades, and the consequences are evident in the accelerating changes in the climate: rising temperatures, altered precipitation patterns, melting glaciers, and rising sea levels.

What is a carbon footprint?
The term "carbon footprint" refers to an estimate of the carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions for which an individual, company, or organization is responsible. Every product, raw material, and service has its own carbon footprint, from a loaf of bread to a smartphone.
The average Slovenian generates seven tons of CO2 per year, which is comparable to the European average. Housing, transportation, and food contribute the most to this.

What is a water footprint?
A water footprint aims to capture all the water we consume each day.
Direct water consumption includes drinking water, which we use from the water supply network. Data on water consumption in households shows that each Slovenian consumed an average of 104 liters of drinking water per day in 2017, which is 16 liters less than in 2007 (SURS 2019). If we consider all the water consumed from the water supply network in Slovenia, the consumption is significantly higher, at 162 liters per capita per day.

What is virtual water? When we buy a product in a store, we don't see the water, and we don't carry it home with us. This is all the invisible water that is used to produce or grow goods. The water used to grow, process, or manufacture food, clothing, paper, and other products is called "virtual water."

Water consumption also affects climate change. Collecting and pumping water requires energy, which is produced in power plants – and these largely use coal, gas, or oil, which means they emit carbon dioxide.

Smallpox is a particularly dangerous infectious disease. It has been known since ancient times. In the past, epidemics of smallpox claimed many lives. Every year, around 10 million people are infected in the European part of the continent. At the same time, the mortality rate reached 40% (and sometimes 80%).
Thanks to mass vaccination in the 20th century, smallpox was eradicated. Vaccinations against it have not been carried out for a long time, but caution regarding the disease remains even today. There are viral diseases that are genetically very close to this infection.
Clinical manifestations
From the moment the virus enters the human body until the first pathological symptoms appear, it takes from 5 to 24 days. The disease begins acutely and has a characteristic clinical picture, the main manifestations of which are:
- elevated body temperature (body temperature rises to 40 degrees and higher, it has a fluctuating course, the first wave is noticeable at the beginning of the disease, the second - during the rash);
- chills;
- nausea, vomiting;
- headache;
- prodromal rash in small spots (becomes noticeable in the first days of the disease and quickly disappears);
- true rash (appears on the 4th and 5th day of the disease after a period of imaginary improvement in the patient's condition, affects the skin of the face, chest, limbs, and mucous membranes, initially looks like vesicles with serous contents, but quickly become infected and turn into pustules, the pustules open on the 15th-17th day and are covered with crusts, which fall off after a few days, leaving rough scars).
The general condition of patients in the acute period of infection is severe. This is especially noticeable during the period of infection with a rash from osinic acid, which is accompanied by high fever, impaired consciousness, low blood pressure, shortness of breath, and tachycardia. After the opening of the pustular elements of the rash, the condition improves, and the body begins the processes of regeneration.
In some patients, osinic acid has an even more severe course. It is observed in the confluent and hemorrhagic forms of the disease:
- The first of these is characterized by severe intoxication and the presence of a large number of rashes, which merge in the period of suppuration. At the same time, there are hemorrhages and bleeding in various locations on the skin. However, death can also occur before the appearance of the rash with the development of toxic shock.
- The hemorrhagic form of smallpox is manifested by increased bleeding and soaking of the pustules with blood.
In the presence of partial immunity in the body, the disease has a mild course with a short-term increase in body temperature and individual elements of the rash, which do not merge or even without them.
Which doctor to contact
Smallpox is a particularly dangerous infection and requires not only treatment by specialists in infectious diseases but also observation of contacts, quarantine, sanitation, and disinfection. If smallpox is suspected, doctors must notify the Roszdravnadzor authorities or similar structures.
Conclusion
The prognosis for smallpox is serious, with a high probability of an unfavorable outcome. The disease can spread rapidly and cause epidemics. Therefore, even individual cases of smallpox can be dangerous.

Layers of mud read like a "history book"
Mud and dirt everywhere, but also a silver lining. The layer of mud that covered the fields and floodplains, in some places several centimeters thick, is not as polluted as initially feared. Forbidden is forbidden
Dioxins, chlorinated hydrocarbons, mercury, cadmium, and arsenic play a major role in the Elbe. The pollutants sink to the ground with the suspended particles and remain there. Therefore, alluvial soils represent a sink in which substances are removed from circulation. But the substances are not harmless. Especially when plants absorb them and introduce them into the food chain, this will affect the oxygen content and acidity, and how much pollutants plants absorb from contaminated soils. This increased production of carbon dioxide reduces the pH level in the water at night. Whirlpools and vortices are two natural phenomena that occur in different parts of the world. Whirlpools are described as rotating bodies of water that can occur anywhere in the world and are primarily caused by turbulence and instability in the wind flowing over a particular area. Whirlpools, on the other hand, are described as rotating bodies of water that form when two currents intersect. Whirlpools differ from vortices in several ways, including the regions they affect and the way they are formed.

Formation
The first major difference between whirlpools and vortices is the way they are formed. Whirlpools are formed by the interaction of water currents that travel in opposite directions. The interaction of the currents creates a rotating body of water, and in some cases, the whirlpool can pull objects beneath the surface of the water. When whirlpools are strong enough to pull objects beneath the surface of the water, they are called vortices. Vortices are formed by air near the ground that has a significant temperature difference just above the air. The temperature difference causes the air to rise and rotate, creating a vortex. The continuous rotation of the air causes the air to become colder than it normally would be.

The second major difference between whirlpools and vortices is the impact they have on their surroundings. Whirlpools are primarily a danger to swimmers and small boats, as the strong currents can easily overwhelm them and cause them to drown or capsize. Po izboljšanju raziskovalnih metod je bilo ugotovljeno, da povečana glukoza v krvi začne škodovati telesu veliko prej kot presega referenčne vrednosti. Izkazalo se je, da obstaja skrita oblika diabetesa mellitusa, ki se morda dolgo ne manifestira, medtem ko poškoduje krvne žile in živčni sistem osebe.
Skupina kroničnih presnovnih bolezni, za katere je značilna visoka vsebnost glukoze zaradi oslabljene proizvodnje insulina, je diabetes mellitus. Diagnosticiran je pri vsaki starosti, otroku, srednjem in starejšem. Sladkorna bolezen pri starejših od 60 do 65 let je skoraj 9% vseh primerov, do 75. leta pa se stopnja pojavnosti močno poveča na 23.
Sladkorna bolezen tipa 2 zahteva neprekinjeno vseživljenjsko zdravljenje. Glavni cilji terapije so omejiti dobavo ogljikovih hidratov iz hrane in odstranitev sladkorja iz telesa predvsem s povečanjem izdatkov za vitalne procese. Glavno vlogo pri zdravljenju sladkorne bolezni imajo pravilna prehrana, nadzor telesne teže, redna vadba.
Popolno zdravilo za sladkorno bolezen je stvar prihodnosti. Trenutno takšna diagnoza pomeni veliko omejitev, vseživljenjsko terapijo, nenehen boj s progresivnimi zapleti. Zato je preprečevanje sladkorne bolezni izjemno pomembno. Vključuje številne preproste ukrepe, ki jih je mogoče opisati z izrazom "zdrav način življenja".
Sladkorna bolezen zahteva, da oseba porabi denar: trakove, droge, prehrano, redne preglede. Poskušali bomo ugotoviti, ali jih država lahko kompenzira, ali dajejo invalidnost v primeru sladkorne bolezni, kako jo lahko dobimo in kakšne koristi imajo invalidi in bolniki brez skupine.
Izračunavanje ogljikovih hidratov v hrani pomeni diabetike s prvo in drugo vrsto bolezni. Za olajšanje te naloge je bil razvit poseben ukrep - enote zrna (HE). Na začetku so jih uporabljali pri bolnikih, ki so prejemali insulin. Tabele krušnih enot v različnih izdelkih zelo olajšajo izračun odmerka hormona.
Znanstveno dokazano dejstvo: redna telesna vzgoja pri drugi vrsti sladkorne bolezni močno olajša potek bolezni. Učinek obremenitev na moč delovanja je primerljiv z antidiabetičnimi zdravili. Med raziskavo je bilo ugotovljeno, da se pri bolnikih po 4 mesecih pouka nadzor diabetesa bistveno izboljša, zmanjša se telesna masa, poveča krvni obtok in zmanjša verjetnost depresije.
Vzrok povečane glukoze je lahko dolgotrajen presežek steroidov v krvi. V tem primeru je diagnoza »steroidni diabetes mellitus«. Najpogosteje pride do neravnovesja zaradi predpisanih zdravil, lahko pa je tudi zaplet bolezni, ki povzročajo povečano sproščanje hormonov.
Cilj zdravljenja sladkorne bolezni je, da se glukoza dolgo časa ohranja na ravni, ki je skoraj normalna. Če to ne uspe, pravijo, da ima bolnik dekompenzirano sladkorno bolezen. Doseganje dolgoročne kompenzacije je možno le s strogo disciplino. Režim zdravljenja vključuje: upoštevanje načina in sestave prehrane, aktivno, vendar ne pretirano vadbo, pravočasno jemanje hipoglikemičnih zdravil, pravilen izračun in vnos insulina.

Si profesionalni prevajalec iz angleščine v slovenščino. Tvoja naloga je ustvariti visoko kakovostne prevode, ki so naravni, tekoči in natančni. Izogibaj se dobesednim prevodom, ki zvenijo nenaravno. Upoštevaj kontekst, idiome in kulturne reference. Ne dodajaj nobenih dodatnih informacij ali komentarjev, samo prevod.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

The functions of the eye and its auxiliary devices
The eye should allow us to see the world as it is. From a medical perspective, the eyes are outgrowths of the brain, very similar to video cameras, and their functions and structure are the same. The development of the visual system in a human embryo begins on the 18th day, and from the seventh month, the fetus can already see.
By the age of 18, the visual analyzer of a person with normal development should be a well-adjusted camera; the formation of the visual system is complete. The eye of an adult weighs 6-8 grams and is a very complex optical device. Let's try to understand the structure of the visual organ.
Human organs of vision
Human vision is a function of the visual analyzer, which is a complex visual system that includes:
- Eyeball;
- protective and auxiliary organs of the eye;
- visual pathways;
- subcortical and cortical centers.
Only with the coordinated and precise work of all components do visual sensations arise, and a person distinguishes brightness, color, shape, and size of observed objects.
How does this happen? To understand how a person sees, we need to be familiar with the structure of the eye.
Structure and function of the visual organ
The main task of the eye is to transmit an image to the optic nerve. This happens with the help of the following structures of the eye.
Cornea and aqueous humor
The most important part of the eye is the cornea – the outer, transparent shell that covers the front of the eye. It is not simply a "glass" covering, but protects against external influences and is a highly refractive lens that affects focus. It is composed of cells that are highly permeable. On 1 square millimeter of the cornea, there are at least 2,000 such cells.
The cornea requires constant moistening; otherwise, it dries out, and microscopic lesions can form. The human eye needs to blink 6 times per minute, while the blinking frequency of a computer screen is reduced by a factor of 2. This leads to drying of the cornea, which becomes cloudy. Therefore, doctors recommend 15-minute breaks for every hour of work that requires visual strain. During this time, the eye has time to relax, remove muscle cramps, and restore its reflexes. Eye exercises are also beneficial.
Aqueous humor
The aqueous humor performs the lubricating function for the cornea. The tear film is very thin, and its size does not exceed 10 microns, while the quality of vision depends on it. The average tear film is watery, transmits light well, and promotes the penetration of oxygen and other nutrients. The intraocular fluid is located between the cornea and the lens.
Iris and pupil
The iris is the front part of the choroid, and it contains pigment that determines the color of the eyes in humans. In the center of the iris is an opening called the pupil. The diameter can vary depending on the illumination. It is regulated by the muscles of the iris, which are responsible for constricting and dilating the pupil.
With the help of the pupil, excess light is regulated, protecting the retina from glare.
The iris is bordered by an opaque membrane called the sclera; in humans, the outer visible part is called the white of the eye. The sclera surrounds the eyeball for 80%, and in the front part, it transitions into the cornea.
Lens
The structure behind the pupil is called the lens. It creates an image together with the cornea, as it is a biconvex lens composed of transparent, ordered fibers. Under normal conditions, the size of the lens is: thickness from 3.5 mm to 5 mm, diameter – 9-10 mm.
On the outside, there is a capsule into which the finest fibers are woven, connected to the ciliary body. Due to the optical power of the lens, the eye focuses the image. The lens changes its shape, which allows for focusing at different distances. When focusing on a close object, the ciliary muscle relaxes the fibers of the lens, and it takes on a convex shape, providing a clear image at close range. When a person looks at a distant object, the muscle relaxes, the fibers stretch, and the lens becomes flatter.
With age, the core of the lens becomes more wrinkled and less elastic, which is why people around the age of 50 begin to have difficulty with near vision. Due to the modern pace of life and eye strain, doctors predict that 75% of the population will have myopia.
When the lens loses its transparency, cataracts develop. Today, this diagnosis is completely treatable, as the operation to replace the cloudy lens with an artificial one takes only 5 to 7 minutes. A properly selected artificial lens can not only save the patient from cataracts but also correct their nearsightedness.
Vitreous body
Immediately behind the lens, up to the retina, is the vitreous body. It gives the eye its shape. The vitreous humor is composed of a viscous, gel-like substance enclosed in a fibrous framework. Normally, these fibrils are arranged in an orderly manner and do not interfere with the passage of light to the retina. However, when the fibrillar structure becomes disturbed and loses its order, the human eye develops a vitreous detachment. This is manifested by the patient seeing floating, thin threads against a light background. This pathology does not affect vision but can cause some discomfort.
Retina
When light enters the eye, it first passes through the cornea and lens, then through the vitreous body, and reaches the inner surface of the eye. There is a layer of light-sensitive cells on which the image is projected. These are the retinal cells, of which there are millions in the depth of the eyeball.
The retina is the most organized tissue and plays an important role in the structure and function of the visual organ. It is composed of 10 highly organized layers, and its structure is not homogeneous. There are cells called rods and cones. Cones provide color vision, and rods provide black and white perception. The function of the visual analyzer as a whole depends on the health of the retina. Millions of fibers of the retina, which merge into one nerve, form the optic nerve, which immediately transmits signals to the brain. Visual perception ends in the cerebral hemispheres of the cerebral cortex.
Anomalies of the eye occur when light rays do not focus on the retina but come in front of it, which leads to myopia, or behind it, which leads to hyperopia. To compensate for myopia, concave lenses are prescribed, and for hyperopia, convex lenses are prescribed.
The transparent surfaces of the eye, through which light passes, determine the refractive power of the eye. It is expressed in diopters (D) and is close to 70 D for near objects and 59 D for distant objects.
All the structures of the visual organ that we have discussed represent the optical and light-sensitive system. Now let's consider the functions of the auxiliary apparatus of the eye.
Auxiliary apparatus of the eye and its functions
The auxiliary apparatus of the eye performs protective and motor functions.
It includes:
- eyelids;
- eyebrows;
- eyelashes;
- muscles of the eyeball;
- lacrimal apparatus.
Motor function
When looking at an object, the human eyes move. The movement is carried out by six muscles attached to the eyeball. There are 4 straight muscles: superior, inferior, lateral, and medial, and 2 oblique muscles: superior and inferior.
The muscles work in such a way that both eyes perform the movement simultaneously and harmoniously.
There are 4 types of eye movements:
- Saccadic movements, which are rapid jumps that last a fraction of a second, and the eye does not feel them when following the outline of an object.
- Smooth tracking movements for a moving image.
- When looking at a close object, the visual axes converge, and convergent movements occur.
- The mechanism that supports the fixation of gaze during head movements is called vestibulo-ocular movement.
The contraction of the oculomotor muscles leads to the eyeball performing complex, coordinated movements, ensuring that both eyes work together.
Eyelids
The eyelids consist of two halves, each of which is skin, and its base is cartilage. The closed eyelids form a protective barrier for the front of the eye. The upper and lower eyelids cover the eye from above and below. In the eyelids, the anterior and posterior parts and the free edges are distinguished. The space between the edges is called the palpebral fissure. Its length in adults is usually about 30 cm, and its width is from 10 to 14 mm.
The edges have corners: medial and lateral. Near the medial corner on both parts of the eyelids is a slight elevation – the lacrimal papilla with a punctum. This is the beginning of the lacrimal canal. The anterior edge of the eyelids is covered with eyelashes, and the inner surface of the eyelids is covered with conjunctiva. The conjunctiva is a mucous membrane, also called the connecting membrane, because it passes from the eyelid through the conjunctival sac to the eyeball.
The eyelids have a developed lymphatic system and many blood vessels, and the skin on the eyelids is thin, easily folded, and contains sweat and sebaceous glands. They not only protect the eyes from damage but also serve as a shield against light.
Eyelashes
Human eyelashes perform two functions: protective and aesthetic. Thick, long hairs on the eyelids protect the eye from foreign bodies, insects, and dust. They also give the face a beautiful expression, framing the eyes with a beautiful halo. The length of the hairs in the upper eyelashes can be up to 10 mm, and the lower ones are usually shorter – 7 mm. The density of eyelashes is an individual indicator, but according to statistics, the upper eyelid contains 3.5 times more eyelashes than the lower eyelid. The lifespan of eyelashes is about 150 days, after which they are replaced.
Eyebrows
Above the eyes is a curved elevation of skin covered with hairs. These are the eyebrows, which are designed to protect the eyes from above from unwanted influences. Eyebrows have a curved shape and play a communicative role in a person's life. As a mimetic means, they help express a person's emotions: surprise, anger, fear.
Lacrimal apparatus
It is difficult to overestimate the protective function of the lacrimal apparatus. With the tear film, it moistens the cornea and protects it from drying out and hypothermia. The lacrimal gland, the excretory ducts, the lacrimal sac, and the nasolacrimal canal are all structures that provide the eye with its daily requirement of moisturizing fluid. Emotional outbursts lead to the activation of the main lacrimal gland, and then a person sheds tears.
Human vision is a complex, interconnected process in which not only the visual organ but also the brain participates. It is not surprising that they say: "He looks with his eyes, but he sees with his brain."

Pokličemo funkcije očesa in pomožne naprave
Oči naj nas vidi svet, kakršen je. Z medicinskega vidika so oči izrastki možganov, so zelo podobni video kameram, njihove funkcije in naprava so enake. Polaganje vizualnega sistema v človeškem zarodku se začne 18. dan in od sedmih mesecev lahko plod že vidi.
Do starosti 18 let mora biti vizualni analizator osebe, ki je pod normalnim razvojem dobro nastavljena kamera, oblikovanje vizualnega sistema je končano. Oko odraslega tehta 6-8 gramov in je zelo zapletena optična naprava. Poskusimo razumeti strukturo vidnega organa.
Človeški organi vida
Človeška vizija je funkcija vizualnega analizatorja, ki je kompleksen vizualni sistem, ki vključuje:
- Eyeball;
- zaščitni in pomožni organi oči;
- vodenje poti;
- podkortični in kortikalni centri.
Samo z usklajenim in natančnim delom vseh komponent sestavljajo vizualne občutke in oseba razlikuje svetlost, barvo, obliko in velikost opazovanih predmetov.
Kako se to zgodi? Da bi razumeli, kako človek vidi, mora biti seznaniti s strukturo očesa.
Struktura in delovanje vidnega organa
Glavna naloga oči je prenašanje slike v optični živec. To se zgodi s pomočjo naslednjih struktur za oči.
Rožnja in vodna vlaga
Najpomembnejši del očesa je roženica - zunanja, prozorna lupina, ki pokriva prednji del očesa. To ni enostavno pokriti "stekla", zaščititi pred zunanjimi vplivi, je zelo refraktivna leča, ki vpliva na fokus. Sestavljen je iz celic, ki dobro prehajajo. Na 1 kvadratni milimetrju roženice je potrebno ne manj kot 2 tisoč takih celic.
Roženica zahteva stalno močenje, sicer se posuši in na njej lahko nastanejo mikroskopi. Oko osebe mora utripati 6 krat v minutah, medtem ko se utripajoča frekvenca računalnika zmanjša za faktor 2. To vodi do sušenja roženice, postane motno. Zato zdravniki priporočajo 15-minutni odmori za vsako uro dela, ki zahteva vizualno napetost. V tem času ima oko časa, da se sprostite, odstranite mišični krči in obnovite svoje reflekse. Pomiri telovadnico za oči.
Vlaga
Vlogo mazanja za roženico opravlja solzna tekočina. Film za trganje je zelo tanek, njegova velikost pa ne presega 10 mikronov, medtem ko je kakovost vizije odvisna od tega. Povprečna široka filmska plast je vodena, dobro prenaša svetlobo in spodbuja prodor kisika in drugih hranil. Intraokularna tekočina je med roženico in šaržo.
Iris in učenec
Iris - sprednji del horroid očesa, vsebuje pigment, ki določa barvo oči pri ljudeh. V središču šarenice je luknja, imenovana učenec. Premer se lahko razlikuje glede na osvetlitev. Urejajo ga mišice šarenice, odgovorne za zoženje in dilatacijo učenca.
S pomočjo učenca je regulirana presežna svetloba ščiti mrežnico od zaslepitve.
Iris meji na neprozorno membrano, imenovano sklero, pri ljudeh pa se zunanji vidni del imenuje bela ocesa. Sclera obkrožuje očesce za 80%, v sprednjem delu pa prehaja v roženico.
Lentikularno
Telo za učenca se imenuje leča. Ustvarja podobo skupaj z roženico, saj je bikonveksna leča, sestavljena iz prozornih naročenih vlaken. Ob normalni meritvi velikosti leče: debelina od 3,5 mm do 5 mm, premer - 9-10 mm.
Zunaj je kapsula, v katero so prepletena najfinija vlakna, povezana s ciliarnim telesom. Zaradi optične moči leče oko se osredotoča na sliko. Objektiv se spremeni v obliko, kar omogoča enako razdaljo in zapiranje. Napenjanje, ciliarna mišica sprošča vlakna leče in prevzame konveksno obliko, ki zagotavlja čisto podobo v bližini. Ko oseba pogleda daleč, se mišica sprosti, vlakna se raztezajo, objektiv postane gostejši.
S starostjo je jedro objektiva postalo bolj gube, postane manj elastično, zato ljudje v starosti 50 let začnejo imeti težave z vidom v bližini. Zaradi sodobnega ritma življenja in očesnih napetosti zdravniki napovedujejo prisotnost kratkovidnosti pri 75% populacije.
Ko leča izgubi svojo prosojnost, se začne katarakta. Danes je ta diagnoza povsem nevzdržna, saj je operacija zamenjanja motne leče z umetno traja od 5 do 7 minut. Pravilno izbrana umetna leča vam omogoča, da pacienta rešite ne le iz katarakte, temveč tudi za nadomestilo njegove bližnje bližnje bolezni.
Vitreous body
Takoj za lečo do mrežnice je steklasto telo. Obožu daje obliko, ki jo ima. Steklenski humor je sestavljen iz viskozne gelaste snovi, ki je zaprta v fibriliranem okviru. Običajno so ti fibrili razporejeni po vrstnem redu in ne vplivajo na prehod svetlobe na mrežnico. Ampak, ko se fibrilacija razburja in izgubijo svoj red, potem človeško telo razvije uničenje steklastega. Izraženo je, da pacient na lahkem ozadju začne videti plavajoče tanke niti. Ta patologija ne vpliva na vid, ampak daje osebi nekaj neugodja.
Retin A
Priti v oči, najprej svetlobe prehaja skozi roženico in leče, nato skozi stekleno telo doseže notranjo površino očesa. Obstaja plast svetlobno občutljivih celic, na katerih je slika predvidena. To so retinalne celice, ki so v globini očesca milijone.
Mrežica je najbolj organizirano tkivo, ki ima pomembno vlogo pri strukturi in funkcijah vidnega organa. Sestavljen je iz 10 visoko organiziranih plasti, njegova struktura pa ni homogena. Obstajajo celice, imenovane palice in stožci. Stožci zagotavljajo barvni vid in palice dajejo črno-belo percepcijo. Funkcije vizualnega analizatorja kot celote so odvisne od zdravja mrežnice. Milijoni vlaken mrežnice, ki se združujejo v eno nit, tvori optični živec, ki takoj prenaša signale v možgane. Vizualna percepcija v možganskih polobah možganske skorje se konča.
Anomalija oči se pojavi, če se žarki svetlobe ne osredotočajo na mrežnico, ampak pridejo pred njo, nato pa se miopija razvije, če je za mrežnico daljnovidnost. Za kompenzacijo bronhialne levkemije so predpisane in za daljnovidnost predpisane bikonveksne kozarce.
Prosojne površine očesa, skozi katere poteka svetloba, določajo refrakcijsko moč očesa. Izraža se pri dioptrih (D) in je blizu 70 D, za oddaljene predmete 59 D.
Vse obravnavane strukture vidnega organa predstavljajo optični in svetlobni sistem. Ostaneva imena funkcij pomožne aparature očesa.
Pomožni aparati za oči in njegove funkcije
Izvaja pomožni aparat očesa zaščitna in motorična funkcija.
Vključuje:
- veke;
- obrvi;
- trepalnice;
- mišice očesnega jabolka;
- solzni aparat.
Motorno vozilo
Ko pogledate predmet, se oči osebe premaknejo. Gibanje izvajajo šest mišic, pritrjenih na očesno jabolko. Obstajajo 4 ravni mišice: zgornji, spodnji, stranski in medialni in 2 poševni: zgornji in spodnji.
Mišice delujejo na tak način, da obe očesi opravljata gibanje hkrati in prijazno.
Obstajajo 4 vrste gibanja oči.
- Sakadni gibi, ki so hitri skoki, ki trajajo delček sekunde, kar se oko ne čuti, ko sledi obrisu predmeta.
- Gladko spremljanje gibanja za gibljivo sliko.
- Pri tesnem stiku s sliko se vizualne osi zrušijo med seboj in pride do konvergentnega gibanja.
- Mehanizem, ki podpira pritrjevanje pogleda med gibanjem glave, se imenuje vestibularno gibanje oči.
Krčenje očulomotoričnih mišic vodi očesno oko v zapleteno ključno gibanje, ki usklajuje delo dveh oči hkrati.
Veke
Veke sestavljajo dve polovici, od katerih je vsaka koža, njena osnova je hrustanec. Zaprta veke so zaščitna pregrada prednjega dela očesa. Zgornja in spodnja veke pokrivajo oko od zgoraj in spodaj. V vekih se razlikujejo sprednji in zadnji in prosti robovi. Prostor med robovi se imenuje očesna vrzel. Njegova dolžina pri odraslih se običajno spreminja v 30 cm in širina - od 10 do 14 mm.
Robovi so vogali: medialni in stranski. V bližini medialnega kota na obeh delih vek je rahlo zvišanje - solzna papilla s krtačo. To je začetek solznega kanala. Sprednji rob vek je prekrit s trepalnicami, notranja stran veke pa je prekrita s konjunktivo. Konjunktiva je sluznica, ki se imenuje tudi povezovalna membrana, ker prehaja iz veke skozi konjunktivno vrečko do očesnega jabolka.
Veke imajo razvit limfni sistem in veliko krvnih žil, koža na vekicah pa je nežna, enostavna za zlaganje, vsebuje znoj in lojnice. Ne ščitijo očesa pred poškodbami, temveč služijo tudi kot ščit na poti svetlobe.
Trepalnice
Človeške trepalnice opravljajo dve funkciji: zaščitno in estetsko. Debele dolge dlake na vekih ščitijo oko od tujih teles, žuželk, prahu. Prav tako obrazu obraza dajo čudovit izraz, ki oklepa oči s čudovitim halojem. Dolžina dlak v zgornjih trepalnicah je lahko do 10 mm, spodnja pa običajno krajša - 7 mm. Gostota trepalnic je individualni indikator, vendar po statističnih podatkih zgornji vek vsebuje 3,5 krat več trepalnic kot spodnji vek. Življenjska doba trepalnic je približno 150 dni, potem se spreminjajo.
Obrvi
Nad očmi je okrogla višina kože, prekrita z dlakami. To so obrvi, ki so namenjeni zaščiti očesa od zgoraj od neželenih vplivov. Obrvi izgledajo kot valji in opravljajo komunikacijsko vlogo v življenju posameznika. Kot mimično pomeni pomagati izraziti čustva osebe: presenečenje, jezo, strah.
Teardrop aparat
Težko je precenjevati zaščitno funkcijo naprave za trganje. S solzno kopeljo očesno jakno in navlaži roženico, ki jo preprečuje sušenje in hipotermija.
