Temperature is a key factor in plant growth and development. Along with light levels, carbon dioxide, air humidity, water, and nutrients, temperature influences plant growth and ultimately yield. All these factors must be balanced. Temperature affects plants both in the short term and the long term.

It is not surprising that much research has been conducted on strategies for regulating temperature for efficient greenhouse production. The optimal temperature for a plant depends on a variety of factors. A plant's response to ambient temperature depends on its developmental stage. Plants have a kind of biological clock that determines their temperature sensitivity.

Differences between air temperature and plant temperature
Most biological processes will be accelerated at higher temperatures, which can have both positive and negative effects. One advantage, in most cases, is faster fruit growth. However, the resulting excessive respiration has a negative effect, as it means less energy is available for fruit development, and the fruits will be smaller. Some effects are short-term, while others are long-term. For example, temperature immediately affects a plant's absorption balance. The onset of flowering, on the other hand, is determined by the climate over a much longer period.

Plant temperature and air temperature are not the same, as plants can cool down through evaporation and heat up through radiation. Plants try to reach their optimal temperature, and the balance between air temperature, relative humidity, and light is important in this process. If light levels are high, the plant will heat up, creating a difference between plant temperature and air temperature. To cool down, the plant must increase its transpiration rate. The transpiration rate depends not only on temperature but also on environmental conditions such as light, CO2 levels in the atmosphere, and relative humidity, as well as the plant species.

Plants are made up of different parts, all of which react differently to temperature. The temperature of the fruits is closely related to the air temperature – as the air temperature rises, so does the fruit temperature, and vice versa. The fruit temperature will fluctuate less than the air temperature, and it will take more time (sometimes several hours) for it to rise or fall. The temperature of the flowers, on the other hand, is higher than the air temperature or the leaf temperature, and the flower petals transpire much more slowly than the plant's leaves. The temperature at the top of the plant canopy fluctuates more than the temperature at the bottom. The top will heat up more easily through radiation and will therefore have a higher temperature than the air when light levels are high.

Vapor pressure deficit
The relative humidity of the environment depends on temperature and wind speed. Higher temperatures usually lead to increased transpiration. This is partly because the molecules move faster, and warm air can hold more water vapor. When the air is not moving, the air around the leaves will become saturated with water vapor, which will slow down the evaporation process. If the air is saturated with water, a film will condense on the water and around the leaves, which will create a good environment for pathogens that will attack the plant.

The difference in water vapor content between the air and the saturation point is called the vapor pressure deficit (VPD). The higher the VPD value, the more water the plant will lose through transpiration. However, if the VPD value is too high, the plant may be stressed, as it cannot replace the water it is losing through transpiration. This does not cause problems in the short term, as the plant will absorb enough water the following night to recover. However, if the VPD value remains high for a long time, the plant will not be able to recover the following night, and irreversible plant damage may occur, such as scorched leaves or flower petals.

Measuring leaf thickness allows for a visual check of the plant's ability to recover. Leaves can actually thin out during the day as they lose water through transpiration, but if a leaf is thinner one night than the previous night, this is a sign that the plant has not been able to recover. Therefore, you may be tempted to keep the VPD value low to avoid damage, but under these conditions, the plant has no incentive to grow and be active, which can negatively affect it when it is exposed to stress.

In general, it can be compared to a car's tachometer. When the engine speed increases, the needle on the tachometer moves into the red zone. This will not immediately damage the engine, but it would if the car were driven in the red zone for a long time. The VPD value should be between 0.45 and 1.25 for most plants, expressed in kilopascals (kPa is a unit of pressure), with an optimal value of around 0.85 kPa. VPD follows more or less the same pattern as the radiation level in the environment – it rises in the morning at sunrise and reaches a peak around noon, then gradually decreases again. To calculate the VPD value, you must first know the air temperature, the plant temperature, and the relative humidity.

Stomata
Plants can regulate the process of transpiration and cooling with special plant organs called stomata. Stomata are special cells in the leaves that can open or close, thereby limiting the amount of water vapor that can evaporate. The higher the temperature rises, the more the stomata will allow evaporation when they are open. It is difficult to measure the openness of the stomata, so the VPD value can be used as an estimate. The more the stomata open, the more gases can pass into and out of the leaves.

The rate of this process (stomatal conductance) is affected by various environmental factors, such as higher relative humidity leading to faster conductance, while higher CO2 levels reduce the rate of stomatal conductance. However, other factors also affect conductance, such as plant hormones and the color (wavelength) of the light the plant receives. The plant hormone abscisic acid regulates the concentration of ions in the stomata and causes the stomata to open very quickly in just a few minutes. Light with a shorter wavelength (approximately 400–500 nanometers (nm), i.e., blue light) causes the stomata to open wider than light with a longer wavelength (approximately 700 nm, i.e., red light).

Optimal day and night temperatures
Different processes take place in plants during the day and at night, and the optimal temperature is therefore different. Sugar transport mainly occurs at night and mainly to the warmer parts of the plant. The leaves cool down faster than the fruits and flowers, so most of the available energy goes to these parts of the plant, which need energy for growth and development.

The optimal combinations of day and night temperatures were researched in the world's first air-conditioned greenhouse, the phytotron at the California Institute of Technology in 1949. The experiments showed that tomato plants grew taller with a combination of high temperature in the light period and lower temperature in the dark period than if the temperature was constant. The ability of plants to "distinguish" between temperature changes during the day and at night is called thermoperiodism and affects flowering, fruit set, and growth.

The amount of sugar transported to the growing tissue, which needs energy for higher respiration rates, can be limited by a higher night temperature, which in turn limits growth. It has also been found that a combination of high day and low night temperatures leads to stem elongation. A low night temperature improves the water balance in the plant, which is the main reason for stem elongation. Temperature can therefore be used as a tool to regulate plant height, and low night temperatures can also save energy. The term thermomorphogenesis is used to describe the thermoperiodic effects on plant morphology.

The optimal air temperature also depends on the intensity of the light and the amount of carbon dioxide in the air. Plants act similarly to cold-blooded animals, as their metabolism and photosynthesis rate increase in relation to the air temperature in the environment. When the temperature is very low (which also depends on the plant variety), there will be almost no photosynthesis, no matter how much light there is. The rate of photosynthesis increases as the air temperature rises. When light and temperature are in balance, the limiting factor will be the level of CO2 in the environment. If enough CO2 is available, the rate of photosynthesis will increase with temperature, although other factors, such as the enzyme RuBisCo, also play a role.

RuBisCo is crucial for photosynthesis. In some cases, a process called photorespiration will occur – this happens when RuBisCo binds to oxygen instead of carbon dioxide, as would happen in normal photosynthesis. The level of CO2 and the optimal temperature will be lower at low light levels than at high light levels, and the activity of the enzymes will be greater at higher temperatures.

Temperature drop and integration (DIF)
The concept of DIF refers to the relationship between day and night temperatures. The effects of daily temperature changes on the long-term growth of plant stems depend on the difference (DIF) between day and night temperatures (calculated by subtracting the night temperature from the day temperature) and not on separate and independent responses to day and night temperatures. In other words, the temperature difference is important, as is whether the night temperature is higher or lower than the day temperature.

DIF does not have a strong effect on leaf growth, but it does affect the growth of stem internodes. Plants grown with a positive DIF are taller than plants grown with a zero DIF, with plants grown with a zero DIF being taller and having larger stem internodes than plants grown with a negative DIF. Other important morphogenetic responses to a negative DIF value (i.e., when the day temperature is lower than the night temperature) include shorter leaf and petiole lengths and leaves.

The differences in stem internode and leaf elongation are the result of differences in the elongation and/or cell division process. If the DIF is negative, both processes are inhibited, which may be due to reduced activity of gibberellin in the subapical growth tip (growth tissue). Gibberellin is a plant hormone that promotes plant growth. DIF has the greatest effect on stem elongation during a period of rapid growth, so seedlings are more sensitive to differences between day and night temperatures compared to adult plants. A negative DIF in the early stages of stem elongation is therefore important for limiting plant height.

Stem elongation can also be caused by a short drop in temperature (for about two hours) in a 24-hour daily growth cycle, usually in the dark period or just before the first daylight. The responsiveness to temperature changes is strongest in the first few hours of the light period in long-day and short-day plants and in day-neutral plants. Therefore, a drop in temperature in the last two hours of the night will affect plant height. This is usually easily achieved in greenhouses in autumn in cold climates due to the naturally low night temperature.

The change in the sensitivity of stem elongation to temperature in the day and night periods can be controlled by an endogenous growth rhythm. A biorhythm of growth (lasting approximately 24 hours) was identified in Chrysanthemum in 1994. Stem elongation in a 24-hour light and dark cycle is not constant. Short-day and long-day plants grown under conditions to promote flowering elongate faster at night than during the day. Orchids need a period of low night temperature to flower.

Temperature integration is one of the strategies used by growers. They calculate the lowest and highest temperature for individual plant species and allow this to fluctuate while still maintaining a certain long-term average temperature. This strategy makes the most of natural heat.

Air temperature is the primary environmental factor that affects plant development and growth rate. However, air temperature is never a factor that is separate from other factors. Every plant growth factor is related to all other factors, and the challenge is to find the weak links in this chain. This article has explored many of these factors, but there are other factors that are equally important, such as water balance and, indirectly, transpiration. Everything that happens to a plant happens at the control point of air temperature – managing this is the first step on the long road to successful cultivation.

Temperatura je ključni dejavnik pri rasti in razvoju rastlin. Skupaj z ravnjo svetlobe, ogljikovim dioksidom, vlago v zraku, vodo in hranili, temperatura vpliva na rast rastlin in nenazadnje tudi na pridelek. Vsi ti dejavniki morajo biti uravnoteženi. Temperatura vpliva na rastlino kratkoročno in tudi dolgoročno.
Ni presenetljivo, da so o strategijah uravnavanja temperature za učinkovito pridelavo v rastlinjakih izvedli veliko raziskav. Optimalna temperatura za rastlino je odvisna od vrste dejavnikov. Reakcija rastline na temperaturo ozračja okoli nje je odvisna od njene razvojne stopnje. Rastline imajo nekakšno biološko uro, ki določa njihovo občutljivost na temperaturo.
Razlike med temperaturo zraka in temperaturo rastline
Večina bioloških procesov se bo pospešila pri višjih temperaturah, kar lahko ima pozitivne in negativne učinke. Ena od prednosti je, v večini primerov, na primer hitrejša rast plodu. Vendar je učinek posledičnega čezmernega dihanja negativen, saj je zaradi njega za razvoj plodu na voljo manj energije, plodovi pa bodo manjši. Nekateri učinki so kratkoročni, drugi pa dolgoročni. Temperatura na primer takoj vpliva na absorpcijsko ravnotežje rastline. Začetek cvetenja po drugi strani določa podnebje v veliko daljšem časovnem obdobju.
Temperatura rastline in temperatura zraka nista enaki, saj se rastline lahko ohlajajo z izhlapevanjem in segrevajo s pomočjo sevanja. Rastline poskušajo doseči svojo optimalno temperaturo, pri tem pa je pomembno tudi ravnotežje med temperaturo zraka, relativno vlažnostjo in svetlobo. Če so ravni svetlobe visoke, se bo rastlina segrela, kar bo povzročilo razliko med temperaturo rastline in temperaturo zraka. Da se ohladi, mora rastlina povečati svojo stopnjo transpiracije. Stopnja transpiracije je razen od temperature odvisna tudi od okoljskih pogojev, kot so svetloba, ravni CO2 v ozračju in relativne vlažnosti, pa tudi od vrste rastline.
Rastline so sestavljene iz različnih delov, ki vsi različno reagirajo na temperaturo. Temperatura plodov je tesno povezana s temperaturo zraka – ko ta naraste, naraste tudi temperatura plodov in obratno. Temperatura plodu bo nihala manj od temperature zraka in za rast ali padec bo potrebnega več časa (včasih tudi do nekaj ur več). Temperatura cvetov je, nasprotno, višja od temperature zraka ali temperature listov, cvetni listi pa transpirirajo precej počasneje kot listi rastline. Temperatura na vrhu krošnje rastline bolj niha kot tista na njenem dnu. Vrh se bodo lažje segrel s sevanjem in bo imel zato višjo temperaturo kot zrak, kadar je raven svetlobe visoka.
Primanjkljaj parnega tlaka
Relativna vlažnost okolja je odvisna od temperature in hitrosti vetra. Višje temperature običajno privedejo do povečane transpiracije. Vzrok temu je deloma to, da se molekule premikajo hitreje, topli zrak pa lahko sprejme več vodnih hlapov. Kadar se zrak ne premika, se bo zrak okoli listov nasitil z vodno paro, kar bo upočasnilo proces izhlapevanja. Če je zrak nasičen z vodo, se bo na vodi in okrog listov kondenziral film, ki bo omogočal dobro okolje za patogene, ki bodo napadli rastlino.
Razlika v vsebnosti vodnih hlapov med zrakom in točko nasičenosti se imenuje primanjkljaj parnega tlaka (VPD). Višja kot je vrednost VPD, več vode bo rastlina oddala s transpiracijo. Če pa je vrednost VPD previsoka, je lahko rastlina pod stresom, saj ne more nadomestiti vode, ki jo izgublja s transpiracijo. To kratkoročno ne povzroči težav, rastlina bo naslednjo noč absorbirala dovolj vode, da si bo opomogla. Če pa vrednost VPD ostane visoka dalj časa, se rastlina naslednjo noč ne bo mogla obnoviti in lahko se pojavi nepopravljiva škoda rastlin, kot so zgoreli listi ali cvetni listi.
Merjenje debeline lista omogoča vizualno preverjanje možnosti rastline za okrevanje. Listi se lahko čez dan dejansko stanjšajo, ker izgubljajo vodo s transpiracijo, toda če je list eno noč tanjši kot prejšnjo noč, je to znak, da se rastlina ni uspela obnoviti. Zato boste morda v skušnjavi, da bi vrednost VPD ohranjali nizko, da bi se izognili škodi, vendar rastlina pod temi pogoji nima spodbude za rast in dejavnost, kar lahko negativno vpliva nanjo, ko bo izpostavljena stresu.
Na splošno jo je mogoče primerjati s števcem vrtljajev motorja. Ko se hitrost vrtljajev motorja poveča, se igla na števcu premakne v rdeče območje. To ne bo takoj poškodovalo motorja, bi pa ga, če bi avtomobil dalj časa vozili v rdečem območju. Vrednost VPD mora pri večini rastlin biti med 0,45 in 1,25, izraženo v kilopaskalih (kPa je enota za tlak) z optimalno vrednostjo okrog 0,85 kPa. VPD sledi bolj ali manj istemu vzorcu kot raven vrednosti sevanja v okolju – zjutraj ob sončnem vzhodu ta naraste in doseže vrhunec okrog poldneva, nato pa se postopoma spet znižuje. Za izračun vrednosti VPD je treba najprej poznati temperaturo zraka, temperaturo rastline in relativno vlažnost.
Stomi
Rastline lahko uravnavajo proces transpiracije in hlajenja s pomočjo posebnih rastlinskih organov, imenovanih stome . Stome so posebne celice v listih, ki se lahko odpirajo ali zapirajo ter s tem omejujejo količino vodne pare, ki lahko izhlapi. Višje, kot temperatura naraste, bolj bodo stome omogočale izhlapevanje, ko so odprte. Odprtost stomov je težko izmeriti, zato lahko za oceno uporabimo vrednost VPD. Bolj kot se stome odpirajo, več plinov lahko preide v liste in iz njih.
Na hitrost tega procesa (prevodnost stomov) vplivajo različni okoljski dejavniki, na primer višja relativna vlažnost vodi v hitrejšo prevodnost, medtem ko višje ravni CO2 znižajo stopnjo prevodnosti stomov. Toda na prevodnost vplivajo tudi drugi dejavniki, na primer rastlinski hormoni in barva svetlobe (valovna dolžina), ki jo rastlina prejema. Rastlinska hormonska abscisinska kislina uravnava koncentracijo ionov v stomih in povzroča, da se stome zelo hitro odprejo v le nekaj minutah. Svetloba s krajšo valovno dolžino (približno 400–500 nanometrov (nm)), torej modra svetloba , povzroči širše odpiranje stomov kot svetloba z daljšo valovno dolžino (približno 700 nm), kar je rdeča svetloba.
Optimalne dnevne in nočne temperature
V rastlinah podnevi in ponoči potekajo različni procesi, optimalna temperatura pa je zato različna. Prenos sladkorjev nastopi večinoma ponoči in v glavnem k toplejšim delom rastline. Listi se ohladijo hitreje kot plodovi in cvetovi, zato večina razpoložljive energije gre v te dele rastline, ki potrebujejo energijo za rast in razvoj.
Optimalne kombinacije dnevnih in nočnih temperatur so bile raziskane pri prvem klimatiziranem rastlinjaku na svetu, fitotronu Kalifornijskega inštituta za tehnologijo leta 1949. Poskusi so pokazali, da so rastline paradižnika zrasle višje pri kombinaciji visoke temperature v svetlem obdobju in nižje temperature v temnem obdobju, kot pa, če je bila temperatura konstantna. Sposobnosti rastlin za »razlikovanje« med temperaturnimi spremembami podnevi in ponoči imenujemo termoperiodizem in vpliva na cvetenje, nastajanje plodov in rast.
Količino sladkorja, preneseno v rastoče tkivo, ki potrebuje energijo za višje stopnje dihanja, je mogoče pri višji nočni temperaturi omejiti, s čimer omejimo tudi rast. Ugotovili so tudi, da pri kombinaciji visoke dnevne in nizke nočne temperature pride do podaljšanja stebla. Nizka nočna temperatura izboljša vodno ravnovesje v rastlini, kar je glavni razlog za daljšanje stebla. Temperaturo je torej mogoče uporabiti kot orodje za uravnavanje višine rastline, z nizkimi nočnimi temperaturami pa lahko prihranimo tudi energijo. Izraz termomorfogeneza se uporablja za opis termoperiodičnih učinkov na morfologijo rastlin.
Optimalna temperatura zraka je odvisna tudi od intenzivnosti svetlobe in količine ogljikovega dioksida v zraku. Rastline delujejo podobno kot hladnokrvne živali, saj se njihova presnova in hitrost fotosinteze poveča glede na temperaturo zraka v okolici. Ko je temperatura zelo nizka (kar je odvisno tudi od rastlinske sorte), ne bo skoraj nikakršne fotosinteze, ne glede na to, koliko je svetlobe. Stopnja fotosinteze se poveča, ko temperatura zraka naraste. Ko sta svetloba in temperatura v ravnovesju, bo omejujoči dejavnik raven CO2 v okolju. Če je na voljo dovolj CO2, bo hitrost fotosinteze naraščala skupaj s temperaturo, čeprav imajo pri tem vlogo tudi drugi dejavniki, kot je encim RuBisCo.
RuBisCo je za fotosintezo odločilen. V nekaterih primerih bo prišlo do procesa, ki ga imenujemo fotorespiracija – to se zgodi, ko se RuBisCo namesto ogljikovega dioksida veže s kisikom, kot bi se zgodilo pri običajni fotosintezi. Raven CO2 in optimalna temperatura bosta nižji pri nizkih ravneh svetlobe kot pri visokih ravneh, dejavnost encimov pa bo večja pri višji temperaturi.
Padec in integracija temperature (DIF)
Koncept DIF se nanaša na razmerje med dnevno in nočno temperaturo. Učinki dnevnih sprememb temperature na dolgoročno rast rastlinskih stebel je odvisen od razlike (DIF) med dnevno in nočno temperaturo (ki se izračunata tako, da nočno temperaturo odštejemo od dnevne) in ne na ločene in neodvisne odzive na dnevno in nočno temperaturo. Povedano drugače – pomembna je temperaturna razlika, pa tudi to, ali je višja nočna ali dnevna temperatura.
Na rast listja DIF ne vpliva močno, vpliva pa na rast medčlenkov stebla. Rastline, pridelane pri pozitivni DIF, so višje od rastlin, pridelanih pri ničelni DIF, pri čemer so rastline, pridelane pri ničelni DIF, višje in imajo večje medčlenke stebla kot rastline, pridelane pri negativni DIF. Drugi pomembni morfogenetični odzivi na negativno vrednost DIF (t.j. če je dnevna temperatura nižja od nočne temperature) vključujejo krajše listne in storževe peclje ter liste.
Razlike pri podaljšanju medčlenkov in listov so posledica razlik v procesu daljšanja in/ali delitve celic. Če je DIF negativna, sta oba procesa zavrta, kar je lahko posledica zmanjšane dejavnosti giberelina v podapikalnem rastnem vršičku (rastnem tkivu). Berelin je rastlinski hormon, ki spodbuja rast rastline. DIF ima največji učinek na podaljšanje stebla v obdobju hitre rasti, zato so sadike občutljivejše na razlike med dnevno in nočno temperaturo v primerjavi z odraslimi rastlinami. Negativna DIF v zgodnji stopnji podaljšanja stebla je zato pomembna za omejitev višine rastline.
Podaljšanje stebla lahko povzroči tudi kratek padec temperature (za približno dve uri) v 24-urnem dnevnem ciklu rasti, običajno v temnem obdobju ali neposredno pred prvo dnevno svetlobo. Zdi se, da je odzivnost na temperaturne spremembe najmočnejša v prvih urah svetlega obdobja pri dolgodnevnih in kratkodnevnih rastlinah ter tistih z nevtralno dolžino dneva. Tako bo padec temperature v zadnjih dveh urah noči vplival na višino rastline. To v rastlinjakih običajno preprosto doseči jeseni v hladnih podnebjih zaradi naravno nizke nočne temperature.
Sprememba občutljivosti podaljšanja stebla na temperaturo v dnevnem in nočnem obdobju lahko nadzira endogeni ritem rasti. Bioritem rasti (ki traja približno 24 ur) so prepoznali leta 1994 v Chrysanthemumu. Podaljšanje rastlinskega stebla v 24-urnem svetlem in temnem ciklu ni konstantno. Kratkodnevne in dolgodnevne rastline, ki jih gojimo v pogojih za spodbujanje nastanka cvetov, se ponoči daljšajo hitreje kot podnevi. Orhideje za cvetenje potrebujejo obdobje nočne nizke temperature.
Integracija temperature je ena od strategij, ki jih uporabljajo gojitelji. Izračunajo najnižjo in najvišjo temperaturo posameznih vrst rastlin in pustijo, da ta niha, pri čemer še vedno ohranjajo določeno dolgoročno povprečno temperaturo. Ta strategija v kar največji meri uporablja naravno toploto.
Temperatura zraka je primarni okoljski dejavnik, ki vpliva na razvoj rastlin in na hitrost rasti. Temperatura zraka pa nikoli ni dejavnik, ki je ločen od drugih. Vsak dejavnik rasti rastlin je povezan z vsemi drugimi dejavniki, izziv pa je najti šibke člene te verige. Ta članek je raziskal številne od teh dejavnikov, obstajajo pa še drugi, ki so prav tako pomembno, kot sta vodno ravnovesje in posredno tudi transpiracija. Vse, kar se z rastlino dogaja, se zgodi pri kontrolni točki temperature zraka – obvladovanje tega je prvi korak na dolgi poti do uspešne pridelave.

4 out of 10 children die from chronic malnutrition.
Chronic malnutrition is a key factor in the spread of infectious diseases due to the lack of nutrients in the body and the resulting weakening of the immune system. Now, at the III World Congress on Nutrition and Public Health, the risks, possible solutions, and the importance of preventing them have been highlighted.
The latest data on chronic malnutrition show that between 35 and 40 percent of deaths before the age of five are caused by chronic malnutrition. This was a major cause of infectious diseases in developing countries, which have increased significantly in recent years.
Malnutrition, a cause of infectious diseases
When malnutrition becomes chronic, the immune system is completely unprotected due to the chronic lack of calories and protein. As a result, the body will not have enough defenses to fight off some infectious diseases, such as Ebola, malaria, AIDS, or influenza, and other diseases such as tuberculosis, diarrhea, and various respiratory diseases.
The main consequence of this is that the body, being completely unprotected, makes people suffering from chronic malnutrition more vulnerable to complications that can lead to death. In addition, the effectiveness of vaccines is significantly reduced in them, making any treatment even more difficult.
Lower mortality through community nutrition
The immune system is strongly affected by the harmful effects of malnutrition. In addition to changes in size and weight, people suffering from malnutrition lack nutrients, calories, and protein, which weaken their immune system. The most serious consequence of these acute levels of malnutrition is an increased risk of other types of diseases, such as respiratory diseases, intestinal diseases, and tuberculosis.
Now, at the III World Congress on Nutrition and Public Health, a group of experts is trying to raise public awareness of the risks of chronic malnutrition and to find solutions that will successfully reduce these levels of malnutrition and, consequently, the infectious diseases they cause, both in the short and long term. Community nutrition, therefore, seems to be an important solution to address the problem and provides the population with a range of tools to reduce mortality.
Preventing malnutrition, a major goal
Health and economic improvements in some developing countries have led to a reduction in mortality from malnutrition. In the last twenty years, these figures have decreased from 53 to 40 percent. However, these figures are still very high and could rise again to higher levels in the current crisis context. The social, health, and economic setbacks that some countries have suffered in recent years of crisis can also lead to a setback in the fight against malnutrition and its devastating effects on society.
Therefore, in the current context, improvements in hygiene or vaccination programs, although still important for preventing the spread of disease and increasing the number of deaths, have ceased to be the main goal of prevention projects. Now, finding solutions for diseases such as obesity, malnutrition, cardiovascular diseases, cognitive impairment, or a sedentary lifestyle is a priority.
Patricia Núñez de Arenas

Podhranjenost, vzrok nalezljivih bolezni
Ko podhranjenost postane kronična podhranjenost, je imunski sistem zaradi kroničnega pomanjkanja kalorij in beljakovin popolnoma nezaščiten. Na imunski sistem močno vplivajo škodljivi učinki podhranjenosti. Applied to the affected area it is used to clean wounds, help remove contact lenses, and help with dry eyes. The customs, traditions, and folk practices surrounding All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day.

All Saints' Day, celebrated on November 1st, was renamed "Day of the Dead" during the communist era. After independence, it was renamed "Day of Remembrance for the Dead." This is similar to renaming Christmas to "Day of Winter" or Easter to "Day of Spring."

This renaming is not only inaccurate but also changes the meaning and significance of the holiday. What exactly do we celebrate on November 1st? For most days of the year, we remember specific saints. Throughout world history, there have been countless unknown saints whom the Catholic Church has never recognized and may never recognize. These unknown saints are celebrated on November 1st. Therefore, November 1st is the feast day of all saints, or all those who, according to Catholic Church belief, are in heaven. November 2nd is the feast day of the faithful departed in purgatory. According to Catholic Church belief, the faithful departed in purgatory are those who have been saved but are still purifying themselves of unconfessed sins.

Therefore, until 3:00 PM, November 1st is traditionally a day of joy, not mourning, as it is the feast day of all saints. However, after 3:00 PM on November 1st, the solemnity and joy of All Saints' Day begin to give way to seriousness and mourning, as it is the eve of the feast of the faithful departed.

How were these two holidays celebrated in Slovenia and in Catholic regions of Europe and the world? The day before All Saints' Day (October 31st) was traditionally a day of fasting and abstinence from meat. This meant that people could only have three meals on October 31st. They could eat their fill at the main meal, but they were not allowed to eat meat from warm-blooded animals at any meal. This fast and abstinence from meat were waived if October 31st fell on a Sunday (as fasting is not traditionally observed on Sundays). On November 1st, until 3:00 PM, the holiday was celebrated with solemnity and joy. In Slovenia, bells rang to call people to Mass. The Masses were solemn, sung, and festive. People did not wear black to Mass. The liturgical color for this holiday was white, due to the joy and solemnity. Churches were decorated with flowers.

At 3:00 PM, solemn litanies of all saints were sung in the churches. The bells rang one last time to call people to the afternoon litanies. Some people already wore black, as they were preparing to visit the cemetery. During the solemn afternoon litanies, the liturgical color was still white, and the church was still decorated with flowers. After the litanies, the flowers were removed from the church. A "tomb" was placed in the church. The tomb was an empty coffin. It was covered with a black cloth, and three candles were placed on each side (six candles in total). At 3:00 PM, the "Libera" (prayers for the dead) were sung. The priest was already wearing black instead of white. Due to the eve of the feast of the faithful departed, the time of seriousness and mourning had begun. After the prayers at the tomb, people went to the cemetery, where prayers for the dead were said, and the graves were sprinkled with holy water. The bells no longer rang with joy but only tolled.

At 5:00 PM or 6:00 PM on November 1st, the three parts of the Rosary were prayed for the dead in the churches. Around 8:00 PM or 9:00 PM, the bells rang for the faithful departed in purgatory.

In some parts of Slovenia, it was customary to prepare food and drink for the faithful departed in the kitchen or living room on the evening of November 1st, as it was believed that the faithful departed would come to the house at night and partake of the food and drink in spirit. This belief was largely symbolic, as people did not truly believe it, but it was a remnant of pagan beliefs. Since the souls in purgatory were only symbolically partaking of the food and drink, the food and drink remained untouched, and the family ate and drank it the next day. In some places, the organ in the church was left unlocked on the evening of November 1st, with the belief that the souls would come from purgatory to the church at night and have Mass, during which they would play the organ. The saying was that they would only play the black keys. People did not truly believe this, but it was just a joke, a remnant of pagan times.

November 2nd was a day of seriousness and mourning. In some places, the bells rang for the faithful departed as early as 5:00 AM or 6:00 AM. Three times every 15 minutes (as the saying goes). In many parts of Slovenia, families woke up early on November 2nd and prayed the three parts of the Rosary for the faithful departed around 5:00 AM. There were no celebrations, concerts, or festivities on November 2nd. Taverns were empty, as people stayed home. Churches were not decorated with flowers. The altar was covered with a black cloth. Empty coffins (tombs) were placed in the churches. Three Requiem Masses were celebrated on November 2nd. The first two were silent, meaning the priest only read and did not sing, and only Slovenian hymns for the dead were sung. The last Requiem was sung, meaning the priest sang, and Latin texts were sung in Gregorian chant. Traditionally, male choirs sang at the sung Requiems, as men have deeper voices than women, and male singing created a greater sense of seriousness and mourning. After the last sung Requiem, the "Libera" was sung, followed by prayers at the tomb, and then the procession to the cemetery. At the cemetery, prayers for the dead were said, and the graves were sprinkled with holy water (as on the previous day). After the prayers, the bells rang for the faithful departed.

There was a special custom that occurred every few years if November 1st fell on a Saturday. Traditionally, the feast of the faithful departed is not celebrated on Sundays. If November 1st fell on a Saturday, the feast of the faithful departed was traditionally celebrated on Monday, November 3rd. In this case, November 1st was a day of joy and celebration, and the seriousness and mourning began the following day, Sunday afternoon, and continued until Monday, November 3rd. In this case, the prayers for the dead began on Sunday, November 2nd, after 3:00 PM, and ended on Monday, November 3rd, in the evening, meaning the prayers and devotions for the dead were moved back by one day.

Today, with the introduction of modernism after the Second Vatican Council, many of these customs have been abandoned, and some things have been changed. For example, the black liturgical color is rarely used on November 2nd in modern liturgy, and purple is used instead. In addition, the tomb, covered with a black cloth and surrounded by six candles, is no longer present in post-conciliar liturgy. In addition, according to the post-conciliar calendar, the feast of the faithful departed is always celebrated on November 2nd, even if it falls on a Sunday. In churches, traditional Requiem Masses are no longer celebrated, but post-conciliar Masses for the dead are celebrated. Many people prefer November 1st as the day of mourning, and many no longer know what is celebrated on November 2nd, but many of the customs I have mentioned have still been preserved. With the spread of Tridentine Masses in recent times and the increase in the number of Catholic traditionalists, the traditional celebration of All Saints' Day and the feast of the faithful departed is gradually being revived in our country, in Europe, and in the Western world.

Since we can go to the cemetery whenever we want, regardless of whether it is an ordinary day or a holiday, we can of course go to the cemetery on the morning of November 1st, but according to our religious, cultural, and folk tradition, if we go to the cemetery on November 1st, we should go in the afternoon, and November 2nd is a day for visiting cemeteries. Therefore, we can conclude that the true Slovenian and Western tradition is that the whole day is for visiting graves on November 2nd, and only in the afternoon on November 1st, and not that November 1st is the "day of the dead" and mourning, and we "forgot" what is celebrated on November 2nd.

MATIJA ŠORLI

Obredi, navade in ljudske šege ob prvem in drugem novembru
Prvega novembra je praznik vseh svetih, ki ga je komunizem preimenoval v »dan mrtvih«, po osamosvojitvi pa je ta dan dobil ime »dan spomina na mrtve«. To je tako, kot če bi npr. božič poimenovali v »dan zime« ali pa veliko noč v »dan pomladi«.
Tako poimenovanje ni samo napačno, ampak spremeni tudi smisel in pomen tega praznika. Kaj sploh praznujemo prvega novembra? Večino dni v letu se spominjamo določenih svetnikov in svetnic. V svetovni zgodovini je živelo ogromno neznanih svetnikov in svetnic, ki jih katoliška Cerkev nikoli ni in morda nikoli ne bo razglasila za svetnike ali za blažene. Ti neznani svetniki pa praznujejo svoj praznik prvega novembra. Tako je prvi november praznik vseh svetnikov oziroma vseh, ki so po verovanju katoliške Cerkve v nebesih. Drugega novembra pa je praznik vernih duš v vicah. Verne duše v vicah so po verovanju katoliške Cerkve rajni, ki so se sicer zveličali in niso v peklu, a se zaradi nespokorjenih grehov iz svojega življenja očiščujejo v vicah.
Zato je prvi november do 15. ure popoldne tradicionalno dan veselja in ne dan žalovanja, ker se praznuje velik praznik vseh svetnikov. Že prvega novembra po 15. ure pa se slovesnost in veselje praznika vseh svetnikov začenjata prevešati v resnost in žalovanje, ker je prvega novembra po 15. uri že predvečer praznika vernih duš v vicah.
Kako je na Slovenskem in po katoliških predelih Evrope ter sveta potekalo praznovanje teh dveh praznikov? Dan pred praznikom vseh svetih (31. oktobra) sta bila tradicionalno post in zdržek od mesa. To pomeni, da so ljudje 31. oktobra lahko imeli le tri obroke hrane. Do sitega so se lahko najedli le pri glavnem obroku in pri nobenem obroku niso smeli jesti mesa toplokrvnih živali. Ta post in zdržek od mesa pa sta odpadla, če je 31. oktober prišel na nedeljo (na nedeljo tudi tradicionalno ne sme biti posta). Prvega novembra do 15. ure je praznik potekal v znamenju slovesnosti in veselja. Na Slovenskem so zvonovi vabili k svetim mašah s prazničnim pritrkavanjem. Svete maše so bile slovesne, pete in praznične. Ljudje k svetim mašam niso hodili v črnih oblačilih. Liturgična barva tega praznika je bila zaradi veselja in slovesnosti tega praznika bela. Cerkve so bile okrašene z rožami.
Ob 14. uri tega praznika so bile po cerkvah slovesne in pete litanije vseh svetnikov. K popoldanskih litanijam so zvonovi v zvonikih še zadnjič vabili s prazničnim pritrkavanjem. Nekateri ljudje pa so k litanijam že hodili v črnini, ker so se pripravljali na obisk pokopališča. Pri slovesnih in petih popoldanskih litanijah je bila liturgična barva še zadnjič bela, cerkev je bila še vedno okrašena z rožami. Po zaključenih litanijah so odstranili iz cerkve rože. V cerkev so postavili »tombo«. Tomba je prazna krsta. Tombo so pokrili s črnim prtom ter na njeno desno in levo stran dali po tri sveče (skupaj šest sveč). Ob 15. uri je sledilo petje libere za rajne. Pri petju libere je bil duhovnik že oblečen v črno barvo namesto v belo. Zaradi predvečera praznika vernih duš v vicah se je že začel čas resnosti in žalovanja. Po obredih ob tombi je sledil odhod na pokopališče, kjer je bil opravljen obred za rajne in kropljenje grobov. Na zvonove se ni nič več pritrkavalo, ampak samo še zvonilo.
Ob 17. ali ob 18. uri prvega novembra so po cerkvah molili vse tri dele svetega rožnega venca za rajne, okoli 20. ali 21. ure pa se je na zvonikih že zvonilo za verne duše v vicah.
V nekaterih predelih Slovenije je bila navada, da so prvega novembra zvečer v kuhinji ali v izbi »pripravili hrano in pijačo za verne duše v vicah«, ker je veljalo »ljudsko verovanje«, da bodo ponoči prišle v hišo verne duše v vicah in se bodo »v duhu pogostile s hrano in pijačo«. To verovanje je bilo le simbolično, ker ljudje v to v resnici niso verjeli, ampak je šlo za ostanek poganskih verovanj. Ker pa so se »duše v vicah ponoči le simbolično pogostile« in ne v resnici, sta hrana in pijača ostali nedotaknjeni ter so jo drugi dan domači v hiši pojedli in popili. Ponekod so v cerkvah prvega novembra zvečer na korih pustili odklenjene orgle »v verovanju«, da bodo ponoči duše prišle iz vic v cerkev in bodo imele v njej mašo, pri kateri bodo tudi igrale na orgle. Ljudski rek je bil, »da bodo igrale le na črne tipke«. Tudi v to ljudje v resnici niso verjeli, ampak je šlo le za šego, ki je bila še ostanek iz poganskih časov.
Drugi november je bil cel dan v resnosti in v žalovanju. Ponekod se je že okoli pete ali šeste ure zjutraj zvonilo za verne duše v vicah. Trikrat na vsakih 15 minut (v ljudskem reku »na tri cuge«). Po mnogih predelih Slovenije so družine 2. novembra zgodaj vstale in zmolile okoli pete ure zjutraj vse tri dele svetega rožnega venca za verne duše v vicah. Drugega novembra ni smelo biti nobenih zabav, koncertov in praznovanj. Gostilne domačih gostov niso videle, ker so domačini na ta dan v svojem kraju opustili njihov obisk. Cerkve so bile na ta dan brez okrasov z rožami. Prostor za maševanje pred oltarjem je bil pogrnjen s črnim prtom. Po cerkvah so bile na ta dan postavljene prazne krste – tombe. Drugega novembra so se maševali trije requiemi (po slovensko »črne maše« za rajne). Prva dva requiema sta bila tiha, se pravi, da ju je mašnik le bral in ne pel ter da so se pri tihih requiemih pele le slovenske žalne pesmi za rajne, zadnji requiem pa je bil pet, se pravi, da ga je mašnik pel in da so se peli latinski teksti v gregorijanskem koralu. Tradicionalno so pri petih requiemih peli moški pevski zbori, ker imajo moški temnejše glasove kot ženske in je moško petje zbujalo občutek večje resnosti in žalovanja. Po zadnjem pétem requiemu je sledilo petje libere, po njem so sledile molitve ob tombi, nato pa odhod na pokopališče. Pri pokopališkem križu so se nato izvajali obredi za rajne, na koncu pa je sledilo še kropljenje grobov na pokopališču (enako kot en dan prej). Po zaključenih obredih je sledilo zvonjenje za verne duše v vicah.
Obstajala pa je posebnost, ki je tradicionalno prišla na vsakih nekaj let, če je prvi november prišel na soboto. V nedeljo se tradicionalno ne sme praznovati praznika vernih duš v vicah. Če je prvi november prišel na soboto, se je tradicionalno praznoval praznik vernih duš v vicah v ponedeljek, 3. novembra. V tem primeru je bil prvi november cel dan čas veselja in slovesnih praznovanj, resnost in žalovanje pa sta se začela šele naslednji dan v nedeljo popoldne ter sta se nadaljevala in zaključila v ponedeljek, 3. novembra. Tako so se v tem primeru obredi za rajne začeli v nedeljo, 2. novembra, po 15. uri popoldne, zaključili pa v ponedeljek, 3. novembra, zvečer, se pravi, obredi in molitve za rajne so se za en dan premaknili.
Danes z uvedbo modernizma po 2. vatikanskem koncilu je bilo precej teh navad opuščenih, nekatere stvari pa so spremenjene. Npr. redko se 2. novembra pri moderni liturgiji še uporablja črna liturgična barva, ampak se uporablja namesto črne barve vijoličasta, poleg tega pri pokoncilskem bogoslužju ni prisotna tomba, ki je pokrita s črnim prtom in je okoli nje šest sveč. Poleg tega se po pokoncilskem koledarju praznik vernih duš vedno obhaja 2. novembra, tudi če ta pride na nedeljo. V cerkvah se po novem prav tako ne mašujejo več tradicionalni requiemi, ampak pokoncilske maše za rajne. Ljudje imajo za dan žalovanja raje prvi november namesto drugi, za drugi november mnogi sploh ne vedo več, kaj se takrat v resnici praznuje, vendar so se mnoge navade, ki sem jih omenil, kljub temu še vedno ohranile. Z širitvijo tridentinskih bogoslužij v zadnjem času in z večanjem števila katoliških tradicionalistov pa se tradicionalno praznovanje praznika vseh svetih in vernih duš v vicah pri nas, po Evropi in po zahodnem svetu postopoma ponovno oživlja.
Ker gremo lahko na pokopališče, kadar hočemo, ne glede na to, ali gre za navaden dan ali pa za kateri koli praznik, gremo seveda lahko na pokopališče tudi prvega novembra dopoldne, ampak v skladu z našo versko, kulturno in ljudsko tradicijo pa je, da če se gre prvega novembra na pokopališče, naj se gre šele popoldne, drugi november pa je cel dan čas za obiskovanje pokopališč. Tako lahko ugotovimo, da je prava slovenska in zahodna tradicija, da je celodnevni čas za obiskovanje grobov v resnici 2. november, prvega pa le popoldne, ne pa, da je prvi november »dan mrtvih« in žalovanja, za drugi november pa smo »pozabili«, kaj se na ta dan v resnici praznuje.
MATIJA ŠORLI

Zinc is one of those minerals that is essential for life. It comes from the soil, is absorbed by plants (including those that produce edible fruits), and then animals and humans eat those plants. For us, zinc is important for maintaining a healthy immune system, building beneficial fats in the body, breaking down certain enzymes, and creating DNA. A lack of zinc in the body can cause growth retardation, stomach problems, impotence, hair loss, a weakened immune system, and other potential problems. Since the human body cannot produce zinc on its own, it is essential to obtain it regularly through diet. Zinc can be found in many foods, but only a few contain it in significant amounts.

We often lack zinc.
Zinc is a trace element that all cells need. The body contains about two grams of it. About 70 percent of it is found in bones, skin, hair, muscles, kidneys, liver, pancreas, eyes, and the prostate. Its metabolism in tissues is slow. Because the body does not store large amounts of zinc that can be used when intake is insufficient, a constant and adequate intake through food is necessary. Research shows that half of the people consume too little of it.
Studies in the UK have found that 43 percent of men and 45 percent of women, aged 19 to 50, do not get enough zinc from their daily diet. In children aged four or older, the percentage was staggering, at 89 percent. Among older people, 62 percent had too little zinc.
By adding just a little zinc supplement to the diet or by consuming foods rich in zinc, we can significantly reduce cases of diarrhea, pneumonia, or malaria in developing countries. By strengthening the immune system, zinc can prevent up to 38 percent of diarrhea attacks, reduce the number of acute respiratory infections by 45 percent, and reduce malaria by 35 percent.
Zinc performs many specific functions in metabolism.
- It is a component or activator of many enzymes in the metabolism of proteins, carbohydrates, fats, and nucleic acids, hormones and receptors (cellular binding sites), in the storage of insulin, and in the immune system.
- Zinc can help improve fertility in both men and women. It also benefits prostate function.
- Because it increases insulin concentration, it helps people with underactive thyroids and also diabetics.
Because zinc is involved in the function of so many different body systems, it has other functions as well.
- Today, it has been proven that zinc speeds up wound healing and skin inflammation, making it a suitable ingredient in various creams and pastes for acne, burns, eczema, psoriasis, and rosacea. It also works well on hair and scalp.
- It has been shown that zinc slows down vision loss in age-related (degenerative) macular degeneration, a common cause of blindness in people over 50.
- In a recent study in Japan, tinnitus improved after using a zinc supplement.
- Zinc can also help with osteoporosis, hemorrhoids, intestinal inflammation, and ulcers.
Symptoms and consequences of zinc deficiency
It has been found that the loss of zinc through secretions and through the skin is at least about 2.2 milligrams in men and at least 1.6 milligrams per day in women. With an average utilization rate (absorption rate) of 30 percent, an average of 5.5 to 7.5 milligrams of zinc must be consumed daily to compensate for these losses. In the second half of pregnancy, the average needs are greater by 0.8 milligrams per day, and during breastfeeding, by one full milligram per day.
In severe deficiency, decreased ability to taste, loss of appetite, skin inflammation (dermatitis), hair loss, diarrhea, and neuropsychiatric disorders occur.
In addition to the above, growth retardation, disorders in male sexual development and reproductive functions, delayed wound healing, and increased susceptibility to infections as a sign of a weakened immune system occur.
Zinc deficiency is more common in people with impaired or incomplete absorption of nutrients in the intestine (malabsorption syndrome), in parenteral nutrition, and in extensive burns.
Stressful events, surgical procedures, major operations, parasitic diseases, and infections also affect zinc utilization.
On the other hand, the toxicity threshold for zinc is very high, and it is difficult to consume too much of it through food. However, the zinc content can be greatly increased by cooking or storing foods containing acid, or in water in zinc-coated (galvanized) containers. After consuming such foods, poisoning can also occur. Acute poisoning with, for example, two grams of zinc causes gastrointestinal disturbances and fever. Long-term intake of more than 100 milligrams per day causes hypochromic anemia and neutropenia, probably due to interaction with copper. Even short-term intake of about 50 milligrams per day leads to interactions with iron and copper metabolism. Therefore, intake of more than 20 milligrams per day is not recommended.
Which foods are rich in zinc?
Avocado
The recommended daily intake of zinc for men is about 11mg, and for women, 8 mg. Avocado is one of the few fruits that has a high concentration of zinc, containing almost 2mg per fruit. It is usually associated with the preparation of sauces, but it can also be eaten raw, sliced in a sandwich, in salads, or in smoothies. Because avocado turns brown when exposed to air, it is best to eat it as soon as possible, or wrap it tightly in foil that has been drizzled with a little lime or lemon juice and store it in the refrigerator.
Pomegranate
Right after avocado, pomegranate is the second-best source of zinc among fruits. It contains about 1 mg of zinc per serving. The juicy seeds that peek out when the fruit is opened can be eaten fresh or dried and sprinkled on sauces, yogurt, or salads.
Pumpkin seeds
In addition to their high zinc content, pumpkin seeds are also rich in other beneficial substances. They can help with sleep problems, and because they have a high content of omega-3 fatty acids, they also help maintain blood sugar levels. The results of the latest research also consider them as anti-inflammatory food. 100 g of pumpkin seeds contains about 8 mg of zinc.
Garlic
Garlic contains a long list of medicinal effects – including zinc. Of course, it does not contain it in huge quantities, but because of all its other beneficial properties, it proves to be a good addition to foods that contain zinc in larger quantities. 100 g of garlic contains about 1 mg of zinc.
Egg yolk
If you prefer egg whites, think again. Yolks are a much richer source of zinc. In addition, the yolk also contains most of the egg vitamins, such as vitamin A, E, D, and K. In addition, it also contains many minerals. 100 g of egg yolk contains about 5 mg of zinc.
Dark chocolate
If you need another reason to eat dark chocolate, the fact that it has a high zinc content is more than excellent. 100 g of dark chocolate contains about 10 mg of zinc. But be careful! You may still not overdo it with chocolate, as in addition to the level of zinc and antioxidants, it also has a high level of calories.

Okoli 70 odstotkov ga je v kosteh, koži, laseh, mišicah, ledvicah, jetrih, trebušni slinavki, očeh in v prostati. Njegovo presnavljanje v tkivih je počasno. Ker telo ne vsebuje velikih zalog cinka, ki bi jih lahko uporabilo ob premajhni preskrbi, je potreben stalen zadosten vnos s hrano. Raziskave pa kažejo, da ga polovica ljudi užije premalo.
Raziskave v Veliki Britaniji so odkrile, da 43 odstotkov moških in 45 odstotkov žensk, starih med 19. in 50. letom, z vsakodnevno hrano ne dobi dovolj cinka. Pri otrocih, starih štiri leta ali več, je bil odstotek osupljiv, kar 89 odstotkov. Med starejšimi osebami jih je imelo premalo cinka 62 odstotkov.
Z dodajanjem le malo cinkovih dopolnil k prehrani ali z uživanjem živil, ki so bogata s cinkom lahko zelo zmanjšamo primere driske, pljučnice ali malarije v deželah v razvoju. Cink lahko s tem, da okrepi imunski sistem, prepreči do 38 odstotkov napadov driske, za 45 odstotkov zmanjša število akutnih respiratornih okužb in za 35 odstotkov malarije.
Cink v presnovi izpolnjuje številne posebne naloge
- Je sestavina ali aktivator številnih encimov v presnovi beljakovin, ogljikovih hidratov, maščob in nukleinskih kislin, hormonov in receptorjev (celična prijemališča), pri skladiščenju inzulina in v imunskem sistemu.
- Cink lahko pomaga pri izboljšanju plodnosti tako moških kot žensk. Koristi tudi delovanju prostate.
- Ker poveča koncentracijo inzulina, pomaga ljudem s premalo dejavno ščitnico in tudi sladkornim bolnikom.
Ker je cink vpleten v delovanje toliko različnih telesnih sistemov, ima še druge naloge
- Danes je dokazano, da cink pospeši celjenje ran in kožnih vnetij, zato je primerna sestavina raznih krem in past za mozoljavost, opekline, ekcem, luskavico in rozaceo. Dobro deluje tudi na lase in lasišče.
- Pokazalo se je, da cink upočasni izgubo vida pri starostni obrabi (degeneraciji) rumene pege, pogostem vzroku za slepoto pri starejših od 50 let.
- V nedavni raziskavi na Japonskem se je zvenenje v ušesih izboljšalo po uporabi cinkovega dopolnila.
- Cink lahko pomaga tudi pri osteoporozi, hemoroidih, vnetju črevesja in razjedah.
Simptomi in posledice pomanjkanja cinka
Ugotovili so, da znaša izguba cinka z izločki in skozi kožo pri moškem vsaj okoli 2,2 miligrama, pri ženski pa najmanj 1,6 miligrama na dan. Pri povprečnem izkoristku (absorbcijska stopnja), ki znaša 30 odstotkov, je za nadomestitev teh izgub treba na dan zaužiti povprečno od 5,5 miligrama do 7,5 miligrama cinka. V drugi polovici nosečnosti so povprečne potrebe večje za 0,8 miligrama na dan in v času dojenja za en cel miligram na dan.
Pri hudem pomanjkanju nastopijo zmanjšana zmožnost okušanja, pomanjkanje teka, vnetje kože (dermatitis), izpadanje las, driska in nevropsihične motnje.
Poleg omenjenega se pojavljajo zaostajanje v rasti, motnje pri moškem spolnem razvoju in pri reprodukcijskih nalogah, upočasnjeno celjenje ran in povečana občutljivost za okužbe kot izraz slabega imunskega sistema.
Pomanjkanje cinka se pogosteje pojavlja pri okvarjenem ali nepopolnem vsrkanju hranil v črevesju (malabsorbcijski sindrom), parenteralnem hranjenju, pri obsežnih opeklinah …
Na izrabo cinka pa vplivajo tudi stresni dogodki, kirurški posegi, velike operacije, zajedavska obolenja in okužbe.
Po drugi strani je prag strupenosti za cink zelo visok in ga s hrano težko zaužijemo preveč. Vendar se vsebnost cinka s kuhanjem ali skladiščenjem živil, ki vsebujejo kislino, ali vode v s cinkom prevlečenih (galvanotehnično) posodah lahko močno poveča. Po uživanju takih živil lahko pride tudi do zastrupitve. Akutna zastrupitev z na primer dvema gramoma cinka povzroči želodčno-črevesne motnje in vročino. Dolgotrajen vnos več kot 100 miligramov na dan pa hipokromno anemijo in nevtropenijo, verjetno zaradi součinkovanja z bakrom. Celo kratkotrajen vnos približno 50 miligramov na dan pripelje do součinkovanj s presnovo železa in bakra. Zato odsvetujemo vnos, večji od 20 miligramov na dan.
Katera živila so bogata s cinkom?
Avokado
Redni vnos cinka v telo naj bi za moške znašal približno 11mg, za ženske pa 8 mg. Avokado je eden izmed redkih sadežev, ki ima visoko koncentracijo cinka saj ga na sadež vsebuje skoraj 2mg. Običajno se njegovo uživanje povezuje s pripravo omak, lahko pa se ga uživa tudi surovega, narezanega v sendviču, v solatah ali pa v smoothijih. Ker avokado v stiku z zrakom porjavi ga je najbolje zaužiti čim prej, v skrajnem primeru pa ga lahko tesno ovijemo v folijo, ki smo jo pred tem pokapali z malo limetinega ali limoninega soka ter ga tako shranimo v hladilniku.
Granatno jabolko
Takoj za avokadom je granatno jabolko drugi najboljši vir cinka med sadeži. Vsebuje približno 1 mg cinka na porcijo. Sočna semena, ki pokukajo na plano, ko sadež razpremo, lahko uživamo sveža ali pa jih posušimo ter jih posujemo po omakah, jogurtih ali solatah.
Bučna semena
Poleg visoke vsebovanosti cinka so bučna semena bogata tudi z drugimi telesu koristnimi snovmi. Tako lahko pomagajo pri težava s spanjem, ker pa imajo visoko vsebovanost omega 3 maščobnih kislin pa skrbijo tudi za nivo sladkorja v krvi. Rezultati najnovejših raziskav jih med drugim celo obravnavajo kot protivnetno hrano. 100 g bučnih semen vsebuje okoli 8 mg cinka.
Česen
Česen vsebuje precej dolg seznam zdravilnih učinkov – med drugim vsebuje tudi cink. Seveda tega ne vsebuje v gromozanskih količinah a zaradi vseh svojih drugih koristnih lastnosti se izkaže kot dober dodatek k jedem, ki cink vsebujejo v večjih količinah. 100 g česna vsebuje okoli 1 mg cinka.
Jajčni rumenjak
Če imate raje beljak, premislite še enkrat. Rumenjaki so namreč precej bolj bogat vir cinka. Poleg tega rumenjak vsebuje tudi večino jajčnih vitaminov kot so denimo vitamin A, E, D in K. Poleg tega pa vsebuje tudi mnogo mineralov. 100 g jajčnega rumenjaka vsebuje okoli 5 mg cinka.
Temna čokolada
Če potrebujete še kakšen dodaten razlog za uživanje tene čokolade je podatek o visoki vsebovanosti cinka več kot odličen. 100 g temne čokolade namreč vsebuje okoli 10 mg cinka. A pazljivo! S čokolado morda vseeno ne pretiravajte, saj je poleg ravni cinka in antioksidantov v njej visoka tudi raven kalorij.

Balance is the ability to maintain the body in a stable position. In addition to stabilizing the body, we also stabilize the image perceived by our eyes. The functioning of balance depends on the balance center in the cerebellum and the balance organ in the inner ear. Balance also depends on the ability to perceive information from the environment and from one's own body in space. This occurs through external senses (sight, hearing, skin) and internal senses (muscles, tendons, joint capsules). Balance disorders primarily occur in later life.

Lili Milanković, MSc in Kinesiology, KinVital Kinesiology Center. Photo: Kinoks
Changes in the Central Nervous System and Musculoskeletal System
Changes in the central nervous system and musculoskeletal system primarily occur in older adults. In addition to vision and hearing, vestibular functions (responsible for balance, head and body position) and somatosensory functions (information about pressure/touch, proprioception, temperature, and pain) also deteriorate. In addition to age, the main risk factors for falls and related fractures include impaired gait ability, muscle weakness, poorer static and dynamic balance, chronic musculoskeletal disorders, and low bone density.
All these factors negatively affect the maintenance of balance and functional abilities. Age is also associated with a reduced ability to stand on one leg with eyes open and closed. Reduced balance abilities consequently lead to an increased risk of falls and, consequently, to injuries to the musculoskeletal system and a loss of independence in activities of daily living.
Microarchitectural Changes and Osteoporosis
One of the most well-known diagnoses in older adults and even in somewhat younger individuals is osteoporosis, which is the most common metabolic, systemic bone disease. It is characterized by low bone mass and microarchitectural changes, which increases the risk of bone fractures, especially in the hip, spine, and wrist. It most often affects the elderly population. The longer an individual's lifespan, the greater the chance of developing the disease. The presence of this disease in older people poses a high risk of loss of balance and, consequently, of falls. As a precursor to osteoporosis, osteopenia can occur, in which bone mineral mass is lower than normal.
Effects of Regular Physical Activity
The effects of regular physical activity have been linked to maintaining and improving psychophysical health, muscle strength, general endurance, and quality of life for decades. In physical activities aimed at rehabilitation and injury prevention, special care must be taken to ensure that they are carried out in accordance with all the basic principles of exercise, namely active and conscious involvement in the training process, comprehensive development, individual approach, specialization, cyclicality and variability, increasing load, systematicity and rationality. We also take care of all these principles of exercise, which apply regardless of age, gender, level of physical fitness and the presence of diseases or injuries, in our kinesiology center.
Exercise Prevents Falls
The most suitable individual exercise for improving balance and increasing muscle strength, combined group exercise, or exercise in a home environment is the best way to prevent falls. Research shows that the most effective approach is a combination of independent exercise at home with organized and supervised group exercise. We have also observed this in our work with older adults. Improved balance after a relatively short period of exercise can also be achieved with specific sensorimotor exercise, which takes into account the importance of sensory information from the visual, vestibular, and proprioceptive systems.
The consequences of reduced ability to maintain balance are particularly critical in older adults and people with altered bone density. It is known that regular and appropriate physical activity throughout life contributes to maintaining and increasing bone density and that this prevents or at least mitigates bone changes and related fractures.
Balance and Coordination Exercises
Balance and coordination exercises, in addition to strength exercises, low-intensity aerobic exercise, and exercises to maintain posture, form the basis of physical activity in people with osteoporosis. The purpose of such exercise is to prevent or reduce the number of falls and fractures, control and reduce pain, improve gait quality, increase muscle strength and coordination, and improve overall well-being.
In people with osteopenia and those with not yet pronounced bone changes, exercises to increase and maintain bone density, moderate to high-intensity aerobic exercise (depending on the age of the participants), resistance exercises, bodyweight exercises, running, and jumping (recommended for people under 50) are in the foreground, and exercises to improve balance are a complement and good prevention for later periods. Of course, it is also important to emphasize socializing and connecting with peers and their influence on motivation for movement and thus maintaining vitality.
Balance Exercises
Before starting the exercises, ensure your safety, as a fall can occur quickly if you have poor balance. Always stand next to a wall or something stable that you can hold onto if you lose your balance. We start the exercises on a hard surface and perform them in place, and then we can move on to dynamic movement and unstable surfaces (pillow, etc.). For better concentration, you can focus on one point in front of you. This can help you achieve greater calmness and better balance while performing the exercises. To make the exercise more difficult, you can simply close your eyes and perform the exercise blindly. You can also include head movement (looking to the side). But first, of course, make sure you are safe.
Exercise 1: Shifting Weight
In this exercise, stand upright. Place your feet shoulder-width apart and shift your weight from one leg to the other. You can also try shifting your weight from your toes to your heels (you can also lift yourself onto your toes/heels). Do 10–20 repetitions.
Exercise 2: Step to the Side
Stand with your feet together. Then slowly move one leg to the side (you can also hold it in the air). The weight remains on the standing leg. Then bring the leg back and repeat with the other leg. Do 10 repetitions (5 on each side – you can do them consecutively or alternately), and you can hold the leg out to the side for several seconds.
Exercise 3: Standing with Crossed Legs and Tandem Standing
Cross your legs over each other and place your feet together. Cross your arms over your chest and hold for 20–30 seconds. If you can hold the position for longer, you can try it with your eyes closed.
The next step in the above exercise can be so-called tandem standing, in which you place one foot in front of the other.
We could say that without balance, we would not have a good quality of life, as balance is one of those abilities that allows us to walk. Because of this, we are also more independent in performing daily tasks and effective in physical and sports activities.

Ravnotežje je sposobnost, s katero telo ohranjamo v stabilnem položaju. Poleg telesa stabiliziramo tudi sliko, ki jo zaznavajo naše oči. Delovanje ravnotežja je odvisno od centra za ravnotežje v malih možganih in ravnotežnega organa, ki je v notranjem ušesu. Ravnotežje je odvisno tudi od sposobnosti zaznavanja informacij iz okolja in lastnega telesa v prostoru. To poteka prek zunanjih čutil (vid, sluh, koža) in notranjih čutil (mišice, tetive, sklepne ovojnice). Okvare ravnotežja se pojavijo predvsem v poznejšem življenjskem obdobju.
Lili Milanković, mag. kineziologije, KinVital kineziološki center. Foto: Kinoks
Spremembe na osrednjem živčevju in mišično-skeletnem sistemu
Spremembe na osrednjem živčevju in mišično-skeletnem sistemu se pojavijo predvsem pri starejših. Poleg vida in sluha se poslabšajo tudi vestibularne funkcije (odgovorne za ravnotežje, položaj glave in telesa) in somatosenzorične funkcije (informacije o pritisku/dotiku, propriocepciji, temperaturi in bolečini). Poleg starosti so glavni dejavniki tveganja za padce in z njimi povezanimi zlomi še okrnjena sposobnost hoje, mišična šibkost, slabše statično in dinamično ravnotežje, kronične mišično skeletne okvare in nizka kostna gostota.
Vsi ti faktorji negativno vplivajo na vzdrževanje ravnotežja in funkcionalne sposobnosti. Starost je povezana tudi z zmanjšano sposobnostjo stoje na eni nogi z odprtimi in zaprtimi očmi. Zmanjšane sposobnosti ohranjanja ravnotežja posledično vplivajo na povečano tveganje za padce in s tem na poškodbe mišično-skeletnega sistema ter izgubo samostojnosti v aktivnostih vsakodnevnega življenja.
Mikroarhitekturne spremembe inosteoporoza
Ena najbolj znanih diagnoz pri starostnikih in tudi nekoliko mlajših posameznikih je osteoporoza, ki je najpogostejša metabolična, sistemska bolezen kosti. Zanjo so značilne nizka kostna masa in mikroarhitekturne spremembe, kar povzroči večje tveganje za zlom kosti, predvsem kolka, hrbtenice in zapestja. Najpogosteje prizadene starejše prebivalstvo. Daljša kot je življenjska doba posameznika, večja je možnost, da ta zboli. Prisotnost te bolezni pri starejših ljudeh predstavlja visoko tveganje za izgubo ravnotežja in posledično za padce. Kot predhodnica osteoporoze pa se lahko pojavi osteopenija, pri kateri je masa kostnih mineralov nižja kot normalno.
Učinki redne gibalne aktivnosti
Učinki redne gibalne aktivnosti se že desetletja povezujejo z ohranjanjem in izboljšanjem psihofizičnega zdravja, mišične moči, splošne vzdržljivosti in na kakovosti življenja. Pri gibalnih aktivnostih, usmerjenih v rehabilitacijo in preventivo poškodb, je treba biti še posebej previden, da se izvajajo skladno z vsemi osnovnimi principi vadbe, in sicer z aktivnim in zavestnim vključevanjem v vadbeni proces, vsestranskim razvojem, individualnim pristopom, s specializacijo, cikličnostjo in spremenljivostjo, z rastočo obremenitvijo, sistematičnostjo in z racionalnostjo. Za vsa ta načela vadbe, ki veljajo ne glede na starost, spol, stopnjo telesne pripravljenosti in prisotnost bolezni ali poškodb, skrbimo tudi v našem kineziološkem centru.
Vadba preprečuje padce
Za preprečevanje padcev je najprimernejša individualna vadba za izboljšanje ravnotežja in povečanje mišične moči, kombinirana skupinska vadba ali vadba v domačem okolju. Raziskave kažejo, da je najučinkovitejša kombinacija samostojne vadbe v domačem okolju z organizirano in nadzorovano skupinsko vadbo. Zadnje smo zaznali tudi pri našem delu s starostniki. Do izboljšanja ravnotežja po precej kratkem obdobju vadbe pride tudi s specifično senzomotorično vadbo, ki upošteva pomen senzoričnih informacij z vidnega, vestibularnega in s proprioceptivnega sistema.
Posledice zmanjšane sposobnosti vzdrževanja ravnotežja so še posebej kritične pri starejših ljudeh in ljudeh s spremenjeno kostno gostoto. Znano je, da z redno in s primerno gibalno aktivnostjo skozi vsa življenjska obdobja prispevamo k ohranjanju in povečevanju kostne gostote ter da s tem preprečimo ali vsaj omilimo kostne spremembe in z njimi povezane zlome.
Vadba za ravnotežje in koordinacijo
Vadba za ravnotežje in koordinacijo poleg vaj za moč, nizkointenzivne aerobne vadbe in vaj za ohranjanje telesne drže predstavlja temelj gibalne aktivnosti pri ljudeh z osteoporozo. Namen take vadbe je preprečiti oz. zmanjšati število padcev in zlomov, nadzorovati in zmanjšati bolečino, izboljšati kakovost hoje, povečati mišično moč in koordinacijo ter izboljšati splošno dobro počutje.
Pri ljudeh z osteopenijo in tistih s še neizraženimi kostnimi spremembami so v ospredju vaje za povečevanje in ohranjanje kostne gostote, zmerno- do visokointenzivna aerobna vadba (odvisno od starosti udeležencev), vaje proti uporu, vaje z lastno telesno težo, tek in poskoki (priporočljivo za ljudi, mlajše od 50 let), vaje za izboljšanje ravnotežja pa predstavljajo dopolnitev in dobro preventivo za poznejša obdobja. Seveda pa je tu treba poudariti tudi druženje in povezovanje s sovrstniki ter njun vpliv na motivacijo za gibanje in s tem ohranjanje vitalnosti.
Vaje za ravnotežje
Preden začnete vaje, poskrbite za svojo varnost, saj lahko hitro pride do padca, če imate slabše ravnotežje. Vedno se postavite ob steno oz. ob nekaj stabilnega, česar se lahko oprimete, če izgubite ravnotežje. Vaje začnemo na trdi podlagi in jih izvajamo na mestu, nato pa lahko preidemo v dinamično gibanje in nestabilne podlage (blazina itn.). Za boljšo koncentracijo se lahko osredinimo na eno točko pred seboj. Tako lahko dosežemo večjo umirjenost in boljše ravnotežje med izvajanjem vaj. Da bi dosegli večjo težavnost vaje, lahko preprosto zapremo oči in vajo izvajamo miže. Prav tako lahko vključimo premik glave (pogled v stran). Najprej pa seveda poskrbimo za svojo varnost.
1. vaja: Prenašanje težišča
Pri tej vaji stojimo pokončno. Stopala postavimo v širino bokov in prenašamo težo telesa z ene na drugo nogo. Lahko poskusimo tudi tako, da prenašamo težišče s prstov proti petam (zraven se lahko tudi dvignemo na prste/pete). Naredimo 10–20 ponovitev.

Recently, the term "carbon footprint" has been mentioned more and more frequently. Can you tell us what it actually refers to and when it all started?
A carbon footprint is the total amount of greenhouse gases emitted by an individual, organization, or community through their activities, either directly or indirectly. A carbon footprint can also be calculated for a product, in which case it represents the total emissions of greenhouse gases generated throughout its life cycle – from the extraction of raw materials, through transportation, processing, storage, sale, use, and finally, disposal.
A carbon footprint is an indicator of the impact on climate change. The fact that human activities that release greenhouse gases affect the climate has been known since the late 19th century. In the 1960s, convincing evidence emerged that carbon dioxide (CO2) is the most important greenhouse gas causing global warming. Since the beginning of the industrial revolution, humans have significantly altered the composition of the Earth's atmosphere by rapidly and dramatically increasing the concentration of CO2, disrupting the balance between CO2 sources and sinks. This has jeopardized the stability of the climate system. The increase in CO2 concentration is largely due to the burning of fossil fuels (oil, coal, and natural gas), as well as human-induced changes in ecosystems (primarily deforestation), which reduces their ability to absorb CO2 from the atmosphere.
Source of image: Umanotera
The growing awareness of the dangers of human-induced climate change and its global implications led to a process of international cooperation in the scientific and political spheres in the late 1980s. Since then, our understanding of the causes and consequences of climate change, as well as the necessary measures to prevent it in a timely manner, has improved. In 2015, the global community set a goal with the adoption of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change to keep the increase in the global average temperature well below 2 °C compared to pre-industrial levels. Scientists have calculated that achieving this goal and preventing catastrophic climate change would require achieving climate neutrality, or net-zero greenhouse gas emissions, by the middle of the 21st century at the latest. This is also a political goal of the European Union.
Why is it necessary to calculate a carbon footprint?
A carbon footprint is used as a tool to monitor greenhouse gas emissions and plan measures to reduce them or mitigate climate change. It helps us identify the largest sources of emissions, which also represent priority areas for action. By periodically calculating the carbon footprint, we monitor the effectiveness of the measures taken and improve them. The carbon footprint is also used for reporting.
Countries calculate their carbon footprint or prepare national inventories of greenhouse gas emissions and removals in order to report on the success of their climate policies to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), which oversees the implementation of the Paris Agreement.
Companies that are major polluters (large producers of electricity and heat using fossil fuels, energy-intensive industries, and aviation) must report their emissions under the Emissions Trading System (EU ETS).
Other companies and organizations calculate their carbon footprint voluntarily. Reporting on the carbon footprint is a matter of their social responsibility and part of a system of continuous improvement. This raises awareness among employees about the impact of the organization's operations on climate change and mitigation measures. By reporting to others – for example, partners, customers, and the public – organizations strengthen their reputation in society. However, the calculation of the carbon footprint itself is not a major achievement. An organization can boast when it achieves a reduction in its carbon footprint through measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
Individuals (and households) calculate their carbon footprint primarily to identify their largest sources of emissions and adjust their lifestyle to minimize their carbon footprint.
So, how can organizations contribute to reducing their carbon footprint?
The largest sources of greenhouse gas emissions in organizations with office activities are the consumption of electricity and heat energy and the consumption of fuels (gasoline, diesel, aviation fuel) for powering vehicles; in industry, it is the combustion of fossil fuels in production processes. Therefore, priority measures are energy conservation in buildings, adherence to the principles of sustainable mobility, and increasing the energy efficiency of any production processes.
And what can an individual do in this area?
The most important areas for action to reduce an individual's carbon footprint depend on their lifestyle. Therefore, it is useful to calculate your carbon footprint and focus on the actions that can achieve the greatest reduction in greenhouse gas emissions.
In general, the priority climate actions at the individual or household level are: a less consumerist lifestyle, avoiding air travel, using a car as little as possible, consuming less meat and dairy products, and reducing food waste, saving energy, and using renewable energy sources.
Not only by changing your lifestyle – you can also help reduce emissions by encouraging conversations about climate change in your environment and by introducing sustainable measures in your workplace. And finally, as active citizens, you can demand that climate action be prioritized – by actively supporting green policies and organizations that advocate for Slovenia's transition to a climate-neutral society, and by rejecting policies that support the continued use of fossil fuels.
The fact is that nature does not need us; we need it. How are we doing in this area in Slovenia?
If we focus on our impact on the climate, Slovenia is among the industrialized countries with high energy consumption and high greenhouse gas emissions; the lifestyle of its inhabitants is carbon-intensive. The carbon footprint of the average resident of Slovenia exceeds 8 tons of CO2 equivalent per year. To transition to a climate-neutral society, we will have to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to one-fifth of their current levels. However, we cannot wait until the middle of the century to take climate action. As a member of the European Union, Slovenia will have to contribute to a 55 percent reduction in emissions in the community compared to 1990 by 2030.
In Slovenia, the biggest challenge in the transition to a climate-neutral society is transport. We have not yet permanently managed the growth in emissions due to transport before the Covid epidemic. Because emissions in other sectors are slowly decreasing, the share of transport in Slovenia's carbon footprint is increasing. Another major challenge is the decarbonization of electricity production, which is technologically feasible, as Slovenia has sufficient and currently underutilized potential for electricity production from solar energy. Reducing emissions from the industry and agriculture sectors will need to be significantly accelerated in light of more ambitious political goals at the European Union level.
We have all the necessary technologies, knowledge, and even financial resources to transition to a climate-neutral society. As much as 25 percent of the EU budget in the period 2021–2027 is earmarked for tackling the challenge of climate change, and countries are expected to spend more than a third of the funds for recovery and resilience after the Covid epidemic on mitigating climate change and increasing biodiversity. Slovenia's timely transition to a climate-neutral society depends primarily on (political) will.

Ogljični odtis je seštevek vseh izpustov toplogrednih plinov, ki jih s svojim delovanjem neposredno ali posredno povzročajo posameznik, organizacija ali skupnost. V šestdestih letih prejšnjega stoletja so postali prepričljivi dokazi, da je ogljikov dioksid (CO2) najpomembnejši toplogredni plin, ki povzroča globalno segrevanje. Od začetka industrijske revolucije je človek s hitrim in močnim povečanjem vsebnosti CO2 v Zemljinem ozračju pomembno posegel v njegovo sestavo in porušil ravnotežje med viri in ponori CO2.
