Globalna skupnost si je leta 2015 s sprejetjem Pariškega podnebnega sporazuma zadala cilj, da bo dvig povprečne globalne temperature zadržala občutno pod 2 °C v primerjavi s predindustrijsko dobo. Znanstveniki so izračunali, da bi bilo za doseganje tega cilja in preprečitev katastrofalnih podnebnih sprememb potrebno najpozneje do sredine 21. stoletja doseči podnebno nevtralnost oziroma ničelno stopnjo neto emisij toplogrednih plinov. To je tudi politični cilj Evropske unije.
Zakaj je potrebno računati ogljični odtis?
Ogljični odtis se uporablja kot orodje za spremljanje izpustov toplogrednih plinov in načrtovanje ukrepov za njihovo zmanjšanje oz. za blaženje podnebnih sprememb. Pomaga nam določiti največje vire izpustov, ki predstavljajo tudi prioritetna področja ukrepanja. S periodičnim izračunavanjem ogljičnega odtisa spremljamo učinkovitost sprejetih ukrepov in jih izboljšujemo. Ogljični odtis se uporablja tudi za poročanje.
Države računajo ogljični odtis oziroma pripravljajo nacionalne evidence emisij in ponorov toplogrednih plinov zato, da lahko o uspešnosti svojih podnebnih politik poročajo Okvirni konvenciji Združenih narodov o spremembi podnebja (UNFCCC), ki bdi nad izvrševanjem Pariškega podnebnega sporazuma.

Ostala podjetja in organizacije računajo svoj ogljični odtis prostovoljno. Poročanje o ogljičnem odtisu je stvar njihove družbene odgovornosti in del sistema stalnih izboljšav. S tem zaposlene ozaveščajo o vplivu delovanja organizacije na podnebne spremembe in ukrepih blaženja. S poročanjem drugim – npr. partnerjem, strankam in javnosti, organizacije v družbi krepijo svoj ugled. Pri tem pa sam izračun ogljičnega odtisa še ni velik dosežek. Posamezniki (in gospodinjstva) računajo svoj ogljični odtis predvsem zato, da bi identificirali svoje največje vire izpustov in prilagodili svoj življenjski slog tako, da bi bil njihov ogljični odtis čim manjši.
Kako torej lahko organizacije pripomorejo k zmanjševanju svojega ogljičnega odtisa?
Največji viri izpustov toplogrednih plinov so v organizacijah s pisarniško dejavnostjo poraba električne in toplotne energije in poraba goriv (bencin, dizel, letalsko gorivo) za pogon prevoznih sredstev, v industriji pa še izgorevanje fosilnih energentov v proizvodnih procesih. Prioritetni ukrepi so torej varčevanje z energijo v stavbah, upoštevanje načel trajnostne mobilnosti ter povečanje energetske učinkovitosti morebitnih proizvodih procesov.
In kaj na tem področju lahko naredi posameznik?
Najpomembnejša področja ukrepanja za zmanjšanje ogljičnega odtisa posameznika so odvisna od njegovega življenjskega sloga. Zato je koristno, da si izračunamo svoj ogljični odtis in se osredotočimo na tista dejanja, s katerimi lahko dosežemo največje zmanjšanje izpustov toplogrednih plinov.
V splošnem pa so prednostni podnebni ukrepi na ravni posameznika oz. gospodinjstva: nepotrošniški življenjski slog, izogibanje letalskim prevozom, v čim večji meri življenje brez avtomobila, uživanje čim manj mesa in mlečnih izdelkov in zmanjševanje količine zavržene hrane, varčevanje z energijo in oskrba z energijo iz obnovljivih virov.

In nenazadnje lahko kot aktivni državljani zahtevate, da se podnebne ukrepe obravnava prednostno – z aktivnim podpiranjem zelenih politik in organizacij, ki se zavzemajo za prehod Slovenije v podnebno nevtralno družbo, in z zavrnitvijo politik, ki podpirajo nadaljevanje uporabe fosilnih goriv.
Dejstvo je, da nas narava ne potrebuje, temveč mi potrebujemo njo. Kako nam na tem področju kaže v Sloveniji?
Če se osredotočimo na naš vpliv na podnebje, se Slovenija prišteva med industrializirane države z veliko potrošnjo energije in velikimi izpusti toplogrednih plinov, življenjski slog njenih prebivalcev je ogljično intenziven. Ogljični odtis povprečnega prebivalca Slovenije presega 8 ton ekvivalenta CO2 na leto. Za prehod v podnebno nevtralno družbo bomo izpuste toplogrednih plinov morali zmanjšati na petino sedanjih. Vendar pa s podnebnim ukrepanjem ne moremo čakati do sredine stoletja. Slovenija bo kot članica Evropske unije morala že do leta 2030 prispevati k 55-odstotnemu zmanjšanju izpustov v skupnosti v primerjavi z letom 1990.
V Sloveniji predstavlja največji izziv prehoda v podnebno nevtralno družbo promet. Rasti izpustov zaradi prometa pred epidemijo Covid še nismo trajno obvladali. Ker se izpusti v drugih sektorjih počasi zmanjšujejo, je delež prometa v ogljičnem odtisu Slovenije vse večji. Velik izziv je tudi razogljičenje proizvodnje elektrike, ki pa je tehnološko izvedljivo, saj ima Slovenija zadosten in zaenkrat le malo izkoriščen potencial proizvodnje elektrike iz sonca. Za prehod v podnebno nevtralno družbo imamo na voljo vse potrebne tehnologije, znanja in celo finančna sredstva. Za spopadanje z izzivom podnebnih sprememb je predvidenih kar 25 % odhodkov proračuna EU v obdobju 2021 – 2027, države naj bi za blaženje podnebnih sprememb in povečanje biotske raznovrstnosti porabile tudi več kot tretjino sredstev za okrevanje in odpornost po epidemiji Covid. Clean water is water that has been purified. Water purification is the process of removing undesirable substances and contaminants from water with the aim of making it disinfected, clean, and safe for human consumption.
71% of the Earth’s surface is covered with water. 97% of this is saltwater, and 3% is freshwater. Clean drinking water, also known as potable water, is essential for human life. We also use water to clean our clothes, shower, bathe, flush toilets, cook, and more. Water can be a source of many diseases, such as cholera or dysentery, so in modern times, the water that is brought to our homes is cleaned and disinfected to make it safe to drink.
Early settlements could only begin to develop in areas near a supply of clean water, such as a river. Then, people dug wells to obtain water, which allowed settlements to be located away from rivers. Early civilizations built systems, such as aqueducts and irrigation, to redirect water flows to cities and towns where water was needed. The first doctor to observe that water quality could affect a person’s health was Alcmaeon of Croton in 470 BC.
In some developing countries, the water supply can be contaminated with sewage or other sources of bacteria. Contaminated water can contain pathogens that cause diseases such as cholera. If people do not have access to clean water and drink contaminated water, they can die from these diseases. Access to clean water allows communities to thrive and grow, but in some areas, clean water is still not available.

Coagulation and Flocculation
Flocculation is the process in which smaller particles are combined to form larger particles. These larger particles, called flocs, are easier to remove from the water.
Sedimentation
Sedimentation is the process in which the flocs settle to the bottom, allowing them to be removed from the water.
Filtration
After the larger particles have been removed, the water passes through filters of various compositions to remove other dissolved particles.
Disinfection
After filtration, the water is disinfected, often with chlorine, to kill any remaining pathogens.

Antifa is a shortened term for anti-fascism, which refers to a political movement dedicated to fighting fascism around the world.

The Antifa movement emerged in the 1920s with the formation of a group of people known as the Communist International of the Soviet Union (Comintern or Comintern in German). The group began to organize itself during the realization of the Third World Congress in Moscow in 1921.

Older dogs can experience cognitive dysfunction, similar to Alzheimer's disease. No one knows exactly why cognitive abilities decline with age. One theory is that copies of genetic material (DNA) become less accurate with each replication in new cells.
DNA damage can also occur due to natural exposure to cosmic radiation and other factors (breathing polluted air or fumes from certain solvents), which can lead to the incorrect formation of enzymes. This often causes cell death in the nervous system and elsewhere. Other theories of aging blame stress. Some theories suggest that aging results from the accumulation of metabolic waste products in cells or an increase in unstable chemicals (free radicals) that affect molecules in cells and their function.
Regardless of the cause of aging, the brain and nervous system of dogs (and humans) undergo significant changes as they age. Older dogs have smaller, lighter brains than younger dogs. The brains of older dogs can be up to 25 percent lighter. It is important to note that this change is not necessarily due to the death of brain cells. Parts of nerve cells that are connected to other cells die or begin to break down as we age. The loss of these connections affects the size and weight of the brain.
With age, chemical changes also occur in the brain, which affect behavior, memory, and learning. In dogs and humans, mitochondria are responsible for converting nutrients into energy. As dogs and humans age, mitochondria become less efficient. They begin to release free radicals, chemicals that oxidize compounds essential for normal cell function. The loss of these compounds threatens cells. As tissues degenerate, protein deposits called amyloid plaques accumulate in the brain. High levels of amyloid, especially in conjunction with clusters of dead and dying nerve cells, are evidence that an individual is suffering from Alzheimer's disease. Studies conducted at the University of Toronto by a group of researchers have shown that dogs with high levels of amyloid in their brains have poorer memory and difficulty learning new skills, especially when it comes to more complex thinking and problem-solving. In dogs, what is similar to Alzheimer's disease in humans is called canine cognitive dysfunction syndrome.
Similar to Alzheimer's disease, the physical signs of age-related brain lesions are similar to those in humans. Dogs also accumulate beta-amyloid. This is a starchy protein that becomes waxy and forms a coating. As the coating thickens, it clogs the brain and inhibits the transmission of signals from the brain. In both Alzheimer's and canine cognitive dysfunction, the number of plaques affects the severity of the cognitive disorder.
There are noticeable changes that indicate a dog has cognitive dysfunction syndrome, and that are not a normal part of aging. The main symptoms can be summarized with the acronym DISH, which stands for disorientation, interaction changes, sleep changes, and house soiling.
Signs of disorientation often include:
• unresponsiveness to well-learned commands
• unresponsiveness to being called
• loss of memory for basic tasks
• staring blankly or at walls
• wandering and getting lost or confused outside
• walking in repetitive patterns, such as around a table or from room to room
• confusion in an otherwise familiar home environment
• agitation
Symptoms of decreased interaction include:
• often, the first thing noticed is that the dog is no longer interested in being petted and may even move away if you try to pet it
• previously social dogs no longer try to get attention
• the dog no longer greets visitors or even family members
Typical changes in sleep habits include:
• the dog may sleep more during the day
• the dog may sleep less at night and wander around in the dark
Sometimes, symptoms include forgetting house training
• some dogs stop signaling that they need to go outside
• some dogs may have accidents indoors. These accidents may also occur shortly after being outside
• the dog may seem to forget why it is outside, often wandering aimlessly
Observing such changes in an otherwise beloved older dog can be very painful for the owner and family, but the good news is that the syndrome can be managed over time.

Podobno kot pri Alzheimerjevi bolezni so fizični znaki generativnih možganskih lezij podobni kot pri ljudeh. Tudi psi kopičijo beta amiloide. Gre za škrobni protein, ki postane voskast in tvori oblogo. Ko se obloga odebeli, to zamaši možgane in zavira prenos signalov iz možganov. Znaki dezorientacije pogosto vključujejo:

• pobeg in izgubljena ali zmedena hoja izven hiše

pes lahko več spi podnevi

ZPS advises: Drinking water is important even in winter.
Without water, a person can survive for only up to 4 days, which is why we often hear the saying, "WATER IS LIFE."
From the first living beings on Earth to the present day, preventing dehydration has been the most important factor for survival. Water makes up 75% of the body mass in infants and 55% in adults, and it is essential for maintaining homeostasis, eliminating waste products from the body, regulating body temperature, and other vital functions. Therefore, make sure to consume enough fluids, even if you are not thirsty.
But what about replenishing the water lost from the body? How much fluid do we need to consume daily to compensate for this loss? What is recommended to drink when thirsty?
In the following ten points, we will briefly explain some dilemmas about drinking water.
1. An adult loses more than 2 liters of water from their body in one day.
As mentioned earlier, we are about 55% composed of water. In an average 78 kg person, this means about 40 kg, or 40 liters of water. This makes up our organs, blood, muscles, and other tissues.
Daily, through sweating and urination, we lose an average of 2.6 liters of water from our bodies. Part of this water (H2O) is replenished by the body during breathing and metabolism – about 330 ml per day – and the rest must be obtained through food and drinks.
2. Lack of fluids causes fatigue and headaches.
If we don't drink enough, we can become tired more quickly and lose concentration. Headaches and constipation are common in many people, often due to insufficient fluid intake. We can survive for a maximum of 2-4 days without water, but even short-term dehydration can cause changes in our body. As a result, muscles and the brain receive less oxygen and nutrients, which can have lasting consequences.
3. A healthy person feels thirsty when they need fluids, but they should still drink at least a liter of water.
We feel thirsty when we are missing 1-2% of our body fluids, and if we are missing 6%, we can fall into a coma. Some argue that a person should drink 2-3 liters of fluid per day. This number is too high for many, as we already consume almost 1 liter through food (fruits, vegetables, soup, etc.). National recommendations state that an adult should consume at least 1.5 liters of fluid per day in addition to food – less than this would be detrimental to our health. If we don't feel thirsty, we should still remember to drink enough fluids daily.
4. During physical activity, a person needs up to one liter more fluid per hour of activity.
During physical shocks, such as heat, extreme cold, injury, vomiting, or diarrhea, the body needs more water. Even during physical exertion, such as intense sports training, the body needs more fluids than in a normal state. As a general rule, we should replace 1 ml of fluid for every kilocalorie consumed.
5. Excessive (too much at once) fluid intake can be harmful to our body.
Athletes should be especially careful, as they can consume large amounts of water at once during sports training. It is recommended to drink water gradually throughout the day, about a deciliter per hour. Before lunch, you can have soup, and during a snack, you can have watermelon (a fruit with 99% water), for example.
The level of sodium in the blood can drop rapidly due to excessive fluid intake at once, which can cause the sodium-potassium pump to malfunction. This can lead to long-term consequences or even death. People with kidney and heart problems should be especially careful about how they consume water.
6. Tap water is just as good for quenching thirst as bottled water.
Slovenian tap water is mostly good and suitable for drinking directly from the tap (source: NIJZ, 2016). Drinking tap water is cheaper and almost everywhere accessible in Slovenia, unlike in other countries, especially in the developing world.
If we need to consume at least 1.5 liters of water per day, that's 45 liters of water per month and 540 liters of water per year. One cubic meter (1000 liters) of tap water in Ljubljana and its surroundings costs €0.58, so we spend about €0.31 per year on drinking water. This is approximately the same as the cost of a 1.5-liter bottle of water in a store.
Drinking water
Drinking water in its original state or after preparation, intended for drinking, cooking, preparing food, or for other household purposes, regardless of its origin and regardless of whether it is supplied from a water supply network, a water tank, or as pre-packaged water;
AND all water used for the production and distribution of food.
7. When drinking flavored beverages, we need to be aware of the amount of "hidden" calories.
Flavored beverages can successfully replace "boring" water, but we need to be careful about the additives they contain. Unsweetened tea or homemade unsweetened lemonade are excellent alternatives, but the same cannot be said for beverages that contain sugar. Sweet drinks do not quench thirst well, so we tend to consume more of them, and therefore more sugar. Obesity, tooth decay, and type 2 diabetes can be the consequences of excessive consumption of sweet drinks. Let's avoid them and instead pour ourselves a glass of tap water and squeeze in some lemon and a few mint leaves.
8. Unsweetened coffee, green tea, and black tea also count towards the recommended amount of fluid intake.
Regardless of whether the beverage contains caffeine or not, it provides our body with fluids. Because caffeine stimulates our body, it speeds up our metabolism and energy consumption, and therefore fluid loss from the body. Therefore, it is recommended to drink a glass of water in addition to coffee.
9. Water as the only source of drink for a child can reduce the risk of being overweight.
Studies show that adolescents who drank more water in childhood are less likely to become obese later in life. If a child quenches their thirst with water, they will have less desire for sweet drinks. Drinking fountains should be installed in all schools to offer children free water. This might discourage them from buying expensive sweet drinks.
10. Drinking more water can overcome the feeling of hunger.
When we drink water, it fills our stomach and helps us overcome the feeling of hunger and wait for the next meal. In people on a diet, the tactic of consuming a larger amount of fluid has proven to be positive in losing weight.

ZPS svetuje: Pitje vode je pomembno tudi pozimi
Brez vode lahko človek preživi le do 4 dni, zato lahko pogosto slišimo stavek VODA JE ŽIVLJENJE.
Od prvih bitji na zemlji pa vse do danes je najpomembnejši faktor preživetja prav preprečevanje dehidracije. Voda sestavlja od 75 % telesne mase pri dojenčkih do 55 % pri odraslih in je ključna za vzdrževanje homeostaze, izločanje odpadnih snovi iz telesa, uravnavanje telesne temperature in drugih vitalnih funkcij. Zato poskrbite za zadostno uživanje tekočine, četudi niste žejni.
Kako pa je z nadomeščanjem izgubljene vode iz telesa? Koliko tekočine moramo zaužiti v dnevu, da bomo to izgubo nadomestili? Kaj je priporočljivo piti za žejo?
V naslednjih desetih točkah vam bomo na kratko pojasnili nekaj dilem o pitju vode.
1. Odrasel človek v enem dnevu iz telesa izgubi zgubi več kot 2 l vode.
Kot že omenjeno, smo v okrog 55 % sestavljeni iz vode. V povprečnem 78 kg človeku je torej okrog 40 kg oziroma 40 l vode. Le ta sestavlja naše organe, kri, mišice in druga tkiva.
Dnevno, med potenjem in uriniranjem, izgubimo s telesa v povprečju 2,6 l vode. Deloma se telo samo oskrbi z vodo (H2O) med dihanjem in presnovo - to je okrog 330 ml na dan – ostalo pa moramo zaužiti s hrano in pijačo.
2. Pomanjkanje tekočine povzroča utrujenost in glavobol
Če ne pijemo dovolj, lahko hitreje postanemo utrujeni in izgubimo koncentracijo. Glavoboli in zaprtost težijo mnogo ljudi, velikokrat prav zaradi premalo zaužite tekočine. Brez vode lahko zdržimo največ 2-4 dni, vendar se že ob kratkotrajni dehidraciji začnejo dogajati spremembe v našem telesu. Posledično tudi do mišic in možganov pride premalo kisika in hranil kar lahko pusti trajne posledice.
3. Zdrav človek občuti žejo kadar potrebuje tekočino, vendar manj kot liter vode naj vseeno ne bi spil.
Žejo čutimo že ob pomanjkanju 1-2 % telesnih tekočin, pri pomanjkanju 6 % pa lahko že pademo v komo. Nekateri trdijo, da naj bi človek na dan popil 2-3 litre tekočine. Ta številka je za mnoge previsoka, saj je skoraj 1 liter vnesemo tudi z uživanjem hrane (sadje, zelenjava, juha,…). Nacionalna priporočila pravijo, da naj bi odrasel človek zaužil poleg hrane še vsaj 1,5 l tekočine dnevno – manj kot to bi bilo za naše zdravje neugodno. V kolikor ne občutimo žeje, se moramo spomniti in vseeno dnevno zaužiti dovolj tekočine.
4. Ob telesni aktivnosti potrebuje človek do enega litra več tekočine na uro aktivnosti.
Ob telesnih šokih, kot so vročina, hud mraz, poškodba, bruhanje, diareja, telo potrebuje več vode. Tudi ob telesnih naporih, kot je intenzivna športna vadba, telo potrebuje več tekočine kot v normalnem stanju. Načeloma velja da moramo za vsako porabljeno kilokalorijo, nadomestiti 1 ml tekočine.
5. Prekomerno (preveč naenkrat) pitje tekočine je za naš organizem lahko škodljivo.
Posebej pazljivi morajo biti športniki, ki lahko med športno vadbo naenkrat zaužijejo večje količine vode. Priporočljivo je piti vodo postopoma čez cel dan, deciliter na uro, pred kosilom je ti lahko juhica, pri malici tudi lubenica (sadje z 99% vode) na primer.
Raven natrija v krvi lahko zaradi prekomerne količine zaužite tekočine naenkrat, hitro pade, kar lahko povzroči nepravilno delovanje natrij-kalijeve črpalke. Utrpimo lahko dolgoročne posledice ali celo umremo. Pri načinu zauživanju vode morajo biti še posebej pazljivi tudi ledvični in srčni bolniki.
6. Voda iz pipe ravno tako poteši žejo, kot tista iz plastenke.
Slovenska vodovodna voda je večinoma dobra in primerna za pitje direktno iz pipe (vir: NIJZ, 2016). Pitje vodovodne vode je cenejše in v Sloveniji skoraj povsod dostopno, za razliko od drugih držav predvsem tretjega sveta.
Če naj bi zaužili dnevno vsaj 1,5 l vode, je to 45 l vode na mesec, 540 l vode na leto. En kubični meter (1000 l) vodovodne vode v Ljubljani in okolici stane 0,58 €, torej za popito vodo zapravimo letno dobrih 0,31 €. Približno toliko, kot stane 1,5 l plastenka vode v trgovini.
Pitna voda
Pitna voda v njenem prvotnem stanju ali po pripravi, namenjena pitju, kuhanju, pripravi hrane ali za druge gospodinjske namene, ne glede na njeno poreklo in ne glede na to, ali se dobavlja iz vodovodnega omrežja sistema za oskrbo s pitno vodo, cistern ali kot predpakirana voda;
IN vsa voda, ki se uporablja za proizvodnjo in promet živil.
7. Pri pijačah z okusom moramo biti pozorni na količino `skritih´ kalorij
Pijače z okusom lahko uspešno nadomestijo »dolgočasno« vodo, vendar moramo biti pazljivi na dodatke, ki jih le te vsebujejo. Če gre za nesladkan čaj ali domačo nesladkano limonado so odličen nadomestek, drugače pa je s pijačami, ki vsebujejo sladkor. Sladke pijače žeje ne potešijo dobro, zato jih večinoma zaužijemo več in s tem tudi veliko sladkorja. Debelost, karies, diabetes tipa 2 so lahko posledice prekomernega zauživanja sladkih pijač. Izognimo se jim in si raje natočimo kozarec vode iz pipe ter vanj stisnimo malo limone ter nekaj listkov mete.
8. Nesladkana kava, zeleni in črni čaj tudi štejejo v priporočeno količino popite tekočine
Ne glede na to, ali pijača vsebuje kofein ali ne, naše telo oskrbi s tekočino. Ker kofein poživi naše telo, s tem pospešimo metabolizem in porabo energije ter s tem izgubo tekočine iz telesa, zato je priporočljivo poleg kave spiti še kozarec vode.
9. Voda, kot edini vir pijače pri otroku, lahko zmanjša riziko za prekomerno telesno težo
Študije kažejo, da mladostniki, ki so v otroštvu popili več vode, redkeje postanejo debeli kasneje v življenju. Če otrok žejo poteši z vodo, bo imel manj želje po sladki pijači. Pitnike vode bi morali namestiti po vseh šolah in s tem otrokom ponuditi brezplačno pijačo – vodo. Morda bi jih tako odvrnili od nakupa dražje sladke pijače.
10. Več popite vode lahko premaga občutek lakote
Ob zaužitju voda zapolni naš želodec in nam tako pomaga premagati občutek lakote in počakati na naslednji obrok. Pri ljudeh na dieti, se je taktika zaužitja večje količite tekočine izkazala za pozitivno pri izgubljanju telesne mase.

Temperature is a key factor in plant growth and development. Together with light levels, carbon dioxide, air humidity, water, and nutrients, temperature affects plant growth and, ultimately, yield. All these factors must be balanced. Temperature affects plants both in the short term and the long term.
Differences between air temperature and plant temperature
Most biological processes will accelerate at higher temperatures, which can have both positive and negative effects. One advantage, in most cases, is faster fruit growth. However, the effect of subsequent excessive respiration is negative, as it means less energy is available for fruit development, and the fruits will be smaller. Some effects are short-term, while others are long-term. For example, temperature immediately affects the plant’s absorption balance. On the other hand, the onset of flowering is determined by the climate over a much longer period.
Plant temperature and air temperature are not the same, as plants can cool down through evaporation and heat up through radiation. Plants try to reach their optimal temperature, and the balance between air temperature, relative humidity, and light is also important. If light levels are high, the plant will heat up, which will create a difference between the plant temperature and the air temperature. To cool down, the plant must increase its transpiration rate. The transpiration rate depends not only on temperature but also on environmental conditions such as light, CO2 levels in the atmosphere, and relative humidity, as well as the type of plant.
Plants are made up of different parts, all of which react differently to temperature. The temperature of the fruit is closely related to the air temperature – when the air temperature rises, the fruit temperature also rises, and vice versa. The fruit temperature will fluctuate less than the air temperature, and it will take more time (sometimes several hours) for it to rise or fall. The temperature of the flowers, on the other hand, is higher than the air temperature or the leaf temperature, and the flower petals transpire much more slowly than the plant’s leaves. The temperature at the top of the plant’s canopy fluctuates more than the temperature at the bottom. The top will heat up more easily through radiation and will therefore have a higher temperature than the air when light levels are high.

Temperatura je ključni dejavnik pri rasti in razvoju rastlin. Skupaj z ravnjo svetlobe, ogljikovim dioksidom, vlago v zraku, vodo in hranili, temperatura vpliva na rast rastlin in ne nazadnje tudi na pridelek. Vsi ti dejavniki morajo biti uravnoteženi. Temperatura vpliva na rastlino kratkoročno in tudi dolgoročno.
Razlike med temperaturo zraka in temperaturo rastline
Večina bioloških procesov se bo pospešila pri višjih temperaturah, kar lahko ima pozitivne in negativne učinke. Ena od prednosti je, v večini primerov, na primer hitrejša rast plodu. Vendar je učinek posledičnega čezmernega dihanja negativen, saj je zaradi njega za razvoj plodu na voljo manj energije, plodovi pa bodo manjši. Nekateri učinki so kratkoročni, drugi pa dolgoročni. Temperatura na primer takoj vpliva na absorpcijsko ravnotežje rastline. Začetek cvetenja po drugi strani določa podnebje v veliko daljšem časovnem obdobju.
Temperatura rastline in temperatura zraka nista enaki, saj se rastline lahko ohlajajo z izhlapevanjem in segrevajo s pomočjo sevanja. Rastline poskušajo doseči svojo optimalno temperaturo, pri tem pa je pomembno tudi ravnotežje med temperaturo zraka, relativno vlažnostjo in svetlobo. Če so ravni svetlobe visoke, se bo rastlina segrela, kar bo povzročilo razliko med temperaturo rastline in temperaturo zraka. Da se ohladi, mora rastlina povečati svojo stopnjo transpiracije. Stopnja transpiracije je razen od temperature odvisna tudi od okoljskih pogojev, kot so svetloba, ravni CO2 v ozračju in relativne vlažnosti, pa tudi od vrste rastline.

Temperatura plodu bo nihala manj od temperature zraka in za rast ali padec bo potrebnega več časa (včasih tudi do nekaj ur več). The main difference – ecology versus ecosystem
Ecology and ecosystem are closely related terms that describe the interactions of organisms with their environment. Ecology is the study of the relationships and interactions between living organisms and their environment, as well as among themselves. An ecosystem is a subfield of ecology. It consists of a biotic component, which includes all the plants, animals, and microorganisms, and an abiotic component, which includes all the non-living physical factors in the environment. The main difference between ecology and ecosystem is that ecology is the study of ecosystems, while ecosystems are the units that are formed by the interaction of communities of organisms with their environment.

Key terms: Ecology, Ecosystem, Food, Nutrients, Water, Animals, Plants, Microorganisms, Autotrophs, Heterotrophs, Food chain, Food web, Environment, Symbiotic relationships, Biodiversity
What is ecology
Ecology describes the relationships between organisms and their environment. The three main components that are studied in ecology are living organisms, the relationships and interactions with other organisms, and the relationships and interactions with the surrounding environment. Symbiotic relationships, such as rhizobium and legumes in plant roots, as well as competition between herbivorous animals for food, are interactions between organisms. All animals and plants rely on various aspects of their environment to obtain food, nutrients, and water. The response of organisms to climate, soil, topography, atmosphere, and water availability are other types of relationships between organisms and their environment. For example, animals in cold environments have small ears, while animals in deserts have long ears, as long ears help to cool the body by increasing heat loss. Ecology has close relationships with physiology, behavior, genetics, and evolution. The broader details that have been explored in ecology include:
- The life processes, interactions, and adaptations of a particular species.
- The impact of environmental factors on organisms in a population.
- The changes that occur in ecosystems over time.
- The distribution and abundance of organisms in an environment.
- The biodiversity within an ecosystem.
Figure 1: Biodiversity of a coral reef
What is an ecosystem
An ecosystem consists of all the living organisms in an area or a community of organisms and the non-living abiotic factors that interact with the community. An ecosystem is classified into biotic and abiotic factors. All living organisms in the environment are defined as the biotic factor. Other non-living physical things that interact with the biotic factor are defined as the abiotic factor. Abiotic factors include climate, sunlight, soil, water, minerals, and other non-living materials. Biotic and abiotic factors are linked by two factors: the flow of energy through the ecosystem and the cycling of nutrients in the ecosystem.
Sunlight is the primary source of energy for most ecosystems. It is used by autotrophs in the ecosystem to produce simple carbohydrates from carbon dioxide and water. Autotrophs are considered the primary producers in the ecosystem. Complex organic compounds, such as proteins, starches, and lipids, are produced within autotrophs. Heterotrophs in the ecosystem rely on the organic matter produced by autotrophs. Heterotrophs are the consumers in the ecosystem. The movement of organic matter from the primary producer level to the consumer level is called a food chain. The final link in the food chain is decomposition, which is carried out by microorganisms. The overlapping and interconnectedness of food chains forms a food web. The entire cycle of the food chain is shown in Figure 2.
Figure 2: The entire cycle of the food chain
Similarities between ecology and ecosystem
- Ecology and ecosystem describe the relationship and interactions between living organisms and their environment.
- These interactions and interdependencies fulfill their basic life requirements, such as food, nutrients, water, and habitat.
Difference between ecology and ecosystem
Definition
Ecology: Ecology is a branch of biology that deals with the relationships between organisms and their physical environment.
Ecosystem: An ecosystem is a community of interacting organisms and their physical environment.
Correspondence
Ecology: Ecology is the study of ecosystems.
Ecosystem: An ecosystem is a subset of ecology.
Relationship
Ecology: Ecology involves the study of the relationship between living organisms and their environment.
Ecosystem: An ecosystem is a place, such as a forest, taiga, grassland, desert, freshwater, river, or stream, coral reef, etc.
Conclusion
Ecology and ecosystem describe the relationship between biotic and abiotic factors in an environmental system. Ecology is the study of ecosystems. An ecosystem describes the relationship between a mass of living organisms that belong to the same or different communities. This is the main difference between ecology and ecosystem. Organisms maintain relationships and interactions with each other and with the external environment in order to obtain basic life requirements, such as food, nutrients, water, and habitat.

Fear is hollow from within; there is nothing around it.
Fear is a feeling that allowed humans to survive the natural selection of history. A story tells of two of our ancestors long ago. It was night, and one of them woke up feeling that something was happening around their dwelling. He immediately woke up his friend and warned him about his premonition. The friend just waved his hand and went back to sleep, while the other recognized the danger in his premonition and retreated to safety. All of us are descendants of the person who recognized the danger, activated by the internal feeling of fear.
Fear as a Survival Mechanism
Fear is a feeling that allowed humans to survive the natural selection of history.
Being afraid is as human as any basic human need. We live in a world where danger can threaten us at every turn. Many people face personal crises that cause sudden and unusual behavior, which can be very dangerous for bystanders. That is why we are under the watchful eye of our parents from an early age. At every turn, they warn us about the dangers that may threaten us – and rightly so. A child is not capable of complex perception of their environment, especially now that technology dictates our progress.
Regulating Fear
If fear was not properly regulated in our childhood, we will have problems dealing with it in later life. It's somewhat like learning to walk on one leg in childhood – and then being forced to step into a world of "bipeds." Of course, various traumatic experiences can also be responsible for dysfunctional responses to fear. The consequence of not coping with them properly is various phobias, panic attacks, or anxiety. In some places, various psychotic and personality disorders can develop from this.
Covering Up Fear
The consequence of not coping with traumatic experiences is various phobias, panic attacks, or anxiety.
People are also very good at covering up fear – with various more impulsive feelings. For example, consider a mother who sees her son burn himself on a hot stove. Although she is deeply afraid for her son's well-being, her reaction is full of anger, which sometimes even leads to violence. Thus, the child receives the wrong signal and can also develop a similar mechanism to regulate feelings of helplessness and fear over time. There are many such examples among young people. And because anger is the most obvious emotion they use, many are quickly labeled and treated as violent.
Fear in a Romantic Relationship
Especially at the beginning of a young couple's journey, fear is a very common phenomenon. It is strongly linked to the internal intimacy of each partner, as every relationship requires the individual to connect with their internal experiences – something we don't show to the world and represents our most guarded secret. The partners are cautious because they don't know how they will react to each other and how they will accept this internal intimacy. Therefore, the process of getting to know each other is very important for serious relationships.
This fear is very normal and positive in every relationship, as it is an indicator that the relationship means a lot to us. However, there are also many couples who cannot enter a relationship relaxed due to bad experiences from the past or fear of abandonment. They fight a daily battle, torn between reality and the life they live. Such relationships are like a ticking time bomb, which ticks only as long as the illusion that the partners create is solid.
Coping with Fear
It is possible to cope relatively well with fear in life by avoiding it.
I am afraid of riding in an elevator – I prefer to walk.
I am afraid of large crowds – I prefer to stay at home.
I am afraid of saying something wrong – I prefer to be quiet.
Fear is functional only when it makes us aware of the environment we are in and brings to the forefront the restraint that creates a perceived safe distance.
But what kind of life is that?
A Slovenian proverb says that fear is hollow from within; there is nothing around it. Too many people are fighting windmills that time has long buried. Fear is functional only when it makes us aware of the environment we are in and brings to the forefront the restraint that creates a perceived safe distance. This must be followed by a thoughtful retreat or action. In both cases, it is necessary to overcome this feeling and use it to achieve a higher quality of life. In its extreme form, fear is an extreme demotivator, so people find it difficult to seek help on their own. In these cases, it is essential that those close to us recognize the distress of others, as we too often read about alternatives in Slovenia in the crime section.

People have always been fascinated by lightning. It is a powerful natural electrostatic discharge. It usually occurs during thunderstorms, which create electromagnetic pulses. This lightning discharge is accompanied by the emission of light, called lightning, and sound, called thunder. However, many people do not know how lightning is formed.
Therefore, this article will be dedicated to explaining how lightning is formed and what the different types of lightning are.
Main characteristics
Lightning discharge is accompanied by the emission of light. This emission of light is called lightning and is the result of the passage of an electric current that ionizes the molecules in the air. Immediately afterward, a sound, called thunder, is produced, which is developed by shock waves. The electricity produced goes through the atmosphere, heats the atmosphere, causes the air to expand rapidly, and produces a special noise from the ground. Lightning is in a plasma state.
The average length of a lightning bolt is approximately 1,500-500 meters. Interestingly, in 2007, the longest lightning strike occurred in Oklahoma, reaching a length of 321 kilometers. Lightning usually travels at an average speed of approximately 440 kilometers per second, up to 1,400 kilometers per second. The potential difference is a million volts with respect to the ground. Therefore, these lightning bolts are very dangerous. Approximately 16 million thunderstorms are recorded on the planet each year.
Most commonly, these different types of lightning are produced by positive particles in the ground and negative particles in the clouds. This is due to the vertical development of clouds called cumulonimbus. When a cumulonimbus cloud reaches the tropopause (the final region of the troposphere), the positive charges in the cloud are responsible for attracting negative charges. This movement of electric charges in the atmosphere forms lightning. It usually forms a back-and-forth effect. It refers to the fact that particles immediately rise and return to cause a flash of light.
Lightning can create 1 million watts of instantaneous power, which is comparable to a nuclear explosion. The discipline responsible for studying lightning and everything related to meteorology is called earth science.
How lightning is formed
How the electric discharge begins remains a controversial question. Scientists have not yet been able to determine what the main cause is. The most well-known are those who say that atmospheric disturbances are the reason for the formation of lightning. These disturbances in the atmosphere are the result of changes in wind, humidity, and atmospheric pressure. Much is discussed about the influence of solar wind and the accumulation of charged solar particles.
Ice is considered a key component in the development. This is because it is responsible for promoting the separation of positive and negative charges in the cumulonimbus cloud. Lightning can also be formed in ash clouds from volcanic eruptions or as a result of dust from violent forest fires, which can cause static charges.
In the assumption of electrostatic induction, the electric charge drives the process, for which people are not yet sure. The separation of charges requires a strong upward flow of air, which is responsible for carrying water droplets upward. In this way, when the water droplets reach a higher altitude, where the surrounding air is colder, accelerated cooling will occur. Usually, these levels are cooled at temperatures of -10 to -20 degrees. The collision of ice crystals forms a combination of water and ice, called hail. Due to the collision, a slightly positive charge was transferred to the ice crystals, and a slight negative charge to the hail.
The flow pushes the lighter ice crystals upward, causing the accumulation of positive charges on the back of the cloud. Finally, the influence of the Earth's gravity causes the hail to fall with a negative charge, because the hail becomes heavier as it approaches the middle and bottom of the cloud. The separation and accumulation of charge continues until the potential is sufficient to trigger a discharge.
Another hypothesis about the polarization mechanism has two components. Let's look at what they are:
- Falling ice and water droplets become polarized as they fall into the natural Earth's electric field.
- Falling ice particles collide and are charged by electrostatic induction.
How lightning is formed and its different types
- The most common lightning is the most frequently observed, known as streak lightning. This is the visible part of the lightning track. Most of it is in the cloud and therefore cannot be seen. Let's look at what the main types of lightning are:
- Cloud-to-ground lightning: is the most well-known and the second most common. This is the greatest threat to life and property. It can strike the ground and discharge between a cumulonimbus cloud and the ground.
- Pearl Ray: This is cloud-to-ground lightning that appears to be divided into a series of short, bright parts.
- Staccato lightning: is another short-duration cloud-to-ground lightning and appears to be a single flash. It is usually very bright and has a large impact.
- Branching lightning: are those cloud-to-ground lightning that show a branching of their path.
- Cloud-to-cloud lightning: is a discharge between the ground and the cloud that begins with an initial upward strike. It is less common.
- Cloud-to-cloud lightning: occurs between areas that are not in contact with the ground. It usually occurs when two separate clouds create a difference in electric potential.

Ko kumulonimbusni oblak doseže tropopavzo (končno območje troposfere), so pozitivni naboji v oblaku odgovorni za privabljanje negativnih nabojev. To gibanje električnih nabojev v ozračju tvori žarke. Običajno tvori učinek naprej in nazaj. Nanaša se na stališče, da se delci takoj dvignejo in vrnejo, da povzročijo padec svetlobe.
Strela lahko ustvari 1 milijon vatov trenutne moči, kar je primerljivo z jedrsko eksplozijo. Disciplina, zadolžena za preučevanje strele in vse, kar je povezano z meteorologijo, se imenuje znanost o zemlji.
Kako nastajajo žarki
Kako se je začel električni udar, ostaja kontroverzno vprašanje. Znanstvenikom še ni uspelo ugotoviti, kaj je glavni vzrok. Najbolj znani so tisti, ki pravijo, da so atmosferske motnje razlog za nastanek vrst strele. Te motnje v ozračju so posledica sprememb vetra, vlažnosti in atmosferskega tlaka. Preveč Razpravlja se o vplivu sončnega vetra in kopičenju nabitih sončnih delcev.
Led velja za ključno sestavino razvoja. To je zato, ker je odgovoren za spodbujanje ločevanja pozitivnih in negativnih nabojev v kumulonimbusnem oblaku. Strele lahko nastanejo tudi v oblakih pepela zaradi vulkanskih izbruhov ali pa so posledica prahu iz silovitih gozdnih požarov, ki lahko povzročijo statične naboje.
V predpostavki elektrostatične indukcije naj bi električni naboj poganjal proces, za katerega ljudje še niso prepričani. Ločevanje polnil zahteva močan pretok zraka navzgor, ki je odgovoren za prenašanje vodnih kapljic navzgor. Na ta način, ko vodne kapljice dosežejo višjo nadmorsko višino, kjer je okoliški zrak hladnejši, bo prišlo do pospešenega ohlajanja. Običajno se te ravni prehladijo pri temperaturah od -10 do -20 stopinj. Trčenje ledenih kristalov tvori kombinacijo vode in ledu, imenovano toča. Zaradi trka je bil rahlo pozitiven naboj prenesen na ledene kristale, rahel negativni naboj pa na točo.
Tok potisne lažje kristale ledu navzgor in povzroči nabiranje pozitivnih nabojev na zadnji strani oblaka. Nazadnje, vpliv Zemljine teže povzroči, da toča pada z negativnim nabojem, ker je toča postaja vse težje, ko se približuje sredini in dnu oblaka. Ločevanje in kopičenje naboja se nadaljuje, dokler potencial ne zadostuje za sprožitev praznjenja.
Druga hipoteza o polarizacijskem mehanizmu ima dve komponenti. Poglejmo, kaj so:
- Padajoči led in vodne kapljice postanejo polarizirane, ko padejo v naravno zemeljsko električno polje.
- Padajoči delci ledu trčijo in se napolnijo z elektrostatično indukcijo.
Kako nastajajo žarki in njihove različne vrste
- Najpogostejša strela. je najpogosteje opažena, znana kot črtasta strela. To je vidni del sledenja žarkov. Večina jih je v oblaku in jih zato ni mogoče videti. Poglejmo, katere so glavne vrste žarkov:
- Strela oblak-zemlja: je najbolj znan in drugi najpogostejši. To je največja grožnja življenju in premoženju. Lahko udari v tla in se izprazni med kumulonimbusnim oblakom in zemljo.
- Pearl Ray: To je strela od oblaka do tal, ki se zdi razdeljena na vrsto kratkih, svetlih delov.
- Staccato strela: je še ena kratkotrajna strela od oblaka do zemlje in zdi se, da je edini blisk. Običajno je zelo svetel in ima velik vpliv.
- Razčlenjen žarek: so tisti žarki od oblaka do tal, ki kažejo razvejanost njihove poti.
- Strela v tleh v oblaku: gre za izpust med zemljo in oblakom, ki se začne z začetnim udarcem navzgor. Redkeje je mošt.
- Strela od oblaka do oblaka: se pojavi med območji, ki niso v stiku s tlemi. Običajno se pojavi, ko dva ločena oblaka ustvarita razliko v električnem potencialu.
Upam, da boste s temi informacijami izvedeli več o tem, kako nastajajo žarki, njihove značilnosti in različne vrste, ki obstajajo.

prompt.content:
Si profesionalni prevajalec iz angleščine v slovenščino. Tvoja naloga je ustvariti visoko kakovostne prevode, ki so naravni, tekoči in natančni. Izogibaj se dobesednim prevodom, ki zvenijo nenaravno. Upoštevaj kontekst, idiome in kulturne reference. Ne dodajaj nobenih dodatnih informacij ali komentarjev, samo prevod.

Prevedi podano angleško besedilo v slovenščino.

Force and Area
When we walk on snow, we sink in. However, if we attach skis to our feet, the sinking is much less. In both cases, we exert the same weight on the surface, but this weight is distributed over a different area each time. This also applies to skiing down a slope, where we only exert the perpendicular component of our weight on the surface. The ratio between the force and the area over which this force acts perpendicularly is clearly an important quantity; we call it pressure:
(10.1)
|p = F⊥ / S|
A suitable unit for pressure is kp/cm2. Not only weight, but also other forces, such as pressing a hand against a wall, exert pressure. When the area over which the force acts is very small, the pressure becomes very large. The pressure under the tip or edge of a knife is so enormous that it can easily pierce and cut various materials.

A Liquid Ocean
Because we live at the bottom of an air ocean, the ground is under pressure due to the weight of the air. At the bottom of the sea, the pressure from the weight of the water is added. However, water or air in a container does not only exert pressure on the bottom but also on the walls, on bodies immersed in it, and on itself. At any point in a liquid, imagine a triangular prism of liquid with a horizontal, vertical, and oblique surface. The prism is at rest, so perpendicular forces must act on its surfaces, and their sum must be equal to zero. This implies that the pressures on each surface are equal. This means that at any point in a liquid, pressure acts equally in all directions; it is isotropic (Pascal).

Pressure and Depth
A column of water or air with a specific weight σ, a cross-section S, and a height h has a weight Fg = σSh, so it causes an increase in pressure below it of Fg/S, i.e.,
(10.2)
|Δp = σh|
This is the hydrostatic equation (Stevin). The equation shows that in the sea, the pressure increases by 1 kp/cm2 every 10 meters of depth. At a depth of 5 km, which is the typical depth of the oceans, the pressure is already enormous. It is said that a piece of wood, weighted and submerged to the bottom and then brought back up, is so compressed that it sinks in a barrel of water like a brick.
In the atmosphere, whose specific weight we do not (yet) know, we cannot say how quickly the pressure decreases with altitude. Since air, as we know, is compressible, its specific weight should decrease with altitude. If we could measure the air pressure at different altitudes, we could calculate the specific weight in the intermediate column.

Equilibrium of Pressures
How can we measure air pressure? By balancing it with a column of some suitable liquid. Due to its high specific weight, mercury is best. We pour mercury into a glass tube 1 m long, closed at one end, up to the top, close it with a thumb, turn it over, and insert it into a container of mercury. The column of mercury in the tube drops, and an empty space forms above it. The pressures of the air and the mercury column are equalized. In places at sea level, the column is on average 760 mm high (Torricelli). This means – with a specific weight of mercury of 13.5 kp/dm3 – a pressure of 1.03 kp/cm2. We will briefly call this pressure 1 atmosphere (atm). With an accuracy of a few percent, 1 atm ≈ 1 kp/cm2, and both units are treated as synonyms. A convenient and illustrative unit for air pressure is also 1 mm Hg = 1/760 atm.

Height of the Atmosphere
The air pressure at sea level is not everywhere and always the same, but fluctuates by up to ± 5%. It decreases with altitude. In the first hundred meters, the mercury column drops by about 9 mm, and then less and less. This means that, according to the hydrostatic equation (10.2), the specific weight of the air in the ground layer is about 1.2 kp/m3, a thousand times less than water. If the specific weight of the air did not change with altitude and was the same as at sea level, the atmosphere would end at 8 km. In reality, however, at the summits of the highest mountains, at an altitude of 8 km, we measure a pressure of about 1/3 kp/cm2.
Measuring pressure is more convenient if the container and tube are combined into a single tube in the shape of a J, where the long arm is closed and the short arm is open. This is a barometer.
In a tube, vertically inserted into water, the liquid level stands at the same height as outside. If, for any reason, the air pressure above the liquid level in the tube were to decrease, but not outside, the external excess pressure would push the water into the tube so high that it would balance it with the weight of the rising column.

Suction Piston
How can we reduce the air pressure in a tube? In the same way we drink water through a straw: we cover it with our tongue and pull it back; the air from the straw occupies the newly created space, becomes thinner, the pressure decreases, and the water in the straw rises. Based on this example, we build a piston pump, in which the role of the mouth and tongue is played by a cylinder with a movable piston. Two movable flaps ensure that the pumped water and air do not flow back. Such a pump can suck water from a maximum depth of 10 m and then, if necessary, push it to any height.

Liquid Lever
In a communicating vessel with a narrow and a wide arm, the water stands at the same height in both. If we pour an additional layer of water of the same thickness into each arm (let's color it red), it will again stand at the same height everywhere. The volume of the added water and, therefore, its weight is greater in the wide arm than in the narrow arm. Instead of pouring water, we can close each arm with a piston and place a corresponding weight on it. A smaller weight in the narrower arm balances a large weight in the wide arm. It is clear that F1/S1 = F2/S2. There is no limit to the size of the two weights, only their ratio must be appropriate. This is a "liquid lever."

Enormous Forces
If we load the narrow piston in a balanced liquid lever with a force F1, the wide piston will push upwards with a large force F2 = F1(S2/S1). We can use this force for various purposes – lifting a load, twisting and piercing sheet metal, etc. The forces we can create in this way can be enormous. Of course, their displacements are correspondingly smaller, since the output work cannot be greater than the input work. In such hydraulics, we use oil instead of water to avoid rusting.
If we block the wide piston so that it cannot move, we create a large pressure in the liquid below it. Of course, the walls must be strong enough to withstand it.

Thinning Air
A piston pump "sucks" water, which is pushed into it by the external air pressure. If we connect the pump via a good valve to a closed, rigid container with air, it "sucks" the air, which is pushed into it by the pressure in the container. The less air remains in the container, the lower the pressure shown by the connected barometer. Good piston pumps can reduce the pressure to 1/103 kp/cm2. If the container is not really rigid, it will be squeezed by the external air pressure into a lump when it is sufficiently emptied. The forces acting on the empty container are surprisingly large: on the lid of a jam jar with a cross-section of 1 dm2, the external air presses with a force of 100 kp!

Compressing Air
A pump with reversed valves becomes a compressor: we can pump air into a container. In this process, the container and the compressor heat up considerably. It is clear that the air heats up when compressed, and the surroundings also heat up.
Weighing Air
Pumping air into a container gives us the idea of how to measure its specific weight in a simple way. We weigh an open glass flask equipped with a tap. We pump additional air into it with a compressor, close the tap, and weigh the flask again. Then, we slowly release the trapped air through a glass tube into an inverted cylinder filled with water and immersed in a container of water; this is a gas cylinder. We mark the volume of the released air on the cylinder, typically a liter. The difference between the two weights and the volume uniquely determine the specific weight of the air: 1 liter weighs 1.2 pounds, as we already know [10.3]. Instead of pumping air into a container, we can pump it out. If we weigh the full and empty container, we again obtain the weight of the air. We must only make sure that we pump out as much air as possible.
Elastic Bellows
A mercury barometer is awkward to carry and use. What would be a better measuring device? Instead of balancing the pressure with a column of liquid, we can balance it with an elastic bellows in the shape of an accordion. A sheet metal bellows, from which part of the air is pumped out and then sealed, is compressed under higher external pressure and expands under lower pressure. A pointer attached to the wall of the bellows indicates all this. We calibrate the device with a mercury barometer or a piston cylinder under weights and obtain a spring barometer or aneroid.
Altimeter and Depth Gauge
With an aneroid, we can conveniently measure air pressure on the ground. If we previously measure the dependence of air pressure on altitude, it can even be used as a measuring device for altitude. In a modified form, it is also suitable for measuring pressure – and thus depth – under the sea. Various forms of aneroid pressure gauges (manometers) cover a measuring range between 1/103 and 103 kp/cm2.
Body in a Liquid
Because the pressure in the sea increases with depth, a submerged body experiences an upward force that opposes its weight. The upward pressure on the lower surface of the body is greater than the downward pressure on the upper surface. Let us imagine an arbitrarily shaped body, made entirely of water, for example, a vertical cylinder. This water body is at rest, so the upward force is obviously equal to its weight. If we replace the water body with a "real" body, the upward force of the surrounding water on it remains the same as before. The upward force on a submerged body of any shape is therefore equal to the weight of the displaced liquid:
(10.3)
|F = σV|
This is Archimedes' law. If the upward force is less than the weight of the body, it sinks; otherwise, it rises to the surface and floats. Under the surface, only as much remains so that the weight of the displaced water is equal to its weight. Bodies denser than water sink, and less dense ones float. Ice floats, so it is less dense than water. Icebergs hide 9/10 of their volume under the surface. It seems that water is also the only substance whose volume increases when it freezes. Due to the upward force, stones seem lighter in water than on land. The same applies to bodies in air: when weighing accurately, the upward force on the object and the weights must be taken into account.
Floating Ships
Boats and ships float, even if they are made of iron. They are simply shaped so that the weight of the displaced water becomes equal to the weight of the ship at a shallow draft. Floating lasts until water enters the ship, increasing its weight (let's imagine that we loaded it with stones instead of water) to the point where it overcomes the upward force.
Like any body, a ship has its center of gravity. It also has a center of buoyancy for the displaced water (we must imagine it in the hole that the ship makes under the surface); this center is called the metacenter. The weight of the ship acts at the center of gravity, and the upward force acts at the metacenter. For the ship to be stable, its center of gravity must be below the metacenter, both in the upright position of the ship and at the greatest possible inclination. Only then will the inclined ship return to its upright position. That is why ships, especially tall sailing ships, have heavily weighted keels.
Float
The upward force on the same body in fresh and salt water is different, which we can see nicely when we swim. Salt water has a higher specific weight, and we sink less in it. If we weigh a metal ball first in air and then – suspended on a thin thread – in fresh and salt water, the ratio of the two weight changes is equal to the ratio of the specific weights of the two liquids. This is how we measure the relative specific weights of liquids. For convenience, we make a float – a closed glass tube, which is weighted at the bottom so that it floats upright. It sinks more in less dense liquids and less in denser ones. We calibrate the float in different liquids and draw a scale on it. With it, we can measure, for example, the proportion of dissolved salt in water or the proportion of alcohol in spirits. □

Sila in ploskev
Ko hodimo po snegu, se vdiramo. Če pa pod noge pritrdimo smuči, je vdiranje dosti manjše. Obakrat pritiskamo na podlago z enako težo, vendar je ta vsakič porazdeljena na drugačno površino. To velja tudi za smuko po klancu, na katerega pritiskamo le s pravokotno komponento teže. Količnik med silo in ploskvijo, na katero ta sila deluje pravokotno, je očitno pomembna količina; rečemo ji tlak:
(10.1)
|p =||

Primerna enota za tlak je kp/cm2. Ne samo teža, ampak tudi druge sile, recimo pritiskanje dlani na steno, izvajajo tlak. Kadar je ploščina, na katero deluje sila, zelo majhna, postane tlak zelo velik. Tlak pod konico ali rezilom noža je tako ogromen, da zlahka prebadamo in režemo razne snovi.
Tekočinski ocean
Ker živimo na dnu zračnega oceana, so tla pod tlakom zaradi njegove teže. Na morskem dnu se doda še tlak zaradi teže vode. Voda ali zrak v posodi pa ne pritiskata zgolj na dno, temveč tudi na stene, vanju potopljena telesa in sebe samo. Na poljubnem mestu v tekočini si zamislimo trikotno tekočinsko prizmo z vodoravno, navpično in poševno ploskvijo. Prizma miruje, zato morajo na njene ploskve delovati pravokotne sile, katerih vsota mora biti eneka nič. Iz tega sledi, da so tlaki na vsako ploskev enaki. To pomeni, da na vsakem mestu v tekočini deluje tlak v vse smeri enako, da je izotropen (Pascal).
Tlak in globina
Vodni ali zračni stolpec s specifično težo σ, presekom S in višino h je težek Fg = σSh, zato povzroča pod seboj prirast tlaka Fg/S, torej
(10.2)
|Δp = σh .|
To je hidrostatična enačba (Stevin). Enačba pove, da v morju naraste tlak vsakih 10 metrov globine za 1 kp/cm2. V globini 5 km, kolikor so tipično globoki oceani, je tlak že strašen. Pravijo, da se kos lesa, z utežjo potopljen na dno in ponovno izvlečen, tako stisne, da v sodu vode potone kot opeka.
V ozračju, ki mu (zaenkrat) ne poznamo specifične teže, ne moremo reči, kako hitro pada tlak z višino. Ker je zrak, kot vemo, stisljiv, bi se morala njegova specifična teža z višino manjšati. Če bi zmogli izmeriti tlak zraka na različnih višinah, bi lahko specifično težo v vmesnem stolpcu izračunali.
Ravnovesje tlakov
Kako bi izmerili zračni tlak? Tako, da ga uravnovesimo s stolpcem kakšne primerne tekočine. Zaradi velike specifične teže je najboljše živo srebro. V stekleno cev dolžine 1 m, na enem koncu zaprto, nalijemo živo srebro do vrha, ga zapremo s palcem, obrnemo in vtaknemo v posodo z živim srebrom. Stolpec živega srebra v cevi se zniža in nad njim nastane prazen prostor. Tlaka zračnega in živosrebrnega stolpca sta izenačena. V krajih na morski gladini je stolpec povprečno visok 760 mm (Torricelli). To pomeni – ob specifični teži živega srebra 13,5 kp/dm3 – tlak 1,03 kp/cm2. Ta tlak bomo na kratko poimenovali 1 atmosfera (atm). Pri natančnosti na nekaj odstotkov velja 1 atm ≈ 1 kp/cm2 in obe enoti obravnavamo kot sinonima. Priročna in nazorna enota za zračni tlak je tudi 1 mm Hg = 1/760 atm.
Višina ozračja
Zračni tlak na morski gladini ni povsod in vedno enak, ampak niha do največ ± 5 %. Z višino pada. V prvih sto metrih pade živosrebrni stolpec za okrog 9 mm, potem pa čedalje manj. To torej pomeni, da znaša po hidrostatični enačbi (10.2) specifična teža zraka v prizemni plasti okrog 1,2 kp/m3, tisočkrat manj od vode. Če se specifična teža zraka z višino ne bi spreminjala in bi bila enaka tisti na morski gladini, potem bi bilo ozračja konec pri 8 km. Dejansko pa na vrhovih najvišjih gora, na višini 8 km, izmerimo tlak okrog 1/3 · kp/cm2.
Merjenje tlaka je bolj priročno, če posodo in cev združimo v enotno cev z obliko črke J, pri kateri je dolgi krak zaprt in kratki odprt. To je barometer.
V cevi, navpično vtaknjeni v vodo, stoji gladina enako visoko kot zunaj. Če bi se pa iz kakršnegakoli razloga zmanjšal tlak zraka nad gladino v cevi, ne pa tudi zunaj, bi zunanji presežni tlak rinil vodo v cev tako visoko, dokler ga ne bi uravnovesil težni tlak dvigajočega se stolpca.
Sesalni bat
Kako naj zmanjšamo tlak zraka v cevi? Tako, kot pijemo vodo po slamici: pokrijemo jo z jezikom in ga povlečemo nazaj; zrak iz slamice zavzame novo ustvarjeni prostor, se zredči, tlak se mu zmanjša in voda v slamici se dvigne. Po tem zgledu zgradimo batno črpalko, v kateri igra vlogo ust in jezika cilinder s premičnim batom. Za to, da črpana voda in zrak ne odtekata nazaj, skrbita dve premični zaklopki. Takšna črpalka lahko sesa vodo največ iz globine 10 m in jo nadalje, po potrebi, še potiska do poljubne višine.
Tekočinski vzvod
V vezni posodi z ozkim in širokim krakom stoji voda v obeh enako visoko. Če v vsak krak nalijemo dodatno, enako debelo plast vode (obarvajmo jo rdeče), bo ta spet stala povsod enako visoko. Prostornina dolite vode in s tem njena teža je v širokem kraku večja kot v ozkem. Namesto dolivanja vode lahko vsak krak zapremo z batom in nanj položimo ustrezno utež. Manjša utež v ožjem kraku drži ravnovesje veliki uteži v širokem kraku. Očitno velja F1/S1 = F2/S2. Nobene omejitve ni glede velikosti obeh tež, le njuno razmerje mora biti ustrezno. To je "tekočinski vzvod".
Ogromne sile
Če v uravnovešenem tekočinskem vzvodu obremenimo ozki bat s silo F1, bo široki bat potisnil navzgor z veliko silo F2 = F1(S2/S1). To silo lahko izkoristimo za več namenov – dvignemo breme, zvijamo in luknjamo železno pločevino in podobno. Sile, ki jih tako ustvarimo, so lahko ogromne. Seveda pa so njihovi premiki ustrezno krajši, saj izhodno delo ne more biti večje od vhodnega. V takšnih hidravlikah uporabljamo olje namesto vode, da se izognemo rjavenju.
Če široki bat blokiramo, da se ne more premikati, ustvarimo v tekočini pod njim velik tlak. Seveda morajo biti stene dovolj močne, da zdržijo.
Redčenje zraka
Batna črpalka "sesa" vodo, ki jo vanjo potiska zunanji zračni tlak. Če črpalko priključimo preko dobrega ventila na zaprto, togo posodo z zrakom, pa "sesa" zrak, ki ga vanjo potiska kar tlak v posodi. Čim manj zraka ostane v posodi, tem manjši tlak pokaže priključeni barometer. Dobre batne črpalke znižajo tlak do 1/103 · kp/cm2. Ako posoda ni zares trdna, jo – ko je dovolj izčrpana – zunanji zračni tlak stisne v kepo. Sile, ki delujejo na prazno posodo, so presenetljivo velike: na pokrov kozarca za marmelado, ki ima presek 1 dm2, pritiska zunanji zrak s silo 100 kp!
Zgoščanje zraka
Črpalka z obrnjenimi ventili postane tlačilka: v posodo lahko tlačimo zrak. Pri tem se posoda in tlačilka močno segrevata. Očitno se zrak pri stiskanju segreva in od njega se segreva tudi okolica.
Tehtanje zraka
Tlačenje zraka v posodo nam da zamisel, kako izmeriti njegovo specifično težo na preprost način. Stehtamo odprto stekleno bučo, opremljeno s pipico. Vanjo s tlačilko natlačimo dodaten zrak, pipico zapremo in bučo spet stehtamo. Nato po stekleni cevki počasi spustimo ujeti zrak v obrnjen cilinder, napolnjen z vodo in potopljen v posodo z vodo; to je plinska kad. Na cilindru označimo prostornino doteklega zraka, tipično kakšen liter. Z razliko obeh tež in s prostornino je specifična teža zraka enolično določena: 1 liter tehta 1,2 ponda, kakor že vemo [10.3]. Namesto da tlačimo zrak v posodo, ga lahko iz nje izčrpamo. Če stehtamo polno in prazno posodo, spet dobimo težo zraka. Paziti moramo le na to, da izčrpamo čim več zraka.
Elastični meh
Živosrebrni barometer je neroden za prenašanje in uporabo. Kakšen bi bil boljši merilnik? Namesto s težo tekočinskega stolpca lahko tlak uravnovesimo z elastičnim mehom v obliki harmonike. Pločevinast meh, iz katerega izčrpamo del zraka in ga nato neprodušno zapremo, se stiska pod večjim zunanjim tlakom in se razteza pod manjšim tlakom. Kazalec, pritrjen na steno meha, vse to pokaže. Napravo umerimo z živosrebrnim barometrom ali z batnim cilindrom pod utežmi in dobimo vzmetni barometer ali aneroid.
Višinomer in globinomer
Z aneroidom udobno merimo zračni tlak po Zemlji. Če predhodno izmerimo odvisnost zračnega tlaka od višine, pa je uporaben celo kot merilec nadmorske višine. V predelani obliki je primeren tudi za merjenje tlaka – in s tem globine – pod morjem. Razne oblike aneroidnih tlakomerov (manometrov) pokrivajo merilno območje med 1/103 in 103 kp/cm2.
Telo v tekočini
Ker tlak v morju narašča z globino, čuti potopljeno telo vzgon, ki nasprotuje njegovi teži. Tlak navzgor na spodnjo ploskev telesa je namreč večji kot tlak navzdol na zgornjo ploskev. Zamislimo si poljubno oblikovano telo, sestavljeno kar iz vode same, recimo navpični cilinder. To vodno telo miruje, zato je očitno vzgon enak njegovi teži. Če nadomestimo vodno telo s "pravim" telesom, ostane vzgon okolišnje vode nanj prav tak, kot prej. Vzgon na potopljeno telo kakršnekoli oblike je torej enak teži izpodrinjene tekočine:
(10.3)
|F = σV .|
To je vzgonski zakon (Arhimed). Če je vzgon manjši od teže telesa, to potone, sicer se pa dvigne na površje in plava. Pod gladino ga ostane toliko, da je teža izpodrinjene vode enaka njegovi teži. Od vode gostejši kosi snovi torej potonejo, redkejši plavajo. Led plava, torej je redkejši od vode. Ledene gore skrivajo 9/10 svoje prostornine pod gladino. Kakor kaže, je voda tudi edina snov, ki se ji pri zmrzovanju poveča prostornina. Zaradi vzgona se nam zdijo kamni v vodi lažji kot na kopnem. Isto velja za telesa v zraku: pri natančnem tehtanju je treba upoštevati tudi vzgon merjenca in uteži.
Plavanje ladij
Čolni in ladje plavajo, tudi če so narejeni iz železa. Oblikovani so pač tako, da teža izpodrinjene vode postane enaka teži ladje že pri plitvem ugrezu. Plavanje traja, dokler v ladjo ne vdere voda, s čimer se ji teža toliko poveča (mislimo si, da smo jo namesto z vodo obremenili s kamenjem), da premaga vzgon.
Kot vsako telo ima tudi ladja svoje težišče. Prav tako ima svoje težišče izpodrinjena voda (predstavljati si jo moramo v luknji, ki jo ladja dela pod gladino); temu težišču rečemo metacenter. Teža ladje prijemlje v težišču in vzgon v metacentru. Da bo ladja stabilna, mora biti njeno težišče pod metacentrom, in to pri pokončni legi ladje ter še pri čim večjem nagibu. Le v tem primeru se nagnjena ladja sama vzravna. Zato imajo ladje, zlasti visoke jadrnice, močno obtežene kobilice.
Plavač
Vzgon istega telesa v sladki in slani vodi je različen, kar lepo vidimo, ko plavamo. Slana voda ima namreč večjo specifično težo in v njej se manj potopimo. Če stehtamo kovinsko kroglico najprej na zraku in nato – obešeno na tanki nitki – še potopljeno v eno in drugo tekočino, je razmerje obeh težnih sprememb enako razmerju specifičnih tež obeh tekočin. Tako merimo relativne specifične teže tekočin. Zaradi udobnosti izdelamo še plavač – zaprto stekleno cevko, ki je spodaj obtežena, da plava pokonci. V redkejših tekočinah se potopi bolj in v gostejših manj. Plavač umerimo v različnih tekočinah in nanj narišemo skalo. Z njim merimo, recimo, delež raztopljene soli v vodi ali delež alkohola v žganju. □
