Patogenost koronavirusov so dokazali na prostovoljcih in po povečanju količine protitelesa pri osebah, ki prebolijo navaden prehlad. Bolezen je klinično docela podobna prehladu, ki ga povzročajo rinovirusi. V nekaterih raziskavah pa so ugotovili tudi povezanost med infekcijo s koronavirusi in boleznijo spodnjih dihal. Koronavirusi so endemični skoraj povsod po svetu. Ponekod so opisane epidemije zlasti pri otrocih, drugod pa pri odraslih, odvisno od tega, na katerem koncu sveta živimo. Te epidemije se pojavljajo v dve- do štiriletnih presledkih, prevladujejo pa predvsem v zimskem času. Uporaba cepiva proti koronavirusom je dvomljiva, kajti sevi, ki so jih doslej osamili, se antigensko razločujejo, in kar je še bolj zapleteno, protitelesa v serumu ne varujejo pred ponovno infekcijo. Priprava cepiva bo napredovala šele, ko bodo korovirusne antigene bolje preučili, kar jih do danes še niso.”
MOJE IZKUŠNJE
Delala sem tudi na intenzivni negi. Me smo še sestre starega kova, ki smo imele prakso vsak dan dopoldan, popoldan pa pouk, tako da smo dale vse skozi in pridobile ogromno znanja. Veliko smo delale in zelo veliko so nas naučili. Danes v srednjih šolah sploh nimajo prakse in pridejo kar delat. Mislim, da osnovnošolske otroke in srednješolce zelo poneumljajo, tako da nas lahko potem lažje vodijo.
Sodelujem tudi z Nacionalnim inštitutom za javno zdravje – s ta poštenimi, da se razumemo – in pogovarjala sem se s tistimi, ki so bili odstavljeni, tudi oni točno vejo, za kaj gre in od kod je to prišlo. Mnoga farmacevtska podjetja – mi temu rečemo farmakomafija – so zaradi svojih zdravil, cepiv in stranskih učinkov že odgovarjala in morala tudi plačati milijonske kazni. Tako da, kar se tega cepiva tiče, če bomo res vsi tožili in se tega držali, mislim, da bodo morali vsi, tudi naši zdravniki, ravnatelji, direktorji, odgovarjati. Moramo pa biti res zelo močni, da peljemo to naprej.
KATERA CEPIVA SO PLACEBO?
Raziskava o cepivu, ki se zdaj trenutno uporablja in se ljudje z njim cepijo, je pokazala, da je 30 % tega cepiva placebo. Ne morete vedeti, ali ste dobili placebo, prav tako nikakor ne morete z gotovostjo vedeti, da ste dobili Johnsona ali AstraZeneco, tudi če si to izberete. Lahko prinesejo cepivo, ki ste ga izbrali, ni pa rečeno, da boste res z njim cepljeni. To se ne dogaja povsod, a glede na informacije, ki jih dobivam od kolegic po Sloveniji, se dogaja tudi to.
Če se greste cepit: ko dobite kartonček, je gor nalepka, na njej pa številka – 1, 2 ali 3. Tisti, ki dobi placebo, zapomnite si – dobi številko 1. Ni 2 in ni 3. Placebo ima vedno številko 1. Oni vejo, komu dajo placebo. Vi pa ne veste. Oni so računali, da nas bodo ogromno pripravili do tega, da se bomo cepili. Nas je pa ogromno takih, ki se ne bomo cepili, in so nas, necepljene, ravno tako vključili v študijo. Tistih 30 % jim ostane za raziskavo (verjetno nas bo več).
STRANSKI UČINKI, KI SE POJAVLJAJO PRI CEPLJENIH
Nekateri zdravniki so zelo striktni in oddajajo poročila o stranskih učinkih na NIJZ, nekateri ne. Eni jih zapišejo v karton, drugi ne. To, kar se pri nas dogaja – ko poročajo, da ni nobene smrtne žrtve, ali pa da jih je samo deset ali kolikor koli že – lažejo. Do zdaj je v Sloveniji zaradi stranskih učinkov cepiva umrlo okrog 500 ljudi. V Evropi pa okoli 700.000. Nekaj pod milijon pa je zelo grdih stranskih učinkov. Pravila so taka, da če se uporablja neko cepivo in ugotovijo, da je zaradi stranskih učinkov umrlo 50 ljudi, se to cepivo odstrani in se ne cepi več z njim. To, kar zdaj delajo, pa vemo, da je genocid nad človeštvom. To lahko 100 % potrdim, ker poznam evropskega poslanca Milana Brgleza in gospoda Dejana Židana. Gospoda Brgleza sem direktno vprašala:
“Kdo je podpisal pogodbo za Slovenijo s Svetovno zdravstveno organizacijo, da se lahko izvaja genocid nad človeštvom?”
“No, no,” je rekel, “tako pa ne bomo govorili.”
“Kaj bomo pa rekli?” sem vprašala. “Poskuse na ljudeh? Mi lahko poveste?”
“Ja, veste, takole je: jaz sem govoril z znanstveniki in jaz zaupam znanstvenikom in znanstvenike in znanost je treba podpirati.”
Rekla sem: “V redu, jaz sem za, da se podpira znanost, naj gre znanost naprej. Ampak znanost na ljudeh, toliko grdih stranskih učinkov, doživljenjskih posledic, s tem, da je v cepivu uran, a vi podpirate to?”
“Ja,” je rekel, “znanost je treba podpirati.”
Tako da veste, da to cepljenje vsi podpirajo. Naj bodo levi, desni, srednji, ni važno, vsi so v tej – kot ji jaz rečem – štali. Vprašala sem gospoda Brgleza, ali se je cepil, in odgovoril je, da se je. Rekla sem mu: “Verjamem, ampak za vas in za vse v Državnem zboru je bil placebo. Zato da se lahko po prsih tolčete, da nimate nobenih stranskih učinkov in da vam popolnoma nič ni. Ampak nisem pa slišala, da bi se cepili tudi drugič in tretjič.”
Ko bodo delali raziskave, septembra, oktobra, novembra, bodo primerjali: kdo bo prej zbolel za gripo oz. koronavirusom, preučevali bodo, kakšni stranski učinki so bili po prvem cepljenju, kakšni po drugem, kakšni bodo po tretjem – kdor bo seveda sploh prišel do tretjega cepljenja. Grdo povedano, ampak tako je, ker vemo, kaj je v cepivu.
Prva študija, ki jo naredijo, je študija randomizina. Druga je placebo študija, tretja pa so opazovalci slepe študije. Diagnoza C45 do C49 je rak mehkih tkiv. Ta se bo pojavil tam nekje od 3 do 10 let po cepljenju. To so dokazali že leta 1960.
IMUNOST OBSTAJA IN MEDIJI LAŽEJO!
Naj vas razveselim: 60 % ljudi že ima imunost. Tisti, ki smo pozitivno naravnani in tisti, ki smo danes tu, smo vsi imuni proti tem virusom. Smrtnost v svetu, kakor smo jo preračunali preko Nacionalnega inštituta poštenih, je bila 0,0002 %. Pri nas pa so se diagnoze pisale kar vsepovprek. Dobili so jih tudi tisti, ki so imeli recimo prometno nesrečo, tako kot moja teta. Imela je hudo prometno nesrečo, zaradi katere je umrla, ampak diagnoza, ki jo je dobila, je bil kovid. Druga moja teta, ki je umrla zaradi trebušne slinavke in je bila negativna na virus – vsi smo vedeli, da bo umrla v enem tednu -, je dobila diagnozo kovid. Toliko, da veste, da tiste zastavice, ki so visele v Ljubljani – 4400 žrtev – niso prave. Prava številka je 2316, kar je dosti manj, kot je bilo lansko leto umrlih za gripo. Vemo, da se letos niso jemali vzorci krvi niti brisi za gripo. Letos gripe ni bilo!
Tisto cepivo proti gripi je samo 50-% učinkovito. Zdravniki vam ne povejo, da vsakomur, ki se cepi proti gripi, pade odpornost za tri mesece. Ne en teden ali dva, tri mesece traja, da si telo opomore! Vemo, kaj je bilo v Bergamu. Od vseh tistih ljudi, ki jih številčno spet ni bilo toliko, kot so naši mediji poročali, so umirali samo tisti, ki so bili oktobra, novembra cepljeni proti gripi. Nakar so začeli decembra oz. januarja, februarja in marca umirati, prvič zaradi starosti, tam so ljudje stari sto let in več, drugič pa zato, ker so imeli vsi pridružene bolezni, s tem, da njihovo zdravstvo ni takšno kot pri nas. To vem, ker je moja prijateljica delala v Milanu in mi je vseskozi o tem poročala. Tudi tiste krste, ki so nam jih kazali, niso bile resnične. Naši mediji, ne bom rekla novinarji, ampak mediji, poročajo o vseh stvareh napačno.
Imam prijateljico v Bosni in Hercegovini. Ne nosijo mask, žurajo, mi pa zaprti, otroci ne smejo v šolo, ne smejo trenirati, oni pa žurajo v zaprtem prostoru brez mask ob čudoviti glasbi. Bosna in Hercegovina ima najmanj mrtvih in okuženih, enako kot Švedska.
KAJ SE ZGODI PO CEPLJENJU PROTI GRIPI?
Kot rečeno, sama sem precej delala tudi na intenzivni negi. In lahko vam povem, da pri vsaki gripi pridejo cepljeni k zdravniku po treh dneh, s povišano temperaturo, bolečinami v mišicah, teče jim iz nosu, imajo glavobol. Vsi vemo, da po cepljenju sledi reakcija. Ampak noben zdravnik vam ne bo v karton napisal, da je to reakcija po cepljenju. NI reakcija. To je “samo visoka temperatura”, to so “samo bolečine v mišicah”, to je “samo glavobol”. Ta človek ostane tri dni doma, potem gre za en teden delat, pride nazaj z bronhitisom, mu damo antibiotik, ostane doma deset, štirinajst dni, odvisno od tega, kaj pokaže kri. Potem gre človek nazaj v službo. Pride čez štirinajst dni spet nazaj, s pljučnico. Težko diha, gre v bolnico, na kisik, in kadar je hudo, tako kot pri koroni, isti potek je, gre na respirator. In če ima srečo, preživi, če pa ne, pa umre. Ravno tako kot pri gripi je tudi pri koroni izventelesni obtok. Če se spomnite govora Beovičeve – vsako leto imamo ogromno gripe, oddelki so polni, ljudje ležijo na hodnikih, ni prostora, intenzivne enote pokajo po šivih, imamo ljudi z izventelesnim obtokom, umirajo nam otroci – to je njeno govorjenje vsako leto, kadar je bila gripa. Imela sem posnetek, bi ga predvajala, pa so mi ga na žalost brisali. Prosila sem tudi RTV, kjer hranijo vse posnetke – od Beovičeve ga nisem dobila.
VSE TO VEMO, AMPAK ZASLUŽKI …
Ko sva govorila z gospodom Brglezom, je rekel: “Ja, saj vse to vemo, ampak tudi zaslužki so …”
“Ja, zdajle vam je pa malo ušlo,” sem rekla, “ne ravno v hlače, ampak malo ste se zagovorili. Jaz točno vem, kakšne zaslužke imate – zdravniki in vsi ostali po stopničkah navzdol.” Vem pa tudi, koliko zasluži en zdravstveni dom in koliko zasluži bolnišnica s tem, ko se jemljejo brisi. Za eno palčko dobi zdravstveni dom 15 evrov, 5 evrov pa dobi od zavarovalnice, zato ker se to šteje kot poseg. Vsi vemo, da so zdaj vsi zdravstveni domovi in bolnišnice prišli na plus. Ampak kam so dali ta plus? Niso ga razdelili odpravam čakalnih dob niti ne novim aparaturam niti vsemu ostalemu, kar zdaj v zdravstvu manjka in nujno potrebujemo. Gre za enormne zaslužke in gre za genocid nad človeštvom. Gospodu Brglezu, ko sem mu to povedala, na koncu ni ostalo kaj dosti drugega, kot da reče: “No, ampak zdaj bova pa nehala, a ima kdo še kaj drugega za vprašat?”
“Ne, ne,” sem rekla, “razložite mi, nisem še izvedela, kdo je podpisal pogodbo.”
Na to so bili vsi tiho. Potem sem pred približno štirinajstimi dnevi izvedela, da sta bila to gospod Janša in gospod Pahor, in to že leta 2011. V letih 2016-2018 je Svetovna banka pobirala seznam, koliko rabimo cepiva in koliko testnih palčk. Tako da veste, da je bilo to že vse vnaprej pripravljeno. Najlažje pa je to, kar je naredila naša vlada – človeka najprej pošteno prestrašiti in potem, ko je prestrašen, postane anksiozen, depresiven, vse mu popusti, in potem samo še 24 ur na dan preži, kaj bodo zdaj novega povedali. Če bi radie in televizije ugasnili in časopise skurili, korone ne bi bilo.”
Pripravila: Sara Zupan
Vir: Zdravstveno osebje odkrito o koroni 1. del OSMA GENERACIJA – Vera Kanalec (bitchute.com)

In the spring, gardeners begin to battle weeds. One of the most common and troublesome is spurge. Many summer residents pull out the roots, although it reappears again and again. This is because a special approach is required to combat this plant.

- What is spurge?
- Harm to cultivated plants
- How to get rid of milkweed in the garden
- Mechanical methods
- Chemicals
- Preventive measures

What is spurge?
Today, there are many varieties of this weed. Of course, after looking at photos, everyone will immediately remember what the flower looks like.
Originally, the birthplace of this plant was Africa and Madagascar. The adaptability of this harmful organism to soil and climate contributed to its spread around the world. This weed cannot be ignored. It is a representative of vegetation that you cannot simply take out with your bare hands. An aggressive plant with triangular leaves, a strong stem, and attractive white sap that children like to paint with are its main characteristics. The root system usually goes deep into the soil, and if the root is not removed in time, it can extend almost 1 meter.
Experienced gardeners do not remove it by hand because they always have a faithful assistant - a shovel. Systematic deep weeding, autumn and spring digging, and the use of herbicides are the main deterrents to its growth.

Harm to cultivated plants
Before getting rid of the harmful organism, the damage and economic feasibility of fighting it are usually calculated. Based on this, farmers use threshold levels of harm. These thresholds include:
- Phytocenotic damage threshold (PDT) - the amount of weeds in crops, which practically do not affect the growth and development of cultivated plants and do not reduce their yield.
- Critical (statistical) power threshold (CPT) - the amount of weeds at which the yield is statistically significantly reduced.
Spurge interferes with the life of cultivated plants grown in the garden. With its developed root system, it very quickly drains all the useful substances from the soil, depriving the crop of nutrients and causing diseases or death.
Despite such harmful properties, this plant is a good indicator of soil.

How to get rid of milkweed in the garden
Spurge is primarily a weed, and there are several successful methods for dealing with it. The methods of control range from folk remedies to the use of modern drugs. Controlling this type of weed is very complex, but it is effective to use both mechanical and chemical methods simultaneously. To get rid of milkweed forever, you need to do everything possible, and in 1-2 years, you will see the result.

Mechanical methods
The best time to fight weeds is in the spring. During this period, the plant has just begun its life cycle. If you find the pest in time, it must be pulled out with the roots and no trace left in the soil, as it will germinate again soon.
If you are fighting it by hand, it is better to use a shovel and dig it out deeply under the root. Many gardeners use pruning or mowing, which we strongly do not recommend.

Chemicals
Another method, without which it is practically impossible to defeat the weed, is the use of various herbicides. For fighting it, both continuous-action herbicides and those specifically designed to combat milkweed are suitable:
- Continuous-action herbicides: "TACK", "Napalm", "Titus".
- Milkweed herbicides: "Lazurite", "Roundup", "Dicamba".
If you use chemical drugs, you need to increase the dosage. It is very effective to use a steam cutter, as after two or three applications of the chemical, the weed does not spread at all.

Preventive measures
After successfully removing the weed, it is worth taking all measures to maintain the achieved result. This will help deep digging of the soil at the site, as well as mulching the soil with organic or inorganic materials.
Inorganic materials that can be purchased in specialized stores. These can be various breathable films, spunbond. They effectively prevent the germination of plants.
Organic materials that can be used include sawdust, shavings, chips, crushed bark, leaves, compost, straw, paper, and cardboard.
We advise experienced gardeners to use excellent home remedies for prevention. The most effective is a water-alcohol solution. The ratio of alcohol to water is 1:10. With this solution, you need to pre-treat the beds that you have prepared for planting cultivated plants.
We hope that these tips will help you keep your site free of weeds and get a good harvest.

Ancient wisdom teaches us that illness originates in the gut. In everyday life, however, we only worry about the state of our gut when we experience problems directly related to it. We have already written about how to help with constipation and irritable bowel syndrome (NZ No. 105, 106). However, an imbalance in the gut microbiome can also be a contributing factor to many other diseases.

An Imbalanced Gut Microbiome as a Source of Chronic Diseases
If there are too many pathogenic gut microbes, they attack the intestinal wall. This makes the intestinal wall permeable, which can cause many serious diseases:
- Allergies. Large pieces of food pass through the permeable intestinal wall and enter the bloodstream. The immune system recognizes them as foreign and remembers them as such. When we consume the same food again, we experience an allergic reaction.
- Autoimmune diseases. Among the food that enters the bloodstream are proteins that have not been fully digested. The immune system remembers them as foreign. If it then finds similar proteins in our organs, it attacks those organs.

- Neurodegenerative diseases. Inflammatory molecules and pathogenic microbes can pass through the blood-brain barrier and enter the brain, causing neurodegenerative inflammation.
It is necessary to balance the gut microbiome by adding beneficial bacteria. This helps to heal the intestinal wall and stimulate the immune system to function normally. Dr. David Perlmutter (2017) states that gut bacteria regulate the function of the immune system and can "reset" it, preparing it to function normally again.

- Asthma and other allergies. A seven-year-old boy suffered from asthma. His breathing problems were alleviated with medication. Due to gut problems, he started taking a bio-probiotic EM. This calmed his gut, and the asthma attacks stopped.

This subsided after a week, and after about a month, I had regular bowel movements. My thyroid also started to function better, so the doctor predicted that I could reduce the dose of my medication by a third."
Neurologist Dr. David Perlmutter described a case of significant improvement in an autoimmune disease, multiple sclerosis, with specific methods of adding beneficial bacteria to the gut. Thirteen-year-old Jason, who had autism, repeated the same movements with his hands, could not tie his shoelaces, did not speak in complete sentences, and avoided communication. He suffered from frequent digestive problems and chronic ear inflammation. Dr. David Perlmutter (2017:150) prescribed him probiotics and vitamin D. After three weeks, Jason's mother said that the boy could now tie his shoelaces himself and talked to her more. They then underwent a fecal microbiota transplant. Kako si pomagamo pri zaprtju in preobčutljivem črevesju, smo že pisali ( NZ št. 105, 106). Neuravnoteženost črevesne biote pa je lahko kriva tudi za mnoge druge bolezni.
Neuravnotežena črevesna biota kot vir kroničnih bolezni
Če je patogenih črevesnih mikrobov preveč, načenjajo črevesno steno. Ta postane prepustna, kar povzroča mnoge resne bolezni:
- Alergije. Skozi prepustno črevesno steno vdirajo v kri preveliki koščki hrane. Imunski sistem jih zazna kot tujke in si jih trajno zapomni kot take. Ko ponovno zaužijemo tako hrano, doživimo alergijski napad.
- Avtoimunske bolezni. Med hrano, ki vdira v kri, so tudi še ne povsem prebavljene beljakovine. Imunski sistem si jih zapomni kot tujke. Če potem najde v naših organih podobne beljakovine, napade te organe.
- Sistemska vnetja. Iz črevesja vdirajo v kri tudi druge vnetne molekule (LPS, gliandin idr.) in patogeni mikrobi, ki lahko povzročijo vnetja v raznih organih.
- Nevro-degenerativna obolenja. Vnetne molekule in patogeni mikrobi lahko vdrejo skozi možgansko krvno bariero v kri in povzročajo nevro-degenerativna vnetja.
V črevesju je potrebno uravnovesiti bioto z dodajanjem dobrih bakterij. S tem zacelimo črevesno steno in spodbudimo imunski sistem k normalnemu delovanju. Dr. David Perlmutter (2017) navaja, da črevesne bakterije uravnavajo delovanje imunskega sistema in ga zmorejo »ponovno nastaviti« ter ga tako pripraviti, da spet deluje normalno.
Primeri učinkovite pomoči z dobrimi bakterijami
- Astma in druge alergije. Sedemletnega dečka je mučila astma. Dihalne težave so mu lajšali z zdravili. Zaradi črevesnih težav je začel uživati bio probiotik EM. Te so se umirile, ob tem pa so prenehali tudi astmatični napadi.
Petletna deklica je zbolela za atopičnim dermatitisom in senenim nahodom. »Bilo je zelo hudo«, nam je pisala njena mati, »saj ji je že skoraj vsaka hrana škodila«. Poskušali so ji pomagati z uživanjem bio probiotika EM. »Prvi dan se je po zaužitju probitika pojavila huda reakcija na koži in v želodcu«, je zapisala gospa. »Predvidevali smo, da je to le reakcija, zato smo vztrajali. Že naslednji dan je bilo veliko bolje in njeno zdravstveno stanje se je vidno izboljševalo. Tako vsako leto dvakrat nabavim 3-litrsko pakiranje tega probiotika za oba otroka in zase, kar se nam zelo pozna pri zdravju in splošnem počutju ter prebavi. Hčerka si je težave s kožo povsem pozdravila. Sedaj sta otroka stara 12 in 13 let«.
- Avtoimunske bolezni. Gospa z avtoimunskim obolenjem ščitnice je zaradi kroničnega zaprtja začela uživati bio probiotik EM. Tako je opisala svojo izkušnjo: »Prva dva dneva pitja probiotika nisem čutila bistvene spremembe. Od tretjega do petega dneva sem odvajala zelo smrdeče blato. To se je potem v tednu dni umirilo in po slabem mesecu sem redno odvajala. Tudi ščitnica je končno začela delovati bolje, tako da je zdravnik že napovedal, da bom odmerek zdravila lahko zmanjšala za tretjino«.
Nevrolog dr. David Perlmutter je opisal primer bistvenega izboljšanja avtoimunske bolezni multiple skleroze s posebnimi načini dodajanja dobrih bakterij v črevesje. Triinštirideset let staremu Carlosu, ki se je zaradi multiple skleroze komajda samostojno premikal, je predlagal, naj trikrat tedensko vnese v črevo dve do tri kapsule probiotika, raztopljene v pol litra mlačne vode. To naj napravi s klistirjem leže na boku in po vsakem vnosu naj ostane v tem položaju 20 minut. Po dveh tednih je Carlos shodil brez uporabe palice. Po nasvetu dr. Perlmutterja si je dal tudi presadili črevesno bioto iz zdravega človeka (FTM – Fecal Microbiota Transplantation). Po desetih ponovitvah te terapije je Carlos lahko hodil skoraj tako dobro, kot da ni zbolel za multiplo sklerozo (Perlmutter, 2017). Opise treh primerov podobnega trajnega izboljšanja multiple skleroze s pomočjo FTM je leta 2011 objavil avstralski zdravnik dr. Thomas Julius Borody v reviji American Journal of Gastroenterology. Izstopa primer moškega, ki je bil zaradi multiple skleroze pri tridesetih že priklenjen na voziček. Imel je vstavljen urinarni kateter. Ker je bil kronično hudo zaprt, so mu petkrat presadili črevesno bioto. S tem so mu odpravili zaprtje. Spet je shodil, pa tudi katetra ni več potreboval. V petnajstih letih po tem posegu se multipla skleroza ni ponovila (Borody et al., 2011a).
- Nevrodegenerativne bolezni in sistemska vnetja. Trinajstletni avtistični Jason je z rokama ponavljal iste gibe, ni si mogel zavezati vezalk, ni govoril v celih stavkih, izogibal se je komunikaciji. Mučile so ga pogoste prebavne motnje in kronično vnetje ušesa. Dr. David Perlmutter (2017:150) mu je predpisal uživanje probiotika in vitamina D. Po treh tednih je Jasonova mati povedala, da si deček zdaj sam zavezuje vezalke, se več pogovarja z njo … Potem so opravili še transplantacijo črevesne biote. Mesec dni po posegu je Jason povsem normalno komuniciral, prešle pa so tudi črevesne težave in vnetje ušesa.
Tudi pri Parkinsonovi bolezni lahko pomagajo dobre bakterije. Dr. Borody (2011b) je opisal primer izboljšanja te bolezni s pomočjo presaditve črevesne mikrobiote (FTM). Nedavno je druga raziskovalna skupina (Huang et al., 2019) zaradi hudega kroničnega zaprtja izvedla FTM terapijo pri enainsedemdesetletnem pacientu s Parkinsonovo boleznijo. Prebava se mu je uredila, po enem tednu pa je izginila tudi tresavica. Žal se je ta deloma (na eni nogi) ponovno pojavila dva meseca po posegu.
Navedeni primeri nakazujejo, da je lahko neuravnotežena črevesna biota bistven dejavnik raznih težkih bolezni, a zdi se, da ni vedno dovolj en sam poseg.
Smrad napoveduje bolezen
Tako kot je smrad iz hladilnika znak gnitja v njem, so neprijetni vonji na stranišču znak gnitja v črevesju in s tem neuravnotežene črevesne biote. Tako stanje imamo skoraj vsi, nekateri bolj izrazito, drugi manj. Zato je verjetno, da je črevesna stena prepustna, tudi če (še) nimamo resnih zdravstvenih težav.
Pri nas doma praktično ni več neprijetnih vonjav na stranišču vse od leta 2003, odkar redno uporabljamo bio probiotik EM. Tako stanje lahko dosežemo tudi s kakim drugim koncentriranim probiotikom. Pomembno pa je, da ga uživamo kontinuirano, sicer blato v tednu ali dveh spet zasmrdi.
Prednost bio probiotika EM je v tem, da je v obliki napitka. Če zvečer po umivanju zob požvrkljamo požirek ali dva in to pogoltnemo, zjutraj ni običajnega zadaha. Zadah je namreč znak gnitja v zgornjem delu prebavnega trakta. Po ugotovitvah dr. Bredesena (2017) so patogeni mikrobi iz ust, nosne votline in sinusov pomemben dejavnik Alzheimerjeve bolezni.
Za ohranjanje zdravja je torej bistveno, da z dobrimi bakterijami odpravljamo vire smradu v celotnem prebavnem traktu. Ob tem pa poskrbimo tudi za zdravo življenje nasploh, saj opisane bolezni lahko povzročajo tudi drugi dejavniki.

Summer frosts, strong gusts of wind, and tropical heat are typical phenomena in temperate zones. You can protect your crops from natural disasters and temperature changes by using a covering material that helps maintain the desired temperature and protects fruits and vegetables from frost, while also refreshing and protecting plants from drying out. However, in addition to temperature and humidity, lighting is also very important for plant growth. Proper use of light and shade helps summer crops achieve the best results.

Index:
Light is one of the essential conditions for plant development and growth. Plants only receive enough energy for photosynthesis when they have sufficient light. Different varieties have different lighting needs, and this primarily depends on the variety, stage of development, and growing season.

When installing a greenhouse or building one yourself, it is advisable to consider its location in relation to the cardinal directions. To ensure the greenhouse receives natural light throughout the day, it is best to orient it in a north-south direction, with the sloping roof facing west and south. This allows light to enter the space on one side for half the day and on the other side for the other half. In greenhouses with this orientation, plants develop evenly without bending in any particular direction.

However, in early spring, during autumn and winter frosts, the daylight hours are short, which is not suitable for the normal growth of vegetables, greens, and flowers. This can lead to a significant reduction in yield or a shorter flowering period and can even cause plants to die. To avoid such catastrophic consequences, it is advisable to extend the daylight hours and provide crops with the amount of light they need.

However, keep in mind that different plant species respond differently to the length of the day. There are two types of plants: long-day plants (onions, cabbage, garlic, root vegetables) and short-day plants (eggplants, peppers, beans, pumpkins, tomatoes).

The first type needs lighting that lasts more than 12 hours, while the second type needs light for 8-10 hours a day.

It is very important to follow the correct lighting regime, as flowering ornamental plants may not flower at all in this case, but only produce vegetative mass; root vegetables, on the other hand, will flower profusely but not produce a yield; and greens (lettuce, dill, chives) will bolt.

To extend the daylight hours in greenhouses, you need to install additional lighting. But before buying lamps, you need to calculate the cost of building the greenhouse and installing the electrical wiring. First, you need to lay the main cable to the greenhouse. This is usually done underground or overhead at a safe height.

Second, the wiring is installed inside the greenhouse. A cable with a cross-sectional area of at least 2 square millimeters is suitable for this. It is better if the cable has two colors – one color for the phase and the other for the neutral. You should also use corrugated tubing to conceal the wires. After that, connect all the wires to a separate panel to which all electrical devices will be connected.

Third, it is worth installing the necessary number of sockets with fuses in the greenhouse, which should be used to quickly switch off the power to the entire greenhouse with a switch. When installing the electrical wiring, remember that the greenhouse is a space with high humidity, so insulate all wire connections. The lamps used must be moisture-resistant.

There is a wide range of lamps for greenhouses available, which differ in purpose and price, intensity of radiation, and spectrum. The main advantage of fluorescent lamps can be seen in a video about building greenhouses. The fact is that they do not heat up, so they do not affect the temperature in the greenhouse. The radiation spectrum is considered favorable for plants. It is better to use LD or LDT lamps, in which the blue spectrum predominates, which is necessary for the photosynthesis process. Another plus in their favor is the economical consumption of electricity.

In different periods of the growing season, sodium lamps are best for lighting greenhouses. For growing green mass, DRIZ lamps are most suitable for the spectral radiation, but they are not suitable for flowering and fruiting. For these purposes, HPS lamps should be purchased, which provide plants with more energy during fruiting.

Energy-saving lamps are suitable for any stage of crop development; you just need to choose the right spectrum. During the growth period, choose ESL lamps with a blue spectrum; during flowering and fruiting, choose ESL lamps with a red spectrum. These lamps are economical and convenient to use, as they are equipped with a built-in ballast.

Metal halide lamps are considered the most complete for lighting fruits and vegetables. They are characterized by high power, a suitable radiation spectrum, and a long service life. The disadvantage of these products is their price – they are quite expensive.

If gardeners try to provide maximum lighting for plants grown in a greenhouse in early spring, in late autumn, and during winter frosts, then in the warm season, too much heat and radiant solar energy enters the greenhouse. Without the use of various shading methods, crops can stop growing and even die. Shading measures should be carried out in conjunction with providing watering and ventilation for the plants.

If the building is equipped with an efficient ventilation system, the plants may not need shading. If different types of plants with different light requirements are grown in the greenhouse, shade-loving plants should be placed under varieties that require intense lighting. It should not be forgotten that if the plants receive too much light, the leaves will turn red. This means that they need to be shaded.

Plants can be shaded externally and internally. This can be achieved in three ways: by painting a transparent coating, by spraying a protective liquid on the glazed surface to prevent light from entering the greenhouse, or by covering the greenhouse with a light-blocking material.

Previously, lime whitewash or emulsion paint diluted with water was used as a shading liquid. However, these substances have a significant disadvantage: at the end of the summer season, they need to be scraped off with a stiff brush, which is quite laborious and time-consuming.

Currently, formulations have been developed that can be easily removed from the painted surface, while they do not wash off in the rain. However, the layer of such a substance can gradually thin and lose its protective properties, so it needs to be renewed from time to time. This work should be carried out only in sunny, dry weather.

The disadvantage of using a liquid shading agent is that the substances remain on the coating, so the plants start to experience a lack of heat and light in cloudy weather. Because of this trend, it is best to use internal and external screens for shading.

Shading screens can be installed outside and inside the greenhouse, and they can be folded away whenever necessary. Retractable blinds can be hung only inside the greenhouse. See a video about how to make a greenhouse and how to install shading screens. External screens help reduce the light transmission of the transparent covering of the greenhouse and prevent the temperature inside the building from rising too much. In addition, such devices provide reliable protection for plants during spring frosts.

Shading screens installed inside the greenhouse are less effective than external devices. They reduce the intensity of light while allowing heat to enter the greenhouse, which causes the temperature in the building to rise.

In addition, internal screens are not suitable for use in buildings with protected ground, where ornamental plants with large flowers and leaves are grown. Therefore, it is better to place them on the outside of the greenhouse, and to prevent them from being damaged by strong gusts of wind, they should be attached to the frame elements of the greenhouse.

The most effective are shading screens made of wooden or plastic slats. They last longer and are easy to adjust and remove. Although some light passes through the gaps between the slats of such structures, this does not harm the crops, as the angle of incidence of the rays changes during the day. In addition, shading screens made of white plastic have proven to be effective.

If your garden is rarely visited, it is advisable to automate the process of raising and lowering the screens by equipping the devices with a motor with built-in photosensitive sensors that can control the operation of the system. In addition, readily available materials can be used for shading: opaque plastic film and bags, which are usually attached from the outside of the structure.

Watering the greenhouse has its own characteristics. If it is not properly organized, the plants can die from a lack or excess of moisture. Watering crops with a watering can or hose is time-consuming and energy-intensive. In this regard, it is more advisable to equip an automatic irrigation system in the greenhouse.

For crops grown in pots, a capillary irrigation system is more suitable, the principle of which is based on the action of the capillary force of wet sand. Water rises through the narrow gaps that form between the individual particles and enters the pots through the drainage holes.

To install a capillary system, lay a plastic film on the bottom of the stand, trench, or pallet, and then place a layer of sand on top, 5-8 centimeters thick. Its surface should be watered regularly with a watering can or moistened with an automatic device from a bottle turned upside down, with a nozzle attached in a special holder.

The sand is moistened with water from the bottle as it dries. A more complex device is a pressure tank, which is connected to the central water supply system. When a special valve is opened, water enters the sand.

On top, you need to place pots with plants and sink them in with rotating movements by about 3 centimeters, so that the sand completely fills the drainage holes.

Plants can also be watered with tubular systems. Among them, the drip irrigation system has become the most popular. This is a system of pipes that run along pipe supports and have holes located above each plant in the garden or above each pot. Thin pipes can be connected to each hole, or the hole can be equipped with a nozzle.

This technique is very suitable for crops that need constant moisture in the soil. The water supply should be connected to a timer and a solenoid valve to ensure the correct amount of water at certain intervals.

When using a drip irrigation system, it is good to regularly inspect each plant. Drip irrigation helps to provide all plants with the same amount of moisture, regardless of the preferences of individual species. As a result, the soil may be too wet in some areas and too dry in others.

The disadvantages need to be corrected manually: those plants whose soil has turned out to be slightly dry need to be watered, and those crops that do not need moisture can be temporarily excluded from the general drip irrigation system and waited until the soil under them dries out, and then continue to water them continuously.

So, after you have made the greenhouse frame and covered it with the chosen material, you can start arranging the lighting and shading system in the greenhouse, and the irrigation system in the greenhouse is also very important. Separately, it is necessary to determine the organization of watering plants in pots and in beds.

Rastline lahko zalivamo tudi s cevastimi sistemi. Med njimi je bil najbolj priljubljen sistem kapljičnega namakanja. Gre za sistem cevi, ki potekajo po cevnih nosilcih in v katerih so luknje, ki se nahajajo nad vsako rastlino na vrtu ali nad loncem. Na vsako luknjo je mogoče priključiti tanke cevi. Ali pa lahko luknjo opremite s šobo.
Ta tehnika je zelo primerna za tiste pridelke, ki potrebujejo stalno vlago v tleh. Dovod vode mora biti povezan s časovnikom in elektromagnetnim ventilom, da se zagotovi pravilna količina vode v določenih časovnih presledkih..
Ko vadite sistem kapljičnega namakanja, je dobro, da vsako rastlino redno pregledujete. Kapljično namakanje pomaga vsem rastlinam zagotoviti enako količino vlage, ne glede na preference posameznih vrst. Posledično je na nekaterih območjih zemlja lahko preveč mokra, na drugih je lahko preveč suha..
Pomanjkljivosti bo treba odpraviti ročno: zalivati je treba tiste rastline, tla, pod katerimi se je izkazalo, da so rahlo suha, in tiste pridelke, ki ne potrebujejo vlage, je mogoče začasno izključiti iz splošnega sistema namakanja s kapljicami in počakati dokler se tla pod njimi ne posušijo, je treba nadaljevati njihovo neprekinjeno zalivanje.
Tako potem, ko ste iz profila naredili rastlinjak in ga pokrili z izbranim materialom, lahko začnete z urejanjem sistema razsvetljave in senčenja v rastlinjaku, zelo pomemben pa je tudi namakalni sistem v rastlinjaku. Ločeno je treba določiti organizacijo zalivanja rastlin v lončkih in gredicah.

Si profesionalni prevajalec iz angleščine v slovenščino. Tvoja naloga je ustvariti visoko kakovostne prevode, ki so naravni, tekoči in natančni. Izogibaj se dobesednim prevodom, ki zvenijo nenaravno. Droughts have always existed and will continue to exist as just another in a series of natural phenomena. Nothing more, nothing less. Just like floods. However, the consequences they have on our society, and unfortunately also on nature, depend on us.
Science is clear and unequivocal. For over 100 years, we have been overstressing the natural ecosystems in which we have established our living environment. Water is no exception, but it is an excellent indicator of all the mistakes we have made in the past and continue to make. The current state of rivers in the Slovenian and Italian coastal areas, as well as elsewhere in Slovenia and Europe, is merely a glimpse into the future if we do not seriously change our attitude and respect for natural environments and their limitations. And we need to do this quickly.
The water cycle can be simply described as a sequence of reservoirs through which water circulates. In natural ecosystems, the amount of water and its flow between reservoirs are balanced, but through numerous excessive interventions, we have disrupted this balance. The basic unit of continental waters (river and lake systems) is a watershed (also a contributing area). A watershed is therefore an area from which all water eventually flows into the river's outlet. Due to this connection between the contributing area and the river, any intervention in the entire watershed is reflected in both the quality and quantity of water in the river. All impermeable surfaces (roads, roofs, parking lots, etc.) prevent water from seeping into the ground and underground to replenish water reserves for dry periods. In the long term, the clearing of native forests adapted to dry areas and their replacement with exotic trees with significantly higher water consumption contributes to the faster drying of the entire watershed. Extensive agricultural areas with crops that are not adapted to water scarcity, without mulch and without buffer strips, take their toll on the water balance. The removal of riparian vegetation, which causes excessive heating of the water, combined with transverse barriers such as dams, weirs, and barriers that stop the water, accelerates the evaporation of water from the river. Regulated riverbeds, surrounded by stone and concrete walls, prevent water from seeping from the riverbed into groundwater during high flows. Flood control embankments prevent water from spreading across wide floodplains, which would allow water to seep into the ground and underground, replenishing reserves for dry periods. We have limited and destroyed almost all the mechanisms of river ecosystems for storing water. Instead, we have established systems for draining water from the landscape as quickly as possible. So, is this really a natural disaster?
We have all the necessary knowledge and tools to limit the intensity, impact, and consequences of droughts on both natural ecosystems and the population. However, we will not achieve this by regulating rivers, cutting down riparian vegetation, and building ever-larger reservoirs. Instead of managing water, we need to start caring for water and adapt to the limits of our natural environment. Caring for water means, for example, giving rivers more space, restoring river meanders, oxbow lakes, and bays. We must allow periodic flooding of floodplains and restore riparian vegetation. Adaptation means, for example, reducing water consumption and increasing the capacity for rainwater harvesting. It is crucial to reduce water consumption in industry and agriculture by adapting technologies, products, and crops. We need to organize the collection of rainwater from impermeable surfaces and the use of so-called grey water in households, industry, and agriculture. In settlements, we need to increase the number and size of green areas and plant them with trees. And so on.
Currently, animals are paying the price for our excessive lifestyles. Will human lives also have to follow suit before we start acting differently?
Dr. Polona Pengal, University Diploma in Biology.

Suše so vedno bile in vedno bodo samo še en v vrsti naravnih pojavov. Nič več in nič manj. Povsem enako kot poplave. Od nas pa je odvisno, kakšne posledice bodo pustile na naši družbi in na žalost tudi na naravi.
Znanost je jasna in glasna. Že več kot 100 let prekomerno obremenjujemo naravne ekosisteme, v katerih smo si uredili življenjsko okolje. Voda ni izjema, je pa odličen pokazatelj vseh napak, ki smo jih naredili v preteklosti in jih še kar naprej ponavljamo. Trenutno stanje rek v slovenskem in italijanskem primorju, pa tudi drugod po Sloveniji in Evropi, je zgolj bežen pogled v prihodnost, če ne bomo resno spremenili svojega odnosa in spoštovanja naravnih okolij in njihovih omejitev. In to hitro.
Vodni krog poenostavljeno opišemo kot zaporedje rezervoarjev, med katerimi voda kroži. V naravnih ekosistemih sta količina vode in njeno pretakanje med rezervoarji uravnotežena, ljudje pa smo s številnimi prekomernimi posegi to ravnovesje porušili. Osnovna enota celinskih vod (sistema rek in jezer) je porečje (tudi prispevno območje). Porečje je torej območje, s katerega vsa voda prej ali slej konča na izlivu reke. Zaradi te povezave med prispevnim območjem in reko se prav vsak poseg na celotnem porečju odraža tako v kakovosti kot v količini vode v reki. Vse neprepustne površine (ceste, strehe, parkirišča itd.) onemogočajo pronicanje vode v zemljo in podzemlje, da bi napolnile zaloge vode za sušna obdobja. Dolgoročno izsekavanje domorodnih gozdov, prilagojenih na sušna območja, in njihovo nadomeščanje s tujerodnimi drevesi z izrazito višjo porabo vode, prispeva k hitrejšemu izsuševanju celotnega porečja. Obsežne kmetijske površine s posevki, ki niso prilagojeni pomanjkanju vode, brez zastirke in brez mejic, zahtevajo svoj davek na vodno bilanco. Izsekavanje obrežne vegetacije, ki povzroča prekomerno segrevanje vode v kombinaciji s prečnimi ovirami, kot so jezovi, pragovi in zapornice, ki ustavljajo vodo, pospešujejo izhlapevanje vode iz reke. By imagining the spirit of Fear that has settled in our body, we become aware that we are not the emotion, that the emotion has come and will also go, making it easier to create distance in the critical situation and look at it from the outside with a more clear perspective.
The Picture Book of 7 Trapped Heroes
The picture book of 7 trapped heroes tells the story of 7 heroes who were locked deep in a cave by Mr. Square (reason). Mr. Square doesn't allow the heroes to come out of the cave and be free. Mr. Square is afraid of life and softness because then he would become vulnerable.
The picture book of 7 trapped heroes is a book that every family should have on their bedside table or in some other visible place. This way, they are reminded every day in a pleasant and lighthearted way to pay attention to their emotions: the knight Anger, the spirit of Fear, the playful prince Joy, the grandmother Sadness, the slime Disgust, and the little boy Shame.
In moments when it's not necessary to pretend to be the ideal image of yourself, but to take the time to face all the not-so-socially desirable ideals of yourself. Emotions, disguised as heroes, help us to face them more easily, to breathe them in – to feel them fully and then let them go.
Sometimes, for example, it's not easy to connect with our sadness. If we imagine it as an old lady who has come to warm up and "complain," we will more easily transfer the warmth we need in moments of sadness to ourselves.
A common misconception is that shame should leave us when we become adults. No matter how old we are, shame visits us. Because we want to be serious and stable, so that nothing throws us off course, we will quickly pretend and suppress feelings of shame within ourselves. But if we imagine that a little boy, who embodies shame and is always "struggling" with shame, has visited us, we can breathe a sigh of relief that shame has only stayed with us for a short time.
When heavy clouds of fear gather around us, we can ease the intensity of the discomfort by imagining fear as a cute little spirit who is sometimes mischievous by magnifying our fears, but sometimes just wants to protect us.
Disgust is also our daily companion, no matter how unpleasant it is. A knight riding a dragon and wielding a sword will quickly deal with our anger when we identify either with him or with the dragon and unleash the energy of anger from ourselves, even if only in our imagination.
No matter how often any of the heroes visit us, they are all welcome. It's important that they are welcome because they bring important messages about ourselves, about what is happening within us, and what within us needs our attention. Only if we authentically express all the emotions that arise within us will we fully experience the dance of Prince Joy and the Lady of Love, which we all long for.
Let's embrace all parts of ourselves!

“I’m so fat, I have such a big belly, I have such a large butt…” These are just some of the phrases used by our teenage girls. Because they compare themselves too much to the role models they see in the media and entertainment world, they also want to lose weight and start diets that are dangerous for their health during a period of growth and development.

Assessing Nutritional Status
Before starting any weight loss program, it is important to assess nutritional status. This is a reflection of their diet and shows whether they are getting all the nutrients their body needs. Therefore, before starting any weight loss program, laboratory tests should be performed to analyze blood count, blood protein levels, serum vitamin levels, and body mass index (BMI). Only then can we assess whether they are overweight or underweight.

In adults, after the age of 20, this is relatively easy. BMI is calculated by dividing weight in kilograms by the square of height in meters.

A BMI between 25 and 29.5 indicates that attention should be paid to diet and exercise to prevent further weight gain. Values above 29.01 at age 15 and above 30 at age 20 indicate a risk of metabolic diseases.

During puberty, children grow by another quarter, so their energy and nutrient needs are also higher at this time.

Menstrual Cycle Disorders
After the age of 10, boys begin to develop muscle mass, while girls gain more body fat (if this increase is excessive, it remains in later adulthood). Therefore, on average, they have 2,5121 kJ (600 calories) fewer needs.

The need for minerals and vitamins is the same for both sexes. The consequences of poor nutrition during this period are reflected in the failure to reach maximum height and uneven development of individual parts of the body, most often the chest.

In girls, menstrual cycle disorders can also occur. In the case of excessive weight gain, it is definitely necessary to seek professional medical help to rule out any possible diabetes.

Rapid Weight Loss is Dangerous for Health
Losing 4 to 5 kilograms in 2 to 3 weeks definitely poses a significant risk to health. Rapid diets during adolescence primarily cause a deficiency of essential nutrients, such as vitamin C, which leads to a decrease in immunity, poor tissue regeneration, and slow growth.

Also, be careful if your teenage daughter starts diets that prohibit the consumption of dairy products, carbohydrates, or fats. Diets with raw fruits and vegetables are also dangerous. With such diets, your teenage daughter will not lose even a gram of fat, but rather, glycogen in the liver and muscles will be broken down. The brain and red blood cells need sugar, which the body takes from the muscles.

After a very restrictive diet, the kilograms also return quickly because the body learns during this time to protect its reserves. It is much better to choose the right type of food and learn how to eat without excess calories and also incorporate appropriate physical activity into your life.

High blood pressure and a sedentary lifestyle are closely linked. Small changes in daily routine can help improve blood pressure (i.e., lower it), and individuals taking medication to regulate blood pressure can naturally improve their health and potentially reduce or discontinue medication over time.
The risk of hypertension (high blood pressure) increases with age, but physical activity significantly reduces this risk. If your blood pressure is already too high, exercise can help improve it. And no, you don't need to run a marathon or join a gym and start training regularly. It's enough to start slowly and gradually incorporate exercise into your daily routine.
What is the connection between exercise and blood pressure?
Regular physical activity strengthens our heart. A stronger heart can pump more blood with less effort. If our heart is stronger and can do its job with less effort, this means that the tension in the arteries decreases because the heart is working with less force, resulting in lower blood pressure.
If we become more active, we can lower our systolic blood pressure (the higher reading) by approximately 4-9 mmHg. This is roughly the same effect as medication prescribed by a doctor. Therefore, for the average person with high blood pressure, it is sufficient to regulate blood pressure through exercise.
Individuals with normal blood pressure (less than 120/80 mmHg) can prevent the risk of increased blood pressure, which typically occurs with age, through exercise.
However, to truly lower blood pressure (and maintain it at that level), consistent physical activity is required. It takes approximately 1-3 months to measure the impact of exercise on blood pressure, and then it is important to continue exercising regularly.
How much exercise do we need?
Aerobic activities are an excellent way to control blood pressure. Try some of these:
- Walking, hiking
- Cycling
- Dancing
- Swimming
- Walking up stairs
- Team sports – basketball, tennis, volleyball
- ALSO: Mowing the lawn, gardening, vacuuming, and mopping…
It is recommended to be active for at least 150 minutes per week. This can be achieved by taking a 30-minute walk every day. What sounds better to you – taking pills for the rest of your life or taking a 30-minute walk each day? You can also split it into two 15-minute walks.
What about weightlifting?
Weightlifting causes a temporary increase in blood pressure (during the exercise itself). However, in the long term, this type of training can also have positive effects on blood pressure. But before you start, consult with your doctor. It is also a good idea to start with aerobic exercise (cardio) and then gradually introduce anaerobic exercise (weightlifting, gym training). Be careful when performing the exercises; work with a trainer the first time to ensure you are performing the exercises correctly.

Methane is a hydrocarbon and one of the greenhouse gases, meaning it traps heat from the sun in the Earth's atmosphere, warming the planet. The effect of methane is particularly pronounced in cows due to their four-chambered digestive system. In one of the chambers, called the rumen, microorganisms break down cellulose through fermentation, producing carbon dioxide and hydrogen. The digestive system of cows also contains methanogenic bacteria, which use these substances for their metabolism, producing methane in the process. Methane is then released through farts and burps. Thus, cows contribute to the amount of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. Of course, they are not entirely to blame; humans are responsible for the large number of cows on farms. Water is a universal solvent. When it rains, rainwater usually dissolves substances that are dispersed in the atmosphere. Today, the Earth's atmosphere has been heavily polluted due to human activities. When there are sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxide gases in the atmosphere, they easily dissolve in rainwater and come down as sulfuric and nitric acid. Then the pH of the rainwater becomes less than 7, and we say it is acidic.
In the last few decades, the acidity of rain has increased significantly due to human activities. For example, SO2 is produced during the burning of fossil fuels, and industrial processes produce H2S and S. Nitrogen oxide is also produced from fossil fuel-burning power plants.
Besides human activities, there are natural processes where these gases are formed. For example, SO2 is produced by volcanoes, and NO2 is produced by soil bacteria, natural fires, etc. Acid rain is harmful to soil organisms, plants, and aquatic organisms. In addition, it promotes the corrosion of metal infrastructure and other stone statues.

Rain is the main form in which evaporated water from the Earth's surface returns to the Earth. This is called liquid precipitation. The atmosphere contains water vapor, and when it becomes saturated in a particular place, it forms a cloud. Air saturation is easier when it cools down than when it is hot. For example, water vapor cools down when it comes into contact with a colder surface.
For rain to occur, the water vapor in the form of tiny droplets must combine to form larger water droplets. This process is called coalescence. Coalescence occurs when water droplets collide with each other, and when a droplet becomes heavy enough, it falls. Precipitation patterns vary depending on geographical differences. Deserts have minimal rainfall throughout the year, while rainforests have very high precipitation. Precipitation patterns are also influenced by various other factors, such as wind, solar radiation, human activities, etc. Rain is very important for agriculture. Differences and Similarities Between Fascism and Nazism

If we want to learn to live in peace and harmony, humanity must be mindful of historical mistakes. Because repetition is the mother of learning, and it is the only option. Today, the political climate in various countries involves a revival of fascist or Nazi ideas. And sometimes – both together. These terrible things can be observed in Norway, Germany, Greece, and the Middle East. What are the ideological systems considered dangerous for society and the state? What criteria are they similar by, and how do they differ?

Fascism and Nazism: Defining the Concepts

Fascism is an ideology, a political system, whose foundation is the complete subordination of the individual citizen to society. The power of the fascist state within its territory is truly unlimited.

Characteristic features of fascism:

- Cult of the personality of the ruler of the state.
- One-party system of government.
- Promotion of the superiority of one nation over other nations.

Fascism originated in Italy during the rule of Benito Mussolini. The symbol of the fascist ideology is the ancient Roman fasces, an attribute of power of the highest magistrates of that republic. It adorned the flag of Italy under Mussolini. This ideology also existed in the history of Brazil, Romania, Portugal, and other countries.

Benito Mussolini

Nazism, or National Socialism, is a combination of a socialist state with the propagation of nationalist views. Such a state forms a government with extremely right-wing political views. Consequently, the ruling elite of the state is extremely hostile to other nations and to competitors for a place in the "trough" of power.

Pure Nazism existed only in one country – Germany during the Third Reich. The symbol of Nazism was the swastika, which ancient peoples associated with life and the sun. It was featured on the flag and coat of arms of Germany. In addition, Nazi authorities made extensive use of the symbol of the cross. It was depicted on military equipment and was a symbol of the Wehrmacht. Today, this ideology is considered illegal by the international community.

Swastika

The Formation of Fascism and Nazism

Fascism appeared on the world historical stage earlier than Nazism. In its early stages, it was merely a theoretical concept. In contrast, National Socialism arose as a practice of implementing fascist ideas in the atmosphere of a country like Germany, from the birth of the Third Reich.

Adherents of both ideologies – fascism and Nazism – recognized the state, its interests, and its needs as the most important things in the world. Human rights, individual characteristics, and the interests of individuals gradually became irrelevant in such an environment.

Man and People

Both ideologies are known for their malevolent attitude towards man. For both fascists and Nazis, the individual citizen is nothing more than expendable material. If necessary, they are cannon fodder. Despite the similarity of views, the assessments of the role of nations in history among the proponents of these political systems are significantly different.

The undeniable superiority of one nation over others is clearly stated in Nazi doctrine. All nations, except for the bearers of this ideology, are considered second-class, underdeveloped, "inferior." The fascist worldview, on the other hand, does not deny the possibility of interstate cooperation – with all countries, with all nations.

What else unites these two ideological trends? Extreme totalitarianism of state power, tensions under which the harmonious development of society and especially individual citizens is impossible.

Ideologists of Fascism and Nazism

Benito Mussolini, a key figure in the implementation of fascist ideas, believed that racial identity was important, but only in the realm of feelings and not objective reality. Adolf Hitler, who implemented the ideas of the doctrine of National Socialism, was concerned with the purity of blood with fanatical precision. The racial doctrine of the ruler of the Third Reich prohibited – denying the right to existence and/or freedom – people with a certain genome and characteristics of the phenotype, and not people who have certain views.

Adolf Hitler

Conclusions. The Difference Between Fascism and Nazism

The ideological systems in question had different approaches to the process of shaping society both in their own country and abroad. Fascism is characterized by a desire to strengthen an ideal ethnic group through totalitarian state power. Nazism does not devote as much attention to this problem: the state declared one people "superhuman," and the state simply deals with suppressing all other nations.

The origin of the doctrine in question is not at all obvious: fascism is one of the ideologies on which National Socialism was based.

Fascism and Nazism differ in their attitude towards representatives of the national ideology that differs from the citizens of the state – the bearer. Thus, the fascist doctrine, taking into account the exclusivity of its own people, does not deny the possibility of interaction with other states – if this interaction aims at reviving the former state. Nazi ideology, on the other hand, cultivates extreme hostility towards certain nations or groups of people (anti-Semitism).

Fear of Fever
We need to be careful with children and take them to a doctor immediately if a baby up to six months old has a high temperature, and if a child refuses to drink fluids. Fever in both children and the elderly can lead to dehydration, so patients should drink plenty of fluids.
When to Lower It
People experience elevated body temperature differently. Some barely notice it, while even a slight increase can incapacitate others. As a general rule, we don’t lower slightly elevated temperatures, especially if they don’t bother us. However, if the temperature rises and the person feels worse, we use medications to lower the body temperature, which are called antipyretics. We should definitely lower very high temperatures; at 40 degrees Celsius, it is already necessary. Much earlier, when it exceeds 38 degrees Celsius, we lower the temperature in the elderly, chronically ill patients, pregnant women, and small children, as they are at risk of febrile seizures.
In adults, elevated body temperature is dangerous for people with heart and vascular diseases, as it increases oxygen consumption, so it should be lowered even before it reaches 38 degrees Celsius, according to infectious disease specialists. If we cannot lower it and symptoms such as rapid breathing, a feeling of difficulty breathing, confusion, difficulty urinating, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, or skin rash are present, we should consult a doctor.
A Sign That Something Is Wrong
The body generally regulates body temperature very well. A deviation is always a sign that something is wrong. The cause can be external, such as infections, or internal, such as autoimmune diseases. It can also be the result of an imbalance between the supply or production of heat and its dissipation. An example of this is heatstroke due to high external temperature.
The fact is that fever, although we are all very afraid of it, is not dangerous in itself. It is usually just one of the symptoms of an illness and an important defense mechanism of the body. However, the illness that caused the fever can be dangerous.

It would only take 5 seconds to completely change the planet. Without oxygen, you could say goodbye to the Hoover Dam and other concrete structures. These structures would immediately collapse. The fact is, oxygen acts as a binder for concrete. Without oxygen, concrete turns to dust.
By the way, all raw metals would instantly corrode. Essentially, it’s the oxidation layer on metals that prevents them from corroding. Feelings of fear in the face of danger trigger a biological response in us (fight, flight, or freeze), as well as a psychological response linked to upbringing. This includes whether or not it is acceptable within the family to talk about and express fear, which fears are considered valuable (fear of death, hunger), and which are not (fear of a classmate, mathematics), and what mechanisms the family uses to express (conversation, reassurance) or suppress fear (ignorance, punishment, ridicule). The transmission of behavioral patterns in response to feelings of fear to offspring occurs at an unconscious, subtle level.

Example of pattern transformation:
An adult individual experiences significant difficulties with public speaking, which is part of their job. In front of an audience, they experience feelings of being frozen, their body is in a state of paralysis, they are unable to coherently present the content, and they are afraid that others will attack them, so they would prefer to escape the situation.
If we try to understand her traumatic response to public speaking from a family context, we realize that there was never room in her life to express and learn how to deal with fear. When she began to express fear as a child, her parents encountered their own suppressed fear, which caused them to feel paralyzed, so they were unable to respond to her need and provide her with a sense of security, but instead ignored her need. This further amplified her feelings of fear, which, out of a need for survival, led her to suppress her fear. As parents, they were raised to be quiet, submissive individuals who were not allowed to express their emotions or stand out in public with their opinions.
They came from families that faced prolonged survival fear during World War II (life in a concentration camp, prolonged hunger, death, and attacks on the family), which had to be suppressed for the sake of survival. Being quiet, inconspicuous, and not expressing one's opinion was a way of surviving during and after the war. Not expressing fear and thus showing weakness was also a way of surviving, which her grandparents unconsciously passed on to her parents, and her parents passed on to her. Today, this person experiences feelings of paralysis in situations that are not life-threatening, but her nervous system has a different pattern.
The family pattern of being trapped in a response to feelings of fear, helplessness with paralysis, and the attitude towards expressing one's opinion has thus been unconsciously passed down through upbringing across generations. As recent neuroscientific research shows, even genetic changes can occur in extremely stressful situations.
Awareness of the broader family context of the pattern of suppressing fear gives us the opportunity for internal biological and psychological liberation and allows us to avoid passing on suppressed fear to the next generation. How we deal with fear today will affect future generations.

Live vaccines
Live vaccines contain pathogens that are capable of replication but have been attenuated. These can replicate, but generally do not cause disease. Nevertheless, the immune system responds to the attenuated pathogens in the vaccine by producing specific antibodies.
Advantages and disadvantages of live vaccines
- Advantage: The protective effect of vaccination after a live vaccination lasts for a long time, in some cases even for life (after complete primary immunization).
Adverse effects usually appear one to two weeks after live vaccination!
Live vaccines and other vaccinations
Live vaccines can be given at the same time as other live vaccines. A well-known example is the primary immunization against measles, mumps, rubella, and chickenpox – all of which are live vaccines. During the first vaccination, children receive the MMR vaccine and the chickenpox vaccine simultaneously. During the second vaccination appointment, they receive a quadrivalent vaccine (MMRV).
An interval between two live vaccinations is necessary because certain processes could interfere with the development of immune protection. For example, the measles vaccine is believed to temporarily weaken the immune system. In addition, researchers believe that signaling substances released after live vaccination prevent immune cells from recognizing and responding to further vaccine viruses injected too early.
Live vaccines and pregnancy
Live vaccines should not be given during pregnancy. The attenuated pathogens could harm the unborn child. It is also advisable to avoid becoming pregnant for four weeks after appropriate vaccination.
However, vaccination with live vaccines is possible during breastfeeding. Although the mother can transmit vaccine viruses through breast milk, this does not appear to pose a risk to the child based on current knowledge.
Inactivated vaccines
There are different types of inactivated vaccines:
- Whole-particle vaccine: whole, killed/inactivated pathogens.
- Subunit vaccine: inactivated fragments of pathogens (therefore, they are often better tolerated)
- Polysaccharide vaccine: sugar chains from the pathogen's envelope (immune cells only activate to a limited extent and are therefore only sufficiently effective in older children and adults)
- Conjugate vaccine: Contains only a specific protein component (antigen) of the pathogen.
- Toxoid vaccine: inactivated components of pathogen toxins
- Adsorbed vaccine: Here, the inactivated vaccine is additionally bound to adsorbents (e.g., aluminum hydroxide), which increases the immunization effect.
Advantages and disadvantages of inactivated vaccines
- Advantage: Inactivated vaccines generally have fewer side effects than live vaccines. Therefore, most vaccines today belong to this category. Unlike live vaccines, they also do not need to be separated from other vaccines (see above).
Undesirable side effects usually appear within one to three days after vaccination with an inactivated vaccine!

Živo cepivo
Živa cepiva vsebujejo patogene, ki so sposobni razmnoževanja, vendar so oslabljeni. Ti se lahko razmnožujejo, vendar na splošno ne povzročajo več bolezni. Kljub temu se imunski sistem na oslabljene patogene v cepivu odzove s tvorbo specifičnih protiteles.
Prednosti in slabosti živih cepiv
- Prednost: Cepilna zaščita po živem cepljenju traja dolgo časa, v nekaterih primerih celo doživljenjsko (po popolni osnovni imunizaciji).
Neželeni učinki se običajno pojavijo en do dva tedna po živem cepljenju!
Živa cepiva in druga cepljenja
Živa cepiva se lahko dajejo sočasno z drugimi živimi cepivi. Dobro znan primer je osnovna imunizacija proti ošpicam, mumpsu, rdečkam in noricam – vsa so živa cepiva. Ob prvem cepljenju otroci prejmejo istočasno cepivo MMR in cepivo proti noricam. Ob drugem terminu cepljenja štirikratno cepivo (MMRV).
Interval med dvema živima cepljenjima je potreben, ker bi lahko določeni procesi motili izgradnjo imunske zaščite. Na primer, cepivo proti ošpicam naj bi začasno oslabilo imunski sistem. Poleg tega raziskovalci domnevajo, da sporočilne snovi, ki se sproščajo po živem cepljenju, preprečujejo imunskim celicam, da bi prevzele in reagirale na nadaljnje viruse cepiva, vbrizgane prezgodaj.
Živa cepiva in nosečnost
Med nosečnostjo se ne sme dajati živih cepiv. Oslabljeni patogeni bi lahko škodovali nerojenemu otroku. Prav tako se izogibajte zanositvi štiri tedne po ustreznem cepljenju.
Med dojenjem pa je možno cepljenje na živo. Čeprav lahko mati prenaša cepilne viruse z materinim mlekom, to po dosedanjih spoznanjih ne predstavlja tveganja za otroka.
Mrtvo cepivo
Obstajajo različne vrste mrtvih cepiv:
- Cepivo iz celih delcev: celi, ubiti/inaktivirani patogeni.
- Razcepljeno cepivo: neaktivni fragmenti patogenov (zato se pogosto bolje prenašajo)
- Polisaharidno cepivo: sladkorne verige iz ovojnice patogena (imunske celice aktivirajo le v omejenem obsegu in so zato dovolj učinkovite le pri starejših otrocih in odraslih)
- Podenotno cepivo (podenotno cepivo): Vsebuje le specifičen proteinski del (antigen) patogena.
- Toksoidno cepivo: neaktivne sestavine toksinov patogenov
- Adsorbatno cepivo: Tu je inaktivirano cepivo dodatno vezano na adsorbente (npr. aluminijev hidroksid), kar poveča učinek imunizacije.

- Prednost: Inaktivirana cepiva imajo praviloma manj stranskih učinkov kot živa cepiva. Zato danes večina cepiv spada v to kategorijo. Za razliko od živih cepiv jih tudi ni treba ločiti od drugih cepiv (glejte zgoraj).

Towards Better Health
Monitoring Measles Infections
The disease occurs worldwide. Its occurrence is influenced by population density and access to vaccination. Before the introduction of vaccination, measles epidemics occurred every 2 to 5 years and lasted 3 to 4 months. In Slovenia, measles was the most common infectious disease for many years. Since 1968, when mandatory measles vaccination was introduced, the number of cases has begun to decline. The last measles epidemic in Slovenia was in 1994/95. In recent years, Slovenia has only recorded isolated imported cases, which cause a few secondary cases.

Causative Agent
The causative agent is the measles virus.

Mode of Transmission
The disease is transmitted directly or indirectly through infectious droplets from the respiratory secretions of an infected person (sneezing, coughing). A person with measles is contagious approximately four days before the rash appears and for another four days after. The disease is most easily transmitted in environments such as kindergartens, schools, and mass gatherings.

Incubation and Course of the Disease
From infection to the first signs of the disease, it takes about 10 days, ranging from 7 to 18 days. The onset of the disease is sudden, with high fever, severe headache, fatigue, runny nose, conjunctivitis, and cough. This is followed by the appearance of a rash in the mouth on the soft palate, tongue, and gums. On the second and third day of the disease, characteristic Koplik spots appear, which are small white spots found on the mucous membrane opposite the molars. Fourteen days after infection, a rash appears on the skin, which lasts up to seven days. Patients are severely affected when the rash appears and have a high fever.

People who have had measles are permanently protected against the disease.
The greatest risk of complications and death is in infants and immunocompromised individuals. Complications occur in approximately 30% of cases. In newborns and infants, the disease can cause severe diarrhea with dehydration. Children can also develop otitis media and severe pneumonia, which is the most common cause of death. Less frequently, inflammation of the central nervous system can also develop as a complication.

Susceptibility
All individuals who have not had measles or have not been successfully protected by vaccination are susceptible to measles.

Treatment
Only supportive treatment is available; the patient must rest and drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration. Antibiotics are only needed for bacterial complications of measles (otitis media, pneumonia, etc.).

Prevention
Measles is prevented by vaccination. Two doses of the vaccine are needed for protection.

On a hot day, clouds float in the sky, casting shadows over the sun.
As we wonder why clouds, which are made of so much water, don't fall, let's explore the science behind it.
Clouds are primarily composed of tiny water droplets or ice crystals.
All the clouds you see contain these minuscule water droplets and ice crystals, which are so small that their falling speed is negligible.
Therefore, this cloud material floats along with the surrounding air.
Its behavior is similar to dust particles that you sometimes see floating in the sunlight; the dust continuously floats in the air.
The radius of these water droplets ranges from a few micrometers to ten micrometers – 1 micrometer is one-millionth of a meter – how tiny!
The speed at which an object falls is related to its mass and surface area, which is why foam falls slower than gravel of the same weight.
For objects with a spherical shape, their mass is proportional to the cube of their radius, while their surface area is proportional to the square of the radius.
As these tiny water droplets grow, their mass becomes more significant than their shape, causing them to fall faster.
Even large water droplets with a radius of 100 micrometers have a falling speed of only about 27 centimeters per second.
And because ice crystals have irregular shapes, their falling speed is relatively slow.
The upward movement of air, also known as updraft, which occurs in the atmosphere, also affects the movement of clouds by counteracting the falling speed of the water droplets.
Clouds form in rising air.
As the air rises, the pressure decreases, causing it to expand and cool.
This cooling causes the water vapor in the air to condense and form water droplets.
Stratiform clouds, a type of cloud that produces steady, moderate rainfall, form in environments with large air masses but weak updrafts.
Convective or cumuliform clouds, a type of cloud that produces heavy rain and sometimes thunderstorms, form in environments with strong updrafts.
The total mass of a cloud compared to the air mass is relatively small.
Imagine a small cloud 3 km above the ground, with a volume of 1 cubic km, containing water with a density of 1 gram per cubic meter.
The total mass of the cloud particles is approximately 1 million kilograms, which is equal to the mass of 500 cars.
However, the total mass of the air with the same volume is approximately 1 billion kilograms, 1000 times heavier than the water in the clouds.
Therefore, even though clouds contain a lot of water, the water is dispersed over several kilometers in the form of tiny water droplets or crystals, which are too small for gravity to have a significant effect.
From our perspective on the ground, clouds appear to float in the air.
These water droplets will only fall as rain when the water content in the clouds becomes so dense and saturated that the droplets combine to form larger raindrops, which have enough mass to fall as rain.
Reference:
Meteorology Today, Donald Ahrens.
